# Appendix F: AQFT Framework for Continuum Emergence and Locality

This appendix outlines the mathematical framework of Algebraic Quantum Field Theory (AQFT) in curved spacetimes (Haag 1996; Brunetti et al. 2015), providing the rigorous setting necessary to formalize the operational-continuum description of the discrete MPU network and to precisely analyze the status of locality and causality within the Predictive Universe (PU) framework. This approach focuses on the algebras of local observables and their relationships, offering a robust way to handle the finite-resolution continuum compression and define concepts like the stress-energy tensor and microcausality. The geometric operational-continuum branch is packaged by Theorem 43.5 under its stated hypotheses; the present appendix states the additional algebraic coarse-graining conditions under which this geometric branch supports a stable local AQFT net.

**F.1 Net of Local Observables ($\mathfrak{A}_n(\mathcal{O})$)**

We associate algebraic structures to regions of the discrete MPU network sequence $(\mathcal{N}_n, d_{\mathcal{N}_n})$ that converges geometrically to the emergent spacetime manifold $(M, g_{\mu\nu})$.

*   <a id="definition-f1-spacetime-regions-and-discrete-correspondences"></a>**Definition F.1 (Spacetime Regions and Discrete Correspondences):** Let $\mathfrak{O}(M)$ be the set of suitable causally complete, bounded, open regions on the separately certified $3+1$ spacetime-promotion branch in the emergent globally hyperbolic spacetime $(M, g_{\mu\nu})$. For $\mathcal{O} \in \mathfrak{O}(M)$, let $R_n(\mathcal{O}) \subset \mathcal{V}_n$ denote the subset of MPU vertices whose emergent location in the continuum limit lies within $\mathcal{O}$, such that $R_n(\mathcal{O})$ fills $\mathcal{O}$ in the limit $n\to\infty$.

*   <a id="definition-f2-microscopic-local-algebras-mathfraka_nmathcalo"></a>**Definition F.2 (Microscopic Local Algebras $\mathfrak{A}_n(\mathcal{O})$):** To each region $\mathcal{O} \in \mathfrak{O}(M)$, associate a local algebra $\mathfrak{A}_n(\mathcal{O})$ acting on the Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}(R_n(\mathcal{O})) = \bigotimes_{v \in R_n(\mathcal{O})} \mathcal{H}_v$, where $\mathcal{H}_v$ is the Hilbert space of MPU $v$ (Proposition 4).
    1.  **Fundamental Operators:** Let $\mathcal{B}_v$ be a chosen basis set of bounded operators on $\mathcal{H}_v$ (e.g., projections related to the spectral decomposition of $\hat{H}_v, \hat{C}_v$, representation of basis states, unitaries corresponding to local transformations).
    2.  **Finite Subsets:** For any finite subset of vertices $F \subset R_n(\mathcal{O})$, the algebra $\mathfrak{A}_n(F)$ is the algebra generated by operators acting only on $\bigotimes_{v \in F} \mathcal{H}_v$. This could be taken as $\bigotimes_{v \in F} \text{Alg}(\mathcal{B}_v)$.
    3.  **Local C*-Algebra:** The local C*-algebra $\mathfrak{A}_n^{C^*}(\mathcal{O})$ is the closure of the union of $\mathfrak{A}_n(F)$ for all finite subsets $F \subset R_n(\mathcal{O})$ under the operator norm: $\mathfrak{A}_n^{C^*}(\mathcal{O}) = \overline{\bigcup_{F \subset R_n(\mathcal{O}), |F|<\infty} \mathfrak{A}_n(F)}^{\|\cdot\|}$.

    4.  **Local von Neumann Algebra:** The local von Neumann algebra $\mathfrak{A}_n^{vN}(\mathcal{O})$ is the weak*-closure of $\mathfrak{A}_n^{C^*}(\mathcal{O})$ in a relevant representation of the full network algebra.

This construction defines a net of algebras $\mathcal{O} \mapsto \mathfrak{A}_n(\mathcal{O})$ indexed by $n$ and regions $\mathcal{O}$, satisfying isotony: if $\mathcal{O}_1 \subset \mathcal{O}_2$, then $\mathfrak{A}_n(\mathcal{O}_1) \subset \mathfrak{A}_n(\mathcal{O}_2)$ (operators localized in $\mathcal{O}_1$ are also localized in $\mathcal{O}_2$).

<a id="theorem-f1d-effective-supplied-coherent-state-contact-hessians-on-an-expanding-massive-scalar-lattice"></a>**Theorem F.1d (Effective Supplied-Coherent-State Contact Hessians on an Expanding Massive Scalar Lattice).** In units $\hbar=1$, fix a computably named positive scalar mass $m$ and real curvature coupling $\xi$, with rational certified bounds $0<m_0\le m\le\overline m$ and $|\xi|\le X$. Parts I–II specify the actual finite lattice, continuous service clock, whole-quadratic occupation compression, trace-one comparison state and full-torus degree-four local phase. Let
$$
\mathcal K=\{xh+yk:x,y\in[-1,1]\},\qquad
h_{12}=h_{21}=b(t)G(x),\quad k_{12}=k_{21}=b(t-4)G(x),
$$
with all other components zero, $b(t)=e^{-1/(1-t^2)}$ for $|t|<1$ and zero otherwise, and $G(x)=e^{-|x|^2/2}$. For each rational $\varepsilon>0$ there is a terminating algorithm returning an original index $N_{\rm Hess}(\varepsilon)$ such that
$$
\sup_{\substack{\alpha\in\{1,i\},\ a,b\in\{+,-\}\\u,v\in\mathcal K}}
|W^{\rho_\alpha}_{n,ab}(u,v)-W^{\rho_\alpha}_{ab}(u,v)|\le\varepsilon
\quad\text{for every }n\ge N_{\rm Hess}(\varepsilon).
\tag{F.1d.1}
$$
The algorithm retains every physical derivative alias, the scalar subtraction, metric seagull, coherent cross-sector term, lost-weight vacuum fill and actual occupation excursion. It supplies the tested action-density and both upper- and lower-index stress-response moduli in Part VII. Its domain is this compact two-direction family and the two specified compact-momentum $C^1$ coherent states, not an arbitrary effective joint-Schwartz or nonzero-curved-metric family. The canonical contact vanishes for these shear directions by its defining tensor formula; the metric and lowering-index contacts do not.

#### Part I. Complete source, state and metric-vertex definitions

For every integer $n\ge1$, set
$$
a_n=\tau_n=4^{-n},\quad R_n=4^n,\quad\ell_n=16^n+1,\quad
L_n=a_n\ell_n=4^n+4^{-n},\quad\delta_n=2\pi/L_n,
$$
$$
X_n=a_n\{-b_n,\ldots,b_n\}^3,\quad
\mathcal P_n=\delta_n\{-b_n,\ldots,b_n\}^3,\quad b_n=(\ell_n-1)/2,
$$
$$
\omega_n(p)^2=m^2+4a_n^{-2}\sum_{j=1}^3\sin^2(a_np_j/2),\qquad
\mathcal H_n=\bigoplus_{r=0}^{R_n}\operatorname{Sym}^r\ell^2(\mathcal P_n),\qquad
H_n=d\Gamma(\omega_n)|_{N\le R_n}.
\tag{F.1d.S1}
$$
The vacuum energy is zero. Time in the interaction is the original continuous source time; the given service clock is $\tau_n$. The continuum one-particle measure is $dp$, with quadratic-kernel factor $(2\pi)^{-3}$, and the finite factor is $L_n^{-3}=\delta_n^3(2\pi)^{-3}$. Define centered cell isometries and the common continuum carrier by
$$
J_ne_p=\delta_n^{-3/2}\mathbf1_{p+[-\delta_n/2,\delta_n/2)^3},\quad
I_n=\bigoplus_{r=0}^{R_n}J_n^{\otimes_s r},\quad Q_n=I_nI_n^*,\quad
\mathcal H=\Gamma_s(L^2(\mathbb R^3,dp)).
\tag{F.1d.S2}
$$
Normal-order the continuum operators on the algebraic finite-Schwartz core; the explicit estimates below also define their required moments on the stated coherent vectors. All real metric directions give unitary finite amplitudes; complex bilinear testing is performed after the real adjoint identities.

Let $r(x)=(1-x^2)^2\mathbf1_{|x|\le1}$, $c=(1/4,1/4,0)$ and
$$
f(p)=8(315/256)^{3/2}\prod_{j=1}^3r(4(p_j-c_j)),\qquad
\Psi_\alpha=e^{-1/2}\bigoplus_{s\ge0}\frac{\alpha^sf^{\otimes s}}{\sqrt{s!}},\quad
\rho_\alpha=|\Psi_\alpha\rangle\langle\Psi_\alpha|,\quad\alpha\in\{1,i\}.
$$
Here $\|f\|_2=1$ and $\|\nabla f\|_2=12$, because $\int r^2=256/315$ and $\int(r')^2=256/105$. The mode is compactly supported and $C^1$; it is not replaced by a Schwartz mode. The actual comparison channel is
$$
\rho_{\alpha,n}=I_n^*\rho_\alpha I_n+
\operatorname{Tr}[(1-Q_n)\rho_\alpha]|\Omega_n\rangle\langle\Omega_n|.
\tag{F.1d.S3}
$$
It is positive and trace one, retaining all cross-sector coherences. For $V=(N+1)^{12}W_{64}$, $W_{64}=(1+\sum_j|p_j|)^{64}$ on each sector, its supplied sufficient moment bound is $E_V\le E_0=3^{128}B_{153}$, with $B_{153}$ the integer Bell number. The effective tails below use the actual compact mode and Poisson coefficients, rather than inferring an algorithm from this finite moment alone.

Use $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $P=-\Box+m^2$ and
$$
D_+(t,x)=\int\frac{d^3p}{(2\pi)^3}\frac{e^{-i\omega(p)t+ipx}}{2\omega(p)},\quad
D_F(t,x)=D_+(|t|,x),\quad G_F=iD_F,\quad PG_F=1.
$$
Normal ordering always uses this flat vacuum. With indices raised by $\eta$, define
$$
v_h=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}_\eta h,\quad
v_{hk}=\tfrac14(\operatorname{tr}_\eta h)(\operatorname{tr}_\eta k)-\tfrac12h_{\mu\nu}k^{\mu\nu},
$$
$$
a_h^{\mu\nu}=v_h\eta^{\mu\nu}-h^{\mu\nu},\quad
a_{hk}^{\mu\nu}=v_{hk}\eta^{\mu\nu}-v_h k^{\mu\nu}-v_k h^{\mu\nu}
+{h^\mu}_{\gamma}k^{\gamma\nu}+{k^\mu}_{\gamma}h^{\gamma\nu}.
\tag{F.1d.S4}
$$
The complete curvature Hessian is fixed as follows:
$$
{C_h^\rho}_{\mu\nu}=\tfrac12\eta^{\rho\gamma}
(\partial_\mu h_{\gamma\nu}+\partial_\nu h_{\gamma\mu}-\partial_\gamma h_{\mu\nu}),
$$
$$
{C_{hk}^\rho}_{\mu\nu}=-\tfrac12\left[
h^{\rho\gamma}(\partial_\mu k_{\gamma\nu}+\partial_\nu k_{\gamma\mu}-\partial_\gamma k_{\mu\nu})
+k^{\rho\gamma}(\partial_\mu h_{\gamma\nu}+\partial_\nu h_{\gamma\mu}-\partial_\gamma h_{\mu\nu})\right],
$$
$$
(A_h)_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\rho{C_h^\rho}_{\mu\nu}-\partial_\nu{C_h^\rho}_{\mu\rho},\quad
R_h=\partial_\mu\partial_\nu h^{\mu\nu}-\Box\operatorname{tr}_\eta h,
$$
$$
\begin{aligned}
R_{hk}={}&\eta^{\mu\nu}\left[
\partial_\rho{C_{hk}^\rho}_{\mu\nu}-\partial_\nu{C_{hk}^\rho}_{\mu\rho}
+{C_h^\rho}_{\rho\gamma}{C_k^\gamma}_{\mu\nu}
+{C_k^\rho}_{\rho\gamma}{C_h^\gamma}_{\mu\nu}\right.\\
&\left.\hspace{8mm}-{C_h^\rho}_{\nu\gamma}{C_k^\gamma}_{\mu\rho}
-{C_k^\rho}_{\nu\gamma}{C_h^\gamma}_{\mu\rho}\right]
-h^{\mu\nu}(A_k)_{\mu\nu}-k^{\mu\nu}(A_h)_{\mu\nu},\\
M_h={}&m^2v_h+\xi R_h,\quad
M_{hk}=m^2v_{hk}+\xi(R_{hk}+v_hR_k+v_kR_h).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1d.S5}
$$
Put $P_hu=-\partial_\mu(a_h^{\mu\nu}\partial_\nu u)+M_hu$, and likewise with $hk$. The action vertices are
$$
S_h=-\tfrac12:\langle\phi,P_h\phi\rangle:
=\tfrac12\int h_{\mu\nu}T_\xi^{\mu\nu},\qquad
S_{hk}=-\tfrac12:\langle\phi,P_{hk}\phi\rangle:,
$$
$$
q_h(x)=-\tfrac12[a_h^{\mu\nu}:\partial_\mu\phi\partial_\nu\phi:+M_h:\phi^2:](x),
$$
$$
T_{\mu\nu}^{(\xi)}=:\partial_\mu\phi\partial_\nu\phi:
-\tfrac12\eta_{\mu\nu}(:\partial_\gamma\phi\partial^\gamma\phi:+m^2:\phi^2:)
+\xi(\eta_{\mu\nu}\Box-\partial_\mu\partial_\nu):\phi^2:.
\tag{F.1d.S6}
$$
These are the two flat derivatives of $-\tfrac12\int\sqrt{-g}(g^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\phi\partial_\nu\phi+m^2\phi^2+\xi R_g\phi^2)$. At finite $n$, periodize each metric direction first, form (F.1d.S4)–(F.1d.S5), then sample. Use $D_0=\partial_t$, $D_i=D_i^+$ and bilinear adjoints $D_0^*=-\partial_t$, $D_i^*=-D_i^-$. The field used to calculate each complete quadratic is
$$
\Phi_n(t,x)=L_n^{-3/2}\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_n}
\frac{a_pe^{-i\omega_n(p)t+ipx}+a_p^\dagger e^{i\omega_n(p)t-ipx}}{\sqrt{2\omega_n(p)}},
\quad[a_p,a_r^\dagger]=\delta_{pr}.
$$
Weyl-symmetrize and vacuum-normal-order the whole quadratic, then compress it to $N\le R_n$. Separately compressing field factors would give different matrices. Their spatial sums are $q_{n,h}(t),q_{n,hk}(t)$, with time integrals $S_{n,h},S_{n,hk}$.

For $\mathsf A=-\sqrt{-g}g^{00}$ and $\mathsf B^i=-\sqrt{-g}g^{0i}$, set
$$
F_{n,h}=\mathsf A_h\pi+\mathsf B_h^iD_i\Phi_n,\quad \pi=\partial_t\Phi_n,
$$
$$
b_n(h,k;t)=a_n^3\sum_x:\operatorname{sym}F_{n,h}F_{n,k}:_{N\le R_n},\quad
B_n(h,k)=\int b_n(h,k;t)dt.
\tag{F.1d.S7}
$$
The fixed-canonical-momentum Hamiltonian density is
$$
\mathcal H=\tfrac12\mathsf A^{-1}(\pi-\mathsf B^iD_i\varphi)^2
+\tfrac12C^{ij}D_i\varphi D_j\varphi+\tfrac12M\varphi^2.
$$
Here $C^{ij}=\sqrt{-g}g^{ij}$ and $M=\sqrt{-g}(m^2+\xi R_g)$. Its exact second metric derivative, with the same ordering and compression, is $-H_{n,hk}=q_{n,hk}-b_n(h,k)$. Thus the canonical interaction seagull is $S_{n,hk}-B_n(h,k)$.

#### Part II. Local subtraction, actual amplitudes and branch signs

Fix a real symmetric tensor basis $E^A$, put $v_A=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}_\eta E^A$ and $a_A^{\mu\nu}=v_A\eta^{\mu\nu}-(E^A)^{\mu\nu}$, and let $r_A(z,q)$ be the coefficient of $e^{-izt+iqx}$ in $R_h$ for that plane-wave direction. Define, with pair-momentum symmetrization,
$$
e_0^+(p)=i\omega_n(p),\quad e_j^+(p)=a_n^{-1}(e^{-ia_np_j}-1),
$$
$$
b_{n,A}(z,q;p)=-\frac{a_A^{\mu\nu}e_\mu^+(p)e_\nu^+(q-p)+m^2v_A+\xi r_A(z,q)}
{4\sqrt{\omega_n(p)\omega_n(q-p)}}.
\tag{F.1d.S8}
$$
The unaliased vacuum multiplier is
$$
\begin{aligned}
\Pi_{n,AB}(z,q)=\frac2{L_n^3}\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_n}\left[
\frac{\overline{b_{n,A}(z,q;p)}b_{n,B}(z,q;p)}{\omega_n(p)+\omega_n(q-p)-z-i0}\right.\\
\left.\hspace{13mm}+
\frac{b_{n,A}(-z,-q;p)\overline{b_{n,B}(-z,-q;p)}}{\omega_n(p)+\omega_n(-q-p)+z-i0}\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1d.S9}
$$
Conjugation is of real-frequency coefficients; poles are Feynman boundary distributions. Interpolate continuous spatial $q$ using the same periodic lattice symbols and keep the continuum derivative polynomial $r_A$. Let $t_4$ be the full Taylor jet of total external four-momentum degree at most four at zero. All its coefficients are ordinary finite derivatives because of the mass gap. With $\widehat h(z,q)=\int e^{izt-iqx}h(t,x)dt\,dx$, the phase is
$$
C_n(h,k)=-L_n^{-3}\sum_{q\in\delta_n\mathbb Z^3}\int\frac{dz}{2\pi}
\widehat h_A(-z,-q)(t_4\Pi_n)_{AB}(z,q)\widehat k_B(z,q).
\tag{F.1d.S10}
$$
Use its transpose-reflected symmetric bilinear kernel. The spatial sum is over the full torus Fourier lattice, not only $\mathcal P_n$. It is a convergent local differential functional with every finite anisotropic coefficient retained. For a joint test, use its double Fourier restriction $\widehat H_{AB}(-z,-q;z,q)$ in place of the product. Equivalently apply the corresponding finite diagonal derivatives of $H$.

This phase is real on real tests. Near zero the two denominators in (F.1d.S9) are subthreshold and real; conjugating interchanges $A,B$, and momentum reflection interchanges the orders. After symmetric reflection the symbol is Hermitian and $\Pi_n(-z,-q)=\Pi_n(z,q)^T=\overline{\Pi_n(z,q)}$. Its Taylor jet preserves both relations. Conjugating (F.1d.S10) and using Fourier reality returns the same pairing. Off-diagonal entries need not individually be real. Polarization gives the bilinear statement, and $e^{iC_n(f,f)/2}$ preserves finite unitarity.

The actual sampled loop $\Pi_n^{\rm samp}$ includes every derivative alias. Equivalently it is fixed by $\langle\Omega_n,\mathcal T_n^{\rm can}(h,k)\Omega_n\rangle=-i\Pi_n^{\rm samp}(h,k)$, with the whole-quadratic chronological matrices already specified in Part I. The explicit sampled shear formula appears in Part III. Put
$$
\mathcal T_{n,R}^*(h,k)=\mathcal T_n^{\rm can}(h,k)+iB_n(h,k)-iC_n(h,k)I.
\tag{F.1d.S11}
$$
For the continuum, use the same two summands as (F.1d.S9) with $e_j^+=-ip_j$ and $\omega(p)=\sqrt{m^2+|p|^2}$, retaining the factor two. If their integrand before momentum measure is $F(z,q;p)$, define
$$
\Pi_R(z,q)=\int\frac{d^3p}{(2\pi)^3}[F(z,q;p)-t_4F(z,q;p)],
\tag{F.1d.S12}
$$
paired first with the external test before removing its internal cutoff at thresholds. The estimates in Part III prove this prescribed pairing on the tests at issue. Use field labels $a\in\{\varnothing,0,1,2,3\}$, with $X_\varnothing=\phi$, $X_\mu=\partial_\mu\phi$, $\mathscr D_\varnothing=I$, $\mathscr D_\mu=\partial_\mu$, and $q_h=\tfrac12b_h^{ab}:X_aX_b:$. Set
$$
\mathcal Q_4=\tfrac14\int b_h^{ab}(x)b_k^{cd}(y):X_a(x)X_b(x)X_c(y)X_d(y):\,dxdy,
$$
$$
\mathcal Q_{2,F}=\int b_h^{ab}(x)b_k^{cd}(y)
(\mathscr D_{x,a}\mathscr D_{y,c}D_F(x-y)):X_b(x)X_d(y):\,dxdy,
\qquad \mathcal T_R^*=\mathcal Q_4+\mathcal Q_{2,F}-i\Pi_RI.
\tag{F.1d.S13}
$$
The label $\varnothing$ means an undifferentiated field; the distinct label $0$ is the time derivative. All propagator derivatives are distributional. In particular
$$
\partial_t\partial_sD_{F,n}=\langle\mathcal T\pi_n\pi_n\rangle
+i\delta(t-s)a_n^{-3}\delta_{xy},
$$
which supplies $+iB_n$ in (F.1d.S11). On sectors at most $r$, when $R_n\ge r+4$, Wick ordering gives exactly
$$
\mathcal T_{n,R}^*=
\mathcal Q_{4,n}+\mathcal Q_{2,F,n}-i[\Pi_n^{\rm samp}+C_n]I.
\tag{F.1d.S14}
$$
The top-sector excursion outside the low head is retained and bounded in Part IV.

For real $f$, define the finite polynomial completion of the source two-jet by
$$
U_n[f]=e^{iC_n(f,f)/2}\mathcal T\exp\left(i\int
[q_{n,f}(t)+\tfrac12q_{n,ff}(t)-\tfrac12b_n(f,f;t)]dt\right),
$$
$$
Z_n[f,g]=\operatorname{Tr}(U_n[f]\rho_nU_n[g]^*),\qquad
W_n=-i\log Z_n\quad\text{as a germ at }(0,0).
\tag{F.1d.S15}
$$
At fixed $n$ all matrix coefficients have integrable norms in time, so their finite-interval unitary propagators converge in norm as endpoints tend to infinity, with omitted-tail bound given by the generator's tail integral. Thus the completion is an actual finite unitary, not a truncated exponential. Since $Z_n(0,0)=1$, derivatives through degree two are ordinary ratio derivatives; no uniform zero-free neighborhood is assumed. Higher coefficients of this chosen completion are not a full nonzero-curved-metric scalar theory.

For real $u,v$ let $\mu(u)=\operatorname{Tr}\rho S_u$, $w(u,v)=\operatorname{Tr}\rho S_uS_v$, $v(u,v)=w(u,v)-\mu(u)\mu(v)$, $d(u,v)=\operatorname{Tr}\rho S_{uv}$, $t(u,v)=\operatorname{Tr}\rho\mathcal T_R^*(u,v)$ and $t_c=t-\mu(u)\mu(v)$. Their finite counterparts use precisely the finite matrices and trace-one channel above. Differentiating (F.1d.S15) gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
W_{n,++}(u,v)&=d_n(u,v)+it_{c,n}(u,v),\\
W_{n,+-}(u,v)&=-iv_n(v,u),\\
W_{n,-+}(u,v)&=-iv_n(u,v),\\
W_{n,--}(u,v)&=-d_n(u,v)+i\overline{t_{c,n}(u,v)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1d.S16}
$$
The continuum coefficients are defined by the same displayed formulas and (F.1d.S13). The bar is the anti-chronological adjoint identity on real tests, before complex bilinear extension. A mixed branch receives no independent counterterm. The backward scalar is minus the conjugate paired scalar. In all branches the scalar is paired before estimating comparison-state loss, and its coefficient is exactly $\operatorname{Tr}\rho_n=1$; no separate $\lambda_nC_n$ or $C_n(Q_n-I)$ convergence is assumed.

For the separated cross pairs, the local metric seagull, canonical contact, scalar phase and density/index contacts vanish exactly because the two time supports and all their derivatives are disjoint. Since $k$ is later than $h$, their four cross coefficients are $iv(k,h),-iv(k,h),-iv(h,k),i\overline{v(k,h)}$. The nonlocal vacuum cross covariance remains. Part V controls these ordinary products; Part IV treats overlapping chronology rather than inferring it from separation.

#### Part III. Complete paired real-time vacuum scalar modulus

The constants in this part are local to the vacuum estimate. Write $a=a_n$, $\delta=\delta_n$ and use a rational $M\ge m$ from the computable mass name. Put $B(z)=\int e^{izt}b(t)dt$, $g(q)=(2\pi)^{3/2}e^{-|q|^2/2}$,
$$
c(t)=\int b(s)b(s+t)ds,\qquad H(E)=i\int_0^2c(t)e^{-iEt}dt.
$$
The exact source-normalized pairing, at every threshold, is
$$
H(E)=\int\frac{dz}{2\pi}\frac{|B(z)|^2}{E-z-i0},\qquad
\operatorname{Im}H(E)=|B(E)|^2/2,\qquad |H^{(r)}(E)|\le2^{r+2}.
\tag{F.1d.V1}
$$
Indeed $(E-z-i0)^{-1}=i\int_0^\infty e^{-i(E-z)t}dt$ as a boundary distribution. Insert a positive exponential regulator, use Fourier inversion and Fubini, then remove it on the compact support of $c$. The sign is the positive $i\pi\delta(E-z)$ sign. The derivative bounds follow from $0\le c\le2$ and support in $[-2,2]$.

For the shear, (F.1d.S8) reduces to the external-energy-independent vertex
$$
b_a(q;p)=\frac{e_1(p)e_2(q-p)+e_2(p)e_1(q-p)+2\xi q_1q_2}
{4\sqrt{\omega_a(p)\omega_a(q-p)}},\quad A_a=|b_a|^2,\quad E_a=\omega_a(p)+\omega_a(q-p).
$$
Reflection $b_a(-q;-p)=\overline{b_a(q;p)}$ and the centered internal grid combine the source factor two and the two chronological half-lines into $4A_aH(E_a)$. Let $M_j=\int z^j|B(z)|^2dz/(2\pi)=\int|b^{(j/2)}|^2dt$, for $j=0,2,4$. The paired total-degree-four jet is exactly $4\sum_{j=0,2,4}M_jt_{4-j}^q(A_aE_a^{-j-1})$, with every spatial multiindex retained. Set
$$
\Psi_a(q;p)=4\left[A_aH(E_a)-\sum_{j=0,2,4}M_jt_{4-j}^q(A_aE_a^{-j-1})\right],
$$
$$
U_n=\delta^3\sum_{q\in\mathcal P_n}e^{-|q|^2}
\frac{\delta^3}{(2\pi)^3}\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_n}\Psi_a(q;p).
\tag{F.1d.V2}
$$
Replacing both sums by integrals gives the prescribed $\Pi_R(h,h)$. The external spatial factor $(2\pi)^{-3}$ cancels the square of $g(q)$. The remaining difference between $\Xi_n:=\Pi_n^{\rm samp}+C_n$ and $U_n$ is precisely the derivative aliases and negative of the full-torus Taylor tail outside $\mathcal P_n$.

For explicit bump bounds, set $P_0(t)=1$ and
$$
P_{r+1}=(1-t^2)^2P_r'+[4rt(1-t^2)-2t]P_r,\quad
\beta_0=1,\quad\beta_r=\|P_r\|_{\ell^1({\rm coefficients})}(2r)^{2r}\ (r\ge1).
$$
Then $b^{(r)}=bP_r/(1-t^2)^{2r}$ inside the support and its zero extension is smooth, giving $|b^{(r)}|\le\beta_r$. Put $\mu_j=2\beta_{j/2}^2\ge M_j$ and $C_6=4\beta_6\ge\int_0^2|c^{(6)}|$. Six integrations by parts use vanishing endpoint derivatives at $2$, odd derivatives of $c$ at zero equal to zero, and $c^{(2r)}(0)=(-1)^rM_{2r}$, yielding
$$
|H(E)-M_0/E-M_2/E^3-M_4/E^5|\le C_6/E^6.
\tag{F.1d.V3}
$$

For arrays of derivative bounds use $(u*v)_r=\sum_{s=0}^r\binom rsu_sv_{r-s}$ and retain orders through five. In the high-momentum region $P=|p|\ge\max(4,2|q|)$, torus distance gives $\omega_a(p)\ge P/2$, $\omega_a(p-\lambda q)\ge P/4$ and $aP<6$, uniformly for $0\le\lambda\le1$, including wrapping faces. Define
$$
d_0=M+2,\quad g_1=3,\quad g_r=2\cdot6^{r-2}\ (r\ge2),\quad
d_r=2\left[g_r+\sum_{s=1}^{r-1}\binom rsd_sd_{r-s}\right],
$$
$$
w_0=v_0=4,\quad
w_r=4\sum_{s=1}^r\binom rsd_sw_{r-s},\quad
v_r=4\sum_{s=1}^r\binom rsd_sv_{r-s},
$$
$$
n_0=4+X,\quad n_1=2+X,\quad n_2=12+2X,\quad
n_r=2\cdot6^{r-1}\ (3\le r\le5),\quad
u=n*n,\quad D_{s,r}=(u*w*v^s)_r/8,\quad A_0=(4+X)^2/2.
$$
Differentiating $\omega_a^2$ bounds an order-$r$ spatial derivative of $\omega_a(p-\lambda q)$ by $d_rP^{1-r}$. Inverse differentiation gives $w_r,v_r$ after factoring $P^{-1-r}$. The vertex numerator derivatives are at most $n_rP^{2-r}$; therefore
$$
|\partial_q^\alpha(A_aE_a^{-s})|\le D_{s,r}P^{2-s-r},\quad
A_a\le A_0P^2,\quad r=|\alpha|.
$$
Taylor's integral remainder along $\lambda q$, $|q|_1\le2|q|$, and (F.1d.V3) give
$$
|\Psi_a(q;p)|\le H_0(1+|q|)^5P^{-4},\quad
H_0=4\left[A_0\,4^6C_6+
\sum_{j=0,2,4}\frac{\mu_j2^{5-j}D_{j+1,5-j}}{(5-j)!}\right].
\tag{F.1d.V4}
$$
This also holds at $a=0$. The spatial remainder orders are $5,3,1$; it is not an unbounded external-energy Taylor estimate. For $\delta\le1$ and $B\ge4$, centered-cell covering and a radial integral give both
$$
\frac{\delta^3}{(2\pi)^3}\sum_{|p|>B}|p|^{-4}\le16/B,\qquad
\int_{|p|>B}\frac{|p|^{-4}dp}{(2\pi)^3}\le16/B.
\tag{F.1d.V5}
$$
A cell radius is below one; $|p|^{-4}\le3|x|^{-4}$ and $|x|>B-1$ give the stated loose constant. Restricting the sum to the Brillouin grid only decreases it.

For global Taylor bounds, define $\eta_1=1$ and
$$
\eta_r=\frac{2+\sum_{s=1}^{r-1}\binom rs\eta_s\eta_{r-s}}{2m_0},\quad 2\le r\le4,
$$
$$
w'_0=m_0^{-1},\quad w'_r=m_0^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^r\binom rs\eta_sw'_{r-s},
\quad v'_0=(2m_0)^{-1},\quad v'_r=(2m_0)^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^r\binom rs\eta_sv'_{r-s},
$$
$$
\nu'_r=2^r(4+2X)^2,\quad G_{s,r}=(\nu'*w'*(v')^s)_r/(16m_0),
\quad S=\sum_{j=0,2,4}\mu_j\sum_{r=0}^{4-j}\frac{2^rG_{j+1,r}}{r!}.
$$
At arbitrary real momentum and $a\le1$, differentiation of $\omega^2$ gives $|\partial^\alpha\omega|\le\eta_r$ for $r\ge1$, using $|\partial_i\omega|\le1$. In particular at $q=0$, $|\partial_q^\alpha(A_aE_a^{-s})|\le G_{s,r}(1+|p|)^4$. Put
$$
L=625(2+X)^2/m_0^2+2500S,\qquad C_{\rm ext}=1000L+4H_0.
$$
Split internal momentum at $4(1+|q|)$. Its low-part volume is at most $1000(1+|q|)^3$, while $|H|\le4$ bounds its unsubtracted integrand by $625(2+X)^2m_0^{-2}(1+|q|)^4$ and its Taylor integrand by $2500S(1+|q|)^8$. Equations (F.1d.V4)–(F.1d.V5) control the high part. Both finite and continuum inner pairings in (F.1d.V2) are consequently bounded by $C_{\rm ext}(1+|q|)^{11}$, including thresholds.

Set
$$
D_{\rm tail}=3\cdot2^{22}\cdot16\cdot14!\,2^{28}/14.
$$
For every $K\ge4$ and $\delta\le1$, both the external integral and $\delta^3$-sum of $e^{-|q|^2}(1+|q|)^{11}$ on $|q|\ge K$ are at most $D_{\rm tail}K^{-14}$. For the sum use centered cells, $e^{-|q|^2}\le e\,e^{-|x|^2/2}$, $(1+|q|)^{11}\le2^{11}(1+|x|)^{11}$ and $|x|\ge K-1\ge K/2$. Then use $(1+|x|)^{11}\le2^{11}|x|^{11}$, $4\pi<16$, $e<3$ and $e^{-x^2/2}\le14!2^{14}x^{-28}$; the radial remainder is $(K-1)^{-14}/14$. These are decreasing explicit tails.

Choose $K\ge4$ and $B\ge\max(4,4K)$ and insert the tent cutoffs $\chi_J(x)=\min(1,\max(0,2-|x|/J))$ in external and internal momentum. They equal one on radius $J$, vanish beyond $2J$, and are $1/J$-Lipschitz. The omitted external part of the two pairings costs at most $2C_{\rm ext}D_{\rm tail}K^{-14}$, and the internal part at most $864H_0(1+2K)^5/B$. For the latter use (F.1d.V4)–(F.1d.V5) and $\delta^3\sum e^{-|q|^2}\le(\sqrt\pi+\delta)^3\le27$; $864=2\cdot27\cdot16$.

Here is the full rational finite compact-constant recipe. Truncate every dummy-variable series after degree six. Set $D=2B+2K+1$ and
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal E(t)&=(D+2t)\exp[(D+2)t+2t^2],\\
\Delta\mathcal G(t)&=3[\mathcal E(t)^2-\mathcal E(0)^2],\quad W_0=M+2D,\\
W_+(t)&=W_0\sum_{l=1}^6\left|\binom{1/2}{l}\right|[\Delta\mathcal G(t)/m_0^2]^l,\\
I_\omega(t)&=m_0^{-1}\sum_{l=0}^6[W_+(t)/m_0]^l,\quad
I_E(t)=(2m_0)^{-1}\sum_{l=0}^6[W_+(t)/m_0]^l,\\
\mathcal N(t)&=2\mathcal E(t)^2+2X(D+t)^2,\quad
\mathcal A(t)=\mathcal N(t)^2I_\omega(t)^2/16,\\
\mathcal H(t)&=\sum_{l=0}^6\frac{2^{l+2}[2W_+(t)]^l}{l!},\quad
\mathcal J(t)=\mathcal A(t)\mathcal H(t),\quad
\mathcal T_s(t)=\mathcal A(t)I_E(t)^s\quad(s=1,3,5).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1d.V6}
$$
All coefficients are nonnegative rationals; the exponential here means its finite jet. These majorize normalized real multiderivatives for $|p_i|\le2B$, $|q_i|\le2K$, $0\le a\le1$, under simultaneous size-$t$ perturbations in $a,p,q$. The removable symbol singularity is controlled by
$$
e_a(v)=-iv\int_0^1e^{-iav\theta}d\theta.
$$
The momentum perturbation is at most $2t$ and its phase increment at most $(D+2)t+2t^2$, giving $\mathcal E$. The finite binomial jet of the positive square root, with base at least $m_0^2$, gives $W_+$, and geometric inverse jets give $I_\omega,I_E$. Equation (F.1d.V1) gives $\mathcal H$. Ordinary multiplication supplies all remaining jets.

Write $J_r=[t^r]\mathcal J$, $T_{s,r}=[t^r]\mathcal T_s$, $c_r=\binom{r+2}{2}$ and define, with $j\in\{0,2,4\}$ in every sum,
$$
L_0=4\left[J_0+\sum_j\mu_j\sum_{r=0}^{4-j}c_r(2K)^rT_{j+1,r}\right],
$$
$$
L_a=L_p=4\left[J_1+\sum_j\mu_j\sum_{r=0}^{4-j}c_r(2K)^rT_{j+1,r+1}\right],
$$
$$
L_q=4\left[J_1+\sum_j\mu_j\sum_{r=1}^{4-j}c_rr(2K)^{r-1}T_{j+1,r}\right],
$$
$$
L_* =\max(L_p+L_0/B,\ L_q+L_0/K+4KL_0),\quad
V_c=(4B+2)^3(4K+2)^3,\quad C_{\rm compact}=V_c(L_a+48L_*).
\tag{F.1d.V7}
$$
The tent cutoffs are Lipschitz, so almost-everywhere derivative bounds suffice. Gaussian differentiation costs $4K$. A derivative in $a$ or $p$ differentiates a variable distinct from the external Taylor variable $q$: the normalized coefficient is $\partial_a\partial_q^\alpha/\alpha!$ or $\partial_{p_i}\partial_q^\alpha/\alpha!$, already majorized by degree $r+1$. There is no missing factor $r+1$. The external $q$ derivative of its Taylor monomial contributes the explicitly present factor $r$ in $L_q$.

If $n\ge2$ and $a_n(2B+2K+2)\le1$, every compact-support cell lies in the original Brillouin grids. Mean-value comparison in $a$ costs $V_ca_nL_a$. Six-coordinate centered-cell quadrature costs $6\delta_nV_cL_*\le48a_nV_cL_*$. This proves a compact error at most $C_{\rm compact}a_n$, directly for the actual periodic symbols, without tracking unpaired pole positions.

For the actual sampled shear put $Q=q+2\pi r/a$ and
$$
\beta_a(q,p)=\sum_{r\in\mathbb Z^3}g(Q)
\frac{e_1(p)e_2(q-p)+e_2(p)e_1(q-p)+2\xi Q_1Q_2}
{4\sqrt{\omega_a(p)\omega_a(q-p)}}.
$$
Its sampled bubble is exactly $4L_n^{-6}\sum_{p,q\in\mathcal P_n}|\beta_a(q,p)|^2H(E_a(q;p))$. The physical improvement polynomial uses $Q_1Q_2$ before sampling; reflection maps $r$ to $-r$. Define $C_{\rm alias}=2^{22}7!$ and $V_{\rm alias}=(2+X)/m_0$. Then
$$
e^{-x^2/2}(1+x)^2\le C_{\rm alias}(1+x)^{-12}.
$$
The alias shell $\|r\|_\infty=l$ has $24l^2+2$ elements, and $|Q|\ge\pi l/a$ for $r\ne0$ on the centered Brillouin cube. Nonprincipal weights sum to at most $52a^{12}$ and all weights to at most $53$. The full vertex is bounded by $V_{\rm alias}a^{-2}(1+|Q|)^2$. Use $||\beta|^2-|\beta_0|^2|\le|\beta-\beta_0|(|\beta|+|\beta_0|)$, $|H|\le4$, $L_n^{-3}|\mathcal P_n|=a^{-3}$ and $(2\pi)^3<512$. All derivative aliases, including both independently aliased vertices, cost at most
$$
45154304V_{\rm alias}^2C_{\rm alias}^2a_n^2.
\tag{F.1d.V8}
$$
The full paired Taylor polynomial is bounded by $4S(1+|p|)^4(1+|q|)^4$. Since $|p|<6/a$, its internal sum is bounded by $9604Sa^{-7}$. Every omitted full-torus external mode has $|q|\ge\pi/a$; the external tail above, with power four bounded by power eleven, therefore gives the additional counterterm-tail error $9604SD_{\rm tail}a_n^7$. No individual divergent coefficient is asserted to vanish.

Combining every part yields the explicit envelope
$$
\begin{aligned}
E_{\rm vac}(n;K,B)={}&2C_{\rm ext}D_{\rm tail}K^{-14}
+\frac{864H_0(1+2K)^5}{B}+C_{\rm compact}a_n\\
&+45154304V_{\rm alias}^2C_{\rm alias}^2a_n^2
+9604SD_{\rm tail}a_n^7,
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1d.V9}
$$
which bounds $|\Xi_n(h,h)-\Pi_R(h,h)|$ whenever the displayed size conditions hold. Given rational $\epsilon>0$, double $K\ge4$ until the first term is at most $\epsilon/5$, double $B\ge\max(4,4K)$ until the second is at most $\epsilon/5$, compute (F.1d.V6)–(F.1d.V7), and choose the least $n\ge2$ satisfying the Brillouin size condition and bounding each last term by $\epsilon/5$. These are monotone rational comparisons. Every search terminates, and every inequality persists at all later original indices. Call this selector $N_{\rm vac}(\epsilon)$.

If desired, for $n\ge3$ minimize (F.1d.V9) over the finite admissible pairs of power-of-two $K,B$, with $K\ge4$, $B\ge4K$ and $a_n(2B+2K+2)\le1$. The set is nonempty at $n=3$ and expands with $n$, while fixed-pair bounds decrease. The resulting rational error sequence decreases to zero. Neither construction searches for favorable loop values. Simultaneously translating $h$ to $k$ leaves $c$ and the scalar local pairing unchanged, giving the same diagonal scalar bound; no time-translation invariance of the coherent state is assumed.

All coefficient evaluation is effective. On $E\le E_{\max}$, $N_s$-cell midpoint quadrature in $s\in[-1,1]$ and $N_t$ cells in $t\in[0,2]$ gives an $H(E)$ error at most
$$
4\beta_1/N_s+(2\beta_1+2E_{\max})/N_t,
$$
plus separately allocated arithmetic error. The inner integrand has Lipschitz constant $2\beta_1$, the correlation derivative is bounded by $2\beta_1$, and $|c|\le2$. For $M_{2r}=\int|b^{(r)}|^2$, the midpoint error is at most $2\beta_r\beta_{r+1}/N_s$. These follow from $L\,\mathrm{length}^2/(4N)$ for a Lipschitz integrand. The finite alias/tori sums use their proved tails; mass/coupling evaluation uses their certified names with denominator lower bound $m_0$. Thus no Hilbert-transform or unspecified seminorm oracle is hidden in the selector.

The underlying threshold-pairing estimate also has the following general test form. For $F\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$ let $\mathsf H_E(F)=\langle(E-z-i0)^{-1},F(z)\rangle$, without the factor $(2\pi)^{-1}$, and put
$$
\mathsf M_r(F)=2\|F^{(r+1)}\|_\infty+\|F^{(r)}\|_1+\pi\|F^{(r)}\|_\infty.
$$
Then
$$
\partial_E^r\mathsf H_E(F)=\mathsf H_E(F^{(r)}),\quad
|\partial_E^r\mathsf H_E(F)|\le\mathsf M_r(F),\quad
|\mathsf H_E(F)-\mathsf H_{E'}(G)|
\le\mathsf M_0(F-G)+|E-E'|\mathsf M_1(G).
\tag{F.1d.V10}
$$
Indeed, writing $x=z-E$ gives $-\operatorname{PV}\int F(E+x)dx/x+i\pi F(E)$. For $|x|<1$ subtract $F(E)$, bounding the remainder by $2\|F'\|_\infty$; for $|x|\ge1$ use $\|F\|_1$. Translation is smooth in Schwartz space, which gives the derivative formula and then the difference estimate. Dividing by $2\pi$ gives the source-normalized version, uniformly through poles.

For the actual nonnegative bump, $\int_0^2c(t)dt=\|b\|_1^2/2\le2$ sharpens the earlier harmless bound to $|H^{(r)}(E)|\le2^{r-1}\|b\|_1^2\le2^{r+1}$. In particular $|H(E)-H(E')|\le4|E-E'|$ and, for an energy-independent scalar coefficient,
$$
|P_nH(E_n)-PH(E)|\le2|P_n-P|+4|P|\,|E_n-E|.
\tag{F.1d.V11}
$$
An alternate completely numerical midpoint certificate uses $|b'(t)|\le8e^{-2}<2$, including the smooth zero extension. Then $\|c\|_\infty\le2$, $\|c'\|_\infty\le4$, and inner/outer midpoint meshes with $M_s,M_t$ cells have total error at most $8/M_s+(2E_{\max}+4)/M_t$, plus certified arithmetic radii. This is the exact compact-time representation of the whole noncompact Fourier pairing, not a subthreshold truncation; it supplies no ultraviolet bound without the subtraction and tail estimates above.

#### Part IV. Complete coherent-state chronology, occupation and metric contacts

Constants in this part are distinct from the vacuum constants. Put $g=b(t)G(x)$ for the first diagonal pair. The complete tensor formulas in Part I give
$$
v_h=0,\quad v_{hh}=-g^2,\quad
(a_{hh}^{\mu\nu})=\operatorname{diag}(g^2,g^2,g^2,-g^2),
$$
$$
R_{hh}=-4gg_{tt}-3g_t^2+4gg_{33}+3g_3^2,\quad
M_{hh}=-m^2g^2+\xi R_{hh},
$$
$$
S_{hh}=-\tfrac12\int\left[g^2(:\phi_t^2:+:\phi_1^2:+:\phi_2^2:-:\phi_3^2:)
+(-m^2g^2+\xi R_{hh}):\phi^2:\right].
\tag{F.1d.C1}
$$
For $G=e^{-|x|^2/2}$ the curvature coefficient is $[-4bb''-3(b')^2+b^2(7x_3^2-4)]G^2$. At finite $n$, use $g=bG_{L_n}$ before taking products: $G_{L_n}G_{L_n,33}$ and $G_{L_n,3}^2$ must be compared separately to their continuum-product periodizations. Moreover $\mathsf A_h=\mathsf B_h^i=0$, hence $F_{n,h}=0$ and $B_n(h,h)=0$ exactly. This does not remove the displayed seagull, scalar phase or stress-index contacts. The first shear vertex is $q_h=g:\operatorname{sym}\phi_1\phi_2:-\xi g_{12}:\phi^2:$; its single contracted propagator has only spatial derivatives and no differentiated-time $\delta$ in this specialization.

Let $g_n=J_n^*f$, $\eta_n=\exp(\|g_n\|^2-1)$, and use the auxiliary untruncated finite-mode vector $u_n=e^{-1/2}\exp(\alpha a^\dagger(g_n))\Omega_n$, of norm squared $\eta_n$, not one. The actual state is exactly
$$
|u_{R,n}\rangle\langle u_{R,n}|+(1-\|u_{R,n}\|^2)|\Omega_n\rangle\langle\Omega_n|,
\qquad u_{R,n}=P_{N\le R_n}u_n.
\tag{F.1d.C2}
$$
If $\chi_n$ is the real classical field obtained from $\Phi_n$ by replacing $a_p$ with $\alpha g_n(p)$ and $a_p^\dagger$ with its conjugate, normal-ordered degree-$d$ expectations in the auxiliary vacuum-filled density are $\eta_n$ times the corresponding classical polynomial. Thus the normal quartic, seagull and single line are respectively $\eta_ns_n^2$, $\eta_nd_n^{\rm cl}$ and $\eta_nL_{F,n}[\chi_n,\chi_n]$. The scalar, after vacuum fill, instead has coefficient exactly one. Wick ordering of the actual compressed chronology gives these normal terms minus the occupation excursion and minus $i\Xi_n$; scalar pairing precedes every state-loss estimate.

Define the following rational arithmetic constants:
$$
H=1+\overline m+X+m_0^{-1}.
$$
For two-variable polynomials set $P_0(t,u)=1$ and $P_{j+1}=\partial_tP_j+2tu^2\partial_uP_j-2tu^2P_j$. Put $D_j=\sum_{a,r}|[t^au^r]P_j|r!$ and $D=\max(D_0,D_1,D_2)=148$. These bound $|b^{(j)}|$ for $j\le2$. Now set
$$
\begin{aligned}
D_G&=64\cdot2^{32}(1+2^{33}33!)(1+X),\\
C_J&=2^{16}3^{32}D_GH^2,\quad B_{\rm st}=2^{60}H^{12}(1+D)^2,\\
Q_*&=2^{24}H^8(1+D)^2,\quad C_{\rm tail}=2^{20}HC_J^2.
\end{aligned}
$$
For $M\ge4$ put $P=M+4$ and
$$
C_{{\rm st},\rm compact}(M)=2^{150}H^{40}P^{40}(1+D)^4(1+C_J)^2,
$$
$$
C_{\rm period}=2^{80}H^{20}(1+D)^4\cdot8!16^8,\quad
A(M)=6C_{{\rm st},\rm compact}(M)+C_{\rm period}.
\tag{F.1d.C3}
$$
For $R=4^n$, $n\ge3$, the error envelope is
$$
\begin{aligned}
E_{\rm occ}(R)&=61440Q_*^2R^{10}(R/2+5)^2\cdot2^{-R/4},\\
E_{\rm st}(R,M)&=E_{\rm occ}(R)+A(M)/R+2C_{\rm tail}/(1+M)^{20},
\quad R\ge\max(64,4P).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1d.C4}
$$
The same constants cover $k$: all time arguments have $|t|\le5$, each support length is two, and the generous difference bound is $|t-s|\le6$. The coherent state is not translated or presumed stationary.

**Occupation and coherence estimate.** The one-particle field vector at a site has squared norm at most $R^3/(2m_0)$; a spatial difference multiplies its norm by at most $2R$. Gaussian sums give $a^3\sum_xG_{L_n}(x)\le64$ and $a^3\sum_x|\partial_{12}G_{L_n}(x)|\le512$. Therefore
$$
\|q_h(t)\psi_s\|\le Q R^5(s+2)|b(t)|\|\psi_s\|,\qquad Q=2048(1+X)/m_0.
$$
A quadratic vertex has three occupation shifts and two vertices at most five. Two time integrations have absolute measure at most four. For the scalar-normal chronological matrix $\mathsf A_n=\mathcal Q_{4,n}+\mathcal Q_{2,F,n}$, these finite counts give
$$
\|\mathsf A_n\psi\|\le256Q_*^2R^{10}\|(N+4)^2\psi\|.
\tag{F.1d.C5}
$$
Subtracting its scalar vacuum coefficient costs at most the same untruncated chronological norm. Whole-quadratic projections are contractions; reversing the orders gives the adjoint bound. The seagull has a smaller bound of this form using its four kinetic entries, derivative coefficients through order two, $\overline m^2$, $X$, and $\omega_n\le\overline m+4R$; the stated $Q_*$ dominates them. Means and ordinary products satisfy this common overestimate.

For $K\ge32$ and $\|g_n\|\le1$,
$$
T_4(K)=\sum_{s>K}(s+4)^4/s!\le
\frac{(K+5)^4}{(K+1)!(1-q_K)},\quad
q_K=\frac{[(K+6)/(K+5)]^4}{K+2}<\tfrac12,
$$
so $\sqrt{T_4(K)}\le2(K+5)^2 2^{-K/2}$. Also $e^{-1}\sum_s(s+4)^4/s!=799<29^2$. Apply (F.1d.C5) to both coherent tails and Cauchy–Schwarz to each head–tail cross term. The resulting expectation error is at most $30720Q_*^2R^{10}\sqrt{T_4(K)}$, hence at most $E_{\rm occ}(R)$ for $K=R/2$. This retains the square-root coherence term, rather than dephasing sectors or replacing it with a linear tail. The safe low-head identity is $R\ge K+4$.

The actual missing excursion before scalar subtraction is
$$
P\int[\theta(t-s)q(t)(1-P)q(s)+\theta(s-t)q(s)(1-P)q(t)]dt\,ds\,P.
$$
It must create two particles then annihilate two; it is number-diagonal and supported on $s=R-1,R$. Its expectation is at most $4Q^2R^{10}\sum_{s=R-1}^R(s+2)^2/s!$. The head–tail estimate already includes it, so it is not charged twice. The occupation bound persists at all later original indices because $E_{\rm occ}(4R)/E_{\rm occ}(R)\le4^{12}2^{-3R/4}<1$ for $R\ge64$.

**Quartic and chronological single line.** Centered-cell projection gives $\|f-J_nJ_n^*f\|_2\le24\delta_n$, support in $[-2,2]^3$ for $n\ge2$, $L^1$ norm at most eight and $L^1$ error at most $192\delta_n$. Also $|\eta_n-1|\le1-\|g_n\|^2\le\|f-J_nJ_n^*f\|_2^2$; the weaker $384\delta_n$ bound suffices below.

For the shear use $b^{12}=b^{21}=g$, $b^{\varnothing\varnothing}=-2\xi g_{12}$ in $q_h=\tfrac12b^{ab}:X_aX_b:$. Insert each external classical sign $\sigma=\pm1$, its compact momentum $p$, and an internal contracted momentum $r$. The spatial vertex is the finite sum
$$
\sum_{a,b}d_a(r)d_b(\sigma p)\widehat G_{ab}(r+\sigma p)
\frac{e^{-i\sigma\omega(p)t}}{\sqrt{2\omega(p)}},
$$
where $d_\varnothing=1$, $d_j(p)=ip_j$ for a spatial derivative on $e^{ipx}$, $\widehat G_{12}=\widehat G_{21}=\widehat G$ and $\widehat G_{\varnothing\varnothing}=-2\xi\widehat{\partial_{12}G}$. Reversed plane-wave signs use their actual derivatives. At finite $n$ use the original $e_i^\pm$, cell-averaged external leg and all aliases $r+\sigma p+2\pi Rz$, with improvement polynomial evaluated at that physical alias. The second vertex has its corresponding reversed internal momentum and its own external sign. The contracted factor is exactly $e^{-i\omega(r)|t-s|}/[2\omega(r)]$. This is the real-time Feynman single contraction, not a Euclidean replacement.

The Gaussian bounds and shell counts give
$$
(1+|q|_\infty)^{32}|\widehat G(q)|,
\ (1+|q|_\infty)^{32}|\widehat{\partial_{12}G}(q)|\le D_G/(1+X),
$$
$$
\sum_z(1+|r+\sigma p+2\pi Rz|_\infty)^{-32}
\le100\,3^{16}(1+|r|_\infty)^{-16},\qquad |p|_\infty\le2,\ R\ge16.
$$
There are $27$ near alias indices; the rest use shell count $24j^2+2$ and the two lower distances from the compact external support and from the alias index. Include the two external signs, $L^1$ norm eight, at most three vertex entries, internal spatial factors at most $|r|$, external factors at most two, and cell comparison $3^{32}$. Each resulting current is bounded by $|b(t-t_0)|C_J(1+|r|_\infty)^{-14}$. With $\omega\ge m_0$, both finite and continuum chronological contraction tails are absolutely integrable. The cube-shell integral $24\int_M^\infty r^2(1+r)^{-28}dr$, with time and cell factors, is at most $C_{\rm tail}/(1+M)^{20}$ on each side. This justifies the contraction interchange and the two-tail term in (F.1d.C4). The quartic expectation is separately the exact $\eta_ns_n^2$ with compact external momenta.

**Compact arithmetic, derivative aliases and the true product-periodization seagull.** On $|p|_\infty\le P$, $0\le a\le R^{-1}$ and the stated time supports, the following elementary bounds suffice:
$$
|d_a(p)|\le P,\quad |\partial_pd_a(p)|\le1,\quad |\partial_ad_a(p)|\le P^2/2,
$$
$$
\omega\ge m_0,\quad\omega\le\overline m+3P,\quad
|\partial_p\omega|\le3HP,\quad |\partial_a\omega|\le3HP^3,
$$
$$
|\partial_x\omega^{-1}|\le H^2|\partial_x\omega|,\quad
|\partial_x\omega^{-1/2}|\le(H+H^2)|\partial_x\omega|,\quad
|\partial_xe^{it\omega}|\le5|\partial_x\omega|.
$$
The symbol integral in Part III includes $a=0$. Differentiating its squared dispersion proves the energy bounds. Gaussian derivatives through order three have Fourier norm at most $2^{12}$ by the degree-three Hermite expansion and $u^je^{-u^2/2}\le2^jj!$. Fourier transforms of $G^2,GG_{33},G_3^2$ and their first derivatives are bounded by $2^{16}(1+P)^4$. Positive normalization factors involving $\pi$ are bounded by powers of eight above and by one when inverted.

For the degree-one jet norm $\mathfrak J(F)=|F|+\sum_j|\partial_jF|$, at most thirteen active variables occur, so sixteen times a value/partial bound bounds the jet. This norm is submultiplicative. An external spatially differentiated field leg has jet at most $2^{12}H^4P^4$. A contracted time factor including both possible internal spatial multipliers has jet at most $2^{14}H^4P^6$, paying also its $a$-phase derivative. A spatial first-vertex coefficient has jet at most $2^{16}HP^3$. A seagull coefficient with its two legs has jet at most $2^{24}H^8P^8(1+D)^2$.

The single-line product uses two vertices, two legs and one contracted factor, with jet at most $2^{70}H^{14}P^{20}$. Its $36$ current-pair summands, two $L^1$ factors eight, time area four and internal volume $8P^3$ cost less than $2^{17}P^3$, yielding $2^{87}H^{14}P^{23}$. A first mean uses twelve entry/sign summands, external $L^1$ factor $64$ and time length two, yielding $2^{51}H^9P^{11}$; its quartic square has jet at most $2^{102}H^{18}P^{22}$. The seagull uses at most sixteen coefficients, four sign choices, external $L^1$ factor $64$ and time length two, yielding $2^{37}H^8P^8(1+D)^2$.

The coefficient comparison displaces $a$ by at most $R^{-1}$ and every momentum coordinate by at most $4R^{-1}$; the jet bounds their total effect by $5/R$. Replacing each external $f$ by its cell projection costs $192\delta_n\le1536/R$ in $L^1$, at most $192/R$ relative to its budgeted factor eight, with at most four legs. The weaker $|\eta_n-1|\le384\delta_n\le3072/R$ is also retained. The sum of these error factors is below $2^{16}/R$. Thus the single-line, quartic, first-mean and continuum-product seagull errors are bounded respectively by
$$
\frac{2^{103}H^{14}P^{23}}R,\quad
\frac{2^{118}H^{18}P^{22}}R,\quad
\frac{2^{67}H^9P^{11}}R,\quad
\frac{2^{53}H^8P^8(1+D)^2}R.
$$
Each is bounded term by term by $C_{{\rm st},\rm compact}(M)/R$ in (F.1d.C3). Times are integrated; no time quadrature or derivative of the chronological step function enters. For the phase use $|e^{-i\omega_n|t-s|}-e^{-i\omega|t-s|}|\le6|\omega_n-\omega|$. Intersected centered cells, not rounded boxes, supply the compact comparison.

All nonprincipal compact aliases, including the Gaussian-square seagull coefficients, obey
$$
\overline q=16![16/(9R^2)]^{16},\qquad
A_{\rm alias}=\frac{24\overline q(1+\overline q)}{(1-\overline q)^3}
+\frac{2\overline q}{1-\overline q}\le R^{-1},\quad R\ge16.
\tag{F.1d.C6}
$$
Here $\overline q<1/2$; use shell counts, physical alias distance at least $\pi R\|z\|_\infty$, and $e^x\ge x^{16}/16!$, after including improvement polynomials. This doubles each compact budget at most.

For derivatives of total order at most two, completing the square gives
$$
\int|(\partial^uG)(x)(\partial^vG)(x+L_nj)|dx
\le2^{16}(1+L_n^2|j|^2)e^{-L_n^2|j|^2/4}.
$$
For the $a_n^3$-weighted sampled sum use $2^{20}$, by the shifted one-dimensional Gaussian bound $\sqrt\pi+a_n\le3$. Summing $j\ne0$ and absorbing the polynomial costs at most $2^{40}e^{-R^2/16}$. Time/curvature/mass/leg factors are covered by $2^{80}H^{20}(1+D)^4$, and $e^{-R^2/16}\le8!16^8/R^{16}$. Hence product periodization contributes at most $C_{\rm period}/R^{16}\le C_{\rm period}/R$. This retains the true finite $G_{L_n}G_{L_n,33}$ and $G_{L_n,3}^2$, rather than replacing them without a bound. Summing the three doubled compact comparisons, periodization, two internal tails and occupation error proves (F.1d.C4) for every relevant scalar-normal expectation and first mean; $|\mu|\le B_{\rm st}$ follows from the same first-vertex budget.

Given rational $\gamma>0$, double $M\ge4$ until $2C_{\rm tail}/(1+M)^{20}\le\gamma/4$, then choose an original $n\ge3$ with $R_n\ge\max(64,4(M+4),4A(M)/\gamma)$ and increase it until $E_{\rm occ}(R_n)\le\gamma/2$. Comparisons with the dyadic occupation factor use integer base-two exponents, without materializing an exponentially long denominator. This terminates, and $E_{\rm st}\le\gamma$ holds for every later original index.

The nonconnected sum of seagull and scalar-normal chronology costs at most $2E_{\rm st}$. The connected subtraction adds at most $2B_{\rm st}E_{\rm st}+E_{\rm st}^2$. Thus, for either phase and either diagonal basis direction,
$$
|W_{n,++}-W_{++}|,\ |W_{n,--}-W_{--}|
\le(2+2B_{\rm st})E_{\rm st}+E_{\rm st}^2+E_{\rm vac}.
\tag{F.1d.C7}
$$
The backward adjoint is taken on real tests before complexification. Opposite branches retain reversed ordinary-product order and receive the separate complete bounds in Part V.

#### Part V. Complete ordinary-product and separated-pair selector

The local names in this part are independent of Parts III–IV. For $t_0=0,4$ put $\beta(E)=\int b(t-t_0)e^{\mathrm{iEt}}dt$, $\widehat G(k)=(2\pi)^{3/2}e^{-|k|^2/2}$, $\widehat G_{12}(k)=-k_1k_2\widehat G(k)$ and $c_0=(2\pi)^{-3}$. Write $e_j^-(p)=\overline{e_j^+(p)}$. The finite pair kernel, divided by its $\delta_n^3$ quadrature factor, is
$$
\begin{aligned}
B_n(p,q)={}&\frac{c_0\beta(\omega_p+\omega_q)}{2\sqrt{\omega_p\omega_q}}
\left[\frac{e_1^+(p)e_2^+(q)+e_2^+(p)e_1^+(q)}2
\sum_z\widehat G(p+q+2\pi z/a)\right.\\
&\left.\hspace{35mm}-\xi\sum_z\widehat G_{12}(p+q+2\pi z/a)\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1d.O1}
$$
The number kernel has factor $c_0/\sqrt{\omega_p\omega_q}$, frequency $\omega_p-\omega_q$, momentum $p-q$, and the second spatial multiplier $e^-$ instead of $e^+$. Its multiplicity is twice the normal pair coefficient. Continuum kernels put $e^+=-ip$, $e^-=ip$ and retain only $z=0$. Improvement derivatives precede sampling, so their polynomial is evaluated at each physical alias, not the principal momentum.

Use $D_0=2$, $D_1=10$, $H_0=512$, $H_2=2048$ and $\gamma_o=\min(1,2m_0)/4$. These bound $|\beta|$, $|\beta'|$, Gaussian aliases and their two-derivative versions. For the latter, reduce coordinates to a fundamental interval and sum distances at least $\pi R(2j-1)$: each one-dimensional Gaussian sum is at most two; use $|x_1x_2|e^{-|x|^2/2}\le4e^{-|x|^2/4}$, $(2\pi)^{3/2}<64$ and $2\pi>6$.

In the two-variable bump recurrence of Part IV set
$$
D_{16}=2\sum_{a,j}|[t^au^j]P_{16}|j!\ge\|b^{(16)}\|_1,\quad
C_B=\frac{5^{14}D_{16}(H_0+XH_2)}{2m_0\gamma_o^{16}}.
$$
The recurrence gives $b^{(r)}=e^{-u}P_r(t,u)$, $u=(1-t^2)^{-1}$, and $u^je^{-u}\le j!$. The positive-frequency chord bound $\omega_n(p)+\omega_n(q)\ge\gamma_o(1+|p|+|q|)$, followed by sixteen integrations by parts, gives for the cell-embedded kernels
$$
|B(p,q)|,\ |\widetilde B_n(p,q)|\le C_B(1+|p|+|q|)^{-14}.
\tag{F.1d.O2}
$$
Two numerator powers and the lower denominator $m_0$ are included; $5^{14}$ pays the passage from centers to cells. Thus a high opposite-momentum pair is controlled by positive time frequency even when its spatial sum is small.

Set
$$
D_G=64\cdot2^{32}(1+2^{33}33!)(1+X),\quad
C_A=(128/m_0)D_G\,100\,3^{30}.
$$
For $g=f$ or the embedded cell average, $\|g\|\le1$, support is in $[-2,2]^3$ and $\|g\|_1\le8$. The number output satisfies
$$
|Af(p)|,\ |\widetilde A_ng_n(p)|\le C_A(1+|p|_\infty)^{-14}.
\tag{F.1d.O3}
$$
To verify the constant, expand $(1+r)^{32}\le2^{32}(1+r^{32})$ and use Gaussian moment bounds. For compact input momentum $|q|_\infty\le2$, put $u=(|p|_\infty-2)_+$. The $27$ near alias indices and the remaining $24j^2+2$ shells give $\sum_z(1+|p-q+2\pi Rz|_\infty)^{-32}\le100(1+u)^{-16}$, since far aliases also have distance at least their index. Now $1+u\ge(1+|p|_\infty)/3$. The numerator costs $8(1+|p|_\infty)^2/m_0$; $D_0$, the input $L^1$ bound eight and a conservative cell factor $3^{14}$ give (F.1d.O3).

Put $a_0=8C_A$, $b_0=20C_B$, $C=a_0+2b_0$ and $D_{\rm tail}=C_A+10C_B$. Then $\|Af\|,\|\widetilde A_ng_n\|\le a_0$ and $\|B\|_{\rm HS},\|\widetilde B_n\|_{\rm HS}\le b_0$. Outside the momentum cube of radius $M\ge4$,
$$
a_{\rm tail}\le C_A(1+M)^{-12},\quad
b_{\rm tail}\le5C_B(1+M)^{-11},\quad
C_{\rm tail}:=a_{\rm tail}+2b_{\rm tail}\le D_{\rm tail}(1+M)^{-11}.
\tag{F.1d.O4}
$$
These follow from the cube-shell integrals in dimensions three and six: $24\int_M^\infty r^2(1+r)^{-28}dr$ and $384\int_M^\infty r^5(1+r)^{-28}dr$, bounded by $(24/25)(1+M)^{-25}$ and $(384/22)(1+M)^{-22}$ before square roots.

Let $u_K=e^{-1/2}\sum_{s\le K}\alpha^sf^{\otimes s}/\sqrt{s!}$ and $\rho^K=|u_K\rangle\langle u_K|+(1-\|u_K\|^2)|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|$, and use the same $g_n$ for the finite state. The coherent head retains all relative phases. For
$$
q_K=\frac{[(K+3)/(K+2)]^{152}}{K+2}<1,\quad
T_K=\frac{3^{128}(K+2)^{152}}{(K+1)!(1-q_K)},
$$
$$
d_V(\rho,\rho^K):=\|V(\rho-\rho^K)V\|_1
\le2\sqrt{E_0T_K}+2T_K.
\tag{F.1d.O5}
$$
On sector $s$ compact support gives $V^2\le3^{128}(s+1)^{152}$, so the first omitted term and decreasing ratio bound give $T_K$; weighted rank-one Cauchy–Schwarz gives the displayed head–tail estimate and the vacuum-fill allowance. Its square root cannot be replaced by a linear tail.

Sharper observable-specific tails are
$$
\tau_K\le\frac1{(K+1)![1-1/(K+2)]},\quad
d_K\le\frac{(K+3)^2}{(K+1)!(1-q_{2,K})},\quad
q_{2,K}=\frac{[(K+4)/(K+3)]^2}{K+2}.
$$
A number vertex on an $s$-particle product has norm at most $sa_0$, its creation part at most $\sqrt{(s+1)(s+2)}b_0$ and annihilation at most $\sqrt{s(s-1)}b_0$. The three-shift overlap estimate gives
$$
\|Su\|\le\sqrt{30}C,\quad
\|S(u-u_K)\|\le\sqrt{3d_K}C,\quad\|u-u_K\|\le\sqrt{\tau_K}.
$$
Here the exact Poisson moment $\mathbb E(N+2)^2=10$ explains the first constant. Orthogonal whole-quadratic compression preserves these bounds. Mean error is at most $12C\sqrt{\tau_K}$ and either ordered connected covariance error is at most
$$
L_K=C^2[20\sqrt{d_K}+2\tau_K+144\sqrt{\tau_K}].
\tag{F.1d.O6}
$$
Indeed the raw-product difference is at most $6\sqrt{10}C^2\sqrt{d_K}+2b_0^2\tau_K$, including changed vacuum fill, and the two first-mean differences, each paired with $|\mu|\le6C$, add at most $144C^2\sqrt{\tau_K}$. The actual uncompressed/compressed excursion $PS_k(1-P)S_hP$ is number-diagonal at $R-1,R$ and bounded by
$$
b_0^2\left[\frac{R(R+1)}{(R-1)!}+\frac{(R+1)(R+2)}{R!}\right].
$$
It vanishes on a head with $R\ge K+4$ and its full-state effect is already included in (F.1d.O6).

For the comparison only, project each stress output onto momenta in $[-M,M]^3$ on the embedded continuum Fock space, retaining intersected boundary cells. This is not a physical operation. Input spectator momenta lie in $[-2,2]^3$, so the mean is unchanged. Orthogonality and the same three-band estimate give raw/connected momentum error at most $32C_{\rm tail}^2$ on each side: $30C_{\rm tail}^2$ for the head plus $2b_{\rm tail}^2$ for vacuum fill.

Set $P=M+1$ and require $R\ge\max(16,K+4,4P)$. With $\overline\delta=8/R$,
$$
|\omega_n(p)-\omega(p)|\le d_\omega:=P^4/(8m_0R^2),\quad
|e_j^+(p)+ip_j|\le p_j^2/(2R).
$$
Use $0\le x^2-\sin^2x\le x^4/3$, divide by $\omega_n+\omega\ge2m_0$, and use the exponential remainder. Define
$$
\overline q=16![4/(9R^2)]^{16},\quad
A_{\rm alias}=\frac{24\overline q(1+\overline q)}{(1-\overline q)^3}
+\frac{2\overline q}{1-\overline q},
$$
$$
L_B=32\left[\frac{2(2P+6P^2+16X)}{m_0}
+(P^2+X)(6/m_0^2+60/m_0)\right],
$$
$$
\eta_B=32\left[\frac{2P^3}{m_0R}+(P^2+X)d_\omega(2/m_0^2+20/m_0)\right]
+\frac{4L_B}{R}+\frac{64(P^2+4X)}{m_0}A_{\rm alias},\qquad\eta_A\le2\eta_B.
\tag{F.1d.O7}
$$
The alias spacing is $2\pi R\ge4P$, so its distance is at least half the spacing times $\|z\|_\infty$. The Gaussian inequality $e^x\ge x^{16}/16!$ and shell sum give $A_{\rm alias}$, with $\overline q<1/2$. Improvement derivatives cost a further factor four. The first bracket in (F.1d.O7) pays multiplier and dispersion change, including $|\beta'|\le10$. The six momentum derivatives have sum at most $L_B$: numerator differentiation costs $2P+6P^2+16X$, inverse-energy differentiation $3/m_0^2$ and time-frequency differentiation $6D_1/m_0$. Coordinate displacement at most $4/R$ gives the cell term. Complex lattice symbols are compared by their actual absolute differences.

Let $\mathrm{Vol}=(2M)^3$, $M_B=64(P^2+X)/m_0$ and
$$
U=4(K+2)\mathrm{Vol}M_B,\quad J=4(K+2)\mathrm{Vol}\eta_B,\quad e_u=36\overline\delta,
$$
$$
x=J+4Ue_u,\quad y=2UJ+J^2+4U^2e_u,\quad z=y+2Ux+x^2.
\tag{F.1d.O8}
$$
These respectively control compact first means, raw products and connected products. $U$ bounds the continuum stress on the head and vacuum, and $J$ bounds its finite difference. The two-momentum pointwise kernel error gives Hilbert–Schmidt factor $\mathrm{Vol}$. Cube averaging gives $\|f-g_n\|\le\sqrt3\delta_n\|\nabla f\|$; tensor telescoping and $\mathbb EN^2=2$ give state-vector error $e_u$, and the vacuum-filled heads differ by trace norm at most $4e_u$. Expanding operator products and connected subtraction proves (F.1d.O8), with both orders retained.

Given rational $\epsilon>0$, use upper square root $\mathsf Q(0)=0$, $\mathsf Q(x)=2^{\lceil\lceil\log_2x\rceil/2\rceil}$ for positive rational $x$, computed by integer bit lengths and exact dyadic comparisons. Then $\sqrt x\le\mathsf Q(x)<2\sqrt x$. Increase $K$ until $q_K<1$, $\max(12C\sqrt{\tau_K},L_K)\le\epsilon/10$ and (F.1d.O5) is at most $\epsilon/10$. Double $M\ge4$ until $32[D_{\rm tail}/(1+M)^{11}]^2\le\epsilon/10$. Increase original $n\ge2$ until its size conditions hold and $\max(x,z)\le\epsilon/5$. Factorial tails, the power-$22$ momentum tail and vanishing $\eta_B,e_u$ prove termination; every bound decreases at all later original indices. The two state tails, two momentum tails and compact comparison cost at most $3\epsilon/5$. Call the selector $N_{\rm ord}(\epsilon)$.

These ordinary-product bounds do not use temporal separation. They therefore control both mixed branches also on $(h,h)$ and $(k,k)$. Separation is used only when equating a chronological cross word to an ordinary ordered word. The overlapping chronology in Part IV was proved separately.

#### Part VI. One original-index modulus for the whole compact Hessian family

For a diagonal branch tolerance $\delta>0$, put $\gamma=\min(1,\delta/[4(3+2B_{\rm st})])$. Run the state selector of Part IV at $\gamma$, the vacuum selector at $\delta/2$ and $N_{\rm ord}(\delta)$; take the maximum of their original indices. For every later index,
$$
(2+2B_{\rm st})E_{\rm st}+E_{\rm st}^2
\le(3+2B_{\rm st})\gamma\le\delta/4.
$$
Thus each diagonal same branch has error at most $3\delta/4$ and each mixed branch at most $3\delta/5$. Both phases and time translates share the constants. For $u=xh+yk$, $v=x'h+y'k$, each branch is bilinear and $|xx'|+|xy'|+|yx'|+|yy'|\le4$. Use $\delta=\varepsilon/4$ for both diagonal pairs and the separated ordinary-product selector at $\varepsilon/4$ for both cross orders, and take the maximum. This is $N_{\rm Hess}(\varepsilon)$ and proves (F.1d.1), with every inequality valid at all larger original indices. A diagonal result has not been relabeled as a general joint-test modulus.

#### Part VII. Action-density response and both metric-index conversions

The exact response of the actual finite source is
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal R_{\rho_n,n}(u,v)={}&\operatorname{Tr}\rho_n[S_{n,uv}-B_n(u,v)]+C_n(u,v)\\
&+i\int dt\,ds\,\theta(t-s)\operatorname{Tr}\rho_n[q_{n,u}(t),q_{n,v}(s)]\\
={}&W_{n,++}(u,v)+W_{n,+-}(u,v).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1d.R1}
$$
This follows from (F.1d.S16) without changing the order of the mixed product. The continuum response is the corresponding expression from the same action/stress vertices. Hence $N_{\rm Hess}(\varepsilon/2)$ gives response error at most $\varepsilon$. It retains the metric seagull, the exact zero canonical contact for this shear, and the scalar phase; it is a flat tested two-jet, not convergence of a fixed nonzero curved-metric amplitude.

Write $u_{12}=u_{21}=g_u=(xb(t)+yb(t-4))G$ and similarly $g_v=(x'b(t)+y'b(t-4))G$. Define the upper and lower tested stress responses by
$$
U(u,v)=\tfrac12\int u_{\mu\nu}\,\delta_v\tau^{\mu\nu},\qquad
L(u,v)=\tfrac12\int u^{\mu\nu}\,\delta_v\tau_{\mu\nu},
$$
with test indices raised by the flat metric. The finite counterparts differentiate the same finite action-density mean, then apply its algebraic density/index conversion with periodize-before-product coefficients. The density conversion is
$$
U=\mathcal R-\tfrac12\int u_{\mu\nu}v_v\tau^{\mu\nu}=\mathcal R,
\qquad v_v=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}_\eta v=0.
$$
Both lowering-index terms survive:
$$
\delta_v\tau_{12}=\delta_v\tau^{12}+g_v(\tau^{11}+\tau^{22}),\quad
L=\mathcal R+J,\quad J=\int g_ug_v(\tau^{11}+\tau^{22}).
\tag{F.1d.R2}
$$
The same identities hold for the actual finite sampled products; no finite-lattice diffeomorphism identity is assumed. Since $b(t)b(t-4)=0$, put
$$
(\ell_h)_{11}=(\ell_h)_{22}=2b(t)^2G^2,\quad
(\ell_k)_{11}=(\ell_k)_{22}=2b(t-4)^2G^2,
$$
with all other components zero. The factor $1/2$ in $S_\ell=\tfrac12\int\ell_{\mu\nu}T^{\mu\nu}$ gives exactly $J=xx'\mu(\ell_h)+yy'\mu(\ell_k)$; the factor two in these directions is compulsory.

For $w=b(t-t_0)^2G^2$, $v_\ell=2w$, $a_\ell=\operatorname{diag}(-2w,0,0,2w)$ and $R_\ell=4w_{tt}-2w_{11}-2w_{22}-4w_{33}$. Thus the complete first quadratic is
$$
S_\ell=\int\left\{w(:\phi_t^2:-:\phi_3^2:-m^2:\phi^2:)
+\xi[-2w_{tt}+w_{11}+w_{22}+2w_{33}]:\phi^2:\right\}.
\tag{F.1d.R3}
$$
The last coefficient is $\{-4[(b')^2+bb'']+b^2(4x_1^2+4x_2^2+8x_3^2-8)\}G^2$, with all time functions shifted by $t_0=0,4$. At finite $n$, use $w_n=b(t-t_0)^2G_{L_n}^2$ and its actual derivatives.

The same $E_{\rm st}(R,M)$ bounds each contact mean error. Its auxiliary normal mean is $\eta_nS_\ell[\chi_n]$, with zero vacuum fill. Its two kinetic, mass, two temporal-curvature and four spatial-curvature entries give at most nine coefficients, below the sixteen-term seagull budget. The largest numerical coefficient is eight. A time leg $\omega/\sqrt{2\omega}$ and its first $p,a$ derivatives obey the same $2^8H^4P^4$ value/partial budget. Thus its whole first quadratic has the same $Q_*$ sector bound and square-root head–tail error. Its compact jet error is at most $2^{53}H^8P^8(1+D)^2/R$, aliases cost at most $C_{{\rm st},\rm compact}/R$, and the order-two product-periodization estimate costs $C_{\rm period}/R$. There is no internal contraction tail, so its inclusion in $E_{\rm st}$ is conservative. Therefore
$$
|\mu_n^{\rm conversion}(\ell_{t_0})-\mu(\ell_{t_0})|\le E_{\rm st}(R,M),
\qquad t_0=0,4.
\tag{F.1d.R4}
$$
The superscript indicates products of the separately periodized original directions; their difference from periodizing the continuum product is included, rather than dropped.

With each branch error at most $\delta$, (F.1d.R1) bounds the upper response error by $2\delta$ and the lower response error by $2\delta+2E_{\rm st}$. For requested $\varepsilon$, use $N_{\rm Hess}(\varepsilon/4)$ and the state selector at $E_{\rm st}\le\varepsilon/4$, and take their maximum. This proves an explicit all-larger-index modulus for both indexed responses.

#### Part VIII. Coefficient computation and conditional implementation tolerances

There is no coefficient-integration oracle in the result. A normally ordered term with $a$ creations and $b$ annihilations, evaluated in a coherent head, has its exact active-mode factor
$$
e^{-1}\overline{\alpha}^{\,a}\alpha^b
\sum_{r=0}^{K-\max(a,b)}\frac{z^r}{r!},\qquad
z=\|g_n\|^2\quad(z=1\text{ in the continuum}).
\tag{F.1d.A1}
$$
Cancellation of the CCR factorials proves this for unequal $a,b$ as well. Vacuum fill restores every scalar coefficient to one. At degree at most four there are at most four active momenta, or twelve real variables. The compact integrands are explicit finite products of the kernels and piecewise-polynomial $f$. Partition at its finitely many support faces. On a box of volume $V_d$, coordinate mesh $h$ and sum of partial-derivative bounds $L$, midpoint error is at most $V_dhL/2$, plus interval arithmetic radii times $V_d$. All derivatives follow by finite differentiation, with denominators bounded by $m_0$.

On the length-two temporal support, a mesh $\eta_t$ for $\beta(E)$ has error at most $\eta_t(2+|E|)$; $|b|\le1$ and $|b'|<2$ give this bound. On compact momenta $|E|\le2\sqrt{\overline m^2+3P^2}$. Part III gives the additional chronological $H$ and moment quadratures. Finite cell averages of $f$ are exact piecewise-polynomial integrals times its computable normalization. Finite alias truncations use the explicit Gaussian shell tails. Interval sums/products carry all coefficient errors and increasing precision/mesh resolution terminates. A loose finite active-index arithmetic count is $100(K+1)^2M_{\rm modes}^4$, $M_{\rm modes}=\ell_n^3$; coefficient generation, precision and storage are additional work, not free preprocessing.

For an implementation of a separated head, the normalized vector $u_{K,n}/\|u_{K,n}\|$ mixed with vacuum at weight $\|u_{K,n}\|^2$ specifies its exact finite density. To control arbitrary leakage on the full register, use the full-register norm bounds
$$
A_{\rm all}=(512R^3)(2/m_0)(16R^2H_0+XH_2),\qquad
O=2(R+2)(A_{\rm all}+b_0),
\tag{F.1d.A2}
$$
where $H_0,H_2,b_0$ are the ordinary-product constants. The full Brillouin-volume and kernel Hilbert–Schmidt bounds, followed by the whole-quadratic sector bounds, give $\|S_h\|,\|S_k\|\le O$. A full-register preparation trace error $\eta_p$ consequently changes first means by at most $O\eta_p$ and connected cross coefficients by at most $3O^2\eta_p$. The sufficient requirement $\eta_p\le\varepsilon/[15\max(1,O^2)]$ allocates $\varepsilon/5$. A certified coefficient-matrix operator error $\eta_s$ changes a product by at most $2O\eta_s+\eta_s^2$, before its connected-subtraction budget.

If a calibrated instrument for a Hermitian real or imaginary part of the cross product is supplied, its outcome norm is at most $O^2$, while a first stress has norm at most $O$. For outcomes in $[-B,B]$, $T$ independent repetitions have deviation at most $\eta$ except with probability $2e^{-T\eta^2/(2B^2)}$; for $r$ real quantities the sufficient union-bound count is $T\ge2B^2\eta^{-2}\log(2r/\delta_{\rm conf})$. This is conditional on actual instrument access, calibration and independence, not a new source measurement primitive. Preparation, coefficient arithmetic, readout bias and sampling uncertainty remain different error rows.

The original carrier has $\ell_n^3$ modes, occupation cutoff $R_n$, exact dimension $\binom{\ell_n^3+R_n}{R_n}$ and clock $\tau_n$. Its chosen coherent head, complex phases, vacuum mixing, coefficient precision, controls and emitted programs/storage are distinct resources. Physical preparation time/generators, achieved leakage, instrument calibration, holding/archives, any selected reset and their prices are not supplied by the mathematical selector. The theorem claims no total physical readout accuracy or source-cost identity from these indexed bounds.

A quantitative pure-gauge extension would also have to retain the insertion-location and both tensor-index contributions in
$$
(\mathcal L_wv)_{\mu\nu}=w^\gamma\partial_\gamma v_{\mu\nu}
+v_{\gamma\nu}\partial_\mu w^\gamma+v_{\mu\gamma}\partial_\nu w^\gamma.
$$
This theorem does not provide a quantitative modulus for an unregistered pure-gauge direction or nonzero canonical-$B$ family. The on-shell zero class is not substituted inside time ordering, nor is exact finite-lattice diffeomorphism symmetry assumed. A fixed nonzero curved-metric amplitude limit or interchange with differentiation away from the flat point requires its own uniform higher-derivative/remainder estimates. The present explicit expanding-lattice companion is distinct from the controlled fixed-cylinder Gaussian source and tensor-local Hermite first-jet construction of Theorem F.1c and Lemma F.1c.2a; neither source's physical or approximation scope is silently transferred to the other.

**F.2 Emergence of Einstein Causality from ND-RID Limits**

Standard relativistic causality (microcausality) — namely that observables in space-like separated regions commute — is obtained in the continuum AQFT limit once the bridge hypotheses of Theorem F.0 are imposed, in particular the uniform Lieb-Robinson control and the identification of the limiting Lieb-Robinson cone with the geometric causal cone.

<a id="theorem-f0q-bounded-quadratic-car-strength-and-spatial-locality"></a>**Theorem F.0q (Bounded Quadratic CAR Strength and Spatial Locality).** Work with the physical CAR modes of a finite set of sites, with arbitrary finite one-particle multiplicity at each site and the vacuum specified before comparison. Suppose the full number-conserving quadratic Hamiltonian has a supported decomposition
$$
H=bI+d\Gamma(K)=\sum_Z h_Z,\qquad h_Z=h_Z^*,\qquad
J=\sup_x\sum_{Z\ni x}\|h_Z\|<\infty.
\tag{F.0q.1}
$$
The individual summands need not be quadratic, number conserving, even, or of bounded range. The one-particle matrix satisfies the sharp bound
$$
\|K\|\le2J.
\tag{F.0q.2}
$$
If the matrices in (F.0q.1) are energies, the one-particle physical-time generator is $K/\hbar$; this fixed conversion is retained throughout. No bound on the extensive norm of $H$ or of its full many-body derivation follows.

For the continuum assertion take $\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C^q)$ with Lebesgue measure, $d\ge1$ and fixed finite $q$. Let uniformly bounded self-adjoint one-particle generators converge strongly on a dense linear field core through the stated isometric embeddings. Require the physical regional net to contain $n_f$ for every unit compactly supported Cauchy mode $f$ in the region containing its support. The precise pre-arrival hypothesis is that, for every pair $f,g$ with compact supports at strictly positive distance, there is $\tau(f,g)>0$ with $[n_g,\alpha_t(n_f)]=0$ for $0\le t<\tau(f,g)$. Then the bounded self-adjoint limit generator commutes with all spatial multiplication projections and is multiplication by an essentially bounded Hermitian $q\times q$ matrix field. It can mix internal components at one point but cannot transport spatial support. The same conclusion holds for a finite-rank Hermitian bundle over an ordinary locally compact spatial manifold with Radon volume, using local trivializations and separated compact sets. In a general direct-integral localization, preservation of the position multiplication projections gives decomposability relative to that algebra; the localization comparison is not inferred from an abstract even-observable core.

There is also a finite-sequence conclusion requiring no generator limit. Let $K_n=K_n^*$ on arbitrary finite one-particle carriers, $\|K_n\|\le M$, and let $f_n,g_n$ be unit orthogonal physical modes. If
$$
\sup_{0\le t\le\tau}
\|[n_{g_n},\alpha_t^{(n)}(n_{f_n})]\|=:\varepsilon_n\longrightarrow0,
\qquad \tau>0,
\tag{F.0q.3}
$$
then $\langle g_n,e^{-itK_n}f_n\rangle\to0$ uniformly on every compact real-time interval. Convergence of the commutators on a common dense subset of the displayed interval also suffices. For $M\tau\le1/2$, every integer $m\ge1$ and $T>0$ give the explicit estimate
$$
\sup_{|t|\le T}|\langle g_n,e^{-itK_n}f_n\rangle|
\le \frac{2\varepsilon_n}{\sqrt3}
\frac{[2m(T+\tau)/\tau]^m}{m!}
+\frac{[M(T+\tau)]^{m+1}}{(m+1)!}.
\tag{F.0q.4}
$$
Here $n_f=a^*(f)a(f)$, and the norm is the actual faithful even-CAR norm. An actual later transport lower bound consequently forces a nonvanishing earlier commutator in this source class. An upper Lieb--Robinson velocity without a response witness is not such a lower bound.

*Proof.* **1. The supported one-particle bound.** Let $P_1$ be the one-particle projection and $\Omega$ the vacuum. Define
$$
k_Z=P_1h_ZP_1-\langle\Omega,h_Z\Omega\rangle I_1.
$$
The vacuum subtraction cancels its action on particles outside $Z$, and a supported operator has no one-particle matrix elements joining $Z$ to its complement. Hence $k_Z=P_Zk_ZP_Z$, where $P_Z$ is the one-particle projection onto the modes in $Z$, and $\|k_Z\|\le2\|h_Z\|$. These statements do not require parity of $h_Z$: its parity-odd part has no matrix elements between the vacuum-preserving one-particle sectors in this compression. Since the full Hamiltonian is $bI+d\Gamma(K)$, the compressed vacuum-subtracted sum is exactly $K$. Thus for every one-particle vector $u$,
$$
|\langle u,Ku\rangle|
\le2\sum_Z\|h_Z\|\|P_Zu\|^2
\le2J\|u\|^2.
$$
Self-adjointness proves (F.0q.2), independently of support size, graph degree, range and mode multiplicity. A single mode with $h=J(2n-I)$ has vacuum energy $-J$ and $K=2J$, so the factor two is attained. For an unshifted on-site and individual hopping decomposition, the usual absolute row-sum estimate can instead give $\|K\|\le J$ in its own coefficient convention; it does not improve (F.0q.2) for arbitrary supported summands.

**2. Bounded limits on the actual field core.** For isometries $V_n$ into a common Hilbert space, extend $V_nK_nV_n^*$ by zero off their ranges. A common norm bound and convergence on a dense linear core extend convergence strongly to every vector: approximate a vector by a core vector before taking the limit. Passing to the limit in the matrix elements proves symmetry of the bounded limit and hence self-adjointness. The norm bound is retained. Power-series approximation then gives compact-time strong convergence of the one-particle unitaries. The CAR identity $\|a(f)\|=\|f\|$ transfers this convergence to each fixed field and CAR polynomial. A core specified only in an abstract even observable algebra, without the compatible one-particle embeddings and linear-field convergence, does not by itself supply this argument. Alternatively, if uniformly bounded one-particle generators have a strongly convergent unitary group already identified, the spectral theorem and Fatou's inequality give the same bounded-generator conclusion from $\|(e^{itK_n}-I)u\|\le M|t|\|u\|$.

**3. Exact even-CAR test.** For unit vectors $f,g$, put $z=\langle g,f\rangle$. On the two-mode CAR algebra, direct diagonalization on its one-particle sector gives
$$
\|[n_g,n_f]\|=|z|\sqrt{1-|z|^2}.
\tag{F.0q.5}
$$
The empty and doubly occupied sectors contribute zero. This is an even observable calculation in the faithful CAR representation. Both roots, $|z|=0$ and $|z|=1$, are retained.

For a bounded self-adjoint $K$, the scalar function $p(z)=\langle g,e^{-izK}f\rangle$ is entire and satisfies $|p(z)|\le e^{M|\operatorname{Im}z|}$ for unit vectors. If initially $f\perp g$, then $p(0)=0$. Exact commutation on a short one-sided interval forces $|p|\in\{0,1\}$ there by (F.0q.5). Continuity and its initial value force the zero branch on an interval. The identity theorem gives $p\equiv0$ at all real and complex times. This argument does not mistake the other root in (F.0q.5) for orthogonality.

Apply this to every compactly supported pair at strictly positive spatial separation. Fix an open set $O$ and $f$ with compact support in $O$. That support has positive distance from the closed complement. Every bounded-support $g\in L^2(O^c;\mathbb C^q)$ is therefore an admissible separated test, and such $g$ are dense in $L^2(O^c;\mathbb C^q)$. Hence $e^{-itK}f\in L^2(O;\mathbb C^q)$. Compactly supported functions are dense in the latter space, so it is invariant. Applying the same argument to $-t$ makes it reducing. Thus the group and its norm derivative $K$ commute with $P_O$. Strong limits of projections extend this to Borel sets and then to their Lebesgue completion; no zero-measure-boundary assumption is used. For scalar $L^2$, commuting with measurable indicators makes the generator multiplication: on a finite-measure set $E$, apply it to $1_E$, use commutation to determine its action on $1_A$, $A\subset E$, and extend from simple functions. Its norm bounds the multiplier almost everywhere. A sigma-finite exhaustion makes the local multipliers agree. Applying this to each entry of the fixed finite fiber gives a bounded Hermitian matrix-valued multiplier. Local trivializations give the stated bundle extension. Spatial regional CAR algebras and their even parts are invariant; component-selective subalgebras can still change under internal mixing.

**4. Finite sequences and the explicit modulus.** The scalar functions $p_n(z)=\langle g_n,e^{-izK_n}f_n\rangle$ obey the same entire bound uniformly in $n$. They form a normal family. Any locally uniformly converging subsequence has a limit with $p(0)=0$, and vanishing even commutators on the common interval give $|p(t)|\sqrt{1-|p(t)|^2}=0$. Continuity selects the zero branch near zero, and analyticity gives the zero function. Every subsequential limit is therefore zero, which proves compact-time convergence for the whole sequence. Uniform equicontinuity first extends convergence from a common dense set of time tests if that is the supplied hypothesis.

For (F.0q.4), $|p_n(t)|\le M|t|\le1/2$ on $[0,\tau]$, so (F.0q.5) bounds $|p_n(t)|\le2\varepsilon_n/\sqrt3$. Interpolate at $t_j=j\tau/m$, $j=0,\ldots,m$. The sum of absolute Lagrange coefficients on $[-T,T]$ is at most
$$
\left[\frac{m(T+\tau)}\tau\right]^m
\sum_{j=0}^m\frac1{j!(m-j)!}
=\frac{[2m(T+\tau)/\tau]^m}{m!}.
$$
Every real derivative obeys $|p_n^{(m+1)}(t)|\le M^{m+1}$. The integral divided-difference formula, valid for complex-valued functions by linearity, bounds the interpolation remainder by $[M(T+\tau)]^{m+1}/(m+1)!$. This proves (F.0q.4). First take $n\to\infty$ at fixed $m$, then $m\to\infty$. A claimed later overlap bounded below away from zero contradicts (F.0q.3); equivalently (F.0q.4) provides its finite pre-arrival lower bound whenever its remainder is smaller than that overlap.

The theorem concerns physical number-conserving quadratic CAR modes in the unchanged clock. A qubit encoding needs its own comparison of supported physical interaction norms, incidence and physical mode localization. General interactions, dissipative evolutions, an unidentified observable-only core and a changed clock are outside this theorem. Unbounded Dirac or finite-difference generators escape the uniform one-particle bound; on-site internal rotations are valid nontransporting examples. The result neither adds a positive attained-cone requirement to Theorem F.0 nor excludes every model admitted by that theorem. $\square$

<a id="proposition-f1-discrete-lieb-robinson-bound"></a>**Proposition F.1 (Discrete Lieb–Robinson Bound).**
Let $\mathcal N_n$ be an MPU network, and suppose its strongly continuous Heisenberg evolution has generator
$$
\mathcal L_n^*=\sum_Z\mathcal L_{n,Z}^*.
$$
Assume each $\mathcal L_{n,Z}^*$ is a Heisenberg-picture Lindblad generator supported on $Z$, and let $\alpha_t^{(n)}=e^{t\mathcal L_n^*}$ for $t\ge0$. Assume constants $r_0,J,z_*,\nu<\infty$, independent of $n$, such that $\operatorname{diam}(Z)\le r_0$, $\|\mathcal L_{n,Z}^*\|_{\infty\to\infty}\le J$, every network has degree at most $z_*$, and at most $\nu$ generator terms meet each site. For bounded operators

$$
A\in\mathfrak{A}_n(X),\quad B\in\mathfrak{A}_n(Y),
$$

supported on vertex sets $X,Y\subset\mathcal V_n$ at graph-distance
$\displaystyle d_{\mathcal N_n}(X,Y)=\min_{x\in X,y\in Y}d_{\mathcal N_n}(x,y)$,
there exist constants $C,\mu>0$ and a finite velocity $v_{LR}^{(n)}$ (controlled by interaction range and bounded local generator strength) such that

$$
\bigl\|\,[\alpha_t^{(n)}(A),B]\,\bigr\|
\;\le\;
C\,\|A\|\|B\|\,|X|\,
e^{-\mu\bigl(d_{\mathcal N_n}(X,Y)-v_{LR}^{(n)}\,t\bigr)}.
\tag{F.1}
$$

**Proof:**
Work in the Heisenberg picture where observables evolve by $\frac{d}{dt}A(t)=\mathcal{L}^*(A(t))$. Assume the Lindbladian decomposes as $\mathcal{L}^*=\sum_{Z}\mathcal{L}_Z^*$ with $\mathrm{diam}(Z)\le r_0$ and $\|\mathcal{L}_Z^*\|_{\infty\to\infty}\le J$ (operator norm on observables). Let $A$ and $B$ be supported on disjoint regions $X$ and $Y$. Define
$$
C_{X,Y}(t):=\sup_{\|A\|_\infty\le 1,\,\|B\|_\infty\le 1}
\|[A(t),B]\|_\infty.
$$
Let
$$
\|\mathcal L\|_\mu
:=
\sup_x\sum_{Z\ni x}|Z|\,\|\mathcal L_Z^*\|_{\infty\to\infty}
e^{\mu\operatorname{diam}(Z)}.
$$
Finite interaction range, uniformly bounded degree, a uniform bound on the number of generator terms meeting each site, and $\|\mathcal L_Z^*\|_{\infty\to\infty}\le J$ imply $\|\mathcal L\|_\mu<\infty$ for every finite $\mu>0$. Each local summand is a Lindblad generator, so removing any collection of interaction terms leaves a unital completely positive contraction semigroup for nonnegative time. The finite interaction-path estimate in Theorem 1 of Barthel and Kliesch (2012), and its autonomous counterpart in Poulin (2010), therefore gives constants $C_\mu<\infty$ and $v_\mu<\infty$, controlled by the local norm, range, degree, and incidence bounds, such that for $t\ge0$
$$
\|[A(t),B]\|_\infty
\le
C_\mu |X|\,\|A\|_\infty\|B\|_\infty
e^{-\mu(d(X,Y)-v_\mu t)}.
$$
This proves (F.1). No formula depending only on $(J,r_0,z_{\max},D,\tau)$ follows unless the incidence convention for the local terms and the walk-counting constant are also specified.

For a depth-$D$ circuit, suppose every layer consists of gates with disjoint supports and every gate support has graph diameter at most $r_0$. A gate disjoint from the support of an observable leaves it unchanged. A gate meeting that support can add only vertices at graph distance at most $r_0$ from it. Thus one layer enlarges support by at most $r_0$, and $m$ depth-$D$ cycles enlarge it by at most $mDr_0$. Hence, for $m\in\mathbb N_0$,
$$
[\alpha_{m\tau}^{(n)}(A),B]=0
\qquad\text{if}\qquad
d(X,Y)>mDr_0.
$$
For $\tau>0$, the circuit support speed is at most $Dr_0/\tau$. A bound by $r_0$ on the radius of a ball containing each gate support gives the diameter bound $2r_0$ and the corresponding speed bound $2Dr_0/\tau$. ∎

<a id="corollary-f1a-lightcone-normalization-on-the-strict-single-clock-branch"></a>**Corollary F.1a (Lightcone Normalization on the Strict Single-Clock Branch).** On a strict finite-range single-clock ND-RID branch, assume one update layer consists of gates with disjoint supports of graph diameter at most $r_0$, with cycle time $\tau_{\min}>0$. Let $\delta_{\mathrm{eff},n}>0$ be the physical edge scale and define
$$
