c_n:=\frac{r_0\delta_{\mathrm{eff},n}}{\tau_{\min}}.
$$
At $t=m\tau_{\min}$, $m\in\mathbb N_0$, the update satisfies
$$
[\alpha_t^{(n)}(A),B]=0
\quad\text{if}\quad
d_{\mathrm{graph}}(\operatorname{supp}A,\operatorname{supp}B)>mr_0.
$$
The physical support-cone speed is therefore at most $c_n$. If the geometric causal cone of Theorem 46 uses this same one-layer support-growth bound, edge scale and clock, and $c_n\to c$, the microscopic support cone is no wider than that geometric cone. Equality of the two slopes requires attainment of the one-step propagation bound. A Hamiltonian or Lindbladian Lieb--Robinson bound with tails requires its separate causal-cone certificate.

*Proof.* The layer argument gives the support inclusion in the $mr_0$-neighborhood. At $m=0$, disjoint tensor factors commute. At $m\ge1$, the ratio of the maximal physical support displacement to elapsed time is
$$
\frac{mr_0\delta_{\mathrm{eff},n}}{m\tau_{\min}}=c_n.
$$
Taking the limit proves containment; attainment supplies equality when assumed. ∎

<a id="corollary-f1-emergence-of-einstein-causality"></a>**Corollary F.1 (Emergence of Einstein Causality).**
Let $a_n>0$ be the physical length represented by one graph edge, with $a_n\to0$. Assume the sequence $\{\mathcal N_n\}$ converges geometrically to a Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g_{\mu\nu})$ with invariant speed $c$ on the complete Corollary 46a/Appendix O promotion branch. Retain only times $t\ge0$ for a completely positive semigroup; a negative time is admitted only with a separately certified reversible evolution and convergence at that time. Suppose the graph-metric Lieb--Robinson bounds hold with decay rates $\mu_n\ge\mu_0>0$, uniformly bounded operator norms, $\log |X_n|=o(a_n^{-1})$, and
$$
a_n v_{\rm LR}^{(n)}\longrightarrow c.
$$
Assume compatible isometric $*$-monomorphisms $\iota_n$ into a common inductive-limit quasi-local $C^*$-algebra are fixed, that $\iota_n(A_n)\to A$ and $\iota_n(B_n)\to B$ in norm, and that the embedded dynamics converge at the retained time,
$$
\iota_n\!\left(\alpha_t^{(n)}(A_n)\right)\longrightarrow\alpha_t(A)
\quad\text{in norm}.
$$
Assume also that every element of each limiting local algebra is a norm limit of a uniformly bounded representative sequence belonging to the corresponding local algebras satisfying the support-growth condition below. If the physical supports of $A_n$ and $B_n$ have a strictly positive spacelike margin at time $t$, so that for some $\varepsilon>0$,
$$
a_n\!\left(d_{\mathcal N_n}(X_n,Y_n)-v_{\rm LR}^{(n)}|t|\right)\ge\varepsilon
$$
for all sufficiently large $n$, then
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\bigl\|[\alpha_t^{(n)}(A_n),B_n]\bigr\|
=0.
$$
Indeed, (F.1) is bounded by
$$
C\|A_n\|\|B_n\||X_n|
\exp\!\left(-\frac{\mu_0\varepsilon}{a_n}\right),
$$
which tends to zero under the support-growth hypothesis, the compatible $*$-monomorphism and norm-convergence hypotheses above, and the stated uniform positive spacelike-support margin. Norm continuity of the commutator and the representative convergence give $[\alpha_t(A),B]=0$ on the corresponding region-local dense representative cores. A second norm-continuity argument extends this identity to the completed local algebras, so
$$
[\mathfrak A(\mathcal O_1),\,\mathfrak A(\mathcal O_2)]=\{0\}.
\tag{F.2}
$$
∎

**F.3 Continuum Limit and Emergent AQFT Net**

The transition from the discrete MPU network to continuum physics is formalized as the convergence of the sequence of discrete nets of algebras $\{\mathfrak{A}_n(\mathcal{O})\}$. The general sufficient-condition route is Theorem F.0. The Mosco-Bochner route closes the stable local-$C^*$-net bridge under the accepted certificate $\mathfrak B_{\mathrm{AQFT}}$ of Definition F.0c and all additional hypotheses of Theorem F.0d. The strict projective single-clock route closes that bridge under the accepted record $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{AQFT}}$ of Definition F.0e and all additional hypotheses of Theorem F.0f; in that branch, generator compatibility is exact on the retained core, while the semigroup and locality conditions remain part of the bridge.

<a id="theorem-f0-conditional-convergence-to-a-stable-local-aqft-net"></a>**Theorem F.0 (Conditional Convergence to a Stable, Local AQFT Net).** Assume the discrete MPU dynamics on the operational-continuum branch satisfy the following sufficient conditions:

1. **Uniform locality and bounded interaction strength.** The Heisenberg generators decompose on each graph as
   $$
   \mathcal L_n^*
   =
   i[H_n,\cdot]+\mathcal D_n^*,
   \qquad
   H_n=\sum_Z h_{n,Z},
   $$
   with finite range or exponential decay, uniformly bounded degree, and
   $$
   \sup_n\sup_x\sum_{Z\ni x}\|h_{n,Z}\|<\infty,
   \qquad
   \sup_n\sup_x\sum_{Z\ni x}\|\mathcal D_{n,Z}^*\|_{\infty\to\infty}<\infty.
   $$

2. **Uniform Lieb--Robinson control in physical units.** Let $a_n>0$ be the physical mesh, with $a_n\to0$. There are constants $C<\infty$ and $\mu_0>0$, decay rates $\mu_n\ge\mu_0$, and graph velocities $v_{\rm LR}^{(n)}$ such that for local $A,B$ and every retained time,
   $$
   \|[\alpha_t^{(n)}(A),B]\|
   \le
   C\|A\|\|B\|
   e^{-\mu_n(d_n(\operatorname{supp}A,\operatorname{supp}B)-v_{\rm LR}^{(n)}|t|)},
   \qquad
   a_nv_{\rm LR}^{(n)}\to c.
   $$
   The retained time domain is $t\ge0$ for a dissipative evolution. Negative times require the reversible certificate specified in Condition 3. The graph velocities may depend on $n$; the physical velocities $a_nv_{\rm LR}^{(n)}$ converge to $c$. This condition is the stated uniform bound for the local representatives entering the net and is stronger than a bound with an unrestricted support-dependent prefactor.

3. **Compatible regional embeddings and local generator convergence.** The maps $j_n^m:\mathfrak A_n\to\mathfrak A_m$, $m\ge n$, are coherent unital isometric $*$-monomorphisms: $j_m^k j_n^m=j_n^k$. They agree on overlaps, preserve region inclusions, and send $\mathfrak A_n(O)$ into $\mathfrak A_m(O)$. Their continuum embeddings satisfy $\iota_mj_n^m=\iota_n$. For each bounded region $O$, a common algebraic core $\mathfrak C_O$ lies in $\bigcup_n\iota_n\mathfrak A_n(O)$, and its norm closure is $\mathfrak A(O)$. For $A\in\mathfrak C_O$, choose an initial stage containing $A$ and its cofinally consistent representatives $A_n$, so that $\iota_nA_n=A$ and $A_m=j_n^mA_n$. Require
   $$
   \lim_{\substack{m\ge n\\n\to\infty}}
   \left\|
   j_n^m(\mathcal L_{n,O}^*A_n)
   -
   \mathcal L_{m,O}^*(A_m)
   \right\|=0.
   \tag{F.0.1}
   $$
   The embedded generator values converge to $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cont},O}^*A$. This operator is closable and $\mathfrak C_O$ is a graph core for its closure. The convergence certificate must specify its applicable theorem. For the common-space route, require strongly continuous contraction semigroups $T_{n,O},T_O$ on one Banach space $X_O$, with generators $A_{n,O},A_O=\overline{\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cont},O}^*}$, and, for some $\lambda>0$, $R(\lambda,A_{n,O})x\to R(\lambda,A_O)x$ on a norm-dense test set. The contraction bound $\|R(\lambda,A_{n,O})\|,\|R(\lambda,A_O)\|\le1/\lambda$ extends this convergence to every $x\in X_O$. Engel and Nagel (2000), Theorem III.4.8(c)$\Rightarrow$(d), then gives $T_{n,O}(t)x\to T_O(t)x$ uniformly on compact positive-time intervals. The certificate identifies these evolutions with the embedded local evolutions on their retained domains. A varying-space or Mosco route must instead supply its own proved comparison and identification theorem; algebra embeddings alone do not supply common-space semigroups. Regional restrictions agree on common cores. These domain and convergence requirements are separate branch premises.

   A $*$-automorphism group is claimed only on an additional reversible branch: every finite evolution is a $*$-automorphism group and the embedded evolutions converge for both signs of time, uniformly on compact time intervals on a common norm-dense core. The two limits are required to retain the composition law. They then obey $\alpha_t\alpha_{-t}=\alpha_{-t}\alpha_t=\mathrm{id}$; multiplicativity, adjoints and unitality pass to the norm limits, yielding the automorphism group.

   A uniform lower bound on finite-volume excitation energies is not, by itself, Condition 3. Such a gap can be used only as part of a local convergence certificate when it also supplies quasi-local spectral-flow or coarse-graining maps compatible with $j_n^m$, uniform Lieb-Robinson constants, a common local algebraic core, and a Trotter-Kato or Mosco convergence estimate implying (F.0.1). The structural SPAP/Landauer floor $\varepsilon_0=\ln2$ is dimensionless entropy cost unless a branch also fixes the physical clock, energy units, and generator normalization; it is therefore not automatically a Hamiltonian or Lindbladian spectral gap.

4. **Causal-cone containment.** The limiting Lieb-Robinson support cone is contained in the geometric causal cone for every retained sector entering the local net. On the strict finite-range single-clock ND-RID branch, Corollary F.1a gives containment when the same update radius, edge scale, and clock are used, and identifies the two cones only under its additional one-step attainment hypothesis. Outside that strict branch, equality and one universal limiting speed require an explicit saturation/attainment bridge or an accepted cone-saturation certificate $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{cone}}$ (Definition O.7.2.5); containment alone is sufficient for Einstein causality.

5. **State convergence.** The microscopic states $\omega_n$ are locally normal and compatible with the embeddings:
   $$
   \omega_m(j_n^mA)-\omega_n(A)\to0
   $$
   on the same local algebraic core.

6. **Time-slice core generation.** For every relatively compact globally hyperbolic region $O$ and every Cauchy time-slice $\Sigma\subset O$, the algebra generated by the evolved slice core is norm-dense in $\mathfrak A(O)$. This is an explicit branch hypothesis.

7. **Regional additivity and represented symmetries.** For every retained cover $O=\bigcup_iO_i$, the regional algebraic core for $O$ lies in the norm closure of the $*$-algebra generated by the cores for the $O_i$. For a represented topological group $G$ of geometric symmetries, specify microscopic unital $*$-automorphisms $\beta_{g,n}$ with $\beta_{gh,n}=\beta_{g,n}\beta_{h,n}$ and $\beta_{e,n}=\mathrm{id}$, compatible with the refinement maps. They transport regional cores in both directions according to $O\mapsto gO$, preserve the selected dynamics, and induce maps on the common core for which $g\mapsto\beta_g(A)$ is norm-continuous for every core element $A$. No continuity or covariance claim is made for geometric maps lacking this record.

Then the inductive-limit net $\mathcal O\mapsto\mathfrak A(\mathcal O)$ exists on the Lorentzian manifold $(M,g_{\mu\nu})$ supplied jointly by Theorem 43.5 and the Appendix O hyperbolic-promotion branch, and carries a strongly continuous local evolution generated on the common core by a closable full operator $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cont}}^*$. If the branch additionally fixes compatible regional microscopic GKLS decompositions and separate domain-preserving convergence certificates for their coherent and completely positive dissipative parts, then the limiting generator has the certified decomposition
$$
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cont}}^*
=
i[H_{\mathrm{cont}},\cdot]+\mathcal D_{\mathrm{cont}}^*.
\tag{F.0.2}
$$
On the additional decomposition branch, the coherent certificate includes
$$
j_n^\infty(H_{n,\mathcal O})\to H_{\mathrm{cont},\mathcal O}
$$
in local strong-resolvent form. Without that record, Condition 3 determines only the full limiting generator and contraction semigroup; it does not select $H_{\mathrm{cont}}$ and $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{cont}}^*$ separately. The emergent net satisfies isotony, additivity, covariance under every emergent isometry action represented by compatible microscopic symmetries, the time-slice property, and Einstein causality
$$
[\mathfrak A(\mathcal O_1),\mathfrak A(\mathcal O_2)]=\{0\}
\qquad
(\mathcal O_1\perp\mathcal O_2).
$$
The dual maps generated by $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cont}}^*$ give the continuum state evolution.

This conclusion is a local $C^*$-net with a strongly continuous contraction evolution. Promotion to a standard relativistic Haag--Kastler or Wightman theory additionally requires, as applicable, reversible automorphisms or a unitary Poincare representation, an invariant cyclic vacuum, and the spectrum condition; a dissipative completely positive semigroup does not supply those properties by itself.

*Proof.* Let $\Lambda_n$ denote the vertex set of the finite graph at stage $n$, with regional vertex sets $\Lambda_n(O)$ and their local matrix algebras $\mathfrak A_n(O)$ as in Definitions F.1--F.2. Use the coherent unital regional embeddings of Condition 3. The physical meshes tend to zero by Condition 2. The Lorentzian geometry and the comparison of its spacelike regions with the microscopic support cones are the complete geometric-promotion and containment premises of Condition 4. No nesting of the vertex sets beyond the specified algebra embeddings is needed.

Define the inductive-limit net. Let $\mathcal A$ be the global quasi-local algebra $\mathcal A:=\overline{\bigcup_{n}\iota_n\big(\mathfrak A_n(\Lambda_n)\big)}^{\|\cdot\|}$, where $\iota_n$ are the canonical embeddings. The local algebra for region $O$ is defined as $\mathcal A(O):=\overline{\bigcup_{n}\iota_n\big(\mathfrak A_n(O)\big)}^{\|\cdot\|}$ inside $\mathcal A$.
<a id="principle-of-compatible-embeddings"></a>**Principle of Compatible Embeddings.** The maps $\iota_n$ are the injective unital $*$-homomorphisms supplied by the accepted embedding record, compatible with the transition maps $j_n^m$ and equal on overlaps. Conditional expectations, when separately supplied, point from a larger algebra to a retained subalgebra and are not used as these inclusions. The accepted embeddings make the inductive limit well defined, and $\mathcal A(O_1)\subset\mathcal A(O_2)$ for $O_1\subset O_2$ follows from their locality compatibility.

Let $\mathcal L_n^*=i[H_n,\cdot]+\mathcal D_n^*$ be the finite Heisenberg generators. On the retained time domain, Condition 2 gives
$$
\|[\alpha_t^{(n)}(A),B]\|
\le C\|A\|\|B\|
e^{-\mu_n(d_n(X,Y)-v_{\rm LR}^{(n)}|t|)},
\qquad
\mu_n\ge\mu_0>0,\quad a_nv_{\rm LR}^{(n)}\to c.
$$
These are graph-metric velocities; their independence of $n$ is not assumed. The regional core, closability and stability certificate of Condition 3 gives a strongly continuous limiting contraction evolution for $t\ge0$. Unitality and complete positivity pass to the point-norm limit: apply positivity to every finite matrix amplification, whose positive cone is norm-closed. For two observables, their embedded product also converges, so multiplicativity passes to a limit of finite automorphisms when that branch is used. Surjectivity requires the additional negative-time convergence and composition certificate of Condition 3; on that branch $\alpha_{-t}$ is the inverse of $\alpha_t$. Without it the conclusion is the certified forward semigroup.

(Locality / LR-causality.) Let $O_1$ and $O_2$ have a strictly positive spacelike margin at time $t$. Under the lightcone-identification hypothesis, there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that
$$
a_n\!\left(
d_n(\Lambda_n(O_1),\Lambda_n(O_2))
-v_{\rm LR}^{(n)}|t|
\right)\ge\varepsilon
$$
for all sufficiently large $n$. Choose norm-convergent representatives $A_n$ and $B_n$ whose support prefactors grow subexponentially in $a_n^{-1}$. Condition 2 gives
$$
\big\|[\alpha_t^{(n)}(A_n),B_n]\big\|
\le
C\|A_n\|\|B_n\|
\exp\!\left(-\frac{\mu_0\varepsilon}{a_n}\right)
\longrightarrow0.
$$
Continuity of the inductive-limit embeddings then yields
$$
[\alpha_t(A),B]
=
\lim_{n\to\infty}
[\iota_n(\alpha_t^{(n)}(A_n)),\iota_n(B_n)]
=0.
$$
Condition 4 places the limiting Lieb-Robinson support cone inside the geometric causal cone. Equality of the cones additionally requires the registered attainment or saturation bridge. Hence
$$
[\mathcal A(O_1),\mathcal A(O_2)]=\{0\}
\qquad\text{for }O_1\subset O_2'.
$$

(Covariance and additivity.) Condition 7 defines $\beta_g$ on the common embedded core, independently of the refinement stage. Its microscopic group law and compatibility give $\beta_g\beta_h=\beta_{gh}$ and $\beta_{g^{-1}}=\beta_g^{-1}$. Isometry extends each map to a $*$-automorphism of $\mathcal A$. The regional transport record gives $\beta_g(\mathcal A(O))=\mathcal A(gO)$. For $A\in\mathcal A$ and a core approximant $A_0$,
$$
\|\beta_g(A)-\beta_{g_0}(A)\|
\le2\|A-A_0\|+\|\beta_g(A_0)-\beta_{g_0}(A_0)\|.
$$
Dense-core continuity therefore gives point-norm continuity on $\mathcal A$. For $O=\bigcup_iO_i$, isotony gives $C^*(\bigcup_i\mathcal A(O_i))\subseteq\mathcal A(O)$, and the regional core-generation premise gives the reverse inclusion. Thus additivity and covariance hold for precisely the covers and symmetry group supplied in Condition 7.

Thus $\{\mathcal A(O)\}_{O}$ with the limiting evolution generated by $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cont}}^*$ satisfies isotony, additivity, covariance for the represented emergent isometry subgroup, the time-slice property under the time-slice core-generation assumption, and locality once the lightcone-identification hypothesis is imposed. A separate coherent-convergence certificate identifies a retained Hamiltonian term as the local limit of the coherent microscopic generators. Without that certificate, the conclusion concerns only the full generator $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cont}}^*$. This is the content of the conditional continuum bridge stated in Theorem F.0. (Bratteli and Robinson 1997; Nachtergaele and Sims 2010) ∎

<a id="definition-f0a-local-generator-convergence-certificate"></a>**Definition F.0a (Local Generator Convergence Certificate).** A finite AQFT-continuum branch supplies a local generator convergence certificate
$$
\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{gen}}
=
(j_n^m,j_n,\mathfrak C_O,\mathcal L_n^*,\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cont}}^*,\varepsilon_{O,n},\tau_O)
$$
when, for every bounded diamond $O$, the following finite data are fixed before continuum claims are made:

1. compatible embeddings $j_n^m:\mathfrak A_n(O)\to\mathfrak A_m(O)$ and $j_n:\mathfrak A_n(O)\to\mathcal A(O)$ satisfying $j_m\circ j_n^m=j_n$ on the retained local algebra;
2. a common local algebraic core $\mathfrak C_O\subset\bigcup_n j_n\mathfrak A_n(O)$ dense in the graph norm of $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cont}}^*$;
3. finite-volume generators $\mathcal L_n^*$ on $\mathfrak A_n(O)$ with uniform locality constants compatible with the Lieb-Robinson bounds used in Proposition F.1;
4. for every $A\in\mathfrak C_O$, choose a stage $n_A$ and cofinally consistent representatives $A_n\in\mathfrak A_n(O)$ for $n\ge n_A$, with $j_n(A_n)=A$ and $A_m=j_n^m(A_n)$ for $m\ge n\ge n_A$, such that
$$
\left\|j_n\mathcal L_n^*(A_n)-\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cont}}^*(A)\right\|
\le\varepsilon_{O,n}(A),
\qquad
\varepsilon_{O,n}(A)\to0;
\tag{F.0a.1}
$$
5. a Trotter--Kato or equivalent stability record $\tau_O$ specifying the domains, closability, graph-core property and contraction-semigroup generation required in Theorem F.0(3), and proving convergence of the embedded finite semigroups uniformly on compact intervals of nonnegative time. The regional embeddings and restrictions obey the coherence and locality requirements of that condition. A reversible group requires its additional two-sided convergence and composition certificate.

A uniform lower bound on finite-volume excitation energies is not by itself a local generator convergence certificate. Such a bound may enter $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{gen}}$ only when it supplies the compatible embeddings, local core, quasi-local comparison maps, uniform locality constants, and convergence estimates listed above. The structural SPAP/Landauer floor $\varepsilon_0=\ln2$ is a dimensionless entropy cost unless a branch also fixes the physical clock, energy units, and generator normalization.

<a id="theorem-f0b-certificate-implies-theorem-f0-condition-3"></a>**Theorem F.0b (Certificate Implies Theorem F.0 Condition 3).** If $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is accepted for every bounded diamond in the branch and the compatibility hypotheses of Theorem F.0 hold, then Condition 3 of Theorem F.0 is satisfied.

*Proof.* Let $O$ be a bounded diamond and $A\in\mathfrak C_O$. For $m\ge n\ge n_A$, the consistent representatives satisfy $A_m=j_n^mA_n$. The isometry of $j_m$ and $j_mj_n^m=j_n$ give
$$
\begin{aligned}
&\|j_n^m(\mathcal L_n^*A_n)-\mathcal L_m^*(A_m)\|\\
&=\|j_n\mathcal L_n^*A_n-j_m\mathcal L_m^*A_m\|\\
&\le\varepsilon_{O,n}(A)+\varepsilon_{O,m}(A)\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
$$
This is precisely (F.0.1) on the regional core. The record $\tau_O$ supplies closability, the graph-core and generation properties, and the stated forward semigroup convergence. Its regional compatibility and the theorem's embedding hypotheses give the remaining parts of Condition 3. A group conclusion uses the additional reversible certificate. ∎

**Definition F.0c (Mosco-Bochner AQFT Bridge Certificate).** A Mosco-Bochner AQFT bridge certificate for a selected operational-continuum branch is a finite record
$$
\mathfrak B_{\mathrm{AQFT}}
=
\left(
\mathfrak D_n,
\mathfrak B_n,
\mathfrak C_n,
\mathfrak R_n,
\mathfrak H_n,
\mathcal E_n,
L_n,
\mathfrak A_n(O),
j_n^m,
\iota_n,
\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{gen}},
v_{\mathrm{LR}},
\mathfrak S_+
\right)
\tag{F.0c.1}
$$
such that:

1. the geometric defects $\mathfrak D_n,\mathfrak B_n,\mathfrak C_n,\mathfrak R_n,\mathfrak H_n$ are those of Theorem D.6e and satisfy $\mathfrak D_n\to0$ on the selected sequence;

2. the finite propagation-cost Dirichlet forms $\mathcal E_n$ Mosco-converge to the quadratic Cheeger energy of the noncollapsed $\mathrm{RCD}^*(K,4)$ limit supplied by Theorem C.6c;

3. on their specified Hilbert spaces and form domains, $L_n$ are the nonnegative self-adjoint operators associated with the closed symmetric Markovian forms $\mathcal E_n$. The associated contraction semigroups are $e^{-tL_n}$, whose dissipative generators are $-L_n$. Their form-domain and interpolation data belong to the Mosco certificate. The full Heisenberg generators on the observable algebras are governed separately by $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{gen}}$; Hilbert-space form convergence alone does not identify those generators;

4. the local finite observable algebras $\mathfrak A_n(O)$ form an inductive compatible system under the embeddings $j_n^m$ and the continuum injections $\iota_n$;

5. $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is the local generator convergence certificate of Definition F.0a on every bounded diamond;

6. if $a_n$ is the physical mesh, the Lieb-Robinson cones satisfy
$$
a_n v_{\mathrm{LR}}^{(n)}\to c,
\tag{F.0c.2}
$$
and the decay rates and support prefactors satisfy the uniform hypotheses of Corollary F.1;

7. the positive-energy spectral ledger $\mathfrak S_+$ fixes a common lower bound for the limiting reversible generator after the vacuum energy convention of the branch is applied.

**Theorem F.0d (Mosco-Bochner Certificate and Locality Side Conditions Give a Stable Local Envelope).** Suppose a branch carries an accepted certificate $\mathfrak B_{\mathrm{AQFT}}$ and the complete geometric-promotion branch used in Theorem F.0. Assume additionally the uniform interaction bounds, physical Lieb--Robinson estimates, causal-cone containment, state convergence, time-slice generation and regional/symmetry compatibility of Theorem F.0(1), (2), (4), (5), (6) and (7). The embeddings and cores in the certificate satisfy the regional requirements of Theorem F.0(3). Then the finite MPU local algebras have the stable local $C^*$-net and contraction-semigroup envelope stated there. A Haag--Kastler or Wightman promotion requires the additional package of Definition F.0h. For the symmetric Hilbert-space form operators, supply a Mosco-to-semigroup comparison certificate identifying its source theorem and verifying the theorem's form-domain, density, weak/strong convergence and interpolation hypotheses. Theorem 35b.6 supplies this comparison on the sequential separable dense-core class, including $t=0$ for dense form domains. Under the selected comparison certificate, for every $t\ge0$,
$$
e^{-tL_n}\to e^{-tL}
\tag{F.0d.1}
$$
strongly after the specified Hilbert-space interpolation maps are applied, where $L\ge0$ is the self-adjoint operator associated with the limiting closed symmetric Dirichlet form and $-L$ is its dissipative semigroup generator.

*Proof.* Item (1) supplies $\mathfrak D_n\to0$. Item (2) supplies Mosco convergence of the rescaled propagation-cost forms and identifies the limit with the quadratic Cheeger energy on the noncollapsed $\mathrm{RCD}^*(K,4)$ branch of Theorem C.6c. Therefore the limiting spatial envelope has a strongly local regular Dirichlet form with the infinitesimally Hilbertian structure required by Theorem 43.5.

Theorem 35b.6 gives (F.0d.1) once the comparison record verifies the selected closed symmetric densely defined forms and the Hilbert comparison structure of Definition 35b.5, equivalently its dense-core presentation. The isometric common-carrier representation of Theorem 35b.12 realizes the registered weak and strong convergence, and its dense-domain conclusion includes $t=0$. The densely defined comparison is also (Kuwae and Shioya 2003, Theorem 2.4). The branch record identifies the selected interpolation maps with that convergence structure. A record using another comparison theorem identifies its source and verifies the corresponding form-domain, density and interpolation hypotheses.

For the observable net, item 5 and Theorem F.0b supply generator convergence; item 4 and the additional regional hypotheses supply coherent algebra embeddings. The separately stated assumptions give Theorem F.0(1), (2), (4), (5), (6) and (7), so that theorem applies on the complete geometric-promotion branch. The slope limit in item 6 alone proves neither causal-cone attainment nor the stronger uniform Lieb--Robinson estimate nor an identification of the form generator with the full Heisenberg generator. ∎

**Definition F.0e (Projective Single-Clock AQFT Certificate).** A projective single-clock AQFT certificate for a selected operational-continuum branch is a finite record
$$
\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{AQFT}}
=
(\mathfrak Z_{\mathrm{cont}},\{\mathfrak A_n(O)\},\{j_n^m\},\{\mathfrak C_O\},\{\mathcal L_{n,O}^*\},\{\omega_n\},r_0,\tau,\chi_{\mathrm{slice}},\mathfrak S_+)
\tag{F.0e.1}
$$
with the following entries.

1. $\mathfrak Z_{\mathrm{cont}}$ is an accepted zero-defect continuum-gluing record in the sense of Corollary 43.5a.
2. For every bounded diamond $O$, $\mathfrak A_n(O)$ is a finite-dimensional local $C^*$-algebra and $j_n^m:\mathfrak A_n(O)\to\mathfrak A_m(O)$ are isometric $*$-monomorphisms for $m\ge n$ which agree on overlaps.
3. $\mathfrak C_O\subset\bigcup_n\mathfrak A_n(O)$ is a common local algebraic core whose image is norm dense in the inductive-limit algebra of $O$.
4. The microscopic update is strict finite-range and single-clock on the retained branch: after one tick $\tau$, support expands by at most graph radius $r_0$, and the same $r_0,\tau$ normalize the Lorentzian causal cone of Corollary F.1a.
5. The local generators are projectively compatible on the core:
$$
j_n^m(\mathcal L_{n,O}^*A)
=
\mathcal L_{m,O}^*(j_n^mA)
\qquad
(A\in\mathfrak C_O, m\ge n).
\tag{F.0e.2}
$$
6. The states are compatible, $\omega_m(j_n^mA)=\omega_n(A)$ on $\mathfrak C_O$, and locally normal in the inductive limit.
7. The time-slice indicator $\chi_{\mathrm{slice}}=1$ records that the evolved slice core is norm dense in every relatively compact globally hyperbolic diamond.
8. The positive-energy spectral ledger $\mathfrak S_+$ fixes the lower-energy convention for the limiting reversible generator.

**Theorem F.0f (Projective Single-Clock Certificate with Semigroup Stability Gives the Local-Net Bridge).** Suppose a selected branch carries an accepted $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{AQFT}}$ and the complete geometric-promotion branch of Theorem F.0. Assume on every bounded diamond the uniform interaction bounds, physical Lieb--Robinson estimates, causal-cone containment and regional/symmetry conditions of Theorem F.0(1), (2), (4) and (7). The projective embeddings are unital, coherent and region-preserving, and the common cores and regional restrictions satisfy Theorem F.0(3). Assume also that each projective core operator is closable, its closure generates a strongly continuous contraction semigroup, and an accepted stability record gives convergence of the finite semigroups on compact nonnegative time intervals. Then the stable local-$C^*$-net conclusions of Theorem F.0 hold, and these records supply $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{gen}}$. A reversible group requires the additional two-sided certificate in Theorem F.0(3); a Haag--Kastler or Wightman promotion remains conditional on Definition F.0h.

*Proof.* Item 1 supplies the operational-continuum envelope on its accepted branch. Items 2 and 3, with the regional hypotheses, give a coherent inductive system and norm-dense common cores. Item 4 bounds one-tick support growth; the separate Theorem F.0(1), (2) and (4) premises supply interaction bounds, physical Lieb--Robinson control and cone containment. Equality of cone slopes requires attainment. For a common core element, use its cofinally consistent representatives. Item 5 makes the generator-convergence difference in (F.0.1) zero at every cofinal pair of stages, so the embedded generator values agree and define the projective core operator. Its closability, graph-core and semigroup-generation/convergence records give Definition F.0a. Item 6 gives state convergence, item 7 gives time-slice generation, and the additional Theorem F.0(7) premise gives additivity and the represented continuous symmetry action. Thus every hypothesis of Theorem F.0 holds. Item 8 retains the lower-energy convention when the reversible subbranch is supplied, but does not establish reversibility. ∎

**Corollary F.0g (Local-Net Ledger Closure on the Stable Projective Branch).** The operational-continuum and stable local-$C^*$-net rows are closed on a branch carrying $\mathfrak Z_{\mathrm{cont}}$, an accepted $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{AQFT}}$, and all geometric-promotion, regional-embedding, locality, causal-cone, symmetry and semigroup-stability premises of Theorem F.0f. A standard relativistic AQFT or Wightman row remains open until the additional reversible representation, invariant state, spectrum, covariance and field-domain entries of Definition F.0h are supplied.

*Proof.* Corollary 43.5a supplies the continuum competitor condition on its branch, and the complete antecedent of Theorem F.0f gives the local-net and generator-convergence conclusions on every bounded diamond. The additional entries of Definition F.0h are required for its stronger promotion. ∎

**Definition F.0h (Complete Local-QFT/Metric Branch Package).** A complete local-QFT/metric branch package is a finite record
$$
\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{loc\mbox{-}grav}}
=
(\mathfrak Z_{\mathrm{cont}},\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{gen}},\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{KMS}},\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{Had}},\mathfrak N_{\mathrm{split}},\mathfrak W_{\mathrm{wedge}},\mathfrak J_{\mathrm{Jost}},\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{field}},\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{GSL}},\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{NC}},\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{EH}},\mathfrak G_n,\mathfrak O_{\mathrm{loc}},\chi_{\mathrm{loc}})
\tag{F.0h.1}
$$
with the following entries fixed on each bounded-diamond family before any continuum or metric comparison: an accepted zero-defect operational-continuum, projective single-clock, Mosco-Bochner, or explicit local generator convergence record; finite generators, common cores, embeddings, locality bounds, and defect bounds; finite KMS descent with $\delta_n\to0$; Hadamard-PCE finite-cost admissibility; split/nuclearity or a weaker finite phase-space compactness certificate sufficient for the claimed local net; faithful wedge states; boost/modular convergence; spectrum condition; modular covariance; finite Reeh-Schlieder replacement; Jost analyticity and Wightman reconstruction domain; local field realization; local-horizon thermodynamics and finite retained GSL; null-convexity or accepted second-variation substitute with zero retained modular/QNEC slack on reversible Einstein branches; the metric-action certificate; the nondegenerate finite-response gravitational-channel ensemble with smooth-envelope record, positive Hessian, linearization radius, and metric covariance; the overlap audit with the stress-energy, area-law, orientation, scrambling, Theorem 48a, and registry entries; and $\chi_{\mathrm{loc}}=1$.

**Theorem F.0i (Local-QFT/Einstein Closure and Outstanding Certificate Inputs).** If $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{loc\mbox{-}grav}}$ is accepted, then the branch derives a stable local AQFT net, Wightman realization, emergent Einstein equation, local horizon thermodynamics, metric response, and metric covariance from finite records, with residuals only in the intervals named by the tuple.

If $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{loc\mbox{-}grav}}$ is absent, the unfilled entries of Definition F.0h are the outstanding hypotheses of this sufficient closure package. In particular, the structural theorems do not by themselves supply all of: local generator convergence outside accepted projective or Mosco-Bochner discharge branches, finite KMS descent with $\delta_n\to0$, Hadamard-PCE finite-cost admissibility, split/nuclearity or weaker phase-space compactness, faithful wedge states, boost/modular convergence, spectrum condition, Jost analyticity, local field realization, finite retained GSL, null-convexity or second-variation substitute, zero modular/QNEC slack on a reversible Einstein branch, nondegenerate gravitational response ensemble, smooth envelope, positive Hessian, linearization radius, and metric covariance.

*Proof.* Theorem F.0 gives the stable local-net conclusion from locality, Lieb-Robinson, tightness, state convergence, and compatibility hypotheses. Definitions F.0a, F.0c, and F.0e give finite discharge routes for generator and operational-continuum data. Definition F.10.12a and Theorem F.10.12c give the KMS descent and emergent-metric closure only when their finite records are accepted. The Wightman realization additionally requires wedge, spectrum, Jost, locality, and local field domain data. The Einstein and thermodynamic conclusions require entropy, null-variation, metric-action, and gravitational-channel data. With the overlap audit, the component theorems compose. If two admissible completions preserve every registered prior constraint but give inequivalent retained local-net, Wightman, thermodynamic, or metric outputs, Theorem P.14.1f proves non-identifiability for that output. An unfilled entry alone establishes that this closure package is incomplete; it does not establish the existence of such a pair or the logical necessity of each entry. ∎

<a id="theorem-f0j-finite-reversibility-gate-for-local-completely-positive-dynamics"></a>**Theorem F.0j (Finite Reversibility Gate for Local Completely Positive Dynamics).** Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra and let $\Phi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ be unital and completely positive. If $\Phi$ has a unital completely positive inverse, then $\Phi$ is a $*$-automorphism. Consequently, every strongly continuous one-parameter group $(\Phi_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$ of such maps fixes the center componentwise and, on each matrix factor in the identity component, has the form
$$
\Phi_t(A)=e^{\mathrm{itH}}Ae^{-itH}
\tag{F.0j.1}
$$
for a self-adjoint $H$, unique up to a central scalar.

*Proof.* Kadison's inequality gives $\Phi(A^*A)\succeq\Phi(A)^*\Phi(A)$. Apply the positive inverse and then Kadison's inequality for $\Phi^{-1}$ to obtain the reverse inequality; hence equality holds for every $A$. The polarization identity puts every $A$ in the multiplicative domain, so $\Phi(AB)=\Phi(A)\Phi(B)$ and $\Phi(A^*)=\Phi(A)^*$. Bijectivity makes it an automorphism. A continuous path of automorphisms cannot permute the discrete minimal central projections. Automorphisms in the identity component of a full matrix algebra are inner, and a strongly continuous one-parameter inner group has the form (F.0j.1). ∎

This theorem completely separates the reversible finite-carrier branch from genuinely dissipative contraction dynamics. A continuum vacuum, spectrum condition, spacetime covariance, and Wightman field domain enter through the promotion package of Definition F.0h.

<a id="theorem-f0k-finite-dimensional-poincaré-covariance-has-trivial-translations"></a>**Theorem F.0k (Finite-Dimensional Poincaré Covariance Has Trivial Translations).** Let $s\ge1$, let $\mathcal P_s=\mathbb R^{1+s}\rtimes SO^+(1,s)$ be the proper orthochronous Poincaré group of $(1+s)$-dimensional Minkowski space, or its universal covering group, and let $U$ be a strongly continuous unitary representation of it on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space. Then $U(a,1)=I$ for every translation $a$. Consequently the joint energy-momentum spectrum is $\{0\}$, every vector is translation invariant, and the spectrum condition holds only in this trivial form. Therefore no Haag--Kastler or Wightman realization $(\mathfrak A,\mathcal H,U)$ with finite-dimensional $\mathcal H$ carries nontrivial Poincaré translations, and a promotion with nontrivial translations beyond the finite gate of Theorem F.0j requires an infinite-dimensional representation space.

*Proof.* The translations form an abelian subgroup. A strongly continuous unitary representation of $\mathbb R^{1+s}$ on a finite-dimensional space has commuting self-adjoint generators and a common orthonormal eigenbasis with $U(a,1)v=e^{ip\cdot a}v$, where $p\cdot a$ is the Minkowski product. Let $S$ be the finite set of joint eigenvalues $p$. For a Lorentz element $\Lambda$, where in the covering case $U(0,\Lambda)$ denotes $U$ at a covering element over $\Lambda$, the group law gives $U(0,\Lambda)U(a,1)U(0,\Lambda)^{-1}=U(\Lambda a,1)$. If $U(a,1)v=e^{ip\cdot a}v$ for all $a$, then
$$
U(a,1)U(0,\Lambda)v=U(0,\Lambda)U(\Lambda^{-1}a,1)v=e^{i(\Lambda p)\cdot a}\,U(0,\Lambda)v,
\tag{F.0k.1}
$$
because $p\cdot\Lambda^{-1}a=(\Lambda p)\cdot a$. Thus $S$ is invariant under $SO^+(1,s)$. Let $p\ne0$ and choose a spatial axis $k$ with $(p^0,p^k)\ne(0,0)$; one exists because $p\ne0$. The boost of rapidity $\theta$ in the $(0,k)$-plane sends $p^0$ to $p^0\cosh\theta-p^k\sinh\theta$. Since $\cosh$ and $\sinh$ are linearly independent, this is a nonconstant continuous function of $\theta$, so the orbit of $p$ is infinite. This contradicts finiteness of $S$. Hence $S=\{0\}$ and $U(a,1)=I$. ∎

Theorem F.0k plays for Poincaré translations the role that Theorem F.10.7e plays for half-sided modular translations: both place every nontrivial geometric flow in an infinite-dimensional limit.

<a id="theorem-f0l-sequential-norm-carrier-obstruction-for-full-weyl-algebras"></a>**Theorem F.0l (Sequential Norm-Carrier Obstruction for Full Weyl Algebras).** Let $S$ be a nonzero real vector space with nondegenerate antisymmetric bilinear form $\sigma$. Let a nonzero unital $C^*$-algebra contain unitaries $W(f)$, $f\in S$, satisfying
$$
W(f)W(g)=e^{-i\sigma(f,g)/2}W(f+g),\qquad W(f)^*=W(-f),\qquad W(0)=1.
\tag{F.0l.1}
$$
Write $\mathcal W(S)=C^*(W(f):f\in S)$ in this representation. Then:

1. $\|W(f)-W(g)\|=2$ whenever $f\ne g$, and $\mathcal W(S)$ is not norm separable.
2. No norm inductive limit of a countable sequence of finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebras with isometric $*$-monomorphisms contains an isomorphic copy of $\mathcal W(S)$. In particular, a regional carrier satisfying the countable finite-algebra, norm-dense-core hypotheses of Definitions F.0c or F.0e cannot be identified, by an isometric $*$-isomorphism, with this full Weyl algebra.
3. Let $(R_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be a one-parameter group of symplectic linear maps of $S$, and suppose $\alpha_t(W(f))=W(R_tf)$. The induced automorphism group on $\mathcal W(S)$ is point-norm continuous exactly when $R_t=I$ for every $t$. If $R_{t_0}f\ne f$ for one $t_0$, then every neighborhood of zero contains a $t$ with $\|\alpha_t(W(f))-W(f)\|=2$.

These conclusions concern the complete norm-closed algebra generated by all real smearings. They leave strong/weak operator limits in regular representations and other source-declared observable algebras subject to their own convergence certificates.

*Proof.* Fix $h\ne0$. Nondegeneracy supplies $k$ with $\sigma(k,h)\ne0$. The Weyl relations give
$$
W(ak)W(h)W(ak)^*=e^{-ia\sigma(k,h)}W(h)\qquad(a\in\mathbb R).
$$
The spectrum of a unitary in a nonzero unital $C^*$-algebra is a nonempty closed subset of the unit circle. Unitary conjugation preserves spectrum, and the displayed phases run through that entire circle. Hence $\operatorname{sp}W(h)$ is the whole circle. For $f\ne g$, $W(f)^*W(g)$ is a scalar phase times $W(g-f)$ and therefore also has the whole circle as spectrum. The continuous functional calculus gives
$$
\|W(f)-W(g)\|=\|1-W(f)^*W(g)\|=\max_{|z|=1}|1-z|=2.
$$
For a fixed $f\ne0$, the uncountable set $\{W(tf):t\in\mathbb R\}$ is thus $2$-separated. A separable metric space has at most countably many points separated by a fixed positive distance: assign to each point the first element of a countable dense set within distance $1/2$; the assignment is injective here. This proves item 1.

Choose a countable norm-dense subset in each finite stage. Their union, transported into the inductive limit, is countable and dense in that limit. Every metric subspace of a separable metric space is separable: for a countable base of balls in the ambient space, select one subspace point from each ball that meets the subspace. Consequently the limit cannot contain the nonseparable algebra of item 1. This proves item 2 with precisely the norm topology in the cited certificates.

For item 3, if $R_{t_0}f\ne f$ and some interval $(-\epsilon,\epsilon)$ fixed $f$, choose an integer $n>|t_0|/\epsilon$. The group law would give $R_{t_0}f=(R_{t_0/n})^nf=f$, a contradiction. Thus every neighborhood has a $t$ with $R_tf\ne f$, and item 1 gives the norm jump. Conversely the identity action is point-norm continuous. Every nonidentity $R_{t_0}$ moves some $f$, so these two implications exhaust the class. ∎

On this Weyl comparison class, choosing a finer mesh or an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space preserves the obstruction to the stated norm-carrier identification. Definition F.10.4c.10, Lemmas F.10.4c.11 and F.10.4c.13–F.10.4c.15, Theorems F.10.4c.16–F.10.4c.19 and Proposition F.10.4c.20 give a represented strong/weak limit with its observable, dynamics, locality and complete-response comparisons for the massive Gaussian source. Theorems F.0d and F.0f retain their original admitted algebras and norm-embedding hypotheses; under hypotheses (a)–(c) of Theorem F.0y their literal event-tensor norm packages retain only scalar event algebras, and the package classification outside those hypotheses remains open. The common massive scalar construction is supplied on its distinct represented comparison route.

<a id="theorem-f0m-event-support-invariance-from-vanishing-cross-event-tails"></a>**Theorem F.0m (Event-Support Invariance from Vanishing Cross-Event Tails).**

###### 1. Exact theorem and hypotheses

Let X be a countable set of persistent physical event labels. Let A be the norm inductive limit of finite-dimensional retained algebras $A_{n}$, with coherent unital isometric embeddings. Assume that the actual embeddings preserve event factors exactly, so that

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_n &= \bigotimes_{x\in X_n} A_{n,x}, \\
A &= \bigotimes_{x\in X} A_x,
\end{aligned}
$$

where $X_{n}$ is finite and the finite event fibres $A_{n,x}$ embed into their corresponding completed fibres $A_{x}$. The factors may be proper finite-dimensional C*-algebras with nontrivial centres. The completed fibres may be infinite AF algebras.

For each n, suppose $A_{n}$ is represented as a tensor subalgebra of an ambient microscopic matrix algebra

$$
\begin{aligned}
M_n &= \bigotimes_{v\in V_n} M_{n,v}, \\
A_{n,x} &\subset M_n(V_{n,x}),
\end{aligned}
$$

where $V_{n}$ is partitioned by the exact physical labels x. The retained event algebra may be proper inside its whole ambient event fibre. It must still have the displayed independent tensor factorization over events; arbitrary non-tensor retained subalgebras are not silently included.

Let $L_{n}$ generate a UCP semigroup on the actual retained algebra $A_{n}$. On that algebra its action is given by the actual ambient supported term family

$$
L_n(a)=\sum_Z L_{n,Z}(a),\quad a\in A_n,
$$

where each $L_{n,Z}$ is a linear map on $M_{n}$, supported on the microscopic tensor factors $Z\subset V_n$, and $L_{n,Z}(I)=0$. Set $\ell_{n,Z}=\lVert L_{n,Z}\rVert$ in the actual tensor-extended ambient observable norm. Individual terms need not separately preserve the retained algebra; their sum is the stated retained generator.

Let $T_{t}$ be the actual point-norm $C_0$ UCP limiting semigroup on $A$, with generator $L$ and a graph core $C$. Every $a\in C$ is the image of some fixed finite-stage element. For its consistent later representatives $a_{n}$, assume actual generator convergence

$$
j_n L_n(a_n) \to L(a)
$$

in C*-norm. This is convergence on the given core only; no convergence on its conditional expectations or on separately chosen local factors is assumed.

###### The quantitative cross-event condition

For each $a\in C$ choose, at one fixed old stage, a finite event set $F$ and a finite elementary-tensor expansion

$$
a=\sum_{\nu=1}^{m} \prod_{x\in F} a_{\nu,x}.
$$

Let $a_{\nu,x,n}$ be the consistent representatives in the whole fine event fibre $x$. Let $X_n(a)$ contain the union of their actual microscopic supports. Define

$$
\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_n(a) = \sum \bigl\{ \ell_{n,Z} : {}&Z\cap X_n(a)\ne\varnothing, \\
&Z \text{ meets at least two whole fibres } V_{n,x},\ x\in F \bigr\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Assume $\varepsilon_n(a)\to 0$ for every $a\in C$. The chosen finite expansion is fixed before $n$ tends to infinity. The bad-interaction condition refers to whole event fibres, not only the supports of individual $a_{\nu,x,n}$; this matters when the reference state has correlations inside one event fibre.

**Conclusion.** For every event subset Y⊂X and $t\ge 0$,

$$
T_t(A(Y)) \subset A(Y).
$$

Thus every point fibre, finite-event algebra, and open-region event algebra is invariant. The conclusion holds in the original inductive-limit C*-norm, with no state quotient.

###### 2. Quantified aggregate exponential tails imply the cross-event condition

A sufficient microscopic condition is the actual unweighted aggregate bound

$$
\sup_{n,v} \sum_{Z\ni v,\ \operatorname{diam}_G Z\ge R} \ell_{n,Z} \le J \exp(-\kappa R),
$$

with common finite J and $\kappa>0$, together with the following geometric/count statement for each fixed old event set F and each chosen core expansion:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{every } Z \text{ meeting two distinct whole } F \text{ fibres has } \operatorname{diam}_G Z\ge r_n(F), \\
&|X_n(a)| \exp(-\kappa\, r_n(F)) \to 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

Indeed,

$$
\varepsilon_n(a) \le |X_n(a)|\, J \exp(-\kappa\, r_n(F)) \to 0.
$$

One usual sufficient realization is $r_n(F)\ge\gamma_F/\delta_n$ with $\gamma_{F}>0$ and $\log|X_n(a)|=o(\delta_n^{-1})$. Exact event preservation and the actual geometric comparison must justify the positive separation of the whole fine fibres of distinct old labels. No unproved identification of different mesh parameters is used.

Fixed finite interaction range is a special case: once $r_n(F)$ exceeds that range, $\varepsilon_n(a)=0$. No interaction-arity moment is present. Conversely, an unquantified phrase such as “exponential decay” is not being substituted for the displayed aggregate condition or the directly sufficient $\varepsilon_n(a)\to 0$ hypothesis.

###### 3. Auxiliary summable resets and compatible finite perturbations

Choose faithful states $\rho_{x}$ on the separable completed event fibres $A_{x}$, and positive comparison rates $\lambda_{x}$ with $\Lambda=\sum_x\lambda_x<\infty$. Let $R_{x}$ replace the $x$ factor by its $\rho_{x}$ expectation, leaving the other factors unchanged. Put

$$
K=\sum_x \lambda_x(R_x-I),\quad \lVert K\rVert\le 2\Lambda.
$$

The series converges in operator norm and generates an onsite UCP semigroup. Let $S_{t}$ be the UCP semigroup with generator $G=L+K$ on $\operatorname{Dom} L$. Bounded perturbation preserves the graph-core property of $C$.

At stage n restrict $\rho_{x}$ to the actual embedded $A_{n,x}$ and define

$$
K_n=\sum_{x\in X_n} \lambda_x(R_{n,x}-I),\quad G_n=L_n+K_n.
$$

Because the embeddings preserve the exact event factors and the reset states are restricted from the same completed states,

$$
j_n K_n(a_n)=K(j_n a_n)
$$

for every stage element. Labels absent from the stage act trivially. Thus $j_nG_n(a_n)\to G(a)$ on $C$. Each $G_{n}$ generates a UCP semigroup on the actual retained finite algebra.

These resets are an auxiliary mathematical comparison only. They are not installed in the physical source, and no reset resource is supplied or declared free. Their rates are fixed in the original time units. The final conclusion is transferred back to the original L and $T_{t}$ in the reset-removal step below.

###### 4. Finite product states with stationary one-event marginals

Fix n. For each $h>0$, send a tuple of event states ($\omega_{x}$) to the event marginals of

$$
\Bigl(\bigotimes_x \omega_x\Bigr) \exp(hG_n).
$$

This is a continuous self-map of the compact convex product of the finite event-state spaces. A finite-dimensional Brouwer fixed point gives a product state $\varphi_{n,h}$ whose individual marginals are fixed at time h. Let h decrease to zero along a convergent subnet. Since $G_{n}$ is bounded at this fixed n,

$$
\exp(hG_n)=I+hG_n+o(h)
$$

in operator norm. The resulting product state $\varphi_{n}$ satisfies

$$
\varphi_n(G_n(b))=0 \text{ for every } b\in A_{n,x}, \text{ every event } x.
$$

No factorization of $\exp(hG_n)$ and no global stationarity of $\varphi_{n}$ has been asserted. Only the one-event marginal generator drifts vanish.

Extend each factor state $\varphi_{n,x}$ from its embedded finite algebra to the completed fibre $A_{x}$ by a state extension; use any fixed state at absent labels. The resulting extension remains product over events. Compactness of the product of completed state spaces gives a cofinal weak* convergent subnet. Denote the limiting product state on A by $\varphi$. All later state evaluations use these extensions, so evaluations on embedded retained stage elements agree exactly with the original $\varphi_{n}$.

###### 5. Compression to an old finite event set

For a finite old set F, let $E_{n,F}$ be expectation over the complementary event states of $\varphi_{n}$. Define

$$
\begin{aligned}
M_{n,F} &= E_{n,F}\, G_n |_{A_n(F)}, \\
M_{n,x} &= E_{n,\{x\}}\, G_n |_{A_{n,x}}, \\
D_{n,F} &= \sum_{x\in F} M_{n,x}\otimes \mathrm{id}_{F\setminus\{x\}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Every $M_{n,x}$ is a bounded UCP generator on its retained event fibre. To prove this directly, the maps

$$
Q_h=E_{n,\{x\}} \exp(hG_n)|_{A_{n,x}}
$$

are UCP, $Q_0=\mathrm{id}$, and $Q_h=\mathrm{id}+hM_{n,x}+o(h)$. In finite dimension, $Q_{t/k}^k\to\exp(tM_{n,x})$; hence the exponential is UCP. The marginal-drift identity gives $\varphi_{n,x}M_{n,x}=0$, so this event state is invariant under $\exp(tM_{n,x})$. Therefore $D_{n,F}$ generates a product UCP semigroup preserving $\varphi_{n,F}$, and is dissipative on its product-state GNS Hilbert space.

###### Proper retained algebras and ambient terms

For the termwise estimate only, extend every $\varphi_{n,x}$ further to a state on the whole ambient event matrix fibre $M_n(V_{n,x})$, and form their product. Its ambient partial expectations restrict on $A_{n}$ exactly to the retained $E_{n,F}$. Consequently one may apply them to individual ambient $L_{n,Z}$ values even if those values are not retained. The sum $G_n(a)$ is retained by hypothesis, and all actual compressed generators above are defined on the retained algebras. No ambient extension of the retained UCP semigroup is assumed.

###### The cross-event estimate

For one elementary product $a_\nu=\prod_{x\in F}a_{\nu,x}$, a term whose microscopic support touches no active input factor vanishes. A term meeting at most one whole old $F$ fibre, say $x$, factors through every other input event. Applying the product expectation over the complementary fibres gives exactly its contribution to $M_{n,x}(a_{\nu,x})$ times the untouched other factors. Thus it cancels from $M_{n,F}(a_\nu)-D_{n,F}(a_\nu)$.

Only terms counted in $\varepsilon_n(a)$ remain. For each such term the compressed full-product contribution has norm at most $\ell_{n,Z}\prod_x\lVert a_{\nu,x}\rVert$, and the sum of the at most $|F|$ one-event contributions has norm at most $|F|$ times that quantity. Expectations are contractions. Define the fixed finite tensor constant

$$
C_a=\sum_\nu \prod_{x\in F}\lVert a_{\nu,x}\rVert.
$$

Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\lVert M_{n,F}(a_n)-D_{n,F}(a_n)\rVert \\
&\quad\le (1+|F|)\, C_a\, \varepsilon_n(a) =: \eta_n(a) \to 0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5.1}
$$

This fixed expansion avoids any assumption that an ordinary map norm controls arbitrary ancillary amplifications. No unproved bound by a bare ||a|| is inserted. $C_{a}$ is independent of n because the embeddings are isometric and event preserving. The reset terms are onsite and cancel exactly in this comparison.

###### 6. The limiting product state is invariant for the auxiliary semigroup

Because $D_{n,F}$ preserves $\varphi_{n,F}$, equation (5.1) gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
&|\varphi_n(G_n(a_n))| \\
&\quad=|\varphi_{n,F}(M_{n,F}(a_n))| \le \eta_n(a) \to 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

Actual norm generator convergence on $C$ and weak* convergence of the extended $\varphi_{n}$ imply $\varphi(G(a))=0$ for every $a\in C$. Graph density extends this to $\operatorname{Dom} G$. Differentiating $\varphi(S_t(a))$ on $\operatorname{Dom} G$ and then using norm density yields

$$
\varphi S_t=\varphi \text{ for every } t\ge 0.
$$

This constructs a product invariant reference state without finite-time cone locality, separated factorization, or any assumption that the physical source state is product.

###### 7. Faithfulness of the product reference state

Write $B=\sum_x\lambda_x R_x$, so $G=L+B-\Lambda I$. The positive Dyson–Phillips expansion gives

$$
S_t=e^{-\Lambda t}\Bigl[T_t + \int_0^t T_{t-s} B T_s\, ds + \text{higher positive terms}\Bigr].
$$

Fix $0\ne a\ge 0$ in one completed event fibre $A_{x}$. Put $r=\rho_x(a)>0$. Norm continuity gives $R_xT_s(a)\to rI$, so $R_xT_s(a)\ge(r/2)I$ for $0\le s\le\delta$ with some $\delta>0$. The single-reset positive term gives

$$
S_t(a) \ge e^{-\Lambda t} \lambda_x \min(t,\delta)(r/2)\, I.
$$

Applying stationarity proves $\varphi_x(a)>0$. Thus every marginal is faithful. The product $\varphi$ is faithful on $A$: if $a\ge 0$ and $\varphi(a)=0$, each finite-event expectation $E_F^\varphi(a)$ has zero value under the faithful finite product state and is therefore zero; these expectations converge to $a$ in norm as $F$ exhausts $X$. Hence $a=0$.

Schwarz's inequality and stationarity now implement $S_{t}$ as a strongly continuous contraction semigroup on $H_\varphi$. Write its generator as $G_{H}$. The state is only a mathematical reference state; it has not replaced the physical source state.

###### 8. The projected dissipative inequality

Fix any event set $Y\subset X$. Let $E_{Y}$ be its $\varphi$-product expectation and let $W=I-E_Y$, viewed on $H_\varphi$ as an orthogonal projection. At stage $n$ use the product expectation associated with $\varphi_{n}$ and define $W_n=I-E_{n,Y}$.

For a fixed core element $a$ supported in the old finite event set $F$, $W_n(a_n)$ still belongs to $A_n(F)$. The product semigroup generated by $D_{n,F}$ commutes with $E_{n,Y∩F}$, because every onsite semigroup is unital and preserves its $\varphi_{n,x}$ marginal. Hence it commutes with $W_{n}$ on $A_n(F)$. Its Hilbert dissipativity gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\operatorname{Re} \varphi_{n,F}\bigl[(W_n a_n)^{*} D_{n,F}(a_n)\bigr] \\
&\quad= \operatorname{Re} \langle W_n a_n,D_{n,F}W_n a_n\rangle_{2,\varphi_n} \le 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

The conditional expectation identity and (5.1) therefore imply

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Re} \varphi_n\bigl[(W_n a_n)^{*} G_n(a_n)\bigr] \\
&\le \lVert W_n a_n\rVert\, \eta_n(a) \\
&\le 2\lVert a\rVert\, \eta_n(a) \to 0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8.1}
$$

For the chosen fixed finite tensor expansion of a, weak* convergence of the event-state marginals gives

$$
j_n W_n(a_n) \to W(a)
$$

in $C^*$-norm: partial expectations simply replace some of the finitely many fixed tensor factors by their state values, and those finitely many coefficients converge. The argument does not require $W(a)\in C$ or $W(a)\in\operatorname{Dom} L$. Together with actual generator convergence on $a$ alone, (8.1) passes to

$$
\operatorname{Re} \langle W a\Omega,G_H a\Omega\rangle \le 0,\quad a\in C.
\tag{8.2}
$$

###### 9. Why the original core is also a Hilbert generator core

For $a\in\operatorname{Dom} G$ in the $C^*$-sense, norm differentiability implies Hilbert differentiability, so $G_H(a\Omega)=G(a)\Omega$. Fix $\lambda>0$. For $b\in A$ put $x=R(\lambda,G)b$ in the $C^*$-generator domain. Approximate $x$ by $c_k\in C$ in the $C^*$ graph norm. Then

$$
(\lambda-G_H)c_k\Omega \to b\Omega
$$

in $H_\varphi$. Since $A\Omega$ is dense, $(\lambda-G_H)C\Omega$ is dense in $H_\varphi$. Explicitly, for $\xi\in\operatorname{Dom} G_H$ choose $c_k\in C$ with $(\lambda-G_H)c_k\Omega\to(\lambda-G_H)\xi$. The bounded Hilbert resolvent gives $c_k\Omega\to\xi$, and then $G_H c_k\Omega=\lambda c_k\Omega-(\lambda-G_H)c_k\Omega\to G_H\xi$. Thus $C\Omega$ is a graph core for $G_{H}$.

Thus (8.2) extends to every $\xi\in\operatorname{Dom} G_H$. No expectation-stability or localized intersection of $C$ was used. For such a $\xi$, differentiate along its $S$-orbit:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d}{dt} \lVert W S_t \xi\rVert^{2} \\
&=2 \operatorname{Re} \langle W S_t \xi,G_H S_t \xi\rangle \le 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating and extending by density gives

$$
\lVert W S_t \xi\rVert\le\lVert W \xi\rVert \text{ for every } \xi\in H_\varphi.
$$

Consequently $\ker W=\overline{A(Y)\Omega}$ is invariant under $S_{t}$. Since $E_{Y}$ is implemented by the orthogonal projection onto that subspace, for $a\in A(Y)$ we have

$$
\lVert S_t(a)-E_Y S_t(a)\rVert_{2,\varphi}=0.
$$

Faithfulness of $\varphi$ gives $S_t(a)=E_Y S_t(a)$ in the original $C^*$-algebra. Therefore $S_t(A(Y))\subset A(Y)$.

###### 10. Remove the auxiliary resets and recover the original dynamics

The bounded operator $K$ preserves every $A(Y)$. The original generator is $L=G-K$. Its bounded-perturbation Dyson series around $S_{t}$ consists of compositions of $S$ and $-K$, with norm-convergent time integrals. Every term maps $A(Y)$ into itself, and the whole series converges in norm on every element. Hence its sum, the original $T_{t}$, preserves $A(Y)$.

No positivity of $-K$ is required. In particular, support invariance is not inferred from the positive domination $S_t\ge e^{-\Lambda t}T_t$; that order inequality alone would not be the needed argument. Bounded perturbation by the support-preserving $-K$ is what returns the conclusion to the actual physical semigroup.

This completes the theorem.

###### 11. Scope and remaining physical audit

The theorem handles arbitrary retained finite-dimensional event centres and infinite AF fibres, provided the retained algebras have the actual event tensor factorization and exact same-event embeddings stated in the preceding hypotheses. It needs neither a sharp norm cone nor a commutant-based interpretation of Lieb–Robinson locality.

Its indispensable inputs are the actual finite generator family, the actual $C^*$-norm generator comparison on the given graph core, and the quantified cross-event error $\varepsilon_n(a)\to 0$. The displayed aggregate exponential tail and geometric/subexponential count package is a sufficient way to prove that error, not a replacement for checking it on the actual source.

This result does not use compatibility between an outer generator and independently named smaller-region generators. It also does not infer convergence on conditional expectations of core elements. Those were precisely the domain and source-identification gaps avoided by the projected-form argument.

Once the actual hypotheses hold, the established independent-event norm gap gives the corresponding obstruction to generation of an outer event algebra by evolution of a proper slice-neighborhood algebra. A scalar-source realization and all other original geometric/physical terminal predicates remain separate questions.

###### Time-slice consequence and the exact stopping point

If $p$ is a faithfully retained nontrivial event projection outside a proper slice-support set $Y$, independence gives, for every $b\in A(Y)$,

\[
\|p-b\|\ge \max\{\|b\|,\|I-b\|\}\ge\tfrac12.
\]

Evaluate the target factor in its $p=0$ and $p=1$ states to obtain the first inequality. Since every $T_t(A(Y))$ stays in $A(Y)$, their generated $C^*$-algebra stays there too and cannot approximate $p$. This uses the tensor projection gap displayed above. A state-dependent $L^{2}$ quotient or vanishing expectation of $p$ does not remove the original $C^*$-norm gap.

Thus the quantified branch fails nontrivial independent-event evolved time-slice generation. A scalar net cannot substitute for a chosen faithfully embedded nontrivial MPU algebra. Positive-source/state/geometry/summable-error constructions on other admitted interpretations remain separate obligations. Theorem F.0y gives the same conclusion from the precone (F.0y.2), for finite-range and exponential locality, under its hypotheses (a)–(c).

###### A nontrivial realization of the hypotheses

The theorem class is nonempty. Refine the dyadic path grids of $[0,1]$, with one fixed $M_{d}$ event algebra at each vertex, $d\ge 2$, and tensor-identity embeddings at persistent dyadic labels. Use a fixed selfadjoint onsite $h$, for example $\operatorname{diag}(0,\dots,d-1)$ in the registered units, and $H_n=\sum_v h_v$ with its original fixed time normalization. The interaction range is zero, the local strengths are uniformly bounded, and every cross-event error is exactly zero. Every fixed old observable has exactly the same onsite evolution at every later stage.

The limiting product automorphism group is point-norm $C_{0}$. The finite-event algebraic union is a genuine graph core: product-trace expectations $E_{F}$ onto finite event sets commute with the group and converge in norm to the identity. For $a$ in the generator domain, $E_F a\to a$ and $L E_F a=E_F L a\to L a$; each $E_{F}a$ belongs to the finite-dimensional local algebra. Product trace or fixed-temperature product Gibbs states are faithful and invariant. No physical bath, reset service or time rescaling is used in this example.

A nontrivial projection at a label outside a chosen neighborhood remains at distance at least 1/2 from all its evolved observables. The example verifies the analytic hypotheses and their nontrivial exclusion consequence. It does not claim the complete original cost, MPU realization, or 3+1 Lorentzian-promotion certificates.

<a id="proposition-f0n-termwise-decay-does-not-imply-aggregate-locality"></a>**Proposition F.0n (Termwise Decay Does Not Imply Aggregate Locality).**

##### Appendix A Why termwise decay cannot replace aggregate decay

###### Result and scope

There is a sequence of full matrix tensor systems on dyadic path graphs with:

1. bounded graph degree and genuine compact measured GH convergence with shrinking physical edges;
2. a decomposition into distinct, genuinely supported GKLS terms, each satisfying a uniform termwise exponential diameter bound;
3. uniformly bounded per-site sums, indeed a uniformly bounded full-generator norm;
4. exact support preservation, so a uniform sharp-form **full ambient** commutator LR bound with any declared finite physical velocity;
5. coherent exact event-preserving unital isometric embeddings, common finite-event algebraic graph cores, and actual point-norm semigroup convergence uniformly on compact time intervals;
6. failure of every uniform aggregate exponential-tail estimate.

The aggregate-tail failure is intrinsic: no alternative decomposition into supported unital-at-identity generators can give the same full generators a uniform aggregate exponential tail. A two-endpoint product-defect lower bound proves this independently of the displayed decomposition.

This is an analytic nonimplication example. It does not instantiate the complete original Lorentzian-promotion/source package, and its support-preserving dynamics fail nontrivial event-algebra time-slice generation. It is not a positive F01 owner witness. Nor does it decide that the original undefined words “exponential decay” were intended to mean termwise decay. It proves that if they are read that way, the other listed analytic hypotheses do not automatically upgrade them to aggregate decay.

###### 1. Dyadic geometry and tensor embeddings

At stage $n\ge 1$, let $L_n=2^n$. Take the path graph with vertices $j=0,\dots,L_n$, edges between successive integers, and physical location $j/L_n$. Set $a_n=1/L_n$ and put one qubit at every vertex. The endpoints are the fixed event labels $x=0$ and $y=1$.

The physical path metric is exactly the Euclidean metric on this dyadic grid. Normalized counting measure converges to Lebesgue measure. Hence these finite metric-measure spaces converge in measured GH sense to `[0,1]`. Their maximum degree is 2 and

$$
a_n \log(L_n+1) \to 0.
$$

Old vertices persist at every refinement. Use the canonical tensor-identity embeddings from old qubits to the same event-labelled fine qubits, with identity on all newly added factors. They are coherent unital isometric *-monomorphisms and preserve the algebra of every region determined by event locations.

Write `V_n` for the fresh odd-indexed vertices. Then

$$
m_n := |V_n| = L_n/2.
$$

The sets $V_{n}$ are disjoint from every older dyadic vertex set. The global inductive-limit algebra is the usual quasi-local tensor C*-algebra over the countable dyadic event labels. Its algebraic finite-event union is norm dense.

###### 2. Distinct genuine GKLS summands

For each subset $S\subset V_n$, put

$$
U_S = Z_x Z_y \prod_{v\in S} Z_v,
$$

where Z denotes the Pauli Z at the indicated qubit, and define

$$
D_{n,S} = 2^{-m_n} (\operatorname{Ad}(U_S)-\mathrm{id}).
$$

Here $\operatorname{Ad}(U)(A)=U^* A U$; all the $U_{S}$ are self-adjoint unitaries. Each term is an exact GKLS generator with zero Hamiltonian and one Lindblad operator

$$
J_S = 2^{-m_n/2} U_S.
$$

Indeed, $J_S^* A J_S - (1/2)\{J_S^*J_S,A\}$ is exactly the displayed term.

Its actual minimal tensor support is

$$
Z_{n,S} = \{x,y\} \cup S.
$$

To check minimality, if `v` belongs to this set, then

$$
D_{n,S}(X_v) = -2^{1-m_n} X_v \ne 0.
$$

A supported superoperator annihilating the identity and missing v would annihilate $X_{v}$. Therefore none of the listed sites is merely padding. Conversely the formula is visibly supported on that set.

Different subsets S give different channels. If S and S' differ at v, their conjugations act with opposite signs on $X_{v}$. There is thus no duplicate-term subdivision masquerading as spatial decay.

The norm is exactly

$$
\ell_{n,S} = \lVert D_{n,S}\rVert_{\infty\to\infty} = 2^{1-m_n}.
$$

The upper bound follows from two norm-one maps, and $X_{x}$ gives equality. Every support includes both endpoints and therefore has graph diameter exactly $L_{n}$.

With

$$
\kappa = (\log 2)/2,
$$

we get the exact termwise exponential estimate

$$
\ell_{n,S} = 2\exp(-\kappa L_n) = 2\exp[-\kappa\,\operatorname{diam}_G Z_{n,S}].
$$

###### 3. Per-site sums and aggregate-tail failure

There are $2^{m_n}$ summands. Every one contains $x$ and $y$. Therefore each endpoint has per-site sum

$$
\sum_{Z\ni x} \ell_Z = \sum_{Z\ni y} \ell_Z = 2.
$$

A fresh vertex belongs to exactly $2^{m_n-1}$ subsets, so its per-site sum is 1. Every other vertex has sum zero. Hence the uniform per-site bound is $J=2$.

All terms at an endpoint have diameter $L_{n}$. Thus

$$
\sum_{Z\ni x,\ \operatorname{diam}_G Z \ge L_n} \ell_Z = 2
$$

for every $n$. No constants $C<\infty$, $\gamma>0$ independent of $n$ can make this less than $C\exp(-\gamma L_n)$.

The Hamiltonian is zero, so the Hamiltonian per-site bound holds trivially. There is no rescaling of the physical clock.

###### 4. Full generator, exact support preservation, and full ambient LR

For a fresh vertex v let

$$
E_v = (\mathrm{id}+\operatorname{Ad}(Z_v))/2,
$$

the one-qubit dephasing conditional expectation. Define

$$
\begin{aligned}
E_{V_n} &= \prod_{v\in V_n} E_v, \\
K &= \operatorname{Ad}(Z_x Z_y).
\end{aligned}
$$

All these superoperators commute. Expanding the product gives

$$
2^{-m_n} \sum_{S\subset V_n} \operatorname{Ad}(U_S) = K E_{V_n}.
$$

Consequently the full generator is exactly

$$
G_n = \sum_S D_{n,S} = K E_{V_n}-\mathrm{id}.
$$

It has norm exactly 2, again tested on $X_{x}$. In particular its norm is uniformly bounded globally, not only per site.

Every $\mathrm{Ad}(U_S)$ is a product of onsite conjugations. It preserves each tensor-support algebra $A_n(F)$, even when its defining $U_{S}$ includes sites outside $F$: those outside factors commute through the input. Therefore $G_{n}$ and its entire semigroup $T_n(t)$ preserve every support algebra exactly.

For disjoint X and Y and arbitrary full matrix observables A supported on X and B supported on Y,

$$
[T_n(t) A,B]=0\quad\text{for every } t\ge 0.
$$

For overlapping supports the universal commutator norm bound is $2\lVert A\rVert\lVert B\rVert$. Thus, for example, the F.0(2)-shaped estimate holds with

$$
C=2,\quad \mu_n=1,\quad v_n=c L_n,
$$

for any chosen $c>0$; then $a_n v_n=c$. These are full ambient matrix tests, not merely diagonal tests. The declared cone is an upper bound; propagation attainment is absent because no support moves.

The maps nevertheless have macroscopic **correlated noise**, measured by the product defect in Section 7. Support preservation and vanishing distant commutators do not imply a tensor product of independent regional channels.

###### 5. Exact eventual generator and semigroup convergence

Fix an observable $A$ belonging to a finite old stage $n_{0}$. For every $n>n_0$, its support is disjoint from $V_{n}$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
E_{V_n} A &= A, \\
G_n A &= (K-\mathrm{id}) A.
\end{aligned}
$$

Its $G_{n}$ evolution stays on that same finite support. Therefore, for every $n>n_0$ and every $t\ge 0$,

$$
T_n(t) A = \exp[t(K-\mathrm{id})] A.
$$

These are exact identities under the canonical embeddings. In particular, all cofinal generator and semigroup comparison errors for a fixed old observable are zero from one further refinement onward.

The limiting bounded generator on the inductive-limit C*-algebra is

$$
G=K-\mathrm{id}.
$$

Since $K^2=\mathrm{id}$, its semigroup has the explicit formula

$$
T(t) = [(1+\exp(-2t))/2]\,\mathrm{id} + [(1-\exp(-2t))/2]\,K.
$$

It is a strongly continuous UCP contraction semigroup. The finite-event algebraic union is a unital *-algebra, invariant under $G$ and $T(t)$, norm dense, and a graph core because $G$ is bounded.

For a common-space formulation, extend each finite $G_{n}$ to the full inductive-limit algebra by the same finite-site formula $K E_{V_n}-\mathrm{id}$. These are uniformly bounded generators. Their eventual agreement with $G$ on the dense finite-event union gives strong operator convergence of generators on the entire C*-algebra. The same dense approximation and contraction bound give point-norm semigroup convergence uniformly on every compact nonnegative time interval. On the original finite local domains these common-space maps are exactly the finite dynamics.

A compatible normalized product trace provides locally normal, refinement-compatible states and is invariant under every displayed channel. None of the operator-norm statements uses a state quotient.

###### 6. Regional restrictions: what is supplied and what is not

Because all support algebras are invariant, the actual restriction $G_{n,O}=G_n|_{A_n(O)}$ exists for every region $O$. The regional semigroups are the corresponding restrictions. They agree exactly on overlaps and inclusions. For fixed old regional observables their convergence is the same eventual equality as in Section 5. The limiting regional generator is the restriction of $K-\mathrm{id}$, with its finite-event regional union as a graph core.

These restrictions are genuine completely positive dynamics. On a regional input, conjugation by an outside Pauli factor has no effect, so each restricted summand may be written using the intersection of its support with O; zero terms can be removed.

A restriction is not being identified with the different operation “discard every original summand whose global support is not contained in O.” The latter operation would generally give another generator. The original phrase about regional restrictions does not by itself equate those two conventions. The present example supplies actual invariant-algebra restrictions and their exact compatibility.

The distinct, unpadded termwise-decay decomposition in Sections 2–3 is the global one. Restricting and regrouping equal regional channels can change the chosen termwise presentation; no additional global-to-regional decomposition convention is silently assumed.

###### 7. Intrinsic aggregate obstruction for every local decomposition

Let $a=X_x$ and $b=X_y$. At every $n$,

$$
G_n(a)=-2a,\quad G_n(b)=-2b,\quad\text{and}\quad G_n(ab)=0.
$$

Thus the bilinear product defect is

$$
\Gamma_{G_n}(a,b) := G_n(ab)-G_n(a)b-aG_n(b) = 4ab,
$$

and has norm 4.

Now suppose the same full generator has **any** finite decomposition

$$
G_n = \sum_Z L_{n,Z},
$$

where each term is supported on Z and annihilates the identity. Genuine local Heisenberg GKLS generators satisfy these conditions.

If $Z$ misses $x$ or $y$, locality and $L_Z(I)=0$ give $\Gamma_{L_Z}(a,b)=0$: for example, when $y$ is outside $Z$,

$$
L_Z(ab)=L_Z(a)b\quad\text{and}\quad L_Z(b)=0.
$$

For every remaining term, the elementary operator-norm bound gives

$$
\lVert\Gamma_{L_Z}(a,b)\rVert \le 3 \lVert L_Z\rVert\,\lVert a\rVert\,\lVert b\rVert = 3\lVert L_Z\rVert.
$$

Summing and using the triangle inequality yields

$$
4 \le 3 \sum_{Z\ni x,y} \lVert L_Z\rVert.
$$

Therefore

$$
\sum_{Z\ni x,\ \operatorname{diam}_G Z \ge L_n} \lVert L_Z\rVert \ge 4/3.
$$

The same endpoint tail fails to decay in **every** such local decomposition. Consequently there is no equivalent decomposition satisfying a uniform positive aggregate exponential decay rate. The failure cannot be repaired merely by regrouping the displayed terms or proposing a more efficient decomposition.

Even if a proposed decomposition is not individually unital-at-identity but its sum is, set

$$
L'_Z(A)=L_Z(A)-L_Z(I)A.
$$

Each $L'_Z$ is supported on $Z$, annihilates $I$, has norm at most $2\lVert L_Z\rVert$, and still sums to $G_{n}$. The same proof gives a lower bound $2/3$ on the original endpoint tail. These normalized summands need not remain GKLS; the point is only that the intrinsic norm obstruction does not depend on individual unitality if support-locality is retained.

###### 8. Exact limits of the example

This construction establishes the requested analytic nonimplication even on full local matrix algebras and with actual core/semigroup convergence. It does not establish a nontrivial time-slice limit. Because every $T_n(t)$ and $T(t)$ preserves support, an observable at an event outside a slice neighborhood cannot be generated from evolved observables of that neighborhood; the standard independent-factor projection gap applies.

The geometry is the compact interval. It is sufficient for this analytic logical counterexample and for genuine shrinking-edge compactness. A complete 3+1 Lorentzian-promotion, MPU source, Mosco/Cheeger, and original time-slice record is neither supplied nor claimed.

The source-level conclusion is precise: **termwise exponential decay plus the other displayed analytic controls does not entail aggregate exponential decay**. A proof requiring the latter must obtain it from an explicit definition or branch certificate, rather than infer it from unweighted per-site sums, full LR, or norm convergence.

<a id="theorem-f0o-center-sensitive-finite-range-norm-localization"></a>**Theorem F.0o (Center-Sensitive Finite-Range Norm Localization).**

##### 1. Finite-volume norm-localization theorem

Let $G$ be a finite graph of degree at most $D$. Work either on the independent retained tensor algebra $A=\bigotimes_x A_x$, with finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebras (centers allowed), or on the full ambient tensor matrix algebra. Let

$$
L = \sum_Z L_Z,\qquad \ell_Z = \lVert L_Z\rVert,
$$

where every $L_{Z}$ is a supported Heisenberg Lindblad generator with $L_Z(1)=0$ and a UCP semigroup, every support has graph diameter at most $r\ge 1$, and

$$
\sup_x \sum_{Z\ni x} \ell_Z \le g.
$$

All constants below are independent of volume and factor dimensions. Write $s=1+D+\dots+D^{\lceil r\rceil}$, so $|Z|\le s$, and $b=s g$. For $X=\operatorname{supp} A$ and $\Omega_R=\{x: d(x,X)\le R\}$, let $L_\Omega$ be the sum of terms $Z$ contained in $\Omega_R$. For $R\ge 0$ set

$$
m = \lfloor R/r\rfloor.
$$

Then, for all $t\ge 0$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert e^{tL} A - e^{t L_\Omega} A\rVert \\
&\le |X|\, g t \lVert A\rVert \sum_{k\ge m} (b t)^{k}/k!
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\le |X|\, g t \lVert A\rVert \exp(b t e^{\theta} - \theta m),\quad \theta > 0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
$$

The second term of (1) is actually supported in $\Omega_{R}$. Therefore (1) is a center-sensitive distance-to-local-algebra estimate, not a commutator estimate.

For $r=0$ all terms are on-site and exact support invariance holds already at finite volume. Terms of zero norm can be omitted.

###### Proof by deletion, overlap paths, and Duhamel

Define $f_Z(t)=\lVert L_Z e^{tL} A\rVert/\ell_Z$. Separate $L$ into the sum $L_{\mathrm{disj}(Z)}$ of terms disjoint from $Z$ and the remaining terms. Disjoint supported maps commute with $L_{Z}$. Since deleting Lindblad summands leaves a UCP contraction semigroup, variation of constants gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
f_Z(t) \le{}& \lVert A\rVert\, 1_{Z \text{ intersects } X} \\
&+ \int_0^t \sum_{W \text{ intersects } Z} \ell_W f_W(u)\, du.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
$$

Indeed the inhomogeneous term is $L_Z L_W e^{uL}A$, bounded by $\ell_Z\ell_W f_W(u)$. Iterating this finite positive integral inequality produces overlap paths $Z_0,\dots,Z_k$ with consecutive supports intersecting and terminal $Z_{k}$ meeting $X$. The weight after multiplication by $\ell_{Z_0}$ is the product of all $\ell_{Z_i}$.

A path of $k$ transitions beginning at a support not contained in $\Omega_{R}$ and ending at $X$ must satisfy $(k+1)r>R$: choose a vertex outside $\Omega_{R}$ in $Z_{0}$ and connect through successive intersections to $X$. Consequently $k\ge\lfloor R/r\rfloor=m$. This includes the case $R/r$ is an integer.

Reverse the path. Its total initial weight over terminal supports meeting X is at most g |X|. At every next step the sum of the weights of supports meeting the current Z is at most

$$
\sum_{x\in Z} \sum_{W\ni x} \ell_W \le |Z|g \le sg = b.
$$

Thus summing (3)'s iterated series over every Z not contained in $\Omega_{R}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{Z\not\subset \Omega_R} \lVert L_Z e^{uL} A\rVert \\
