&\le \lVert A\rVert\, g |X| \sum_{k\ge m} (b u)^{k}/k!.
\end{aligned}
$$

There is no count of sites in the outside region and no growth assumption on graph spheres. All bounds are uniform in finite volume. Duhamel's identity is

$$
\begin{aligned}
(e^{tL}-e^{tL_\Omega}) A \\
&= \int_0^t e^{(t-u)L_\Omega} (L-L_\Omega) e^{uL} A\, du.
\end{aligned}
$$

Contractivity and the preceding estimate prove (1), with the integral bounded by $t$ times the series at $t$. Finally $1_{k\ge m}\le\exp(\theta(k-m))$ proves (2).

###### Retained algebras need not be invariant term by term

If the actual local summands act on the ambient matrix algebra and only the full evolution preserves the retained tensor subalgebra, the truncated evolution need not preserve it. This does not invalidate localization. At each site take the normalized-trace-preserving conditional expectation $P_{x}$ from the ambient matrix algebra onto $A_{x}$, and put $P=\bigotimes_x P_x$. This is UCP, contractive, fixes $A$, and preserves every tensor support. For a retained input with $e^{tL}A$ retained,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert e^{tL}A - P(e^{tL_\Omega}A)\rVert \\
&\le \lVert e^{tL}A - e^{tL_\Omega}A\rVert.
\end{aligned}
$$

The approximant is now retained and $\Omega_R$-local. No compatibility of these expectations between stages is needed. If instead the summands are supported Lindblad generators directly on the retained tensor algebra, $P$ is unnecessary. An unspecified ambient GKLS extension without the same local support/strength bounds is not enough.

##### 2. Why these are the actual inherited finite-range constants

Proposition F.1 supplies graph diameter $r_{0}$, local norm $J$, degree $z_*$, and at most $\nu$ terms per site, all independent of $n$ (source lines 27–70). Therefore $g\le\nu J$ and $s$ depends only on $r_0,z_*$. Formula (1) follows directly from these printed constants.

Alternatively, under a genuinely uniform finite range, the two original unweighted F.0(1) sums give $g\le 2J_{H}+J_{D}$, in its written clock convention $L=i[H,\cdot]+D$. This uses $\lVert i[h,\cdot]\rVert\le 2\lVert h\rVert$ and requires the dissipative decomposition to consist of actual supported local Lindblad generators so that term deletion is contractive. For a convention with explicit $\hbar$, use $2J_H/\hbar$. No bound on the number of terms is needed in this aggregate version.

The finite-range cardinality estimate $|Z|\le s$ is derived from bounded degree. In particular a size-weighted norm, if displayed, would be a conclusion

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sup_x \sum_{Z\ni x} |Z|\, \ell_Z \exp(\mu \operatorname{diam} Z) \\
&\le s \exp(\mu r)\, g,
\end{aligned}
$$

not a strengthened premise. This deduction cannot be exported to arbitrary unbounded-range exponential summands.

F.0c(5) imports F.0a, whose item 3 references uniform locality constants compatible with Proposition F.1. The theorem applies to the inherited finite-range realization using that actual tuple. A different exponential certificate must be judged on its own exact locality theorem and domain. F.0c(6) explicitly imports Corollary F.1's support-prefactor hypotheses, including $\log|X_n|=o(a_n^{-1})$. Mosco convergence of the separate Hilbert-space forms does not replace these observable-generator conditions (F.0c(3), F.0d proof).

##### 3. Zero physical motion on the literal event-tensor branch

Fix an old retained observable $a$, with cofinally consistent representatives $A_{n}$ and actual finite event support $F$ in the limit. Assume the original event-localizing comparison really identifies graph neighborhoods with the same event metric $\rho$: for each fixed $\epsilon>0$, one can choose

$$
R_n = \epsilon/(2K a_n)
$$

so that all vertices in the $R_{n}$ graph-neighborhood of supp $A_{n}$ have limiting labels in $F_{\epsilon}$, for all sufficiently large n. A sufficient comparison is that representatives lie at the labels F and every graph edge has rho-length at most K $a_{n}$ + a compatible vanishing error; an error must be uniform on the paths used, not merely pointwise per edge. The source's actual registered metric comparison must discharge this statement. Abstract algebra isometry alone does not.

Suppose also $\log|\operatorname{supp} A_n|=o(a_n^{-1})$, the local constants are uniform in the physical clock, and the identified embedded observable evolutions converge in norm to $T_{t}a$. For fixed $T$, $\epsilon$ and $\theta>0$, formula (2) gives uniformly for $0\le t\le T$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{distance}\bigl(\iota_n(e^{tL_n} A_n), A(F_\epsilon)\bigr) \\
&\le |X_n|\, g T \lVert a\rVert \exp\bigl(b T e^{\theta} - \theta \lfloor R_n/r\rfloor\bigr) \to 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

The retained conditional-expectation correction in Section 1 makes the approximant embeddable even when the truncated ambient evolution is not retained. Actual region/event-preserving embeddings put it in the same closed target $A(F_{\epsilon})$. Taking norm limits yields $T_{t}a$ in $A(F_{\epsilon})$ for every $\epsilon>0$. The independent-tensor support intersection identity gives

$$
T_t a \in \bigcap_{\epsilon>0} A(F_\epsilon) = A(F).
\tag{3*}
$$

Coincident vertices may be grouped; no bound on their dimension or multiplicity is used except the stated representative support prefactor. Whenever the estimate is available on a dense set of inputs in a particular support algebra $A(Y)$, contractivity extends it to that algebra. Global core density alone does not assert this relative density for every arbitrary $Y$. For the time-slice obstruction it suffices to apply (3*) to each actual finite-event slice-core input, with the support-growth condition verified for its cofinally consistent representatives. The proof applies to each joint observable, so it does not infer product invariance from singleton invariance.

This conclusion is obtained for every fixed finite physical time. There is no appeal to $S$, no center loophole, and no need for the finite-core Banach theorem. The formal F.0(2) velocities can still be chosen inflated with $a_n v_n\to c>0$: an upper-bound velocity is not an attained response velocity. Such an inflated estimate does not contradict the sharper zero-motion conclusion.

###### Nontriviality and response are different

Unital isometric embeddings cannot send a nonscalar old observable to a scalar: distance to scalar multiples of 1 is preserved. A nontrivial event factor therefore remains nontrivial. If $b=b^*$ at an omitted event has spectral diameter $\Delta>0$, two product states agreeing on a proper slice and taking $b$ to its spectral endpoints give

$$
\operatorname{dist}(b, A(\mathrm{slice})) \ge \Delta/2.
$$

By (3*) all evolved genuinely localized slice-core inputs covered by the representative condition remain in $A(\text{slice})$; their generated algebra has the same obstruction. Thus the localized time-slice norm-density premise fails whenever the diamond contains such an omitted independent event. This is a nontriviality gap, not a lower bound on dynamical response.

Conversely a propagating-response contradiction would require an actual normalized witness with $\operatorname{distance}(T_t a,A(F_{\epsilon}))\ge\delta>0$, or an equivalent verified response lower bound in the same metric and clock. Neither isometric embeddings nor the upper-bound slope $a_n v_n\to c$ supplies $\delta$. The preceding slice contradiction uses the expressly localized time-slice generation premise instead and does not invent such a response floor.

##### 4. Full ambient LR testing: what it proves, and what is printed

At a finite stage, let $E_{\Omega}$ average conjugation over all unitaries in the full ambient complement matrix algebra. For any retained evolved A,

$$
\lVert A-E_\Omega A\rVert \le \sup_{u \text{ ambient complement unitary}} \lVert [A,u]\rVert.
$$

$E_{\Omega}$ is partial trace on the complement, so it maps an independent retained tensor algebra back into its Omega-local retained algebra, even when its factors have centers. If F.0(2)'s uniform estimate genuinely covers those ambient probes, the right side has the asserted LR tail and gives quasi-local norm approximation immediately. A complement unitary can have very large support; the support-independent constant printed in F.0(2) is important here. A theorem carrying an uncontrolled probe-support factor cannot be substituted.

Alternatively one can average one whole event factor at a time, pass to the fixed closed algebra omitting that event, then intersect over omitted labels. This avoids summing over all complement sites. A single-site estimate is insufficient for an event containing many registers unless the corresponding event-block estimate or an error summation is certified.

The generic printed quantifiers do not unambiguously provide these cross-domain tests:

- F.2 defines $A_n(F)$ as $\bigotimes\operatorname{Alg}(B_v)$, not expressly the full matrix tensor product.
- Proposition F.1 explicitly declares $A\in A_n(X)$, $B\in A_n(Y)$.
- F.0(2) closes with “the local representatives entering the net”.
- Corollary F.1 requires norm-convergent embedded representatives for both $A_{n}$ and $B_{n}$.

Thus proper retained centers cannot be eliminated merely by reinterpreting these B's as arbitrary ambient matrices. However an actual full-ambient supported Lindblad realization satisfying Proposition F.1's tuple gives the direct theorem in Section 1, without needing that reinterpretation. A certified full-ambient exponential LR theorem would also give the averaging route at its actual hypotheses.

##### A. Exact point pinning is already forced on the literal tensor realization

F.1 assigns each finite-stage vertex its actual emergent location $p_n(v)$. F.2's independent tensor realization gives $A_n(O)$ by those labels. F.0(3) preserves every retained region. With all small bounded diamonds retained, those diamonds separate any two distinct labels. For $b$ in the entire stage-$n$ factor at label $x$,

$$
j_n^m b \in \bigcap_{O\ni x} A_m(O) = A_m(\{x\}).
$$

The equality follows by finite-stage tensor expectations and separation of labels. Thus old factors are pinned exactly to x, not merely to shrinking neighborhoods. All microscopic registers at x must be treated as one whole-point factor; their count may grow. Unital isometry prevents collapse of a nonscalar old factor to the scalar algebra.

This proof uses no graph-distance estimate. It also does not require every later vertex label to have existed earlier. Distinct old whole-point factors remain tensor independent at every common later stage; their inductive tensor product is the actual limit algebra. These are deductions from F.1/F.2/F.0(3), not a new embedding axiom. If the region family does not include a separating neighborhood basis, the same argument identifies only the equivalence classes indistinguishable by that family. F.1's literal all-small-diamond realization has the separating property.

##### B. The support-growth condition need NOT hold for consistent representatives

The simplest limit proof uses consistent representatives. That hypothesis is stronger than necessary and is not an extra source demand.

F.0c(6) imports the uniform hypotheses of Corollary F.1. That corollary states both $\log|X_n|=o(a_n^{-1})$ and that every element of every limiting local algebra has a uniformly bounded norm-approximating regional representative sequence satisfying its support-growth condition. These representatives need not be the cofinally consistent ones used for generator convergence.

The difference is harmless. Suppose an old element $a$ has consistent representatives $A_{n}$ and region-local $B_{n}$ satisfy $\iota_n B_n\to a$. Isometry gives

$$
\lVert B_n-A_n\rVert = \lVert \iota_n B_n-a\rVert \to 0.
$$

Consequently, by contraction and the certified convergence for $A_{n}$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert \iota_n \alpha_n(t) B_n - T_t a\rVert \\
&\le \lVert \iota_n B_n-a\rVert + \lVert \iota_n \alpha_n(t) A_n-T_t a\rVert \to 0,
\end{aligned}
$$

uniformly for t in compact positive intervals. Convergence on the graph core extends first to every fixed old element by the same contraction/density argument. This comparison concerns semigroups, not convergence of generators on $B_{n}$.

To recover an old point observable $a_{x}$, choose any small diamond $U$ around $x$ and use the corollary's $B_{n}$ in $A_n(U)$. The norm-localization theorem places its evolution arbitrarily near $U$ in the positive geometric metric. Shrink $U$ to $x$. This proves point support invariance without any bound on the number of registers in the consistent $A_{n}$.

For an old joint observable a supported at finitely many labels F, approximate a in norm by a finite sum of elementary tensors of whole-point observables. For each tensor factor choose growth-controlled representatives in a small diamond around its own label. Form the same finite sums/products in a common stage. Their embeddings converge in norm to the chosen tensor sum. Their microscopic support is contained in the finite union of the factor supports; a finite sum of subexponential cardinalities is subexponential. Norms remain bounded, since each finite product is norm bounded. Apply the localization theorem to this joint representative, then let the tensor-sum approximation error tend to zero. No multiplicativity of the dynamics is used.

Thus the inherited regional representative hypothesis is sufficient for *all* finite-event old observables and their norm completions. A separate growth certificate for every actual slice-core consistent sequence is unnecessary. In particular every genuinely localized finite-event slice-core input is covered.

##### C. What the physical metric comparison supplies

Three original records must be read together, with their actual common sequence, not just similarly named symbols:

1. Definition 35 defines the positive propagation metric on the actual MPU graph by edge lengths $\delta_n w_e$, with $0<w_{\min}\le w_e\le w_{\max}<\infty$. Therefore

   $$
   d_{\mathrm{phys},n}(u,v) \le \delta_n w_{\max} d_{\mathrm{graph},n}(u,v).
   $$

2. Theorem 43.5 and Theorem 44 take the common normalized propagation metric to a positive measured-GH limit. Theorem 44 expressly uses the propagation metric that already includes the microscopic length, and interpolation discrepancy tends to zero on bounded sets. On a bounded window a GH comparison $p_{n}$ has additive distortion $\eta_n\to 0$:

   $$
   d_\infty(p_n u,p_n v) \le d_{\mathrm{phys},n}(u,v)+\eta_n.
   $$

3. F.1 uses the vertices' actual emergent locations for its regional algebras; Corollary F.1 calls $a_{n}$ the physical length represented by one graph edge. On this actual common-metric interpretation, the physical mesh calibration gives $\delta_n w_{\max}\le Ka_{n}$ for a fixed $K$, with $K$ absorbing bounded edge-cost calibration. It follows that

   $$
   d_\infty(p_n u,p_n v) \le K a_n d_{\mathrm{graph},n}(u,v)+\eta_n.
   \tag{A}
   $$

The additive GH error is applied once to the endpoints. It is NOT summed once per edge. Hence no rate $\eta_n=o(a_n)$ is necessary.

For $B_{n}$ supported at labels in $U$ and $R_n=\epsilon/(2K a_n)$, every vertex within $R_{n}$ graph edges is in $U_{\epsilon}$ for all large $n$. This is exactly the neighborhood comparison assumed in Section 3. It includes labels timelike separated in the subsequently promoted Lorentzian structure, because $d_{\mathrm{infty}}$ is the original positive four-dimensional metric. Theorem 43.5(5) selects one of these four directions as temporal; it does not discard that direction or replace it by an independent clock.

Therefore, when “actual emergent locations,” “physical mesh,” and the imported common geometric convergence record mean the same maps and edge scale as stated, (A) is a deduction. No new cone-support S, interaction weighting, or response-floor hypothesis is involved. On that literal common-metric branch the norm-localization proof closes: take limits, shrink U and $\epsilon$, and intersect independent tensor support algebras to obtain

$$
T_t A(F) \subset A(F),\quad \text{every finite } F \text{ and every finite } t\ge 0.
$$

Contractivity and the finite-tensor density give invariance of $A(Y)$ for arbitrary label sets $Y$.

###### Exact limitation of a weaker reading

The spacelike-margin inequality in the locality step of the proof of Theorem F.0, taken *alone*, is not (A). It compares spacelike regional pairs and gives no estimate for graph neighborhoods crossing timelike labels. Likewise abstract measured-GH convergence guarantees the existence of comparison maps, but does not identify an unrelated chosen location map with them. Finally “$a_n\to 0$” by itself does not compare $a_{n}$ with $\delta_{n}$.

Thus a record supplying only the spacelike inequality, an unlabelled metric-limit existence statement, and an unrelated mesh sequence has not supplied the actual common-metric interpretation above. The missing items can be stated exactly: its regional location maps must be the geometric comparison maps (up to uniformly vanishing error), and its LR mesh must be the actual bounded-cost edge scale. These are identifications inherent in the literal common-source reading; they are not conclusions from the scalar spacelike-margin formula. A source that declines these identifications is outside the proved common-metric realization, rather than a counterexample to it.

##### D. Time-slice endpoint

F.0(6) requires norm density of the algebra generated by the evolved slice core. It does not separately define the localization of that core. On its genuinely localized meaning, every input belongs to the algebra of a Cauchy neighborhood $S$ (or the slice itself where defined). The invariance above puts every evolved input in $A(S)$, including joint inputs. If a nontrivial independent event $y$ of the diamond is omitted from $S$, choose a self-adjoint $b$ at $y$ with spectral diameter $\Delta>0$. Two product states agreeing on $S$ and attaining the extreme spectral values at $y$ prove

$$
\operatorname{dist}(b,A(S)) \ge \Delta/2 > 0.
$$

Hence evolved-slice norm density is impossible. This is exact and needs no lower bound on propagation response. It is also not a claim that every nontrivial diamond has an off-slice event on every imaginable degenerate label realization: the omitted nontrivial event must be present. On the literal region-filling nontrivial MPU event net and every-Cauchy-neighborhood demand, choose a proper neighborhood omitting such an event. Treating a future-event operator as an input to the slice core would abandon this localized meaning.

The fully explicit neighborhood formulation occurs separately in F.10.2(3): it requires the evolved algebraic core of every Cauchy-surface neighborhood to be dense in its causal development. That wording supports the localized application, but the quotient/comparison theorem must not automatically be imposed on an unrelated F.0 construction. If someone formalizes F.0(6) with a nonlocal “slice core,” the exact unresolved original wording is the localization of that core, not a failure of norm localization or an absent response floor.

##### Resulting classification

For the original Mosco branch actually inheriting Proposition F.1's uniform finite-range tuple, F.0c(6)'s regional representative hypotheses, the literal common geometric maps/edge scale of F.1 and the geometric promotion, and genuinely localized time-slice generation, the direct norm-localization theorem proves the negative classification without S. The old finite-event representative pinning and the needed representative-growth coverage are deductions, not open extra conditions. The common-metric graph-neighborhood estimate follows from the actual GH comparison and bounded edge calibration; it is not derived from spacelike commutators.

A broader syntactic reading that withholds the common location/mesh identification or leaves “slice core” nonlocal remains underdetermined at those exact clauses. The general exponential alternative is not universally upgraded to the finite-range tuple. Theorem F.0y supplies a norm-localization theorem for that alternative under the precone hypothesis (F.0y.2), with the same common-metric and localized-slice readings and without a finite-range or weighted-tail estimate.

<a id="proposition-f0p-retained-commutator-and-ambient-termwise-countermodels"></a>**Proposition F.0p (Retained-Commutator and Ambient-Termwise Countermodels).**

##### 5. Exact coverage obstruction, not an all-original counterexample

For the retained diagonal algebra of two qubits x,y, let

$$
\begin{aligned}
K_{x,y}&=|y,y\rangle\langle x,y|, & E(A)&=\sum_{x,y} K_{x,y}^{*} A K_{x,y}, \\
L&=\lambda(E-I), & T_t&=e^{-\lambda t}I+(1-e^{-\lambda t})E.
\end{aligned}
$$

The Kraus operators satisfy $\sum K^* K=I$; $E^{2}=E$. This is a full ambient UCP semigroup preserving the diagonal algebra. It has

$$
T_t Z_x=e^{-\lambda t}Z_x+(1-e^{-\lambda t})Z_y.
$$

All retained commutators vanish, while the ambient probe $X_{y}$ gives norm $2(1-e^{-\lambda t})$. The distance from the evolved observable to the $x$-local diagonal algebra is exactly $1-e^{-\lambda t}$: for fixed $x$, take half the difference between its values at $y=0$ and $y=1$; deleting the $Z_{y}$ term attains the bound.

This is an exact norm obstruction to retained-commutator-to-support reconstruction. It is not an F01 common-source, metric, Mosco or time-slice counterexample. If $x,y$ become separated by order $1/a_n$ graph edges while $\lambda$ stays fixed, this single summand violates the inherited fixed-range tuple. Calling it exponentially local requires a separately verified tail convention; its existence does not refute Section 1.

##### 1. One sequence and one clock

For $k\ge 0$ put $n=2^{k}$. Take the path with vertices

$$
V_n=\{j/n: 0\le j\le n\},
$$

edges between consecutive labels, graph distance $d_{n}$, physical mesh $a_n=1/n$, and actual positive location metric $\rho(x,y)=|x-y|$. The endpoints $a=0$ and $b=1$ persist. The graph degree is at most two and

$$
\rho(x,y)=a_n d_n(x,y).
$$

At every vertex put a qubit. The ambient algebra is $M_n=\bigotimes_{x\in V_n} M_2$ and the retained algebra is its entire diagonal tensor algebra $D_n=\bigotimes_{x\in V_n}\mathbb{C}^{2}$. Embeddings at dyadic refinement append identities at the new labels. They are coherent unital isometric *-monomorphisms and preserve every region defined by the actual labels. No factor moves or collapses to scalars.

Let $\lambda>0$ be fixed in the physical time unit, independently of n. No accelerated clock or rescaling of the generator is used.

##### 2. Distinct genuine ambient interaction supports

Let $I_n=V_n\setminus\{a,b\}$; it has $n-1$ elements. For EVERY subset $S$ of $I_{n}$, define

$$
\begin{aligned}
Z_S&=\{a,b\} \cup S,\qquad M_{n,\mathrm{count}}=2^{n-1}, \\
E_S&=\operatorname{Ad}(W_{ab}) \otimes \Bigl(\bigotimes_{x\in S} D_x\Bigr) \otimes \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{elsewhere}}, \\
L_{n,Z_S}&=(\lambda/M_{n,\mathrm{count}})(E_S-\mathrm{id}).
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $W_{ab}$ is the unitary swapping the two endpoint qubits, $\operatorname{Ad}(W_{ab})(A)=W_{ab}^* A W_{ab}$, and $D_{x}$ is complete dephasing in the $Z$ basis. These factors act on disjoint tensor components and commute. The notation $M_{n,\mathrm{count}}$ distinguishes the number of terms from the ambient matrix algebra $M_{n}$.

Every $E_{S}$ is UCP and trace preserving, so $E_S-\mathrm{id}$ is a legitimate bounded Heisenberg Poisson-jump Lindblad generator: for Kraus operators $K_{j}$ of $E_{S}$, its standard GKLS expression is

$$
\sum_j K_j^{*} A K_j - (1/2)\Bigl\{\sum_j K_j^{*} K_j,A\Bigr\}=E_S(A)-A.
$$

Thus each local summand separately generates a UCP semigroup and annihilates 1.

The minimal AMBIENT tensor support of $L_{n,Z_S}$ is exactly $Z_{S}$. For $x\in S$,

$$
L_{n,Z_S}(X_x)=-(\lambda/M_{n,\mathrm{count}})X_x,
$$

whereas a unital local generator supported away from x must annihilate every x-only observable. For endpoints,

$$
\begin{aligned}
L_{n,Z_S}(Z_a)&=(\lambda/M_{n,\mathrm{count}})(Z_b-Z_a), \\
L_{n,Z_S}(Z_b)&=(\lambda/M_{n,\mathrm{count}})(Z_a-Z_b).
\end{aligned}
$$

Hence neither endpoint can be removed. Outside $Z_{S}$ the map acts identically at channel level and trivially at generator level. All $2^{n-1}$ supports are distinct. Different subsets give different superoperators, as the $X_{x}$ test distinguishes them. This is not repetition of the same ambient interaction under different names.

The operator norm is exactly

$$
\lVert L_{n,Z_S}\rVert_{\infty\to\infty}=2\lambda/M_{n,\mathrm{count}}.
$$

The upper bound follows from $\lVert E_S\rVert=1$. For equality use $A=(Z_a-Z_b)/2$ of norm 1: $E_S A=-A$, so $(E_S-\mathrm{id})A=-2A$.

##### 3. Original-strength bounds and precisely termwise exponential decay

Every $Z_{S}$ contains both endpoints, so $\operatorname{diam}_{\mathrm{graph}}(Z_S)=n$. The endpoint aggregate norms are exactly

$$
\sum_{Z\ni a} \lVert L_{n,Z}\rVert = \sum_{Z\ni b} \lVert L_{n,Z}\rVert =2\lambda.
$$

Each interior vertex lies in half the subsets, giving aggregate $\lambda$. Thus

$$
\sup_n \sup_x \sum_{Z\ni x} \lVert L_{n,Z}\rVert \le 2\lambda.
$$

Set $H_{n}=0$ and use these as dissipative summands. This is precisely an unweighted dissipative per-site norm bound of the printed F.0(1) shape. For any fixed $0<\mu\le\log 2$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert L_{n,Z_S}\rVert&=4\lambda \exp(-(\log 2)n) \\
&\le 4\lambda \exp(-\mu \operatorname{diam}_{\mathrm{graph}} Z_S).
\end{aligned}
$$

There is therefore a uniform TERMWISE exponential diameter bound with genuine ambient minimal supports.

This does NOT give an aggregate exponential tail. For every $R<n$,

$$
\sum_{Z\ni a,\ \operatorname{diam} Z>R} \lVert L_{n,Z}\rVert=2\lambda.
$$

Likewise, for every $\mu>0$,

$$
\sum_{Z\ni a} \exp(\mu \operatorname{diam} Z)\lVert L_{n,Z}\rVert=2\lambda \exp(\mu n),
$$

and the size-weighted version is exactly

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{Z\ni a} |Z| \exp(\mu \operatorname{diam} Z)\lVert L_{n,Z}\rVert \\
&=\lambda(n+3)\exp(\mu n),
\end{aligned}
$$

since the average subset size is $(n-1)/2$ and $|Z|=2+|S|$. The incidence count at an endpoint is $M_{n,\mathrm{count}}$ and the range is $n$. The inherited Proposition F.1 fixed-range/incidence hypotheses therefore fail explicitly.

##### 4. Retained dynamics and exact norm nonlocality

Dephasing fixes every diagonal observable. On $D_{n}$ all $E_{S}$ restrict to the same endpoint-swap automorphism $S_{ab}$. Therefore the total retained generator is exactly

$$
L_n|_{D_n}=\lambda(S_{ab}-\mathrm{id}),\qquad S_{ab}^{2}=\mathrm{id}.
$$

In the physical clock,

$$
\begin{aligned}
T_t|_{D_n}&=p(t)\,\mathrm{id}+q(t)S_{ab}, \\
p(t)&=(1+\exp(-2\lambda t))/2, \\
q(t)&=(1-\exp(-2\lambda t))/2.
\end{aligned}
$$

In particular

$$
T_t Z_a=p(t)Z_a+q(t)Z_b.
$$

For every fixed $t>0$ and every retained region U containing a but not b,

$$
\operatorname{dist}(T_t Z_a,D_n(U))=q(t)>0.
\tag{1}
$$

The upper bound follows by deleting $q(t)Z_b$. For the lower bound, fix every bit in $U$, and compare two configurations differing only at $b$. Any $U$-local approximant has the same value on them, while $T_t Z_a$ differs by $2q(t)$. The maximum approximation error is at least $q(t)$. This argument also works in the limit tensor algebra.

Thus there is macroscopic center-sensitive dependence across distance $\rho(a,b)=1$ at every positive physical time, with a fixed normalized witness and explicit response $q(t)$. This lower bound is PROVED for this countermodel; it is not inferred from nontriviality in the general theory.

All retained commutators are zero. Consequently the printed F.0(2) inequality on retained $A,B$ holds for any $C>0$, $\mu_n=\mu_0>0$, and prescribed finite $c>0$ with $v_n=c n$. Then $a_n v_n=c$ exactly. This is a valid upper-bound record, not attainment or a support-cone certificate. For $t<1/c$, (1) is incompatible with a genuine speed-$c$ support cone.

Ambient probes expose the failure: with $B=X_b$,

$$
\lVert [T_t Z_a,X_b]\rVert=2q(t)=1-\exp(-2\lambda t).
$$

A full-ambient sharp LR bound with $\mu_n\ge\mu_0$ and $v_n=c n$ would tend to zero at fixed $0<t<1/c$, contradicting this identity. Hence the example also precisely distinguishes retained from ambient LR test domains.

##### 5. Global embedding, semigroup, state, and detailed balance are exact

The refinement embeddings intertwine the retained generators and semigroups exactly, since the same two endpoint labels are swapped at every stage. The inductive-limit retained algebra is the independent tensor algebra over all dyadic labels in [0,1]. The bounded generator

$$
L=\lambda(S_{ab}-\mathrm{id})
$$

has norm 2lambda and generates a norm-continuous UCP semigroup. Every embedded finite retained evolution already equals the limit on its input. Global generator/semigroup comparison errors are zero, hence summable. The algebraic finite-support union is a graph core because L is bounded.

There is even exact GLOBAL ambient compatibility. Averaging all subsets gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\bar{E}_n&=(1/M_{n,\mathrm{count}})\sum_S E_S \\
&=\operatorname{Ad}(W_{ab}) \otimes \Bigl(\bigotimes_{x\in I_n} Q_x\Bigr), \\
Q_x&=(\mathrm{id}+D_x)/2, \\
L_n&=\lambda(\bar{E}_n-\mathrm{id}).
\end{aligned}
$$

When an old ambient observable is embedded, every new $Q_{x}$ acts on the identity. Thus $\bar{E}_m j_n^m=j_n^m\bar{E}_n$, and the same holds for generators and semigroups. These compatible contractions define the corresponding ambient product channel and bounded generator on the infinite quasi-local algebra. This stronger global fact is not regional support invariance.

The normalized product traces are faithful at every finite stage, compatible with the embeddings, and stationary. Each $D_{x}$ is an orthogonal projection for the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product, $\operatorname{Ad}(W_{ab})$ is self-adjoint there because $W_{ab}=W_{ab}^*=W_{ab}^{-1}$, and they commute. Therefore each $E_{S}$ and each $L_{n,Z_S}$ is Hilbert-Schmidt self-adjoint. Both ambient and retained generators satisfy tracial detailed balance. The compatible product state in the limit is faithful as well: the finite-tensor trace expectations are faithful and approximate local observables in norm, or equivalently use the faithful product-trace representation of this UHF tensor algebra.

##### 6. Minimal-support convention audit: the decisive limitation

The preceding support certificate is AMBIENT. Restricted to $D_{n}$, every summand has minimal support only {a,b}; the spectator dephasings become invisible. If the interaction convention requires every retained superoperator to be indexed by its minimal RETAINED support and combines equal supports, then all terms merge into the single retained interaction

$$
L_{a,b}=\lambda(S_{ab}-\mathrm{id}),\qquad \lVert L_{a,b}\rVert=2\lambda,
$$

at graph diameter n. It fails any uniform termwise bound C exp(-mu n), $\mu>0$. Under that convention this is NOT a retained-termwise-exponential example.

If “supported on Z” means only acts trivially outside Z, rather than minimal support, the retained restricted terms can still be indexed by the ambient $Z_{S}$, but the retained labeling is padded. The construction avoids this padding at the physical ambient level: there every spectator is detectably acted on, every $Z_{S}$ is minimal, and no two terms coincide. It does not pretend that this ambient distinction survives diagonal restriction.

Thus the exact theorem furnished by this example is:

bounded-degree graph + full ambient local GKLS decomposition with
genuine distinct supports + uniform unweighted per-site norm sum +
uniform TERMWISE ambient exponential diameter decay + exact global
coherent isometric embeddings + physical-clock norm convergence +
faithful tracial detailed balance + retained commutator LR

DO NOT imply retained center-sensitive norm localization or an aggregate weighted exponential norm.

It is not a theorem about a convention requiring minimal retained supports, and it is not a counterexample to an aggregate-tail definition of exponential locality. These distinctions must be specified before using the example to interpret the generic F.0(1) phrase “exponential decay.”

##### 7. Other original gates deliberately not claimed

- The actual generator is not regional-support preserving: a region containing a but not b cannot carry the restriction of the full evolution on $Z_{a}$. Therefore global projectivity does not establish F.0(3)'s full regional dynamics/restriction package.
- The path continuum is one-dimensional, not the noncollapsed RCD*(K,4) Mosco/geometry branch. No assertion of F.0c geometry or common Cheeger/full-Heisenberg identification is made.
- Literal center-sensitive F.0(4) fails by (1). Retained commutator LR cannot be passed off as a certificate of it.
- The entire localized time-slice requirement is not verified. No complete original positive alternative is claimed.
- No endpoint-only or uniformly local-home auxiliary construction is invoked; these are large genuine ambient interaction supports.
- The strength and graph are common and the physical clock is fixed. The failure cannot be blamed on a hidden clock acceleration, a nonisometric quotient, scalar collapse, or duplicated identical ambient terms.

<a id="theorem-f0v-exact-small-region-norm-gap-in-car"></a>**Theorem F.0v (Exact Small-Region Norm Gap in CAR).**

Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, $F=\mathrm{CAR}(H)$, and $P_j$ orthogonal projections with $P_j\to 0$ strongly. Put $K_j=P_jH$ and $F_j=\mathrm{CAR}(K_j)$, all viewed as the canonical unital subalgebras of $F$. Then, for every fixed $A\in F$,

$$
\lim_j \operatorname{dist}(A,F_j) = \operatorname{dist}(A,\mathbb{C} 1).
\tag{F.0v.1}
$$

The projections need not be nested. In particular, if they are nested with strong limit zero,

$$
\bigcap_j F_j = \mathbb{C} 1.
\tag{F.0v.2}
$$

The same distance limit and intersection statement hold for any unital subalgebras $B_j\subset F_j$, including the local even or compact-gauge-fixed CAR subalgebras.

##### Proof: the actual CAR expectations, including odd operators

For every closed subspace K of H there is a trace-preserving UCP conditional expectation

$$
E_K : \mathrm{CAR}(H) \to \mathrm{CAR}(K).
$$

To obtain it without confusing CAR with an ordinary spatial tensor product, choose orthonormal bases of $K$ and $K^\perp$. This identifies the pair with the complementary mode-subset CAR inclusions. Araki–Moriya, Theorem 4.7, gives $E_{K}$ and the complementary expectation, with

$$
E_{K^{\perp}}(B) = \tau(B)\, 1,\quad B \in \mathrm{CAR}(K).
\tag{F.0v.3}
$$

The basis change is an exact CAR *-isomorphism used for this algebraic identity; the source's regional coordinates are unchanged. For the complementary expectation $E_{K^\perp}$, equivalently average the parity on $K$, then take the normalized-trace slice on the resulting even $K$ factor, as in that theorem. Odd $K$ operators have zero trace and are killed; no commutation between odd $K$ operators and odd complementary operators is used. The expectations are norm-one on the original C*-algebra, with no vacuum GNS quotient.

If $Q\in\mathrm{CAR}(K^\perp)$, contractivity and (F.0v.3) imply, for every $B\in\mathrm{CAR}(K)$,

$$
\lVert Q-B\rVert \ge \lVert Q-\tau(B)1\rVert \ge \operatorname{dist}(Q,\mathbb{C}1).
$$

The reverse inequality follows from $\mathbb{C}1\subset\mathrm{CAR}(K)$. Hence

$$
\operatorname{dist}(Q,\mathrm{CAR}(K)) = \operatorname{dist}(Q,\mathbb{C}1).
\tag{F.0v.4}
$$

Now approximate $A$ by a finite polynomial $Q$ in creators/annihilators smeared with $f_1,\dots,f_s$. Replace every smearing in precisely that polynomial by $(I-P_j)f_l$, obtaining $Q_j\in\mathrm{CAR}(K_j^\perp)$. The exact CAR norm identity and telescoping products show $\lVert Q_j-Q\rVert\to 0$. For example, for a monomial of degree $d$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Bigl\lVert \prod_l a^{\#}(f_l) - \prod_l a^{\#}((I-P_j)f_l)\Bigr\rVert \\
&\le \sum_l \lVert P_j f_l\rVert \prod_{k \ne l} \lVert f_k\rVert.
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $a^{\#}$ independently denotes creation or annihilation, and zero-norm factors cause no problem. By (F.0v.4) and the fact that distance to a closed set is 1-Lipschitz,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{dist}(A,F_j) \\
&\ge \operatorname{dist}(Q_j,\mathbb{C}1)-\lVert A-Q_j\rVert \\
&\ge \operatorname{dist}(A,\mathbb{C}1)-2\lVert A-Q_j\rVert.
\end{aligned}
$$

First let $j$ tend to infinity, then make the initial approximation $\lVert A-Q\rVert$ arbitrarily small. The upper bound $\operatorname{dist}(A,F_j)\le\operatorname{dist}(A,\mathbb{C}1)$ holds for every $j$, proving (F.0v.1). The scalar-intersection consequence is immediate. Finally

$$
\operatorname{dist}(A,F_j) \le \operatorname{dist}(A,B_j) \le \operatorname{dist}(A,\mathbb{C}1)
$$

proves the subnet claim. This proof is valid for non-self-adjoint, even and odd A alike. ∎

<a id="corollary-f0v1-no-point-factor-in-the-free-fermion-norm-net"></a>**Corollary F.0v.1 (No Point Factor in the Free-Fermion Norm Net).**

For the actual free Weyl-fermion and massive-Dirac Cauchy data, take

$$
\begin{aligned}
&H=L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{3},E),\quad P_r f=1_{B_r(x)} f, \\
&F(D(B_r(x)))=\mathrm{CAR}(L^{2}(B_r(x),E)),
\end{aligned}
$$

with the finite spin/species fibre $E$ of the source. Lebesgue measure has no atom at $x$, so $P_r\to 0$ strongly as $r\downarrow 0$. Consequently

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lim_{r \downarrow 0} \operatorname{dist}\bigl(A,F(D(B_r(x)))\bigr) &= \operatorname{dist}(A,\mathbb{C}1), \\
\bigcap_{r>0} F(D(B_r(x))) &= \mathbb{C}1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.0v.5}
$$

At any other time use the **same** fixed free-evolution CAR automorphism for the whole shrinking family. It preserves norm and scalars, so (F.0v.5) is unchanged. The compact spin-cylinder version is identical on a Cauchy ball whose measure shrinks to zero. No duality, split property, field-domain hypothesis or Haag–Kastler/Wightman promotion is used.

In the full filled-sea representation, CAR is represented faithfully: the CAR algebra is simple and its unital representation is nonzero (or use the explicit faithful CAR realization). Thus (F.0v.5) is also an operator-norm statement for the represented norm-CAR subalgebras. Restricting that faithful representation to an even or gauge-fixed subalgebra remains faithful. The statement concerns these C*-algebras; intersections of their vacuum von Neumann closures and nonfaithful sector compressions lie outside it.

<a id="corollary-f0v2-no-literal-old-event-norm-embedding-into-the-car-net"></a>**Corollary F.0v.2 (No Literal Old-Event Norm Embedding into the CAR Net).**

Suppose a nontrivial finite-dimensional event algebra $D$ at a fixed physical event $p$ is assigned by F.1/F.2 to every retained diamond containing $p$. Suppose one and the same unital injective *-map $\iota:D\to F$ sends it into the actual CAR local algebra of each such diamond. These are precisely the all-diamond point-locality and fixed-map premises needed here; a buffered cell assignment would not be this premise.

Choose a nontrivial projection $e\in D$, which exists in every nonscalar finite-dimensional C*-algebra, including a commutative one. Its image $q=\iota(e)$ is a projection different from 0 and 1, so

$$
\operatorname{dist}(q,\mathbb{C}1)=1/2.
$$

But the shrinking diamond family at $p$ gives $q\in F(D(B_r))$ for every $r$, in contradiction with (F.0v.5). Therefore no such map exists. The conclusion applies equally if the target is the even or gauge-invariant norm-CAR subnet.

Literal F.0(3) provides one fixed continuum image of every old-stage observable, because $\iota_m j_n^m=\iota_n$; it preserves each retained diamond. Definitions F.1/F.2 put the whole old event factor in every diamond containing its actual label. Hence the contradiction applies already at one nontrivial old event, before any generator, LR, state, form, clock or time-slice calculation. F.0o §A independently derives the analogous exact point pinning between finite stages.

There is also a robust approximate version: a fixed nontrivial limiting projection $q$ cannot have $\operatorname{dist}(q,F(D(B_r)))\to 0$; its limit is exactly 1/2. If source images $q_n\to q$ in norm and $r_n\to 0$, then $\operatorname{dist}(q_n,F(D(B_{r_n})))\to 1/2$. A shrinking packet can remain a nontrivial projection, but it cannot at the same time converge in norm to one fixed nontrivial point observable. Moving-observable response comparisons, finite-resolution buffered maps and comparison-quotient constructions lie outside these premises.

<a id="proposition-f0w-connected-geometric-symmetries-fix-independent-point-factors"></a>**Proposition F.0w (Connected Geometric Symmetries Fix Independent Point Factors).**

This is a second, CAR-independent obstruction on the literal tensor realization already identified by F.0o §A. Suppose

$$
\begin{aligned}
A&=\text{norm-}\bigotimes_{x\in X} A_x, \\
A(O)&=\text{norm-}\bigotimes_{x\in X \cap O} A_x,
\end{aligned}
$$

with independent event fibres, scalar identities outside the indicated set, and a separating basis of retained diamonds. Then

$$
\bigcap_{O\ni x} A(O)=A_x,
\tag{F.0w.1}
$$

where $A_x=\mathbb{C}1$ if $x$ has no event fibre. To see (F.0w.1), use product-state expectations onto finite event sets. For any fixed finite set $F$, finitely many diamonds around $x$ exclude every point of $F\setminus\{x\}$; the finite expectation of an element in the intersection therefore belongs to $A_{x}$. Those expectations converge in norm to the original element. No commutant-to-support or duality inference occurs.

Let a topological group G act geometrically, and let `beta_g` be point-norm continuous automorphisms with the exact regional transport required by F.0(7),

$$
\beta_g(A(O))=A(gO).
$$

If $0<p<1$ is a projection at event $x$, equation (F.0w.1) puts $\beta_g(p)$ in $A_{gx}$. When $gx\ne x$, its nontriviality and tensor independence imply

$$
\lVert\beta_g(p)-p\rVert=1.
\tag{F.0w.2}
$$

For the lower bound, take a product state with value 1 on $p$ and 0 on $\beta_g(p)$; the upper bound is the norm bound for a difference of projections. If $A_{gx}$ were scalar there could be no nontrivial image at all.

Point-norm continuity at the identity gives an identity neighborhood on which the left side of (F.0w.2) is less than 1. Every element of that neighborhood fixes x. Thus the stabilizer of x is an open subgroup, and the identity component of G fixes x. In particular a connected represented geometric group fixes every nontrivial event factor's label. The proof uses neighborhoods and needs no first-countability or sequential-continuity assumption.

This rules out nontrivial continuous geometric translations of the literal independent point-event norm net, independently of interaction strength or exponential convention. F.0(7) demands covariance for the group actually represented, so a trivial or discrete represented group is unconstrained by this proposition, and internal automorphisms may act at fixed labels.

##### Source of the CAR conditional expectations

Araki and Moriya (2003): §4.1 supplies the CAR polynomial algebra and finite matrix inclusions; Proposition 4.6 supplies the tracial product identity; Theorem 4.7 supplies C*-conditional expectations, including complementary scalar restriction; Corollary 4.8 records parity compatibility. The passage to arbitrary orthogonal subspaces is the explicit basis identification above. Formula (F.0v.1), its quantitative projection gap and the contradiction of Corollary F.0v.2 are proved here; the source supplies the cited conditional expectations.

<a id="theorem-f0x-minimal-retained-support-exponential-locality-countermodel"></a>**Theorem F.0x (Minimal-Retained-Support Exponential-Locality Countermodel).**

There is a sequence with all of the following:

1. bounded-degree shrinking-edge physical path graphs and coherent exact point-region-preserving tensor embeddings;
2. diagonal retained algebras and full ambient, individually GKLS interaction terms whose supports are distinct and **minimal on both the ambient and retained algebras**;
3. uniform per-site interaction-norm sums and uniform termwise exponential graph-diameter decay;
4. exact global generator/semigroup compatibility in the original fixed clock, compatible faithful trace states and tracial detailed balance;
5. the retained-commutator LR bound in F.0(2), with any prescribed positive physical upper-bound slope;
6. a fixed positive center-sensitive endpoint transport distance and hence failure of norm localization and aggregate-tail locality.

This strengthens the convention countermodel F.0p by removing its spectator-invisibility/minimal-retained-support limitation. Regional restrictions, a genuine causal support cone, four-dimensional Mosco geometry and time-slice generation lie outside the construction.

##### One actual finite construction

Let $n=2^k\ge 2$, $V_n=\{j/n:0\le j\le n\}$, with nearest-neighbor path edges, $a_n=1/n$, and locations in $[0,1]$. Let $a=0$, $b=1$, $I_n=V_n\setminus\{a,b\}$, and $M_n=2^{n-1}$. Put a qubit at each vertex, use the full matrix tensor algebra as ambient and its computational-basis diagonal tensor algebra $D_n$ as retained. Refinement keeps every old factor at the same dyadic label and appends identities.

For every subset $S\subset I_n$, define

$$
\begin{aligned}
U_S &= W_{ab} \prod_{x\in S} X_x, \\
E_S &= \operatorname{Ad}(U_S), \\
L_{n,S} &= (\lambda/M_n)(E_S-\mathrm{id}),\qquad \lambda>0 \text{ fixed}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.0x.1}
$$

$W_{ab}$ is the unitary exchanging the endpoint qubits. Each $X_{x}$ is the actual Pauli bit flip. Their supports are disjoint, so the factors commute and $U_{S}$ is a self-adjoint unitary. The sole jump $\sqrt{\lambda/M_n}\,U_S$ gives the displayed supported GKLS term. Every $E_{S}$ preserves $D_{n}$.

##### Minimal supports and exact norms

For each spectator x,

$$
L_{n,S}(Z_x) = \begin{cases} -2\lambda Z_x/M_n & \text{if } x\in S,\\ 0 & \text{if } x\notin S.\end{cases}
$$

For the endpoints,

$$
\begin{aligned}
L_{n,S}(Z_a)&=(\lambda/M_n)(Z_b-Z_a), \\
L_{n,S}(Z_b)&=(\lambda/M_n)(Z_a-Z_b).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.0x.2}
$$

A supported unital-at-identity generator omitting x annihilates every x-only observable. Therefore every listed site is indispensable **even after restriction to D_n**. The minimal support is exactly `{a,b} union S`. Distinct subsets give distinct retained superoperators, detected by $Z_{x}$. There is one term per support; no support padding and no duplicate-term subdivision is used.

Testing the norm-one diagonal observable $(Z_a-Z_b)/2$ shows, together with the difference-of-contractions upper bound,

$$
\lVert L_{n,S}\rVert_{\mathrm{ambient}} = \lVert L_{n,S}\rVert_{\mathrm{retained}} = 2\lambda/M_n.
$$

Every support has graph diameter n. Thus

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\lVert L_{n,S}\rVert=4\lambda \exp[-(\log 2)n], \\
&\sup_x \sum_{S:\, x\in \operatorname{support} L_{n,S}} \lVert L_{n,S}\rVert=2\lambda.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.0x.3}
$$

Interior sites have sum $\lambda$. This verifies exponential **termwise** diameter decay at rate log2 and exactly the unweighted per-site shape of F.0(1). The endpoint aggregate tail is 2lambda at distance n and does not decay.

##### Actual global dynamics, refinement and states

The sum has the explicit form

$$
\begin{aligned}
L_n&=\lambda(\bar{E}_n-\mathrm{id}), \\
\bar{E}_n&=\operatorname{Ad}(W_{ab}) \prod_{x\in I_n} Q_x, \\
Q_x&=(\mathrm{id}+\operatorname{Ad}(X_x))/2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.0x.4}
$$

Every $Q_{x}$ is UCP, norm one, trace preserving, and fixes the identity. Under dyadic refinement the newly introduced Q factors act only on appended identities, whereas the old Q factors are unchanged. Hence the full ambient equality

$$
\bar{E}_m\, j_n^m = j_n^m\, \bar{E}_n
$$

holds exactly; the same holds for $L$ and $\exp(tL)$, and in particular on $D_{n}$. These maps define a bounded UCP map $\bar{E}$ on the quasi-local norm inductive limit and $L=\lambda(\bar{E}-\mathrm{id})$, $\lVert L\rVert\le 2\lambda$. Its semigroup is the norm-convergent Poisson series. All embedded comparison errors are zero on the actual finite-support algebraic graph core, and therefore summable. The compatible product trace is faithful and invariant. Every $E_{S}$ is Hilbert–Schmidt self-adjoint because $U_{S}$ is an involution, so $L_{n}$ satisfies tracial detailed balance on ambient and retained algebras.

This compatibility is global; (F.0x.6) below shows that regional algebras are not invariant. Retained commutators vanish identically because all $D_{n}$ are commutative. Hence F.0(2)'s retained-test inequality holds with any positive constants $C,\mu$ and $v_n=cn$, giving $a_n v_n=c$.

On endpoint-only observables all $Q_{x}$ act trivially and Ebar acts by the endpoint swap. Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
T_t Z_a&=p(t)Z_a+q(t)Z_b, \\
p(t)&=(1+\exp(-2\lambda t))/2, \\
q(t)&=(1-\exp(-2\lambda t))/2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.0x.5}
$$

For any retained support set Y containing a but not b, two diagonal configurations agreeing on Y and differing only at b give

$$
\operatorname{dist}(T_t Z_a,D(Y))=q(t)>0,\quad t>0.
\tag{F.0x.6}
$$

Deleting the second term attains the upper bound; the half-spread of the two configurations gives the lower bound. The full ambient probe $X_{b}$ detects norm $2q(t)$, so a sharp physical LR bound for all ambient probes fails at fixed $0<t<1/c$. A genuine speed-$c$ support cone fails for the same reason.

##### Why regrouping or minimal-support convention cannot repair this example

Minimal retained supports are already used. Regrouping preserves the total active retained spectator action; it cannot replace the sum by an endpoint-only channel on $D_{n}$. In particular, for every interior $x$ the total $\bar{E}_n$ annihilates $Z_{x}$, whereas an endpoint-only channel fixes $Z_{x}$. More intrinsically, in **any** decomposition of the same retained generator into supported maps $K_{Z}$ with $K_Z(1)=0$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lambda &= \operatorname{dist}(L_n Z_a,D_n(V_n\setminus\{b\})) \\
&\le \sum_{Z\ni a,b} \lVert K_Z\rVert.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.0x.7}
$$

Indeed terms omitting $a$ vanish on $Z_{a}$, while terms omitting $b$ produce an element of the $b$-free retained algebra. Only terms meeting both endpoints can contribute to the quotient distance. Formula (F.0x.2) for the full sum gives $L_n Z_a=\lambda(Z_b-Z_a)$, whose quotient distance is $\lambda$. Thus the endpoint tail stays bounded below in **every** supported decomposition and cannot satisfy an aggregate exponential bound. The same argument uses ambient conditional expectation to give the ambient norm lower bound.

The construction proves that **minimal retained termwise locality plus the other displayed global controls does not supply genuine regional generator restriction, center-sensitive cone containment or an aggregate exponential tail**. It uses unbounded support cardinalities and exponentially growing incidence, so a uniform-arity, uniform-incidence or weighted-aggregate convention excludes it.

**Scope of Theorems F.0v/F.0x and Proposition F.0w.**

Corollary F.0v.2 excludes the norm-CAR target net under the literal all-diamond old-event geometry for every locality convention. Proposition F.0w excludes nontrivial connected geometric motion on the literal independent-point norm net. Norm-inductive point-event nets with trivial or discrete represented symmetries, and targets with additional point factors, are the subject of Theorem F.0y.

Theorem F.0x shows, with minimal retained supports, that termwise exponential decay and a retained-commutator bound do not supply the genuine causal support and regional restrictions of an affirmative package. Theorem F.0y takes that support requirement as its hypothesis (F.0y.2).

<a id="theorem-f0y-exact-precone-rigidity-of-event-tensor-norm-packages"></a>**Theorem F.0y (Exact-Precone Rigidity of Event-Tensor Norm Packages).** Let $X$ be a countable set of persistent event labels and let
$$
\mathcal A=\bigotimes_{x\in X}^{\min}\mathcal A_x,
\qquad
\mathcal A(Y)=\bigotimes_{x\in Y}^{\min}\mathcal A_x
\quad(Y\subseteq X),
\tag{F.0y.1}
$$
with identities at omitted factors and norm closure of the finite-event union. The unital event fibres may have centres and may be infinite AF algebras. Let $(T_t)_{t\ge0}$ be a strongly continuous semigroup of unital contractions on $\mathcal A$, with generator $L$ and a linear graph core $\mathcal C$ contained in the finite-event union. Suppose that for disjoint finite event sets $E,H$ there is $\delta(E,H)>0$ such that
$$
T_t\mathcal A(E)\subseteq\mathcal A(X\setminus H)
\qquad(0\le t<\delta(E,H)).
\tag{F.0y.2}
$$
The time bound is uniform over the whole source-support algebra $\mathcal A(E)$. This is norm-support exclusion, a stronger condition than commutation with retained target probes. Then
$$
T_t\mathcal A(Y)\subseteq\mathcal A(Y)
\qquad(Y\subseteq X,\ t\ge0).
\tag{F.0y.3}
$$
The theorem applies to general UCP dynamics, without trace preservation, an invariant state, a finite-dimensional completed fibre, a bound on the full generator, or a domain assumption on every old observable. On a reversible group branch with the corresponding precone for both signs of time, (F.0y.3) holds for all real times.

Application to the norm packages of Theorem F.0. Let a projective-single-clock or Mosco–Bochner norm package satisfy F.0(1)–(7) on the literal F.1/F.2 event-tensor realization, and assume:

(a) *Common location and mesh.* The regional location maps are the geometric comparison maps up to uniformly vanishing error, and the Lieb–Robinson mesh $a_n$ is the bounded-cost edge scale, so that (F.0y.12) holds on bounded windows.

(b) *Regional support precone.* For each bounded diamond $O$, the regional evolution $T_O$ satisfies (F.0y.2) for all disjoint finite event sets $E,H\subset O$ at positive $d_\infty$-distance.

(c) *Localized slice core.* For each Cauchy time-slice $\Sigma\subset O$, the slice core of F.0(6) is contained in the algebra of the event labels on $\Sigma$.

Then every retained event algebra is scalar: the package retains no nonconstant MPU event response. Hypothesis (b) follows from (a), F.0(2) and F.0(3) when every event fibre is a full matrix algebra at every stage; for retained fibres with nontrivial centre it is assumed. Under (b) no finite-range, aggregate-tail or interaction-arity convention is used. Hypotheses (a) and (c) are the common-metric and localized-slice readings of Theorem F.0o, sections C and D. The proof and the binding to Theorem F.0 follow.

#### I. Support expectations and differentiation only on the supplied domain

Choose any state $\rho_x$ on each event fibre. These are auxiliary mathematical states; they need not be faithful or invariant. Their product partial expectations $E_F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A(F)$, for finite $F$, are contractions, fix $\mathcal A(F)$, and satisfy
$$
E_F\mathcal A(Y)\subseteq\mathcal A(F\cap Y),\qquad
E_F\mathcal A(X\setminus H)\subseteq\mathcal A(F\setminus H).
\tag{F.0y.4}
$$
They converge pointwise in norm to the identity as $F$ exhausts $X$. These assertions follow on elementary tensors and extend by norm density. In particular,
$$
\mathcal A(F)\cap\mathcal A(Y)=\mathcal A(F\cap Y),\qquad
\bigcap_{y\notin F}\mathcal A(X\setminus\{y\})=\mathcal A(F).
\tag{F.0y.5}
$$
For the second identity, finite-coordinate expectations of an element in the intersection lie in $\mathcal A(K\cap F)$ for every finite $K$ and converge in norm to that element. No commutant-to-support inference is used. Contractivity also gives, for $a\in\mathcal A(F)$,
$$
\operatorname{dist}(a,\mathcal A(Y))
=\operatorname{dist}(a,\mathcal A(F\cap Y)).
\tag{F.0y.6}
$$
Indeed, applying $E_F$ to $a-b$, with $b\in\mathcal A(Y)$, gives the nontrivial inequality; the other follows from inclusion.

If $a\in\operatorname{Dom}L\cap\mathcal A(F)$, fix $y\notin F$. By (F.0y.2), the norm difference quotients $(T_ta-a)/t$ belong to the closed algebra $\mathcal A(X\setminus\{y\})$ for all sufficiently small positive $t$. Their norm limit $La$ belongs there too. Equation (F.0y.5) gives
$$
L\bigl(\operatorname{Dom}L\cap\mathcal A(F)\bigr)
\subseteq\mathcal A(F).
\tag{F.0y.7}
$$
Only observables already in the actual generator domain have been differentiated. No norm-Lipschitz orbit is asserted to belong to that domain, and no conditional expectation is assumed to preserve it.

#### II. The quotient dissipativity estimate

Fix any $Y\subseteq X$, and let $q:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A/\mathcal A(Y)$ be the Banach-space quotient map. The subalgebra need not be an ideal; this is not a C*-algebra quotient. Take $a\in\mathcal C\cap\mathcal A(F)$, with $F$ finite. Apply (F.0y.2) to $E=F\cap Y$ and $H=F\setminus Y$. For all sufficiently small $t\ge0$, the contractions
$$
S_t^F=E_FT_t|_{\mathcal A(F)}
\tag{F.0y.8}
$$
preserve $\mathcal A(F\cap Y)$ by (F.0y.4). Thus they induce contractions on $\mathcal A(F)/\mathcal A(F\cap Y)$; they need not form a semigroup. By (F.0y.7), $La\in\mathcal A(F)$, so
$$
E_FT_ta=a+tLa+o(t).
$$
The quotient contraction and (F.0y.6) imply
$$
\limsup_{t\downarrow0}
\frac{\|qa+tqLa\|-\|qa\|}{t}\le0.
\tag{F.0y.9}
$$
The real function $s\mapsto\|qa+s qLa\|$ is convex. Its left secant slope at zero is at most its nonpositive right derivative. Hence $\|qa-sqLa\|\ge\|qa\|$ for every $s>0$, or equivalently
$$
\|q(\lambda a-La)\|\ge\lambda\|qa\|
\qquad(a\in\mathcal C,\ \lambda>0).
\tag{F.0y.10}
$$
This step differentiates only $a$, not a nearest approximant or its conditional expectation. Nearest-point existence is unnecessary.

#### III. Graph-core extension, resolvents and all retained times

For $a\in\operatorname{Dom}L$, choose $a_j\in\mathcal C$ converging in the $L$ graph norm. Passing to the limit in (F.0y.10) gives that inequality on all of $\operatorname{Dom}L$. If $b\in\mathcal A(Y)$, put $a=R(\lambda,L)b$. Since $L$ generates contractions, this positive resolvent exists, and
$$
0=\|qb\|=\|q(\lambda a-La)\|
\ge\lambda\|qR(\lambda,L)b\|.
$$
Therefore every positive resolvent preserves $\mathcal A(Y)$. For $t>0$,
$$
T_tb=\lim_{n\to\infty}
\left[\frac ntR\!\left(\frac nt,L\right)\right]^n b
\quad\hbox{in norm}.
\tag{F.0y.11}
$$
For a direct verification, write the resolvent as the Laplace integral of $T$. Its displayed $n$th power averages $T_sb$ against the $\gamma$ distribution with mean $t$ and variance $t^2/n$. Concentration, strong continuity at $t$ and $\|T_sb\|\le\|b\|$ give the norm limit. Each approximant belongs to the closed algebra $\mathcal A(Y)$, proving (F.0y.3). This avoids any assertion that $\mathcal C\cap\mathcal A(Y)$ is dense or is a graph core. If the reversible group and both-sign precone are supplied, apply the same argument to $T_{-t}$, whose generator $-L$ has the same graph core.

#### IV. Binding to the regional norm packages of Theorem F.0

Apply the theorem separately inside one bounded globally hyperbolic diamond $O$, using its actual regional evolution $T_O$, generator $L_O$ and graph core $\mathcal C_O$. F.0(3) explicitly supplies these regional objects; no unproved global graph-core gluing is required. Every member of $\mathcal C_O$ belongs to a finite-stage regional algebra and therefore has finite event support.

Definitions F.1/F.2 assign each microscopic site its actual spacetime point and take independent tensor factors over those sites. F.0(3) preserves every retained small diamond. For an old event label $x$ and any distinct fine label $y$, choose such a diamond containing $x$ but excluding $y$. Intersecting the resulting finite-stage support algebras pins the whole old factor to the fine fibre at exactly $x$, as in F.0o section A. Distinct event factors remain independent under the injective common embeddings. Refinement can enlarge the fibre at $x$ without bound; it cannot move the old factor to a different label or identify two independent factors. This produces (F.0y.1) regionally, including arbitrary centres and collocated infinite AF fibres. If a required same-label fine fibre is absent, a nontrivial old factor has no unital isometric regional image at that stage, so the proposed package already fails its embedding requirement.

The precone of hypothesis (b) is a **clock-truncated physical LR support** condition; Einstein causality and the untruncated causal future are not used. The endpoint calculation under hypothesis (a) follows. Definition 35 gives the positive propagation metric with edge lengths $\delta_nw_e$ and uniformly bounded positive edge costs. Theorem 44 uses that same metric, already including microscopic length, in the common macroscopic normalization. F.1 uses the actual geometric location maps, and Corollary F.1 calls $a_n$ the physical length represented by a graph edge. Under hypothesis (a) these are the comparison maps $p_n$ of that normalization and the bounded-cost edge scale, $\delta_nw_{\max}\le Ka_n$; as assembled in F.0o section C, on a bounded comparison window there are then $K<\infty$ and $\eta_n\to0$ such that
$$
d_\infty(p_nu,p_nv)\le K a_n d_n(u,v)+\eta_n.
\tag{F.0y.12}
$$
The distortion is applied once to the endpoints, not once per graph edge. No rate $\eta_n=o(a_n)$ is needed. Theorem 43.5(5) selects one of these four positive operational directions as temporal; it does not discard that direction or append an independent clock. Thus, under (a), (F.0y.12) covers timelike-separated as well as spacelike-separated event labels; the spacelike-margin inequality in the proof of Theorem F.0 does not give it (F.0o, section C).

For disjoint finite event sets $E,H\subset O$, let $r=d_\infty(E,H)>0$. Exact point pinning places every register in their consistent representatives at its corresponding label. Consequently
$$
a_n d_n(E_n,H_n)\ge\frac{r-\eta_n}{K}.
$$
Choose $C_0>0$ with $a_nv_{\rm LR}^{(n)}\le C_0$ eventually, supplied by F.0(2), and set $\delta=r/(4KC_0)$. For all sufficiently large $n$, uniformly for $0\le t\le\delta$,
$$
a_n\bigl[d_n(E_n,H_n)-v_{\rm LR}^{(n)}t\bigr]
\ge\frac{r}{2K}-C_0\delta=\frac{r}{4K}>0.
\tag{F.0y.13}
$$
Hence $H$ lies strictly outside the clock-truncated limiting LR cone throughout a positive time interval. Hypothesis (b) states that this cone is a norm-support cone for the regional evolution, which is (F.0y.2) for some $\delta(E,H)>0$. In the proof of Theorem F.0, Condition 4 enters through the comparison of spacelike regions with the microscopic support cones, which gives commutation; (b) is the stronger norm-support requirement. The exclusion is uniform over the source-support algebra; norm completion preserves it by contraction and closedness of the omitted-event algebra. Neither a microscopic support-count bound nor a bound on the completed fibre generator enters this passage.

For a retained algebra with nontrivial centre, (b) does not follow from the retained-commutator bound of F.0(2). Proposition F.0p distinguishes that bound from a support-cone certificate, and the diagonal retained algebras of Theorem F.0x satisfy it while $L_nZ_a=\lambda(Z_b-Z_a)$ transports support between endpoints at a fixed positive distance. Such dynamics violate (F.0y.2). Theorem F.0m, under its vanishing cross-event error, and Theorem F.0o, under its finite-range hypotheses, prove the invariance (F.0y.3) with centres allowed; the case not covered is a retained algebra with nontrivial centre outside those hypotheses. A record using unrelated location maps or an unrelated mesh does not satisfy (a); one using an untruncated $J^+(E)$ in place of the common clock-truncated LR cone does not satisfy (b).

*Derivation of (b) for full matrix fibres.* Let every event fibre be a full matrix algebra at every stage, as the local matrix algebras of Definitions F.1/F.2 are in the proof of Theorem F.0. By F.0(3), $T_O(t)a=\lim_n\iota_n\bigl(\alpha_t^{(n)}(A_n)\bigr)$ in norm for every core element $a$ with consistent representatives $A_n$: the certificate identifies the regional evolutions with the embedded local evolutions, and the proof of Theorem F.0 uses this identity in its locality step, where it applies the bound of F.0(2) to $\alpha_t^{(n)}$. Contraction and density extend the identity to every finite-stage element (Theorem F.0o, section B). The bound of F.0(2) therefore applies to the evolutions that define $T_O$, and (F.0y.2) follows from (a). Let $a\in\mathcal A(E)$ and $b\in\mathcal A(H)$ be finite-stage elements with consistent representatives $A_n,B_n$. Exact point pinning places their supports in the stage-$n$ fibres over $E$ and $H$, so F.0(2), $\mu_n\ge\mu_0$ and (F.0y.13) give, for $0\le t\le\delta$ and all sufficiently large $n$,
$$
\bigl\|[\alpha_t^{(n)}(A_n),B_n]\bigr\|
\le C\|a\|\,\|b\|\exp\!\left(-\frac{\mu_0r}{4Ka_n}\right).
$$
The limit identity and norm density give $[T_ta,b]=0$ for all $a\in\mathcal A(E)$, $b\in\mathcal A(H)$ and $0\le t\le\delta$, where $T_t=T_O(t)$. Let $M_k\subseteq\mathcal A(H)$ be the increasing finite-stage full matrix algebras, whose union is norm dense in $\mathcal A(H)$, let $\operatorname{tr}$ be their normalized trace, and let $P_k(c)=\int_{U(M_k)}ucu^*\,du$ be the Haar average over the unitary group of $M_k$. Each $P_k$ is a contraction on $\mathcal A$ that fixes every element commuting with $M_k$, and $P_k(hc')=\operatorname{tr}(h)\,c'$ for $h\in M_j$, $j\le k$, and $c'\in\mathcal A(X\setminus H)$. Hence $P_k$ converges pointwise in norm to the slice map $\operatorname{tr}\otimes\operatorname{id}$, whose range is $\mathcal A(X\setminus H)$, and every element of $\mathcal A$ commuting with $\mathcal A(H)$ lies in $\mathcal A(X\setminus H)$. Applied to $T_ta$, this is (F.0y.2). The relative-commutant step uses the trivial centre of $\mathcal A(H)$.

#### V. Localized slice contradiction and the nontrivial response gate

By the regional application, every $\mathcal A_O(Y)$ is invariant under every retained evolution time, including negative times when the reversible certificate admits them. Suppose a retained event $x\in O$ has a nonconstant selfadjoint observable $b_x$, with spectral diameter $\Delta>0$. Choose a Cauchy time-slice $\Sigma$ omitting $x$, and let $Y$ be the support set of that localized slice (or of the chosen thin time-slice region, if slices are represented by open regions). F.0(6) quantifies over every such Cauchy time-slice; by hypothesis (c) the slice core is contained in $\mathcal A_O(Y)$. The every-neighborhood axiom of F.10.2 is not imported, and no large neighborhood containing all events is chosen. Product states that agree on $\mathcal A_O(Y)$ and attain the two spectral endpoints of $b_x$ give
$$
\operatorname{dist}\bigl(b_x,\mathcal A_O(Y)\bigr)
\ge\frac{\Delta}{2}>0.
\tag{F.0y.14}
$$
All evolved slice-core inputs, their finite products and their norm closure stay in $\mathcal A_O(Y)$ by (F.0y.3). They cannot generate $\mathcal A(O)$ in norm, contradicting F.0(6). Isometric embeddings preserve the nonconstant observable and its spectral diameter; a state quotient or vanishing event weight cannot remove this C*-norm gap. Every event can be omitted by a suitable Cauchy level in a diamond containing it. Thus the only possible retained observable sector under F.0(1)–(7) with (a)–(c) is scalar.

The conclusion is a necessity statement for a package that faithfully retains a nonconstant MPU response. Existence of a scalar geometric/source package is a separate question, and ambient Hilbert dimension alone supplies no nontrivial retained algebra. On the full-context Hilbert branch, Theorem 23 supplies effects $E_j$ and states $\rho_i$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_iE_j)=\delta_{ij}$; any such retained effect is nonconstant and is already enough for (F.0y.14). More generally one nonconstant chosen finite event response suffices, without assuming the full eight-response branch at every site.

The proof makes no positivity-of-transport, saturation, spatial-translation, Poincare, or Wightman assumption. Uniform local strength gives no bound on a coded old observable's derivative when its collocated microscopic support grows (Proposition F.0s); the graph-core and precone argument covers that case directly. Ordinary continuum QFT and the strong/weak, moving/buffered-observable and comparison-quotient constructions are unaffected: they do not assert this literal independent-point norm embedding together with the same finite-event graph-core package. $\square$

<a id="theorem-f0z"></a>

<a id="theorem-f0z-countable-event-labels-and-sharp-cauchy-localization"></a>**Theorem F.0z (Countable Event Labels and Sharp Cauchy Localization).** In a bounded globally hyperbolic region $O$, let the regional norm algebra be the independent event tensor product of Definitions F.1 and F.2 and Theorem F.0y. Assume its finite-dimensional stages form a sequence with coherent isometric embeddings. Assume the retained slice family includes every level of a Cauchy temporal function $s:O\to\mathbb R$. Let the evolved slice algebra be generated in norm by the images of the same slice core under the regional unital evolution maps at the retained times. If each slice core is localized on its exact slice, as in Theorem F.0y(c), Condition F.0(6) forces $\mathcal A(O)=\mathbb C I$. This conclusion is independent of the common location and mesh condition F.0y(a) and of the regional norm-support precone F.0y(b).

The same conclusion holds when for each fixed slice-core observable $a$ at a level $\Sigma_r=s^{-1}(r)$ the norm distance to its shrinking collar algebras tends to zero:
$$
\lim_{\eta\downarrow0}\operatorname{dist}\!\left(
a,\mathcal A_O(\{x\in O:|s(x)-r|<\eta\})\right)=0 .
\tag{F.0z.1}
$$
In particular (F.0z.1) holds when $a$ is the norm limit of embedded representatives supported in stage-dependent collars with temporal widths tending to zero.

*Proof.* Write $X_O$ for the set of event labels with nontrivial retained fibres in $O$. A countable inductive union of finite-dimensional algebras is separable in its norm completion. The product and norm facts used in Theorem F.0y hold for independent event fibres with centres as well. For any two distinct $x,y\in X_O$, choose positive contractions $a_x\in\mathcal A_x$ and $a_y\in\mathcal A_y$ with both $0$ and $1$ in their spectra. Such a contraction is obtained by normalizing a nonscalar self-adjoint element by its spectral endpoints. Product states attain $1$ on one and $0$ on the other, so $\|a_x-a_y\|\ge1$. A separable metric space has at most countably many elements separated pairwise by one, by assigning them distinct balls of radius $1/3$ from a countable dense family. Thus $X_O$ is countable. On the literal realization it can also be counted directly from the union of the finite stage label sets, since the embeddings pin each nontrivial old fibre to its event as in Theorem F.0y.

A globally hyperbolic region has a Cauchy temporal foliation. Use the given $s$ and choose $r\in\mathbb R\setminus s(X_O)$. The whole event algebra on $\Sigma_r$ is $\mathbb CI$. In the sharp localization case every core observable on $\Sigma_r$ is scalar. Every regional unital evolution fixes these scalars, so the evolved slice core generates at most $\mathbb CI$. Condition F.0(6) gives the claim. For the Cauchy temporal splitting on a smooth globally hyperbolic region, see Bernal and Sánchez (2004, Theorem 1.1).

For the collar assertion, take a finite subset $F\subset X_O$ and a product-state partial expectation $E_F:\mathcal A(O)\to\mathcal A_O(F)$ as in (F.0y.4). For $F\ne\varnothing$, let $\eta_F=\frac12\min_{x\in F}|s(x)-r|>0$. For $0<\eta\le\eta_F$ the collar omits $F$, and $E_F$ maps its entire algebra into $\mathbb CI$. Contractivity then gives
$$
\operatorname{dist}(E_Fa,\mathbb CI)
\le
\operatorname{dist}\!\left(a,\mathcal A_O(\{x\in O:|s(x)-r|<\eta\})\right).
\tag{F.0z.2}
$$
By (F.0z.1) the right hand side tends to zero. Every $E_Fa$ is scalar, and $E_Fa\to a$ in norm as $F$ exhausts $X_O$, since the finite-event union is dense. Hence $a$ is scalar. Finally, if $a=\lim_n\iota_n(a_n)$ in norm and the support of each $a_n$ is in a collar of width $\eta_n\to0$, for each $\eta>0$ the sufficiently late embedded representatives lie in that collar algebra, using the common event identifications. This gives (F.0z.1).

Consequently an event tensor net with a nonconstant regional response and Condition F.0(6) must have a slice-core observable at every level $r\notin s(X_O)$ whose norm distance to the collar algebras has strictly positive limit as $\eta\downarrow0$. These levels have full Lebesgue measure on the temporal parameter line. A separately assigned core in a fixed positive-thickness Cauchy neighbourhood can have nontrivial support at such a level. The statement concerns exact slices and shrinking collars in the same event tensor norm realization. $\square$

<a id="proposition-f0z1"></a>

<a id="proposition-f0z1-exact-finite-regional-truncation-and-fixed-thickness-slices"></a>**Proposition F.0z.1 (Exact Finite Regional Truncation and Fixed-Thickness Slices).** In the literal event tensor realization, fix a bounded region $O$ and write $\mathcal A_n(O)=\bigotimes_{x\in X_n(O)}\mathcal A_{n,x}$ at stage $n$. Let $L_{n,O}=\sum_Z L_{n,Z}$, a finite sum of supported generators on the actual retained algebra. Each $L_{n,Z}$ acts on the factors over its support $Z$ and is the identity superoperator on the omitted factors under tensor extension. Each term generates a unital completely positive contraction semigroup on the retained algebra. Suppose for every event $x\in X_n(O)$ a smaller retained diamond $Q$ isolates it, and the following exact comparison holds on the whole finite event fibre:
$$
L_{n,O}(a)=L_{n,Q}(a)
\quad(a\in\mathcal A_{n,x}),\qquad
L_{n,Q}=\sum_{Z\subseteq X_n(Q)} L_{n,Z}\big|_{\mathcal A_n(Q)}.
\tag{F.0z.3}
$$
Here $X_n(Q)=\{x\}$ and the first equality uses its tensor inclusion. A physical term supported on several microscopic registers at the same event counts as internal to that event. Under (F.0z.3) the full finite evolution preserves the algebra on every subset of event labels. The regional norm-limit evolution has the same invariance if the embeddings preserve event labels and the norm semigroup comparisons of F.0(3) hold. This excludes Condition F.0(6) whenever its localized slice core is supported in a fixed positive-thickness collar that omits an independently retained nonconstant event observable of $O$.

*Proof.* Suppress $n,O$. Let $L_{\mathrm{one}}$ be the sum of all one-event terms and $K$ be the sum of all terms meeting at least two distinct event labels. A supported generator with empty support vanishes by unitality. A term at a distinct event kills $a\in\mathcal A_x$ because its generator annihilates the identity on that distinct factor. Thus $L_{\mathrm{one}}(a)$ on $\mathcal A_x$ is the internal term sum in (F.0z.3), so $K(a)=0$. For $t\ge0$, the matrix-exponential product formula for the finite sum $K$ gives $e^{tK}$ as the norm limit of finite products of the term semigroups at time $t/m$. Those products and their norm limit are unital completely positive contractions. The map $e^{tK}$ fixes every $\mathcal A_x$ elementwise. Both Schwarz equalities for every $a\in\mathcal A_x$ follow because $a$, $a^*a$ and $aa^*$ are all fixed. Hence every event fibre is in the multiplicative domain of $e^{tK}$. That map fixes products of event-fibre elements and their finite linear span, which is the entire retained algebra. Differentiating at zero gives $K=0$ on the entire algebra. The remaining one-event generators preserve every finite support algebra, including fibres with centres.

For a finite-stage $a$ supported on $Y$, every consistent later representative remains supported on $Y$ by exact event pinning. The embedded finite-time evolutions remain in the closed algebra $\mathcal A_O(Y)$. The F.0(3) convergence on the regional norm-dense core extends to all finite-stage elements: approximate $a$ by a core element $b$, compare their consistent representatives at a common late stage, and bound the two added errors by $\|a-b\|$ each using the finite and limiting contraction bounds. Hence $T_O(t)a\in\mathcal A_O(Y)$, and density of the finite-event union in $\mathcal A_O(Y)$ gives invariance on the whole algebra. If a nonconstant self-adjoint observable at an omitted event has spectral diameter $\Delta>0$, the two product states of (F.0y.14) give its distance at least $\Delta/2$ from the invariant collar algebra. This excludes norm-dense evolved slice generation.

Condition (F.0z.3) uses exact equality on each finite-stage isolated fibre with the internal-term sum. Agreement of limiting generators on selected common core elements gives a different test. The class includes onsite UCP dynamics with nonconstant fibres and can include a decomposition with nonvanishing cross-event norm sums. For example, place two qubits at distinct events and include the two terms $i[Z_1Z_2,\cdot]$ and $-i[Z_1Z_2,\cdot]$ together with any one-event terms, where $Z_j$ is Pauli $Z$ on qubit $j$. Each cross-event term generates a unitary-conjugation group and has genuine two-event support, as seen on either single-qubit Pauli $X$. Their sum vanishes, giving the exact isolated-fibre comparison despite the nonzero sum of their norms. This proposition uses no metric comparison, range or decay estimate. Theorem F.0m controls cross-event norm sums and Theorem F.0o controls their support approximation. $\square$

<a id="proposition-f0z2"></a>

<a id="proposition-f0z2-quantitative-regional-truncation"></a>**Proposition F.0z.2 (Quantitative Regional Truncation).** Use the finite retained regional tensor algebras and the termwise unital completely positive contraction semigroups of Proposition F.0z.1. On a stage write $L=L_{\mathrm{one}}+K$, where $L_{\mathrm{one}}$ sums terms internal to one event and $K$ sums terms meeting two or more events. For a finite event fibre define
$$
\epsilon_x=\bigl\|K\big|_{\mathcal A_x}\bigr\|_{\infty\to\infty}.
\tag{F.0z.5}
$$
This is the generator error in the whole isolated-fibre comparison with the actual internal-term truncation. For distinct events $x_1,\ldots,x_k$ and contractions $a_i\in\mathcal A_{x_i}$, one has, for $t\geq0$,
$$
\left\|e^{tL}(a_1\cdots a_k)-e^{tL_{\mathrm{one}}}(a_1\cdots a_k)\right\|
\le t\left(\sum_{i=1}^k\epsilon_{x_i}
      +3\sum_{1\le i<j\le k}\sqrt{\epsilon_{x_i}\epsilon_{x_j}}\right).
\tag{F.0z.6}
$$
No uniform bound on the total generator, number of microscopic registers in a fibre, or absolute cross-event term sum is needed. In the regional norm limit of F.0(3), if $\epsilon_{n,x}\to0$ on the whole stage-$n$ fibre of each persistent event $x$, the evolution preserves every event-set algebra, with the fixed-collar exclusion of Proposition F.0z.1.

*Proof.* The finite sum $K$ generates a unital completely positive contraction semigroup $S_s=e^{sK}$ by the finite product formula. For a contraction $a\in\mathcal A_x$, integration of $S_sK(a)$ gives $\|S_s(a)-a\|\le s\epsilon_x$. Since $a^*a$ and $aa^*$ are contractions in the same fibre, the two Schwarz defects satisfy
$$
0\le S_s(a^*a)-S_s(a)^*S_s(a),\qquad
\|S_s(a^*a)-S_s(a)^*S_s(a)\|\le 3s\epsilon_x ,
\tag{F.0z.7}
$$
and the same estimate holds with $a^*$ in place of $a$. For the norm bound, insert $a^*a$ and use $\|S_s(a)\|\le1$ on each of the two product differences.

Represent the retained algebra faithfully on a finite Hilbert space. Write a Stinespring representation of $S_s$ as $S_s(b)=V^*\pi(b)V$ with isometry $V$, and set $P=VV^*$. Equation (F.0z.7) bounds both off-diagonal blocks of $\pi(a)$ for the decomposition $P\oplus(1-P)$ by $\sqrt{3s\epsilon_x}$ in operator norm. For a product of contractions, an off-diagonal block is bounded by the sum of the constituent bounds, by inserting $P+(1-P)$ between the factors and applying the resulting two-block identity inductively. Consequently,
$$
\begin{aligned}
