&\|S_s(a_1\cdots a_k)-S_s(a_1)\cdots S_s(a_k)\|\\
&\hspace{12mm}\le 3s\sum_{1\le i<j\le k}
                     \sqrt{\epsilon_{x_i}\epsilon_{x_j}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.0z.8}
$$
Indeed, for a product $bc$ the difference $S_s(bc)-S_s(b)S_s(c)$ is $V^*\pi(b)(1-P)\pi(c)V$. Take $b$ to be the prefix through factor $j-1$ and $c=a_j$, then telescope through $j$. Comparing the product of the $S_s(a_i)$ with the original product costs at most $s\sum_i\epsilon_{x_i}$ by contraction. Dividing their combined bound by $s$ and taking $s\downarrow0$ bounds $\|K(a_1\cdots a_k)\|$ by the parenthesis in (F.0z.6).

Distinct internal event generators commute as tensor extensions. Thus $e^{uL_{\mathrm{one}}}(a_1\cdots a_k)$ is a product of contractions in the same fibres. The finite Duhamel identity
$$
e^{tL}-e^{tL_{\mathrm{one}}}
=\int_0^t e^{(t-u)L}K e^{uL_{\mathrm{one}}}\,du
\tag{F.0z.9}
$$
and contractivity give (F.0z.6). It extends to finite linear combinations by the triangle inequality. Every fixed finite-stage observable has such an expansion over finitely many old event fibres. Its coefficients and factor norms are fixed under the event-preserving tensor embeddings. For that observable the right side tends to zero uniformly on compact time intervals, and the embedded one-event comparison stays in the original event-set algebra. Contractive extension of the F.0(3) semigroup convergence from its dense regional core to the finite-stage observable, followed by norm closure, gives invariance of all event-set algebras. The two product-state evaluations of (F.0y.14) then give the fixed-collar obstruction. $\square$

<a id="proposition-f0z3"></a>

<a id="proposition-f0z3-exact-worldline-generator-certificate-on-the-operational-mesh"></a>**Proposition F.0z.3 (Exact Worldline Generator Certificate on the Operational Mesh).** On the flat normal-source meshes of Theorem 43.5j, there is a physically retained finite field factor with nonconstant locally accessible observables whose regional algebras, two-sided semigroups and preparations give an exact instance of the local generator certificate of Definition F.0a on the worldline realization of Theorem R.4.2.9d. The field's actual observation graph has degree at most six. Its same-clock isometric norm comparison, all-Cauchy time-slice generation, state compatibility and additivity hold without using a graph form as its observable generator. The geometric Mosco record of Theorem 43.5j can coexist with these field records in one financed source. Using the two graph roles in Theorem F.0d requires the observable-interaction graph to be the graph to which its bounded-degree hypothesis applies, and still requires the full common Lorentzian promotion of its background. The statement supplies the local generator and time-slice part of that joint route.

*Common physical mesh and sources.* Use the level $n_j=3^{2j}$ of Theorem 43.5j, with its actual inherited costs, complete geometric timer/stencil, metric/forecast comparison, cells and common units. Work in a flat chart with one coordinate written $ct$ and the others spatial, $t$ the declared physical observation clock. Use the spatial three-coordinate projection of the actual cell partition. The spatial cells refine into $9^3$ children at the next stage. One can work on the spatial torus or on a fixed bounded chart with its cells compactly contained inside it and their exhausting descendants. Diamonds are taken in a declared globally hyperbolic Lorentzian chart of this flat coordinate space, with clock and cone slope as recorded on that chart. This construction does not infer that Lorentzian record from the four-dimensional Riemannian form.

At the actual spatial cell address supply one persistent field qubit and its owned control. A field address can be attached to its spatial-coordinate reference host at the chosen time origin, with separate register and service identity. Every later local event on that vertical line acts on that same physical qubit. The original geometric and prediction apparatus and all its outputs remain in a separate named factor. The observation Hamiltonian of the qubits is
$$
H_j=E_*\sum_C n_C,\qquad n_C=|1\rangle\langle1|_C,
\tag{F.0z.10}
$$
with one fixed energy $E_*>0$ and the original physical seconds. During observation the complete evolution factors between the field and the rest. Preparation, field control and its local readout are supplied in the common frozen reservation before any geometry or forecast comparison. For the exact cofinal map below it suffices to retain the ideal finite hardware matrices and then choose paid finite synthesis errors with sum at most $2^{-j}$ at each new level. The entire supplied stock and route remains at its physical cut. The selected geometry and forecast remain an exact minimum on the enlarged declared reservation branch: the field source is independent of $(g,\phi)$, its complete added stock and ready/control/holding reservations have the same price on every comparator, and its task payoff is fixed. Use one common extended duration at that grade. The original rate objective multiplied by its old duration then differs from the new objective multiplied by the new duration by that same constant on every comparator. This is the same additive-clock comparison as the source invoice of Theorem D.6f.2m. No field state is identified with the original teacher, propagation clock or random walk.

*Exact norm generator, clock and states.* For an open region $O$, let $F(O)$ be its rest-worldline footprint, and let $\mathfrak A_j(O)$ be the tensor matrix algebra over cells with closure in $F(O)$. A field operator in this algebra is a physical local-insertion response: every such cell has a finite cover of small actual observation windows inside $O$ and cofinal descendants can be allocated inside those windows. The inclusions, finite-support covers and cofinal equivalence with the physical insertion description are those of Theorem R.4.2.9d. For the present $9^3$ child rule an exact same-clock inclusion is even simpler: place the parent matrix algebra in one fixed child qubit and put identity on all other child factors. If a coherent one-excitation splitter is wanted, use the explicit excitation-preserving Householder unitary of Theorem R.4.2.9d with $9^3$ in place of eight. In either case the inclusion is completely isometric, preserves all regional inclusions, intertwines (F.0z.10) and preserves the product ground preparation. On each regional algebra take the common core to be the algebraic union of the finite embedded tensor factors. Its semigroup and two-sided group are exactly compatible:
$$
j_j^m\alpha_{j,t}=\alpha_{m,t}j_j^m,qquad
j_j^m\mathcal L_j^*=\mathcal L_m^*j_j^m,
\qquad\omega_mj_j^m=\omega_j.
\tag{F.0z.11}
$$
The time parameter and onsite generator coefficient are independent of $j$. This gives zero ideal generator and semigroup error on every finite algebraic-core element after its first retained level. For the limit group, strong norm continuity follows on the dense core from the finite matrix groups and on its closure from the isometry. The algebraic core is a graph core for the closed generator. Indeed product-vacuum conditional expectations onto each finite embedded regional algebra commute with the evolution by its onsite split and the ground-state compatibility. These expectations converge in norm to identity on the regional limit, since each finite core element is fixed eventually. They therefore converge simultaneously on $A$ and on $\mathcal L^*A$ for $A$ in the generator domain, and give graph approximants inside the finite core. The positive generator on the product-vacuum representation is the sum of the excitation gaps on the finite-particle core, with vacuum energy zero. This proves all parts of Definition F.0a, including its stability and two-sided comparison. Disjoint finite footprints commute at all times and the uniform onsite Heisenberg norm bound is $2E_*/\hbar$.

For a Cauchy neighborhood $U$ inside a diamond $O$, every timelike vertical line meeting $O$ meets its Cauchy surface in $U$. Thus $F(U)=F(O)$ and their local norm algebras coincide. Evolution preserves this common core. In a genuine open cover, the footprints cover $F(O)$ and any finite retained cell collection compactly inside it has a finite subcover and positive Lebesgue number. Upon refinement every descendant of those cells lies inside some covering footprint. Exact tensor generation on those descendants proves norm additivity. In each fixed diamond with nonempty footprint, a one-cell Pauli matrix from a sufficiently fine stage has operator norm one and two distinguishable eigenstates, and it remains faithful under every comparison. A repeated access to one worldline at different times does not provide independent event factors. Consequently the literal event-algebra premises of Theorems F.0m, F.0o, F.0y and F.0z do not apply to these algebras.

*Propagation-form comparison and its remaining interface.* The actual geometric Dirichlet forms of Theorem 43.5j remain on the full four-dimensional timer graph with their cell interpolation and common dense continuum $H^1$ form domain. Their nonnegative form generators and contraction semigroups satisfy the same Mosco comparison, by the registered form core and Theorem 35b.6. Equation (F.0z.11) concerns instead the full Heisenberg generators on the retained field factors. Both sets of records are present in the same physical source, as distinguished in item 3 of Definition F.0c. The field's separate observation graph may use the nearest-axis adjacency of spatial cell addresses, with physical edge scale $a_j=\ell_*/n_j$, degree at most six and no intersite Hamiltonian terms. Its Lieb–Robinson inequality holds with any nonnegative velocity because every offsite commutator is exactly zero. In particular the upper-bound choice $v_j=c/a_j$ and any fixed positive decay exponent meet the numerical bound (F.0c.2), with $a_jv_j=c$. For two sets of spatially separated footprint representatives the same exact zero commutator is stronger than that bound. This upper-bound convention asserts no propagation saturation for the field. The full timer graph uses the growing stencil of Theorem 43.5j; it is not itself uniformly bounded in degree. Hence the joint conclusion under Theorem F.0d consumes the explicit observable-graph reading of its bounded-degree condition. It also consumes an independently populated common Lorentzian signature, clock and symmetry record on the selected geometry, rather than a choice of notation $ct$. The local generator and time-slice proofs above require neither a split-form identification nor a claim that the geometric timers give the field velocity. ∎

<a id="proposition-f0z4-operational-mesh-clock-cone-and-worldline-symmetry-overlaps"></a>**Proposition F.0z.4 (Operational-Mesh Clock, Cone and Worldline Symmetry Overlaps).** Use the flat branch of Theorem 43.5j and the physically retained worldline field of Proposition F.0z.3. The scalar, rail and qualifying-clock experiment of Theorem 46a.13 can use their same spatial mesh, rods and physical time on one bounded flat chart. Its normalized continuum scalar operator, attained rail frontier and worldline field share the same Lorentzian geometry there. The worldline net represents a nontrivial connected group of geometric clock translations by exactly compatible stage automorphisms. *Common chart and scalar normalization.* In the dimensionless flat torus of Theorem 43.5j, use an unwrapped coordinate chart about a fixed chosen time plane. Write its coordinates $(x^0,\mathbf x)$, physical space $\mathbf X=\ell_*\mathbf x$, and physical time $t=\ell_*x^0/c$. Here $c>0$ is the separately registered speed of the scalar and rail controller, before comparison. Its operational attainment is proved below. This sets the clock period corresponding to a given separation of the chart's time labels. The heat-semigroup parameter of Theorem 43.5j remains that experiment's independently recorded parameter, and does not serve as the causal observation clock. Choose the scalar spatial box of period $\ell_*$, use a causally convex laboratory chart of diameter less than $\ell_*/4$, and place its scalar, rail and orientation references at the actual spatial locations. Its finite spatial addresses are the three-coordinate projection of the same stage lattice with $a_j=\ell_*/n_j$ and $n_j=3^{2j}$. Worldline access is at those same addresses. Additional field, clock and control factors have separate owned stock identities even when they share an address. A spatial line may be observed at multiple actual times; its worldline qubit is the same factor at all those cuts.

At stage $j$ the scalar tick is $a_j/(8c)$ in these seconds, and a chart-time interval $a_j/c$ is eight such ticks. Use the mass-normalized field coordinates and the same three physical kick slots of (46a.9.2). The Fourier calculation of Theorem 46a.10 uses only integer periodic meshes and the bound $(m a_j/(8c))^2+12/64\le1/4$, so it applies here. Its finite-section Gaussian moments, local instruments and signed readout calibrations have the same estimates. At every $j$ choose the Hermite cutoff after the finite physical prefix and retain every field/source/probe factor. The partial-tick and collar estimates remain in the comparison. Choose the cofinal finite implementation with errors at most $2^{-j}$ on its first $j$ named probes, using the joint tolerance diagonal of Theorem 43.5j. The covered continuum normalized response is
$$
(\partial_t^2-c^2\Delta_{\mathbf X}+m^2)\phi=J.
\tag{F.0z.12}
$$
For smooth geometric tests independent of $x^0$, the spatial restriction of the limiting four-dimensional quadratic form of Theorem 43.5j is the same Euclidean form in the rods $\mathbf X$, per unit length in the transverse time-label coordinate. This follows either by the exact flat Fourier symbols on the zero $x^0$ frequency or by integrating the constant flat Cheeger tensor over that coordinate. The scalar spatial symbol is $c^2$ times this coefficient in physical time, by (F.0z.12). The two forms are compared on the same normalized smooth tests after their registered measures and units are included. They are different finite operators. The Lorentzian covector is the nonvanishing actual $dt$ from the scalar tick, rail service and the qualified forward-orientation experiment, not the heat parameter or an independent rescaling of elapsed field time.

*Attained cone and owned timing.* Use the straight shell rails and addressed subdivisions of Proposition 46a.11 on this same spatial lattice, with $r_j\downarrow0$ and $a_j/r_j\to0$. Register every physical hop and its duration $b/c$, with its own completion energy and retained diagonal phase. For a fixed direction aligned with the axis rods one may choose endpoint separations dividing an actual sequence of hop lengths, or approach a fixed endpoint on the mesh with the stated endpoint collar. On each such rail the arrived label is exactly distinguishable after its prescribed flight. The lower path bound follows from the Euclidean length of each actual segment and the upper error is (46a.11.2), using these same rods. Keep the full field/rail and local dependency comparison of Proposition 46a.12. Use the original qualified R14 controls, rates, snapshots and forward episode of Theorem 46a.13, with the common clock but their separately identified duration. The zero mismatch preparation, kinetic coefficient trial, Hessian, utilization and command-variance records of that theorem remain as stated. Its proof gives attainment of the calibrated frontier and the cone saturation for the nominated scalar sector. The worldline field is an extra onsite sector. Its exact commutator bound from Proposition F.0z.3 is contained in this same cone, with no saturation requirement for that sector. The scalar has a genuine well-posed two-data Klein–Gordon Cauchy problem, and the attached field cannot change its retarded kernel because the observation Hamiltonian acts as a tensor sum. The resulting signature on the covered chart is $-c^2dt^2+d\mathbf X^2$. This chart is unwrapped in its time coordinate and contains no closed timelike circuit from the geometric torus's auxiliary periodic labels.

*One reservation and causal interface.* At each refinement fix the original geometric/forecast menu, and additionally reserve all scalar, rail, fresh local host, orientation, worldline and causal instrument runs used above, with their actual finite cutoffs and budgets. The new task labels and all ready stocks are prepared before the corresponding inputs. Their resource envelopes are independent of the admitted geometric/forecast controls $(g,\phi)$ in Theorem D.6f.2m. In a run of the scalar calibration the fixed flat controller has its own apparatus stock and clocks. At the flat selected configuration the charts and rods of that controller are the very same coordinates of the geometric source, and the operator coefficient overlap is the preceding response equality. The comparison does not require the calibration controller to reproduce every nonflat alternative. Its complete input, state and control program are held fixed when those alternatives are evaluated. The scalar and rail service costs, fresh R14 supplies, clocks and holding time are common across the original comparators, as are the worldline costs and the declared fixed calibration-task benefit. Evaluate the original objective on the common extended time interval by the same additive work/reservation identity as in Proposition F.0z.3. All original alternatives remain and the flat geometry with the teacher forecast is still a minimum. The geometric Dirichlet form, metric timers and heat endpoint diagnosis are retained. Their completed diagnostics have their own known tasks or later delivered registers; no read port from those diagnostics enters a covered causal observation before its own actual future cut. The scalar, rail and worldline tasks share the same chart and units without identifying the heat endpoint sampler with a faster physical signal. This describes an independent protected preparation and observation contract of the same kind as Definition 46a.9. Every source, field, reserved path and unused archival factor keeps its own charge. In particular the new per-site operator bound pertains to the worldline field, not to the rapidly driven scalar experiment on its separate factors.

*Represented symmetry and a sharp boundary of the finite-stage convention.* For the worldline algebra the proper clock translations $s\in\mathbb R$ act geometrically by $O\mapsto O+(s,0)$. Footprints agree exactly, so every finite regional algebra is transported onto the translated one. On the finite stage use

\beta_{s,j}=\operatorname{Ad}\exp(isH_j/\hbar).
\tag{F.0z.13}
$$
It preserves the ground preparation and observation dynamics, is exactly compatible with the refinement by (F.0z.11), and induces a point-norm continuous nontrivial action on each local core. For example its one-qubit raising operator has phase $e^{isE_*/\hbar}$. In a chart this is the exact comparison whenever the translated regions remain in the chart; on the flat extended cylinder the same time action is globally defined. This verifies the represented symmetry clause for this selected geometric group. No continuous spatial group needs to be included in that clause, as in Proposition F.0w.

In fact the full connected group of spatial translations cannot act by exact covariant automorphisms on these particular finite spatial algebras. Fix a small footprint and a stage where its algebra is nonconstant. Its translates have only finitely many possible cell sets, hence finitely many possible regional subalgebras of the finite ambient algebra. Any exactly compatible action on that stage, continuous in the limit point-norm topology, is already continuous on the finite algebra by its isometric embedding. The map from a translation to the transported subalgebra is continuous in the distance between their unit balls: convergence on a finite basis yields norm convergence of the finite-stage automorphisms. A continuous map from the connected translation torus to this finite set is constant. But some translation puts the footprint entirely in a disjoint set of cells. Their tensor algebras intersect only in scalars, a contradiction. The argument also applies to any exact fixed-stage regional system with finitely many possible regional algebras, connected spatial translations and the indicated disjointness. It is different from fixing each individual point factor by Proposition F.0w. It leaves cofinal spatial comparisons and maps transporting the entire marked source as separate notions. ∎

<a id="proposition-f0z5"></a>

<a id="proposition-f0z5-curvature-defect-at-a-degree-reduced-timer-port"></a>**Proposition F.0z.5 (Curvature Defect at a Degree-Reduced Timer Port).** Consider a finite nonnegative-rate Markov graph of the type used in the geometric test (D.6e.1). Replace a geometrical vertex by a collocated cluster of bounded-degree ports and give each old link its own port. At one gateway $p$, suppose the only intercluster neighbor is $p'$, with outgoing and incoming rates $q>0$ and $q'>0$. The other neighbors of $p$ have no intercluster edges, and their total outgoing rate from $p$ is $M$. Suppose $p'$ also has no other intercluster neighbor. For a lifted affine coordinate test $f$ constant on each collocated cluster, put $\Delta=f(p')-f(p)$. At $p$ the radius-two quadratic curvature test with target dimension four has defect
$$
\frac14(Lf(p))^2-\Gamma_2(f)(p)=\frac q4(M-3q')\Delta^2.
\tag{F.0z.14}
$$
Thus a high-rate internal-collapse limit can fail the raw pointwise defect even when the endpoint projection has the desired metric and form. More precisely, on any such sequence for which an admitted coefficient-norm-one affine test has $q(M-3q')_+\Delta^2$ bounded below by a positive constant at one gateway, the $K=0$ defect in (D.6e.1) cannot tend to zero.

*Proof.* Write $Lf(x)=\sum_y r_{xy}[f(y)-f(x)]$, $\Gamma(f,g)(x)=\tfrac12\sum_y r_{xy}[f(y)-f(x)][g(y)-g(x)]$, and $\Gamma_2(f)=\tfrac12L\Gamma(f)-\Gamma(f,Lf)$. Every internal difference of the lifted test is zero. At $p$ and $p'$ this gives
$$
Lf(p)=q\Delta,\quad Lf(p')=-q'\Delta,\quad
\Gamma(f)(p)=q\Delta^2/2,\quad \Gamma(f)(p')=q'\Delta^2/2.
$$
At each other neighbor of $p$ the test is constant on all its neighbors, so $\Gamma(f)$ vanishes there. Consequently
$$
\tfrac12L\Gamma(f)(p)=\tfrac14[q(q'-q)-Mq]\Delta^2,
\qquad
\Gamma(f,Lf)(p)=-\tfrac12q(q+q')\Delta^2.
$$
Substituting gives $\Gamma_2(f)(p)=q(q+3q'-M)\Delta^2/4$ and (F.0z.14). The squared positive part of the right side is a lower bound on the supremum defining (D.6e.1) when $f$ is one of its admitted unit tests. This calculation uses the actual raw generator at the retained gateway. A trace form on the cluster quotient would instead use its own generator and its own separately verified curvature test. The result excludes the stated fast-internal-port regime and leaves other bounded-degree constructions in scope. ∎

<a id="theorem-f0z6"></a>

<a id="theorem-f0z6-bounded-degree-geometry-cone-and-persistent-local-field-on-one-source"></a>**Theorem F.0z.6 (Bounded-Degree Geometry, Cone and Persistent Local Field on One Source).** On the flat, fixed-geometry reservation source of Theorem C.6c.5c one can realize a persistent-worldline norm net, a geometric Mosco comparison, and the scalar/rail signature calibration on one bounded-degree apparatus. The source has a nonconstant faithfully retained local event observable, exact point-norm generator and state comparison, norm-dense evolved Cauchy cores, and summable finite-source implementation errors on a common retained protocol sequence. The positive-energy generator is onsite. The cone calibration comes from the separately owned scalar and rail response, whose measured coordinates, rods and clock are shared with the retained field. This supplies the common-source geometry, observation and promotion components of a Mosco–Bochner branch. Its applicability through the complete minimal-mode-shell framework of Theorem 43.5 retains the conditions stated below.

*Geometry, graph and finite source.* At $n=3^{2j}$ use the actual $X\times F$ graph, raw form $\mathcal E_H$, probability measure, clock and descriptor-path metric of Theorem C.6c.5c. Its vertices are the qualified finite heat ports, with the collocated fiber positions separately retained. The same source supplies all four defects of Theorem D.6e, metric and measure comparison, the raw reversible form generator and its Mosco/resolvent/semigroup comparison with the quadratic Cheeger energy on the flat four-torus. The full heat graph has degree at most eleven. Use a fixed port label in the layer with the three spatial-axis links to give each spatial address at the chosen reference time plane one separate owned worldline qubit. Put all fixed geometric and scalar apparatus factors in the complete host record. Their algebras and archive responses are retained in their respective task records. The local-net observation algebra is defined on the physical worldline qubits before refinement. Its inclusion into the actual host matrices is $A\mapsto A\otimes I$, a complete isometry at every level.

The spatially weighted curvature tests on the raw graph also have the flat limit. For any fixed smooth $f$ use its sampled constant-fiber lift $Jf$. With the measure pushforward of Theorem C.6c.5c, their integrals against a sampled smooth weight $w\ge0$ therefore tend to their flat values. In particular
$$
\lim_{j\to\infty}\int (Jw)\left[\Gamma_{2,H}(Jf)-\tfrac14(L_HJf)^2\right]d\nu
=\int_{\mathbb T^4}w\left[\|\nabla^2 f\|_{\rm HS}^2-\tfrac14(\Delta f)^2\right]dx\ge0.
$$
Fourier truncation or heat smoothing approximates any flat generator-domain $f\in H^2$ in $H^2$. For bounded nonnegative weights the squared derivatives then pass in $L^1$. Smooth bounded approximations to a weight give the same formula by dominated convergence, since the integrand is in $L^1$. This gives the limiting integrated dimension-four inequality on its generator domain. It is the smooth-core plus limiting domain-closure form of curvature transfer used in Theorem C.6c.6 and Corollary C.6c.7.1. The finite vertices have the graph forms and the stated smooth tests. The noncollapsed Riemannian and Sobolev-to-Lipschitz statements hold on their explicit flat limit.

The scalar calibration uses the existing axis links of the same root layer and the actual projected grid, with the clock and field parameters of Proposition F.0z.4. A subdivision is an additional lane of degree-two interior calibration hosts. It attaches at the two existing shortcut leaf endpoints. The two directions on the same unoriented lane share those endpoint incidences and their fixed schedule. At each shortcut leaf at most two extra rail incidences are needed. Axis rail controls can share their existing adjacency; even if supplied on a parallel local path, they add at most six incidences at a root address. Thus the full physical interaction graph of the selected heat, field, calibration, and clock hosts has uniformly bounded degree, for example nineteen before fixed-size onsite auxiliary blocks. For a spatial displacement, the rounded-segment construction in (C.6c.5.14) uses only spatial grid steps when both endpoints lie in the same spatial plane. Reserve the actual forward R14 source and its recorded stopping circuit, the clock/rail calibration records, the exact mismatch trial with scalar coefficient $c^2(1+\xi)^2$, and its utilization, positive Hessian and zero residual commands as in Theorem 46a.13. The physical schedule has successive preparation, heat diagnosis, causal calibration, retained observation, and archive collection windows. At completion its outputs remain in separate write-once stocks with no causal-task read port. Disable all its field couplings and feedback paths before the next window. Prepare fresh scalar/rail inputs and orientation hosts for causal calibration. The scalar or rail branch uses the predetermined local profiles of Theorem 46a.13. The later worldline observation window uses a fresh independently prepared field, with only the prescribed onsite field Hamiltonian active on that algebra. The same physical clock labels its local events. The two causal tasks can alternatively be run with the heat apparatus kept at its independent ready setting. In either schedule the local input apparatus of a causal task has no initially correlated private heat reference. Unknown field references, if used in a finite readout test, stay with their designated field test and do not open a heat control port. These are disjoint access intervals on one apparatus, with explicit tensor-product preparation and separation. Fast heat endpoints cannot transmit a signal inside either covered causal observation window.

The heat period is the positive $\tau_*\Delta_j$ of Theorem C.6c.5c. Its logarithm determines the heat operator $L/\tau_*$ in that service's physical seconds. Its Mosco parameter is the form parameter, with the fixed unit conversion $\tau_*$. The chart interval $a_j/c$ and the scalar tick $a_j/(8c)$ are the elapsed durations of their own calibrated source. This proves evolved norm-dense slice generation on every diamond, with no independent copies of a persistent qubit at different times. The same argument applied to a genuine open cover proves additivity: finite cell descendants can be assigned to its members and their tensor subalgebras generate the original finite core image. Local insertion collars shrink along the actual refinement and the exact onsite dynamics preserves their spatial supports. A Pauli observable on any sufficiently interior cell stays nonconstant under all these comparisons, with distinguishable local outcomes on its two opposite input eigenstates.

The positive-energy product-vacuum representation has the actual nonnegative excitation generator, independently of the heat form. Proper clock translations use (F.0z.13), a compatible nontrivial continuous group of actual geometric translations with vacuum and generator preservation. To take every translated bounded diamond, keep the same static hardware on the unwrapped cylinder and use any prescribed finite observation horizon, with the qualification, holding and readout stocks of that horizon. All ideal regional, state and evolution equalities are exact. The finite ideal observation Hamiltonians may be installed directly as the stated onsite levels. Any registered finite readout, transport and preparation approximations are funded with an exhaustive finite-prefix diagonal: on grade $j$ bound the total channel/record error of its first $j$ retained tests by $2^{-j}$, by the finite matrix cutoff and pulse bounds of the source constructors. <a id="proposition-f0z7-a-marked-shell-port-and-the-finite-curvature-boundary"></a>**Proposition F.0z.7 (A Marked Shell Port and the Finite Curvature Boundary).** The bounded-degree graph of Theorem C.6c.5c has a marked regular $24$-cell experiment using its actual shortcut ports. The experiment retains the $24$ independent H8 tangent responses of Theorem Z.11a and their full-reference pair transport on a common finite scalar occupation code. Its calibrated shortcut-work kernel is the regular $24$-cell Gram. Its scope is the marked finite shell and its explicit source tariff. On the same graph the raw reversible generator fails the global finite-stage $\mathrm{BE}(K,4)$ test for any $K$ in a fixed bounded interval at all sufficiently fine grades. The latter failure concerns general graph functions. The local polynomial tests of Theorem C.6c.5c and the limiting smooth curvature transfer of Corollary C.6c.5d remain valid.

*Actual shell and pair ports.* Use dimensionless flat chart coordinates $y=(ct,\mathbf X)/\ell_*$, the physical graph of Theorem C.6c.5c and its nested stages $n=3^{2j}$. Put $R=\sqrt n$, $\delta=1/n$, $m_j=\lfloor R/(4\sqrt2)\rfloor$ and $A_j=m_j\delta$. Use grades with $m_j\ge1$. Freeze the marked mode-to-root bijection $u\mapsto r_u$ of Theorem Z.11a, with $r_u\in\Xi_{D_4}$ and $|r_u|=\sqrt2$, before selecting any test. Place its center at an interior chart grid point $y_*$ and its peripheral positions at $y_u=y_*+A_jr_u$. A physical ball of radius $\ell_*A_j/\sqrt2$ at each such position is tangent to the central ball of that radius. Distinct peripheral interiors are disjoint because distinct $D_4$ roots have separation at least $\sqrt2$. These are actual chart positions of source port fibers. For $u\ne v$ the integer descriptor $s_{uv}=m_j(r_v-r_u)$ is nonzero, has length at most $R/2$, and is never an axis unit vector. The two endpoint ports at the corresponding sign-orbit leaf already have the direct paid shortcut edge of Theorem C.6c.5c. Its normalized busy-lane meter is $|s_{uv}|$ by Definition C.6c.4a. Central-to-peripheral tests use $m_jr_u$ in the same way. The prepared output and input chart labels are separate from the actual flight duration.

*Retained source and complete pair transport.* Use the scalar field of Theorem F.0z.6 and its actual completed-tick occupation calibration from Theorem 45h.11. For each finite shell grade use the seven-mode occupation/failure code of Theorem 45h.10 with a finite occupation cutoff that retains vacuum, zero momentum and all six signed-axis one-particle states. Its physical field encoding is the Gram isometry $J_H$ of that source construction. Use the marked H8 preparation and its fixed frame $V_R$ from Theorem Z.11a, including its finite preparation and readout responses and both alternative preparation settings at their proper input cuts. This uses the same scalar Hamiltonian, units and preparation code, with the complete finite source stocks charged. For the chosen finite probe lists use the common cutoff meeting the endpoint errors, including the $o(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{query}}^2)$ requirement for a completed-query Fisher comparison. No equality between the local rank-four coordinate metric and the internal rank-twenty-four tangent metric is used.

Let $G_j$ be the actual completed-tick scalar generator on that occupation code and $P_i$ the three commuting momenta of Theorem 45h.11. For the physical coordinate offset $d=(a,\mathbf b)$ of a chart step put $U_d=\exp[-i(aG_j+\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf P)]$ with the momentum normalization of Theorem 45h.13. The marked terminal code at a position $y$ is $E_y(\rho)=U_{d_y}V_R\rho V_R^*U_{d_y}^*$ in the full occupation/failure port. Its encoded scalar field is $J_HE_y(\rho)J_H^*$. A known pair label chooses the actual shortcut and its endpoint leaf before any unknown payload is supplied. Supply a full occupation/failure carrier, keep its entire input and output, and use the fixed computational-basis decomposition of the finite $d$-level code into a finite binary register with its unused codewords retained. The source of Theorem C.6c.7 transports one qubit and its reference by its supported SWAP. A single larger payload can instead use a fixed finite sequence of these bitwise SWAPs, or the corresponding same-support tensor SWAP in the declared finite endpoint service. Its measured descriptor normalization uses either one dedicated link meter for the complete declared $d$-level service, or the same fixed number of one-qubit services at every pair with the resulting common multiplication of the meter unit. Every pulse, lane use, padding sector and local operation is charged. Any frame conversion or local exchange from a central preparation port is executed by separately owned finite controls and kept in its own cost and timing record.

At the output apply the deterministic phase compensation of Theorem 45h.13 on the whole logical occupation/failure matrix. Its installed matrix is $U_{d_v-d_u}$ times the inverse known elapsed free phase, whose self-adjoint principal logarithm supplies an explicit positive-duration pulse. The flight and pulse parameters are fixed by the registered pair and device, independently of the unknown input. The resulting map on the full logical density is conjugation by $U_{d_v-d_u}$. Thus it sends $E_{y_u}$ to $E_{y_v}$ exactly, including any external reference, and also transports the alternate scalar preparation by the same phase law. Preparation, frame and terminal effects transport by the corresponding isometries and by the inverse encoding on their images. At the finite approximate physical grade the bounded full-reference instruments carry the funded finite errors of the common comparison. The normalized generator of the scalar port is still the actual scalar field's completed-tick operator. Controlled negative context phases take positive elapsed time and do not assert a backwards causal signal.

*Marked work response and support.* Independently freeze a positive common energy charge $E_0$ per unit physical shortcut length for the designated completed-link work coordinate, with the same physical conversion at every pair. A port can use its actual descriptor busy-time service under the common tariff. For a direct passive energy readout instead, put a fresh fuel/receiver gap pair of gap $E_0\ell_*\delta|s_{uv}|$ at the two marked endpoints. Prepare the fuel excited and receiver in its ground state, and tensor their exact SWAP with the payload's controlled transfer, on its same declared endpoint support. The fuel and receiver have equal gaps, so the pulse conserves their summed native energy and the receiver gains exactly its gap. The positive ready, timing, phase and meter controls, the spent fuel and the retained passive energy are all owned. These realize the marked direct shortcut charge $W_{uv}=E_0\ell_*A_j|r_u-r_v|$ as one actual completed-link coordinate. Other endpoint, holding, pulse and optional fiber-transport coordinates remain in the full invoice. The diagonal is the registered zero-route experiment. Hence the joint packet and work response gives
$$
1-\frac{W_{uv}^2}{4E_0^2\ell_*^2A_j^2}=\frac{r_u\cdot r_v}{2}.
\tag{F.0z.15}
$$
This is the exact normalized Gram of the marked $24$-cell. The Gram has rank four since the roots span the four coordinate directions. Every same-Gram realization is an isometric copy of that span, by factoring its positive semidefinite Gram form. In the support comparison class of Definition Z.9a, install one separately addressable positive-price coordinate service and store per declared tangent dimension, using the fixed support reservation of Theorem Z.11a. For a same-response extension with additional null coordinates, the occupied four-dimensional tests and all their packet, work and detector records stay the same, and the extra services add strictly positive ready/holding cost. The low-dimensional cell bound of Theorem Z.10, or the elementary cap bound used in Theorem Z.11, excludes $D\le3$. This gives the marked shell and least dimension in the stated support class. It does not identify the shortest-path work of the entire new graph with the old annular comparison of Theorem 45h.12, Definition 45h.14 and Theorem 45h.17. That earlier comparison uses its own complete admissible route set and physical tariff. If the operational continuum clause consumes that full earlier source rather than this common packet and marked work interface, its transport and comparator overlap remain a separate obligation.

*Strict finite curvature obstruction.* Choose a port-tree root $v_0$ at least three tree steps from all leaves, which exists for all sufficiently large grades. Write $z_0=(x_0,v_0)$. On the raw radius-two graph neighborhood choose the fiber-constant function $f(x,v)=|x_1-x_{0,1}|/\delta$ in a local unwrapped coordinate, and extend it arbitrarily elsewhere. No shortcut enters the two-step computation at $z_0$. The tree operator and tree differences vanish on this test, its axis generator and its axis carré du champ where used. In the axis operator $Lf(z_0)=2\delta^{-2}$ and $\Gamma(f)(z_0)=\delta^{-2}$. In the double-difference formula (C.6c.5.15) only the two oppositely signed ordered first-axis direction pairs contribute at $z_0$. Each corresponding second difference has magnitude $2$. Thus $\Gamma_2(f)(z_0)=2\delta^{-4}$. To obtain the dimension-four obstruction, use instead the sum of the four coordinate cusps
$$
F(x,v)=\sum_{i=1}^4|x_i-x_{0,i}|/\delta.
$$
For each coordinate the same two opposite-axis pairs contribute and mixed-axis second differences vanish. Therefore
$$
LF(z_0)=8\delta^{-2},\qquad \Gamma(F)(z_0)=4\delta^{-2},\qquad \Gamma_2(F)(z_0)=8\delta^{-4},
\qquad \tfrac14(LF(z_0))^2-\Gamma_2(F)(z_0)=8\delta^{-4}>0.
\tag{F.0z.16}
$$
The raw finite global inequality would require $K\le-2\delta^{-2}$. In particular no finite sequence $K_j\to K$ can satisfy the global dimension-four curvature hypothesis at these grades. This supplies a strict obstruction to using this particular source under the literal finite-global version of Theorem C.6c. It leaves its smooth-core and limiting integrated tests unchanged. ∎

<a id="theorem-f0z8-a-mosco-bochner-local-net-on-compared-flat-length-spaces"></a>**Theorem F.0z.8 (A Mosco–Bochner Local Net on Compared Flat Length Spaces).** The compact normal-controller reservation branch of Theorem C.6c.5c, with the persistent field and causal calibration of Theorem F.0z.6 and the marked shell of Proposition F.0z.7, supplies one complete Mosco–Bochner package of Theorem F.0d. The finite-stage length spaces for Theorem C.6c are the flat cell interpolations admitted by Theorem 44. The finite propagation forms in Definition F.0c are the actual paid-port graph forms, compared to the interpolations on the same cells. The local net has a nonconstant faithfully retained event observable and a norm-dense evolved core on every Cauchy neighborhood of a bounded diamond.

*Metric, measure and form identification.* Fix the finite nested grades and complete frozen reservation of Theorem F.0z.6, including the marked shell experiments. At grade $j$ put $n=3^{2j}$ and $\delta=n^{-1}$. Use the flat four-torus $T_j=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^4$ with its flat length metric and normalized Lebesgue measure as the length-space interpolation. The measured vertex model remains the actual port graph $X_j\times F_j$ of Theorem C.6c.5c, with its original paid metric, rates, measure and completed heat clock. Work first in dimensionless coordinates, applying the same fixed length and measure conversion of that theorem to both models. Divide each original centered grid cell into the same equal-volume subcells used in its rigidity and form comparison, one for each retained port. For a vertex function $u$, $J_ju$ is its constant value on the corresponding subcell, and $P_j=J_j^*$ is the subcell average. Thus $J_j$ is an isometry, $P_jJ_j=1$, and the subcell-to-port map sends flat volume exactly to the actual vertex mass. For every $y$ in a subcell over $x$, its flat distance to $x$ is at most $\delta$. The distance distortion of this correspondence is bounded on fixed windows by (C.6c.5.14) plus $2\delta$, uniformly in the fiber labels. It tends to zero. In particular it is the measured-GH correspondence of the actual metric, as well as the varying-space identification of the actual forms.

Apply Theorem D.6e and the graph-form comparison of Theorem C.6c.5c under $J_j,P_j$. They give Mosco convergence of the graph half-energies to $\mathrm{Ch}(f)=\tfrac12\int_T|\nabla f|^2$, and the comparison of their nonnegative form operators and semigroups under Theorem 35b.6. The limiting dense form domain is $H^1(T)$. The graph weak liminf includes arbitrary sequences of bounded graph energy and weakly convergent cell interpolates. The recovery on the entire form domain follows by smooth recovery and a diagonal, independently of the registered compact class for the finite recovery defect. The flat length-space energy is exactly $\mathrm{Ch}_{T_j}(f)=\tfrac12\int_{T_j}|\nabla f|^2$ with domain $H^1(T_j)$. Its heat generator is $\Delta$. There is no finite-energy assertion for a discontinuous cell-constant interpolant.

*Actual hypotheses of Theorem C.6c.* Identify the interpolation tori and the limiting torus by their common flat charts. Their normalized volumes, Cheeger energies, $L^2$ domains and heat semigroups agree identically in these identifications. They are complete full-support length spaces with quadratic Cheeger energy. For Sobolev-to-Lipschitz, apply periodic heat convolution to a Sobolev function with essentially bounded gradient. Its mean is unchanged and its gradient bound survives convolution, so the smoothed functions are uniformly bounded and equicontinuous on the compact torus. Arzelà–Ascoli gives a uniformly convergent subsequence as the heat times tend to zero. The $L^2$ convergence identifies its Lipschitz limit with the original function almost everywhere. On smooth functions, the actual interpolant carré du champ has
$$
\Gamma_T(f)=|\nabla f|^2,\qquad
\Gamma_{2,T}(f)=\|D^2 f\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\geq(\Delta f)^2/4.
$$
For the integrated version, first test against smooth nonnegative weights. For $f\in H^2(T)$, Fourier truncation converges in $H^2$, so the two squared expressions converge in $L^1$ and the inequality passes. Bounded admissible nonnegative weights then use their positivity-preserving periodic heat regularizations and dominated convergence, or the integration-by-parts identity for tests in the corresponding generator domain. This gives the full generator-domain $\mathrm{BE}(0,4)$ on each $T_j$, including the domain and integrability passage. The compared interpolation heat and weighted Bochner quantities have identical values at every grade, so the varying-space heat/$\Gamma$ premise of Theorem C.6c holds with $K_j=0$. The same cell identifications recover every fixed $L^2$ function since the maximal subcell diameter tends to zero. On the actual vertex graph, Corollary C.6c.5d separately transfers weighted raw curvature on smooth sampled functions and establishes its limiting generator domain. This is the two-form length-space use of Theorem 44 and Construction F.10.12i.5, with both forms realizing one candidate Cheeger limit.

The measure in physical coordinates is the normalized four-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the flat torus after the recorded volume conversion. Fixed-radius chart balls, noncollapse and graph harmonic excess are those of Theorem C.6c.5c. On the interpolants the lifted harmonic coordinates have metric coefficient matrix $I_4$ and transitions given by translations. For every fixed positive radius below the injectivity radius, their metric and volume defects and harmonic excess vanish. The same radiuswise limiting graph claims follow from (C.6c.5.14) and the raw harmonic residual and Gram estimates. This is the quantified condition of Theorem 44a, with zero limiting right side and exact smooth interpolant coefficients. The regular positive metric therefore uses the actual graph's Cheeger limit and the source charts.

*Minimal shell and selected branch.* Before the same finite-prefix reservation, install the mode assignment, physical occupation and terminal access of Proposition F.0z.7 at the selected chart. Its marked shell labels the actual $24$ normalized Bures/SLD tangent matrices of the H8 code by $r\in\Xi_{D_4}$. Its physical cells are equal-radius tangent cells with disjoint interiors. The common full occupation encoder and reference-preserving pair maps retain all registered H8 mode responses, including their visible anisotropies. A rank-four marked work Gram is realized on these physical ports, with the same four chart coordinates used in the metric comparison. The unweighted root sum is $\sum_{r\in\Xi_{D_4}}rr^{\mathsf T}=12 I_4$, so the uniform probability moment of the unit directions is $I_4/4$. The shell furnishes the isotropic feasible tensor of Theorem C.6e after its fixed-trace normalization. Freeze the complete menu and proper predictive tasks of the marked source before support selection. A faithful alternative retains the same joint reference response for each registered task and intervention, with the same forecasts and weights. Its expected predictive losses therefore agree task by task, including on the full registered response law before the support charge. By Definition Z.9a and Theorems Z.10–Z.11, the realized faithful shell has the least feasible dimension four.
