<a id="theorem-f0r-regional-semigroup-coherence-slice-generation-and-completely-positive-countermodels"></a>**Theorem F.0r (Regional Semigroup Coherence, Slice Generation and Completely Positive Countermodels).**

##### 1. Intertwining on the smaller graph core

Let $i:X_Q\to X_O$ be the actual bounded inclusion of Banach realizations of two regional $C^*$-algebras. Let $G_Q,G_O$ generate strongly continuous contraction semigroups $T_Q,T_O$. Suppose $D_Q$ is a graph core for the **smaller** generator and
$$
iD_Q\subset\operatorname{Dom}G_O,\qquad G_Oix=iG_Qx\quad(x\in D_Q).
\tag{F.0r.1}
$$
Then
$$
i\operatorname{Dom}G_Q\subset\operatorname{Dom}G_O,\qquad
G_Oi=iG_Q,\qquad T_O(t)i=iT_Q(t)\quad(t\ge0).
\tag{F.0r.2}
$$
Indeed, approximate $x\in\operatorname{Dom}G_Q$ by $x_k\in D_Q$ in the $G_Q$ graph norm. Boundedness of $i$ and closedness of $G_O$ give the domain inclusion and generator identity. For $\lambda>0$, applying that identity to $x=R(\lambda,G_Q)y$ gives $(\lambda-G_O)ix=iy$, hence $R(\lambda,G_O)i=iR(\lambda,G_Q)$. Equivalently, $u(t)=iT_Q(t)x$ is a classical solution of $u'=G_Ou$; differentiating $T_O(t-s)u(s)$ proves uniqueness. Density and contraction give (F.0r.2) on all of $X_Q$. No Hamiltonian, interaction-range or geometric-refinement premise is needed for this implication.

Equality merely on the intersection of independently chosen cores does not suffice, even with finite-dimensional $C^*$-approximants and unital algebraic cores. For an exact counterexample, put $H=\ell^2(\mathbb N)$, $\mathcal A=\mathcal K(H)+\mathbb CI$, and let $\mathcal A_n$ be the operators arbitrary on $\operatorname{span}(e_1,\ldots,e_n)$ and scalar on its orthogonal complement. Thus $\mathcal A_n\cong M_n(\mathbb C)\oplus\mathbb C$, with coherent unital isometric embeddings and norm-dense union. Construct dense algebraic subspaces $V_1,V_2\subset c_{00}$ with zero intersection as follows. Take repeated rational finite-support dense target lists with tolerances tending to zero along every repeated target. At step $k$, select its target $q_k$, tolerance $\varepsilon_k>0$, and a coordinate $r_k$ beyond the supports of all earlier choices and of $q_k$; set $v_k=q_k+\varepsilon_ke_{r_k}$. Alternate the two lists between odd and even $k$, and take the corresponding complex spans. Both spans are dense. In any finite linear relation the largest-index vector has a fresh nonzero coordinate absent from its predecessors, so all $v_k$ are independent and $V_1\cap V_2=0$.

The algebras
$$
D_i=\mathbb CI+\operatorname{span}\{|v\rangle\langle w|:v,w\in V_i\}
\tag{F.0r.3}
$$
are unital $*$-algebras in $\bigcup_n\mathcal A_n$ and norm dense in $\mathcal A$, by rank-one approximation. Their finite-rank parts have ranges in $V_i$, so $D_1\cap D_2=\mathbb CI$. Set $G_1=0$ and $G_2=i[p,\cdot]$, $p=|e_1\rangle\langle e_1|$. Both generators are bounded, so each $D_i$ is a graph core for $G_i$. They agree on the intersection, but for $x=|e_1\rangle\langle e_2|$ their evolutions give $x$ and $e^{it}x$. Their finite-stage generators are their actual restrictions. This counterexample concerns the stated direct-sum approximants; it is not a full-matrix independent-event source witness.

##### 2. Precisely sufficient slice-invariance hypotheses

Let
$$
\mathcal A_N=C^*\bigl(\mathcal A(Q):Q\subset N\text{ a retained small region}\bigr).
\tag{F.0r.4}
$$
The localized slice core is assumed to lie in $\mathcal A_N$. Suppose a faithfully retained independent event outside $N$ contains a nontrivial projection $p$. Two product states agreeing on $\mathcal A_N$ and giving $p$ the values $0,1$ imply
$$
\operatorname{dist}(p,\mathcal A_N)\ge\tfrac12.
\tag{F.0r.5}
$$
This includes an abelian nontrivial event factor. Under the genuine regional intertwining of part 1, each of the following conditions suffices for $T_t\mathcal A_N\subset\mathcal A_N$:

1. $N$ itself has a regional semigroup whose inclusion intertwines the common evolution;
2. the common evolution is multiplicative at every retained time;
3. at each retained time, every generating $\mathcal A(Q)$ is in the multiplicative domain of the common UCP map $T_t$.

The first assertion is (F.0r.2). In the second, invariance of each generator algebra extends to finite products, linear combinations and norm closure. In the third, the multiplicative domain is a $C^*$-subalgebra containing all the generator algebras, and the same argument applies. A UCP map homomorphic on a $C^*$-subalgebra has that subalgebra in its multiplicative domain, by the two Schwarz equality conditions. Consequently the evolved slice core cannot generate an outer algebra containing $p$, because of (F.0r.5). Multiplicative forward endomorphisms and reversible interacting automorphisms are included, without a propagation-attainment assumption. On an every-slice local realization, a thin Cauchy neighborhood avoiding any chosen surviving event gives the corresponding scalar-only conclusion on these branches. This is a statement about these slice-invariance hypotheses, not a classification of all dissipative evolutions or a nontrivial-source realization of a scalar net.

##### 3. An explicit seven-event countermodel to the UCP product step

In $3+1$ Minkowski coordinates, with $c=1$, put six share events at $a_{j,\pm}=(0,\pm e_j)$, $j=1,2,3$, and a future event at $z=(1/4,0)$. Put one qubit at each event and assign the full tensor algebra of exactly the events belonging to each region. Every open diamond containing all six share events contains $z$. To verify this, if its future tip is $(q_0,y)$, then
$$
q_0>\max_{j,\pm}|y\mp e_j|
=\sqrt{|y|^2+1+2\max_j|y_j|}\ge |y|+1/\sqrt3.
\tag{F.0r.6}
$$
The last inequality follows by squaring and $\max_j|y_j|\ge |y|/\sqrt3$. Therefore $q_0-1/4>|y|$. The past-tip inequality likewise puts $z$ in its chronological future. Two shares alone would not provide this margin in three spatial dimensions.

For $r=X,Z$, define $P_s^r=(I+sr_z)/2$ and, on the six shares $S$,
$$
K_{s,\varepsilon}^{r}=2^{-5/2}\bigotimes_{j\in S}r_j^{\varepsilon_j}\otimes P_s^r,
\quad\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^6,\quad (-1)^{\sum_j\varepsilon_j}=s.
\tag{F.0r.7}
$$
There are $32$ words for each $s$. These self-adjoint Kraus operators satisfy $\sum K^*K=I$, so $\Phi_r(A)=\sum K^*AK$ is UCP. The generator and semigroup
$$
L=(\Phi_X-I)+(\Phi_Z-I),\qquad T_t=e^{tL}
\tag{F.0r.8}
$$
are genuine finite-dimensional nonmultiplicative autonomous dynamics. Each summand is the Lindblad dissipator $\Phi_r(A)-\tfrac12\{I,A\}$; its Poisson expansion is UCP, and the product formula gives the same for their sum.

On any proper share subset, the parity-conditioned word distribution has a uniform marginal independent of $s$. Thus $\Phi_r$ restricts there to the product of the $r$-dephasing maps. A subset already containing $z$ is preserved directly by the Kraus formula. The only potentially noninvariant subset is all six shares without $z$, and (F.0r.6) excludes it as a diamond. Hence every diamond algebra is invariant under both the generator and semigroup. Their actual restricted generators agree on inclusions, and every regional domain and graph core is its entire finite algebra.

Nevertheless, with $P=X_1\cdots X_6$ and $Q=Z_1\cdots Z_6$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
&\Phi_Z(P)=PZ_z,\quad \Phi_Z(PZ_z)=P,\quad
\Phi_X(P)=P,\quad\Phi_X(PZ_z)=0,\\
&L(P)=-P+PZ_z,\qquad L(PZ_z)=P-2PZ_z.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.0r.9}
$$
The same block holds on $Q,QX_z$. The matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-1&1\\1&-2\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
T_tP&=a(t)P+b(t)PZ_z,&T_tQ&=a(t)Q+b(t)QX_z,\\
a(t)&=e^{-3t/2}\!\left[\cosh\frac{\sqrt5t}{2}+\frac1{\sqrt5}\sinh\frac{\sqrt5t}{2}\right],&
b(t)&=\frac2{\sqrt5}e^{-3t/2}\sinh\frac{\sqrt5t}{2}>0\quad(t>0).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.0r.10}
$$
A thin time-zero slice neighborhood contains the shares but not $z$. Its algebra and its evolved elements generate
$$
Z_z=\frac{P T_tP-a(t)I}{b(t)},\qquad
X_z=\frac{Q T_tQ-a(t)I}{b(t)}.
\tag{F.0r.11}
$$
They therefore generate the full seven-qubit algebra; the recovered future algebra is noncentral, since $\|[X_z,Z_z]\|=2$. Individual diamond invariance alone does not imply invariance of the algebra generated by a slice cover.

There is also a one-channel version isolating the same logical failure. Put $P=Z_1\cdots Z_6$, $\omega_s=2^{-6}(I+sP)$ and $\Pi_s^z=(I+sZ_z)/2$. The measure-and-prepare channel
$$
\Phi_*(\rho)=\sum_{s=\pm1}\operatorname{tr}[(I_S\otimes\Pi_s^z)\rho]\,
\omega_s\otimes I_z/2
\tag{F.0r.12}
$$
is CPTP. Every proper share marginal of $\omega_s$ is maximally mixed; its dual maps any observable on a subset missing a share, even if that subset includes $z$, to its normalized trace times $I$. It preserves every diamond algebra. But $\Phi(P)=Z_z$, $\Phi(Z_z)=0$ and $\Phi(I)=I$, so for $L=\Phi-I$ the Poisson expansion gives
$$
T_tP=e^{-t}P+te^{-t}Z_z,\qquad
\|[T_tP,X_z]\|=2te^{-t}.
\tag{F.0r.13}
$$
It recovers a nontrivial future projection from the slice, though not the full future matrix algebra.

Both countermodels fail the physical precone comparison if their fixed-distance experiment is retained under refinement. In (F.0r.10), $\|[T_tP,X_z]\|=2b(t)>0$ at every $t>0$; (F.0r.13) has the same immediate influence. For $a_nd_n(S,z)\to r>0$ and $a_nv_n\to c>0$, any fixed $0<t<r/c$ makes the physical LR upper bound tend to zero while these commutators remain positive. They are not continuum, every-Cauchy-slice or MPU/PCE source witnesses. Shrinking the entire gadget removes this fixed macroscopic future factor rather than furnishing those missing properties.

##### 4. A valid infinitesimal support criterion

Let $A\in\operatorname{Dom}G$ have genuinely finite event support $S$. If the actual physical comparison gives $[T_tA,B]=0$ on $0\le t<\tau$ for a complementary observable $B$ at positive separation, then division by $t$ and the norm derivative give $[GA,B]=0$. To infer $GA\in\mathcal B_S$ one needs the actual full-complement relative-commutant identity; testing only a retained abelian algebra does not establish it.

If every finite event algebra $\mathcal B_S$ is finite dimensional, lies entirely in $\operatorname{Dom}G$, and satisfies $G\mathcal B_S\subset\mathcal B_S$, then its bounded restriction generates $u(t)=\exp(tG|_{\mathcal B_S})A$, a classical solution of the full equation. Semigroup uniqueness gives $T_t\mathcal B_S\subset\mathcal B_S$, and finite-tensor density gives region invariance. The three hypotheses cannot be deleted: collocated refinement can produce infinite AF fibres; a norm-dense algebraic graph core need not contain each whole finite-stage algebra; and bounded norm difference quotients need not converge in the $C^*$-norm. This criterion and parts 1–3 delimit the regional-coherence argument. Theorems F.0m/F.0o provide separate support-invariance results using their actual quantitative source hypotheses. $\square$

<a id="proposition-f0s-collocated-refinement-and-bounded-generator-precone-rigidity"></a>**Proposition F.0s (Collocated Refinement and Bounded-Generator Precone Rigidity).**

##### 1. Exact membership can retain unbounded event fibres

Condition on any supplied finite geometric sequence $(V_k,f_k,\mu_k)$ whose positive weighted image measures converge weakly to a full-support nonatomic measure on a compact metric space $M$, with asymptotically dense image and its stated uniformly vanishing metric-comparison error. There is a subsequence $k_n$ and maps $g_n:V_{k_n}\to M$ satisfying
$$
\sup_{v\in V_{k_n}}d(g_n(v),f_{k_n}(v))\longrightarrow0
\tag{F.0s.1}
$$
for which the finite image sets $P_n=g_n(V_{k_n})$ are nested and every persistent image point has a fibre whose cardinality tends to infinity. With one qubit per vertex, there are exact coherent unital isometric tensor embeddings preserving membership in **every** region defined by those image points. The underlying graphs, their metric/form data and their original form-interpolation maps are unchanged.

Here is the construction. The largest atom of $(f_k)_*\mu_k$ tends to zero: otherwise a subsequence of atoms with mass at least $\varepsilon>0$ has locations converging by compactness to $p$; the closed-ball bound for weak convergence gives mass at least $\varepsilon$ in every closed ball about $p$, contradicting non-atomicity. Thus the largest vertex weight also tends to zero. Every fixed open ball has positive limiting mass by full support, so, by the open-set weak-limit bound and the vanishing largest vertex weight, it contains arbitrarily many vertices at sufficiently late stages.

Suppose $P_{n-1}$ and its old fibre sizes $m_{n-1}(p)$ have been fixed. Choose pairwise disjoint balls about its finitely many points with radius at most $\varepsilon_n\downarrow0$. Select $k_n$ so late that each ball contains at least $m_{n-1}(p)+n$ vertices. Send these selected vertices exactly to $p$ and leave all other locations at $f_{k_n}(v)$. This defines $g_n$; accidental repetitions only enlarge its fibres. The old points remain in its image, each old fibre embeds injectively into the new fibre at the same point, and the unused qubits receive identities. Compose these chosen tensor-identity embeddings at later stages to obtain exact coherence. Every regional membership factor is preserved because every old qubit stays at its exact old location. Equation (F.0s.1) preserves the supplied weak measure and uniform metric-comparison limits. It makes no assertion about derivatives of the newly rounded coordinate maps, nor does it identify the unchanged Hilbert-form generator with the observable generator.

For a compatible bounded onsite example, put a Pauli $Z$ of norm one on every microscopic qubit and use the sum of these onsite Hamiltonians with the same fixed clock. The tensor embeddings intertwine their derivations exactly, product traces are compatible, and every event/region algebra is invariant. Nevertheless, a completed fibre containing arbitrarily many qubits has unbounded generator: for the norm-one product $A_N=\sigma_1^+\cdots\sigma_N^+$,
$$
\left\|i\left[\sum_{j=1}^NZ_j,A_N\right]\right\|=2N.
\tag{F.0s.2}
$$
Uniform microscopic onsite strength is therefore not a uniform bound on a completed event-fibre generator. The example does not satisfy nontrivial evolved time-slice generation and does not construct a missing geometric or MPU source.

##### 2. A uniformly bounded full generator cannot acquire a finite precone onset

Let $A_n,B_n$ have uniformly bounded norms and let $L_n$ be bounded linear maps on the actual normed observable realizations with
$$
\sup_n\|L_n\|\le M<\infty.
\tag{F.0s.3}
$$
Write $F_n(z)=[e^{zL_n}A_n,B_n]$. If $\|F_n(t)\|\to0$ on a nonempty real interval, or on a real set with an accumulation point, then $\|F_n(t)\|\to0$ uniformly on every compact real time interval. No positivity or quadratic structure is needed.

To prove this, the entire extension satisfies $\|F_n(z)\|\le2ABe^{M|z|}$, where $A,B$ are the uniform input bounds. If compact-uniform convergence failed, take $t_n$ in a fixed compact set with $\|F_n(t_n)\|\ge\varepsilon$, pass to $t_n\to t_*$, and choose norm-one complex linear functionals $\varphi_n$ detecting at least $\varepsilon/2$. The scalar entire functions $f_n(z)=\varphi_nF_n(z)$ have Taylor coefficients bounded by $2ABM^k/k!$. A diagonal subsequence of coefficients, with these summable bounds on every compact disk, converges compact-uniformly to an entire $f$. It vanishes on the assumed interval or accumulation set, and hence identically by the identity theorem. The same uniform convergence and $t_n\to t_*$ imply $f_n(t_n)\to0$, contradicting their choice. This proves the assertion.

This statement concerns a **full-generator** bound. A per-site bound, even with bounded degree, does not bound the full $\|L_n\|$ in a growing volume, as part 1 already illustrates. It is not a universal physical-locality obstruction for an unbounded continuum generator. Separately, Corollary F.1a already gives $c_n=r_0\delta_{\mathrm{eff},n}/\tau_{\min}$: on its literal fixed-$r_0$, fixed-positive-clock branch with $\delta_{\mathrm{eff},n}=a_n\to0$, this slope tends to zero. Inflating a distinct LR upper bound does not alter that actual strict clock identity. An alternative scale or clock must be compared through its own specified maps. $\square$

*   <a id="definition-f3-emergent-local-net-and-promotion-conditions"></a>**Definition F.3 (Emergent Local Net and Promotion Conditions).** On a branch satisfying Theorem F.0, Theorem F.0d, or Theorem F.0f, the limit is a local $C^*$-net $\mathcal O\mapsto\mathfrak A(\mathcal O)$ on $(M,g_{\mu\nu})$ with the properties proved by the invoked theorem. A standard relativistic Haag--Kastler or Wightman promotion additionally requires the reversible representation, invariant vacuum, spectrum, covariance, and field-domain entries stated in Definition F.0h; a dissipative contraction semigroup is not itself a Haag--Kastler dynamics.

**F.4 Admissible States and Dynamics**

*   **Admissible continuum states:** A state on $\mathfrak A=\overline{\bigcup_{\mathcal O}\mathfrak A(\mathcal O)}$ is a positive normalized linear functional $\omega:\mathfrak A\to\mathbb C$. A compatible locally normal microscopic family supplies a continuum state through the state-convergence clause of Theorem F.0. If only subsequential compactness is proved, every cluster point is admissible and no unique state is selected. A unique vacuum, KMS state, or realized state requires its own invariance, spectral or KMS, faithfulness, and strict-selection certificate.

*   **Emergent dynamics generator:** On the common local core, Theorem F.0 determines the full limiting Heisenberg generator. Only a branch carrying compatible regional microscopic GKLS decompositions and separate domain-preserving convergence certificates for their coherent and completely positive dissipative parts may write the certified split
    $$
    \mathcal L_{\mathrm{cont}}^*
    =
    i[H_{\mathrm{cont}},\cdot]+\mathcal D_{\mathrm{cont}}^*.
    $$
    *   **Hamiltonian part:** Convergence of the full generator in (F.0.1) does not select a Hamiltonian component, because a GKLS coherent/dissipative decomposition has gauge freedom. A branch may define $H_{\mathrm{cont}}$ only after it fixes one microscopic decomposition on every region and supplies a separate compatible strong-resolvent certificate for the coherent operators. It vanishes only under a further cancellation condition proving $\Phi_b(H_{b,\mathcal O})=z_b(\mathcal O)I+o(1)$ in the declared local operator topology.
    *   **Dissipative part:** $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{cont}}^*$ is obtained only from a microscopic completely positive generator and a convergence certificate that preserves complete positivity, domains, and the semigroup law. The registered-reset inequality $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{phys}}\ge H_q(P\mid R)$ bounds heat for an identified reset; it neither constructs nor normalizes a GKLS generator. A Schwinger--Keldysh description is available only on the separate Appendix X.5 branch carrying its effective-action, noise, dissipation, regularization, and convergence records.

**F.5 Rigorous Definition of $T_{\mu\nu}^{(MPU)}$**

AQFT allows for a rigorous, state-dependent definition of the macroscopic MPU stress-energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}^{(MPU)}$ as an operator-valued distribution, capturing the energy and momentum content of the emergent fields derived from the MPU network activity.

*   <a id="definition-f4-macroscopic-t_munumpu-in-aqft"></a>**Definition F.4 (Macroscopic $T_{\mu\nu}^{(MPU)}$ in AQFT):** Within the emergent AQFT framework of Definition F.3, assume that the branch supplies the renormalized stress-energy distribution, the effective-action hypotheses of Theorem X.5a, and the variational-identification hypotheses of Theorem B.8c, and absolute continuity $\mathbf T\ll dV_g$ of its limiting stress measure. On this branch the macroscopic MPU stress-energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}^{(\mathrm{MPU})}(x)$ has two consistent representations:
    1.  **As Expectation Value:** As the expectation value of a symmetric, operator-valued distribution $\hat{\Theta}_{\mu\nu}(x)$ affiliated with the algebra $\mathfrak{A}$. This distribution $\hat{\Theta}_{\mu\nu}(x)$ represents the continuum limit of the microscopic symmetric tensor operator $\hat{\Theta}_{\mu\nu}^{(MPU)}(v)$ (defined in Theorem B.4, Appendix B). This requires a process of regularization and renormalization in the continuum limit. $T_{\mu\nu}^{(\mathrm{MPU})}(x) = \omega(\hat{\Theta}_{\mu\nu}(x))$, where $\omega$ is the physical state (Section F.4). This definition connects the macroscopic tensor to the underlying MPU activity and costs.
    2.  **Via Variation of the Derived Effective Action:** Under its seven stated hypotheses on the regular Lorentzian branch, Theorem X.5a constructs a generally covariant coarse-grained effective action $S_{\mathrm{eff}}[\omega,g]$. The stress-energy tensor is therefore variationally defined, with the sign convention matching Equations (B.15a), (B.21), and (67e), by
        $$
        T^{\mu\nu}_{(\mathrm{MPU})}(x)
        :=
        \frac{2}{\sqrt{-g(x)}}\,
        \frac{\delta S_{\mathrm{eff}}[\omega,g]}{\delta g_{\mu\nu}(x)},
        \qquad
        T_{\mu\nu}^{(\mathrm{MPU})}(x)
        =
        -\frac{2}{\sqrt{-g(x)}}\,
        \frac{\delta S_{\mathrm{eff}}[\omega,g]}{\delta g^{\mu\nu}(x)}
        \tag{F.3}
        $$
        The second equality follows from
        $$
        \delta g^{\alpha\beta}
        =
        -g^{\alpha\mu}g^{\beta\nu}\delta g_{\mu\nu}.
        $$
        Under hypotheses (H B.8c.1)–(H B.8c.3) and the additional absolute-continuity premise $\mathbf T\ll dV_g$, Theorem B.8c (Variational Identification) identifies this variational tensor with the coarse-grained expectation-value tensor of Appendix B.
    Agreement of the two representations follows on this variational-identification branch. On-shell covariant conservation additionally follows under the hypotheses of Theorem F.1.

*   <a id="theorem-f1-covariant-conservation-of-t_munumpu-in-aqft"></a>**Theorem F.1 (Covariant Conservation of $T_{\mu\nu}^{(MPU)}$ in AQFT).** Assuming the effective action $S_{\mathrm{eff}}[\omega, g]$ is generally covariant (invariant under diffeomorphisms of $M$), the variationally defined stress-energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}^{(\mathrm{MPU})}(x)$ (Equation F.3) is covariantly conserved ($\nabla^{\mu} T_{\mu\nu}^{(\mathrm{MPU})} = 0$) when the emergent dynamical equations for the state $\omega$ (derived from $\delta S_{\mathrm{eff}} / \delta \omega = 0$) and the geometry $g_{\mu\nu}$ (if it is also dynamical) are satisfied (on-shell).

*Proof:* Let $\xi^\mu$ be a smooth compactly supported vector field on $M$ generating an infinitesimal diffeomorphism. General covariance of the effective action means
$$
\delta_\xi S_{\mathrm{eff}}[\omega,g]=0.
$$
On shell, the variation with respect to the state $\omega$ vanishes by the emergent equations of motion, so only the metric variation contributes. Using the covariant-metric form of Equation (F.3),
$$
\frac{1}{\sqrt{-g}}\frac{\delta S_{\mathrm{eff}}}{\delta g_{\mu\nu}}
=
\frac12 T^{\mu\nu}_{(\mathrm{MPU})},
$$
hence
$$
0=\delta_\xi S_{\mathrm{eff}}
=\frac{1}{2}\int_M d^4x\,\sqrt{-g}\,T^{\mu\nu}_{(\mathrm{MPU})}\,\delta_\xi g_{\mu\nu}.
$$
For an infinitesimal diffeomorphism,
$$
\delta_\xi g_{\mu\nu}=\nabla_\mu \xi_\nu+\nabla_\nu \xi_\mu.
$$
Since the variational stress-energy tensor is symmetric in its indices,
$$
0=\int_M d^4x\,\sqrt{-g}\,T^{\mu\nu}_{(\mathrm{MPU})}\nabla_\mu \xi_\nu.
$$
Integrating by parts and using the compact support of $\xi$ to remove the boundary term gives
$$
0=-\int_M d^4x\,\sqrt{-g}\,\bigl(\nabla_\mu T^{\mu}{}_{\nu\,(\mathrm{MPU})}\bigr)\xi^\nu.
$$
Because $\xi^\nu$ is arbitrary, the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations implies
$$
\nabla_\mu T^{\mu}{}_{\nu\,(\mathrm{MPU})}=0.
$$
Thus the variationally defined stress-energy tensor is covariantly conserved on shell. ∎

<a id="theorem-f0t-weighted-local-superoperator-localization-without-a-target-size-factor"></a>**Theorem F.0t (Weighted Local-Superoperator Localization without a Target-Size Factor).** On a finite graph $G=(V,E)$, let the observable carrier be $B(\bigotimes_{x\in V}\mathcal H_x)$ and $L=\sum_ZL_Z$, where each $L_Z$ is a supported Heisenberg Lindblad generator. Thus $L_Z(I)=0$, and deleting any collection of terms leaves a UCP contraction semigroup. Coherent terms $i[h_Z,\cdot]$ are included. All superoperator norms below are the norms after their actual tensor extension to this finite carrier. Put
$$
\ell_Z=\|L_Z\|_{\infty\to\infty},\qquad
K_\mu=\sup_{x\in V}\sum_{Z\ni x}|Z|\ell_Ze^{\mu\operatorname{diam}_GZ}.
\tag{F.0t.1}
$$
For an observable $A$ supported on $X$ and any supported linear superoperator $K_Y$ with $K_Y(I)=0$, $X\cap Y=\varnothing$, one has, for $\mu>0$ and $t\ge0$,
$$
\|K_Ye^{tL}A\|\le\|K_Y\|\,\|A\|\,|X|e^{-\mu d_G(X,Y)}(e^{K_\mu t}-1).
\tag{F.0t.2}
$$
If every term has graph diameter at most $r>0$, then the stronger bound is
$$
\|K_Ye^{tL}A\|\le\|K_Y\|\,\|A\|\,|X|
\sum_{k\ge\lceil d_G(X,Y)/r\rceil}\frac{(K_0t)^k}{k!}.
\tag{F.0t.3}
$$
For $r=0$ the left side is zero. No target-cardinality, total-volume or on-site-dimension factor occurs, and no multiplicative property of $e^{tL}$ is required. For a bounded-degree family with fixed range, $J=\sup_{n,x}\sum_{Z\ni x}\ell_{n,Z}$ and a uniform graph-$r$ ball bound $q$ imply $K_\mu\le qJe^{\mu r}$. Under the local Hamiltonian/GKLS bounds of F.0, $J\le2J_H+J_D$ on the same physical clock. This is the local-superoperator method of Poulin (2010) and Barthel–Kliesch (2012), with its complete autonomous path proof here.

**Proof.** For a set $W$ define
$$
C_A(W,t)=\sup\{\|Ke^{tL}A\|:K\text{ supported on }W,\ K(I)=0,\ \|K\|\le1\}.
$$
Let $L_{W^c}$ sum the terms disjoint from $W$. It generates contractions and commutes with each such $K$. Duhamel's equation for $Ke^{tL}A$ therefore gives
$$
C_A(W,t)\le\|A\|1_{W\cap X\ne\varnothing}
+\sum_{Z\cap W\ne\varnothing}\ell_Z\int_0^tC_A(Z,s)\,ds.
\tag{F.0t.4}
$$
A nonzero term $L_Z/\ell_Z$ belongs to the defining class on $Z$, which justifies the second term. Also $C_A(W,t)\le\|A\|$ by contractivity. Iterate (F.0t.4). At a fixed finite stage the remainder tends to zero, since the finite total norm sum is dominated by the time-simplex factorial. A surviving length-$k$ path obeys
$$
Z_1\cap Y\ne\varnothing,\quad Z_i\cap Z_{i+1}\ne\varnothing,\quad Z_k\cap X\ne\varnothing,
\qquad d_G(X,Y)\le\sum_i\operatorname{diam}_GZ_i.
$$
Put $w_Z=\ell_Ze^{\mu\operatorname{diam}_GZ}$ and reverse the path, starting at $X$. Its weighted total is at most $|X|K_\mu^k$. Indeed a last continuation from $W$ has total at most $|W|K_\mu$; at every preceding step the factor $|Z|$ is absorbed by $\sup_x\sum_{Z\ni x}|Z|w_Z\le K_\mu$. The endpoint requirement of meeting $Y$ only reduces the sum. Factoring out $e^{-\mu d_G(X,Y)}$ and summing $t^k/k!$ proves (F.0t.2). Fixed range requires $k\ge\lceil d_G(X,Y)/r\rceil$ and uses the same argument at $\mu=0$, proving (F.0t.3). At zero range, disjoint factors cannot be connected.

Let $E_{Y^c}$ be normalized partial trace over $Y$, tensored with its identity. Then $I-E_{Y^c}$ is supported on $Y$, annihilates $I$ and has norm at most two. Thus
$$
\operatorname{dist}(e^{tL}A,B(\mathcal H_{Y^c})\otimes I_Y)
\le\|e^{tL}A-E_{Y^c}e^{tL}A\|
\le2\|A\|\,|X|e^{-\mu d_G(X,Y)}(e^{K_\mu t}-1),
\tag{F.0t.5}
$$
with the same factorial replacement. These are ambient norm approximants; neither multiplicativity of this expectation nor refinement compatibility is assumed. Hamiltonian evolution admits either sign of physical time by changing the generator sign; general dissipative evolution uses nonnegative time. ∎

<a id="proposition-f0u-compact-chart-counts-weak-tail-truncation-and-the-weighted-moment-boundary"></a>**Proposition F.0u (Compact-Chart Counts, Weak-Tail Truncation and the Weighted-Moment Boundary).** Consider bounded-degree finite regional graphs $V_n$ with $a_n\downarrow0$ and actual location maps into a fixed compact metric set $(K,d_K)$. Suppose the same physical metric and graph comparison satisfy
$$
b_-a_nd_{G_n}(x,y)\le d_n^{\mathrm{phys}}(x,y)\le b_+a_nd_{G_n}(x,y),\qquad
|d_n^{\mathrm{phys}}(x,y)-d_K(f_nx,f_ny)|\le\eta_n\longrightarrow0,
\quad0<b_-\le b_+<\infty.
\tag{F.0u.1}
$$
Then
$$
a_n\log\max(1,|V_n|)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{F.0u.2}
$$
In particular arbitrary bounded-norm representatives in the chart have subexponential support cardinality. On a uniformly weighted-moment family as in Theorem F.0t, observables whose actual label supports have a fixed positive metric separation from a target event have ambient outside-target norm approximants with error tending to zero on every bounded physical-time window.

If instead the actual interaction satisfies only the aggregate tail
$$
\sup_{n,x}\sum_{Z\ni x,\,\operatorname{diam}Z\ge R}\ell_{n,Z}
\le Je^{-\kappa R},\qquad\kappa>0,
\tag{F.0u.3}
$$
deleting terms of diameter greater than $R$ gives
$$
\|e^{tL_n}-e^{tL_n^{\le R}}\|_{\infty\to\infty}
\le t|V_n|Je^{-\kappa R}.
\tag{F.0u.4}
$$
There is a choice $R_n\to\infty$ with $a_nR_n\to0$ for which this error tends to zero uniformly on bounded physical times. Aggregate decay alone still does not imply a uniform $K_\mu$ in (F.0t.1), even with the genuine metric comparison and subexponential collocated supports. The counterexample and the precise sufficient support-growth condition are given in the proof.

**Proof. I. Entire-chart cardinality and localization.** A degree bound $\Delta$ supplies constants $C_\Delta,\kappa_\Delta$ with $|B_G(x,R)|\le C_\Delta e^{\kappa_\Delta R}$, uniformly in the graphs; one may take $B=\max(2,\Delta+1)$, $C_\Delta=B^2$, $\kappa_\Delta=\log B$ by counting paths. Cover the compact set by $M_\epsilon$ metric balls of radius $\epsilon$, independently of $n$. In each nonempty preimage choose a vertex. Every other vertex in that preimage is at physical distance at most $2\epsilon+\eta_n$, and therefore lies in a graph ball of radius $(2\epsilon+\eta_n)/(b_-a_n)$. Hence
$$
|V_n|\le M_\epsilon C_\Delta
\exp\left[\frac{\kappa_\Delta(2\epsilon+\eta_n)}{b_-a_n}\right].
$$
Take $a_n$ times its logarithm, then $\limsup_n$, then $\epsilon\downarrow0$. This proves (F.0u.2) without polynomial volume growth, lower atom masses or a microscopic convergence rate.

For finitely many exact event labels $P$, every nonempty fibre $F_n(p)=f_n^{-1}(p)$ lies in a graph ball of radius $\eta_n/(b_-a_n)$. Thus $a_n\log|\bigcup_{p\in P}F_n(p)|\to0$ as well. If $d_K(P,q)\ge d_*>0$, the same comparison gives
$$
d_{G_n}\left(\bigcup_{p\in P}F_n(p),F_n(q)\right)
\ge\frac{d_*-\eta_n}{b_+a_n}.
\tag{F.0u.5}
$$
Exact all-open-region-preserving tensor embeddings pin each old site algebra to its same-label fine fibre: choose a small open region containing the old event but excluding each distinct fine event, use preservation of that regional algebra, then intersect the finite tensor supports. Finite products give the union for finitely many old sites. No finite limiting fibre is assumed. Alternatively actual representatives may have arbitrary supports inside the whole compact chart as long as the stated label separation holds. Insert the support count and (F.0u.5), or its separated-support version, in (F.0t.5). For bounded observable norm and $0\le t\le T$, the logarithm of the bound multiplied by $a_n$ has upper limit at most $-\mu d_*/b_+<0$. This proves the asserted localization. Faithful retained transfer and the Cauchy-neighborhood arguments have their separate native proofs in Theorems F.0m and F.0o.

**II. Whole-regional truncation.** Both the full and term-deleted semigroups are contractions. Their Duhamel difference is bounded by $t\sum_{\operatorname{diam}Z>R}\ell_{n,Z}$. Count each omitted term through at least one of its sites and use (F.0u.3) to obtain (F.0u.4). Set
$$
R_n=\kappa^{-1}(\log\max(1,|V_n|)+g_n),\qquad
 g_n\to\infty,\quad a_ng_n\to0.
\tag{F.0u.6}
$$
Equation (F.0u.2) gives $a_nR_n\to0$, and the uniform error is at most $TJ e^{-g_n}$. Integer ceilings preserve these conclusions. Thus the aggregate-tail dynamics have a uniform approximation by dynamics of vanishing *physical* range. Their graph ranges can diverge, and their path constants need not remain bounded, so this is not a substitution of varying-range generators into a fixed-graph-range theorem.

**III. Exact failure of the proposed moment implication.** Attach a complete binary tree of height $R_n$ at a root of a bounded-degree approximating base graph, with $R_n\to\infty$ and $a_nR_n\to0$. Give every added vertex the root's label. The metric distortion increases by at most $2a_nR_n$; degrees remain bounded. Positive vertex masses may have total tending to zero, or redistribute the root's former mass, preserving the corresponding measured metric limit. This tests those degree/metric/cardinality consequences, not the entire original physical-source certificate.

Let $Z_n$ be the full tree and give it one Lindblad term of exact norm $\ell_n=e^{-2\kappa R_n}$. A nontrivial tensor-product Pauli unitary $U_n$ gives the explicit generator $(\ell_n/2)(U_n^*(\cdot)U_n-\operatorname{id})$ of that norm. Its support diameter is $2R_n$, and at every site at most this one term is present. For a threshold not exceeding $2R_n$ its norm is at most $e^{-\kappa R}$; above it the tail is zero. Thus (F.0u.3) holds with $J=1$. But $|Z_n|\ge2^{R_n}$ gives
$$
|Z_n|\ell_ne^{\mu\operatorname{diam}Z_n}
\ge\exp[(\log2-2\kappa+2\mu)R_n].
\tag{F.0u.7}
$$
For $0<\kappa<(\log2)/2$, this diverges for every $\mu>0$, while $a_n\log|Z_n|=O(a_nR_n)\to0$. This nearly stationary example refutes the inference to the weighted moment, not continuum transport or the stronger support-invariance proof of Theorem F.0m.

**IV. A quantitative sufficient subclass.** If actual supports obey $|Z|\le C e^{\beta\operatorname{diam}Z}$, integer diameter shells and (F.0u.3) give, for $0<\mu<\kappa-\beta$,
$$
K_\mu\le CJ\sum_{r\ge0}e^{-(\kappa-\beta-\mu)r}
=\frac{CJ}{1-e^{-(\kappa-\beta-\mu)}}<\infty.
\tag{F.0u.8}
$$
Bounded degree supplies an exponential support bound, so aggregate decay faster than that growth suffices. Bounded arity or polynomial support growth $|Z|\le C(1+\operatorname{diam}Z)^p$ instead gives $K_\mu\le CJ\sum_{r\ge0}(1+r)^pe^{-(\kappa-\mu)r}<\infty$ for every $0<\mu<\kappa$. These are quantitative implications for the stated inputs; they do not strengthen an unquantified original locality premise. ∎

<a id="theorem-f1b-finite-variational-stress-identification-and-counterterm-fiber"></a>**Theorem F.1b (Finite Variational Stress Identification and Counterterm Fiber).** Let $g=(g^1,\ldots,g^m)$ be finite regulator metric coordinates, let $H(g)$ be a differentiable finite Hamiltonian, and let $\rho(g)$ be a differentiable stationary state for
$$
\Gamma(g,\rho)=\operatorname{tr}[\rho H(g)]+\mathcal R(g,\rho),
\qquad
D_\rho\Gamma(g,\rho(g))[\dot\rho]=0
\quad\text{for every admissible tangent }\dot\rho.
\tag{F.1b.1}
$$
Assume also that every parameter derivative $\partial_a\rho(g)$ is an admissible tangent.
Then the on-shell effective action $\Gamma_{\mathrm{os}}(g)=\Gamma(g,\rho(g))$ obeys the exact Hellmann--Feynman identity
$$
\partial_a\Gamma_{\mathrm{os}}
=
\operatorname{tr}[\rho(g)\partial_aH(g)]
+
\partial_a\mathcal R(g,\rho(g)).
\tag{F.1b.2}
$$
Thus microscopic expectation and metric variation coincide on the regulator exactly when the explicit regularization term in (F.1b.2) is included in the microscopic stress record.

If a finite symmetry acts infinitesimally as $\delta g=R\xi$ and leaves $\Gamma_{\mathrm{os}}$ invariant, its exact Ward identity is
$$
R^{\mathsf T}\nabla_g\Gamma_{\mathrm{os}}=0.
\tag{F.1b.3}
$$
If admissible local counterterms form a finite vector space $\mathcal C$ and $V:C\mapsto\nabla_gC$ is their stress-variation map, all renormalized stresses compatible with one bare record form the affine fiber
$$
T_0+\operatorname{im}V.
\tag{F.1b.4}
$$
For a prescribed normalization value $b$, require the affine constraint set
$$
\{T\in T_0+\operatorname{im}V:N(T)=b\}
$$
to be nonempty. It then contains exactly one stress if and only if the linear normalization map $N$ is injective on $\operatorname{im}V$. Without the nonemptiness premise, injectivity gives at most one stress.

*Proof.* The chain rule for $\Gamma(g,\rho(g))$ has a state-variation term $D_\rho\Gamma[\partial_a\rho]$, which vanishes because $\partial_a\rho$ is an admissible tangent and the state is stationary. This gives (F.1b.2), with $\partial_a\mathcal R$ denoting the explicit parameter derivative with the state held constant. Differentiating symmetry invariance gives (F.1b.3), and linear counterterm gradients give (F.1b.4). Choose an admissible normalized stress $T_*$ in the nonempty constraint set. Every other such stress differs from $T_*$ by an element of $\ker N\cap\operatorname{im}V$, and every such difference gives another admissible stress. Thus the constraint set is the affine space $T_*+(\ker N\cap\operatorname{im}V)$, a singleton exactly when that intersection is zero. This is equivalent to injectivity of $N$ on $\operatorname{im}V$. ∎

The theorem is exact at a fixed finite regulator. Operator-valued-distribution convergence, local covariance, and removal of the regulator remain the independent continuum requirements in Definition F.0h.

<a id="theorem-f1j-paid-finite-gibbs-preparation-and-retained-predictive-comparisons"></a>**Theorem F.1j (Paid Finite Gibbs Preparation and Retained Predictive Comparisons).** The finite controlled source below prepares an arbitrary faithful target with an exact mean-work, bath-energy and finite-excess ledger. Within this supplied controlled Gibbs-swap class, it realizes constrained Gibbs free energy as an infimum of actual preparation work, with uniform value and first-jet bounds. A cyclic predictive completion cancels its ideal entropy regularizer, whereas the separately specified retained-output task has a strictly convex Gibbs-optimal comparison. These are distinct implementation classes. All energies are in Joules, all entropy logarithms are natural, and $\theta=k_BT>0$ is an energy, with $\beta=1/\theta$.

**I. The complete preparation source.** Let $S$ have dimension $D$, final physical Hamiltonian $H$, and target $\sigma>0$. Its supplied initial state is $\eta=I/D$, with zero initial Hamiltonian. This is an equilibrium input at the registered temperature; its supply is a real thermal resource. Put
$$
L=\log\sigma,\quad K=-\theta L,\quad t_j=j/m,\quad K_j=t_jK,
\qquad \sigma_j=\frac{e^{t_jL}}{\operatorname{Tr}e^{t_jL}},\quad j=0,\ldots,m.
\tag{F.1j.1}
$$
Supply $m$ independent $D$-state bath registers $B_j$, each with Hamiltonian $K_j$ and Gibbs state $\sigma_j$. For $j=1,\ldots,m$, change the system Hamiltonian from $K_{j-1}$ to $K_j$, then swap it with $B_j$. Finally change $K_m$ to $H$, without a final thermalization. The initial bank, its programmed energy gaps and the finite control table are source inputs, and the spent bank is retained. With
$$
d_m(\sigma)=\sum_{j=1}^mD(\sigma_{j-1}\Vert\sigma_j),
$$
the actual mean control work, actual bath-energy gain and system-energy change are
$$
\begin{aligned}
W_m(H,\sigma)&=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma H)+\theta[\log D-S(\sigma)]+\theta d_m(\sigma),\\
Q_m&=\theta[\log D-S(\sigma)+d_m(\sigma)],\qquad
\Delta U_S=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma H),\quad W_m=\Delta U_S+Q_m.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1j.2}
$$
The final bank state is the product $\sigma_0\otimes\cdots\otimes\sigma_{m-1}$. Its relative entropy from its initial product Gibbs state is $d_m$, and there is no discarded final system-bank mutual information. Writing $B=\operatorname{osc}(\log\sigma)$,
$$
0\le d_m(\sigma)\le\frac{B^2}{8m}.
\tag{F.1j.3}
$$
Thus the preparation action is an infimum with explicit nonnegative finite excess, rather than an exact reversible finite-reservoir equality.

*Proof.* For $F(A)=-\theta\log\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta A}$, substitution of the Gibbs logarithms gives
$$
\operatorname{Tr}[\sigma_{j-1}(K_j-K_{j-1})]
=F(K_j)-F(K_{j-1})+\theta D(\sigma_{j-1}\Vert\sigma_j).
$$
Sum, using $F(K_m)=0$, $F(0)=-\theta\log D$, and the last work $\operatorname{Tr}[\sigma(H-K_m)]=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma H)-\theta S(\sigma)$. This proves the work formula. Each swap transfers the old system state to its own bath and leaves $\sigma_j$ on the system. Its bath-energy gain is $\operatorname{Tr}K_j(\sigma_{j-1}-\sigma_j)$, which telescopes by the entropy identity to the heat formula. Initially independent factors are merely permuted, proving the product-bank and relative-entropy claims.

For $f(t)=\log\operatorname{Tr}e^{tL}$, $f''(t)=\operatorname{Var}_{\sigma_t}L\le B^2/4$. Therefore
$$
D(\sigma_t\Vert\sigma_{t+d})=f(t+d)-f(t)-df'(t)
=\int_0^d(d-s)f''(t+s)\,ds.
$$
Take $d=1/m$ and sum, proving (F.1j.3). No commutation of $H$ with $\sigma$ is used, since $H$ enters only the final mean work. $\square$

**Physical time, pulses and the reverse record.** A swap in a chosen duration $d_j>0$ is generated by the interaction $\pi\hbar(I-\operatorname{SWAP})/(2d_j)$, of norm $\pi\hbar/d_j$, together with the two equal free Hamiltonians $K_j$. The interaction commutes with that free sum. Its on/off mean work cancels, while its temporary energy, duration and programmed gaps remain owned. Ladder ramps may have positive durations: their Hamiltonians commute with the current states and do not alter the populations. If the pulse norm is bounded by a registered $J$, the swap durations alone total at least $m\pi\hbar/J$. There are $m$ whole $D$-state Gibbs bodies; neither increasing $m$ nor increasing $D$ has a free throughput or storage limit.

When $H$ and $\sigma$ share a basis, retain the full classical path $(i_0,\ldots,i_m)$, with $i_0$ uniform and $i_j$ the independent initial label of $B_j$. Its forward and physical reverse probabilities are
$$
P_F=D^{-1}\prod_{j=1}^m\sigma_j(i_j),\qquad
P_R=\sigma(i_m)\prod_{j=1}^m\sigma_j(i_{j-1}),\qquad
Q=\sum_j[K_j(i_{j-1})-K_j(i_j)].
$$
The reverse begins the system in $\sigma$, reverses the final Hamiltonian change and then every swap/change, with fresh banks of the same Gibbs laws. Direct cancellation of their Gibbs factors gives
$$
\log\frac{P_F}{P_R}=-\log D-\log\sigma(i_m)+\beta Q,\qquad
P_F=\sqrt{P_FP_R}\,e^{\frac12\log(P_F/P_R)},\qquad
W=H(i_m)+Q.
\tag{F.1j.4}
$$
The mean log ratio is $d_m$. Boundary law and symmetric path activity are retained. For noncommuting $H,\sigma$, (F.1j.2)–(F.1j.3) remain quantum mean identities. A final two-point energy measurement would generally dephase the intended target and is not silently added to this instrument.

**II. Exact noncommuting completion and ordinary-ramp errors.** To use only strictly positive ramp durations, choose a smooth nonnegative $f$ on $[0,\tau]$ with $f(0)=0$, $f(\tau)=1$, and define
$$
U=\exp\left[-\frac{iH}{\hbar}\int_0^\tau f(s)\,ds\right],\qquad
\sigma'=U^*\sigma U,\qquad K'=-\theta\log\sigma'.
\tag{F.1j.5}
$$
Ladder-prepare $\sigma'$; lower $K'$ to zero along scalar multiples of $K'$, then run the physical ramp $f(s)H$. The first ramp preserves $\sigma'$ and has work $-\theta S(\sigma)$. The second returns exactly $U\sigma'U^*=\sigma$ and has work $\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma'H)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma H)$ because $[U,H]=0$. Unitary conjugation preserves every ladder spectrum, entropy and relative entropy. Hence (F.1j.2)–(F.1j.3) are unchanged. The target, bath bases, conjugation and finite durations are explicit source data; no local compiler or cutoff-uniform bandwidth is inferred. On a smooth finite $H(g),\sigma(g)$ family this identity also preserves its first jets exactly.

If instead the unmodified target is subjected to the ordinary ramp $H_s=(1-s/\tau)K+(s/\tau)H$, put $M=\max(\|K\|,\|H\|)$. Duhamel and the closed-ramp first law give
$$
\|\sigma_{\rm out}-\sigma\|_1\le\frac{2\tau M}{\hbar},\qquad
|W_{\rm actual}-W_m|\le\frac{2\tau M\|H\|}{\hbar}.
\tag{F.1j.6}
$$
The bath heat is still (F.1j.2); the work error is exactly $\operatorname{Tr}[(\sigma_{\rm out}-\sigma)H]$. The slew rate $\|H-K\|/\tau$ is a control resource. For a parameter direction with $M'=\max(\|DK\|,\|DH\|)$ and fixed $\tau$, Duhamel differentiation gives $\|DU\|\le\tau M'/\hbar$ and
$$
|D(W_{\rm actual}-W_m)|\le\frac{2\tau}{\hbar}
\left\{M\|DH\|+[M\|D\sigma\|_1+M']\|H\|\right\}.
\tag{F.1j.7}
$$
Here $D(U\sigma U^*-\sigma)$ has trace norm at most $2\tau(M\|D\sigma\|_1+M')/\hbar$. Thus a cutoff schedule must pay both the norm growth and the selected ramp duration; a finite noncommuting ramp is not assumed to freeze the state.

**III. Uniform preparation values and first jets.** Suppose $\sigma(g)>0$ is $C^1$ on a compact parameter set and
$\operatorname{osc}(\log\sigma)\le B_*$, $\|D\log\sigma[\delta g]\|\le L_*\|\delta g\|$. At fixed $\theta$, with $A(H,\sigma)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma H)+\theta[\log D-S(\sigma)]$,
$$

<a id="theorem-f1k-born-paid-energy-and-euclidean-clock-comparisons-on-the-common-scalar-branch"></a>**Theorem F.1k (Born, Paid-Energy and Euclidean-Clock Comparisons on the Common Scalar Branch).** The following statements compare specified source maps. They do not equate an instantaneous Born law, a constrained Gibbs variational functional, a real-time Feynman/CTP functional and a Euclidean path measure. All finite occupation-register approximants retain their actual controls and errors as in Theorem F.1j. The continuum statements below have the explicitly stated common-state or sampler scope; other controlled, correlated, hidden-state and non-Gaussian constructions are not classified by them.

**I. A two-mode Born/energy floor.** Let $K>0$ be a finite oscillator stiffness, $\Omega=K^{1/2}$, and use the usual common Schwartz/Fock domain for
$$
H=\tfrac12(P^{\mathsf T}P+Q^{\mathsf T}KQ),\qquad
[Q_a,P_b]=i\hbar\delta_{ab}.
\tag{F.1k.1}
$$
The vacuum joint Born law of the commuting position coordinates has covariance $C_0=(\hbar/2)\Omega^{-1}$. Its actual real cumulant and convex dual are
$$
W_B(J)=\tfrac12J^{\mathsf T}C_0J,\qquad
\Gamma_B(\phi)=\tfrac12\phi^{\mathsf T}C_0^{-1}\phi
=\hbar^{-1}\phi^{\mathsf T}\Omega\phi.
\tag{F.1k.2}
$$
A Weyl displacement by $\phi$, with zero mean momentum, preserves entropy and has actual excitation-energy increment
$$
E(\phi)=\tfrac12\phi^{\mathsf T}K\phi.
\tag{F.1k.3}
$$
These statements follow from $Q=\sqrt{\hbar/(2\omega)}(a+a^*)$ mode by mode, Gaussian square completion, and conjugation of the Hamiltonian by the displacement. They concern energy differences; no absolute vacuum or preparation cost is deleted.

For a retained linear subspace with orthogonal projection $P$, equality $\alpha\Gamma_B=E$ is exactly the compressed-form condition
$P\Omega^2P=(2\alpha/\hbar)P\Omega P$. On an $\Omega$-invariant subspace, positivity makes this equivalent to $\Omega=(2\alpha/\hbar)I$ there. In particular, on two orthogonal modes with $\omega_1<\omega_2$,
$$
\inf_{\alpha>0}\max_{i=1,2}
\left|\frac{\alpha\Gamma_B(e_i)}{E(e_i)}-1\right|
=\frac{\omega_2-\omega_1}{\omega_2+\omega_1},\qquad
\alpha_* =\frac{\hbar\omega_1\omega_2}{\omega_1+\omega_2}.
\tag{F.1k.4}
$$
To prove this, set $b=2\alpha/\hbar$. The two errors are $|b/\omega_i-1|$. Their maximum is minimized between the two frequencies, where they are equal at $b=2\omega_1\omega_2/(\omega_1+\omega_2)$. An affine normalization does not change the Hessians, and a common invertible linear relabeling acts on both by the same congruence, preserving their nonproportionality.

For the common massive scalar sequence, choose two fixed smooth momentum packets in disjoint sufficiently small neighborhoods of unequal limiting frequencies. Their generalized energy/Born ratios converge to distinct values, so a positive two-probe floor persists. Narrowing the packets approaches (F.1k.4). This is a fixed-retained-probe statement, not a demand for full-unit-ball convergence; summable lattice and occupation errors for those probes do not remove its limiting floor.

**II. Gibbs variational response is not the measured Gibbs cumulant.** At physical inverse thermal energy $\beta=1/\theta$, the same oscillator has
$$
\begin{aligned}
W_G(J)&=\log\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H+J^{\mathsf T}Q}
       -\log\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H}
       =\frac1{2\beta}J^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}J,\\
\theta\Gamma_G(\phi)&=E(\phi).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1k.5}
$$
Indeed shift $Q$ by $\beta^{-1}K^{-1}J$ in the completed Hamiltonian square. Unitary translation leaves the trace unchanged and retains exactly the displayed scalar. By contrast the actual position-measurement law in that thermal state has
$$
W_{\rm meas}(J)=\tfrac12J^{\mathsf T}C_\beta J,\qquad
C_\beta=\frac\hbar2\Omega^{-1}\coth(\beta\hbar\Omega/2).
\tag{F.1k.6}
$$
The Gibbs occupation formula gives this covariance. Since $\coth x>1/x$ for $x>0$, it differs from $\theta K^{-1}$ at every positive frequency and finite $\beta$. Thus a paid Gibbs variational Hessian does not itself supply the measured positive source law. The units are fixed by $J^{\mathsf T}Q$ being dimensionless; $\theta\Gamma_G$ is an energy, not an action assigned by setting $\theta=\hbar$.

There is a completely finite noncommuting diagnostic. For a two-level Hamiltonian $H=aZ$, feature $X_{\rm P}=\sigma_x$ and $b=\beta a>0$, the Born measurement of $X_{\rm P}$ is fair in the diagonal Gibbs state, so its real cumulant is $\log\cosh J$. The Gibbs variational cumulant instead is
$$
\log\cosh\sqrt{b^2+J^2}-\log\cosh b.
\tag{F.1k.7}
$$
Their curvatures at zero are respectively $1$ and $\tanh b/b<1$. This follows by diagonalizing $-bZ+J\sigma_x$; no oscillator or continuum approximation is involved.

**III. The squeezed-Born escape and its state-class price.** At a finite set of modes, a centered Gaussian state with position covariance $C_Q=\theta K^{-1}$ gives the desired identity $\theta\Gamma_B=E$. This is a genuine different Born source, not ruled out by convexity. In each diagonal mode the uncertainty inequality gives
$$
\operatorname{Var}P\ge\frac{\hbar^2}{4\operatorname{Var}Q}
=\frac{\hbar^2\omega^2}{4\theta},\qquad
\langle n_\omega\rangle\ge
\frac{\theta}{2\hbar\omega}+\frac{\hbar\omega}{8\theta}-\frac12.
\tag{F.1k.8}
$$
The first assertion drops only the nonnegative squared covariance term from Robertson's determinant inequality. Substitute it into
$\langle n\rangle=[\operatorname{Var}P+\omega^2\operatorname{Var}Q]/(2\hbar\omega)-1/2$ for the second. At fixed $\theta>0$ the lower occupation grows linearly with $\omega$.

On a periodic massive scalar volume, enforcing this exact position covariance on all ultraviolet modes changes the vacuum covariance by
$$
\frac{\theta}{\omega^2}-\frac{\hbar}{2\omega}.
\tag{F.1k.9}
$$
Its nonzero order-$\omega^{-1}$ leading tail is not rapidly decreasing, so the equal-time covariance difference is not a smooth kernel. Two Hadamard two-point functions must differ smoothly. Hence an ultraviolet family with this exact covariance on every mode at fixed $\theta$ is outside that common Hadamard/stress-state class. A scalar vacuum-energy subtraction does not alter this nonsmooth covariance.

The minimal pure Gaussian product has squeeze parameters $e^{-2r_\omega}=2\theta/(\hbar\omega)$ and vacuum probability $1/\cosh r_\omega$ per mode. For any finite set $F$ of modes and larger finite $G$, the projection requiring vacuum on $G\setminus F$ has probability $\prod_{\omega\in G\setminus F}1/\cosh r_\omega$. These products tend to zero. If a normal state on the same vacuum Fock representation had those finite-mode product marginals, normality would pass that limit through the decreasing projections, giving probability zero to the projection $P_F$ onto the Fock space generated by $F$. Yet $P_F$ increases strongly to the identity as $F$ exhausts the modes, forcing its probabilities to tend to one. This contradiction excludes that particular common-Fock normal product limit. It is not an inference from infinite expected particle number alone and does not exclude arbitrary normal states by that criterion.

In three spatial dimensions the same occupation lower bound gives leading excitation-energy growth of order $\Lambda^5/\theta$ at momentum cutoff $\Lambda$, with the fixed physical constants retained. Large finite resources are allowed; the obstruction just proved concerns the nominated state class. A fixed smooth ultraviolet cutoff on a low-momentum squeeze avoids that obstruction, while restricting the Born/energy identity to that retained sector. Varying temperature with cutoff, choosing another covariance/reference or changing the field domain requires its own common-source comparison and is not ruled out here.

**IV. Paid preparation does not change the accepted real-time functional.** At every canonical finite cutoff use its actual Hilbert space and published physical $H_n$, with all field/stress readouts and controls unchanged. Theorem F.1j prepares its faithful targets or the stated rank regularizations with a finite paid bank and chosen error schedule. This does not replace the accepted stationary/Feynman Legendre functional, with its chronological/covariant differential ordering and counterterms, by (F.1k.2), or replace the positive-state CTP amplitudes by an instantaneous position cumulant.

For a coherent finite-stage drive $H(t)=H_0-f(t)\cdot Q$, the actual mean work is $\int\operatorname{Tr}[\rho(t)\partial_tH(t)]dt$. If the drive vanishes at both boundaries, this equals its actual excitation-energy change. Those preparation/drive data can be used by the accepted CTP response at its original test/state scopes. They do not alone construct a positive real spacetime path law with the same physical generator, metric and convex transform. Conversely, the comparisons above do not refute the separately supplied correlated transfer-source law of Lemma F.1c.1.

**V. A positive Euclidean law has a different sequential generator.** The massive scalar Euclidean comparison has zero-temperature mode covariance
$$
C_E(t)=\frac\hbar2\Omega^{-1}e^{-|t|\Omega}.
\tag{F.1k.10}
$$
Finite periodic Euclidean time has the corresponding positive thermal bridge. It is a path measure rather than the single-time measurement of Part II. Euclidean correlation time is not automatically the laboratory update clock.

At a finite periodic chart suppose the same complete position vector is a stationary continuous Gaussian Markov state, with nonsingular $C_E(0)$ and time-homogeneous linear drift $A$, so $C(t)=e^{-At}C_E(0)$ for $t\ge0$. Exact agreement with (F.1k.10) forces

A=-C'(0+)C(0)^{-1}=\Omega=\sqrt K.
\tag{F.1k.11}
$$
For $K=m^2-\Delta_h$ this is not an exact stencil of uniformly fixed finite range on arbitrarily large periodic charts. Restrict its Fourier symbol to one axis:
$$
\Omega_h(k)=\left[m^2+\frac2{a^2}(1-\cos ak)\right]^{1/2}.
\tag{F.1k.12}
$$
A finite-range translation-covariant stencil has Laurent-polynomial symbol $P(z)$, $z=e^{iak}$. If its square were $m^2+2/a^2-(z+z^{-1})/a^2$, the largest nonzero Laurent exponent in $P^2$ would be twice the largest exponent in $P$, with nonzero squared leading coefficient. It cannot be the target exponent one. For a uniformly retained range $R$, multiplying $P(z)^2-[m^2+2/a^2-(z+z^{-1})/a^2]$ by $z^{2R+1}$ gives a polynomial of degree at most $4R+2$. Exact equality at more than $4R+2$ distinct chart roots would force that polynomial identity, giving the contradiction. In the continuum, a translation-invariant distribution supported at the spatial origin has polynomial multiplier, whereas $\sqrt{m^2+|k|^2}$ is not polynomial. Thus the required sequential drift is spatially nonlocal. This is a necessary-generator result for the stated Gaussian Markov position state; it does not classify hidden-state, non-Gaussian or controlled samplers.

A local four-dimensional Euclidean batch sampler is a different alternative. Even if its heat-bath/Metropolis updates give the desired path distribution, it updates an entire history register in an additional execution clock. Its physical Hamiltonian, heat currents and controls are those of that sampler, not automatically those of the original three-dimensional oscillator source. Paying for the history register with Theorem F.1j does not equate these generators. A stationary distribution alone therefore supplies neither the common-current pullback of Theorem B.8c nor the source and normalization clauses of X.5a. This is not a rejection of Euclidean geometry: the Riemannian branch of D.6d remains available with its separate signature/coefficient bridge, and a proved source/time/normalization pullback could give a different realization.

These comparisons leave finite paid preparations, low-mode restrictions, altered rate/replica normalizations, correlated or unbounded records and other supplied source maps available at their own declared scopes. $\square$

**F.6 Rigorous Formulation of Locality and Statistical FTL**

AQFT provides the precise language to formulate PU's stance on locality, distinguishing between operator-level locality, Bob-marginal-preserving state-mediated influence, and the stronger branch-(iii) statistical-FTL marginal anomaly. This section gives the AQFT consistency setting for the local CPTP and joint/conditional branches, while Section 10 supplies the finite-window zero-error analysis needed for the branch-(iii) statistical-FTL hypothesis on the regular branch (Definition 10.2a).

1.  **Emergent Einstein Causality for Algebra $\mathfrak{A}$:** When the continuum-bridge hypotheses of Theorem F.0 hold, Corollary F.1 yields the standard AQFT axiom of Einstein Causality:
$[\mathfrak{A}(\mathcal{O}_1), \mathfrak{A}(\mathcal{O}_2)] = \{0\}$ for space-like separated regions $\mathcal{O}_1, \mathcal{O}_2$. In that continuum AQFT regime, local measurements or operations performed in $\mathcal{O}_1$ cannot causally influence local measurements or operations performed in $\mathcal{O}_2$ in a way that violates the commutation relation for local observables.

2.  **CC Influence Mediated by Global State $\omega$:** The CC mechanism (Hypothesis 3) acts locally on a pre-existing global state $\omega$, which may contain entanglement (Proposition 10). A context-dependent local CPTP implementation in $\mathcal O_A$ may change Alice-local statistics and post-comparison joint or conditional correlations, but pre-existing entanglement does not permit it to change Bob's unconditional marginal in a spacelike-separated region $\mathcal O_B$. That marginal invariance follows from the trace-preserving identity used in Equation (F.4a) and Corollary L.12.8a. A late-randomized Bob-marginal shift is therefore not generated by the local mechanism described here; it belongs to the separate nonlocal/state-mediated anomaly class of Postulate 3. A certified observation of such a shift would support that class and falsify the exact causal branch by Theorem 39c and Corollary 39c.1.

3.  **State-Mediated Statistical Influence (Postulate 3 by Branch):** Consider Alice and Bob performing local measurements on a shared entangled state $\omega$. On the local CPTP and AQFT-compatible joint/conditional branch, Alice's choice of context $C_A\in\{C_{A,1},C_{A,2}\}$ in region $\mathcal O_A$ can influence the joint probability distribution over outcomes for her measurement $A\in\mathfrak A(\mathcal O_A)$ and Bob's measurement $B\in\mathfrak A(\mathcal O_B)$ without changing Bob's unconditional marginal. Specifically, this branch asserts
$$
    \omega_{C_{A,1}}(A\otimes B)\ne \omega_{C_{A,2}}(A\otimes B)
    \quad
    \text{(state-mediated joint-correlation branch)}
    \quad
    \tag{F.4}
$$
    together with
$$
    \omega_{C_{A,1}}(\mathbf 1_A\otimes B)
    =
    \omega_{C_{A,2}}(\mathbf 1_A\otimes B)
    \quad
    \forall B\in\mathfrak A(\mathcal O_B).
    \tag{F.4a}
$$
    The stronger branch-(iii) marginal anomaly of Postulate 3 is distinct: it hypothesizes a late-randomized context-dependent shift of Bob's marginal, which goes beyond local CPTP AQFT no-signaling and is constrained, on the regular finite-window branch (Definition 10.2a), by Theorem 39, Theorem 39a, and Theorem 42. Thus Appendix F supplies the operator-local baseline and the branch-(i) consistency setting, while Section 10 carries the separate statistical-FTL consistency analysis.

4.  **Compatibility with Operational Causality:** Operator locality together with local CP‑TP structure implies no‑signaling at the level of marginals: for any local CPTP map $\Phi_A$ on $A$,
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\!\big[(\Phi_A\!\otimes\!\mathrm{id}_B)(\rho_{AB})\big]=\operatorname{tr}_A(\rho_{AB}),\qquad
\big\|\operatorname{tr}_A[(\Phi_A^{(1)}\!\otimes\!\mathrm{id}_B)\rho]-\operatorname{tr}_A[(\Phi_A^{(2)}\!\otimes\!\mathrm{id}_B)\rho]\big\|_1=0,
$$
so Alice’s local choice cannot alter Bob’s marginal on the local CPTP branch. Different contexts may correspond to different shared-past global state preparations $\omega_{C_A}$, or to Bob-marginal-preserving joint/conditional deformations, or—on the stronger branch-(iii) hypothesis—to a statistical marginal anomaly. The following constraints bound endpoint forcing and finite-window reliability, but Theorem 39c makes exact marginal invariance the separate condition for operational causality:
   *   CC Endpoint-Complete Bound: the bounded-bias branch declares $\text{CC}\le\alpha_{CC,max}<0.5$, and Theorem 39 proves that this excludes a single protocol from forcing both binary endpoints; forcing one endpoint remains admissible under this bound when the baseline lies sufficiently close to it.
   *   Zero-Error Statistical-FTL Gate: Theorem 39a shows that, on the regular finite-window branch (Definition 10.2a), a branch-(iii) marginal shift can have positive statistical information while still having zero finite-window zero-error capacity.
   *   ND-RID Information Limits: Registered ND-RID interactions carry the following limits only on their stated reset, refresh/minorization, and support-deficit branches: ($\varepsilon_{\mathrm{phys}}\ge H_q(P\mid R)\quad(\text{registered reset branch; a positive uniform floor inferred from this entropy bound requires }H_q(P\mid R)\ge h_{\min}>0)$, Theorem 31), the completed reset-support capacity deficit ($C_{\max}\le\ln d_0-\ln2$, Proposition E.2a), and, on refresh/minorization branches, strict contractivity ($f_{RID}<1$, Lemma E.1) with strict finite channel capacity ($C_{\max}<\ln d_0$, Theorem E.2). These ledgers bound cost, rate, or contraction on their stated branches. The finite-window zero-error conclusion instead uses Definition 10.2a and Theorems 39a and 42, while any freely selectable nonzero pre-lightcone marginal channel remains signaling by Theorem 39c.

AQFT formalizes how operator locality for observables, when the continuum bridge applies, coexists with constrained state-mediated statistical non-locality for expectations and outcome probabilities. The influence is in the preparation of the global state ensemble, not in the local interaction rule.

**Shannon-causality scope rule.** On the AQFT/local-CPTP branch, causality requires exact invariance of Bob's unconditional pre-lightcone marginal under every independently selectable Alice context. Theorem 39a is a zero-error coding lemma. By Theorem 39c, a branch-(iii) late-randomized marginal shift has positive Shannon capacity and is outside this causal branch; finite-window noise does not restore AQFT compatibility.

**F.7 Maintaining Lorentz Invariance**

Lorentz/AQFT compatibility is maintained on the exact marginal-invariant and shared-past branches. A freely selectable branch-(iii) pre-lightcone marginal shift is not covered by that compatibility claim, because Theorem 39c makes it a positive-capacity superluminal channel:
1.  **State Dependence:** The statistical influence (Equation F.4) depends on the global state $\omega_{C_A}$. Lorentz transformations act consistently on both the operators $B \in \mathfrak{A}(\mathcal{O}_B)$ and the description of the state $\omega$.
2.  **No Preferred Frame Signaling:** On the regular finite-window branch, Theorems 39a and 42 exclude zero-error finite-window decoding, so the influence cannot supply the zero-error decoding step in the contradiction protocol covered by Theorem 42. If the late context changes Bob's pre-lightcone marginal, Theorem 39c gives a signaling channel, so no preferred-frame or Lorentz-compatibility conclusion follows for that branch.
3.  **Lorentz Covariance of Dynamics:** The underlying effective action $S_{\mathrm{eff}}$ (Section F.5) and dynamics generator $\mathcal{L}^*$ (Section F.4) are assumed to be Lorentz or generally covariant in the emergent spacetime. The process of state preparation $\omega_{C_A}$ and the resulting statistical correlations transform consistently under Lorentz boosts.
4.  **Analogy with Entanglement:** This is analogous in causal role, though not identical in marginal structure, to the non-locality of standard quantum entanglement: the relevant compatibility condition is exact absence of a freely selectable pre-lightcone marginal channel, as stated by Theorem 39c. Only the Bob-marginal-invariant or shared-past CC branches fall into this causal category.

**F.8 Conclusion: AQFT as Arena for Verification and Locality**

Algebraic quantum field theory provides the continuum setting in which the model can describe local observables, states, dynamics, stress and energy, and spacelike locality. Theorem F.0 supplies that setting once the discrete network is shown to converge with the required causal and stability properties. A late choice that changes a remote pre-lightcone outcome distribution is the branch-(iii) statistical-FTL hypothesis of Postulate 3; it lies outside this causal setting, and Section 10 analyzes its channel consequences.

**Technical ledger.**

AQFT provides a robust mathematical framework for analyzing the properties of the hypothesized continuum limit of the MPU network. The analysis presented here holds on branches satisfying the hypotheses of Theorem F.0 (the convergence to a stable AQFT) and Theorem 43 (geometric regularity). Subject to these assumptions, AQFT allows for:
*   Precise definition of emergent physical states and dynamics.
*   Rigorous definition of the macroscopic MPU stress-energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}^{(MPU)}$ (Definition F.4).
*   Formulation of Einstein Causality (Microcausality) through Corollary F.1 when the lightcone-identification hypothesis of Theorem F.0 is satisfied.
*   A clear formulation of the framework's stance on locality, allowing for hypothesized state-mediated statistical influence (Equation F.4, Postulate 3) on the Bob-marginal-preserving branch, while distinguishing the stronger branch-(iii) marginal anomaly analyzed in Section 10 on the regular finite-window branch (Definition 10.2a).
*   Separation of exact operational causality (Theorem 39c) from the weaker endpoint, finite-window zero-error, sample-complexity, and information-rate bounds of Theorems 39–42.

The full AQFT bridge is status-split. On the strict projective single-clock branch, Definition F.0e supplies exact core compatibility, while Theorem F.0f requires its additional locality, causal-cone, and semigroup-stability hypotheses for the stable local-$C^*$-net conclusion. On the Mosco-Bochner branch, Definition F.0c and all side conditions of Theorem F.0d supply the corresponding Dirichlet-form and local-net conclusions. The separate coherent Hamiltonian limit requires an accepted coherent-convergence record. A standard relativistic AQFT or Wightman realization additionally requires the representation, state, spectrum, covariance, and field-domain data of Definition F.0h. Missing entries remain bridge obligations on the selected branch.
