Those endpoints are retained or removed from a fixed interior test window by the quantitative long-boundary projection, not declared local overlap errors.

A general time-dependent curved 4D family, its compact metric variations, nonminimal curvature contacts, and its finite regulator/continuation map are not supplied by G18–G22. They are separate physical first-jet obligations. Likewise the normalized path action has no vacuum log determinant: any actual metric-only determinant/reference influence and its stress/noise must remain in the source's appropriate reference sector rather than silently being included in G5.

<a id="lemma-f1c1a-finite-positive-transfer-trotter-constants-and-normalized-source-errors"></a>**Lemma F.1c.1a (Finite Positive Transfer, Trotter Constants and Normalized-Source Errors).**

All matrices and coordinate grids below are finite. The transfer parameters $t$, $T$ and $\delta$ in $\exp(-tH)$ have inverse-energy units; a physical Euclidean duration $\epsilon$ uses $\delta=\epsilon/\hbar$. The constants retain their actual coordinate cutoff and finite boundary normalization.

#### 1. Exact finite ground-state bridge

Let $X$ be a finite configuration set and $H=H^T$ a real matrix, $H_{xy}\le 0$ for $x\ne y$, with connected off-diagonal graph. Choose $c\ge\max_x H_{xx}$. The matrix $M=cI-H$ is entrywise nonnegative and irreducible. For every $t>0$, each entry of $\exp(tM)$ is strictly positive: a graph path from $x$ to $y$ contributes a positive term in its power series (the zeroth term handles $x=y$). Hence $\exp(-tH)>0$ entrywise. Perron–Frobenius, applied to this strictly positive symmetric matrix, gives a unique normalized ground vector $\psi>0$ and lowest eigenvalue $E_0$; all other energies exceed $E_0$.

Write $D=\operatorname{diag}(\psi)$, $\pi_x=\psi_x^{2}$, and

$$
P_t = \exp(E_0 t)\, D^{-1} \exp(-tH)\, D.
$$

Then $P_{t}$ is entrywise positive for $t>0$, $P_t 1=1$, $P_s P_t=P_{s+t}$, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
\pi_x P_t(x,y) &= \exp(E_0t)\, \psi_x [\exp(-tH)]_{xy}\, \psi_y \\
&= \pi_y P_t(y,x).
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $\pi$ is stationary and the process is reversible. Its generator is

$$
\begin{aligned}
Q_{xy} &= -H_{xy}\, \psi_y/\psi_x\quad (x\ne y), \\
Q_{xx} &= E_0-H_{xx} = -\sum_{y\ne x} Q_{xy}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The map $U:L^{2}(\pi)\to\ell^{2}(X)$, $Uf=Df$, is unitary, with

$$
U P_t U^{-1} = \exp[-t(H-E_0)].
\tag{F.1c.1a.T1}
$$

For any finite ordered times, the **normalized** path law is

$$
\mu(x_0,\ldots,x_m)=\pi_{x_0} \prod_j P_{t_j-t_{j-1}}(x_{j-1},x_j).
$$

Telescoping D factors give the equivalent endpoint expression

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mu &= \exp[E_0(t_m-t_0)]\, \psi_{x_0} \psi_{x_m} \\
&\qquad \prod_j \bigl[\exp(-(t_j-t_{j-1})H)\bigr]_{x_{j-1},x_j}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.1a.T2}
$$

These consistent finite distributions define the stationary process. Nothing here claims a local preparation of $\psi$ or of (F.1c.1a.T2).

#### 2. Reflection positivity, quotient, and physical correlators

Take a finite symmetric time grid containing 0. Let F,G be arbitrary complex functions of the nonnegative-time coordinates, and let $\theta$ replace every t by -t. Define

$$
u_F(x) = \mathbb{E}[F \mid X_0=x].
$$

Given $X_{0}$, the future and reflected past are independent and have the same law. This follows directly from the above product formula and detailed balance, not from a named reconstruction theorem. Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
\langle F,G\rangle_{\mathrm{OS}} &:= \mathbb{E}\bigl[\overline{F(\theta X)}\, G(X)\bigr] \\
&= \sum_x \pi_x\, \overline{u_F(x)}\, u_G(x).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.1a.T3}
$$

It is positive semidefinite. Its null space is exactly $u_{F}=0$. Every $f$ in $L^{2}(\pi)$ is attained by $F=f(X_0)$, so the quotient is exactly $L^{2}(\pi)$, with no missing finite-dimensional sector. Shifting every time in $F$ to $t+s$ gives $u_{\tau_s F}=P_s u_F$. Consistency lets us enlarge the finite time window when needed. Consequently positive-time translation on the quotient is $P_{s}$, and (F.1c.1a.T1) identifies its positive self-adjoint generator with $H-E_0$. If time-zero observables are excluded, $P_{t}$ is invertible at finite dimension, so functions at any fixed $t>0$ still span the same quotient.

For diagonal observables $M_{f}$ and $t_0<\dots<t_m$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}\Bigl[\prod_j f_j(X_{t_j})\Bigr] \\
&= \bigl\langle \psi, M_{f_0} \exp[-\Delta_1(H-E_0)]\, M_{f_1} \cdots \\
&\qquad \exp[-\Delta_m(H-E_0)]\, M_{f_m} \psi\bigr\rangle.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.1a.T4}
$$

This follows by direct matrix multiplication of the path probabilities. In finite dimension each right-hand side is entire in the time differences. With $f(s)=\exp(iHs/\hbar)M_f\exp(-iHs/\hbar)$, substituting $\Delta_j=-i(s_j-s_{j-1})/\hbar$ gives exactly $\langle\psi,f_0(s_0)\cdots f_m(s_m)\psi\rangle$ in the displayed order. Substituting the opposite sign gives the chronological, latest-time-left product $\langle\psi,f_m(s_m)\cdots f_0(s_0)\psi\rangle$: transposition reverses all factors because $H$ and the diagonal $M_{f}$ are symmetric. These signs specify the convention rather than hiding it in the name “Wick rotation.” Real-time positivity of a path measure is neither asserted nor needed.

**Energy information lost by normalization.** Replacing $H$ by $H+cI$ leaves $\psi$, $\pi$, every $P_{t}$, and all (F.1c.1a.T3)–(F.1c.1a.T4) unchanged. It changes unnormalized kernels by $\exp(-ct)$, and changes physical energy by $c$. If $c=c(q)$ depends on geometry, its force $dc/dq$ is also lost. The physical Hamiltonian $H$ and this scalar energy ledger must therefore be supplied separately; normalized paths reconstruct only $H-E_0$. The usual ground-state global phase cancels in the correlators, but this does not erase physical vacuum-energy or lapse responses.

#### 3. Local finite oscillator register and the Doob locality obstruction

Let $X=\prod_{i\in\Lambda}G_i$, where each $G_{i}$ is a finite connected coordinate chain. Let $K_{i}$ be a nonnegative weighted nearest-grid graph Laplacian on $G_{i}$, extended to the product, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
K&=\sum_i K_i,\quad H=K+V, \\
V(q)&=\sum_A V_A(q_A).
\end{aligned}
$$

Each A has uniformly bounded spatial diameter; a typical quadratic potential is

$$
V(q)=\sum_i (m_i^{2}/2)\, q_i^{2} + \sum_{(ij)} (\kappa_{ij}/2)(q_i-q_j)^{2}.
$$

All terms are actual finite operators. Dirichlet-grid diagonal corrections can be moved into the local $V$; no row-sum-zero claim is then made for those corrections. $H$ is irreducible and stoquastic. Its nonzero off-diagonal matrix elements change one coordinate by one grid step. However the associated rate is the kinetic coefficient times $\psi(q')/\psi(q)$. That ratio generally depends on coordinates arbitrarily far from the changed site. Sparse allowed moves are **not** a proof of local rate dependence.

#### 4. Positive local spacetime law without ground-state ratios

Since the $K_{i}$ commute,

$$
\begin{aligned}
k_\delta(q,q')&=[\exp(-\delta K)]_{q,q'} \\
&=\prod_i k_{i,\delta}(q_i,q'_i),
\end{aligned}
$$

where each $k_{i,\delta}>0$ is symmetric and stochastic. Define the symmetric positive-definite transfer matrix

$$
S_\delta = \exp(-\delta V/2) \exp(-\delta K) \exp(-\delta V/2).
\tag{F.1c.1a.T5}
$$

It is entrywise strictly positive. On a periodic time ring with $M\ge 3$ slices,

$$
\begin{aligned}
w_\delta(q)&=\prod_n \exp[-\delta V(q_n)] \\
&\qquad \prod_{n,i} k_{i,\delta}(q_{i,n},q_{i,n+1}), \\
Z_\delta&=\sum_q w_\delta(q)=\operatorname{Tr}(S_\delta^{M}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.1a.T6}
$$

Indices n are cyclic. The exponent is a sum of finite-range spatial factors and same-site temporal-neighbor factors. Matrix elements $k_{i}$ may connect several field-grid values at once, but do not couple distinct spatial sites. “Local” here means finite-range dependence in the **spacetime history register**.

For an open symmetric slab use positive product boundary amplitudes $\eta(q)=\prod_i\eta_i(q_i)$ and the weight

$$
\eta(q_{-N}) \prod_{n=-N}^{N-1} S_\delta(q_n,q_{n+1})\, \eta(q_N).
$$

Its normalization is $\eta^T S_\delta^{2N}\eta$. It remains local, with half-strength potential terms at the endpoints. Splitting the slab at 0 directly gives an OS Gram form $\sum_x\overline{B_F(x)}B_G(x)/Z$, where $B_F(x)$ is the weighted sum over one half-slab with center $x$ and boundary $\eta$. Thus finite-slab reflection positivity also holds by a literal sum of squares. The finite slab has the declared boundary state, not the exact stationary ground state.

An exact alternative before time discretization is the Feynman–Kac formula for independent continuous-time coordinate walks with generator -K:

$$
\begin{aligned}
[\exp(-TH)]_{x,y} \\
&= \mathbb{E}_x\Bigl[ \exp\Bigl(-\int_0^T V(X_s)\, ds\Bigr)\, 1_{X_T=y} \Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.1a.T7}
$$

Conditioning on the first short interval gives derivative -(K+V) of the right-hand-side operator and initial value I, proving (F.1c.1a.T7) by uniqueness of the finite matrix ODE. Its reference walk has one-site nearest-grid jumps and its potential weight factorizes over local A. It is a local weighted path ensemble, not a normalized local single-slice Doob process. Continuous-time paths have unbounded possible jump count, despite finite state dimension.

#### 5. Explicit finite Trotter and Hamiltonian errors

Put $v_*=\min_q V(q)$, $V'=V-v_*I\ge 0$, $M_*=\lVert K\rVert+\lVert V'\rVert$, and

$$
C = \lVert[V,[V,K]]\rVert/24 + \lVert[K,[V,K]]\rVert/12.
$$

For $T=n\delta$, in the spectral operator norm,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert S_\delta-\exp(-\delta H)\rVert &\le \exp(-\delta v_*)\, C \delta^{3}, \\
\lVert S_\delta^{n}-\exp(-TH)\rVert &\le \exp(-T v_*)\, C T \delta^{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.1a.T8}
$$

Here is a direct contraction proof of the constant. Set $A=-V'$, $B=-K$, $C_0=[A,B]$, and $S(t)=\exp(tA/2)\exp(tB)\exp(tA/2)$. Its defect $S'-(A+B)S$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
&[\exp(tA/2),B] \exp(tB)\exp(tA/2) \\
&\quad + (1/2)\exp(tA/2)[\exp(tB),A]\exp(tA/2).
\end{aligned}
$$

Expand both commutators using $[\exp(tA),B]=\int_0^t\exp(sA)[A,B]\exp((t-s)A)\,ds$. Their terms linear in $t$ cancel. Commuting $C_0$ through the remaining $A$ and $B$ factors leaves defect norm at most

$$
(t^{2}/8)\lVert[A,C_0]\rVert+(t^{2}/4)\lVert[B,C_0]\rVert.
$$

Every exponential in the integrals is a contraction. Duhamel integration from 0 to $\delta$ gives $\delta^{3}$ times the displayed $1/24$ and $1/12$ constants. Telescoping $n$ contraction steps gives (F.1c.1a.T8); the scalar shift restores $\exp(-Tv_*)$. A commutator-free fallback is $C\le M_*^{3}/3$, obtained by matching Taylor coefficients through degree 2 and bounding both third derivatives by $M_*^{3}$.

The finite effective Hamiltonian

$$
H_\delta = -\delta^{-1} \log S_\delta
$$

is real symmetric and satisfies

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert H_\delta-H\rVert &\le \epsilon_\delta \\
&:= C \delta^{2} \exp(\delta M_*).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.1a.T9}
$$

Indeed, after the scalar shift, both positive matrices $S'_\delta$ and $\exp[-\delta(K+V')]$ are bounded below by $\exp(-\delta M_*)I$. The resolvent integral for $\log$ gives $\lVert\log A-\log B\rVert\le m^{-1}\lVert A-B\rVert$ whenever $A,B\ge mI$. Combine with (F.1c.1a.T8). $H_{\delta}$ need not itself be finite-range or stoquastic: locality belongs to the factorization (F.1c.1a.T5)–(F.1c.1a.T6), and (F.1c.1a.T9) is the controlled bridge back to $H$.

Let $g=E_1-E_0>0$. Weyl's inequality gives $|E_{0,\delta}-E_0|\le\epsilon_\delta$ and $g_\delta\ge g-2\epsilon_\delta$. If $\epsilon_\delta<g/2$, the positive normalized ground vectors obey

$$
\lVert\psi_\delta-\psi\rVert \le \sqrt{2}\, \epsilon_\delta/(g-\epsilon_\delta).
\tag{F.1c.1a.T10}
$$

For a direct proof, project $(H-E_{0,\delta})\psi_\delta=(H-H_\delta)\psi_\delta$ onto $\psi$-perpendicular, where the inverse has norm at most $1/(g-\epsilon_\delta)$. Positive overlap fixes the sign.

At a fixed $\delta$, the Perron eigenpair $S_\delta\psi_\delta=\lambda_0\psi_\delta$ yields an exact discrete stationary law $P_\delta=\lambda_0^{-1}D_{\psi_\delta}^{-1}S_\delta D_{\psi_\delta}$, whose OS transfer is $S_\delta/\lambda_0=\exp[-\delta(H_\delta-E_{0,\delta})]$. It is not exactly $H$ at nonzero $\delta$, and fractional powers of $P_{\delta}$ need not be entrywise nonnegative: the assertion here is a discrete-time Markov law, not continuous-time Markov embeddability. A periodic finite ring gives thermal traces of $S_{\delta}$, not vacuum correlators of $H$. Equation (F.1c.1a.T1) is the exact vacuum theorem; (F.1c.1a.T8)–(F.1c.1a.T10) and boundary projection quantify using local finite slabs to approximate it.

For a normalized positive product $\eta$, let $a_0=\langle\psi_\delta,\eta\rangle>0$. The exact projection estimate is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert\lambda_0^{-N} S_\delta^{N} \eta-a_0 \psi_\delta\rVert \\
&\le \sqrt{1-a_0^{2}}\, \exp(-g_\delta N \delta).
\end{aligned}
$$

After normalization the vector error is at most $2\sqrt{1-a_0^{2}}\exp(-g_\delta N\delta)/a_0$. Thus a long local slab approximates the ground boundary, with a quantified buffer cost. No finite exact preparation or regulator-uniform gap/mixing estimate has been assumed.

For completeness, normalization can also be bounded rather than discarded. Use the shifted $H'=H-v_*I$, a positive normalized boundary $\eta$, and a slab of total duration $T$ with $Z=\eta^T\exp(-TH')\eta>0$. With finitely many diagonal insertions $M_{j}$, let $B=\prod_j\lVert M_j\rVert$ and $\epsilon=CT\delta_{\max}^{2}$ for a common Trotter mesh respecting all insertion times. Telescoping through the insertions bounds the numerator error by $B\epsilon$ and the partition error by $\epsilon$. Positivity of the exact path law gives $|\text{numerator}|\le BZ$. If $\epsilon<Z$, the two normalized inserted expectations differ by at most

$$
2 B \epsilon/(Z-\epsilon).
\tag{F.1c.1a.T11a}
$$

For real counting sources, take $M_j=\exp(J_j F_j)$; on a fixed bounded source set $B$ is explicit. This is a finite normalized-source bound, not a regulator-uniform estimate; $Z$ and $B$ must remain in the common limit accounting.

<a id="lemma-f1c2-common-oscillator-domain-and-actual-finite-precursors"></a>**Lemma F.1c.2 (Common oscillator domain and actual finite precursors).**

#### F.1c.2 — U1. Common Hilbert space and operator core at fixed h

Let the unchanged admitted core network be finite dimensional, with Hilbert space $H_{\mathrm{core}}$. On a finite spatial graph with d real oscillator coordinates take

$$
\begin{aligned}
H_h&=H_{\mathrm{core}} \otimes L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^d,dq), \\
D_h&=H_{\mathrm{core}} \otimes S(\mathbb{R}^d).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.2.U1}
$$

The Schwartz space is dense. Every $Q_{i}$ and $P_i=-i\hbar\partial_i$ maps it into itself. Every Weyl-ordered polynomial of degree at most two, including every actual local energy, quadratic metric vertex and their commutators, is defined on this common invariant domain.

For the source's positive oscillator Hamiltonian

$$
H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\frac{1}{2} P^{\mathsf T} M^{-1} P+\frac{1}{2}(Q-m)^{\mathsf T} A(Q-m)+E_{\mathrm{ref}} I,
\tag{F.1c.2.U2}
$$

M and A are strictly positive finite matrices and $E_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the explicit scalar reference. A finite linear canonical change reduces U2 to a finite sum of harmonic oscillators. Its Gaussian-times-polynomial eigenvectors are complete, it is essentially self-adjoint on Schwartz space, bounded below, and has a unique normal Gaussian ground state and trace-class Gibbs states at every positive inverse temperature.

More generally each real Weyl quadratic has the self-adjoint metaplectic-generator closure on this domain. Its linear Hamiltonian system is a finite matrix ODE; the resulting strongly continuous unitary group implements the corresponding real symplectic flow. Schwartz space is invariant. Finite-dimensional core-controlled blocks are direct sums of these closures; explicitly owned nonquadratic core gate pulses remain bounded tensor factors or separately certified controls.

Thus the static dynamics, all required finite quadratic vertices, and their finite-time Duhamel variations exist on one actual common domain. No formal commutator is taken between unrelated closures.

#### F.1c.2 — U2. Exact local energy current and continuity on that domain

Decompose the actual closed Hamiltonian as $H_{\mathrm{total}}=\sum_v\epsilon_v$ with the same local supports, core price terms, half-edge energy shares and explicit auxiliary interactions as in Appendix B. On the nominated autonomous observation sector, the immutable ready/flag coefficient algebra is a common commuting block algebra. Each block of $\epsilon_{v}$ is therefore an ordinary local quadratic polynomial plus its registered scalar/core terms. This commutativity is an actual branch condition, satisfied by fixed ready projectors and diagonal retained flags; it is not asserted for arbitrary matrix coefficients. On $D_{h}$ define

$$
J_{v\leftarrow u}=(i/\hbar)[\epsilon_u,\epsilon_v].
\tag{F.1c.2.U3}

Within those commuting blocks the commutator of two Weyl quadratics is again a Weyl quadratic (plus any explicitly computed scalar), so U3 maps $D_{h}$ into itself. Noncommuting core coefficients can produce quartic terms, for example through $[A,B]\otimes Q^{2}P^{2}$, and are outside this quadratic-current statement. The separate driven preparation gates are treated by their explicit finite metaplectic/control sequence, not silently included in this autonomous commuting-block claim. Disjoint supports commute there. Antisymmetry is exact, and

$$
(i/\hbar)[H_{\mathrm{total}},\epsilon_v]=\sum_u J_{v\leftarrow u}
\tag{F.1c.2.U4}
$$

holds on $D_{h}$. The total sum of currents cancels. The actual unitary dynamics preserves the form domain needed to turn U4 into differentiated matrix elements; on Schwartz vectors it is an ordinary exact identity. This supplies the extension of the finite algebraic continuity proof, not a separate postulated energy tensor.

A real symmetric metric/Noether tensor, spin improvement and its continuum comparison still require their own source proof. The finite oscillator Hamiltonian and domain alone do not imply a Lorentzian momentum-flux identity. F05's actual quadratic metric vertices and Ward calculation are the appropriate further input.

#### F.1c.2 — U3. Finite MPU approximants and the common diagonal

The final joined construction uses the independently proved tensor-Hermite implementation in Lemma F.1c.2a, including full gate/state/metric jets, weighted currents, trace normalization and bounded-source exponential-MGF errors. Its actual finite propagator is generated by $P_{N}$ G $P_{N}$, not the nonunitary compression $P_{N}$ U $P_{N}$. On Gaussian-times-polynomial eigenfunction prefixes the box error is bounded by a polynomial in $R$ times $\exp(-c_h R^{2})$, and the centered kinetic error by $C_h\delta^{2}$ times the fourth-derivative norm. Choose the box/grid only after those data, so the total error is below a prescribed $\epsilon_{h}$. This yields an actual finite-MPU common diagonal for all nominated observations and stress tests. It does not claim uniform operator norm convergence of unbounded Q,P or exact finite-dimensional CCR. It also does not claim that the finite cutoff law is exactly Gaussian or exactly Legendre-local.

#### F.1c.2 — U4. Normal states, measured observables and source preparation

The exact fixed-h Gaussian states are normal states of U1 with finite polynomial moments and finite mean oscillator energy. Position/Weyl observables can be retained mathematical source observables without asserting free exact classical storage of every real outcome. A finite-resolution pointer/readout is an additional actual instrument; its backaction, storage and work must be included if executed.

The histories' Gaussian law can be represented by the commuting quadratures of an explicitly prepared Gaussian pointer register. The exact positive Gaussian path law, the oscillator transfer identities, and the discrete Doob/reflection and Trotter statements are proved in Lemma F.1c.1, parts G4, G5 and G8a. Neither a state-preparation channel nor the equality of static covariances alone proves the full physical source/action square. #### F.1c.2 — U5. Continuous fresh ports and their reference measure

A uniform probability distribution on all of R does not exist. Thus the finite fresh-uniform-port factorization must not be copied unchanged to an unbounded q alphabet.

A valid registered alternative uses microscopic port coordinate $u\in(0,1)$, with its actual uniform reference state, and a fixed smooth monotone map $q=F_0^{-1}(u)$, where $F_{0}$ is a nominated normal Gaussian distribution function. A normal uniform $u$ reference is available on $L^{2}((0,1),du)$, for example the constant unit vector for its coordinate law. Its physical Hamiltonian, preparation and conversion to the $q$-observable must be declared. This measure bookkeeping establishes the conditional algebra; it does not prove a free physical continuous sampler or remove its finite-resolution implementation costs.

<a id="lemma-f1c2a-quantitative-gaussian-finite-registers-and-counting-source-jets"></a>**Lemma F.1c.2a (Quantitative Gaussian Finite Registers and Counting-Source Jets).**

#### F.1c.2a — 1. Exact normalization and first jets

Write $x=q-m$, $\kappa I\le K(g)\le\Lambda I$ on compact parameter set $G$. Use a fixed coordinate measure $dq$. The normalized state is

$$
\psi_g(q) = (\det K)^{1/4} (2 \pi)^{-d/4} \exp(-x^{\mathsf T} K x/4).
$$

For any nominated metric direction denoted by a dot,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot\psi / \psi &= \frac{1}{4} \operatorname{tr}(K^{-1} \dot K) \\
&\quad -\frac{1}{4} x^{\mathsf T} \dot K x +\frac{1}{2} \dot m^{\mathsf T} K x.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.2a.1}
$$

Thus the normalization contact is compulsory. For an unnormalized transfer history $w=c(g)\exp(-x^T Kx/2)$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
Z &= c(g)\, (2 \pi)^{d/2} \det(K)^{-1/2}, \\
\dot Z/Z &= \dot c/c -\frac{1}{2} \operatorname{tr}(K^{-1} \dot K).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.2a.2}
$$

The scalar transfer c includes every kinetic determinant and scalar energy reference. It cancels from normalized p and $\psi$; it does NOT cancel from the absolute transfer partition/metric ledger. This matches stress S6a–S6c. A numerical covariance check cannot check c.

Let $a_j,a_j^*$ be standard oscillator ladder operators, $W=1+\sum_j a_j^*a_j$. Every $W^s\psi$ and $W^s\dot{\psi}$ is a polynomial times a Gaussian. Their norms can be evaluated by Gaussian moments, or bounded by $\kappa$, $\Lambda$, $\sup|m|$, $\sup|\dot{m}|$ and $\sup\lVert\dot{K}\rVert$. Define the actual retained constants

$$
M_s=\sup_g\bigl(\lVert W^s\psi_g\rVert+\sum_{\text{directions}}\lVert W^s\dot\psi_g\rVert\bigr).
$$

They are finite for every nonnegative integer s. Constants are allowed to depend on the fixed graph/history length. C1 parameter dependence suffices for first metric jets; the arbitrary s here is a coordinate regularity index, not a parameter derivative order.

#### F.1c.2a — 2. One tensor-local finite register, with normalization retained

Use $P_N=\prod_j 1_{0\le n_j\le N}$; its rank is $(N+1)^{d}$. This is a tensor product of finite local oscillator registers, not a total-energy projector that changes tensor locality. $P_N$ commutes with $W$. On its complement $W\ge N+2$. Consequently, for any Schwartz vector $v$ and integers $s,r\ge 0$,

 $$
 \lVert W^s(1-P_N)v\rVert\le(N+2)^{-r}\lVert W^{s+r}v\rVert.
 \tag{F.1c.2a.3}
 $$

Put $v_N=P_N\psi$, $n_N=\lVert v_N\rVert$, $\psi_N=v_N/n_N$. With $\eta=\lVert(1-P_N)\psi\rVert\le 1/2$, $n_N\ge\sqrt{3}/2$ and

 $$
 \begin{gathered}
 \lVert W^s(\psi_N-\psi)\rVert\le\tau_s+2\eta^{2}\lVert W^s\psi\rVert, \\
 \tau_s=\lVert W^s(1-P_N)\psi\rVert.
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{F.1c.2a.4}
 $$

The derivative is EXACTLY

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot\psi_N&=P_N \dot\psi/n_N - P_N \psi\, \dot n_N/n_N^2, \\
\dot n_N&=\operatorname{Re}\langle P_N \psi,P_N \dot\psi\rangle/n_N \\
&=-\operatorname{Re}\langle(1-P_N)\psi,(1-P_N)\dot\psi\rangle/n_N.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.2a.5}
$$

The second equality uses normalization of the real positive $\psi$. Equations (F.1c.2a.3)–(F.1c.2a.5) give the explicit weighted jet bound

 $$
 \lVert W^s(\dot{\psi}_N-\dot{\psi})\rVert\le\tau'_s+2\eta^{2}\lVert W^s\dot{\psi}\rVert+2\eta\eta'\lVert W^s\psi\rVert,
 \tag{F.1c.2a.6}
 $$

where $\eta'=\lVert(1-P_N)\dot{\psi}\rVert$, $\tau'_s=\lVert W^s(1-P_N)\dot{\psi}\rVert$. The loose factors 2 are valid for $\eta\le 1/2$. No unrecorded renormalization is used.

For independent reference modes, $P_{N}$ factorizes, so normalized truncation of the product reference is again a product reference. These finite reference states are supplied/prepared resources, as in the original branch convention. Equations (F.1c.2a.4)–(F.1c.2a.6) alone are not a protocol for acquiring an unavailable resource for free.

#### F.1c.2a — 3. Actual finite unitaries for preparation, conditional gates, and encoder

Use the nominated finite sequence of displacement, shear, swap/rotation, and squeeze gates, with smooth coefficients on $G$. More robustly, implement the positive covariance factor by $\exp(B(g))$ with $B=(1/2)\log\Sigma(g)$, together with fixed routing. SPD matrix logarithm is smooth on the compact positive family. Schur elimination uses triangular unit-diagonal shear matrices. This avoids a pivot-dependent elimination algorithm with discontinuous gate choices. Fixed swaps are parameter-independent.

Each continuous pulse has a self-adjoint real Weyl polynomial $G(t,g)$ of degree $\le 2$, with bounded $C^1$ coefficient functions and a finite time interval. The finite actual generator is $G_N=P_N GP_{N}$ restricted to $\operatorname{ran}P_{N}$. Its exponential/time-ordered propagator $U_{N}$ is EXACTLY unitary in that finite register. This is not the generally nonunitary compression $P_{N}UP_{N}$. Termwise compression retains each original bounded-site tensor support.

Here are usable constants rather than an invocation of strong convergence. In the Hermite basis $G$ has bandwidth at most two in total occupation, and its entries grow at most linearly in $W$. For each $s$ choose constants $C_s,D_s$ from its finite list of ladder coefficients so that

 $$
 \begin{gathered}

 \lVert[W^s,G]W^{-s}\rVert\le D_s.
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{F.1c.2a.7}
 $$

These bounds follow by normal ordering and the formulas $a_j|n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j}|n-e_j\rangle$. For the commutator, $|W_m-W_n|\le 2$ and $|G_{mn}|\le CW_n$; the difference $(W_m/W_n)^s-1$ is $O_s(1/W_n)$. A finite row/column sum (Schur bound) gives $D_{s}$. The same constants work after tensor compression because $P_{N}$ commutes with $W$. Include $\text{coefficients}/\hbar$ in $G$, or divide $C_s,D_s$ by $\hbar$ throughout.

Weighted energy estimates give, uniformly in N,

 $$
 \lVert W^s U_N(t,u)v\rVert\le\exp(\int_u^t D_s)\lVert W^s v\rVert,
 \tag{F.1c.2a.8}
 $$

and the same estimate for $U$. For $e_N=U_N(t,0)P_N v-P_N U(t,0)v$, Duhamel yields

 $$
 \lVert W^s e_N\rVert\le\int_0^t\exp(\int_u^t D_s)\,C_s\lVert W^{s+1}(1-P_N)U(u,0)v\rVert\,du\le t\exp(t\sup D_s)\sup C_s(N+2)^{-r}\sup_u\lVert W^{s+r+1}U(u,0)v\rVert.
 \tag{F.1c.2a.9}
 $$

Add the final projection tail (F.1c.2a.3), and any normalized-reference error (F.1c.2a.4). Equation (F.1c.2a.8) bounds the remaining exact moment by $\exp(tD_{s+r+1})\lVert W^{s+r+1}v\rVert$. Every constant is fixed before $N$ is chosen.

For first metric jets differentiate the actual evolution:

 $$
 \dot{u}(t)=U(t,0)\dot{v}-i\int_0^t U(t,u)\dot{G}(u)u(u)\,du.
 $$

The pair (u,dot u) is a triangular inhomogeneous system. Apply (F.1c.2a.7)–(F.1c.2a.9) to dot G as well as G, using one extra W power for each generator insertion. This yields

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\sup_t \bigl(\lVert W^s(u_N-u)\rVert+\lVert W^s(\dot u_N-\dot u)\rVert\bigr) \\
&\quad \le C_{s,r,T,G,\dot G} (N+2)^{-r} \\
&\qquad \bigl(\lVert W^{s+r+2}v\rVert+\lVert W^{s+r+2}\dot v\rVert\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.2a.10}
$$

The constant is obtained by the displayed integrals and (F.1c.2a.8); for a finite gate list sum the integral constants and multiply their finite $\exp(TD_s)$ factors. Higher finite insertion prefixes require further finite $W$ powers. This is a quantitative common-cutoff theorem, not a uniform operator-norm assertion.

P2 adds finitely many fresh modes and archives for a fixed schedule: include ALL of them from the beginning, then apply the same $P_{N}$. The old field is swapped into the archive. $$

<a id="lemma-f1c2b-finite-current-compression-boundary"></a>**Lemma F.1c.2b (Finite Current Compression Boundary).**

The normal canonical observation currents are quadratic; actual finite commutators include controlled cutoff-boundary terms, estimated through the same polynomial-weighted product bounds.

For $P=P_N$, $Q_\perp=1-P$, and two normal local quadratic operators $A,B$, the exact identity is

$$
\begin{aligned}
[PAP,PBP] - P[A,B]P \\
&= -P A Q_\perp B P + P B Q_\perp A P.
\end{aligned}
$$

The right side can be nonzero, even with scalar coefficients. For example direct compression of $A=P_{\mathrm{momentum}}^{2}/2$ and $B=Q_{\mathrm{coordinate}}$ has a nonzero top-level defect; multiplying $B$ by a neighboring coordinate gives the corresponding local two-site mechanism. This is distinct from the already acknowledged noncommuting-core quartic issue.

It causes no residual gap here. Quadratic operators obey $\lVert W^s A v\rVert\le C\lVert W^{s+1}v\rVert$. Apply the projection tail estimate between $A$ and $B$, or use the fact that these leakage terms are supported on finitely many top Hermite layers. For any fixed $r$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert([PAP,PBP]-P[A,B]P)v\rVert \\
&\le C_r (N+2)^{-r} \lVert W^{r+2}v\rVert,
\end{aligned}
$$

after a harmless finite adjustment of $C_{r}$ for the top-layer offset and finitely many small N. One parameter derivative is a sum of the same products with one differentiated quadratic; Heisenberg propagation is covered by the same weighted evolution bound. Thus the actual finite currents retain exact continuity and converge to their normal current with finite extra weight loss already accommodated by $p=8$. There is no need to claim exact finite quadratic closure or to change the physical source.

#### F.1c.4 — S6. Why the classical Gaussian bank fails and the quantum history succeeds

For the equal-time classical bank with $\operatorname{Var}(Q)=s^{2}/(Nv)$ and physical energy $NvE_*(Q-m)^{2}/(2s^{2})$, a centered actual draw has energy $E_*Z^{2}/2$. Its variance is $E_*^{2}/2$, independently of $v$. A fixed-width compact observation containing $O(1/v)$ independent cells therefore has a centered-energy Gaussian CLT with diverging scale. No scalar centering makes those spectral laws tight. Shrinking $E_*$ removes this noise only by changing the same off-shell physical energy/action coefficient unless a new physical normalization is supplied.

For a genuine quantum oscillator vacuum the kinetic and potential energies are correlated: their sum has exactly sharp ground energy. Replacing the actual quantum state by independent samples of its position and momentum marginals destroys this property. A coherent displacement has excitation energy proportional to v and variance proportional to v at fixed oscillator gap; its complete stress includes the kinetic sector. In the spatial field, the sum-frequency estimate S21 is the stronger local spacetime version of this mechanism.

A minimally coupled lapse does not change the oscillator's equal-time ground width, so that position-only law still cannot supply the desired lapse action. The full history law S4–S5 does supply it. A separately prepared squeezed position state whose width varies with N has nonzero squeezing energy and pair fluctuations, generally of order one per cell at fixed nonzero squeezing. It therefore is not a uniform metric-neighborhood repair of the dense independent oscillator source. Its preparation/frame contacts must be included even at first order.

#### F.1c.5 — 0. Result and exact scope

A forecast-optimizer-preservation argument is insufficient here. The new exact result is

on the complete registered compact configuration class. The physical stress arrow is distinct from the derivative of an isolated meter at a fixed prepared state. Equations (F.1c.5.7.1)–(F.1c.5.7.7) explicitly distinguish these derivatives. No claim identifies a Euclidean time index, sampler execution time and physical observation time.

This is a designed restricted compatibility witness. It does not establish a universal PCE potential, optimality over all implementations, an aggregate theoretical \(C_P\) minimum, spontaneous metric selection, a new autonomous controller, a new SI measurement of \(G\), or the full result of Lemmas 12.1h.1–12.1h.5 and Theorem 12.1h.6.

 W_{\rm on}=\operatorname{Tr}\rho G,\quad

The source is a single-use reversible-control service with consumed paid output stock. It is not a perpetually reusable zero-cost computer. #### F.1c.5 — 6. Full configuration theorem and finite approximation

<a id="theorem-f1c5a-full-configuration-scalar-potential"></a>**Theorem F.1c.5a (Full Configuration Scalar Potential).**

On (F.1c.5.2.1) with the actual cycle and prices above,

\[
 r_h(g,\phi)=\Gamma_h(\phi,g)+d_h/2,\quad
 \Gamma_h=\tfrac12(\phi-m)^TK_h(g)(\phi-m),                    \tag{F.1c.5.6.1}

and

\]

\(C_h\) is invariant under every admitted field/metric/program variation at fixed stage. In particular

\[
 \tau_*\delta(T_hV_h)=\hbar\delta\Gamma_h,
 \qquad \operatorname{argmin}_{(g,\phi)}V_h
      =\{(g,m):g\in\mathcal G_h\}.                         \tag{F.1c.5.6.3}
\]

The equality of argmin sets assumes \(m\in\mathcal F_h\) for every geometry; strict positivity of \(K_h\) makes this the only minimizing field. Geometry remains degenerate, not selected. The literal Gaussian MGF with the original cell-volume pairing is

\[
 W_h[J]=J^TVm+\tfrac12J^TVK_h^{-1}VJ,
\]

whose ordinary Legendre transform is exactly the \(\Gamma_h\) in (F.1c.5.6.1). Thus (F.1c.5.6.2) identifies the complete declared PCE objective with the **literal source's** action over its full configuration domain.

**Proof.** Write \(Q=m+Z\), \(\mathbb EZ=0\), \(\mathbb EZZ^T=K_h^{-1}\). Expanding (F.1c.5.3.4) gives

\[
 r_h=\tfrac12(\phi-m)^TK_h(\phi-m)
              +\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(K_hK_h^{-1})
      =\Gamma_h+d_h/2.
\]

By (F.1c.5.4.1)–(F.1c.5.4.2) the only nonconstant final physical charge is (F.1c.5.3.2). Insert (F.1c.5.6.1) into all four terms (F.1c.5.5.3), including the same-task benefit. This gives (F.1c.5.6.2) with no omitted configuration-dependent function. The stock/reservation endpoints, host record, \(d_h,T_h,R_{\max,h}\), and all conversion prices were fixed before comparison, proving invariance of \(C_h\). Differentiation and strict positivity give (F.1c.5.6.3). Completing the square in the actual Gaussian integral and Legendre supremum gives the final assertion. QED.

#### F.1c.5 — Finite-precursor bound

At a finite cutoff use the positive local compression of (F.1c.5.3.2), actual finite gates, exact inverses of those finite gates, and finite forecast/readout precision. Let the already proved weighted Gaussian/circuit approximation make source moments, first parameter jets, the spring expectation and normalized Gaussian Legendre value/first jets each accurate to \(\varepsilon_h\) on the nominated compact prefix. The actual finite covariance need not equal \(K_h^{-1}\), and its Legendre transform need not be exactly local.

With the ACTUAL finite measured potential \(V_{h,N}\), its fixed tariff constant \(C_{h,N}\), and its actual finite-source Legendre action \(\Gamma_{h,N}\), the triangle inequality yields, after absorbing the fixed price factors into the selected accuracy budget,

\[
 \left|\frac{T_hV_{h,N}-C_{h,N}}{E_{\rm eff}}
                     -\Gamma_{h,N}\right|\le2\varepsilon_h,
\quad
 \left\|\delta\left[\frac{T_hV_{h,N}-C_{h,N}}{E_{\rm eff}}
                     -\Gamma_{h,N}\right]\right\|
       \le2\varepsilon_h.                                  \tag{F.1c.5.6.4}
\]

The real finite output charge is not replaced by a Gaussian formula without this error. Choose the single common cutoff/precision after the compact source/metric/observable prefix, with \(\varepsilon_h\le h^2\) and summable on the existing outer sequence. The earlier exact-normal H6 theorem and its admitted iterated unbounded-extension interpretation are unchanged. No newly proved exact finite-cutoff locality is claimed.

#### F.1c.5 — 7. The response square, including the otherwise missing contacts

#### F.1c.5 — 7.1 Re-prepared configuration derivative

For any directional variation of \(K\) at fixed \(m,\phi\), let \(\Sigma=K^{-1}\). The actual source-family derivative of the meter expectation is

\[
 \delta\mathbb E_gH_{\rm err}
 =\frac{E_m}{2}(\phi-m)^T\delta K(\phi-m)
 +\frac{E_m}{2}\operatorname{Tr}(\delta K\Sigma+K\delta\Sigma).
                                                                    \tag{F.1c.5.7.1}
\]

Differentiating \(K\Sigma=I\) proves the trace terms cancel for EVERY admitted metric direction, not only forecast changes:

\[
 \delta\Sigma=-\Sigma\delta K\Sigma,\qquad
 \operatorname{Tr}(\delta K\Sigma+K\delta\Sigma)=0.           \tag{F.1c.5.7.2}
\]

This includes the real preparation/covariance programme derivative. It is exactly why the full configuration baseline is invariant.

In contrast, at a fixed prepared state,

\[
 \mathbb E_g[\delta H_{\rm err}]
 =E_m\delta\Gamma_h
        +\frac{E_m}{2}\operatorname{Tr}(\Sigma\delta K).     \tag{F.1c.5.7.3}
\]

Equation (F.1c.5.7.3) is generally different. Neither moving preparation nor future error charging out of the observation compact removes this functional source-program contact. An argument that drops it is false.

#### F.1c.5 — 7.2 The normalized source and physical transfer insertion

Differentiating the ACTUAL normal density gives

\[
 \delta\log p_g(q)=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(\Sigma\delta K)
                -\tfrac12(q-m)^T\delta K(q-m).              \tag{F.1c.5.7.4}
\]

Its mean vanishes. The first term is required by probability normalization. The same transfer has, on a kinetic step,

\[
 \delta\log K_\epsilon(q',q)
 =\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(M^{-1}\delta M)
 -\frac{(q'-q)^T\delta M(q'-q)}{2\hbar\epsilon}.             \tag{F.1c.5.7.5}
\]

By the momentum Fourier integral this is exactly the kernel of the Duhamel insertion of
\(\delta H_{\rm kin}=-P^TM^{-1}\delta M M^{-1}P/2\), with the factor \(-\epsilon/\hbar\). The potential half-step inserts its actual \(\delta A\) term. Thus the metric map is derived from the very coefficients used in (F.1c.5.3.1)–(F.1c.5.3.2), including the normalization contact; it is not the stress of an arbitrary remote spring bank.

For the ordinary Legendre action, the envelope theorem at fixed expectation \(\phi\) and the normalized source's exact Gaussian integral give

\[
 \delta_g\Gamma_h(\phi,g)
       =\tfrac12(\phi-m)^T\delta K_h(\phi-m).               \tag{F.1c.5.7.6}
\]

Equations (F.1c.5.7.1)–(F.1c.5.7.6) constitute the missing common-source response square: full-priced PCE family → literal normalized positive source/Legendre action → actual transfer insertion. The first arrow includes the teacher/preparation contact. The second includes the transfer determinant and normalized boundary contact. No arrow says raw fixed-state meter force equals the physical scalar stress.

#### F.1c.5 — 7.3 Forecast field, teacher mean, and physical coherent mean

The teacher mean is fixed \(m\). The PCE forecast is the freely compared \(\phi\). The Legendre field is identified with that same forecast value only through the proved action equality (F.1c.5.6.1), with source \(J=V^{-1}K(\phi-m)\). This is an actual statistical tilt, not an assertion that the un-tilted teacher physically has mean \(\phi\).

The encoder prepares the physical same-H thermal reference at zero statistical source. A physical field with mean \(\phi\) is obtained instead by the actual displacement/linear-drive programme: write \(x=\phi-m\) and use

\[
 M\ddot x+Ax=j,\qquad j=D_Rx                                \tag{F.1c.5.7.7}
\]

with its registered initial position/momentum. The retarded, advanced and thermal covariance kernels are spectral continuations of the same transfer kernels. The exact doubled CTP source and its Legendre inverse, including its initial thermal boundary and final sewing, are those in the consumed driven theorem. An arbitrary Euclidean off-shell history is not an unforced physical state and is not asserted to be analytically continuable pointwise. Kernel continuation and the actual compatible real-time drive supply the declared map.

For the conserved F05 witness the physical mean is on shell in the observation compact and \(j=0\) there; its preparation/displacement and any earlier drive are paid and later echoed. For off-shell response the controller force and source-work Legendre subtraction are retained. The full controller is never called stress-free merely because its net lifecycle work is zero.

#### F.1c.5 — 7.4 Physical metric legs and the moving service boundary

Place the whole finite preparation before \(-L_h\), the physical field/required flags on the observation interval, and the complete echo/decharge/final meter after \(+L_h\), with \(L_h\to\infty\) after choosing the actual finite durations. For any fixed physical compact, the latter operations have zero local stress pairing eventually. The retained mandatory ready flags keep their already registered local material tensor/reference. This support statement does not delete global lifecycle cost.

The full configuration derivative changes \(g\), its source preparation, the intended observation programme, its intended echo and final calibrated meter together. The physical compact metric insertion holds those supplied programmes/boundaries fixed and varies the actual Hamiltonian on the compact. In particular an unknown perturbation is not magically undone by retuning the echo. The resulting derivative of the later final work in this fixed-program physical experiment need not equal the full configuration derivative of (F.1c.5.6.2), and that equality is not asserted. These are different legs of the same actual source/response object, and (F.1c.5.7.1)–(F.1c.5.7.7), not spatial separation alone, compare them. Faithfulness of the physical response is inherited from its actual transfer kernels, Duhamel insertions and doubled-source inverse, not from the zero-net-work echo identity.

The existing physical ADM, signature-flag and fixed thermal/material-reference theorem then gives at the flat background, for every compact smooth metric test \(f\),

\[
 \delta_g S^{\rm MPU}_{h,\rm matter}[f]
  =\tfrac12\langle T^{\rm MPU}_{h,\rm ren}(f)\rangle+O(h),   \tag{F.1c.5.7.8}
\]

with its same operator distribution, reference complement, physical local energies and half-edge currents. The full pure/matter signature map uses the actual controlled curvature flag and volume reference already specified; it is not unmodified Wick continuation of a positive Euclidean curvature term. Combining (F.1c.5.6.2) with this map identifies the action appearing in (F.1c.5.7.8) with the full branch PCE source, with the fixed conversion \(\tau_*E_{\rm eff}=\hbar\). It does not identify the final meter's worldline stress with a four-dimensional scalar tensor.

#### F.1c.5 — 8. Resource/reference audit and inheritance of the limit

- Ground and thermal energy: retained during field loading, evolution and decharging; only actually returned work cancels. The same-H thermal material reference used in the OVD is held fixed across coherent fields; it is not a new subtraction fitted for each \(\phi\).
- Final meter: strictly retained and consumed; positive work \(E_m(\Gamma+d_h/2)\), plus finite approximation error. No final inverse, no free erase, no split between an uncharged teacher and a secretly charged clone.
- Initial blanks and purity: explicit supplied stock with its fixed price/reference boundary. It is not produced by a claimed zero-work pure reset.
- Gates, routing, correction, inverse and phases: actual finite programme plus actual inverse on all affected modes. Every finite pulse, peak and duration is inside its explicit envelope. Zero net energy does not imply zero variance or zero available capacity.
- Precision/controller and readout: charged fixed common reservation levels derived from compact-domain bounds; a larger required level changes the contract and must be recharged. Finite cutoff errors are (F.1c.5.6.4).
- Geometry and field variations: change the actual covariance/preparation, transfer coefficients, drive, inverse programme and final spring Hamiltonian. The only canceled covariance baseline is the exact trace identity (F.1c.5.7.2); other costs cancel only by actual endpoint identities or fixed charged reservations.
- Physical background references: all required flags and material densities remain or have the already admitted explicit reference; arbitrarily large new stocks are not inserted into the observation region and then discarded by fiat.
- Benefit: the exact same prediction service's risk, with a fixed uniform performance origin; the original host task and core certification remain unchanged.

Subtract \(C_h\) and multiply by \(\tau_*\) before the action comparison. The result is exactly \(\hbar\Gamma_h\) on the normal source and has the controlled finite error (F.1c.5.6.4). The existing componentwise consistency/common recovery gives the same local covariant Riemannian action, same normalized pure/matter split and same quantitative/jet convergence. Constants depending on cutoff are not a hidden metric counterterm because their derivatives with respect to every admitted configuration control vanish identically. Their bare resource magnitude remains recorded.

The same finite prefix/inner-cutoff/metric-jet diagonal can be strengthened by the finite set of new meter/reservation/echo tests, then chosen with summable \(\varepsilon_h\). Operator support is still bounded per primitive; long compilation/routing is paid. This adds no new F01 fixed-regional physical-clock theorem and no new horizon/boost-flux theorem.

<a id="lemma-f1c6-actual-finite-target-and-all-test-comparison-repair"></a>**Lemma F.1c.6 (Actual finite target and all-test comparison repair).**

#### F.1c.6 — 1. The finite target is an actual observable

Fix the same finite history graph, compact positive precision family $K(g)$, fixed mean $m$, forecast domain, and source preparation/encoder/observation/echo programme as in the bridge. At cutoff $N$ let $P_{N}$ be the tensor product of the Hermite projections onto levels $0,\dots,N$. In dimensionless oscillator coordinates with $[Q_i,P_i]=i\hbar$, define

$$
q_{i,N}=P_N Q_i P_N\quad\text{restricted to }\operatorname{ran}P_{N}.
$$

The different $q_{i,N}$ commute because they act on distinct tensor factors. The finite target is the joint spectral outcome $q$ of these actual finite observables, demodulated from the balanced cue as before. The predictor supplies $s\phi$ before that outcome is read. The joint spectral labels are finite symbols; their fixed real codebook is part of the registered apparatus. Finite codebook/control rounding, if used, has its own charged precision tolerance.

Use the following actual final Hamiltonian, rather than directly compressing the continuum square:

$$
H_{\mathrm{err},N}^{\mathrm{poly}}(g,\phi) = E_m/2 \sum_{ij} K_{ij}(g)(q_{i,N}-\phi_i I)(q_{j,N}-\phi_j I).
\tag{F.1c.6.F1}
$$

It is positive since the $q_{i,N}$ commute and $K>0$. Its support is the same local precision stencil. All its coefficients and their parameter derivatives are bounded at this finite stage. An eigenvalue $q$ incurs exactly the classical loss

$$
\begin{aligned}
\ell_N(q,\phi,g) &= (q-\phi)^{\mathsf T} K(g)(q-\phi)/2, \\
H_{\mathrm{err},N}^{\mathrm{poly}}(q) &= E_m \ell_N(q,\phi,g).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.6.F2}
$$

Thus this is an actual finite prediction trial whose physical charge equals its score. It does not score a spectral energy outcome as if that outcome were the earlier coordinate target.

The final smooth ramp $a(t)H_{\mathrm{err},N}^{\mathrm{poly}}$ commutes with every $q_{i,N}$. Its unitary changes no joint-target probability, exactly, for every finite $N$. Its work is the actual final mean charge. A joint-target measurement after the ramp is nondemolition for the charge. Its supplied pointer, output record, finite spectral resolution and routing are in the same fixed reservation inventory; no teacher or pointer is uncomputed after the charge. The earlier observation/drive echo remains exact on all affected modes. No target measurement is introduced before that echo.

#### F.1c.6 — 2. What direct Hermite compression would have measured

In one coordinate,

$$
P_N Q^2 P_N - (P_N Q P_N)^2 = \hbar(N+1) \Pi_N/2,
\tag{F.1c.6.F3}
$$

where $\Pi_{N}$ projects onto the top retained Hermite level. For i different from j, tensor compression has no analogous cross-term difference. Consequently

$$
\begin{aligned}
&P_N H_{\mathrm{err}} P_N - H_{\mathrm{err},N}^{\mathrm{poly}} \\
&\quad = E_m \hbar(N+1)/4 \sum_i K_{ii}(g)\, \Pi_{i,N}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.6.F4}
$$

The right side is positive. Direct compression is a legitimate physical meter, but its spectral readout is not exactly the loss of the finite target $q_{N}$. It also generally fails to commute with $q_{N}$. These are finite identities, not matters of nomenclature. Using a spectral readout of the compressed energy proves retention of that energy; it does not establish (F.1c.6.F2).

The repair changes only the finite precursor's final meter. The ideal normal source's multiplication Hamiltonian, positive Gaussian law, response square and physical observation remain unchanged.

#### F.1c.6 — 3. Common value and first-jet estimates

Let $\psi_N(g)$ be the actual finite prepared history state, formed with the actual compressed gate generators, and let $\psi(g)$ be the exact normal Gaussian. Use the common weighted preparation/first-jet bounds already proved in Lemma F.1c.2a. For any chosen integer $s$, on the fixed compact parameter family,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sup_g (\lVert W^s \psi_N\rVert + \lVert W^s \partial_g \psi_N\rVert) &\le M_s, \\
W&=1+\sum_i a_i^* a_i,
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.6.F5}
$$

after increasing $M_{s}$ to cover finitely many small $N$. This follows directly from its uniform-in-$N$ weighted propagator estimate; it is not inferred from convergence of a few matrix elements. Since $W\ge N+1$ on $\Pi_{i,N}$,

$$
\begin{gathered}
\lVert\Pi_{i,N}\psi_N\rVert\le(N+1)^{-s}M_s, \\
\lVert\Pi_{i,N}\partial_g\psi_N\rVert\le(N+1)^{-s}M_s.
\end{gathered}
\tag{F.1c.6.F6}
$$

From (F.1c.6.F4), uniformly over the compact (g,phi) family,

$$
\begin{gathered}
\lvert\langle P_N H_{\mathrm{err}}P_N-H_{\mathrm{err},N}^{\mathrm{poly}}\rangle\rvert\le C_s(N+1)^{1-2s}, \\
\lvert\partial_g\langle P_N H_{\mathrm{err}}P_N-H_{\mathrm{err},N}^{\mathrm{poly}}\rangle\rvert\le C'_s(N+1)^{1-2s}.
\end{gathered}
\tag{F.1c.6.F7}
$$

The derivative includes both $\partial_g K$ and the derivative of the prepared state. Field derivatives of this difference vanish because (F.1c.6.F4) has no $\phi$ dependence. Mixed retained jets follow by applying the same argument to the finite number of state/control derivatives. Thus substituting (F.1c.6.F1) does not lose the previously proved common cost/moment/first-jet convergence. For the scalar Gaussian preparation family, its stronger exponential Hermite tails can also be used, but they are not needed for (F.1c.6.F7).

If a unitary comparison after the final charge is required, it is also controlled: (F.1c.6.F1) and the compressed quadratic differ by (F.1c.6.F4), a boundary-supported operator of size $O(N)$. Duhamel applied to the exact quadratic normal evolution gives a polynomial-in-$N$ factor times its Gaussian Hermite tail. The finite polynomial meter has bandwidth at most two and entries $O(W)$, so the same weighted commutator/propagation estimate applies. No exact finite CCR is assumed.

#### F.1c.6 — Literal finite generating function and Legendre transform

Let $p_N(q;g)$ be the Born law of the commuting $q_{N}$ in $\psi_N(g)$. It is unchanged by the echo and final meter ramp. Set

$$
W_N(J,g)=\log \sum_q p_N(q;g) \exp[J^{\mathsf T} V(g)q].
\tag{F.1c.6.F8}
$$

It is the literal normalized finite-target MGF. The existing exponential-tail refinement applies to this finite source: for every fixed bounded source set, source derivatives through order two and first parameter jets converge uniformly to the Gaussian $W$. The argument uses the actual compressed preparation, the estimate $\lVert J^T Vq_N\rVert\le C_J\sqrt{N+1}$, and the Gaussian leakage bound; its error has the form

$$
C (N+1)^b \exp[-a N + C_J \sqrt{N+1}].
\tag{F.1c.6.F9}
$$

Polynomial moment convergence alone would not prove (F.1c.6.F9).

The exact source lemma is Lemma F.1c.2a, §7, equations (F.1c.2a.14)–(F.1c.2a.15), together with its actual-unitary preparation estimate (F.1c.2a.9) and first-jet estimate (F.1c.2a.10). The distinction between those uses matters. For the preparation gates, compact nonsingular Gaussian intermediate vectors and their polynomial jets have $\exp(aW)$ moments; their Hermite leakage gives exponential error under the actual bounded finite **unitary** propagators. For the MGF, $\exp(tF_N)$, $F_N=J^T Vq_N$, is **not unitary**. Its norm is bounded by $\exp(C_J\sqrt{N+1})$. Its nonunitary Duhamel leakage is $P_N F(1-P_N)\exp(tF)\psi$, and $\exp(tF)\psi$ is an unnormalized shifted Gaussian with the same strictly positive real quadratic part. This yields (F.1c.6.F9), including the $\exp(C_J\sqrt{N+1})$ loss. Differentiating at most twice in $J$ and once in $g$ inserts only finitely many linear factors or polynomial Gaussian jets; each contributes a polynomial in $N$ while the same bound survives after reducing $a$. Constants $a,C_J$ and $b$ are registered at each fixed outer graph. The argument neither treats $\exp(F_N)$ as a contraction nor infers exponential integrability from polynomial moments.

For completeness, local convergence of $W$ does imply convergence of the **global** finite Legendre maximizer on the nominated compact field domain. Fix the outer graph. The normal maximizer $J_*(g,\phi)=V^{-1}K(\phi-m)$ lies in a compact source set. Enlarge this set by a fixed radius $r$. Its Gaussian Hessian $VK^{-1}V$ has a positive uniform smallest eigenvalue $\lambda_{h}$. If $\lVert\nabla_J W_N-\nabla_J W\rVert<\lambda_h r/2$, then on the sphere $|J-J_*|=r$,

$$
(J-J_*)\cdot[\nabla_J W_N-V\phi]>0.
$$

Therefore $W_N-J^T V\phi$ has an interior minimum in that ball. Its stationary point is a global minimum by convexity; uniform Hessian convergence makes it unique in the ball and bounds $|J_N-J_*|$ by $O(\text{error}/\lambda_h)$. A second global minimum would contradict the strict convexity on the connecting segment near that point. No assumption of global source-uniform convergence is needed.

The envelope identity is

$$
\partial_g \Gamma_N = J_N^{\mathsf T} (\partial_g V) \phi - \partial_g W_N(J_N,g).
\tag{F.1c.6.F10}
$$

The source-pairing term must be retained when V varies. Equations (F.1c.6.F9)-(F.1c.6.F10), the inverse bound and compactness give value/first-jet convergence of $\Gamma_{N}$ to $\Gamma$ uniformly on the admitted (g,phi) domain. The constants may depend on the outer graph; choose N only after those constants are bounded. This is not a cutoff-independent inverse-response assertion.

#### F.1c.6 — 4. The actual finite full PCE potential

Evaluate all four D.1 terms with $r_N=\mathbb{E}\ell_N$, actual final charge $E_m r_N$, the original fixed reservation package, the same fixed $R_{\max}$ and positive prices, and $\mathrm{PP}_N=(1+k_{\mathrm{PP}}r_N)^{-1}$. Choose $R_{\max}$ once above the compact normal risk bound plus a strict margin; increase $N$ until the finite uniform error lies within that margin. Finitely many excluded small $N$ are not part of the chosen realizing sequence.

Then the exact finite identity is

$$
(T_h V_{h,N}-C_{h,N})/E_{\mathrm{eff}} = r_N-d_h/2,
\tag{F.1c.6.F11}
$$

with the genuine configuration-independent $C_{h,N}$ given by the same tariff formula as the bridge. It is not exactly $\Gamma_{h,N}$ at finite $N$. Combining the moment/jet, (F.1c.6.F7), and Legendre estimates yields

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\sup_{g,\phi} \bigl(|r_N-d_h/2-\Gamma_{h,N}| + \lVert D_{g,\phi}[r_N-d_h/2-\Gamma_{h,N}]\rVert\bigr) \\
&\quad \le \epsilon_{h,N} \to 0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.1c.6.F12}
$$

Every tolerance and price factor is included before selecting $N$. This establishes the bridge's desired finite estimate for an actual measured predictor target, not only an energy observable. The finite mean need not equal $m$ exactly; its small bias and covariance defect are part of $\epsilon_{h,N}$. Consequently exact finite minimizers can differ slightly from $m$, while uniform convergence and compact recovery give the stated normal and outer variational conclusion.

No exact locality is claimed for $\Gamma_{h,N}$. Exact H6 belongs to the separately admitted normal $h$-source. Hard operator-norm reservations apply to each finite precursor. Divergent absolute reservation constants remain in $C_{h,N}$; no finite ultraviolet total cost or convergence of those absolute tariffs is claimed. The normalized action limit is (F.1c.6.F11), not an equation involving subtraction of two infinite costs.

#### F.1c.6 — 5. Repairing the finite-prefix/all-test step

A growing countable list of tested metric functions alone does not prove convergence against every compact smooth function. An unbounded functional can vanish on every early test while growing on an untested direction. The comparison needs a uniform test-seminorm bound, or an equivalent graph-norm estimate. Here the existing weighted gate construction supplies one.

Fix an outer spatial/history stage $h$ and observation compact $K$. The physical metric vertex is a finite sum of actual quadratic operators, with coefficients obtained by evaluating a metric test $f$ and its derivatives of order at most two on the registered stencil. The local curvature term is included. On the fixed time interval each coefficient is bounded by $C_{h,K}\lVert f\rVert_{C^2(K)}$; time integration multiplies by the finite interval length. The actual vertex and its first source derivatives therefore obey weighted bounds

$$
\begin{gathered}
\lVert O_h(f)v\rVert\le C_{h,K}\lVert f\rVert_{C^2}\lVert W_h v\rVert, \\
\lVert D_g O_h(f)v\rVert\le C'_{h,K}\lVert f\rVert_{C^q}\lVert W_h^s v\rVert,
\end{gathered}
\tag{F.1c.6.F13}
$$

for fixed finite s,q determined by the retained insertion list. The finite compressed generators obey the same banded-matrix bounds uniformly in N. The tensor-Hermite Duhamel estimate is valid for **every** v in the corresponding $W_{h}$ graph domain, not just a finite vector prefix. Apply it to every finite local coefficient operator and take the finite maximum. This gives

$$
\lVert i_N O_{h,N}(f)P_N v-O_h(f)v\rVert\le A_{h,K,r}(N+2)^{-r}\lVert f\rVert_{C^q(K)}\lVert W_h^{s+r+2}v\rVert.
\tag{F.1c.6.F14}
$$

Here $P_{N}$ is the actual coordinate tensor projection and $i_{N}$ is its inclusion into the ideal coordinate Hilbert space; the final projection tail is included in (F.1c.6.F14). This is a graph-norm comparison, not a fictitious isometry from an infinite space into a finite one. Actual fixed normalized input states use the earlier explicit normalization estimate. The common Fourier/Schwartz representation is applied after this inclusion.

Initial-state, encoder/corrector and differentiated-state errors obey the analogous scalar estimate with their recorded Gaussian weighted moments. The finitely many site sums and growing stencil factors belong to $A_{h,K,r}$; no $h$-uniform assertion is made about that constant before $N$ is selected.

At a fixed $h$, the positive oscillator comparison energy and $W_{h}$ have equivalent polynomial graph norms. This follows from their positive finite-dimensional quadratic forms (or their exact symplectic diagonalization), with explicit finite $h$-dependent constants. For the field core, the physical comparison energy $A_{h}$ is the finite Fourier restriction of the common massive energy; hence $\lVert A_h^p\psi\rVert\le C_p\lVert A^p\psi\rVert$ under the retained Fourier identification, using the already proved dispersion comparison. Fixed auxiliary Gaussian states contribute their known $h$-dependent moments to the constant. Absorb these constants into $A_{h,K,r}$.

Choose $r$ once large enough for the desired insertion order, and choose $N_{h}$ so that the complete factor in (F.1c.6.F14), after this graph-norm conversion and the finite site sums, is at most the nominated summable $\epsilon_{h}$. For each compact exhaustion $K_1,\dots,K_h$ take the maximum. The result is a bound of the form

$$
\lVert(i_{N_h}T_{h,N_h}(f)P_{N_h}-T_h(f))\psi\rVert\le\epsilon_h\lVert f\rVert_{C^q(K)}\lVert A^p\psi\rVert,
\tag{F.1c.6.F15}
$$

with **fixed p,q** for the quadratic stress family and every $f$ supported in a fixed $K$ once $K$ has entered the exhaustion. One deliberately nonoptimal choice is $r=2$, $p=8$ and $q=16$: the stress/current vertices have degree at most two on the commuting observation-control branch, a single parameter derivative inserts at most one additional quadratic generator, and the projection/Duhamel estimate uses at most $s+r+2$ powers with $s\le 2$ for this retained list. Enlarging to $p=8$ absorbs these losses and fixed reference/normalization products. $q=16$ dominates the actual metric stencil order two and the finite-order compact-smearing seminorms used in the inherited stress kernel bound. More gates or more sites increase the numerical constant $A_{h,K,r}$, not these derivative or polynomial degrees. A first derivative of a long product is a sum of single-insertion terms, not a product with one derivative at every gate. Thus $p$ and $q$ do not grow with $h$. Noncommuting matrix-valued preparation controls, when retained, still have degree-two generator estimates; their possible quartic local currents are outside the autonomous observation stress sector and are not substituted for its quadratic current. The same construction controls the mean action first variation, including its normalization, and the new meter scalar risk/jet on its compact controller family. Increasing the retained derivative order later requires its own finite larger graph norm, rather than silently asserting uniform control over all orders.

Combine (F.1c.6.F15) with the already established ideal-lattice stress bound and compact-test continuity. This proves convergence for every compact smooth metric test and every vector in the declared all-polynomial-moment core along one common actual finite sequence. It supplies the needed equicontinuity instead of inferring it from countable-prefix agreement. On the nominated coherent/thermal mean family the finite inner error can be chosen below $h^{2}$, so the existing $O(h)$ B.8c first-variation remainder is unchanged.

Preparation and post-window meter operations still have disjoint physical support from each fixed observation compact eventually. This support fact removes their local pairings there; it does not remove functional derivatives of the separately re-prepared configuration family. Those remain the bridge's explicit covariance/source contacts.

#### F.1c.6 — 6. Literal allocation of the unchanged core cost operator

The total objective is unchanged by the following explicit allocation, which avoids conflating auxiliary tariffs with the original core complexity proxy. Split the bridge's fixed $R_{\mathrm{op}}$ into $R_{\mathrm{core}}+R_{\mathrm{aux}}$, where $R_{\mathrm{core}}$ is the actual lifecycle integral of the unchanged cores' registered $R/R_I$ operational operators on their original clock, and $R_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is the fixed incoming-stock/reservation service charge. Keep the original $R/R_I$ and B.6 calibration unchanged. Write

$$
\begin{aligned}
V_{\mathrm{op}} &= R_{\mathrm{core}}/T_h, \\
V_{\mathrm{prop}} &= R_{\mathrm{prop}}/T_h, \\
V_{\mathrm{penalty}} &= (R_{\mathrm{aux}}+R_{\mathrm{fixed}}+E_m r_N)/T_h, \\
V_{\mathrm{benefit}} &= [B_{\mathrm{host}}+bE_m(R_{\max}-r_N)]/T_h.
\end{aligned}
