#### F.5a.2.8 A localized parity charge and finite sector separation

For any normalized compact local mode $f_0$ define the odd self-adjoint unitary $F_0=c(f_0)+c(f_0)^*$. The automorphism

$$
\rho_{F_0}(A)=F_0 A F_0,\quad A\in A,
$$

is localized in its diamond: $F_0$ commutes with every spacelike even observable. It is transportable. If $G_0$ is another normalized local Majorana unitary, $V=G_0F_0$ is even, belongs to a common containing local algebra, and $\operatorname{Ad}(V)\rho_{F_0}=\rho_{G_0}$. Also $\rho_{F_0}^2=\mathrm{id}$, so its conjugate is itself and its statistical dimension is one.

The full Fock representation restricted to $A$ splits into even and odd parity representations. Their irreducibility and inequivalence follow from the global CAR irreducibility: the even-algebra commutant is $\operatorname{span}\{I,\Gamma\}$. An even and an odd implementer of the same automorphism would have an odd quotient commuting with $A$, impossible in that commutant. $F_0$ maps $H_{\mathrm{even}}$ unitarily to $H_{\mathrm{odd}}$, giving the positive-energy covariant implementation $U_\rho(g)=F_0U(g)|_{H_{\mathrm{odd}}}F_0$ on $H_{\mathrm{even}}$. Since $U(2\pi)=\Gamma$ for the spinor Fock representation,

$$
U_\rho(2\pi)=-I,\quad U_{\mathrm{vac}}(2\pi)=+I.
\tag{F.5a.2.9}
$$

This is one irreducible localized covariant finite-statistics sector and its conjugate, not a claim about every possible charge of the net.

The registered response-faithful test family consists of the two specifically prepared normal states $\omega$ and $\omega_{F0}$; it is not asserted that one local effect separates every state belonging to two globally inequivalent locally normal sectors. For their finite, physical separating response take $f_0=F_b$ from §3, with the fixed $b=R/256$ of §7 (so $a=b$ for this test only) and the actual even effect $n_f=c(f_0)^*c(f_0)$. Its probabilities in the vacuum and the odd state $F_0\Omega$ are $q_{a}$ and $1-q_a$, because $F_0n_fF_0=I-n_f$. Their gap is at least 7/8 by (F.5a.2.2). The same finite positive-duration number-pointer instrument used in §4 reads the effect locally. The sector test has its own single lab clock: prepare during $[0,b/4]$, couple the number pointer during $[b/4,b/2]$, and commit during $[b/2,3b/4]$. All field-dependent strokes use lab smearing $S_{t}f_0$ with this common $t$, so they prepare and read the same interaction-picture mode inside the declared $B_b$-based laboratory. For exact preparation, take a local reservoir Majorana $R_0$ and run the even self-adjoint Hamiltonian $\pi iR_0F_0/(2\tau_p)$ for any declared $\tau_{p}>0$, using transported compact smearings as in §4. Its propagator is $R_0F_0$, so it sends the field vacuum to $F_0\Omega$ and flips the reservoir parity. Its norm is $\pi/(2\tau_p)$, and its field-energy commutator is bounded by $\pi\lVert Df_0\rVert/\tau_p$. Thus the compensating parity is retained in an actual charged reservoir; no superposition of different total parity is required. The separating record is the measured $n_{f}$ response, not an unobserved parity label.

If $F_0,G_0$ are spacelike separated, $F_0G_0=-G_0F_0$. For the actual even charge transporter $V=G_0F_0$,

$$
\varepsilon(\rho,\rho)=V^{*}\rho_{F_0}(V)=F_0G_0F_0G_0=-I.
\tag{F.5a.2.10}
$$

Thus this retained charge is the sVec sign, not $\mathrm{Rep}(\mathbb{Z}_2)$'s sign. Equations (F.5a.2.9)–(F.5a.2.10) supply the spin/statistics comparison independently of an argument from fusion data alone. The imported Guido–Longo field theorem provides the compatible CPT and $\Gamma=U(2\pi)$ conclusion under Reeh–Schlieder, normal graded commutation and modular covariance; those premises have been identified above. We do not invoke its observable-sector theorem while leaving its extra hypotheses unverified.

#### F.5a.2.9 An actual retained exchange-sign experiment

An isolated global phase on a two-fermion state is not a retained outcome. The following finite local interferometer makes it one. Take two normalized smooth compact modes $f_1,f_2$ in one laboratory diamond. For the fixed laboratory in §7 use support radius $b/4$, centers $\pm(b/2)e_2$ relative to $(2,0,0)$, one identical spinor polarization, and the same smooth bump profile. Their supports are disjoint and contained in $B_{b}$, so they are orthogonal spatial modes of the same field. Write $a=c(f_1)$, $b_{\mathrm{op}}=c(f_2)$, and let $\tau_{\mathrm{ex}}=2b>0$. In the following displayed exchange formula the operator letter $b$ abbreviates $b_{\mathrm{op}}$; the geometric radius $b$ is only used in the timing and support statements. Prepare both modes occupied by two of the parity-safe reservoir resets above, each lasting $b/4$ with a fresh preloaded reservoir; the fixed occupied input makes source-label encoding unnecessary for this calibration experiment. This gives $|11\rangle$ on these two field modes exactly, independently of prior vacuum correlations. Keep the reservoirs in the accounting.

Define the positive even quadratic interaction-picture exchange Hamiltonian

$$
H_{\mathrm{ex}}^{I}=\pi(n_a+n_b-a^{*}b-b^{*}a)/(2\tau_{\mathrm{ex}}).
$$

Use one global lab clock $t$ measured from the first preparation stroke. Both occupied-mode resets and the exchange use lab smearings $S_{t}f_i$, so every stroke acts on the same fixed interaction-picture modes $c(f_i)$. The exchange begins at $t=b/2$; in its own elapsed time $s$ its lab smearings are therefore $S_{s+b/2}f_i$, not $S_{s}f_i$. Its interaction-picture form is exactly $H_{\mathrm{ex}}^I$, including free drift, and finite propagation confines its support to the initial mode support enlarged by $t$. Its one-particle interaction-picture unitary after $\tau_{\mathrm{ex}}=2b$ is the mode transposition $S$; the output-mode calibration at exchange completion is relative to the same freely propagated labels $S_{5b/2}f_i$. On the full two-mode algebra its propagator is the fermionic second quantization $\Gamma(S)$:

$$
|00\rangle\to|00\rangle,\quad |10\rangle\to|01\rangle,\quad |01\rangle\to|10\rangle,\quad |11\rangle\to-|11\rangle.
\tag{F.5a.2.11}
$$

These identities fix the phase convention by the vacuum action and calibrate the actual one-particle exchange. The doubly occupied sign is $\det(S)=-1$ and is not inserted as a two-particle phase label. Adding an extra quartic controlled-phase to remove it changes the specified physical control.

Prepare a bosonic pointer $Q$ in $|+\rangle$. Run the parity-even controlled interaction-picture Hamiltonian $|1\rangle\langle 1|_Q\otimes H_{\mathrm{ex}}^I$ for duration $\tau_{\mathrm{ex}}$. It produces

$$
|{+}\rangle_Q|11\rangle\to|{-}\rangle_Q|11\rangle.
$$

A Hadamard lasting $b/4$ followed by a CNOT lasting $b/4$ to a fresh classical record reads $X_{Q}=-1$. Their bounded generators may be taken as $\pi(I-U)/(2(b/4))$ for the corresponding Hermitian involutions $U$, with norm at most $4\pi/b$. Along with the two preparation strokes and the exchange, total duration is $3b$. On the separately retained vacuum calibration $|00\rangle$, the same apparatus reads $X_Q=+1$. One-particle calibrations verify the exchange action of $S$. Thus the retained outcome distinguishes the CAR exchange sign through the measured field-controlled interferometer, rather than merely recording “fermion” in metadata.

With the fixed $b$ and $\tau_{\mathrm{ex}}=2b$ above, the exchange stroke lies in $[b/2,5b/2]\times B_{7b/2}$. Including the two preparations and the pointer readout, the complete history lies in $[0,3b]\times B_{4b}$, with the containing laboratory diamond and $7b$ cover bound already given in §7. This common causal region, together with the declared positive duration and support, is part of the record; the duration is not confused with the diameter of the enlarged diamond. We make no claim to implement this joint two-mode gate by independently selectable spacelike controls or to derive a pointwise microscopic transport circuit. If desired, the two smooth modes can be co-located orthogonal spatial/spin modes, making the laboratory character literal; their labels are then exchanged by the stated local quadratic field operation. The protocol witnesses the exchange intertwiner of the retained CAR charge, not an experimental trajectory of macroscopic particles.

The generator norm is $\pi/\tau_{\mathrm{ex}}$. Since $[H_{\mathrm{phys}},c(f_i)]$ is bounded with norm $\lVert Df_i\rVert$, the energy increase has a finite bound obtained from the integrated commutator. For example $4\pi(\lVert Df_1\rVert+\lVert Df_2\rVert)$, together with the preparation bounds, is conservative. The pointer gates add their explicit $\pi/\text{duration}$ norm entries and no field energy. Clock, reservoirs and every final readout are retained in the budget. The source and all gates are on the very same CAR algebra used for the cone and modular record.

#### F.5a.2.10 Reflected response and fermionic CPT comparison

The geometric antiunitary $R_{W}$, and its conformal transport, reverse the time orientation and preserve the source characteristic cone. A reflected null pair $j_Wx,j_Wy$ is read in forward order with the endpoint roles exchanged. Construct a fresh forward pulse experiment by the same recipe at these reflected endpoints. For a charge-conjugated pulse use the corresponding hole mode and its actual even hole-number effect $I-n$; the vacuum hole occupancy is small just as the particle occupancy was in (F.5a.2.2). This is a physical conjugate observable and conjugate preparation, not reusing a bit label without an instrument.

For completeness, equal vacuum occupations $q$ of the source and propagated detector modes give, with $r=\langle F,h\rangle$ and $w=\langle F,Qh\rangle$, $b_{\mathrm{forward}}=q(1+|r|^2)-2\operatorname{Re}(\overline{r}w)$. Exchanging $F$ and $h$ conjugates both $r$ and $w$, so it leaves this baseline and the contrast $|r|^2$ unchanged. Antiunitary conjugation preserves the resulting real probabilities, CAR inner-product moduli, all operator norms and the even grading; charge conjugation replaces particle number by the declared hole-number effect. The reversed geometric order is compared using this independently constructed forward apparatus, not by inverting the noisy measurement channel or erasure. On the transformed chart clocks it has the same completion interval and the same probabilities (F.5a.2.5). The scalar value $-I$ in the charge-exchange intertwiner is real, so reflection leaves the sign in (F.5a.2.10) unchanged; the reflected controlled-exchange experiment again has $X_{Q}=-1$. CPT sends the odd parity sector to its conjugate, which is the same sector here, while exchanging particle and hole field representatives.

**Definition F.5b.1 (PU One-Particle Sector Label).** On a regular AQFT/DHR response branch with emergent Poincaré asymptotics, a retained one-particle sector is labeled by
$$
\mathfrak s=(\mathcal O_p,\lambda_{\mathrm{Wig}},\rho_{\mathrm{int}},\chi),
$$
where $\mathcal O_p$ is a positive-energy Poincaré momentum orbit, $\lambda_{\mathrm{Wig}}$ is the Wigner little-group label $(m,s)$ for $m>0$ or $(0,h)$ for $m=0$, $\rho_{\mathrm{int}}$ is a simple object of the retained finitely generated DHR response category, and $\chi$ records chirality data when the Lorentz representation is Weyl. On branches where retained multiplicities arise, the label is enriched to
$$
\mathfrak s_{\mathrm{mult}}=(\mathcal O_p,\lambda_{\mathrm{Wig}},\rho_{\mathrm{int}},\chi,\iota_{\mathrm{mult}}),
$$
with $\iota_{\mathrm{mult}}$ recording the retained-multiplicity index.

The conjugate sector is
$$
\overline{\mathfrak s}=(\mathcal O_p,\overline{\lambda}_{\mathrm{Wig}},\overline{\rho}_{\mathrm{int}},\overline\chi),
$$
where $\overline{\rho}_{\mathrm{int}}$ is the DHR conjugate object. Antiparticles are represented by conjugate response sectors, not by appending a central $\mathbb Z_2$ label to Poincaré representation theory.

**Proposition F.5b.2 (Wigner-DHR-PU Sector Representation).** On a regular particle-sector branch satisfying the modular spin-statistics-CPT gate, assume:

1. every retained one-particle state belongs to an isolated positive-energy Wigner mass shell or a separately certified massless finite-helicity shell;
2. a covariant particle-to-DHR assignment sends each retained shell to a localized, transportable finite-statistics endomorphism and preserves conjugation;
3. the assignment is multiplicity-free and separates PPI-equivalence classes;
4. every label declared retained is realized by such a particle-sector object.

Then retained asymptotic one-particle sectors are represented up to PPI response equivalence by the labels of Definition F.5b.1, via the map
$$
\Psi:\{\text{retained one-particle sectors}\}/\!\equiv_{\mathrm{PPI}}
\longrightarrow
\{(\mathcal O_p,\lambda_{\mathrm{Wig}},\rho_{\mathrm{int}},\chi)\},
$$
where:

1. (Injectivity) Distinct PPI-equivalence classes give distinct labels by the separating-label branch hypothesis. The Wigner orbit and little-group label, the DHR object, and $\chi$ are the registered components of Definition F.5b.1; Theorems F.4 and F.5a supply the corresponding branch realizations but do not by themselves prove injectivity. The multiplicity-free retained branch hypothesis excludes a hidden retained multiplicity within one registered label.

2. (Surjectivity onto retained labels) A label is in the image of $\Psi$ exactly when the branch supplies a retained response-sector object realizing the Wigner data and DHR class; labels with no retained response-sector object are not in the image.

3. (Functoriality) Conjugate sectors are represented by conjugate labels via $\mathfrak s\mapsto\overline{\mathfrak s}$, and the spin-statistics descent of Theorem F.5a is the statistics descent on the right-hand side.

If the multiplicity-free hypothesis fails on a given branch, $\Psi$ is replaced by an enriched map
$$
\Psi_{\mathrm{mult}}:\{\text{retained sectors}\}/\!\equiv_{\mathrm{PPI}}
\to
\{(\mathcal O_p,\lambda_{\mathrm{Wig}},\rho_{\mathrm{int}},\chi,\iota_{\mathrm{mult}})\}
$$
carrying a retained-multiplicity label $\iota_{\mathrm{mult}}$, and the injectivity statement is rephrased for the enriched labels.

The exclusion is branch-relative: the representation excludes only labels that are response-null, violate the fixed branch constraints, or lack a retained response-sector object. Continuous-spin (infinite-helicity) massless Wigner representations are excluded *by branch retention*, not by Poincaré representation theory itself: they have no finite retained response-sector realization on the standard particle-sector branch.

*Proof.* Hypothesis 1 assigns the Wigner orbit and little-group label. Hypothesis 2 assigns the DHR object and preserves conjugation, while the Lorentz representation supplies the chirality label when applicable. Hypothesis 3 makes the resulting label map injective on PPI classes. Hypothesis 4 makes it surjective onto the declared retained labels. If multiplicities are retained, adjoining the multiplicity index gives the enriched map and restores injectivity. ∎

**Remark F.5b.3 (CPT Is Not a Three-Label Shortcut).** CPT closure is not obtained by merely naming abstract $C$, $P$, and $T$ involutions. It requires either the Wightman/Jost package of Theorem F.4 or the antiunitary modular reflection plus DHR conjugate-sector implementation of Theorem F.5a, with vanishing modular cocycle obstruction. The thermodynamic arrow remains the entropy-increasing realization branch and is compatible with CPT symmetry of the retained field algebra.

**Theorem F.5c (Categorical Gauge Reconstruction and Conditional Field-Net Reconstruction).** Suppose a branch supplies the finitely generated datum $\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{DHR}}$ of Definition F.5b, including its full tensor closure and a faithful symmetric $*$-preserving fiber functor $\omega_{\mathrm{fib}}$ to finite-dimensional super Hilbert spaces with the graded flip. Then
$$
G_{\mathrm{resp}}=\operatorname{Aut}^{\otimes}(\omega_{\mathrm{fib}})
$$
is compact and $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{resp}}\simeq\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathrm{fin}}(G_{\mathrm{resp}},k)$ as symmetric tensor $C^*$ categories with super fiber functor, where the central involution $k$ implements Bose/Fermi parity. The ordinary Hilbert-space specialization requires $k=1$ on every sector. If $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{resp}}$ has only finitely many inequivalent simple objects, $G_{\mathrm{resp}}$ is finite; a continuous compact gauge group requires an infinite representation-category closure even when finitely generated.

A field net $\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{PU}}$ with a faithful $G_{\mathrm{resp}}$ action and
$$
\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{obs}}(O)=\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{PU}}(O)^{G_{\mathrm{resp}}}
\tag{F.9.5c.1}
$$
may be asserted by Doplicher–Roberts reconstruction only on a further certified branch: $\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{obs}}$ has the requisite vacuum net, duality and property-B structure, and $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{resp}}$ is equivalent to the **complete** finite-statistics DHR category of that net, rather than just a selected retained subcategory. The resulting normal field system contains all those sectors. If only a selected response subcategory is supplied, the first categorical conclusion holds but (F.9.5c.1) and completeness of the charged-field net are not established by the source theorem.

Each nontrivial irreducible representation of $G_{\mathrm{resp}}$ occurs as an object in the reconstructed tensor category. An extra factor acting trivially on every object of this complete response category is absent from $\operatorname{Aut}^{\otimes}(\omega_{\mathrm{fib}})$; its removal from the physical description is a separate PPI/PCE response-equivalence step, not a consequence of the Doplicher–Roberts theorem alone.

If Appendix G supplies a symmetric tensor **and fiber-functor** equivalence
$$
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{resp}}\simeq\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathrm{fin}}(G_{\mathrm{SM}}/Z,k_{\mathrm{SM}})
\tag{F.9.5c.2}
$$
for the full tensor closures, preserving the parity involutions, Tannaka reconstruction identifies $G_{\mathrm{resp}}$ with the represented compact quotient. Agreement of a finite matter roster, fusion table or gauge algebra alone does not establish (F.9.5c.2) or fix the global compact group. For a category generated by retained representations $\mathcal S$ of $G$, the effective group is $G/N_{\mathcal S}$ with $N_{\mathcal S}=\bigcap_{\rho\in\mathcal S}\ker\rho$; this closed normal subgroup need not be central.

*Proof.* Apply super Tannaka reconstruction (Müger, Appendix B, Theorem B.18 in Halvorson 2006); the ordinary even case is Theorem B.6. An ordinary symmetric Hilbert-space fiber functor would force all sectors to be even (Proposition B.10). A compact group with only finitely many irreducible representation classes is finite by Peter–Weyl, proving the finite-roster consequence. Doplicher–Roberts reconstruction, under the additional vacuum-net, duality, property-B and category-completeness hypotheses, constructs the complete normal field system with gauge-fixed observable net (Doplicher and Roberts 1990; Halvorson 2006, §10). These hypotheses are not supplied by a selected subcategory. The remaining response-equivalence and Appendix G identification statements follow only under their explicitly stated independent certificates. ∎

<a id="theorem-f5d-finite-group-fiber-functor-reconstruction-and-response-kernel"></a>**Theorem F.5d (Finite-Group Fiber-Functor Reconstruction and Response Kernel).** Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\omega:\operatorname{Rep}(G)\to\mathrm{Hilb}_{\mathrm{fin}}$ be the forgetful symmetric tensor functor. Evaluation on every representation gives
$$
G\cong\operatorname{Aut}^{\otimes}(\omega).
\tag{F.9.5d.1}
$$
If the supplied category is the full subcategory generated by retained representations $\mathcal S$ under tensor products, conjugates, finite direct sums and subrepresentations, its reconstructed group is
$$
G/N_{\mathcal S},
\qquad N_{\mathcal S}:=\bigcap_{\rho\in\mathcal S}\ker\rho.
\tag{F.9.5d.2}
$$
Thus the retained action is faithful exactly when $N_{\mathcal S}=\{e\}$.

*Proof.* Every $g\in G$ gives the unitary monoidal natural family $(\rho(g))_\rho$. Conversely, let $T$ be such a natural family. On $\mathbb C(G)$ use the left regular action $(L_gf)(x)=f(g^{-1}x)$. Pointwise multiplication and the constant unit are intertwiners. Naturality and the tensor rule therefore make $T_{\mathbb C(G)}$ a unital algebra automorphism, which permutes the primitive idempotents $\delta_x$. The right translations $(R_hf)(x)=f(xh)$ are intertwiners, so this permutation commutes with all $R_h$. If it sends $\delta_e$ to $\delta_g$, it sends $\delta_x=R_{x^{-1}}\delta_e$ to $\delta_{gx}$; hence $T_{\mathbb C(G)}=L_g$, with $g$ unique.

For any representation $\rho$ on $H_\rho$, give the multiplicity space $H_\rho$ the trivial action and define the injective intertwiner
$$
J_\rho:H_\rho\longrightarrow\mathbb C(G)\otimes H_{\rho,\mathrm{triv}},
\qquad
(J_\rho v)(x)=\rho(x^{-1})v.
$$
Naturality with maps from the tensor unit makes $T$ the identity on every trivial multiplicity space. Thus
$$
J_\rho T_\rho=(L_g\otimes I)J_\rho=J_\rho\rho(g),
$$
and injectivity gives $T_\rho=\rho(g)$. The faithful regular representation makes evaluation injective, proving (F.9.5d.1).

Because $G$ is finite, a finite subfamily of $\mathcal S$ already has common kernel $N_{\mathcal S}$. Its direct sum is a faithful representation of $G/N_{\mathcal S}$. Its matrix coefficients and their complex conjugates separate the points of this finite quotient. The unital algebra they generate is all functions on the quotient: for each point, finite products of functions separating it from every other point construct its indicator function. Products and conjugates of matrix coefficients are coefficients of tensor products and conjugate representations. For any tensor word $\rho$ and linear functional $\ell$, the map $v\mapsto[x\mapsto\ell(\rho(x^{-1})v)]$ is an intertwiner into the left regular function representation. The coefficient-span identity therefore gives an equivariant surjection from a finite direct sum of such words onto $\mathbb C(G/N_{\mathcal S})$. An invariant orthogonal complement to its kernel splits this surjection because the representations are unitary. Thus the regular quotient representation belongs to the generated category. The map $J_\rho$ above embeds every quotient representation into a finite sum of regular representations, so closure under finite direct sums and subrepresentations includes every quotient representation. The generated category is therefore $\operatorname{Rep}(G/N_{\mathcal S})$. Applying the result just proved yields (F.9.5d.2). ∎

This exact finite reconstruction does not itself construct localized transportable endomorphisms or a continuum field net; those remain the premises of Definition F.5b and Theorem F.5c.

<a id="proposition-f5d1-fusion-data-do-not-fix-the-reconstructed-finite-group"></a>**Proposition F.5d.1 (Fusion Data Do Not Fix the Reconstructed Finite Group).** Let $D_8=\langle r,s\mid r^4=s^2=1,\ srs=r^{-1}\rangle$ and $Q_8=\{\pm1,\pm i,\pm j,\pm k\}$. For $G\in\{D_8,Q_8\}$, the simple objects of $\operatorname{Rep}(G)$ are four one-dimensional sectors $\chi_{ab}$, $(a,b)\in\mathbb Z_2^2$, and one two-dimensional sector $\rho$, with the same fusion rules
$$
\chi_{ab}\otimes\chi_{a'b'}\cong\chi_{a+a',\,b+b'},
\qquad
\chi_{ab}\otimes\rho\cong\rho,
\qquad
\rho\otimes\rho\cong\bigoplus_{a,b}\chi_{ab},
\tag{F.9.5d.3}
$$
the same dimensions, and the same conjugation, every simple object being self-conjugate. The forgetful fiber functors nevertheless reconstruct nonisomorphic groups by Theorem F.5d: $D_8$ has five elements of order two and $Q_8$ has one. The Frobenius--Schur indicator $\frac18\sum_g\chi_\rho(g^2)$ equals $+1$ for $D_8$ and $-1$ for $Q_8$. Fusion rules, statistical dimensions and conjugation therefore do not determine the reconstructed response group; Theorem F.5d reads that group from the full tensor structure through the fiber functor of Definition F.5b.

*Proof.* In both groups the commutator subgroup is the center of order two, $\{1,r^2\}$ or $\{\pm1\}$, and the quotient by it is $\mathbb Z_2^2$. Hence each group has exactly four one-dimensional characters, which form $\mathbb Z_2^2$ under pointwise multiplication. Since $8=4\cdot1^2+2^2$, there is exactly one further irreducible representation $\rho$, of dimension two: the symmetry action of $D_8$ on the square and the defining action of $Q_8$ on $\mathbb C^2$. For a one-dimensional $\chi$, $\chi\otimes\rho$ is irreducible of dimension two, hence isomorphic to $\rho$. The character $\chi_\rho$ is real, so $\langle\chi_\rho^2,\chi\rangle=\langle\chi_\rho,\bar\chi\chi_\rho\rangle=\langle\chi_\rho,\chi_\rho\rangle=1$ for each one-dimensional $\chi$; the dimension count $4=4\cdot1$ gives the last rule in (F.9.5d.3). All characters are real, so every simple object is self-conjugate. The elements of order two are $r^2,s,sr,sr^2,sr^3$ in $D_8$ and $-1$ in $Q_8$. In $D_8$, $g^2=1$ for six elements and $g^2=r^2$ for $r,r^3$, so the indicator is $\frac18(6\cdot2+2\cdot(-2))=1$; in $Q_8$, $g^2=1$ for $\pm1$ and $g^2=-1$ otherwise, so it is $\frac18(2\cdot2+6\cdot(-2))=-1$. ∎

<a id="theorem-f5e-compact-car-parity-sector-and-internal-gauge-boundaries"></a>**Theorem F.5e (Compact-CAR Parity Sector and Internal-Gauge Boundaries).**

#### 1. Concrete limiting net and vacuum

Let $K=L^2(\mathbb{R}^3,\mathbb{C}^2\otimes R_{\mathrm{SM15}})$, $h=c\,\sigma\cdot(-i\nabla)\otimes 1$, and $C=P_-(h)$. Let $F=\mathrm{CAR}(K)$, with bounded generators $a(f)$, $\lVert a(f)\rVert=\lVert f\rVert$, and vacuum quasifree state $\omega_C(a^*(f)a(g))=\langle g,Cf\rangle$ (equivalently use the opposite inner-product convention consistently). $C$ is a projection, so this is the pure filled-sea Fock representation. Concretely, on the Fock space over $(1-C)K\oplus\overline{CK}$, the represented $a(f)$ is the particle annihilator for $(1-C)f$ plus the hole creator for $\overline{Cf}$. Taking $f$ in either spectral subspace recovers every particle/hole creation and annihilation operator, whose global representation is irreducible. Its parity $\Gamma$ is implemented on particle/antiparticle Fock space and $\Gamma\Omega=\Omega$. The one-particle excitation Hamiltonian is $|h|$, hence positive; zero momentum is a null set and provides no extra normalizable zero mode.

For a ball $B$ in the $t=0$ slice, let $D(B)$ be its causal completion and define $F(D(B))=\mathrm{CAR}(L^2(B,\mathbb{C}^2\otimes R))$, represented in this vacuum; use translated Cauchy slices and Weyl evolution for other diamonds. The Weyl equation's finite propagation speed and CAR give graded locality. In particular $a(f)$ for $f\in C_c^\infty(B)$ is a genuine bounded local field. The compact internal action $G_6$ preserves supports and $C$, and intrinsic parity commutes with it. Write $E=F^{\mathrm{even}}$ and $A=F^{G_6\times\mathbb{Z}_2}=E^{G_6}$. $E$ and $A$ are ordinary local nets. These are continuum net data; they do not supply the microscopic geometric/regional maps of Definition F.0c.

All explicit algebra identities below hold already in the abstract CAR algebra and thus in this representation; von Neumann closure is unnecessary for the identities.

#### 2. Theorem: exact localized fermionic Z2 automorphism and polynomial transport

For any normalized $f\in C_c^\infty(B,\mathbb{C}^2\otimes R)$, set $U_f=a(f)+a^*(f)$. Then $U_f^*=U_f$, $U_f^2=1$, and $U_{f}$ is odd. Define $\rho_f(X)=U_fXU_{f}$ for $X\in E$.

1. $\rho_{f}$ is an automorphism of $E$, $\rho_f^2=\mathrm{id}$, and it acts identically on $E(O)$ whenever $O$ is spacelike to $D(B)$. Indeed conjugation by an odd unitary preserves evenness, and even spacelike operators commute with $U_{f}$.
2. For any other normalized compact $g$ on a Cauchy slice of another diamond (transported by Weyl evolution to the common one-particle $K$), $W_{gf}=U_gU_f$ belongs to $E$ and obeys $\rho_g=\operatorname{Ad}(W_{gf})\circ\rho_f$. $W_{hg}W_{gf}=W_{hf}$ exactly. Every open spacetime diamond contains a smaller standard diamond based on a constant-time ball; choose $g$ there, then use graded spacetime locality to obtain identity on the full causal complement of the larger diamond. Thus this charge is transportable to every diamond, with an explicit even polynomial transporter in the algebra of any larger diamond containing the two supports.
3. For spacelike disjoint supports $f,g$, $U_fU_g=-U_gU_f$. Therefore $\rho_f(W_{gf})=-W_{gf}$, and, with statistics convention $\epsilon=W_{gf}^*\rho_f(W_{gf})$, the exchange operator is $-1$ (the inverse convention has the same value). The sector has fermionic statistics, dimension one, and is its own conjugate because $\rho_f^2=\mathrm{id}$.
4. In the pure filled-sea vacuum this sector is not the vacuum sector. Let $H_\pm$ be parity eigenspaces, let $\pi_{0}$ be the restriction of $E$ to $H_+$, and identify $H_+=\operatorname{closure}(E\Omega)$; finite even particle/hole excitations prove this cyclicity. Irreducibility of the global field representation gives $F''=B(H_+\oplus H_-)$. Averaging bounded strong approximants over parity gives $E''=B(H_+)\oplus B(H_-)$. Consequently the restrictions of $E$ to $H_+$ and $H_-$ are irreducible and inequivalent: an intertwiner between them would also intertwine this weak closure, but its central projection onto $H_+$ makes that impossible. Conjugation by $U_{f}$ identifies the $\rho_f$-twisted vacuum representation on $H_+$ with the restriction on $H_-$. Hence $\rho_{f}$ is a nontrivial localized transportable sector. This argument uses the pure vacuum; a general mixed finite-cutoff thermal representation does not supply this conclusion.

The bounded approximants in item 4 can be justified directly by the bicommutant/Kaplansky density property: for parity-even $T\in B(H)$, take bounded field approximants $X_i\to T$ strongly and replace them by $(X_i+\Gamma X_i\Gamma)/2$. The resultant even approximants converge strongly to $T$. The central projections need only lie in $E''$, not in the $C^*$-algebra $E$.

This supplies exactly two displayed inequivalent simple representatives under tensor products, $\mathrm{id}$ and $\rho_{f}$, with scalar endomorphisms, $\rho_f\otimes\rho_f=\mathrm{id}$, and fermionic graded flip. Additive/direct-sum completion has further nonsimple objects; no claim of exactly two objects after that completion is made. It is NOT a classification of every sector of $E$, and it is not a construction of the complete DHR category of $A$. If a convention reserves “DHR category” for a Haag-dual net, the conclusion here is the explicit localized transportable representation/endomorphism with its computed statistics; no unproved Haag-duality premise is being smuggled in.

#### 3. Theorem: the same construction fails on the actual G6-even observables

Use the $e^{c}$ species, an $SU(3)\times SU(2)$ singlet with integer hypercharge $q=6$. Let $f,g$ be orthonormal compact smearings of that species in one ball. Then $B=a^*(f)a(g)$ is $G_6$ invariant and even, so $B\in A$. CAR give

$$
\rho_f(B)=-a(f)a(g).
$$

The right side is nonzero and has hypercharge $-12$, hence is not $G_6$ invariant. Therefore $\rho_f(A)$ is not contained in $A$. Locality and parity alone do not make this a sector of the intended observable net. Nor is $W_{gf}$ generally in $A$: its pair-annihilation and pair-creation terms have hypercharges $\mp 12$.

This is a direct failure on an actual SM15 component, not merely an absence of a reconstruction theorem. Passing from $E$ to the smaller $A$ is a substantive operation. To repair this specific route one needs localized field multiplets whose induced maps preserve $A$, and intertwiners belonging to $A$, with the appropriate charge-isometry/Cuntz relations or another explicit endomorphism construction. Merely $G_6$-transforming $a(f)$, or having a faithful internal representation, is insufficient. This does not contradict a separately specified $U(1)$ Dirac/von Neumann charge-unitary construction.

A neutral external reference cannot remove this gauge failure. An apparatus carrying compensating gauge charge can make a joint operation invariant, but then it is an operation on the larger field-plus-apparatus system and must be shown to induce the required endomorphism on A; tracing or postselecting that apparatus generally gives a channel, not an automorphism.

#### 4. Theorem: compact support forces particle and hole content

Let $0\ne f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3,\mathbb{C}^2)$, normalized, and $P_\pm(p)=(1\pm\sigma\cdot p/|p|)/2$. Then

$$
0<\nu_f=\langle f,P_-f\rangle<1.
$$

Proof. The Fourier transform $F(p)$ of a compactly supported smooth spinor is entire, hence real analytic on every real line. Suppose $P_-f=0$. For each unit vector $n$, positive $t$ obey $(\sigma\cdot n)F(tn)=F(tn)$. The equality initially holds almost everywhere, then everywhere $t>0$ by continuity. Real analyticity extends it to every real $t$. But the positive-energy hypothesis at $t<0$ gives $(\sigma\cdot n)F(tn)=-F(tn)$. Thus $F(tn)=0$ for negative $t$, and analytic continuation gives $F(tn)=0$ for all $t$. Doing this for every $n$ gives $F=0$, contradiction. The negative-energy case is identical with signs reversed. Since $P_++P_-=1$, both squared norms are strictly positive. QED.

The proof applies componentwise to the SM15 direct sum. It does not give a uniform positive lower bound over every compact smearing in a fixed ball. Oscillatory high-energy packets can have small opposite-energy leakage; the assertion concerns each fixed nonzero compact test and a fixed continuum limit.

For a common 15-component compact packet, the limiting covariance on its packet subspace is $\nu_fI_{15}$. Hence the quasifree packet-empty and packet-full probabilities are exactly

$$
p_{\mathrm{empty}}=(1-\nu_f)^{15},\qquad p_{\mathrm{full}}=\nu_f^{15},
$$

both strictly between zero and one. A finite source satisfying the corresponding fixed-test moment convergence has these limiting probabilities. Thus substituting a fixed compact f for a pure-helicity annular momentum packet preserves a well-defined heralded finite protocol, but its failure probability tends to a positive constant. The vanishing-disturbance/gentle-conditioning conclusion cannot be carried over. This is a stronger distinction than merely observing that the old packets have spatial tails.

#### 5. A localized charged field is not a deterministic localized charge preparation

Choose compact normalized $f$ in the $e^{c}$ species and consider its creation outcome $a^*(f)$. It is strictly localized and transforms with its definite internal charge; its vacuum success weight is $1-\nu_f>0$. The normalized output state is $\omega_f(X)=\omega_C(a(f)Xa^*(f))/(1-\nu_f)$.

For normalized $g$ of the same species with support spacelike separated on the $t=0$ slice, $n_g=a^*(g)a(g)$ belongs to $A$ and commutes with $a(f)$. Wick's rule and $\langle f,g\rangle=0$ give

$$
\omega_f(n_g)-\omega_C(n_g)=|\langle g,Cf\rangle|^{2}/(1-\nu_f).
$$

There exists such a compact $g$ outside any chosen bounded region containing $\operatorname{supp} f$ with nonzero numerator. Otherwise $Cf$ would vanish outside that region and would itself be compactly supported. Its Fourier transform is entire (compact support and $L^2$ suffice); it is purely negative energy, so the line-analyticity proof above forces $Cf=0$, contradicting $\nu_{f}>0$. Smooth exterior tests are dense, establishing the asserted $g$.

Thus the selected creation outcome changes some exterior observable expectation through vacuum correlations. This is not superluminal signaling: the complete local instrument with Kraus operators $a^*(f)$ and $a(f)$ is trace preserving, since $a(f)a^*(f)+a^*(f)a(f)=1$, and its outcome-forgotten channel fixes every exterior even observable. It also does not disprove DHR localization of the representation generated by a charged field. DHR asks local equivalence of representations; it does not require every chosen charged vector state to coincide with the vacuum outside a diamond. What fails is the shortcut identifying this normalized elementary outcome with the deterministic localized-vacuum state produced by a localized unitary charge implementer.

The parity Majorana unitary of Section 2 avoids postselection by coherently including particle and antiparticle pieces. It therefore supplies exact localization on E, while Section 3 proves precisely why its charge mixing is incompatible with the full internal-gauge observable algebra.

#### 6. Theorem: no gauge-invariant odd unitary in the norm-CAR SM15 field algebra

The gauge obstruction cannot be repaired merely by replacing $U_{f}$ by the odd invariant baryon polynomial and norm-unitarizing it. In fact $F=\mathrm{CAR}(L^2(\mathbb{R}^3,\mathbb{C}^2\otimes R_{\mathrm{SM15}}))$ contains **no** $G_6$-invariant odd unitary. This concerns the norm-CAR algebra, not its local von Neumann completion.

Proof. First take any nonzero finite-dimensional, $G_6$-stable one-particle subspace $V$. Its hypercharge weights belong to $\{1,-4,2,-3,6\}$, with finite multiplicities; no zero weight occurs. In its finite Fock representation $\Lambda V$, let $\Gamma_V=(-1)^N$ and let $D_V(z)$ implement a pure hypercharge group element $z=e^{i\theta}$. The parity supercharacter is

$$
\operatorname{Tr}(\Gamma_V D_V(z))=\det(1-z^Y|_V)=\prod_q (1-z^q)^{m_q}.
$$

For $\theta/2\pi$ irrational every factor is nonzero. If a gauge-invariant odd unitary $T$ existed in $\mathrm{CAR}(V)=B(\Lambda V)$, it would commute with $D_V(z)$ and anticommute with $\Gamma_{V}$. Cyclicity of the finite trace would give $\operatorname{Tr}(\Gamma_VD_V(z))=-\operatorname{Tr}(\Gamma_VD_V(z))$, contradiction. The same contradiction works for $V=0$ because its odd subspace is zero.

Now suppose $U\in F$ were a $G_6$-invariant odd unitary. Approximate $U$ in norm to error $\varepsilon<1$ by an element $X$ of $\mathrm{CAR}(V)$ for a finite $G_6$-stable $V$: every finite set of smearings has finite-dimensional gauge orbit, so such subspaces are norm dense. Average $X$ over the compact $G_6$ action and take its odd part; the result $Y$ remains in $\mathrm{CAR}(V)$, is invariant and odd, and $\lVert Y-U\rVert\le\varepsilon$. Thus $Y$ is invertible in $F$. The finite unital matrix subalgebra is inverse closed, so $Y$ is invertible in $\mathrm{CAR}(V)$. Its polar unitary $T=Y(Y^*Y)^{-1/2}$ is still invariant and odd, contradicting the finite result. QED.

The phase action is a legitimate subgroup action of the effective $G_6$ quotient; selecting an irrational phase does not require a new group or an extra physical symmetry. This proof allows odd invariant nonunitary composites, so it is consistent with $\epsilon u^c d^c d^c$. It also allows charged multiplets and proper von Neumann isometries. It excludes only this particularly simple attempt at a gauge-invariant odd norm-unitary implementer, not all localized endomorphisms of $A$.

There is also a quantitative norm separation: if a $G_6$-invariant odd unitary $U$ exists in the represented von Neumann field algebra, then $\operatorname{dist}(U,\pi(F))\ge 1$. Otherwise choose a finite matrix approximation $X$ with $\lVert U-X\rVert<1$, average and take its odd part as above, and obtain an invariant odd finite matrix $Y$ invertible as an operator. Faithfulness of its finite matrix representation makes $Y$ invertible in $\mathrm{CAR}(V)$, giving the same forbidden polar unitary. Thus even a single such weak-closure implementer cannot be norm-approximated by arbitrary CAR polynomials, including ones not initially invariant or odd.

This sharpens the narrow missing premise: an invariant odd charge implementer, if sought in the local weak closure, necessarily leaves norm CAR and needs a separate weak-topology, state-domain, and physical-instrument descent theorem. Alternatively one must construct gauge-covariant localized charge multiplets/endomorphisms directly; the polynomial Majorana shortcut cannot establish them.

The localized parity construction is on the supplied pure free-Weyl Fock/parity-even net. It is not a classification of the full internal-gauge observable DHR category or a construction of physical charge-control and Wigner realization maps.

<a id="theorem-f5f-complete-massive-dirac-parity-reconstruction-on-the-direct-source-quotient-route"></a>**Theorem F.5f (Complete Massive-Dirac Parity Reconstruction on the Direct Source-Quotient Route).**

The positive-mass source of Constructions F.10.12i.3–8 and F.10.12i.15 realizes a complete double-cone-localized finite-statistics sector category, its charged field net and faithful parity gauge action, and a positive-energy spin-one-half particle response. #### 1. Fixed source, observable and representation domains

$$
A(O)=F(O)^{\operatorname{Ad}\Gamma}|H_0.
$$

The retained source preparations, controls, measurements and finite records are the actual code-domain experiments of F.10.12i, augmented by the explicitly described charge reservoirs below. They include both resulting parity sectors and all finite matrices acting on their retained multiplicity spaces. The classification claim concerns the complete **locally normal, transportable, double-cone-localized finite-statistics DHR category of A**; cone-localized BF representations and arbitrary representations of the abstract CAR algebra lie outside it.

The observable algebra $A_{C}$ and its state are fixed first. Neither a desired gauge group nor an assumed sector census is part of its response definition. The field presentation is used to calculate these observable data and to verify completeness; the reconstructed group is computed from the resulting category in Section 4.

#### 2. The finite source and its regional limit are the same system

Here is the precise source import. At stage n the original finite box, nested fine cell projection $P_{n}$, central-difference matrix

and actual Hamiltonian $d\Gamma(D_n)$ are those of F.10.12i.3. Its finite hopping terms have their actual nearest-neighbor supports. uses the polar isometry $V_n^m$; the original choice gives a summable geometric upper bound. The same bounded-Stinespring estimate holds after adjoining every fixed finite reservoir or pointer register.

once the physical box contains the propagation tube and its buffer. These records identify the compatible-family norm quotient, region by region, with $F_{C}$ and $A_{C}$ and identify its state with $\omega_{C}$. #### 3. Observable-first local sectors and their complete census

For normalized smooth compact f in a Cauchy ball of O, put

Completeness is the substantive extra step. Property B can be verified on this complex-Dirac observable net without changing to a Majorana model. Translates of any fixed small double cone generate $A$: partition compact field labels into translated local pieces and join their even bilinears along a chain of overlapping translates, using $U_fU_g=(U_fU_h)(U_hU_g)$ for a normalized intermediate mode $h$ in an overlap. The resulting global even algebra acts irreducibly on $H_{0}$. Thus the net is weakly additive, local, translation covariant and positive-energy with invariant vacuum. Borchers (1999, Section 1.2 and Theorem 5.3.1) gives equivalence of each nonzero projection in $A(O_1)$ to its central support in $A(O_2)$ when $O_{1}$ is strictly collared inside $O_{2}$. The small-translation collar puts that support in the global center, hence it is $I$ by irreducibility. This is property B and supplies the localized finite sums/subobjects. Strict-collar split was already proved for this same complex-Dirac model by the Doplicher–Piacitelli specialization above; no additional nuclearity assumption or Majorana-to-charged-field extension is used.

Every finite-statistics object is accordingly a finite direct sum of id and $\rho_{f}$, up to unitary equivalence. It does not assign proper local isometries norm-CAR approximants: a proper isometry cannot be a norm limit of elements in a unital finite matrix system with asymptotically vanishing isometry defects. The physical source realizes the complete sector skeleton and its finite intertwiners; the normal replete category is its stated representation-theoretic completion.

#### 4. Explicit reconstructed field algebra and gauge action

Send $\mathrm{id}$ to an even line and $\rho_{f}$ to an odd line, extend by finite sums, and use the just computed exchange map. #### 6. One-particle realization and the retained multiplicity

The same Fock representation gives, with a fixed particle-hole phase convention,

$$
\begin{aligned}
U_f\Omega&=((1-C)f) \oplus \overline{Cf} \in H_1, \\

For normalized compact $f$ this is an exact normalized one-excitation vector, although it generally contains both particle and hole amplitudes. The deterministic joint preparation (F.5f.4) therefore realizes it. Smooth compact $f$ have finite energy moments. Their resulting vectors are dense in $H_{1}$ as a real vector space, and their complex span is dense; in fact any $(q,\overline{r})$ with $q\in(1-C)K$ and $r\in CK$ is obtained from $f=q+r$, with compact approximations converging in norm. In momentum space

$$
\begin{aligned}
E_p&=\sqrt{|p|^{2}+m^{2}}, \\
P_\pm(p)&=(I\pm(\alpha\cdot p+m\beta)/E_p)/2.
\end{aligned}
$$

Both projectors have rank two. Particle momenta are p and hole momenta are -p, while both energies are $E_{p}$. At rest the rotation subgroup acts as the spin-one-half representation on each rank-two space. Transport by standard boosts gives the positive-energy induced representation; thus

$$
U|H_1 \cong U_{m,1/2} \otimes \mathbb{C}^{2}.
\tag{F.5f.7}
$$

The two-dimensional factor records particle/hole copies. For $n$ future mass-$m$ momenta, their sum has invariant mass at least $nm$: in the rest frame of their sum its energy is the sum of energies, each $\ge m$. Consequently the odd Fock subspace has its one-particle shell $p^2=m^2$ isolated from the three-and-higher-particle spectrum $p^2\ge 9m^2$. The even vacuum sector has no one-particle shell. Both copies in (F.5f.7) lie in the **same** nontrivial DHR parity sector; they are not two different reconstructed gauge charges. The retained label is therefore $(m,1/2,\rho_f,\iota)$, with $\iota$ spanning the two-copy multiplicity space, and arbitrary coherent matrices on that space remain part of the response.

<a id="theorem-f5g-scalar-collapse-of-f5b-sources-on-the-f0c-f0d-norm-bridge"></a>**Theorem F.5g (Scalar Collapse of F.5b Sources on the F.0c–F.0d Norm Bridge).** Let a source satisfy the F.0c–F.0d antecedent of Definition F.5b on the literal F.1/F.2 event-tensor realization, together with hypotheses (a)–(c) of Theorem F.0y. The compact-CAR and direct-quotient constructions of Theorems F.5e–F.5f do not pass through that antecedent and are unaffected.

*Proof.* Definition F.5b requires the Mosco–Bochner bridge of Definition F.0c and Theorem F.0d before it supplies its response datum; Theorem F.5c explicitly consumes that datum. Theorem F.0d imports conditions F.0(1)–(7) of Theorem F.0, including the regional embeddings and graph cores. With hypotheses (a)–(c), Theorem F.0y applies to the source, irrespective of the later category, field-net or Wigner construction. It forces every retained event algebra to be scalar. The norm closure of their finite tensor union, and hence each regional observable algebra, is then $\mathbb C I$. Taking a representation or weak closure of this scalar algebra cannot restore a nonscalar local observable.

The conclusion holds for every source in this class, without requiring the candidates to be the same free-field model. Its cyclic vacuum representation is one dimensional and has no nontrivial particle response. Hidden charge labels or a larger noncyclic carrier invisible to all scalar observables do not meet Definition F.5b's observable-first response completeness or the particle-response identification. A complete reconstruction from the scalar response category retains only trivial gauge response and vacuum content.

The retained source of Theorem F.5e cannot be scalarized. In Theorem F.5e choose a normalized compact smooth Cauchy packet $f$ in the $e^c$ species and put
$$
p_f=a(f)^*a(f).
\tag{F.5g.1}
$$
Here $a(f)$ is the bounded full CAR field of the filled-sea construction, not a positive-frequency operator presumed to annihilate the vacuum. The species is a color and weak singlet of integer hypercharge six. Consequently $p_f$ is even and invariant under the declared global internal $G_6$ action, since its two character phases cancel. It belongs to the actual internally invariant observable net $\mathcal A=\mathcal F^{G_6\times\mathbb Z_2}$ of a diamond containing the packet.

The CAR imply $p_f^*=p_f^2=p_f$ and $p_f\ne0,I$: $a^2=0$ gives $a^*aa^*a=a^*(I-a^*a)a=a^*a$; if $p_f=0$, the $C^*$ identity gives $a=0$, and if $p_f=I$, then $aa^*=0$ again gives $a=0$, both contradicting $aa^*+a^*a=I$. Equivalently, Theorem F.5e gives $\nu_f=\omega(p_f)\in(0,1)$. The spectral states
$$
\psi_1=\nu_f^{-1/2}p_f\Omega,\qquad
\psi_0=(1-\nu_f)^{-1/2}(I-p_f)\Omega
\tag{F.5g.2}

have probabilities one and zero for the same effect $p_f$. They are the positive-probability branches of the bounded even invariant instrument $(p_f,I-p_f)$, with its result retained, and need not be one-particle states. This displays the source response that the observable identification must preserve.

A unital injective observable-net map cannot send this nontrivial projection to a scalar projection. If the comparison is instead stated through retained finite-protocol response equivalence, any scalar effect $rI$ has the same probability in both normalized states, and
$$
\max\{|r|,|1-r|\}\ge\frac12.
\tag{F.5g.3}
$$
Thus even a vanishing-error response identification cannot discard the distinction. The observable need not itself be pinned to one microscopic event: scalarity of every event factor makes the entire regional norm limit scalar. On the separate parity-even branch, the inequivalent fermionic sector of Theorem F.5e is an additional nontriviality witness; by Section 3 of that theorem its Majorana endomorphism does not preserve the smaller internal-gauge observable net.

Every completion in this class must therefore supply both a scalar local net, by its source antecedent with (a)–(c), and the nontrivial retained observable response, by its source-faithful identification. This contradiction covers every completion through the F.0c–F.0d bridge that satisfies (a)–(c); the inverse-mesh obstruction of Theorem F.5f, Section 8, concerns one regulator. The direct quotient route of Theorem F.5f is a different source class and does not enter Definition F.5b. A scalar-only category, an empty particle roster, or deletion of every distinguishing observable is not a completion of the retained data. The CAR/Fock source with its two spectral states shows that the retained-response class is nonempty, and the onsite tensor examples of Theorem F.0m and Proposition F.0s show that the analytic class of Theorem F.0y is nonempty; their common completion under (a)–(c) is empty. $\square$
