## F.10 Discrete Net-Convergence and Local KMS Closure

<a id="theorem-f101-discrete-net-convergence-under-coherent-comparison-maps"></a>**Theorem F.10.1 (Discrete Net-Convergence under Coherent Comparison Maps).** Let $M_{\mathrm{reg}}$ be the regular Lorentzian branch from Theorem 44a. For each relatively compact causal diamond $O$, let $\mathfrak A_n(O)$ be finite unital local algebras approximating it. Assume the cell unions converge in measure and causal thickness, and let $j_n^m:\mathfrak A_n(O)\to\mathfrak A_m(O)$, $m\ge n$, be UCP maps. Their multiplicativity and coherence defects tend to zero uniformly on every norm-bounded family of local elements used below, as $m\ge n\to\infty$ and $k\ge m\ge n\to\infty$, respectively. Assume also asymptotic isometry on those families. The local dynamics are compatible with these maps on bounded time windows, with boundary errors tending to zero in norm.

A bounded family $(A_n)$ is compatible when
$$
q(A):=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{m\ge n}
\|A_m-j_n^mA_n\|=0,
$$
where the displayed limit means that the nonnegative expression tends to zero. Quotient compatible families by the ideal of norm-null families. They form a $C^*$-algebra $\mathfrak A(O)$ with norm $\limsup_n\|A_n\|$. For two admissible approximations, assume cofinal UCP comparison maps in both directions preserve compatibility, are asymptotically multiplicative and isometric, and have composites asymptotic to the identity. They induce mutually inverse isometric $*$-isomorphisms, canonical relative to these comparison data.

*Proof.* Put $\mathcal P=\prod_n\mathfrak A_n(O)$ and $\mathcal I_0=\{A:\|A_n\|\to0\}$. UCP maps are contractions, so changing a bounded family by a norm-null family does not change the compatibility condition. Sums and adjoints of compatible families are compatible. For compatible bounded $A,B$, expand
$$
\begin{aligned}
A_mB_m-j_n^m(A_nB_n)
={}&(A_m-j_n^mA_n)B_m\\
&+j_n^mA_n(B_m-j_n^mB_n)\\
&+j_n^mA_n\,j_n^mB_n-j_n^m(A_nB_n).
\end{aligned}
$$
The first two terms tend uniformly to zero by compatibility and boundedness, and the last by the multiplicativity premise. Thus products are compatible; the constant unit family is compatible by unitality.

To prove closedness in $\mathcal P/\mathcal I_0$, suppose compatible classes $[A^{(r)}]$ converge to $[A]$. For every $r$,
$$
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{m\ge n}\|A_m-j_n^mA_n\|
\le 2\limsup_n\|A_n-A_n^{(r)}\|.
$$
The right side is $2\|[A]-[A^{(r)}]\|$, which tends to zero. Hence $[A]$ is compatible. The quotient norm equals $\limsup_n\|A_n\|$: deleting finitely many entries proves the upper bound, and addition of a norm-null family cannot decrease that limsup. The compatible classes are therefore a closed unital $*$-subalgebra.

Compatibility and asymptotic isometry also make $\|A_n\|$ a Cauchy sequence, so every cofinal subsequence has the same limiting norm. For the two-system comparison, the assumed compatibility preservation makes each induced map well-defined on these classes. Asymptotic multiplicativity and exact adjoint preservation make it a $*$-homomorphism; asymptotic isometry preserves the quotient norm. The two composite errors are null families, so the induced maps are mutual inverses. ∎

<a id="theorem-f102-emergent-haag-kastler-net-under-net-compatibility-hypotheses"></a>**Theorem F.10.2 (Emergent Haag--Kastler Net under Net-Compatibility Hypotheses).** Assume Theorem F.10.1 for every relatively compact causal diamond. Assume additionally:

1. comparison maps commute with the finite region inclusions, which induce injective maps $\mathfrak A(O_1)\hookrightarrow\mathfrak A(O_2)$ for $O_1\subset O_2$;
2. the algebra of each retained union is generated by the algebras of its members;
3. the evolved algebraic core of every Cauchy-surface neighborhood is dense in the algebra of its causal development;
4. each retained geometric map has a compatible microscopic action inducing a covariant $*$-homomorphism, and these assignments preserve identity maps and composition. The action of an invertible geometric map and its inverse are mutual inverses;
5. the physical meshes satisfy $a_n\to0$. On norm-dense regional cores, every pair of elements has bounded compatible representatives in a common larger regional algebra, with the norm and support-growth bounds of Corollary F.1. The same representatives satisfy its positive spacelike-margin and Lieb--Robinson inequalities for each spacelike pair of regions. All time-dependent statements use the certified evolution's time domain.

Then the quotient algebras satisfy isotony, additivity, the time-slice property, covariance for the represented maps, and Einstein locality.

*Proof.* Items 1--3 are the respective inclusion, generation and time-slice assertions. Item 4 supplies the geometric composition law and covariance, including inverse maps where applicable. For a pair of spacelike regional core elements, use the common larger regional quotient of item 5. Corollary F.1's exponential estimate gives
$$
\|[A_n,B_n]\|\longrightarrow0
$$
for their compatible representatives. Products in the quotient are represented componentwise, so
$$
\|[[A_n],[B_n]]\|
=\limsup_n\|[A_n,B_n]\|=0.
$$
Thus the core elements commute; norm continuity of the commutator extends the equality to their regional completions. This proof uses the quotient norm and does not require isometric embeddings of each finite algebra into that quotient. The stated properties follow on these supplied net and geometric branches. ∎

<a id="theorem-f103-conditional-local-rindler-kms-limit"></a>**Theorem F.10.3 (Conditional Local Rindler KMS Limit).** Let $p\in M_{\mathrm{reg}}$, let $\kappa(p)>0$ be the certified proper acceleration, and let $W_\ell(p)$ be a local Rindler wedge. Assume a strongly continuous limiting boost automorphism group $\sigma_t$, with $t$ measured in the observer's proper time. Supply an independent geometric/state normalization certificate identifying the thermal imaginary proper-time period as
$$
\tau_U=\frac{2\pi c}{\kappa(p)}.
$$
For a norm-dense $\sigma$-invariant analytic $*$-algebra, assume:

1. compatible representatives $A_n,B_n$ converge in norm to $A,B$; the states $\omega_{n,\ell}$ converge to $\widehat\omega_{W_\ell}$ on that algebra, and the real-time boost automorphisms converge there in norm uniformly on compact time intervals;
2. the finite states are KMS for the finite boost groups with the same imaginary-time period $\tau_U$. Their bounded strip functions satisfy
$$
F_n(t)=\omega_{n,\ell}(A_n\sigma_t^{(n,\ell)}(B_n)),
\qquad
F_n(t+i\tau_U)=\omega_{n,\ell}(\sigma_t^{(n,\ell)}(B_n)A_n);
$$
3. these functions are analytic for $0<\operatorname{Im}z<\tau_U$, continuous on the closed strip, bounded there by $\|A_n\|\|B_n\|$, and converge uniformly on every compact subset of the closed strip;
4. any vacuum-normalized contribution of $K_{\mathrm{PCE}}^{(n,\ell)}$ retained in the limiting boost generator is central.

Then $\widehat\omega_{W_\ell}$ is KMS for $\sigma_t$ with imaginary proper-time period $\tau_U$. The inverse energy-temperature parameter and temperature are
$$
\beta_{\mathrm{energy}}
=\frac{\tau_U}{\hbar}
=\frac{2\pi c}{\hbar\kappa(p)}
=\frac1{k_BT_U},
\qquad
T_U=\frac{\hbar\kappa(p)}{2\pi c k_B}.
$$
In natural units the corresponding parameter is $\beta_U=2\pi/\kappa(p)$.

*Proof.* Compact uniform convergence gives a holomorphic limit $F$ in the open strip and a continuous extension to its boundary. The global finite-KMS bound gives $|F(z)|\le\|A\|\|B\|$. State convergence and real-time norm convergence identify the two boundary values as
$$
F(t)=\widehat\omega_{W_\ell}(A\sigma_t(B)),
\qquad
F(t+i\tau_U)=\widehat\omega_{W_\ell}(\sigma_t(B)A).
$$
Thus the bounded-strip KMS condition holds on the dense analytic algebra. Bilinearity and the strip norm bound extend it by norm approximation to the completed wedge algebra. A central additive generator contribution cancels from conjugation; it does not establish the KMS boundary relation. Finally the dimensionless boost period is $\kappa\tau_U/c=2\pi$, and $\tau_U=\hbar\beta_{\mathrm{energy}}$, giving the displayed units and coefficient. The independent period/state certificate supplies this normalization; convergence alone does not select it. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104-finite-regulator-entanglement-first-law-and-conditional-horizon-flux"></a>**Theorem F.10.4 (Finite-Regulator Entanglement First Law and Conditional Horizon Flux).** Let $\sigma$ be a faithful density matrix on a finite-dimensional cutoff algebra, set $K_\sigma=-\log\sigma$, and let $\rho(\epsilon)$ be a trace-norm differentiable family of density matrices with $\rho(0)=\sigma$. Then
$$
\left.\frac d{d\epsilon}S_{vN}(\rho(\epsilon))\right|_0=\left.\frac d{d\epsilon}\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\epsilon)K_\sigma)\right|_0,
$$
because $D(\rho\|\sigma)=\Delta\langle K_\sigma\rangle-\Delta S_{vN}$ has vanishing first derivative at $\rho=\sigma$. If a separate wedge certificate identifies
$$
K_\sigma=\beta_UH_{\mathrm{boost}}+cI,\qquad\delta Q=\delta\langle H_{\mathrm{boost}}\rangle,\qquad\beta_U=(k_BT_U)^{-1},
$$
then
$$
\delta Q=k_BT_U\,\delta S_{vN}=T_U\,\delta S_{\mathrm{th}},
\qquad
S_{\mathrm{th}}:=k_BS_{vN}.
$$
For type-III local algebras the finite entropy is replaced by the Araki relative-entropy/modular formulation. ∎

<a id="corollary-f1041-conditional-wedge-aqft-kms-input-for-t1-and-t2"></a>**Corollary F.10.4.1 (Conditional Wedge-AQFT KMS Input for T1 and T2).** On a branch satisfying Theorem F.10.2 and all state-convergence, analytic-strip, modular/boost-identification, and normalization hypotheses of Theorem F.10.3, the wedge restriction of the limiting state is KMS for the local boost flow at the Unruh temperature. This supplies the wedge-KMS and temperature components of inputs (T1) and (T2) of §12. Their first-law, flux, and area-entropy components require the separate certificates stated there. A Lieb–Robinson bound supplies locality but does not supply this thermodynamic certificate. ∎

### F.10.4a Predictive Spectral Triple

<a id="definition-f104a1-finite-predictive-spectral-triple"></a>**Definition F.10.4a.1 (Finite Predictive Spectral Triple).** Let $\mathcal G=(V,E)$ be a connected finite undirected MPU carrier graph with $|V|\ge2$ on a regular finite-resolution branch. Assign each edge $e=\{v,w\}$ a positive propagation-cost length $\ell_e>0$. Define
$$
\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{PU}}=C(V),
\qquad
\mathcal H_{\mathrm{PU}}=\bigoplus_{e=\{v,w\}\in E}\mathbb C^2,
$$
with representation
$$
\pi_e(f)=
\begin{pmatrix}
f(v)&0\\
0&f(w)
\end{pmatrix}
$$
on the summand indexed by $e=\{v,w\}$. Define
$$
D_{\mathrm{pred},e}
=
\frac{1}{\ell_e}
\begin{pmatrix}
0&1\\
1&0
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
D_{\mathrm{pred}}
=
\bigoplus_{e\in E}D_{\mathrm{pred},e}.
\tag{F.10.4a.1}
$$
The finite predictive spectral triple is
$$
(\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{PU}},\mathcal H_{\mathrm{PU}},D_{\mathrm{pred}}).
$$

<a id="theorem-f104a2-connes-distance-equals-propagation-cost-distance"></a>**Theorem F.10.4a.2 (Connes Distance Equals Propagation-Cost Distance).** For $x,y\in V$, define
$$
d_{D_{\mathrm{pred}}}(x,y)
=
\sup
\left\{
|f(x)-f(y)|:
f\in C(V),\,
\lVert[D_{\mathrm{pred}},\pi(f)]\rVert\le1
\right\}.
\tag{F.10.4a.2}
$$
Then
$$
d_{D_{\mathrm{pred}}}(x,y)
=
d_{\mathcal G,\ell}(x,y),
\tag{F.10.4a.3}
$$
where $d_{\mathcal G,\ell}$ is the shortest-path distance with edge lengths $\ell_e$.

*Proof.* On one edge $e=\{v,w\}$,
$$
[D_{\mathrm{pred},e},\pi_e(f)]
=
\frac{f(w)-f(v)}{\ell_e}
\begin{pmatrix}
0&1\\
-1&0
\end{pmatrix}.
$$
The matrix on the right has operator norm $1$, hence
$$
\lVert[D_{\mathrm{pred}},\pi(f)]\rVert
=
\max_{e=\{v,w\}}
\frac{|f(v)-f(w)|}{\ell_e}.
\tag{F.10.4a.4}
$$
Thus the condition $\lVert[D_{\mathrm{pred}},\pi(f)]\rVert\le1$ is exactly the condition that $f$ is $1$-Lipschitz on every edge.

If $f$ is edgewise $1$-Lipschitz and $\gamma:x=v_0\to v_1\to\cdots\to v_m=y$ is any path, then
$$
|f(x)-f(y)|
\le
\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}|f(v_{r+1})-f(v_r)|
\le
\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}\ell_{\{v_r,v_{r+1}\}}.
$$
Taking the infimum over paths gives
$$
|f(x)-f(y)|\le d_{\mathcal G,\ell}(x,y),
$$
so $d_{D_{\mathrm{pred}}}(x,y)\le d_{\mathcal G,\ell}(x,y)$.

For the reverse inequality, fix $y$ and define
$$
f_z=d_{\mathcal G,\ell}(z,y).
$$
The triangle inequality gives
$$
|f_v-f_w|\le\ell_{\{v,w\}}
$$
for every edge $\{v,w\}$, so $\lVert[D_{\mathrm{pred}},\pi(f)]\rVert\le1$. Therefore
$$
d_{D_{\mathrm{pred}}}(x,y)
\ge
|f_x-f_y|
=
d_{\mathcal G,\ell}(x,y).
$$
The two inequalities prove (F.10.4a.3). ∎

<a id="corollary-f104a3-metric-and-gauge-covariant-edge-extension"></a>**Corollary F.10.4a.3 (Metric and Gauge-Covariant Edge Extension).** On the finite branch, the propagation-cost metric is recovered from $D_{\mathrm{pred}}$. For a chosen family of edge transporters $U_{vw}\in U(n)$ with $U_{wv}=U_{vw}^*$, define
$$
D_{U,e}
=
\frac{1}{\ell_e}
\begin{pmatrix}
0&U_{vw}\\
U_{vw}^*&0
\end{pmatrix}.
$$
A vertex gauge transformation $u\in C(V,U(n))$ acts by
$$
U_{vw}\longmapsto u(v)U_{vw}u(w)^*.
$$
Conjugating the untwisted operator by $u$ gives the pure-gauge special case $U_{vw}=u(v)u(w)^*$.

*Proof.* The metric statement is Theorem F.10.4a.2. Direct block-matrix multiplication gives the displayed transformation law. Products of the $U_{vw}$ around cycles may have nontrivial holonomy, whereas the pure-gauge products telescope to the identity. ∎

<a id="definition-f104a4-finite-chiral-regulator-data"></a>**Definition F.10.4a.4 (Finite Chiral Regulator Data).** On a regular finite spectral-triple branch carrying chiral fermions, let $\Gamma_5=\Gamma_5^*=\Gamma_5^{-1}$ be the finite chirality operator on the active spinor module, and set the finite MPU regulator spacing to
$$
a_{\mathrm{PU}}=\delta=\sqrt{8\ln2}\,L_P.
\tag{F.10.4a.4.1}
$$
A naive finite chiral regulator is a local finite Dirac operator $D$ satisfying:

1. $\Gamma_5D+D\Gamma_5=0$;

2. $D^*=\Gamma_5D\Gamma_5$;

3. on the regular translation-covariant subbranch its symbol has the single continuum Dirac zero required by the target chiral continuum limit;

4. no additional doubler zero represents an independent low-energy species.

A Ginsparg-Wilson regulator representative is a finite operator of the form
$$
D_{\mathrm{GW}}
=
\frac{1}{a_{\mathrm{PU}}}(1-V),
\tag{F.10.4a.4.2}
$$
where $V$ is unitary and
$$
\Gamma_5V\Gamma_5=V^*.
\tag{F.10.4a.4.3}
$$

<a id="theorem-f104a41-ginsparg-wilson-chirality-gate"></a>**Theorem F.10.4a.4.1 (Ginsparg-Wilson Chirality Gate).** On the regular finite-regulator branch:

1. the naive regulator conditions are jointly infeasible on the branch carrying the complete Nielsen--Ninomiya no-go hypotheses: an infinite periodic lattice or its uniformly local thermodynamic family, a continuous periodic momentum symbol on the full compact Brillouin torus with the smoothness required for its index argument, the stipulated Hermiticity and chiral symmetry, isolated regular continuum zeros with the target nonzero net chirality, and the theorem's finite-band and locality requirements. A finite matrix sampled at finitely many momenta alone is not this branch;

2. every $D_{\mathrm{GW}}$ of (F.10.4a.4.2) satisfies the finite chiral relation
$$
\Gamma_5D_{\mathrm{GW}}+D_{\mathrm{GW}}\Gamma_5
=
a_{\mathrm{PU}}D_{\mathrm{GW}}\Gamma_5D_{\mathrm{GW}};
\tag{F.10.4a.5.1}
$$

3. the finite action
$$
S_F(\bar\psi,\psi)=\bar\psi D_{\mathrm{GW}}\psi
$$
is invariant under the exact modified chiral transformation
$$
\delta\psi=i\theta\,\widehat\Gamma_5\psi,
\qquad
\delta\bar\psi=i\theta\,\bar\psi\Gamma_5,
\qquad
\widehat\Gamma_5:=\Gamma_5(1-a_{\mathrm{PU}}D_{\mathrm{GW}});
\tag{F.10.4a.5.2}
$$

4. the finite chiral index is
$$
\operatorname{ind}_{\mathrm{PU}}(D_{\mathrm{GW}})
=
\operatorname{Tr}\left(\Gamma_5\left(1-\frac{a_{\mathrm{PU}}}{2}D_{\mathrm{GW}}\right)\right)
=
n_+(0)-n_-(0)\in\mathbb Z,
\tag{F.10.4a.5.3}
$$
where $n_\pm(0)$ are the dimensions of the zero-mode subspaces with $\Gamma_5$-chirality $\pm1$;

5. on an anomaly-free gauge-descended branch, the total anomaly class represented by the finite chiral index characters, including the permitted counterterm and inflow data, vanishes on gauge redundancies. If that total class is nonzero for a declared gauge redundancy, the branch fails predictive anomaly descent in the sense of Theorem X.8d and Theorem X.9.5b.

The Ginsparg--Wilson construction therefore supplies an exact finite chiral identity and integer index under the stated algebraic hypotheses. Its use as a local chiral regulator requires separate locality, spectrum and anomaly-descent certificates. Agreement with the continuum chiral index data of Appendices R and Y additionally requires a specified limiting elliptic operator, compatible bundles and boundary conditions, and an index-matching theorem controlling the regulator limit; the finite trace formula alone does not establish that agreement.

*Proof.* Item 1 invokes Nielsen and Ninomiya [1981, *Absence of neutrinos on a lattice: I. Proof by homotopy theory*] only on the complete periodic-symbol branch specified there. Its topological zero-counting obstruction excludes a nonzero unmatched chirality when all of those locality, Hermiticity, regularity and periodicity hypotheses hold. The full Brillouin symbol and its zero data belong to this independent source-application certificate; finite matrix size or a list of sampled momenta does not establish them. A regulator on that branch must relax at least one premise of the no-go theorem. The following finite-dimensional identities apply to any unitary $V$ with $\Gamma_5V\Gamma_5=V^*$ and do not, by themselves, prove locality, absence of doublers, or a continuum limit.

For item 2, use (F.10.4a.4.2) and (F.10.4a.4.3). Since $V$ is unitary and $\Gamma_5V\Gamma_5=V^*$,
$$
V\Gamma_5V=\Gamma_5.
\tag{F.10.4a.5.4}
$$
Therefore
$$
\Gamma_5D_{\mathrm{GW}}+D_{\mathrm{GW}}\Gamma_5
=
\frac{1}{a_{\mathrm{PU}}}
(2\Gamma_5-\Gamma_5V-V\Gamma_5),
$$
while
$$
a_{\mathrm{PU}}D_{\mathrm{GW}}\Gamma_5D_{\mathrm{GW}}
=
\frac{1}{a_{\mathrm{PU}}}
(1-V)\Gamma_5(1-V)
=
\frac{1}{a_{\mathrm{PU}}}
(\Gamma_5-\Gamma_5V-V\Gamma_5+V\Gamma_5V).
$$
Substituting (F.10.4a.5.4) gives (F.10.4a.5.1).

For item 3,
$$
\delta S_F
=
i\theta\,\bar\psi(\Gamma_5D_{\mathrm{GW}}+D_{\mathrm{GW}}\widehat\Gamma_5)\psi.
$$
Using $\widehat\Gamma_5=\Gamma_5(1-a_{\mathrm{PU}}D_{\mathrm{GW}})$,
$$
\Gamma_5D_{\mathrm{GW}}+D_{\mathrm{GW}}\widehat\Gamma_5
=
\Gamma_5D_{\mathrm{GW}}+D_{\mathrm{GW}}\Gamma_5-a_{\mathrm{PU}}D_{\mathrm{GW}}\Gamma_5D_{\mathrm{GW}}
=
0
$$
by (F.10.4a.5.1). Hence $\delta S_F=0$.

For item 4, (F.10.4a.4.3) gives
$$
\widehat\Gamma_5^*
=
(\Gamma_5V)^*
=
V^*\Gamma_5
=
\Gamma_5V
=
\widehat\Gamma_5,
$$
and
$$
\widehat\Gamma_5^2
=
\Gamma_5V\Gamma_5V
=
V^*V
=
1.
$$
Thus $\widehat\Gamma_5$ is a finite self-adjoint involution. Since
$$
\Gamma_5\left(1-\frac{a_{\mathrm{PU}}}{2}D_{\mathrm{GW}}\right)
=
\frac12\Gamma_5(1+V),
$$
decompose the finite spinor space into eigenspaces of the unitary $V$. The relation $\Gamma_5V\Gamma_5=V^*$ maps the eigenspace $E_\lambda$ to $E_{\overline\lambda}$.

If $\lambda\notin\{1,-1\}$, then $E_\lambda$ and $E_{\overline\lambda}$ are distinct orthogonal spaces. Relative to their direct sum, $\Gamma_5(1+V)/2$ has only off-diagonal blocks, so its trace is zero. On $E_{-1}$ the factor $1+V$ vanishes. On $E_1=\ker D_{\mathrm{GW}}$, $\Gamma_5$ preserves the eigenspace and
$$
\frac12\Gamma_5(1+V)=\Gamma_5.
$$
Therefore
$$
\operatorname{Tr}\left(\Gamma_5\left(1-\frac{a_{\mathrm{PU}}}{2}D_{\mathrm{GW}}\right)\right)
=
\operatorname{Tr}_{E_1}\Gamma_5
=
n_+(0)-n_-(0)\in\mathbb Z.
$$

For item 5, distinguish the finite axial measure factor from the full gauge-anomaly certificate. For independent Grassmann variables $\psi,\bar\psi$ with the conventional Berezin measure, integrate the displayed axial transformation as
$$
\psi'=e^{i\theta\widehat\Gamma_5}\psi,
\qquad
\bar\psi'=\bar\psi e^{i\theta\Gamma_5}.
$$
The top-degree Grassmann coefficient transforms by the determinant, so the integration measure transforms by its inverse. At a specified regulator background its Jacobian is therefore
$$
J_{\mathrm{axial}}(\theta)
=\det(e^{i\theta\widehat\Gamma_5})^{-1}
 \det(e^{i\theta\Gamma_5})^{-1}
=\exp\!\left[-i\theta\operatorname{Tr}(\widehat\Gamma_5+\Gamma_5)\right]
=\exp\!\left[-2i\theta\,\operatorname{ind}_{\mathrm{PU}}D_{\mathrm{GW}}\right].
$$
Independent fermion blocks multiply these factors. This axial identity does not, by itself, determine a gauge-anomaly class. The branch must separately specify the gauge action, fermion representations and measure, and certify how their full gauge variation, permitted counterterms and inflow define the total anomaly class. Its vanishing is the gauge-descent condition of item 5; a nonzero total class obstructs the declared redundancy under Theorems X.8d and X.9.5b.

Identification with the continuum Atiyah--Singer or Atiyah--Patodi--Singer index data of Appendices R and Y additionally requires an index-matching certificate for the limiting elliptic operator, its bundles and domain, and any boundary spectral correction. That certificate must establish the relation to the finite Ginsparg--Wilson index; neither the finite trace formula nor anomaly descent alone establishes it. ∎

<a id="definition-f104a42-operational-paley-wiener-sector"></a>**Definition F.10.4a.4.2 (Operational Paley--Wiener Sector).** Equip $C(V)$ with the counting-measure inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{v\in V}f(v)\overline{g(v)}$, linear in its first argument. Let $L_{\mathrm{PU}}\ge0$ be the self-adjoint graph operator associated with the quadratic form
$$
\mathcal E_{\mathrm{PU}}(f)
=\frac12\sum_{\{v,w\}\in E}
\frac{|f(v)-f(w)|^2}{\ell_{\{v,w\}}^2}.
\tag{F.10.4a.6.1}
$$
For $\Omega\ge0$, define
$$
PW_\Omega(L_{\mathrm{PU}})
=\operatorname{Ran}\mathbf1_{[0,\Omega]}(L_{\mathrm{PU}}).
\tag{F.10.4a.6.2}
$$
Let $\mathcal C=\{C_i\}_{i=1}^N$ be a finite cover of $V$ by nonempty subsets. Then $\|1_{C_i}\|=\sqrt{|C_i|}>0$, and the normalized cell vectors and linear sampling map are
$$
\phi_i=\frac{1_{C_i}}{\|1_{C_i}\|},
\qquad
\mathcal A_\Omega f=(\langle f,\phi_i\rangle)_{i=1}^N.
\tag{F.10.4a.6.3}
$$

<a id="theorem-f104a43-paley-wiener-frame-reconstruction-of-observable-fields"></a>**Theorem F.10.4a.4.3 (Paley-Wiener Frame Reconstruction of Observable Fields).** If the sampling map
$$
\mathcal A_\Omega:PW_\Omega(L_{\mathrm{PU}})\to\mathbb C^N
$$
is injective, then the cell averages form a stable finite frame on $PW_\Omega(L_{\mathrm{PU}})$: there are constants $0<A_\Omega\le B_\Omega<\infty$ such that
$$
A_\Omega\lVert f\rVert^2
\le
\sum_{i=1}^N|\langle f,\phi_i\rangle|^2
\le
B_\Omega\lVert f\rVert^2
\qquad
(f\in PW_\Omega(L_{\mathrm{PU}})).
\tag{F.10.4a.7.1}
$$
Moreover, with frame operator
$$
S_\Omega f
=
\sum_{i=1}^N
\langle f,\phi_i\rangle
P_\Omega\phi_i,
\qquad
P_\Omega=\mathbf 1_{[0,\Omega]}(L_{\mathrm{PU}}),
\tag{F.10.4a.7.2}
$$
every $f\in PW_\Omega(L_{\mathrm{PU}})$ is reconstructed by
$$
f
=
\sum_{i=1}^N
\langle f,\phi_i\rangle
S_\Omega^{-1}P_\Omega\phi_i.
\tag{F.10.4a.7.3}
$$
On a regular continuum-limit branch, the same reconstruction conclusion holds only for sampling covers carrying a continuum frame certificate: for the limiting spectral subspace $PW_\Omega$, the cell-average map must satisfy
$$
A_{\Omega,\mathrm{cont}}\|f\|^2
\le
\sum_i|\langle f,\phi_i\rangle|^2
\le
B_{\Omega,\mathrm{cont}}\|f\|^2
$$
with $A_{\Omega,\mathrm{cont}}>0$, and the finite sampling maps must converge to these functionals with error smaller than $\sqrt{A_{\Omega,\mathrm{cont}}}$. Under this certificate, the finite lower frame bounds remain positive and the retained fields are stably reconstructed from the cell data.

*Proof.* The space $PW_\Omega(L_{\mathrm{PU}})$ is finite-dimensional. The upper bound in (F.10.4a.7.1) follows because $\mathcal A_\Omega$ is a linear map between finite-dimensional normed spaces. If the lower bound failed, there would be a sequence $f_n\in PW_\Omega$ with $\lVert f_n\rVert=1$ and $\mathcal A_\Omega f_n\to0$. Compactness of the unit sphere in $PW_\Omega$ gives a convergent subsequence $f_{n_k}\to f$ with $\lVert f\rVert=1$. Continuity gives $\mathcal A_\Omega f=0$, contradicting injectivity. Hence $A_\Omega>0$.

The frame operator $S_\Omega=\mathcal A_\Omega^*\mathcal A_\Omega$ is positive. The lower frame bound makes it invertible on $PW_\Omega$. Applying $S_\Omega^{-1}$ to
$$
S_\Omega f
=
\sum_i\langle f,\phi_i\rangle P_\Omega\phi_i
$$
gives (F.10.4a.7.3).

For the regular continuum branch, let $\mathcal A_{\Omega,\mathrm{cont}}$ be the certified continuum sampling map and let $\mathcal A_{\Omega,h}$ be a transported finite sampling map on the retained spectral subspace. The continuum lower frame bound gives
$$
\|\mathcal A_{\Omega,\mathrm{cont}}f\|_2
\ge
\sqrt{A_{\Omega,\mathrm{cont}}}\,\|f\|.
$$
If the certified sampling-map error is $\varepsilon_h<\sqrt{A_{\Omega,\mathrm{cont}}}$, the reverse triangle inequality gives
$$
\|\mathcal A_{\Omega,h}f\|_2
\ge
\left(\sqrt{A_{\Omega,\mathrm{cont}}}-\varepsilon_h\right)\|f\|,
$$
so the finite lower frame bound is at least
$$
\left(\sqrt{A_{\Omega,\mathrm{cont}}}-\varepsilon_h\right)^2>0.
$$
The same frame-operator argument therefore gives stable reconstruction on the certified continuum branch. On its separately certified lattice/bandlimit, dispersion, regulator, and matching branch, Theorem K.10.4 permits the corresponding effective-cutoff interpretation; it supplies neither that branch nor the sampling certificate from spacing alone. ∎

<a id="proposition-f104a410-conditional-d4-graph-real-line-history-and-continuum-frame"></a>**Proposition F.10.4a.4.10 (Conditional D4 Graph, Real-Line History and Continuum Frame).**

This is the existing mathematical graph/history/frame component on declared geometric graph data. References to a ROUND 99 physical scalar source remain conditional imports. No native propagation-cost or common fermionic, chiral, index/anomaly net admission is inferred.

##### 1. Literal owner requirements and fixed units

Definition F.10.4a.4.2 uses the counting norm and the form

$$
E(f) = (1/2) \sum_{\text{unordered edges } \{v,w\}} |f(v)-f(w)|^{2} / \ell_e^{2}.
$$

The graph samples are exactly $\sum_{v\in C} f(v)/\sqrt{|C|}$. Theorem F.10.4a.4.3 requires injectivity at finite resolution and, for the continuum statement, a positive continuum frame bound and a transported **linear** analysis error below its square-root margin. The catalogue row also requires the regulator, carrier/net, index/anomaly and sampling records to have a common physical-net realization. The actual source definitions and maps are Constructions F.10.4a.8p.10/11/13 and Theorem F.10.4a.8p.12.

Choose a reference length $l_0=1$ metre, time $t_0=1$ second and fixed speed $c=l_0/t_0$. In formulas below $x$ has length units, $t$ and the source internal variable $s$ have seconds, and $y=(x,ct)$. The analysis measure is $dx\,dt$, not $dx\,d(ct)$. The spatial carrier is $X=(\mathbb{R}/l_0\mathbb{Z})^3$, of volume $V_X=l_0^3$. Numerical checks use $l_0=t_0=c=1$, without changing these definitions.

For integers $n\ge 4$ put

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho_n &= l_0\, 2^{-n}, & T_n &= t_0\, 2^{n}, \\
M_n&=l_0/\rho_n, & N_n&=c\, T_n/\rho_n.
\end{aligned}
$$

Both $M_{n}$ and $N_{n}$ are even. Let $\Gamma_n=l_0\mathbb{Z}^3\times cT_{n}\mathbb{Z}$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}
V_n &= \rho_n D_4 / \Gamma_n, \\
D_4&=\Bigl\{z \in \mathbb{Z}^{4} : \sum z_i \text{ even}\Bigr\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Join each vertex to its 24 nearest roots $\rho_{n}v$, $v=\pm e_i\pm e_j$, $i<j$. Take the undirected edge once, with the explicitly declared geometric length $\ell=\sqrt{2}\rho_n$. The graph is finite and connected, with

$$
\begin{aligned}
|V_n|&=M_n^{3} N_n/2, \\
\mu_n &= 2 \rho_n^{4}/c, \\
\mu_n |V_n| &= V_X T_n.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
$$

Here $\mu_{n}$ is the dx dt volume of one D4 Voronoi cell. Formula (1) is the exact counting/volume conversion. Calling ell a native propagation-cost record would require the separate admission certificate; declaring it mathematically is not that certificate.

##### 2. The original operator, not a normalized replacement

Since the edge sum is unordered, polarization of the original form gives

$$
(L_n f)(v) = (1/(4 \rho_n^{2})) \sum_{r \in R_{24}}[f(v)-f(v+\rho_n r)].
\tag{2}
$$

The factor 1/4 is essential. A coefficient 1/6 would instead produce a normalized comparison Laplacian and would not be the same original operator with these edge lengths.

Characters are represented by $k=(2\pi m_1/l_0,2\pi m_2/l_0,2\pi m_3/l_0,2\pi m_4/(cT_n))$, modulo $(2\pi/\rho_n)D_4^*$. The normalized character has values $\exp(ik\cdot y)/\sqrt{|V_n|}$. Its eigenvalue is

$$
\lambda_n(k) = \Bigl[6-\sum_{i<j} \cos(\rho_n k_i)\cos(\rho_n k_j)\Bigr]/\rho_n^{2}.
\tag{3}
$$

The exact root identities are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_r (k \cdot r)^{2}&=12|k|^{2}, \\
\sum_r (k \cdot r)^{4}&=12|k|^{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The cosine remainder therefore gives

$$
0 \le (3/2)|k|^{2}-\lambda_n(k) \le \rho_n^{2} |k|^{4}/8.
\tag{4}
$$

No rescaling of physical time is performed to remove 3/2.

For $\lambda_n(k)<\rho_n^{-2}$, the sum of the six cosine products is $>5$, so every product is positive. All four cosines have the same nonzero sign. A reciprocal translate by $(\pi/\rho_n)(1,1,1,1)$, when necessary, makes them positive; subsequent coordinate reciprocal translates give $|\rho_nk_i|<\pi/2$. For $a,b$ in $[0,1]$, $1-ab\ge((1-a)+(1-b))/2$. Consequently

$$
\lambda_n(k) \ge (3/\pi^{2})|k|^{2}.
\tag{5}
$$

We select the original graph cutoff $\Lambda=l_0^{-2}$. This is a graph eigenvalue cutoff, not an angular frequency. Because any nonzero spatial $k_{i}$ has magnitude at least $2\pi/l_0$, (5) would give $\lambda_n\ge 12/l_0^2>\Lambda$. Thus the **entire** selected graph band is spatially constant. It is not an arbitrarily discarded part of a larger band.

Write $\nu_m=2\pi m/T_n$, and define

$$
\begin{aligned}
b_n &= (c/\rho_n) \arccos(1-\Lambda \rho_n^{2}/3), \\
K_n &= \lfloor b_n T_n/(2\pi)\rfloor.
\end{aligned}
$$

For an effective implementation, determine $K_{n}$ as the largest integer satisfying (6)$\le\Lambda$ by exact cyclotomic algebraic comparison; the displayed floor is the closed-form value. Threshold equality is included and is not delegated to an undecidable arbitrary-real comparison. Then $\mathrm{PW}_\Lambda(L_n)$ is exactly the span of $-K_n\le m\le K_n$, with

$$
\lambda_n(m) = 3[1-\cos(\rho_n \nu_m/c)]/\rho_n^{2}.
\tag{6}
$$

The limiting frequency is $B=c\sqrt{2\Lambda/3}$. Throughout $n\ge 4$, all frequency bins below lie in the fixed larger band $[-B_*,B_*]$, $B_*=2/t_0$. The limiting differential operator on the declared temporal sector is $-(3/(2c^2))\,\partial_t^2$; the full comparison operator would be $(3/2)(-\Delta_x-c^{-2}\partial_t^2)$.

##### 3. An isometric real-line source map

Expand a graph field as

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(v)&=|V_n|^{-1/2} \sum_{m=-K_n}^{K_n} a_m \exp(i \nu_m t_v), \\
\lVert f\rVert_{\mathrm{count}}^{2}&=\sum_m |a_m|^{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Define $\delta_n=2\pi/T_n$ and disjoint half-open bins

$$
I_{n,m}=[\nu_m-\delta_n/2,\nu_m+\delta_n/2).
$$

The unitary temporal Fourier convention is $(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int\exp(-i\nu t)F(t)\,dt$. Define $U_{n}$ by

$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{(U_n f)}(x,\nu)&=V_X^{-1/2} \delta_n^{-1/2} \\
&\qquad \sum_m a_m 1_{I_{n,m}}(\nu).
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
$$

This is an exact isometry from the whole finite graph band into `L2(X x R,dx dt)`. Its histories are genuinely nonperiodic L2 functions, including the graph zero mode. In real time,

$$
\begin{aligned}
U_n f(x,t)&= w_n(t) P_n f(x,t), \\
P_n f&= (V_X T_n)^{-1/2} \sum_m a_m \exp(i \nu_m t), \\
w_n(t)&=\operatorname{sinc}(\pi t/T_n),\quad \operatorname{sinc}(z)=\sin(z)/z.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
$$

$P_{n}$ alone is periodic and is not relabeled as an L2 real-line field. The sinc envelope is retained in every map below. Real graph fields give real histories because the bins and coefficients are conjugation symmetric. Complex fields use two separately budgeted real preparations.

Let $L_{\inf}=-(3/(2c^2))\partial_t^2$ on this spatially constant sector. Since the graph multiplier is $\lambda_n(m)$ while the source frequency $\nu$ runs through its bin, (4) gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert L_\infty U_n-U_n L_n\rVert \\
&\le \rho_n^{2} B_*^{4}/(8c^{4}) + 3 B_* \delta_n/(2c^{2}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
$$

This is an operator-norm estimate on the entire changing finite graph band. It tends to zero. Let $R_n(\tau)$ multiply $a_{m}$ by $\exp(-i\nu_m\tau)$, and let $T_\tau F(t)=F(t-\tau)$. Then

$$
\lVert T_\tau U_n-U_n R_n(\tau)\rVert \le |\tau|\, \delta_n/2.
\tag{10}
$$

Tau is the SAME physical number of seconds on both sides. For $\tau=r\rho_n/c$, $R_n$ is the literal D4 graph translation by $r\rho_n(e_1+e_4)$, restricted to the spatially constant sector (with the inverse sign for the stated pullback convention). A bare $\rho_ne_4$ is not a D4 translation and is not used. The accompanying spatial increment has no effect on this entire selected sector. For other $\tau$ it is its specified low-band functional calculus, not an assertion that finite source dynamics is an autonomous group.

##### 5. Spectral-band convergence and comparisons

Extend $U_{n}$ by zero off the graph band and let $Q_n=U_nU_n^*$. In temporal Fourier space $Q_{n}$ averages over the bins in (7) and discards the exterior. Their union is the interval

$$
[- (K_n+1/2)\delta_n,\ (K_n+1/2)\delta_n).
$$

Its endpoints tend to +/-B. Conditional averaging on shrinking intervals converges strongly to the identity locally in L2. The endpoint sliver has measure tending to zero. Hence

$$
Q_n \to P_B \text{ strongly},
\tag{13}
$$

where $P_{B}$ is the actual real-line spectral projector for $L_{\inf}$ at $\Lambda$. For every $F$ in the limiting band, $f_n=U_n^*F$ satisfies $U_nf_n\to F$ in $L^2$ and $\lVert f_n\rVert\to\lVert F\rVert$. Inverse Gaussian preparation converges in $L^2$ and uniformly, because all supports lie in the same fixed band and its multiplier is bounded. This provides actual state/preparation compatibility on the retained R99 scalar quotient, not just matching mode labels. It is not a claim of trace-norm convergence of the entire growing hardware states.

There is deliberately NO operator-norm claim $Q_n\to P_B$ on the entire infinite-dimensional limiting band; each $Q_{n}$ has finite rank. Nor is a finite cover a global frame for that whole space. Operator-norm estimates (9), (10) and the cover/instrument estimates below hold on the entire corresponding finite graph sector. On each fixed finite-dimensional limiting core, (13) is uniform; diagonal choices give arbitrary specified errors there. The infinite continuum frame itself is proved directly in Section 7. These are the distinct legitimate convergence statements.

##### 6. Exact real-time output transport and its uniform tail

Choose representatives $t_{v}$ in $[-T_n/2,T_n/2)$. Lift every graph vertex to actual real-time events $t_v+jT_n$, $j$ in $\mathbb{Z}$, at the same spatial coordinates. The exact source map gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sqrt{\mu_n}\, F(x_v,t_v+jT_n) \\
&= w_n(t_v+jT_n)\, f(v).
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
$$

Thus the correct counting-volume factor is $\sqrt{\mu_n}$, but there is also the explicitly retained envelope. Define the output transport $D_{n}$ from graph data by the right side of (14). For every $x$ in $[-1/2,1/2]$,

$$
\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} \operatorname{sinc}^{2}(\pi(x+j))=1.
\tag{15}
$$

At integer $x$ this is immediate by continuity. Otherwise it follows from $\sum_j(x+j)^{-2}=\pi^2\csc^2(\pi x)$, equivalently Parseval for the Fourier series of a unit-modulus exponential on a unit interval. Therefore

$$
\lVert D_n f\rVert_{\ell^{2}(V_n\times\mathbb{Z})}=\lVert f\rVert_{\mathrm{count}}.
\tag{16}
$$

This is an explicit counting-isometric analysis transport, not an unnamed unitary chosen after seeing a Gram matrix. All its entries have a direct same-clock physical-history meaning by (14). It is not asserted to be a local homomorphism of a quantum field net. Similarly $U_{n}$ is a Hilbert-space coefficient/source-preparation map, not an unproved multiplicative identification of the graph algebra $C(V_n)$ with the retained scalar $C(K)$ algebra.

Retain only $|j|\le J$. Since $|x+j|\ge|j|-1/2$ and $|\sin|\le 1$, comparison with an integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert(D_n-D_{n,J})f\rVert &\le \tau_J \lVert f\rVert, \\
\tau_J^{2}&=2/[\pi^{2}(J-1/2)],\quad J\ge 1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
$$

Here $D_{n,J}$ is extended by zero on omitted outputs. In particular

$$

<a id="lemma-f104a8p1-full-transit-chain-schur-complement"></a>**Lemma F.10.4a.8p.1 (Full-Transit Chain Schur Complement).**

##### 3. Exact all-transit Schur complement

Put $t=1/(2h^2)$, exactly the original unordered-edge convention. Partition the FULL original counting operator by central vertices $B$ and all noncentral vertices $I$:

$$
L=\begin{bmatrix} C & B^{*} \\ B & A \end{bmatrix}.
$$

$A$ is the direct sum of path-interior Dirichlet blocks $t\,\operatorname{tridiag}(2,-1,-1)$ and leaf blocks $t$. A path of $m$ edges has first Dirichlet eigenvalue $4t\sin^2(\pi/(2m))\ge 4t/m^2$. Hence

$$
A\ge g I,\quad g=\min(t,4t/R^{2}).
$$

For $0\le\lambda<g$, eliminating interior coordinates is legitimate and exact:

$$
S(\lambda)=C-\lambda I-B^{*}(A-\lambda I)^{-1}B.
$$

Let $Hb=(b,-A^{-1}Bb)$ be harmonic extension, $W=H^*H$, and $L_{\mathrm{eff}}=S(0)$. Then

$$
S(\lambda)=L_{\mathrm{eff}}-\lambda W-\lambda^{2} B^{*}(A-\lambda I)^{-1}A^{-2}B,
\tag{1}
$$

$$
0\le\text{last term}\le\lambda^{2}/(g-\lambda)\,(W-I).
\tag{2}
$$

These formulas are consequences of the resolvent identity; no discarded transit mass is hidden. Each path gives series conductance $t/m_z$. Therefore at reciprocal momentum $k$,

$$
\mu_{\mathrm{eff}}(k)=(1/(2h^{2}))\sum_z [1-\cos(h\, k\cdot z)]/m_z.
\tag{3}
$$

The harmonic mass WITHOUT the P leaves is exactly

$$
w_0(k)=M_0-\sum_z (m_z^{2}-1)/(6m_z)\, [1-\cos(h\, k\cdot z)],
\tag{4}
$$

and WITH those leaves it is $w(k)=w_0(k)+P$. Equation(4) follows by summing the squared linear interpolation along every path, using

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}|(1-j/m)a+(j/m)b|^{2} \\
&= (m-1)(|a|^{2}+|b|^{2})/2 - (m^{2}-1)|a-b|^{2}/(6m).
\end{aligned}
$$

In particular $P\le w(k)\le 2M_0$. Translation symmetry diagonalizes the boundary Schur matrix into scalar functions. It is strictly decreasing below $g$ because its derivative is negative definite. For each $k$ it therefore has at most one zero below $g$, with exact eigenvector supplied by $(A-\lambda)^{-1}$. No eigenvector below $g$ can have all central values zero. Thus this is exhaustive low-spectrum analysis.

If a low eigenvalue exists, set $x=\mu_{\mathrm{eff}}(k)/w(k)$. From (1)-(2),

$$
x/(1+x/g)\le\lambda\le x,\quad 0\le x-\lambda\le x^{2}/g.
\tag{5}
$$

Existence for every bounded-$x$ mode follows for sufficiently large $g$: $S(0)\ge 0$ and $S(x)\le 0$, with the zero mode treated exactly. Internal Dirichlet resonances are outside this window because $g\to\infty$.

<a id="theorem-f104a8p2-three-dimensional-native-counting-band-frame-and-cost-metric"></a>**Theorem F.10.4a.8p.2 (Three-Dimensional Native Counting Band, Frame and Cost Metric).**

For $|m|^2\ge 2$, with $k=2\pi m$, the lower bound is $.99\cdot(2\pi^2/3)-.1>4$. For $|m|^2\le 1$, the upper bound is $1.01\cdot\pi^2/3+.1<4$. The corresponding roots exist below $g$. Thus the ENTIRE original $\mathrm{PW}_4$ consists of exactly the seven characters

##### Literal fixed-cell sampling

Use $q=4$ spatial cells per coordinate. Every cell contains $(N/4)^3$ complete clusters, and its finite vector is its literal normalized indicator of all actual graph vertices. The regular spatial metric is also proved, rather than inherited from the old fixed stencil. A subdivided direction $z$ costs $m_zh\ge h|z|$. Therefore base-to-base graph distance is at least the flat torus Euclidean distance. Pendant excursions cannot shorten it.

The exact finite edge spectral triple recovers its graph distance by the accepted F.10.4a.2 template. No finite fixed-stencil Euclidean identity is being asserted.

<a id="lemma-f104a8p4-retained-marked-regulator-inverse-estimate"></a>**Lemma F.10.4a.8p.4 (Retained Marked-Regulator Inverse Estimate).**

The shared continuum object need not be asserted from matching names. Here is an explicit restricted comparison. On a temporal circle $T$ with antiperiodic time and the same spatial spin twist, let $p_0=2\pi(n_0+1/2)/T$. Select the WHOLE spinor momentum ball $|p|\le P$, with spatial momenta automatically contained in $K_L$ when $L\ge P$. Let $D_E(p)=i\gamma\cdot p$, and take exactly the marked overlap symbol $D_{a}$ of Construction F.10.4a.8p.3, with a lattice supporting these momenta without aliasing. This is a spinor sector, not a substitution for the original scalar PW space.

For $aP\le 1$, write $u_\mu=1-\cos(ap_\mu)$, $W=\sum u_\mu$, $b=1-W$, $r^2=1+2\sum_{\mu<\nu}u_\mu u_\nu$. Elementary trigonometric bounds give

$$
\begin{aligned}
&0\le r-1\le a^{4} |p|^{4}/8, \\
&|\sin(ap)-ap|\le a^{3} |p|^{3}/6, \\
&0<r^{-1}\le 1.
\end{aligned}
$$

The scalar real part of $D_{a}$ has norm $\le a|p|^2/2+a^3|p|^4/8$. Its imaginary Clifford part differs from $i\gamma\cdot p$ by at most $a^2|p|^3/6+a^4|p|^5/8$. Consequently

$$
\lVert D_a(p)-D_E(p)\rVert \le (11/12)\, a P^{2} \le a P^{2}.
$$

The spatial spin gap gives $|p|\ge\pi$ independently of $T$. If $aP^2\le\pi/2$, Neumann inversion yields

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert D_a(p)^{-1}-D_E(p)^{-1}\rVert &\le 2aP^{2}/\pi^{2}, \\
\lVert D_a(p)^{-1}\rVert &\le 2/\pi.
\end{aligned}
$$

These are operator bounds on the ENTIRE selected finite spinor sector, not modewise point convergence with an uncontrolled number of modes. The GW identity and finite index zero remain exact at each a. This proves an explicit low-energy regulator/covariance comparison to the very Euclidean Dirac operator reconstructed from the finite/full CAR family above. At fixed T, its finite Dirac kernel is thermal. The temporal image estimate of Construction F.10.4a.8p.3 controls T to infinity on fixed time-separation windows; the spatial projection commutes with that kernel and cannot increase its operator error.

The two stated estimates use different topologies: the overlap inverse estimate is a retained Fourier-sector bound; the temporal image estimate is a separated-time kernel bound. One may apply both to declared test classes, but cannot claim that their sum proves full time-point convergence of the untruncated overlap kernel. In particular this does not prove finite-overlap reflection positivity, determine its heavy spectral measure, or extend a hard temporal cutoff to a local real-time algebra. It supplies a precise downstream active-regulator square on retained spinors, while the upstream native carrier/event/clock square remains open.

<a id="theorem-f104a8p5-cell-local-car-refinement-and-complete-compatible-family-net"></a>**Theorem F.10.4a.8p.5 (Cell-Local CAR Refinement and Complete Compatible-Family Net).**

##### Fixed local embeddings and refinement

Let $a=1/N$ with even $N$ and use cubic spatial cells of side $a$ on the unit torus. Use the same antiperiodic $x_1$ spin structure as Construction F.10.4a.8p.3. $K_{a}$ is the four-spinor lattice one-particle space with counting norm. Let $J_{a}$ send the basis at each cell to its normalized constant spinor section, $a^{-3/2}$ times its indicator. Thus $J_{a}$ is an isometry into continuum $K=L^2(T^3,\mathbb{C}^4)$. The spin seam is a measure-zero boundary and is handled by the fixed spin trivialization and twisted finite differences, not by changing the CAR inner product.

The induced CAR map $j_{a}$ is a unital isometric *-embedding. The algebra generated by cells inside $O$ maps into the full continuum equal-time field algebra of $O$. Disjoint cell algebras graded-commute exactly. For dyadic refinement, each normalized coarse cell is $1/\sqrt{8}$ times the sum of its eight fine subcells. This defines exact nested one-particle and CAR embeddings and makes $j_{a/2}i_a=j_a$. Unlike the Fourier-cutoff construction, a small cell region does NOT generate the entire finite CAR algebra.

##### Local Hamiltonian and explicit retained-sector clock comparison

Let $\alpha_{j}$ be the spatial Clifford matrices of Construction F.10.4a.8p.3 and choose $\beta=\gamma_0$, so $\beta$ anticommutes with each $\alpha_{j}$. On the twisted lattice define the nearest-neighbor spatial Wilson Hamiltonian by its symbol

$$
h_a(p)=\sum_j \alpha_j \sin(ap_j)/a + \beta \sum_j(1-\cos(ap_j))/a.
$$

It is Hermitian. Its particle-hole Fock Hamiltonian is positive, using its own positive/negative spectral projectors. This is a physical real-time spatial regulator, not the four-dimensional marked overlap matrix. The two need not be equal, but their common comparison is a separate declared theorem.

Allowed momenta in one Brillouin representative set have $p_1=2\pi(n_1+1/2)$, $p_2,p_3=2\pi n$. Its energy magnitude is

$$
E_a(p)=\sqrt{\sum \sin(ap_j)^{2} + \Bigl(\sum(1-\cos(ap_j))\Bigr)^{2}}\,/a.
$$

It has no zero on the spin-twisted momentum grid: vanishing would force all cosines$=1$, excluded by $p_1$. No extra zero branch is discarded. All $4N^3$ modes are retained.

Let $e_{p}$ be a continuum normalized plane spinor, and $s_a(p)$ its normalized cell-center sampled lattice vector, with norm 1. Distinct retained momenta are orthogonal. Put $T_ae_p=s_a(p)$. For the WHOLE physical momentum ball $|p|\le P$ contained in the Brillouin set, direct cell integration gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\langle e_p,J_a T_a e_q\rangle &= \delta_{pq} \prod_j \operatorname{sinc}(ap_j/2), \\
\lVert(J_a T_a-I)|_{|p|\le P}\rVert &\le aP/\sqrt{12}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Indeed the squared norm is diagonal with entries $2(1-\prod\operatorname{sinc}(ap_j/2))$; for $aP\le 1$, the factors are positive and $1-\operatorname{sinc}x\le x^2/6$. This bound is uniform over the entire finite band, not a sum growing with its dimension.

On the same band, the Clifford symbol estimate is

$$
\lVert h_a(p)-h(p)\rVert \le a|p|^{2}/2+a^{2}|p|^{3}/6 \le (2/3)aP^{2}.
$$

Duhamel for the finite $4\times 4$ matrices and the preceding isometric transport give, uniformly for $|t|\le T$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert J_a \exp(-it h_a) T_a u-\exp(-it h)u\rVert \\
&\le \bigl[aP/\sqrt{12}+(2/3)T aP^{2}\bigr] \lVert u\rVert.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the physical time variable is the SAME $t$, not a diffusive rescaling. For a general smooth local $u$, project onto $|p|\le P$ and add the two high-frequency norm tails, yielding at most

$$
aP/\sqrt{12}+(2/3)T aP^{2}+2P^{-s} \bigl\lVert\, |h|^{s} u\bigr\rVert
$$

for $\lVert u\rVert\le 1$, provided the lattice input is chosen as $T_{a}$ of its spectral truncation. This last input is not exactly cell-local. For exact cell-local input use $J_a^*u$; its difference from $T_au_{\mathrm{low}}$ is bounded by the same cell transport defect plus the high-frequency tail, so the total propagation defect is at most

$$
2aP/\sqrt{12}+(2/3)T aP^{2}+2P^{-s} \bigl\lVert\, |h|^{s} u\bigr\rVert.
$$

The lattice input $J_a^*u$ occupies only cells meeting $\operatorname{supp}(u)$, hence lies in the $\sqrt{3}a$ neighborhood of that support. This is an actual local-input comparison through the fixed cell embedding, with an explicitly vanishing geometric thickening. Taking, for example, $P=a^{-1/4}$ gives convergence on every fixed smooth family and bounded time window. CAR generator norms and polynomial telescoping transfer the bound to retained local observable polynomials. Finite lattice dynamics have tails outside the continuum cone; no exact finite light cone is claimed. Full continuum finite propagation and the comparison yield asymptotic causality on these controlled families.

##### Vacuum comparison

Write $P_-(p)=(I-h(p)/|p|)/2$ and $P_{a,-}(p)=(I-h_a(p)/E_a(p))/2$. For $|p|\le P$ and $aP\le 1$, normalization of nonzero Hermitian Clifford vectors gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert P_{a,-}(p)-P_-(p)\rVert &\le \lVert h_a(p)-h(p)\rVert/|p| \\
&\le (2/3)a|p| \le (2/3)aP.
\end{aligned}
$$

The inequality follows from $|E_a-|p||\le\lVert h_a-h\rVert$ and the decomposition $h_a/E_a-h/|p|=(h_a-h)/|p|+h_a(1/E_a-1/|p|)$. Hence the two terms each cost at most $\lVert h_a-h\rVert/|p|$ before division by 2. This proof does not assume a commuting cutoff polarization.

The finite vacuum covariance is $P_{a,-}$. Through $J_{a}$, it approaches the full vacuum covariance on retained test families, by this symbol bound plus the explicit cell transport and tail estimates. Higher quasifree correlations are determinants of their covariance matrices, so fixed-degree correlation errors follow by finite multilinear expansion. The finite vacuum is NOT the exact restriction of the full vacuum; only its quantified convergence is asserted.

This supplies the F.10.1-style norm-completion mechanism for the explicit Cauchy-cell carrier. It does not assert all geometric hypotheses of Theorem 44a or F.10.2 for the native source.

Fix a relatively compact spatial region $O$ with boundary of volume zero. Use dyadic cubic cells whose closures lie in $O$; their nested unions $O_{n}$ increase to $O$ up to a null set. Let $K_n(O)$ be their spinor step-function spaces and $A_n(O)=\mathrm{CAR}(K_n(O))$. The dyadic refinement maps $i_{n}^{m}$ are exact unital isometric *-homomorphisms, hence UCP. Multiplicativity, coherence and norm defects are identically zero on ALL bounded elements, not only generators. The physical embeddings $j_{n}$ obey $j_mi_n^m=j_n$.

For a bounded family $A_{n}$,

$$
\lVert A_m-i_n^m A_n\rVert=\lVert j_m A_m-j_n A_n\rVert.
$$

It is therefore compatible in F.10.1's sense if and only if $j_nA_n$ is a norm-Cauchy family in $\mathrm{CAR}(K)$. Its limit lies in the closure of the union of the local cell algebras. Step spinors in these cells are dense in $L^2(O,\mathbb{C}^4)$, so the CAR norm identity and polynomial density identify that closure with the full continuum equal-time CAR algebra $\mathrm{CAR}(L^2(O,\mathbb{C}^4))$. Conversely every element of that algebra admits a norm-convergent sequence from the nested finite algebras, hence a compatible family. Norm-null families are exactly the kernel, and the quotient norm is the norm of the limit. The even observable subalgebras obey the same conclusion. Region inclusions commute exactly with the maps.

The free dynamics comparison also extends to EVERY bounded compatible family, not merely a named fixed polynomial. Suppose $j_nA_n\to A$. Approximate $A$ in norm by a polynomial $B$ in smooth local test spinors. Its cell-average representatives $B_{n}$ satisfy $j_nB_n\to B$, and the one-particle clock estimate above plus polynomial telescoping gives

$$
\sup_{|t|\le T}\lVert j_n \alpha_n(t)(B_n)-\alpha(t)(B)\rVert\to 0.
$$

Automorphisms and $j_{n}$ are isometric. Therefore replacing $B_{n}$ by $A_{n}$ and $B$ by $A$ costs at most $\lVert j_nA_n-j_nB_n\rVert+\lVert A-B\rVert$, uniformly in $t$. Let $n\to\infty$ and then $\lVert A-B\rVert\to 0$. This proves the bounded-compatible-family physical-time comparison on every fixed bounded window.

Finite lattice evolution need not remain exactly in a finite enlarged region because it has tails. If a continuum evolved smooth core lies inside an enlarged Cauchy region O' with positive margin, multiply its lattice test representatives by the indicator of O'_n. The norm of the removed one-particle tail tends to zero by the propagation comparison above and the margin. Polynomial telescoping gives a norm-vanishing boundary error. For general compatible bounded families extend by the same density/isometry argument. If an explicit finite regional UCP map is desired, the trace-preserving conditional expectation onto the finite cell subalgebra is contractive and doubles at most the distance to that subalgebra, so the same boundary error tends to zero. No exact finite cone is inferred.

This establishes the quotient algebra and the dynamics extension required for this particular Cauchy comparison. It also identifies precisely where a genuine native region/clock map must enter: the finite $A_n(O)$, $\alpha_n$ and $i_{n}^{m}$ must be the actual admitted native active CAR systems, not an independent mathematical attachment. The construction does not assume that Euclidean OS history functionals are multiplied by these maps; OS reconstruction remains its separate graded/linear correlation comparison.

<a id="theorem-f104a8p6-exact-native-controlled-local-car-port-and-single-port-cone"></a>**Theorem F.10.4a.8p.6 (Exact Native-Controlled Local CAR Port and Single-Port Cone).**

##### 9. Stronger region-supported finite-duration port and exact scalar response

The port below is supported in an arbitrarily small but nonzero region O, with a quantitative support statement.

Choose a normalized real smooth bump $\phi$ compactly supported in a spin-trivializing spatial ball $O$, and a constant unit spinor $u$. Put $f=\phi u$. Integration by parts gives $\langle f,h_Df\rangle=0$. Set $s=\lVert h_Df\rVert>0$ and $g=ih_Df/s$. Then $f,g$ are orthonormal, smooth, and supported in $O$. In the vacuum covariance $P_-$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\langle f,P_- g\rangle=-i \langle f,|h_D|f\rangle/(2s), \\
&\eta=\langle f,|h_D|f\rangle/s,\quad 0<\pi/s\le\eta\le 1.
\end{aligned}
$$

The bounded even observable $B=\psi(f)^*\psi(g)+\psi(g)^*\psi(f)$ has norm 1 and spectrum contained in $\{-1,0,1\}$. Its initial mean is 0. Conjugating by $\exp(i\theta N_f)$ rotates its cross-covariance, yielding mean $\eta\sin(\theta)$ in the final convention $g=+ih_Df/s$ and negative Hamiltonian phase of Theorem F.10.4a.8p.7. Therefore $\theta=\arcsin(z)$, $z\in[-1,1]$, yields an exactly linear normalized response $z$. No equation-of-motion quotient of off-shell linear smears is being declared injective: this is a different, explicitly bilinear controlled-source response.

Let Q be the rank-two projector onto span{f,g}. The operator $h_{D}$ Q is bounded because both modes are in the domain. Define

$$
W_0=-h_D Q-Q h_D+Q h_D Q.
$$

It is finite rank, self-adjoint, supported in $O\times O$ as an integral kernel, and $(h_D+W_0)Q=Q(h_D+W_0)=0$. Write $K_0$ for its CAR bilinear with the vacuum scalar subtracted. The Hamiltonian $H_{\mathrm{free}}$ is the positive-energy particle/antiparticle normal-ordered representation of $h_{D}$, NOT naive second quantization of the unbounded-below $h_{D}$ on an empty particle Fock space. In this representation, the bounded perturbation $K_0$ implements exactly the one-particle perturbation $W_0$ by the CAR commutator identity. Thus $H_{\mathrm{free}}+K_0$ commutes with every field mode in $Q$. The rest of the unbounded field remains active.

With $A=(\lVert h_Df\rVert^2+\lVert h_Dg\rVert^2)^{1/2}$, $\operatorname{rank}(W_0)\le 4$ and $\lVert W_0\rVert\le 3A$. The normal-ordered bilinear satisfies the conservative bound $\lVert K_0\rVert\le 2\lVert W_0\rVert_1\le 24A$. For duration $d>0$ the actual controlled Hamiltonian

$$
H_{\mathrm{free}}+K_0 - S(-1)^{M} (\arcsin z/d)\, N_f
$$

therefore realizes the required phase while its $H_{\mathrm{free}}+K_0$ evolution commutes with $B$ and $N_{f}$. Its possible action on the vacuum elsewhere does not affect the $B$ expectation. The fluctuation/excitation cost is not set to zero; it is bounded by the owned perturbation work ledger.

For readout, $P_\pm=(B^2\pm B)/2$ and $P_0=I-B^2$ are local even polynomials. A degenerate three-level pointer and controlled cyclic shifts for these three projectors supply an exact finite-duration readout of $B$. A Hermitian logarithm of the pointer shift has norm $\le\pi$, so readout pulse norm $\le\pi/d_r$. Retaining $K_0$ during readout ensures its background evolution commutes with the measured algebra. Preparing and later retaining the pointer, switches, classical $S,M$ controls, timings and outcome registers are physical source resources. The total turn-on/off mean-work allocation is bounded by

$$
4\lVert K_0\rVert+2|\arcsin z|/d+2\pi/d_r,
$$

with separate finite ready/maintenance/controller prices. This is a bounded driven-port construction, not a finite autonomous battery theorem or a universal cost law.

On $S=0$ no phase is applied and B retains mean0. On $S=1$ the sign is the actual protected native forecast, with success probability $s_{\mathrm{native}}>1/2$ on Native14. Consequently the unconditional correlation record has

$$
\mathbb{E}[S(-1)^{M} B]/(s_{\mathrm{native}}\, \eta)=z,
$$

with the final negative Hamiltonian phase convention of Theorem F.10.4a.8p.7. All failure records remain. Unknown outcomes are not conditioned away; $s_{\mathrm{native}}$ and $\eta$ are source quantities with independently computable bounds. Finite shots, finite-angle synthesis and readout errors must be amplified by $1/(s_{\mathrm{native}}\eta)$ in the precision ledger.

Use the actual full Wilson Hamiltonian $h_{a}$ of Theorem F.10.4a.8p.5 and its own negative-energy vacuum covariance $P_{a,-}$. Choose a real lattice bump $\phi_{a}$ supported in a proper cell patch, away from the spin seam, and a constant unit spinor $u$ with $\langle u,\beta u\rangle=0$. Such $u$ exists, for example $(1,0,1,0)/\sqrt{2}$ for $\beta=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,-1,-1)$. Let $f_a=\phi_au$ normalized. Each central-difference expectation vanishes because $\phi_{a}$ is real and that derivative is imaginary antisymmetric. The Wilson contribution vanishes because $\langle u,\beta u\rangle=0$. Therefore $\langle f_a,h_af_a\rangle=0$ EXACTLY, not just in the continuum limit.

Set $s_a=\lVert h_af_a\rVert>0$ and $g_a=ih_af_a/s_a$. They are orthonormal. The support of $g_{a}$ is contained in the original patch plus one lattice-neighbor layer. This is a genuine local cell mode, not a global Fourier mode. Let $Q_{a}$ project onto their span and put

$$
W_a=-h_a Q_a-Q_a h_a+Q_a h_a Q_a.
$$

Then $W_{a}$ is self-adjoint, rank at most 4, and $(h_a+W_a)Q_a=0$. Its support grows at most two neighbor layers beyond the original patch. Define $K_a={:}\psi_a^*W_a\psi_a{:}$ relative to the actual finite vacuum, $N_a=\psi_a(f_a)^*\psi_a(f_a)$, and $B_a=\psi_a(f_a)^*\psi_a(g_a)+\text{adjoint}$. Their algebra is a literal subalgebra of the same finite cell-CAR carrier used for the Wilson dynamics and local embeddings.

Since $h_{a}$ has no zero, $P_{a,-}=(I-h_a/|h_a|)/2$, and

$$
\langle f_a,P_{a,-} g_a\rangle=-i \langle f_a,|h_a| f_a\rangle/(2s_a).
$$

Write $\eta_a=\langle f_a,|h_a|f_a\rangle/s_a$, so $0<\eta_a\le 1$. The initial mean of $B_{a}$ is 0. The actual positive particle-hole Hamiltonian $H_{a}$ plus its bounded normal-ordered $K_{a}$ commutes with all $Q_{a}$ field generators. During duration $d$, the additional native-classical controlled term

$$
-S(-1)^{M} \arcsin(z)\, N_a/d
$$

therefore produces $\mathbb{E}[B_a|S,M]=S(-1)^M\eta_az$, with the final negative Hamiltonian phase convention of Theorem F.10.4a.8p.7. With the unchanged Native14 success probability $s_{N}$,

$$
\mathbb{E}[S(-1)^{M} B_a]/(s_N \eta_a)=z.
$$

Failures remain included. This is an EXPECTATION identity, not a deterministic pointer outcome. Each trial starts from the declared finite quasifree vacuum; no reset resource is assumed free. A finite qutrit pointer can measure the exact spectral projectors of $B_{a}$ because the two modes are EXACTLY orthonormal. The bounded three-level pointer readout above consequently applies to $B_{a}$ with exact spectral projectors.

For a fixed smooth continuum bump $\phi$ and the compatible spinor, normalized cell averages give $f_a\to f$. First- and SECOND-order consistency are needed. Componentwise centered differences commute with cell averaging. Taylor integral remainders give consistency $O(a\lVert f\rVert_{H^2}+a^2\lVert f\rVert_{H^3})$ for $h_{a}$, and $O(a\lVert f\rVert_{H^3}+a^2\lVert f\rVert_{H^4})$ for $h_{a}^{2}$ relative to $h^{2}$; equivalently $h_{a}^{2}$ is the scalar discrete sum-of-sine-squares plus Wilson-mass-square symbol, whose difference from $|p|^2$ is $O(a^2|p|^4)$ on smooth fixed data. The weaker displayed $O(a)$ bound is sufficient. The same estimates apply to the cell averages and their normalization. Thus $J_ah_af_a\to hf$ AND $J_ah_a^2f_a\to h^2f$. Consequently $s_a\to s>0$, $J_ag_a\to g$ and $J_ah_ag_a\to hg$.

Expand $W_{a}$ as the finitely many rank-one terms involving $f_a,g_a,h_af_a,h_ag_a$. Each converges in trace norm, since $\lVert|x_a\rangle\langle y_a|-|x\rangle\langle y|\rVert_1\le\lVert x_a-x\rVert\lVert y_a\rVert+\lVert x\rVert\lVert y_a-y\rVert$. Therefore $J_aW_aJ_a^*\to W$ in trace norm, not merely strongly. The corresponding bounded CAR bilinears converge in norm by the trace-norm estimate. Normal-ordering scalars also converge: pair each of these finitely many convergent vectors with the strongly convergent embedded vacuum covariance of Theorem F.10.4a.8p.5, using its uniform norm bound 1. For $\eta_{a}$, $\langle f_a,|h_a|f_a\rangle$ convergence follows from the spectral measure convergence plus uniform integrability: $\lVert h_af_a\rVert$ remains bounded, so the energy first-moment tail above $L$ is at most $\lVert h_af_a\rVert^2/L$. Thus $\eta_a\to\eta$. This supplies the unbounded-energy step rather than inferring it solely from bounded polarization convergence. Bounded perturbation Duhamel, together with the free comparison on the finitely many smooth port modes, yields the fixed-window controlled comparison. This statement is for fixed smooth ports; shrinking supports need an explicit uniform derivative/rate schedule.

Scope: a further analytical component, not an assertion of exact finite microscopic causality or a completed native source. It applies to one fixed spatial port region per trial and its time-dependent quadratic controls.

Let $h$ be the full continuum Dirac Hamiltonian with exact speed-one propagation. Let $O$ be a bounded spatial region of diameter $r$. Let $W(t)$ be bounded self-adjoint one-particle perturbations whose integral kernels are supported in $O\times O$, locally integrable in operator norm. The compensation $W_0$ and the phase control of the port construction above satisfy this for their declared region. Write $U_W(t,0)$ for the perturbed propagator, $t\ge 0$.

For initial Cauchy data $u$ supported in $A$, set $d=\operatorname{dist}(A,O)$. Duhamel gives

$$
u_W(t)=U_0(t)u-i \int_0^t U_0(t-s)\, W(s)u_W(s)\, ds.
$$

The restriction of $u_W(s)$ to $O$ is zero for $s<d$. To prove this, restrict the equation to $O$ on $[0,d)$, where the free term vanishes; the resulting homogeneous Volterra equation has only the zero solution by its norm estimate and Gronwall. Hence the integral starts at $s=d$. Its source is supported in $O$, and free propagation shows

$$
\operatorname{supp} u_W(t) \subset N_t(A) \cup N_{t-d}(O),
$$

where the second set is empty for $t<d$. Every point of $N_{t-d}(O)$ is within $t+r$ of $A$: choose near-minimizers for $\operatorname{dist}(A,O)$ and $\operatorname{dist}(x,O)$, and connect their two points inside $O$ by the ambient distance at most $\operatorname{diam}(O)$. Therefore

$$
\operatorname{supp} U_W(t,0)u \subset N_{t+r}(A).
$$

The bound is independent of ||W|| and counts the region diameter only ONCE, even if the trajectory undergoes repeated interactions with the same port. The CAR anticommutator between the evolved generator and a test supported at distance greater than t+r is exactly zero. Even observable products inherit the corresponding causal separation statement. Backward evolution uses the same reasoning.

Thus $r_n\to 0$ gives an exact zero limiting cone defect for these single-port propagators. It does NOT show convergence of the propagators, make finite $r$ propagation exactly causal, or bound all protocols with many active disjoint ports. Nor does it implement the classical control broadcast or pointer readout at zero cost. A collection of ports can create a sequence of shortcuts; its cumulative geometry/time requires a separate bound. This lemma should not be exported as a universal source light-cone theorem.

<a id="theorem-f104a8p7-whole-band-physical-preparation-dense-syntax-and-retained-sampling"></a>**Theorem F.10.4a.8p.7 (Whole-Band Physical Preparation, Dense Syntax and Retained Sampling).**

This is essential to the common preparation diagram. The finite example $z=f(v)$ remains an exact response identity but, for normalized low modes, its pulses vanish like the inverse square root of the vertex count. It is NOT the final continuum-matched preparation rule.

Let $V_R=2M_0N^3$ be the ACTUAL number of graph vertices and let $T_{R}$ map the whole original seven-mode $\mathrm{PW}_4$ isometrically to the corresponding continuum Fourier span, using the exact normalized graph eigenvectors with positive central phase. Write $F=T_Rf$, $\lVert f\rVert_{\mathrm{count}}\le 1$. Each continuum basis character has absolute value 1, so $\lVert F\rVert_\infty\le\sqrt{7}$.

##### A pointwise bound for the FULL graph eigenvectors

For a chain of $m\le R$ links, $t=1/(2h^2)$, let $A$ be its interior Dirichlet block. Direct solution of $Ab=1$ gives $b_j=j(m-j)/(2t)$, so $\lVert A^{-1}\rVert_\infty\le m^2h^2/4$. For $\lambda\le 4$ and the stated $h,R$, $\lambda\lVert A^{-1}\rVert_\infty<1/2$. Thus

$$
\lVert(A-\lambda)^{-1}\rVert_{\infty}\le m^{2}h^{2}/2.
$$

The harmonic extension $H_0$ between unit-modulus endpoint phases has infinity norm $\le 1$ and differs from its initial endpoint by at most $hR|k|$. The dynamic correction $\lambda(A-\lambda)^{-1}H_0$ is at most $2h^2R^2$. A pendant value is $1/(1-2\lambda h^2)$, whose difference from 1 is at most $16h^2$. Therefore every component of the full unnormalized fiber extension $H_{\lambda}$ differs from its cluster's central phase by at most

$$
d_R=2\pi hR+16h^{2}R^{2}.
$$

Its fiber norm divided by $\sqrt{2M_0}$ lies in $[1-d_R,1+d_R]$. After exact FULL-counting normalization, every mode's rescaled value differs from the corresponding continuum character at the assigned base by at most

$$
b_R=2d_R/(1-d_R).
$$

Consequently, uniformly over EVERY graph vertex and EVERY f in the whole counting unit ball,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&|\sqrt{V_R}\, f(v)-F(x_{\mathrm{base}}(v))|\le\sqrt{7}\, b_R, \\
&\sqrt{V_R}\,|f(v)|\le\sqrt{7}(1+b_R)\le 2\sqrt{7}<8.
\end{aligned}
$$

These bounds retain transit and pendant values; they are not endpoint-only estimates. They also prove a uniform preparation comparison, rather than only an l2 sampling statement.

##### Actual source rule and retained scalar calibration

Choose the FIXED amplitude cap $r=8$. The physical native source input on the real quadrature is

$$
z_{R,v}(f)=\sqrt{V_R}\, \operatorname{Re} f(v)/8,
$$

and the imaginary quadrature uses $\operatorname{Im}f(v)$. These lie in $[-\sqrt{7}/4,\sqrt{7}/4]$, strictly inside $[-1,1]$. The corresponding continuum source is $z_{\mathrm{cont},v}(F)=\operatorname{Re}F(x_{\mathrm{base}}(v))/8$. The same fixed cell-CAR maps carry the actual port operators, independent of $f$.

Since arcsin has Lipschitz constant at most 4/3 on that interval,

$$
|\arcsin z_{R,v}(f)-\arcsin z_{\mathrm{cont},v}(F)|\le\sqrt{7}\, b_R/6.
$$

<a id="construction-f104a8p11-complete-native-source-guarded-interfaces-and-signed-resource-ledger"></a>**Construction F.10.4a.8p.11 (Complete Native Source, Guarded Interfaces and Signed Resource Ledger).**

##### 1. Finite descriptor and graph identity

The version is `f08-spatial-native-source-2-normalized`. Put $h=1/N$. Enumerate $Z=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^3:0<|z|^2\le R^2\}$ in lexicographic order; take the half $Z_+$ whose first nonzero coordinate is positive. Coordinates are comparisons, not node identities: base $v$ maps to $v/N$; chain vertex to $(v+jz/m_z)/N$; every leaf maps to its base (a cost-positive edge may have coincident comparison coordinates). All wrapped coordinates are on $T^3$. The cluster-owner map $b$ sends every auxiliary vertex to its named base. The path from a transit node back to its owner has $j\le R$ edges and from a leaf has one. An addressed query uses that literal path; no relay node is deleted. <a id="theorem-f104a8p12-total-conservative-source-extension-and-all-stage-closure"></a>**Theorem F.10.4a.8p.12 (Total Conservative Source Extension and All-Stage Closure).**

##### 1. Exact old interface and new finite namespace

The source extension in Construction F.10.4a.8p.13 uses the unchanged native source and interpreter of Definition 2.4.1g, Theorem 2.4.1h and Definition 2.4.1i. Original $U$ and all constructor bytes remain unchanged. Native outputs still have kind finite_tree_collision_ready_state. compile_source builds the complete new descriptor from $R$, native depth, canonical finite query list and mode. check requires the exact key set, law recipe map, owner list, positive rational unit fields, cap 8, no native write ports, no live feedback ports and pre-private immutable program. The native subdescriptor is compared with the full original source_code(depth), not with a reduced working-state quotient. $R$ is a power of two at least $2^{40}$; the finite source does not admit small-$R$ normalized amplitudes based on an unproved cap. No desired qualification, complexity, frame winner or native success predicate occurs in the decoder.

The literal operator/graph/control recipes in LAWS are canonical constructors, not user-provided black-box operators. Altering a recipe tag is rejected. Their meanings are the finite constructions in Construction F.10.4a.8p.11, Theorems F.10.4a.8p.7–F.10.4a.8p.9 and Construction F.10.4a.8p.10. A name/hash binds a fixed definition; neither names nor hashes prove its mathematical soundness.

No new prefix-machine constructor is introduced. Original short constructors continue to print only original Native(h) bytes. A finite printer for any new canonical descriptor exists in the original optimal universal namespace $1^{16}0p$, length at least 17. Existence follows from the unchanged explicit enumeration of finite-table transducers and its prefix-filter universality, not from solving tail halting. Therefore every admitted new source has a finite persistent program, while no new source can appear from an old short constructor.

##### 2. Populated owners and primitive leaves

The finite owner cycle is exactly the following twelve entries, also printed as OWNERS in Construction F.10.4a.8p.13:

The explicit constitutive ideal leaves are: (a) original native physical leaves, unchanged; (b) paid write-once classical copy/latch apparatus; (c) supplied finite quasifree ready state and nearest-neighbor Wilson evolution; (d) supplied exact restricted-expression angle control, bounded finite-rank compensation and extended local qutrit instrument; (e) declared calibrated clocks, ready/maintenance prices and signed work-reservoir law; (f) the instrument-restricted forward-latched service interface. Algebraic identities, finite unitary/channel composition, response identities and ledger conservation are CONSEQUENCES, not extra unproved primitive equations. No universal laboratory synthesis/precision law is asserted. These leaves are stated on the ideal-source basis allowed by the parent; no assertion of already executed hardware is needed.

##### 3. Full guards and finite outputs

The elementary step function of Construction F.10.4a.8p.13 checks only a phase projection. Construction F.10.4a.8p.13 gives the complete fixed-schedule guard machine for the declared route-query service. schedule expands every addressed route and assigns exact rational physical times, source-copy bank, each actual relay bank, setup, pulse, readout and seal. Larger routings can be supplied as a new finite service descriptor, but arbitrary adaptive or simultaneous feedback is not implicitly admitted.

##### 4. Total generated hierarchy and coverage

For $j\ge 0$, obligation(j) chooses owner $\mathrm{OWNERS}[j\bmod 12]$ and payload $b(\lfloor j/12\rfloor)$, the binary expansion of $m+1$ with its initial 1 removed. Byte-aligned strings are canonically decoded. Typed payload nodes are source, primitive(owner), sequence(items), branch(cases), prefix(n), coefficient(n), and precision(n), with nonnegative integer $n$. Malformed payloads denote a tautology/local-owner repetition. The normative encoding for arbitrary finite semantic depth is a SHALLOW flat DAG: a finite nodes array, each sequence/branch node referring only to earlier integer node indices, and an explicit root index. Every finite typed tree has this encoding by postorder enumeration; conversely backward references give a finite acyclic unfolding. Its finite structural nesting is bounded independently of semantic depth. Therefore every finite semantic tree and precision/prefix/coefficient request has a finite canonical payload that occurs at a finite index for every owner. For native outputs, hierarchy invokes the original machine.test_obligation VERBATIM at every old index. This is not a semantic assertion oracle: the following induction proves those fixed canonical premises imply every eligible generated instance. The $n=0$ convention is unchanged, and native behavior is identical at every $n$ by literal dispatch.

Eligible-law coverage is relative to THIS closed source/instrument grammar. It includes every finite admitted event prefix, finite outcome coarse-graining, typed composition/branch and requested approximation accuracy. It does not claim coverage of unrestricted local instruments, arbitrary feedback, arbitrary quantum programs or all laboratory physics. Every owner is explicit and every finite payload is enumerated. No hidden law family remains to be silently checked after acceptance.

##### 5. Primitive/composition/branch/prefix/semigroup induction

Primitive step: each canonical native state/kernel/instrument diagram is its original proven diagram. New classical copies are finite permutations with fresh records and preserved origin. New quantum drifts are finite-dimensional unitary conjugations; qutrit readout has the exact projectors $(B^2\pm B)/2$ and $I-B^2$, summing to $I$. Complete positivity and normalization follow from finite sums; impossible branches contribute zero without dividing by their probabilities. This covers adaptive native instruments already present in the original local task, but does not invent new external feedback ports.

All forbidden events have false admissibility antecedent, not an invented physical result. Event-time/readout guards are part of the primitive interface and preserved by schedule induction.

Semigroup/coefficient: each fixed finite quantum segment has a bounded finite matrix H, so its exponential power series is absolutely norm-convergent at every finite declared time. Generator intertwiners imply all powers by induction, and hence the full exponential by norm convergence. This also applies to the finite original native generators under their original proof. The statement is NOT an unjustified Taylor expansion of an infinite-dimensional interacting generator. Piecewise segments and finite outcomes then follow by sequence/branch induction.

Precision: finite algebraic isolation plus certified analytic function/exponential approximation supplies arbitrary-precision unnormalized response kernels. Spectral gaps and the whole-band amplitude cap are explicit proofs, not exact-real tests. Refinement is driven by rigorous error bounds, not by deciding equality to zero. The computable-real supplied-angle semantics is distinct from exact finite-bit computation. The source does not grant uncharged numerical calibration work.

These inductions establish every generated instance from the fixed local owner premises. They constitute the specialized external normalizer theorem for this source extension. Therefore a canonical new descriptor satisfies every $L_{n}$ via its finite tail printer, conditional only on the named constitutive physical leaves of §2 and the mathematical proof premises, not on a future unspecified semantic checker.

For each host, projection onto the ENTIRE native carrier intertwines every new operation with identity (after its unchanged native task), and every old native operation with itself. No early/private feedback, resetting, archive replacement or modified native marginal exists. ##### 8. Exact registry, ranks and resource adapter

Construction F.10.4a.8p.13 binds every owner to its fixed native definition and strictly lower-rank dependencies. The closed descriptor grammar excludes altered recipe names, missing owners and invalid dependency assignments.

Finite-tree traversal and the ordered node-index test decide the request grammar. A flat node list represents arbitrarily large finite semantic depth.
