<a id="construction-f104a8p13-literal-finite-stock-guard-and-source-algorithms"></a>**Construction F.10.4a.8p.13 (Literal Finite Stock, Guard and Source Algorithms).**

This construction specifies the finite physical source of Construction F.10.4a.8p.11 and the total conservative extension of Theorem F.10.4a.8p.12 by mathematical constructors. Its quantum operations are the actual finite instruments of Theorems F.10.4a.8p.6–8. Classical guards specify when and where those instruments are available; they do not calculate a future quantum outcome.

#### 1. The exact graph, addresses and route constructor

For an even integer $R\ge2$, let
$$
 \mathcal Z_R=\{z\in\mathbb Z^3:0<|z|^2\le R^2,
 \text{ the first nonzero coordinate of }z\text{ is positive}\},
 \qquad m_z=\lceil|z|\rceil.
$$
Use lexicographic order. Put
$$
 N=R^8,\quad P=1+\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z_R}(m_z-1),\quad
 V=2PN^3,\quad E=N^3\left(\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z_R}m_z+P\right).
$$
These are the actual graph and its counts in Lemma F.10.4a.8p.1 and Theorem F.10.4a.8p.2, including every transit and pendant vertex. Base addresses are $(\mathrm{base},v)$ with $v\in\{0,\ldots,N-1\}^3$; leaf addresses are $(\mathrm{leaf},v,j)$ with $1\le j\le P$; transit addresses are $(\mathrm{transit},v,z,j)$ with $z\in\mathcal Z_R$ and $1\le j<m_z$. No other address is admitted.

The route $\mathcal P(q)$ from a base address is the singleton base. From a leaf it is that leaf followed by its base. From a transit address it is
$$
 (\mathrm{transit},v,z,j),(\mathrm{transit},v,z,j-1),\ldots,
 (\mathrm{transit},v,z,1),(\mathrm{base},v).
$$
Every step is an actual graph edge. This fixes the full route and its origin, not merely its length.

The closed spatial-source family uses $R=2^r$ with integer $r\ge40$, a native depth $h\in\mathbb N$, and a nonempty finite query list. The smaller even-$R$ constructor also defines the finite auxiliary examples without changing that closed-family restriction.

#### 2. Actual finite queries and their source maps

A normalized-band query specifies an address, a quadrature $\mathrm{real}$ or $\mathrm{imag}$, and seven complex rational coefficients $c_j=a_j+ib_j$ satisfying $\sum_j(a_j^2+b_j^2)\le1$. Every rational is encoded by its reduced numerator and positive denominator. Use the actual seven-mode counting-normalized $PW_4$ basis of Theorem F.10.4a.8p.7, not an independently assigned seven-dimensional carrier. For its vector $f$ the actual source input and retained output scale are
$$
 z=\frac{\sqrt V}{8}\operatorname{Re}f(q)
 \quad\hbox{or}\quad
 z=\frac{\sqrt V}{8}\operatorname{Im}f(q),
 \qquad s_{\rm rec}=\frac8{\sqrt V}.
$$
The whole-band bound proves $|z|\le1$. The physical port uses the cell-average product-square profile of power twelve and $\rho=1/(32R)$, the $-\arcsin z$ control with its rank-four drift compensation, and the late qutrit spectral readout of the fixed $B$. Its projectors are $(B^2+B)/2$, $(B^2-B)/2$ and $I-B^2$. They sum to the identity. All four spinor modes per base cell and the full twisted Wilson carrier remain present.

The auxiliary direct finite example instead specifies a rational $z\in[-1,1]$ at an address and uses that same finite port. It is a separate finite query type. The closed seven-mode source decoder admits the normalized-band type only. Thus a direct example does not replace the whole-band input class.

#### 3. Native stock and complete resource formulas

Write $w(n)=\max(1,\lceil\log_2 n\rceil)$ for $n\ge1$. The complete original native source of depth $h$ has
$$
 D_h=2h+2,\quad G_h=h+3,
$$
$$
 B_h=D_h+w(D_h+1)+5+9+3+2+w(h+1)+2w(G_h+1),
$$
$$
 J_h=h+4+w(h+1),\qquad
 I_h=(h+3)B_h+2h+42+J_h+B_h+16,
$$
$$
 C_h=B_h+2h+(h+3)B_h+42+(h+5)+w(h+1)+J_h
       +4I_h+3+4+(4B_h+32),
$$
$$
 \mathcal N(h)=C_h+B_h2^{B_h+4}+2^{I_h}.
$$
This is the unchanged complete stock of Definition 2.4.1g, including its controller and verifier ROM; it is not a count of a reduced predictor register.

Fix positive physical $\delta,c,\tau_{\rm native},\hbar$. For $Q$ queries let $\ell_q=|\mathcal P(q)|-1$ and set
$$
 K=\max(1,\sum_q\ell_q),\quad B_{\rm copy}=2KE+Q,
 \quad L=\delta N,\quad \rho=1/(32R),
$$
$$
 s=\min\left(N,2\left\lceil\frac N{32R}\right\rceil+7\right),
 \quad S_{\rm loc}=s^3,\quad a_b=3w(N).
$$
The route-ROM count is
$$
 b_{\rm route}=\sum_q|\mathcal P(q)|
 [a_b+3w(2R+1)+w(R+1)+3].
$$
The fixed-description store retains exactly $153328$ bits. The finite recipe and canonical descriptor stores, defined in part 6, are separate. If $b_{\rm rec}$ and $b_D$ are their bit lengths, put
$$
 b_{\rm prog}=153328+b_{\rm rec}+b_{\rm route}
               +QS_{\rm loc}a_b+256Q.
$$
The full stock is the following mathematical inventory.

| Physical resource | Number |
|---|---:|
| Classical bits | $V\mathcal N(h)+6B_{\rm copy}+b_{\rm prog}+26Q+w(K+1)+3+b_D$ |
| CAR modes | $4N^3Q$ |
| Mode mounts | $N^3Q$ |
| Wilson ports | $4N^3Q$ |
| Local control ports | $2S_{\rm loc}Q$ |
| Instrument ports | $S_{\rm loc}Q$ |
| Qutrit pointers | $Q$ |
| Clocks | $V+Q+1$ |
| Preparation devices | $Q$ |
| Work-store pairs | $Q$ |
| Copy banks | $B_{\rm copy}$ |

The initial classical energy-token count is $V(h+6)+B_{\rm copy}+5Q$. Quantum work reserves remain the separate sum of the actual $W_q$ at their normalized $z$; they are not classical tokens. The two holding horizons are
$$
 T_{\rm query}=h\tau_{\rm native}
 +\sum_q\left(\frac{\ell_q\delta}{c}+\frac{3L\rho}{c}\right),
 \qquad T_{\rm metric}=h\tau_{\rm native}+\frac{K\delta}{c}.
$$
The corresponding reserved event counts are $3V+\sum_q\ell_q+6Q$ and $3V+B_{\rm copy}+5Q$. For readiness prices $r_i\ge0$, maintenance prices $m_i\ge0$ and event price $e\ge0$, with exactly the displayed resource types, the resource cost is
$$
 \mathcal R=\sum_i n_i(r_i+m_iT_{\rm mode})+eN_{\rm event}.
$$
The closed descriptor fixes every $r_i=m_i=e=1$, hence $\mathcal R=\sum_i n_i(1+T_{\rm mode})+N_{\rm event}$. Its physical token energy is $\hbar c/\delta$; the field Hamiltonian/work unit is $\hbar c/(\delta R^8)$. Varying $\hbar$ changes literal energies and returned work, not the integer storage or mode counts. The old native calibration remains unchanged and is converted by its declared token/time map.

#### 4. Fixed schedule, local guards and complete state transitions

The mode and entire query list are latched before any private native result. Start the following finite schedule at $t=h\tau_{\rm native}$. For query $q$, create a fresh source bank at the first vertex of $\mathcal P(q)$ with its immutable origin label and the actual two native snapshot bits followed by the validity bit one. At each next vertex create a fresh link bank after time $\delta/c$, copying that same payload and origin. The previous banks remain retained. In query mode append setup, pulse and readout, each lasting $L\rho/c$, at the route endpoint and controlled by its delivered bank. In metric mode append no CAR setup, pulse or readout. Process the finite query list in order, then seal. A possible earlier metric seal does not shorten its reserved holding horizon $T_{\rm metric}$ or its maintenance invoice.

The coarse phase transitions are ready to metric-ready or query-ready according to the latched mode; metric-ready permits copies and seal. A query passes through routed, setup, pulsed and read states in that order; only after read may it start the next fresh query or seal. The exact schedule refines those transitions and fixes every address, bank identity and event time.

An event is admissible precisely when it is the next event of that schedule, is generated by the internal controller, occurs at its specified time not before the native deadline or the preceding event, and satisfies all its freshness and delivery conditions. Source banks and target banks must be new. A copy must use an already delivered bank whose time is no later than the copy and whose origin is the query origin. Setup, pulse and readout require query mode and the preceding phase of that same query. The readout is the actual spectral instrument of part 2, with its original setting and gain retained. Seal prohibits all further events.

A bank inspection before its creation or delivery returns the fixed not-ready record. A later inspection is admitted only at that bank's actual location. Pointer inspection additionally requires query mode and the completed readout at its actual receiver location; it likewise returns not-ready earlier. There is no public advance/command socket, private snapshot overwrite, nonlocal read or live feedback. The two source bits are supplied by the entire unchanged native carrier after its deadline, not by a new outcome oracle.

#### 5. Finite owner derivations and all-stage hierarchy

Keep the original source $R_h$, its canonical output word, constructor $0\gamma(h+1)$, universal namespace, exact bounded virtual interpreter and all twelve original owner rules exactly as in Definitions 2.4.1g and 2.4.1i and Theorem 2.4.1h. In particular its raw transducer indexing and output convention are those definitions; this extension substitutes no new reference machine. Every old primitive, transition, stopping rule, archive, resource and response is unchanged.

The new owners are ordered
$$
 (\mathrm{whole\_native},\mathrm{graph\_and\_cost},\mathrm{full\_car},
 \mathrm{finite\_local\_port},\mathrm{normalized\_scalar\_join},
 \mathrm{guarded\_events},\mathrm{retained\_output},\mathrm{physical\_units},
 \mathrm{full\_stock},\mathrm{signed\_work},\mathrm{regulator\_bridge},\mathrm{finite\_semantics}).
$$
Their complete mathematical dependencies are:

| Owner | Rank | Immediate owners | Owning result |
|---|---:|---|---|
| whole native | $0$ | none | Definitions 2.4.1g/i; Theorem 2.4.1h |
| physical units | $0$ | none | Construction F.10.4a.8p.10 |
| full CAR | $1$ | physical units | Construction F.10.4a.8p.3; Theorem F.10.4a.8p.5 |
| guarded events | $1$ | whole native, physical units | Construction F.10.4a.8p.11 and part 4 above |
| graph and cost | $2$ | whole native, guarded events | Lemma F.10.4a.8p.1; Theorem F.10.4a.8p.2 |
| finite local port | $2$ | full CAR, guarded events | Theorems F.10.4a.8p.6/8 |
| full stock | $2$ | whole native, physical units, full CAR, guarded events | Construction F.10.4a.8p.11 and part 3 above |
| normalized scalar join | $3$ | graph and cost, finite local port | Theorem F.10.4a.8p.7 |
| signed work | $3$ | finite local port, full stock | Construction F.10.4a.8p.11 |
| regulator bridge | $3$ | full CAR, physical units | Theorem F.10.4a.8p.9 |
| retained output | $4$ | normalized scalar join, guarded events | Theorem F.10.4a.8p.12 |
| finite semantics | $5$ | retained output, signed work, regulator bridge | Theorem F.10.4a.8p.12 |

Every dependency strictly decreases rank. The cited statements and their full native proofs give the owner content; the ordering is a finite induction, not an assumption that a data identifier proves a physical law.

An atomic request is source; primitive of one of these twelve owners; or precision, prefix or coefficient with a nonnegative integer parameter. Finite sequence and finite branch form new requests from finite ordered lists of earlier requests. A flat presentation uses a nonempty node list and a root index in its range; every child reference is strictly smaller than its node index. This forbids cycles and gives arbitrarily large finite depth without a nesting bound. The equivalent nested finite-tree presentation has the same atoms and two constructors. Empty lists are empty logical conjunctions; they do not create a physical exhaustive instrument. Requests describe the registered law instances, not extra quantum-program or feedback sockets. An invalid or duplicated outcome selection has a false physical-admissibility antecedent.

For exact enumeration, write $j=12m+r$, $0\le r<12$. Remove the leading one of $\operatorname{bin}(m+1)$. If the remaining bit count is a multiple of eight, read its bytes by the canonical finite-map convention of part 6. A well-typed request is assigned to owner $r$ in the displayed order; any other byte word gives the tautological request. Thus every finite request occurs. Decoding, finite forward-reference checks and one owner cycle all terminate. The corresponding new-source test is precisely the closed constructor conditions of parts 1–4 and 6. Theorem F.10.4a.8p.12 proves all generated requests by its primitive, sequence, unnormalized-branch, prefix, finite-exponential and precision inductions.

At hierarchy stage $n$, run the unchanged bounded interpreter. An unreturned computation is retained. A returned original native descriptor is tested by its unchanged original owner rules for indices $j<n$. A returned new descriptor is retained exactly when the closed constructor conditions hold, equivalently when they and its first $n$ generated owner requests hold. Every other return is rejected. This gives the same decreasing finite-stage extension and leaves all old strings and outputs unchanged. A finite universal-tail printer supplies each finite new descriptor. The length-eight constructor `00001111` still returns the identical original depth-fourteen native word; all shorter programs and their original nonqualification proof are unchanged. Therefore the original constituent result $C_P=C_{\rm op}=8$ persists on the original native task, without assigning that value to the larger field/regulator source.

#### 6. Exact source-word, recipe and price representation

The source record contains exactly these fifteen named components: kind, registry_sha256, version, R, native, queries, mode, owners, laws, units, prices, amplitude_cap, pre_private_program, native_write_ports and live_feedback_ports. They have the following mathematical values. The kind is the literal ASCII word `F08_SPATIAL_NATIVE_NORMALIZED_SOURCE`; version is the integer two; $R$ and the query list are those above; native is the entire original descriptor of $R_h$ with its identical canonical encoding; mode is query or metric; owners is the ordered twelve-owner list of part 5. The amplitude cap is the integer eight, pre_private_program is true, and both port lists are empty. The fixed registry component is the ASCII identifier
$$
 \texttt{ada052544e3e68f78c0e31344ff5abb1ca575e3140ac55d1028c3ae971e97da2}.
$$
This fixes the preexisting source-word identity. The mathematical owner content is the complete ranked construction in part 5.

The units map has exactly $\delta$, $c$, $\hbar$ and native_time, with the positive reduced rational values $\delta,c,\hbar,\tau_{\rm native}$. The prices map has ready_each, maintenance_each and event equal to the ordered rational pair $[1,1]$, and energy_token equal to the literal string `hbar*c/delta`. Each query has exactly address, coefficients and quadrature. Addresses are ordered arrays: base with its three-coordinate array; leaf with that array and its leaf index; transit with that array, its three-displacement array and its transit index. Each coefficient is an ordered pair of reduced rational pairs representing its real and imaginary parts, in the fixed seven-mode order. All denominator entries are positive and coprime to their numerator. Extra or missing fields, invalid addresses or modes, altered owner order, noncanonical native bytes, changed prices, changed cap or added ports are outside the source grammar.

The laws map is the following fixed set of mathematical recipe names; the physical maps and constants denoted by them are the full constructions already specified above.

| Key | Literal recipe name |
|---|---|
| graph | `d3-all-transit-pendant-R8` |

For source bytes, order all map keys lexicographically by ASCII. Use braces for maps, square brackets for arrays, comma separators and a colon between key and value, with no whitespace outside strings and no final line feed. Integers have their full signed decimal expansion without leading zeros. Strings use double quotes, escaping a quote or backslash by a backslash and using the ordinary short escapes for control characters. True and false are their lowercase words. All source strings above are ASCII. This is the unchanged canonical encoding, including the complete embedded native descriptor. The decoder accepts exactly these canonical words. Define $b_D$ to be eight times their byte length, not a size inferred from a shortened description.

The recipe store uses a distinct finite tuple convention. An integer uses its signed decimal expansion; a string is single-quoted ASCII; a list has square brackets and a tuple has parentheses, with comma followed by one space between entries and a trailing comma for a singleton tuple. All strings occurring in this recipe contain neither a quote nor a backslash. A direct recipe is the tuple of `direct_finite_example`, its address array and the rational numerator/denominator tuple. A normalized recipe is the tuple of `normalized_pw4`, its address array, its seven real/imaginary rational-pair lists, its quadrature string, the tuple (`physical_input`, `sqrt`, $V$, `times_component`, `divide`, $8$), and the tuple (`retained_record_scale`, $8$, `divide_sqrt`, $V$). The coefficient rationals are tuples within their ordered coefficient lists. The complete recipe word is the tuple of `f08-spatial-native-source-2-normalized`, $R$, $h$, and the ordered list of recipes. Let $b_{\rm rec}$ be eight times its ASCII length. These finite rules give its exact byte length, including every separator, for every input.

The nominal constructor uses unit rational values in the four units slots; the admitted family also includes their positive reduced rational choices. All source observations, support comparisons and invoices use the consumed values just specified. The $153328$-bit fixed-description stock, route/support ROM, recipe store and additional full descriptor store remain separately charged. No arbitrary finite integer is excluded by a host-size rule: its digit recursion terminates at that finite integer and its actual encoded length contributes to the stock.

#### 7. Soundness of the complete finite construction

The graph and route sums are finite integer constructions. Every request is a finite acyclic object. Source and query parsing checks finite syntax, integer inequalities and rational unit-ball membership. Every actual history is a prefix of the fixed finite schedule. Induction over that schedule proves freshness, location, source-origin preservation, native-deadline separation and absence of private feedback. Copies are finite permutations with retained records; local quantum controls and the three spectral projectors are the complete normalized instruments already proved on this source. Native-controlled maps preserve the whole native restriction, while finite branch sums retain unnormalized zero-probability cases without division.

Composition preserves the commuting source/state/response diagrams by associativity. Prefix maps commute with later events because archives and delivered banks are write-once. For a bounded finite Hamiltonian, generator intertwiners pass to every power and then to its norm-convergent exponential. Algebraic isolation and the explicit gap/amplitude estimates supply terminating precision refinements for the admitted analytic controls without deciding equality of arbitrary reals. The rank table and these inductions prove every generated owner request. Thus the construction supplies the exact source extension and all its declared finite responses, guarded access, resources and comparison maps at the scopes of Construction F.10.4a.8p.3, Lemma F.10.4a.8p.4, Theorems F.10.4a.8p.5–9, Constructions F.10.4a.8p.10–11 and Theorem F.10.4a.8p.12. $\square$

### F.10.4b Modular Prediction Time

<a id="definition-f104b1-finite-modular-prediction-flow"></a>**Definition F.10.4b.1 (Finite Modular Prediction Flow).** Let $\mathfrak A$ be a finite local algebra and let $\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ be a faithful state with $\rho>0$. The modular prediction flow of $\omega$ is
$$
\sigma_t^\omega(A)
=
\rho^{it}A\rho^{-it}.
\tag{F.10.4b.1}
$$

**Definition F.10.4b.1a (Finite Tomita Standard Form).** Let $\mathfrak A=\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ be a full finite matrix factor and let $\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ with $\rho>0$. Set
$$
\mathcal H_\omega:=\mathcal B_2(\mathcal H),
\qquad
\Omega_\omega:=\rho^{1/2},
\qquad
\pi_\omega(A)X:=AX.
\tag{F.10.4b.1a.1}
$$
The finite Tomita operator is
$$
S_\omega\bigl(A\rho^{1/2}\bigr)
=
A^*\rho^{1/2},
\tag{F.10.4b.1a.2}
$$
and its polar decomposition is
$$
S_\omega=J_\omega\Delta_\omega^{1/2},
\tag{F.10.4b.1a.3}
$$
where
$$
\Delta_\omega(X)=\rho X\rho^{-1},
\qquad
J_\omega(X)=X^*.
\tag{F.10.4b.1a.4}
$$
The modular Hamiltonian is
$$
K_\omega:=-\log\rho.
\tag{F.10.4b.1a.5}
$$
For a finite direct sum of factors, these formulas apply blockwise in the standard $L^2(\mathfrak A,\omega)$ representation, and central scalar shifts are immaterial to each modular automorphism.

**Theorem F.10.4b.1b (Finite Tomita-Takesaki Modular Closure).** For every finite faithful local branch of Definition F.10.4b.1a:

1. $\Omega_\omega$ is cyclic and separating for $\pi_\omega(\mathfrak A)$;

2. the modular group is implemented by
$$
\Delta_\omega^{it}\pi_\omega(A)\Delta_\omega^{-it}
=
\pi_\omega(\rho^{it}A\rho^{-it})
=
\pi_\omega(\sigma_t^\omega(A));
\tag{F.10.4b.1b.1}
$$

3. the modular conjugation maps the represented algebra to its commutant:
$$
J_\omega\pi_\omega(\mathfrak A)J_\omega
=
\pi_\omega(\mathfrak A)'.
\tag{F.10.4b.1b.2}
$$

Hence the modular automorphism group, the KMS clock, and the commutant/opposite-perspective algebra are not independent structures on a finite faithful branch; they are determined by the single state-algebra pair $(\mathfrak A,\omega)$.

*Proof.* Because $\rho>0$, the vectors $A\rho^{1/2}$ span $\mathcal B_2(\mathcal H)$, so $\Omega_\omega$ is cyclic. If $A\rho^{1/2}=0$, then $A=0$ because $\rho^{1/2}$ is invertible, so $\Omega_\omega$ is separating.
For $X\in\mathcal B_2(\mathcal H)$,
$$
\Delta_\omega^{it}X=\rho^{it}X\rho^{-it}.
$$
Therefore
$$
\Delta_\omega^{it}\pi_\omega(A)\Delta_\omega^{-it}X
=
\rho^{it}A\rho^{-it}X
=
\pi_\omega(\rho^{it}A\rho^{-it})X,
$$
proving (F.10.4b.1b.1). The commutant of the left representation consists of right multiplications. Since $J_\omega(X)=X^*$ exchanges left and right multiplication, (F.10.4b.1b.2) follows. The final statement is immediate from the polar decomposition and the uniqueness of the modular objects. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104b2-prediction-time-as-modular-time-on-a-local-equilibrium-branch"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.2 (Prediction Time as Modular Time on a Local Equilibrium Branch).** Let $H=H^\dagger$ on a finite factor, let $\beta>0$ have units of inverse energy, and use the physical Heisenberg flow
$$
\alpha_\tau(A)=e^{i\tau H/\hbar}Ae^{-i\tau H/\hbar}.
$$
Suppose the faithful state $\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ satisfies the upper-strip KMS condition with imaginary-time period $\beta\hbar$. Then
$$
\rho=\frac{e^{-\beta H}}{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})},
\qquad
\sigma_t^\omega=\alpha_{-\beta\hbar t}.
\tag{F.10.4b.2}
$$
Thus the dimensionless modular parameter and physical prediction time obey
$$
\tau=-\beta\hbar t.
\tag{F.10.4b.3}
$$
On a direct sum of factors, the faithful state has arbitrary strictly positive central weights summing to one and the normalized Gibbs state within each factor; the flow identity holds blockwise.

*Proof.* Every matrix is entire analytic for the finite flow. The KMS boundary identity is
$$
\omega(A\alpha_{i\beta\hbar}(B))=\omega(BA).
$$
Choose an energy eigenbasis and write $A=E_{ab}$, $B=E_{cd}$. Since $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho E_{ad})=\rho_{da}$, this gives
$$
\delta_{bc}e^{-\beta(E_c-E_d)}\rho_{da}
=\delta_{da}\rho_{bc}.
$$
Taking $b=c$ and $a\ne d$ makes every off-diagonal entry $\rho_{da}$ vanish, including within a degenerate energy eigenspace. Taking $b=c$ and $d=a$ then gives
$$
\rho_{aa}e^{-\beta(E_b-E_a)}=\rho_{bb}.
$$
Normalization yields the displayed Gibbs state. The finite modular formula of Theorem F.10.4b.1b gives
$$
\rho^{it}A\rho^{-it}
=e^{-i\beta tH}Ae^{i\beta tH}
=\alpha_{-\beta\hbar t}(A).
$$
A central block weight and its partition function cancel in conjugation, proving the direct-sum statement. ∎

<a id="corollary-f104b3-unruhkms-time-as-modular-prediction-time"></a>**Corollary F.10.4b.3 (Unruh/KMS Time as Modular Prediction Time).** On a finite faithful local Rindler regulator satisfying Theorem F.10.4b.2, retain the physical Heisenberg orientation and the accepted wedge-state, observer and proper-time certificate of Theorem F.10.3. With proper acceleration $\kappa>0$, the imaginary proper-time period is $\tau_U=2\pi c/\kappa$, the energy inverse temperature is $\beta_U=\tau_U/\hbar$, and
$$
\sigma_t^\omega=\alpha_{-\tau_U t},
\qquad \tau=-\tau_U t.
$$
In units $c=\hbar=1$, this is $\tau=-\beta_U t$ with $\beta_U=2\pi/\kappa$. A statement for the limiting wedge algebra requires a compatible limiting modular-flow identification.

*Proof.* The finite-factor, faithfulness, physical-flow and upper-strip KMS hypotheses allow Theorem F.10.4b.2 to be applied with $\beta=\tau_U/\hbar$. Its flow identity gives the displayed relation. Theorem F.10.3 supplies the continuum thermal certificate but does not identify the limiting wedge algebra with a finite factor. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104b3a-finite-classification-of-modular-intertwining-passivity-and-complete-passivity"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.3a (Finite Classification of Modular Intertwining, Passivity and Complete Passivity).** Let $\mathfrak A=\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ with $2\le\dim\mathcal H<\infty$, let $H=H^\dagger$ be a Hamiltonian that is not a scalar multiple of $I$, let $\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ with $\rho>0$, and let $\alpha_\tau$ be the physical Heisenberg flow of Theorem F.10.4b.2. The state $\omega$ is passive for $H$ when $\operatorname{Tr}(U\rho U^*H)\ge\operatorname{Tr}(\rho H)$ for every unitary $U$, and completely passive when $\rho^{\otimes n}$ is passive for
$$
H_n=\sum_{k=1}^nI^{\otimes(k-1)}\otimes H\otimes I^{\otimes(n-k)}
$$
for every $n\ge1$. Then:

1. $\sigma_t^\omega\alpha_\tau=\alpha_\tau\sigma_t^\omega$ for all $t,\tau\in\mathbb R$ if and only if $\omega\circ\alpha_\tau=\omega$ for all $\tau$, if and only if $[H,\rho]=0$;
2. $\omega$ is passive if and only if $[H,\rho]=0$ and every common orthonormal eigenbasis, with $He_a=E_ae_a$ and $\rho e_a=p_ae_a$, satisfies
$$
(E_a-E_b)(p_a-p_b)\le0\qquad\text{for all }a,b;
\tag{F.10.4b.3a.1}
$$
3. the following are equivalent: (a) $\omega$ is completely passive; (b) $\rho=e^{-\beta H}/\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H}$ for some $\beta\in[0,\infty)$; (c) $\sigma_t^\omega=\alpha_{-\beta\hbar t}$ for all $t$ and some $\beta\in[0,\infty)$; (d) $\omega(A\,\alpha_{i\beta\hbar}(B))=\omega(BA)$ for all $A,B$ and some $\beta\in[0,\infty)$. For $\beta>0$, (d) is the upper-strip KMS condition of Theorem F.10.4b.2 with imaginary-time period $\beta\hbar$; for $\beta=0$ it is the trace condition $\omega(AB)=\omega(BA)$. The values of $\beta$ in (b), (c) and (d) coincide and are unique;
4. the implications $3\Rightarrow2\Rightarrow1$ are strict. With $H=E_0\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2)$ and $E_0>0$, the state $\rho_1=\operatorname{diag}(\tfrac12,\tfrac16,\tfrac13)$ satisfies item 1 and violates (F.10.4b.3a.1), while $\rho_2=\operatorname{diag}(\tfrac12,\tfrac13,\tfrac16)$ is passive but not completely passive. In fact $\rho_2^{\otimes n}$ is passive exactly for $n\le4$. For $n=5$ the product eigenvectors $e_{22000}$ and $e_{11111}$ have energies $4E_0<5E_0$ and weights
$$
\left(\tfrac16\right)^2\left(\tfrac12\right)^3=\tfrac1{288}<\tfrac1{243}=\left(\tfrac13\right)^5.
\tag{F.10.4b.3a.2}
$$

Thus the physical flow commutes with the modular flow exactly on stationary faithful states, and the modular-time identification of Theorem F.10.4b.2 holds, with $\beta\ge0$, exactly on the completely passive ones. For $\beta=0$ item 3 reads $\rho=I/\dim\mathcal H$, $\sigma_t^\omega=\mathrm{id}$ and $\omega(AB)=\omega(BA)$. For simple spectrum, the equivalence (a)$\Leftrightarrow$(b) is Theorem G.1.9.3c; the present statement covers every nonscalar spectrum, including degenerate levels, and adds items 1, 2, 3(c) and 4. Items 3(a), 3(b) and 3(d), including $\beta=0$ and the uniqueness of $\beta$, agree with Theorem 48a.2 in Section 12, which proves the same equivalence for every nonscalar spectrum by product-eigenvector exchanges.

*Proof.* (1) If $[H,\rho]=0$, the unitary groups $\rho^{it}$ and $e^{i\tau H/\hbar}$ commute, so the two automorphism groups commute, and cyclicity of the trace gives $\omega\circ\alpha_\tau=\omega$. If $\omega\circ\alpha_\tau=\omega$ for all $\tau$, trace duality gives $e^{-i\tau H/\hbar}\rho e^{i\tau H/\hbar}=\rho$, and differentiation at $\tau=0$ gives $[H,\rho]=0$. If the automorphism groups commute, then $W(t,\tau)=\rho^{it}e^{i\tau H/\hbar}\rho^{-it}e^{-i\tau H/\hbar}$ implements the identity automorphism of the factor and is therefore a scalar unitary $c(t,\tau)I$. Since $\det W=1$, $c(t,\tau)$ is a $(\dim\mathcal H)$-th root of unity; it depends continuously on $(t,\tau)$ and equals $1$ at $\tau=0$, so $c\equiv1$. Differentiating $\rho^{it}e^{i\tau H/\hbar}\rho^{-it}=e^{i\tau H/\hbar}$ at $\tau=0$ and then at $t=0$ gives $[\log\rho,H]=0$, hence $[\rho,H]=0$.

(2) Let $\omega$ be passive. For self-adjoint $K$, the function $f(s)=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{\mathrm{isK}}\rho e^{-isK}H)$ is minimal at $s=0$, so $0=f'(0)=i\operatorname{Tr}(K[\rho,H])$. Writing $[\rho,H]=iM$ with $M$ self-adjoint and choosing $K=M$ gives $\operatorname{Tr}M^2=0$, so $[\rho,H]=0$. In a common eigenbasis, the unitary exchanging $e_a$ and $e_b$ and fixing the other basis vectors changes the energy by $-(E_a-E_b)(p_a-p_b)$, which proves (F.10.4b.3a.1). Conversely, under commutation and (F.10.4b.3a.1),
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(U\rho U^*H)=\sum_{a,b}p_a\,|\langle e_b,Ue_a\rangle|^2\,E_b
$$
has a doubly stochastic coefficient matrix, which by the Birkhoff--von Neumann theorem is a convex combination of permutation matrices. Ordering the basis by increasing energy, and by decreasing weight inside each energy level, makes the weights nonincreasing by (F.10.4b.3a.1). The rearrangement inequality then gives $\sum_ap_aE_{\pi(a)}\ge\sum_ap_aE_a$ for every permutation $\pi$, so $\omega$ is passive.

(3) (b)$\Rightarrow$(a): for $\beta=0$, $\rho^{\otimes n}$ is a multiple of the identity and every comparison is an equality. For $\beta>0$, $\rho^{\otimes n}=\gamma_n:=e^{-\beta H_n}/\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H_n}$, and every state $\tau$ satisfies
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(\tau H_n)-\beta^{-1}S(\tau)-\bigl[\operatorname{Tr}(\gamma_nH_n)-\beta^{-1}S(\gamma_n)\bigr]=\beta^{-1}D(\tau\|\gamma_n)\ge0.
$$
Taking $\tau=U\gamma_nU^*$, for which $S(\tau)=S(\gamma_n)$, gives passivity.

(a)$\Rightarrow$(b): the case $n=1$ and item 2 give a common eigenbasis $(e_a)$ with $p_a>0$. The product basis $e_x=e_{x_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{x_n}$ diagonalizes $\rho^{\otimes n}$ and $H_n$, with energy $\sum_kE_{x_k}$ and weight $\prod_kp_{x_k}$. Put $l_a=-\log p_a$. If $k_a$ is the number of occurrences of $a$ in $x$, item 2 applied to $(\rho^{\otimes n},H_n)$ gives, for all rational probability vectors $q_a=k_a/n$ and $q'_a=k'_a/n$ with a common denominator,
$$
\langle q,E\rangle<\langle q',E\rangle
\Longrightarrow
\langle q,l\rangle\le\langle q',l\rangle.
\tag{F.10.4b.3a.3}
$$
Suppose the points $P_a=(E_a,l_a)\in\mathbb R^2$ are not collinear. Three of them are affinely independent, and $q\mapsto(\langle q,E\rangle,\langle q,l\rangle)$ maps the probability simplex on those three labels homeomorphically onto a triangle $T$ with nonempty interior. Choose an interior point $(e,\lambda)$ and $\delta>0$ such that the open discs of radius $\delta/2$ about $(e-\delta,\lambda+\delta)$ and $(e+\delta,\lambda-\delta)$ lie in $T$. Rational simplex points are dense, so rational $q,q'$ have images in the first and second discs, respectively. Then $\langle q,E\rangle<\langle q',E\rangle$ and $\langle q,l\rangle>\langle q',l\rangle$, contradicting (F.10.4b.3a.3). Hence the points are collinear. Since $H$ is not scalar, the energies are not all equal, so $l_a=\beta E_a+c$ for real $\beta,c$, and $\rho$ is the displayed Gibbs matrix. If $\beta<0$, two levels with $E_a<E_b$ would have $p_a<p_b$, violating (F.10.4b.3a.1). Therefore $\beta\ge0$.

(b)$\Leftrightarrow$(c): the Gibbs form gives $\rho^{it}=(\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H})^{-it}e^{-i\beta tH}$, hence $\sigma_t^\omega=\alpha_{-\beta\hbar t}$. Conversely, if $\operatorname{Ad}\rho^{it}=\operatorname{Ad}e^{-i\beta tH}$ for all $t$, then $\rho^{it}e^{i\beta tH}=c(t)I$ with $c(t)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^{it}e^{i\beta tH})/\dim\mathcal H$ differentiable and $c(0)=1$. Differentiation at $t=0$ gives $\log\rho=-\beta H-ic'(0)I$, where $-ic'(0)$ is real because $\log\rho$ and $H$ are self-adjoint. Normalization gives (b). (b)$\Leftrightarrow$(d): here $\alpha_{i\beta\hbar}(B)=e^{-\beta H}Be^{\beta H}$. Setting $A=I$ in (d) and using trace duality gives $e^{\beta H}\rho e^{-\beta H}=\rho$. With $Y=e^{\beta H}\rho=\rho e^{\beta H}$, cyclicity turns (d) into $\operatorname{Tr}(YAe^{-\beta H}B)=\operatorname{Tr}(Ae^{-\beta H}YB)$ for all $B$, so $Y$ commutes with every matrix $Ae^{-\beta H}$, hence with every matrix. Thus $Y$ is a positive scalar, which is (b). Conversely, for the Gibbs matrix cyclicity gives $\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H}Ae^{-\beta H}Be^{\beta H})=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H}BA)$, which is (d). These implications and those between (b) and (c) keep the same $\beta$. If (b) held for $\beta\ne\beta'$, then $(\beta-\beta')H$ would be scalar, which is excluded because $H$ is not scalar; hence $\beta$ is unique.

(4) Both states commute with $H$. For $\rho_1$, the levels $E_0<2E_0$ carry weights $\tfrac16<\tfrac13$, violating (F.10.4b.3a.1). For $\rho_2^{\otimes n}$, a product eigenvector with $k_1$ factors at level $1$ and $k_2$ at level $2$ has energy $E=(k_1+2k_2)E_0$ and
$$
-\log p=n\log2+\frac{E}{E_0}\log\tfrac32+k_2\log\tfrac43.
$$
At energy $mE_0$ the admissible values are $\max\{0,m-n\}\le k_2\le\lfloor m/2\rfloor$. Condition (F.10.4b.3a.1) holds for all pairs exactly when, for every $m$, the largest value of $-\log p$ at level $m$ does not exceed the smallest at level $m+1$, since every level $0,\ldots,2n$ is occupied and nonadjacent comparisons follow by chaining through the intermediate levels; that is, exactly when
$$
\bigl(\lfloor m/2\rfloor-\max\{0,m+1-n\}\bigr)\log\tfrac43\le\log\tfrac32 .
$$
Since $1<\log\tfrac32/\log\tfrac43<2$, this is the integer condition $\lfloor m/2\rfloor-\max\{0,m+1-n\}\le1$. For $m\le n-1$ it requires $\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor\le1$, and for $m\ge n$ it requires $\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1\le1$; both hold exactly when $n\le4$. Item 2 therefore gives passivity for $n\le4$. For $n=5$, exchanging $e_{22000}$ and $e_{11111}$ lowers the energy by $E_0(\tfrac1{243}-\tfrac1{288})=\tfrac{5E_0}{7776}>0$, which is (F.10.4b.3a.2). Item 3 then excludes complete passivity of $\rho_2$, as does the inequality of its consecutive weight ratios $\tfrac32\ne2$ for equally spaced levels. ∎

<a id="definition-f104b4-thermally-regularized-predictive-otoc"></a>**Definition F.10.4b.4 (Thermally Regularized Predictive OTOC).** On a finite faithful KMS branch with density matrix $\rho_*$ and energy inverse temperature $\beta>0$, set $y=\rho_*^{1/4}$. For Hermitian contractions $A,B$, define
$$
F_{AB}(t)=
\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(yA(t)yB\,yA(t)yB)}
{F_{\mathrm{disc}}(t)}.
\tag{F.10.4b.4}
$$
The nonzero disconnected normalization, its lower bound on the retained window, and the analytic and disk bounds below are separate certificate data. An exponential-window claim must include derivative control: writing
$$
1-F_{AB}(t)=c_{AB}e^{\lambda_Lt}(1+r(t)),
\quad c_{AB}>0,\quad 1+r(t)>0,
\tag{F.10.4b.5}
$$
requires $r$ to be differentiable and $r'(t)/(1+r(t))\to0$ in the declared window limit. A value asymptotic alone does not supply this derivative conclusion.

<a id="theorem-f104b5-conditional-modular-chaos-bound"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.5 (Conditional Modular Chaos Bound).** Put $a=2\pi/(\beta\hbar)$. Suppose a normalized OTOC $F$ is holomorphic in the half-strip
$$
\{z:\operatorname{Re}z>0,\ |\operatorname{Im}z|<\beta\hbar/4\},
$$
has $|F(z)|\le1$, and is real with $-1<F(t)<1$ at the positive real times under consideration. Then
$$
\left|\frac{d}{dt}\log(1-F(t))\right|
\le \frac a2(1+F(t))\coth(at)
\le a\coth(at).
$$
A window limit with $t\to\infty$ and $\frac{d}{dt}\log(1-F(t))\to\lambda_L$ therefore satisfies
$$
\lambda_L\le\frac{2\pi}{\beta\hbar}.
\tag{F.10.4b.6}
$$
The window limit may run through a certified family of finite systems; it need not be an infinite-time exponential law on one finite carrier. Any factorization or finite-size errors used to infer the logarithmic derivative must be controlled in both value and derivative on that window.

*Proof.* The map $w=\sinh(az)$ maps the half-strip conformally onto the right half-plane, and $\zeta=(w-1)/(w+1)$ maps that half-plane onto the disk. Schwarz--Pick, pulled back to the real line, yields
$$
\frac{|F'(t)|}{1-|F(t)|^2}
\le \frac{|w'(t)|}{2\operatorname{Re}w(t)}
=\frac a2\coth(at).
$$
Divide by $1-F(t)>0$ and use $1-F(t)^2=(1-F(t))(1+F(t))$. Since $\coth(at)\to1$, the derivative limit gives the claimed rate bound. For Definition F.10.4b.4,
$$
\frac{d}{dt}\log(1-F(t))
=\lambda_L+\frac{r'(t)}{1+r(t)},
$$
which identifies the limit under its derivative certificate. The real line lies inside this half-strip; no boundary version of Schwarz--Pick is being assumed. These are conditional analytic hypotheses for the Maldacena--Shenker--Stanford application, not a derivation of an OTOC certificate from finite dimensionality. ∎

**Definition F.10.4b.6a (Scrambling-Saturation Certificate $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{scr}}$).** A scrambling-saturation certificate is a finite record
$$
\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{scr}}
=
(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{KMS/OTOC}},\;\mathcal G_{\mathrm{mix}},\;\Delta_{\mathrm{mix}},\;\mathcal F_{\mathrm{design}},\;N_{\mathrm{eff}},\;r_{\mathrm{scr}},\;\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{TV}}\ \text{if entropy continuity is claimed},\;\text{structural independence record})
$$
where $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{KMS/OTOC}}$ supplies the analyticity and boundedness hypotheses of Theorem F.10.4b.5, $\mathcal G_{\mathrm{mix}}$ is the retained boundary channel or interaction graph, $\Delta_{\mathrm{mix}}$ is a certified expander/spectral-gap or frame-potential contraction datum, $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{design}}$ records the approximate-design quality when a Page or Haar comparison is used, $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the finite effective number of retained boundary degrees of freedom, and $r_{\mathrm{scr}}\in[0,1)$ is a dimensionless saturation residual bounded by the declared model. The dependency record verifies Definition 2.4.1d for the mixing data and saturation bound. Capacity saturation alone is not a scrambling-saturation certificate.

**Proposition F.10.4b.7a (Fast Scrambling Requires $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{scr}}$).** The chaos bound $\lambda_L\le2\pi/(\beta\hbar)$ holds on the complete branch of Theorem F.10.4b.5. For a fast-scrambling conclusion, assume $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{scr}}$ additionally supplies $\beta>0$, $N_{\mathrm{eff}}>0$, constants $c_0,q_*>0$, and a nonnegative disturbance $g(t)$ with
$$
g(0)\ge c_0/N_{\mathrm{eff}},\qquad
g(t)\ge g(0)e^{\lambda_Lt}\quad(0\le t<t_*),
$$
where $t_*=\inf\{t\ge0:g(t)\ge q_*\}$, with $\inf\varnothing=\infty$. Suppose
$$
\lambda_L\ge\frac{2\pi}{\beta\hbar}(1-r_{\mathrm{scr}}),
\qquad 0\le r_{\mathrm{scr}}<1.
$$
Then, writing $[x]_+=\max\{x,0\}$,
$$
t_*\le
\frac{\beta\hbar}{2\pi(1-r_{\mathrm{scr}})}
\left[\ln\frac{N_{\mathrm{eff}}q_*}{c_0}\right]_+.
$$

*Proof.* If $g(0)\ge q_*$, then $t_*=0$ and the bound holds. Otherwise $\ln(q_*/g(0))>0$. If $t_*>\lambda_L^{-1}\ln(q_*/g(0))$, a time strictly between these two values would be below $t_*$ but would have $g(t)>q_*$ by the growth bound, a contradiction. Thus
$$
t_*\le\lambda_L^{-1}\ln(q_*/g(0))
\le\frac{\beta\hbar}{2\pi(1-r_{\mathrm{scr}})}
\ln\frac{N_{\mathrm{eff}}q_*}{c_0}.
$$
The logarithm in this second case is positive. This proves the positive-part formula in both cases. An area interpretation of $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$ and a Page-entropy conclusion retain their separate certificates. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104b7b-no-exact-exponential-otoc-window-on-a-finite-closed-carrier"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.7b (No Exact Exponential OTOC Window on a Finite Closed Carrier).** Let $\mathcal H$ be finite-dimensional, let $H=H^*$, and let $A,B$ and a faithful density matrix $\rho$ be fixed with $[H,\rho]=0$. Every correlation function obtained by taking a finite product of the matrix entries of
$$
A(t)=e^{\mathrm{itH}}Ae^{-itH}
$$
and then tracing against fixed matrices is an exponential polynomial
$$
P(t)=\sum_{k=1}^N c_ke^{i\nu_kt},
\qquad \nu_k\in\mathbb R.
\tag{F.10.4b.7b.1}
$$
Let $P$ be the connected OTOC numerator and let $Q$ be a nonzero disconnected normalization of this form. If $Q$ is nonzero on a real open interval $I$, there are no constants $c>0$ and $\lambda>0$ for which
$$
1-\frac{P(t)}{Q(t)}=ce^{\lambda t}
\tag{F.10.4b.7b.2}
$$
throughout $I$. Consequently a strictly finite closed Hamiltonian carrier cannot exactly saturate the positive-exponent chaos differential bound on an open time interval. Approximate exponential windows, open-system generators, refining carrier limits, and the mixing and tail entries of $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{scr}}$ are not classified by this obstruction.

*Proof.* Diagonalize $H$. Every matrix entry of $A(t)$ is a finite sum of phases $e^{i(E_j-E_k)t}$, and multiplication and tracing preserve the form (F.10.4b.7b.1). If (F.10.4b.7b.2) held on $I$, then
$$
Q(t)-P(t)=ce^{\lambda t}Q(t)
\tag{F.10.4b.7b.3}
$$
there. Both sides extend to entire exponential polynomials, so the identity theorem extends (F.10.4b.7b.3) to all complex $t$. The exponents on the left have real part zero, whereas every exponent on the right has real part $\lambda>0$. Linear independence of finitely many exponentials with distinct exponents forces every coefficient on both sides to vanish. This would give $Q=0$, contrary to the premise. Exact equality in the chaos differential bound with positive rate integrates to (F.10.4b.7b.2), so it is excluded on this class. ∎

Theorem F.10.4b.7b rules out the exact-saturation route. Theorem F.10.4b.5 gives the chaos bound on every branch whose certificate supplies its analytic-strip hypotheses; the explicit source of Definition F.10.4b.7h supplies the original unsaturated approximate/refining thermal and complete-response branch through Theorems F.10.4b.7h.1–3 and F.10.4b.7h.5–6 with Construction F.10.4b.7h.4. This does not assert a classification of every thermal family or saturation.

<a id="theorem-f104b7c-exact-window-obstruction-on-finite-open-carriers"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.7c (Exact-Window Obstruction on Finite Open Carriers).** Let $\mathcal H$ be finite-dimensional, let $\mathcal L^*$ be a linear map on $\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ with $\mathcal L^*(X^*)=\mathcal L^*(X)^*$, for example a GKLS Heisenberg generator or $i[H,\cdot\,]$, let $A\ne0$, and put $A(t)=e^{t\mathcal L^*}A$. Let $P(t)=\Phi(A(t),A(t))$ for a complex bilinear form $\Phi$ on $\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$, and let
$$
Q(t)=\kappa\,\|MA(t)N\|_2^2,\qquad\kappa\ne0,
\tag{F.10.4b.7c.1}
$$
with invertible $M,N$ and the Hilbert--Schmidt norm. Then:

1. no real open interval $I$ on which $Q\ne0$ carries constants $c\ne0$ and $\lambda>0$ with $1-P(t)/Q(t)=ce^{\lambda t}$ throughout $I$. In particular, for a faithful density matrix $\rho_*$, $y=\rho_*^{1/4}$ and self-adjoint $A,B\ne0$, the regularized numerator of Definition F.10.4b.4 with the disconnected normalization
$$
F_{\mathrm{disc}}(t)=\operatorname{Tr}(y^2A(t)y^2A(t))\,\operatorname{Tr}(y^2By^2B)
\tag{F.10.4b.7c.2}
$$
admits no exact positive-exponent window, whether or not $\rho_*$ is stationary;
2. hypothesis (F.10.4b.7c.1) cannot be weakened to a nonzero exponential-polynomial normalization generated by the carrier. For the dephasing qubit $\mathcal L^*(X)=\gamma(\sigma_zX\sigma_z-X)$ with $\gamma>0$, $\rho_*=I/2$, $A=\sigma_x+\sigma_z$ and $B=\sigma_z$, the numerator is $P(t)=1-e^{-4\gamma t}$. With $Q(t)=-\operatorname{Tr}(y^2A'(t)y^2A'(t))=-e^{-4\gamma t}$ for $A'=\sigma_x$,
$$
1-\frac{P(t)}{Q(t)}=e^{4\gamma t}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).
\tag{F.10.4b.7c.3}
$$

*Proof.* Decompose $\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ into generalized eigenspaces of $\mathcal L^*$. Then
$$
A(t)=\sum_k\sum_{j=0}^{J_k}t^je^{\nu_kt}A_{k,j}
$$
with distinct $\nu_k\in\mathbb C$. Let $r$ be the largest real part of a $\nu_k$ carrying a nonzero coefficient, let $J$ be the largest $j$ with $A_{k,j}\ne0$ and $\operatorname{Re}\nu_k=r$, and put $C(t)=\sum_{\operatorname{Re}\nu_k=r}e^{i(\operatorname{Im}\nu_k)t}A_{k,J}$, a nonzero matrix-valued trigonometric polynomial. For real $t$, $\|MA(t)N\|_2^2=\operatorname{Tr}(N^*A(t)^*M^*MA(t)N)$ expands into terms $t^{j+j'}e^{(\bar\nu_k+\nu_l)t}$. Every exponent has real part at most $2r$, and the terms with real part $2r$ and degree $2J$ sum to $t^{2J}e^{2rt}g(t)$ with $g(t)=\|MC(t)N\|_2^2$. Since $M,N$ are invertible and $C\not\equiv0$, $g$ is a nonzero trigonometric polynomial, so $Q$ contains a term $t^{2J}e^{(2r+i\eta)t}$ with nonzero coefficient. Every exponent $\nu_k+\nu_l$ of $P$ has real part at most $2r$.

If $1-P/Q=ce^{\lambda t}$ on $I$, then $Q-P=ce^{\lambda t}Q$ on $I$. Both sides are finite linear combinations of the real-analytic functions $t^me^{zt}$, so the identity holds on $\mathbb R$, and linear independence of these functions for distinct pairs $(m,z)$ forces equal coefficients. The right side contains $c\,t^{2J}e^{(2r+\lambda+i\eta)t}$ with nonzero coefficient, whereas every exponent on the left has real part at most $2r<2r+\lambda$. This contradiction proves item 1 in general. For the regularized OTOC, $\mathcal L^*$ preserves self-adjointness, so $A(t)^*=A(t)$ for real $t$; hence $\operatorname{Tr}(y^2A(t)y^2A(t))=\|yA(t)y\|_2^2$, $\operatorname{Tr}(y^2By^2B)=\|yBy\|_2^2>0$, and $\operatorname{Tr}(yA(t)yByA(t)yB)$ is bilinear in $A(t)$.

For item 2, $e^{t\mathcal L^*}\sigma_x=e^{-2\gamma t}\sigma_x$ and $e^{t\mathcal L^*}\sigma_z=\sigma_z$. With $y^4=I/2$, $\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_x\sigma_z\sigma_x\sigma_z)=-2$, $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_z^4=2$ and vanishing mixed traces, $P(t)=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(A(t)\sigma_zA(t)\sigma_z)=1-e^{-4\gamma t}$, while $\operatorname{Tr}(y^2A'(t)y^2A'(t))=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(A'(t)^2)=e^{-4\gamma t}$. Substitution gives (F.10.4b.7c.3). ∎

<a id="lemma-f104b80-metric-clock-and-closed-strip-comparison"></a>**Lemma F.10.4b.8.0 (Metric Clock and Closed-Strip Comparison).**

**Metric clock and discrete reconstruction.** Restore $c$ and $\hbar$. The orbit $ct(s)=\rho\sinh s$, $x(s)=\rho\cosh s$ has
$$
c^2d\tau^2=c^2dt^2-dx^2=\rho^2ds^2,\qquad
\kappa=\frac{c^2}{\rho},\qquad
\alpha_\tau^{\mathrm{phys}}=\alpha_{c\tau/\rho},\qquad
\sigma_u^\varphi=\alpha_{-2\pi\rho u/c}^{\mathrm{phys}}.
\tag{F.10.4b.8.0.8}
$$
This proves the proper-time and temperature formulas, with $e^{i\tau H_\chi/\hbar}=U(\Lambda(c\tau/\rho))$. The metric, orbit and registered units define the clock before the BW identity supplies its thermal period. The inverse temperature is unique: trivial boost action on the wedge would, by separation and vacuum invariance, make $U$ trivial on the dense set $\mathfrak M(W)\Omega$. A different orbit radius specifies a different observer and proper clock.

For an independently calibrated chart and tick sequence, let $a_n\to0$, $\tau_n=a_n/c$, and choose integers $N_n\to\infty$ with $h_n=N_n\tau_n\to0$. For a one-axis $C^2$ trajectory $x(t)\in\mathbb R$ on a compact coordinate-time window with $|x'(t)|\le v_*<c$, round the sampled position to the length lattice:
$$
x_{n,j}=a_n\operatorname{round}(x(jh_n)/a_n),\qquad
v_{n,j}=\frac{x_{n,j+1}-x_{n,j}}{h_n},\qquad
|v_{n,j}-x'(jh_n)|\le\frac12\|x''\|_\infty h_n+\frac{a_n}{h_n}=:\varepsilon_n\longrightarrow0.
\tag{F.10.4b.8.0.9}
$$
The two scale conditions imply $a_n/h_n=c/N_n\to0$. For large $n$ the integer displacement is realizable by at most $N_n$ nearest-neighbor hops, with idle ticks filling the block. Define
$$
\tau_n^{\mathrm{rec}}=\sum_j h_n\sqrt{1-v_{n,j}^2/c^2}.
\tag{F.10.4b.8.0.10}
$$
On $|v|\le(c+v_*)/2$, the proper-time integrand is Lipschitz. Equation (F.10.4b.8.0.9), the Riemann-sum error and a separately bounded last partial interval give
$$
\left|\tau_n^{\mathrm{rec}}-\int\sqrt{1-x'(t)^2/c^2}\,dt\right|
\le C_T(h_n+a_n/h_n).
$$
For $x(t)=\sqrt{\rho^2+c^2t^2}$ this tends to $(\rho/c)\operatorname{arsinh}(ct/\rho)$, independently of the grouping sequence satisfying the two scale conditions. The reconstructed metric clock uses the supplied chart and tick units. A sum of microscopic light-speed-hop and rest-tick proper intervals instead gives $t(1-|v|/c)$ at monotone average velocity $v$, which differs strictly from $t\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}$ when $0<|v|<c$. Thus the two clock constructions have different limiting readouts. ∎

For the uniformly bounded difference of finite and limiting strip functions, the subharmonic maximum principle bounds its modulus by the harmonic-measure average of its two boundary moduli. Given a compact horizontal window, choose a larger boundary window so that the strip Poisson kernel's remote tails have uniformly small mass at all heights. Then use uniform convergence on the larger retained window; on the strip boundary use the boundary estimates directly. This proves compact uniform convergence on the closed strip, including both edges.

For products, expand a telescoping difference and charge each factor error on the corresponding intermediate input vector, multiplied by the other factor norms. Include these vectors in the finite grammar. Fixed finite matrix amplifications are treated entrywise or on their amplified vectors with the resulting finite norm bound. Direct the approximations by finite local words and adjoint words, finite ancillary dimension, compact boost windows and tolerance. A countable chosen grammar admits a diagonal sequence. This controls the specified responses rather than the full observable unit ball or an unbounded spectator. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104b8a-finite-car-realization-of-a-geometric-wedge-kms-flow"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.8a (Finite CAR Realization of a Geometric Wedge KMS Flow).** On the massive free-Dirac branch, let $\mathcal K=L^2(\{x^1>0\},\mathbb C^4)$ be the right-half-space Cauchy Hilbert space, let $C$ be the negative-energy vacuum covariance compressed to $\mathcal K$, and let $\omega_C$ be its gauge-invariant quasifree state. Fix the wedge-preserving geometric Lorentz boost before analyzing the state. Then $\ker C=\ker(I-C)=0$, the operator $h=\log[(I-C)/C]$ is self-adjoint on its maximal spectral domain, and the geometric one-particle boost is $v(s)=e^{ish/(2\pi)}$.

For increasing finite-dimensional $\mathcal K_n$ with dense union, the compressed covariances $C_n=P_nCP_n|_{\mathcal K_n}$ define faithful exactly compatible states on $\mathfrak A_n=\operatorname{CAR}(\mathcal K_n)$. Their norm inductive limit is $\operatorname{CAR}(\mathcal K)$. With $h_n=\log[(I-C_n)/C_n]$ and $\tau_U=2\pi\rho/c$ fixed by the metric proper time $\tau=\rho s/c$, the finite states are KMS for the Hamiltonians $(\hbar/\tau_U)d\Gamma(h_n)$ at inverse energy temperature $\tau_U/\hbar$. The finite dynamics converge in operator norm on every fixed CAR polynomial, uniformly on compact proper-time windows, with the analytic-core and closed-strip limits proved below. The vacuum von Neumann wedge state is normal and faithful; the physical, modular and Gaussian reversible generators have the stated common spectral graph cores. Even observables have ordinary spacelike locality on their cyclic even GNS space.

*Proof.* In natural units the all-space Cauchy Hilbert space is $\mathcal K_{\mathrm{all}}=L^2(\mathbb R^3,\mathbb C^4)$, with Dirac Hamiltonian $H_D=-i\alpha\cdot\nabla+m\beta$, $m>0$. The Hermitian Dirac matrices satisfy $\{\alpha^i,\alpha^j\}=2\delta_{ij}I$, $\{\alpha^i,\beta\}=0$ and $\beta^2=I$. The negative-energy projection and compressed covariance are
$$
P_-(p)=\frac12\left[I-\frac{\alpha\cdot p+m\beta}{\sqrt{|p|^2+m^2}}\right],\qquad
C=\chi_+P_-\chi_+|_{\mathcal K}.
\tag{F.10.4b.8a-C1}
$$
Zero extension identifies $\mathcal K$ with a subspace of $\mathcal K_{\mathrm{all}}$. Use annihilators antilinear in $f$, with $\{a(f),a(g)^*\}=\langle f,g\rangle I$, $\{a(f),a(g)\}=0$, and occupation convention $\omega_C(a^*(f)a(g))=\langle g,Cf\rangle$. Then $\|a(f)\|=\|f\|$. The positive-energy projection would give the complementary two-point ordering.

The vacuum restriction is the quasifree state whose higher moments are Wick determinants of $C$. The Dirac time-slice construction identifies $\operatorname{CAR}(\mathcal K)$ with the norm field algebra of the right wedge: solve the Cauchy equation, use finite propagation and conserved current, and generate compact half-space Cauchy data by spacetime smearings with a time cutoff inside the wedge. Its vacuum weak closure is the field wedge $\mathfrak F(W)$ with graded locality. The free Dirac spectrum condition, wedge Reeh--Schlieder standardness and fermionic BW theorem give cyclic separation and
$$
\sigma_u^{\omega_C}=\alpha_{-2\pi u}^{\mathrm{geom}}.
\tag{F.10.4b.8a-C3}
$$
The fermionic BW theorem is the imported geometric input (Bisognano and Wichmann 1976). Araki's quasifree construction supplies the modular standard representation (Araki 1970). The geometric Cauchy action $v(s)$ is defined by solving the Dirac equation, applying the Lorentz spinor transformation and restricting to the right half-space at time zero. Current conservation makes it unitary; finite propagation and wedge preservation make it a strongly continuous group on $\mathcal K$.

If $Cf=0$, then $a(f)\Omega=0$, so separation and the CAR norm give $f=0$. Applying the same argument to $a^*(f)$ proves $\ker(I-C)=0$. Thus every nonzero finite compression lies strictly between zero and the identity. Spectral calculus defines
$$
h=\log[(I-C)/C],\qquad
\operatorname{Dom}h=\left\{f:\int_{[0,1]}\left|\log\frac{1-\lambda}{\lambda}\right|^2
\,d\langle f,E_C(\lambda)f\rangle<\infty\right\}.
\tag{F.10.4b.8a-C4}
$$
It is densely defined and self-adjoint. The quasifree modular formula is
$$
\sigma_u(a(f))=a(e^{-iuh}f).
\tag{F.10.4b.8a-C5}
$$
For one mode of occupation $c$, the density $\operatorname{diag}(1-c,c)$ has $h=\log((1-c)/c)$ and sends $a$ to $e^{\mathrm{iuh}}a$ under modular conjugation. Antilinearity of $a(f)$ gives exactly (F.10.4b.8a-C5); finite-mode diagonalization and the standard representation give the general formula. Comparing (F.10.4b.8a-C3) and (F.10.4b.8a-C5), injectivity of $f\mapsto a(f)$ gives the equality of groups, hence of generators and domains,
$$
v(s)=e^{ish/(2\pi)}.
\tag{F.10.4b.8a-C6}
$$
For $x^1=\rho\cosh s$, $ct=\rho\sinh s$, the independent metric clock of Lemma F.10.4b.8.0 gives
$$
\alpha_\tau^{\mathrm{phys}}=\alpha_{c\tau/\rho}^{\mathrm{geom}},\quad
\tau_U=2\pi\rho/c,\quad
\beta_{\mathrm{energy}}=\tau_U/\hbar,\quad
T_U=\hbar c/(2\pi k_B\rho).
\tag{F.10.4b.8a-C7}
$$

**Exact finite states and norm controls.** The algebra/state and norm-dynamics argument applies to any increasing dense sequence of finite-dimensional spans. For regional localization choose the $\mathcal K_n$ as spans of an increasing complete family of compactly supported smooth half-space spinors; Gram--Schmidt changes the bases without changing the spans. Set
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak A_n&=\operatorname{CAR}(\mathcal K_n)\cong M_{2^{\dim\mathcal K_n}},\\
C_n&=P_nCP_n|_{\mathcal K_n},\quad 0<C_n<I,\quad
h_n=\log[(I-C_n)/C_n],\\
D_n&=\det(I-C_n)e^{-d\Gamma(h_n)},\qquad
H_n=\frac{\hbar}{\tau_U}d\Gamma(h_n).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.10.4b.8a-C9}
$$
In a $C_n$ eigenbasis, $D_n$ is a product of $\operatorname{diag}(1-c_a,c_a)$, hence faithful of trace one. Its Wick determinants equal the original state's determinants on $\mathcal K_n$. Therefore these states are exactly $\omega_C|_{\mathfrak A_n}$ and are exactly compatible under the isometric unital CAR embeddings. The norm limit is the UHF algebra $\operatorname{CAR}(\mathcal K)$ with the specified vacuum weak closure.

Extend $C_n$ by $I/2$ on $\mathcal K_n^\perp$ to obtain $\widetilde C_n=P_nCP_n+(I-P_n)/2\to C$ strongly, and let $\widetilde h_n=h_n\oplus0$. The continuous endpoint-zero function
$$
g(\lambda)=\left[\log\frac{1-\lambda}{\lambda}-i\right]^{-1},\quad
g(0)=g(1)=0
$$
gives $g(\widetilde C_n)=(\widetilde h_n-i)^{-1}\to(h-i)^{-1}$ strongly. Thus $\widetilde h_n\to h$ in strong resolvent sense. Compact-time unitary convergence and $P_n\to I$ imply
$$
\varepsilon_n(f,T):=\sup_{|\tau|\le T}
\|e^{i\tau h_n/\tau_U}P_nf-e^{i\tau h/\tau_U}f\|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{F.10.4b.8a-C10}
$$
Since $\alpha_{n,\tau}(a(f_n))=a(e^{i\tau h_n/\tau_U}f_n)$, the CAR norm makes this exactly the annihilator's operator-norm error. For a word $X=a^{\#}(f_1)\cdots a^{\#}(f_r)$, with $X_n$ made from $P_nf_j$, telescoping yields
$$
\sup_{|\tau|\le T}\|\alpha_{n,\tau}(X_n)-\alpha_\tau^{\mathrm{phys}}(X)\|
\le\sum_{j=1}^r\varepsilon_n(f_j,T)\prod_{k\ne j}\|f_k\|.
\tag{F.10.4b.8a-C11}
$$
Finite sums with matrix coefficients cost the coefficient norms, so the same bound covers every fixed finite ancillary system. It is a word-response estimate rather than a unit-ball completely bounded approximation.

Finite-stage words have exact representatives. General vectors give compatible families because $\sup_{m\ge n}\|P_mf-P_nf\|\le\|(I-P_n)f\|$. The CAR inclusion maps have zero multiplicativity/coherence defects; their dynamical compatibility defects tend to zero by (F.10.4b.8a-C11). Vector substitution $a(f)\mapsto a(P_nf)$ changes the CAR scalar term and is a word approximant, not a homomorphism on the full algebra. A representation-independent preparation is the UCP trace-complement expectation onto $\mathfrak A_n$ in the finite-mode CAR decomposition. It fixes $\mathfrak A_n$ and tends point-norm to the identity by density; its multiplicativity defect consequently tends to zero. Its normality or global vacuum preservation on the von Neumann closure is unnecessary, because exact state compatibility is supplied by restrictions and Wick determinants. Finite boosts are asymptotically, rather than exactly, refinement compatible.

**Analytic algebra, graph representatives and KMS strip.** The union of bounded spectral subspaces $\operatorname{Ran}1_{[-R,R]}(h)$ is dense in $\mathcal K$. CAR polynomials in those vectors form an invariant entire analytic *-algebra norm dense in $\operatorname{CAR}(\mathcal K)$, since $\|e^{\mathrm{izh}}f\|\le e^{R|\operatorname{Im}z|}\|f\|$ on each such subspace. Because annihilation is antilinear, its holomorphic proper-time continuation is $a(e^{i\overline z h/\tau_U}f)$; creation uses $a^*(e^{izh/\tau_U}f)$.

For $f\in\operatorname{Dom}h$ choose
$$
f_n=(h_n-i)^{-1}P_n(h-i)f.
$$
Resolvent convergence gives $f_n\to f$ and $h_nf_n=P_n(h-i)f+if_n\to hf$. Thus annihilators and their generator values converge in norm on varying graph representatives. Bounded Gaussian spectral filters give joint analytic approximants; their polynomially weighted values also converge by bounded functional calculus. This provides graph recovery without assuming fixed-vector cofinal domain equality.

Each finite state is exactly KMS at imaginary proper-time width $\tau_U$. The finite strip functions are bounded by the product of their word norms. Exact state restriction, (F.10.4b.8a-C11) and norm approximation of analytic words give uniform convergence on compact parts of both strip boundaries. The Poisson-kernel argument of Lemma F.10.4b.8.0 gives compact uniform convergence on the closed strip. The present free-Dirac construction retains no noncentral additive $K_{\mathrm{PCE}}$ contribution: its retained contribution in Theorem F.10.3(4) is zero, and an added central scalar would cancel from conjugation. Thus the stated thermal/norm hypotheses of F.10.3 are populated on this flat wedge core; source identification is a separate requirement.

**Canonical implementations and exact domains.** In the Araki--Wyss standard representation on $\Gamma_-(\mathcal K\oplus\overline{\mathcal K})$, the left CAR fields have coefficient vectors built from $(I-C)^{1/2}f$ and $C^{1/2}f$. The vacuum is cyclic separating because both endpoint kernels vanish. Its implementations are
$$
U_\tau=\Gamma_-(e^{i\tau h/\tau_U}\oplus e^{-i\tau\overline h/\tau_U}),\qquad
\log\Delta=d\Gamma(-h\oplus\overline h).
\tag{F.10.4b.8a-C12}
$$
Embed finite standard representations by their finite doubled Fock spaces. Strong convergence of $\widetilde C_n$ and its square roots gives norm convergence of represented field coefficients. Strong convergence of one-particle unitaries gives strong convergence of second quantizations, first on finite wedges of vectors and then on all Fock space by unitarity. These are canonical representations of the varying quasifree states; an arbitrary full-CAR preparation is not substituted for the vacuum-fixing implementation.

The differential boost and Weyl sequences in Theorem F.10.4b.8b give $\sigma(h)=\mathbb R$. Put $B=(2\pi)^{-1}d\Gamma(h\oplus-\overline h)$. Its domain and that of $L=-B^2$ are respectively the maximal spectral domains $\int\lambda^2\,d\|E_B(\lambda)\xi\|^2<\infty$ and $\int\lambda^4\,d\|E_B(\lambda)\xi\|^2<\infty$. The union
$$
\bigcup_{N,R}P_{\le N}1_{[-R,R]}(B)\mathcal H
$$
is invariant under boosts, modular groups, Gaussian semigroups and their generators. Spectral truncation proves a core in every finite joint graph norm. The powers $\Delta^a=e^{-2\pi aB}$ have their maximal exponentially weighted spectral domains. Gaussian averaging of geometric boosts on $\mathfrak F(W)$ gives normal UCP state-preserving GNS-symmetric dynamics with implementation $e^{-tB^2}$. Its finite averaged controls converge strongly by Gaussian integration of (F.10.4b.8a-C12), with the same normal faithful limiting vacuum.

**Even observables and regional tests.** Let $\mathfrak A^+=\operatorname{CAR}(\mathcal K)^{\mathbb Z_2}$. For $d_n=\dim\mathcal K_n\ge1$, its finite algebra is $M_{2^{d_n-1}}\oplus M_{2^{d_n-1}}$. States and controls restrict faithfully and remain KMS. The parity expectation $(\mathrm{id}+\gamma)/2$ preserves every stage, so finite even algebras are norm dense in $\mathfrak A^+$. Moving odd fields in one even word through a spacelike-separated even word produces an even number of minus signs, proving ordinary commutation. Isotony, spacetime covariance and time-slice localization come from the geometric Dirac field.

Use the cyclic Hilbert space $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{even}}=\overline{\mathfrak A^+\Omega}$ for the observable vacuum representation. The full charged-field Hilbert space is larger. Parity commutes with modular and boost groups, so the restricted state is normal and faithful with the same clock identity. For a countable rational regional base, choose the nested spans to include an enumerated dense family of compact spacetime-smearing/Cauchy vectors in every relatively compact region inside $W$.
