Finite boosts have a regional support-comparison error tending to zero on the retained compact responses by (F.10.4b.8a-C10)--(F.10.4b.8a-C11); they need not map finite regional subspaces exactly.

The logarithmic matrices $h_n$ are generally nonlocal in this localized basis. For example, the covariance $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&a\end{pmatrix}$ with $b\ne0$ has a nonzero off-diagonal logarithmic odds, because $x\mapsto\log((1-x)/x)$ is strictly decreasing. The exact-state-compatible construction therefore has a different control record from the nearest-neighbor construction below. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104b8b-geometry-first-local-car-regulator-with-charged-response-errors"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.8b (Geometry-First Local CAR Regulator with Charged Response Errors).** In dimensionless coordinates $x^1=\ell e^y$, $x^\perp=\ell z$, the massive Dirac boost is the closure on $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3,\mathbb C^4)$ of
$$
K=-i\alpha^1\partial_y+e^y(-i\alpha^2\partial_{z^2}-i\alpha^3\partial_{z^3}+m\ell\beta).
\tag{F.10.4b.8b-L2}
$$
Its spectrum is $\mathbb R$. The nested dyadic cell construction below supplies finite Hermitian nearest-neighbor fermionic controls $K_n$ and faithful states $D_n=Z_n^{-1}e^{-2\pi d\Gamma(K_n)}$, with physical Hamiltonians $H_n=(\hbar c/\rho)d\Gamma(K_n)$. They are exactly KMS at $\beta_{\mathrm{energy}}=2\pi\rho/(\hbar c)$. Equations (F.10.4b.8b-L5)--(F.10.4b.8b-L11) give explicit operator-norm response and state errors on fixed smooth compact responses and their norm closure. The finite states are asymptotically compatible and have the common closed-strip KMS limit. Every finite mode, including high-frequency branches, remains in the source and its resource count.

*Proof.* Differentiate the geometric Lorentz action on Dirac solutions, including the spinor factor. On compact smooth half-space Cauchy data this gives
$$
K_B=\tfrac12(x^1H_D+H_Dx^1)
=-i\alpha^1(x^1\partial_1+\tfrac12)
+x^1(-i\alpha^2\partial_2-i\alpha^3\partial_3+m\beta).
\tag{F.10.4b.8b-L1}
$$
Its group is the independently defined $v(s)$ in Theorem F.10.4b.8a. Finite propagation and a finite Lorentz transformation carry compact Cauchy supports to compact Cauchy supports at positive distance from the horizon; smoothness is preserved. The compact-smooth domain is therefore dense, invariant and differentiable for this group. To verify its core property, approximate a vector by compact-smooth vectors and average against a compact smooth group kernel. The orbit supports over the kernel's compact time support are jointly compact, so the averages remain compact smooth. Differentiating the kernel gives simultaneous convergence of each average and its generator value. Approximate identities then recover every generator-domain vector in graph norm. Thus the closure of (F.10.4b.8b-L1) is exactly the self-adjoint geometric generator.

Choose the registered reference length $\ell>0$ and write $\mu=m\ell$. Multiplication of the transformed spinor by $\ell^{3/2}e^{y/2}$ makes the coordinate change unitary on the Cauchy norm and gives (F.10.4b.8b-L2) on $L^2(\mathbb R^3_{y,z},\mathbb C^4)$. Take normalized approximate plane waves in $y$ in the $+1$ eigenspace of $\alpha^1$, with increasing support width, bounded transverse momentum, and centers tending sufficiently rapidly to $y=-\infty$. Derivative cutoff errors tend to zero and $e^y$ suppresses the transverse and mass terms. These are Weyl sequences at each prescribed real boost frequency, so $\sigma(K)=\mathbb R$. The physical one-particle generator is $(\hbar c/\rho)K$, with proper time and thermal period already fixed by (F.10.4b.8a-C7).

**Finite matrices, exact boundary convention and cost.** Take $a_n=2^{-n}$ and $B_n=[-n,n]^3$, partitioned into cubes of side $a_n$. Let $\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{lat}}$ be the spinor cell space with its ordinary $\ell^2$ norm. The isometry $I_n$ sends cell coefficients to normalized piecewise-constant spinors; $E_n=I_n^*$ is scaled cell averaging, and $P_n=I_nE_n\to I$ strongly. The ranges are nested. There are
$$
q_n=4(2n2^n)^3
$$
one-particle modes and the full finite Fock algebra is $M_{2^{q_n}}$. The induced CAR embeddings are exact.

For each coordinate, let $S_j$ be the forward cell shift with zero outside $B_n$, set $D_{j,n}=(S_j-S_j^*)/(2a_n)$, and let $Y_n$ multiply by the exponential of the cell-center $y$ coordinate. Define
$$
K_n=-i\alpha^1D_{1,n}-iY_n\alpha^2D_{2,n}-iY_n\alpha^3D_{3,n}+\mu Y_n\beta.
\tag{F.10.4b.8b-L3}
$$
The difference matrices are skew-Hermitian, $Y_n$ commutes with transverse shifts, and the spin matrices commute with cell operators, so each term is Hermitian. Zero-extension is part of the finite definition; it assumes no self-adjoint continuum first-order boundary condition on a fixed finite box. The box boundary moves beyond the collar of every fixed response. The Hamiltonian and state are
$$
H_n=\frac{\hbar c}{\rho}d\Gamma(K_n),\qquad
D_n=Z_n^{-1}e^{-2\pi d\Gamma(K_n)},\qquad
C_n=(I+e^{2\pi K_n})^{-1}.
\tag{F.10.4b.8b-L4}
$$
These define every mode and occupation. The finite Gibbs state is faithful and KMS at the displayed inverse energy temperature. The control matrix was specified geometrically before the state. The CAR Hamiltonian is a finite sum of even on-site and nearest-neighbor quadratic terms. An exact Jordan--Wigner encoding into ordinary tensor registers can introduce long parity strings in three dimensions; a same-radius tensor-MPU circuit requires an additional encoding/control record.

**Smooth-response consistency.** Retain prescribed $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3,\mathbb C^4)$ and their finite CAR words, with the boost orbit $|s|\le T$. Its supports are jointly compact and its required derivatives uniformly bounded. Choose $n$ so that the support and one stencil collar lie inside $B_n$, and let $Y$ bound its $y$ support. For every such smooth $g$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\|K_nE_ng-E_nKg\|\le{}&\frac{a_n^2}{6}
\left[\|\partial_y^3g\|+e^{Y+a_n}(\|\partial_{z^2}^3g\|+\|\partial_{z^3}^3g\|)\right]\\
&+\frac{a_ne^{Y+a_n}}2
\left[\|\partial_{z^2}g\|+\|\partial_{z^3}g\|+\mu\|g\|\right]
=:r_n(g).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.10.4b.8b-L5}
$$
All norms on the right are continuum $L^2$ norms. Away from the zero boundary collar,
$$
D_{j,n}E_ng=E_n\frac{g(\cdot+a_ne_j)-g(\cdot-a_ne_j)}{2a_n}.
$$
Taylor's centered-difference remainder costs $a_n^2\|\partial_j^3g\|/6$, using contractivity of cell averaging. The multiplier difference is at most $(a_n/2)e^{Y+a_n}$, which gives the second line of (F.10.4b.8b-L5). Cellwise Poincaré gives
$$
\|I_nE_ng-g\|\le\frac{a_n}{\pi}\|\nabla g\|.
\tag{F.10.4b.8b-L6}
$$
Set $R_n(f,T)=\sup_{|s|\le T}r_n(v(s)f)$ and $G(f,T)=\sup_{|s|\le T}\|\nabla v(s)f\|$. Duhamel integration of the finite versus averaged continuum evolution yields
$$
\sup_{|s|\le T}\|I_ne^{isK_n}E_nf-v(s)f\|
\le T R_n(f,T)+\frac{a_n}{\pi}G(f,T)
=:\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{geom}}(f,T)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{F.10.4b.8b-L7}
$$
Every constant is a seminorm of the actual compact geometric orbit. CAR word telescoping (F.10.4b.8a-C11), with $s=c\tau/\rho$, gives the operator-norm errors for sums and products, including fixed finite ancillary matrix coefficients with their norms charged.

Extend $I_nK_nE_n$ by zero on $P_n^\perp$. Equations (F.10.4b.8b-L5)--(F.10.4b.8b-L6), also applied to $Kg$, imply convergence to $K$ on its compact-smooth core. The self-adjoint core-convergence theorem gives strong-resolvent convergence. Unitary bounds and norm approximation therefore extend the limit to each fixed $L^2$ spinor; the displayed rate belongs to the smooth grammar. The zero complement is a comparison operator, rather than an additional band of the physical finite source.

**Covariance and state errors.** Equations (F.10.4b.8a-C3)--(F.10.4b.8a-C6) identify the actual transformed wedge covariance as
$$
C=(I+e^{2\pi K})^{-1}.
\tag{F.10.4b.8b-L8}
$$
Bounded continuous functional calculus with spectral cutoffs gives $I_nC_nE_n+(I-P_n)/2\to C$ strongly, hence convergence of every fixed Wick determinant. The scalar integral identity $\int_0^\infty\sin(tx)/\sinh(t/2)\,dt=\pi\tanh(\pi x)$ gives, on the smooth domain,
$$
C=\tfrac12I-\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^\infty\frac{\sin(tK)}{\sinh(t/2)}\,dt.
\tag{F.10.4b.8b-L9}
$$
Near zero the domain condition makes the integral convergent; its tail is exponentially integrable. The finite formula is identical. For $0<t\le T$, Duhamel bounds the finite-versus-averaged sine difference by $tR_n(f,T)$, and for $t>T$ contractivity bounds it by $2\|f\|$. Since
$$
\int_0^\infty\frac{t}{\sinh(t/2)}\,dt=\pi^2,\qquad
\int_T^\infty\frac{dt}{\sinh(t/2)}=-2\log\tanh(T/4),
$$
one obtains
$$
\|C_nE_nf-E_nCf\|
\le\frac\pi2R_n(f,T)-\frac{2\|f\|}{\pi}\log\tanh(T/4)
=:b_n(f,T).
\tag{F.10.4b.8b-L10}
$$
Choose $T$ to control the tail, then $n$ to control $R_n$. For a second smooth test $g$, projection and Cauchy--Schwarz give
$$
|\langle E_ng,C_nE_nf\rangle-\langle g,Cf\rangle|
\le\|g\|b_n(f,T)+\frac{a_n}{\pi}\|\nabla g\|\,\|f\|.
\tag{F.10.4b.8b-L11}
$$
For normalized vectors, the permutation formula bounds the difference of $r\times r$ Wick determinants by $r\,r!$ times the largest entry error; unnormalized vectors retain their product-of-norm factors.

For a trace-norm comparison on a fixed $r$-mode algebra, first identify modes exactly. Choose orthonormal smooth $f_1,\ldots,f_r$, let $F_n$ have columns $E_nf_i$, and put $G_n=F_n^*F_n$. Then
$$
\gamma_n=\|I-G_n\|\le\sum_i\|(I-P_n)f_i\|^2
\le(a_n/\pi)^2\sum_i\|\nabla f_i\|^2.
$$
When $\gamma_n<1/2$, the vectors $g_{n,i}=F_nG_n^{-1/2}e_i$ are orthonormal. Their distance from $E_nf_i$ is at most $(1-\gamma_n)^{-1/2}-1\le2\gamma_n$. Since $\|C_n\|\le1$, the covariance entry errors increase by at most $4\gamma_n$. The resulting mode map is an exact CAR *-embedding. Write matrix-unit expectations as finite Wick polynomials and apply their coefficient-weighted determinant bounds. If $\delta_n$ bounds each resulting density-matrix entry error, Hilbert--Schmidt comparison gives trace-norm error at most $(2^r)^{3/2}\delta_n$. Thus the trace-norm claim uses canonical orthonormal modes, rather than silently identifying nonorthogonal averages with them.

The finite KMS functions obey the common norm bound. Equations (F.10.4b.8b-L7), (F.10.4b.8b-L11), state convergence and polynomial telescoping give compact uniform convergence on both boundaries. The strip Poisson argument gives compact uniform closed-strip convergence. The analytic core and varying generator-graph representatives follow as in Theorem F.10.4b.8a. State compatibility here is asymptotic, in contrast to the exact restrictions of (F.10.4b.8a-C9).

**Retained modes and physical budgets.** The infinite uniform-grid centered-difference symbol is $\sin(a_np)/a_n$, with extra zeros near the Brillouin-zone edge. All these finite branches are present in $K_n$, $H_n$, $D_n$ and the dimension count. An $n$-dependent alternating cell vector has a divergent third-derivative budget and is outside the uniform smooth estimate (F.10.4b.8b-L5). Under the specified nested cell identifications such alternating vectors do not make a norm-compatible family; a different continuum interpretation needs a new interpolation and retained-source record. Their presence is fully charged, rather than treated as physical response-nullity.

The resource record includes all $q_n$ modes, full $2^{q_n}$ Fock dimension, every nearest-neighbor entry, box and collar, actual derivative seminorms, boost-time window and thermal tail. The nonzero longitudinal derivative spin blocks have operator norm $\hbar c/(2\rho a_n)$, the nonzero transverse derivative spin blocks have operator norm $\hbar c e^{y_c}/(2\rho a_n)$, and the on-site mass term has operator norm $\hbar c\mu e^{y_c}/\rho$. The derivative couplings grow with refinement, and the exponential factors grow with box size. Therefore this construction supplies finite nearest-neighbor fermionic controls and the F.10.1/F.10.3 norm/KMS comparison on its declared grammar; the resolution-independent physical interaction norms of F.0(1), the complete finite-source regional/time-slice/Lieb--Robinson package of F.10.2, same-radius tensor-register locality, and UV/current/source-exhaustion records are separate, stronger source predicates. The exact causal locality of the limiting free field follows from its independent geometric construction. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104b8c-bounded-radius-tensor-realization-of-the-geometric-dirac-source"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.8c (Bounded-Radius Tensor Realization of the Geometric Dirac Source).** Fix the flat massive Dirac wedge, lengths $\ell,\rho>0$, geometric boost $K_B$, and proper time $\tau=\rho s/c$ of Theorems F.10.4b.8a–F.10.4b.8b. The following ordinary tensor source realizes every finite even-CAR control of (F.10.4b.8b-L3), including both original parity sectors, with bounded-radius Hamiltonian terms and the same physical clock. It uses the retained-response route F.10.1/F.10.3, with all inverse-mesh energies retained.

**Carrier and parity.** Use the bounded-degree edge encoding of Bravyi and Kitaev (2002), with its parity and locality verification supplied below. Put a $K_4$ on the four modes of every cell and a $K_{4,4}$ between neighboring cells. Attach one extra parity-reservoir mode $0$ by a leaf edge. The graph has $q_n+1$ vertices, maximum degree $D\le28$, and
$$
 e_n=6N_n+16L_n+1,\qquad q_n=4N_n,\qquad r_n^{\rm g}=e_n-q_n,
 \tag{F.10.4b.8c.1}
$$
where $N_n=(2n2^n)^3$ and $L_n$ counts neighboring cell pairs. Every edge, including edges unused by $K_n$, carries an ordinary qubit at its midpoint. On its full $2^{e_n}$-dimensional tensor carrier, order incident edges at each vertex and set
$$
 B_i=\prod_{e\ni i}Z_e,\quad
 A_{ij}=\epsilon_{ij}X_{ij}
 \prod_{e<_i ij}Z_e\prod_{e<_j ij}Z_e,
 \quad\epsilon_{ij}=-\epsilon_{ji}\in\{\pm1\}.
 \tag{F.10.4b.8c.2}
$$
The edge subscript is unordered except on $A_{ij}$. For an oriented length-$p$ cycle $C$, let
$S_C=i^p\prod_{(ij)\in C}A_{ij}$ in cyclic order. Choose an independent cycle basis from onsite triangles, cycles of length at most four replacing intercell edges through one distinguished mode per cell, and elementary square plaquettes of the distinguished-mode cubic lattice. The common $+1$ eigenspace $\mathcal C_n$ has dimension $2^{q_n}$. There is a unitary
$$
 V_n:\mathcal F(\mathbb C^{q_n})\longrightarrow\mathcal C_n
 \tag{F.10.4b.8c.3}
$$
identifying $B_i=-i\gamma_i\eta_i$ and $A_{ij}=-i\gamma_i\gamma_j$ on the total-even sector of $q_n+1$ fermion modes. The extra occupation equals the original $q_n$-mode parity. Thus the representation $\pi_n$ of the original even CAR algebra is faithful on both central parity blocks, each of dimension $2^{q_n-1}$. Even monomials supported on a connected cell set have representatives supported on its one-cell collar: pair their Majoranas and join each pair by a path in that set. Distinct paths agree on $\mathcal C_n$. For a norm-controlled full-carrier lift of a regional smeared even word, choose a spanning tree of its connected cell-mode subgraph and extend it to a spanning tree of $G_n$. Use its $A$ generators and all $B_i$ to represent the total-even Clifford algebra. Tree generators have no cycle relation beyond the Clifford relations, so on the full carrier this is a direct sum of $2^{r_n^{\rm g}}$ faithful copies of $M_{2^{q_n}}$. Consequently the lift has exactly the original even-CAR norm, independent of the number of cell coefficients. Regional paths stay in the chosen regional tree. Different tree lifts agree on the code and retain their explicit gauge-sector comparison off code.

**Hamiltonian.** For $k_{ij}=(K_n)_{ij}=u_{ij}+iv_{ij}$ and one orientation $i<j$, define on the entire qubit carrier
$$
 \widetilde H_n=\frac{\hbar c}{\rho}\left[
 \sum_i\frac{k_{ii}}{2}(I-B_i)
 +\sum_{i<j}\left\{\frac{iu_{ij}}{2}A_{ij}(B_i-B_j)
 -\frac{v_{ij}}{2}A_{ij}(I-B_iB_j)\right\}\right].
 \tag{F.10.4b.8c.4}
$$
Every summand commutes with the cycle stabilizers and
$V_n^*\widetilde H_nV_n=(\hbar c/\rho)d\Gamma(K_n)$.
The state update is $U\varrho U^*$ and Heisenberg update is $U^*AU$, where $U=e^{-i\tau\widetilde H_n/\hbar}$. The code preparation $V_nD_nV_n^*$ is faithful on the full original Fock carrier and exactly KMS at $\beta_E=2\pi\rho/(\hbar c)$.

If a faithful state on every gauge sector is retained, use
$$
 H_n^{\rm all}=\widetilde H_n+\frac{\Delta_n}{2}\sum_{C\in\mathcal B_n}(I-S_C),
 \qquad\Sigma_n=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta_EH_n^{\rm all}}.
 \tag{F.10.4b.8c.5}
$$
Its conditional code state is exactly $V_nD_nV_n^*$. With $\mathcal H_n=\|\widetilde H_n\|$,
$$
 p_n^{\rm bad}\le(2^{r_n^{\rm g}}-1)e^{-\beta_E\Delta_n+2\beta_E\mathcal H_n}.
 \tag{F.10.4b.8c.6}
$$
Taking $\Delta_n\ge2\mathcal H_n+\beta_E^{-1}(r_n^{\rm g}\log2+\log\eta_n^{-1})$ bounds this probability by $\eta_n$. Every norm-$M$ retained representative then has expectation error at most $2M\eta_n$. Both finite references are exactly KMS for their stated Hamiltonians and use the same $\beta_E\hbar$; the gauge penalty and every off-code sector are charged.

**Physical locality.** The line graph of edge qubits has degree at most $2D-2$. Each nonconstant Pauli term in (F.10.4b.8c.4) has at most $2D$ qubits, line-graph diameter at most three, and at most $\nu=8D+2$ terms meet an edge qubit. In a fixed compact buffer $y\le Y$, a valid energy bound per term is
$$
 J_{n,Y}=\frac{\hbar c}{\rho}
 \left[\frac{1+2e^{Y+a_n}}{ a_n}+\mu e^{Y+a_n}\right],
 \quad\mu=m\ell,\quad
 \delta_{n,Y}=\ell a_n\max\{e^{Y+a_n},1\}.
 \tag{F.10.4b.8c.7}
$$
Line-graph neighbors are separated by at most $\delta_{n,Y}$ in the physical $t=0$ slice. Set $\kappa_{n,Y}=2D\nu eJ_{n,Y}/\hbar$. The buffer-restricted Hamiltonian obeys
$$
 \|[\alpha_{n,\tau}(A),B]\|
 \le2|X|\|A\|\|B\|
 \exp[-d_{\rm line}(X,Z)/3+2\kappa_{n,Y}|\tau|].
 \tag{F.10.4b.8c.8}
$$
Here $X,Z$ are the edge-qubit supports. Its physical speed bound is

$$
v_{n,Y}=6\kappa_{n,Y}\delta_{n,Y},
$$

uniformly finite as $n\to\infty$ at fixed $Y$; the exponent is bounded above by
$-[d_{\rm phys}(X,Z)-v_{n,Y}|\tau|]/(3\delta_{n,Y})$.
The gauge penalty cancels from this bound for retained representatives because it commutes with them and with $\widetilde H_n$.

For the actual expanding-box source, split the Hamiltonian into inside, outside and crossing terms. If there are $N_\partial$ crossing terms, each of norm at most $J_{n,Y}$, and their distance from $X$ is at least $b$, Duhamel comparison gives
$$
 \|\alpha_{n,\tau}(A)-\alpha^{\rm in}_{n,\tau}(A)\|
 \le4|X|\|A\|N_\partial(J_{n,Y}/\hbar)|\tau|
 e^{-b/3+2\kappa_{n,Y}|\tau|}.
 \tag{F.10.4b.8c.9}
$$
The strengths beyond the crossing collar do not enter. The bound applies to buffers exceeding this retained LR distance. Equations (F.10.4b.8c.7)–(F.10.4b.8c.9) keep the inverse-mesh energy and physical units explicitly. The F.10.1/F.10.3 response route has no F.0(1) uniform-strength premise. Literal F.10.2(5) has the additional imported graph-decay and limiting-speed certificate; the above loose velocity does not identify that speed with $c$.

**Preparation, gates and budgets.** Retain $e_n$ edge qubits, the parity-reservoir mode, $r_n^{\rm g}$ gauge checks, $q_n$ thermal occupation bits and their purification/archive bits, and the actual routing, clock and readout workspace. The independent cycle checks together with $q_n$ independent $B_i=+1$ specify the unique encoded vacuum. Symplectic Gaussian elimination prepares it using $O(e_n^2)$ elementary Clifford gates; routing two-qubit gates along a spanning tree uses at most $O(e_n)$ local gates per gate, giving $O(e_n^3)$ bounded-radius gates. This charges the constraint preparation.

Diagonalize the actual Hermitian $K_n$. Prepare independent eigenmode occupations $p_j=(1+e^{2\pi\varepsilon_j})^{-1}$ with purified bits. A controlled path product of $A$ operators changes the chosen mode and reservoir occupancies together. Move the occupation-control bit along the path, or copy its classical basis value to local temporary controls and uncompute them; every edge step is then locally controlled, with its outward and return routing charged. This adds $O(q_ne_n)$ local gates and the actual temporary bits. The number-conserving eigenbasis unitary uses at most $q_n(q_n-1)/2$ Givens rotations. Each distant rotation is routed by fermionic swaps along a graph path and returned; at most $2e_n$ swaps suffice per rotation on a spanning tree. All swaps, rotations and controlled path steps are even local operators represented by (F.10.4b.8c.2). The total finite preparation bound is $O(e_n^3+q_n^2e_n)$ gates and their charged archive/workspace. If the occupation probabilities have total error $\epsilon_p$ and the preparation unitary has operator-norm error $\epsilon_U$, the reduced state has trace-norm error at most $2\epsilon_p+2\epsilon_U$. Exact parameters define its zero-error endpoint. If the optional full-qubit reference $\Sigma_n$ itself is prepared, diagonalize its full $2^{e_n}$-dimensional Hamiltonian, prepare its Schmidt weights on $e_n$ purification qubits, and apply that eigenbasis unitary. QR and two-level elimination, followed by tree routing, give a finite $O(4^{e_n}\operatorname{poly}(e_n))$ local-gate bound; those $e_n$ purifying qubits, all eigenvalue/rotation precision and the full spectral preparation time are additional charged resources. This separate prescription prepares the all-syndrome reference rather than substituting the code preparation for it.

A Pauli rotation $e^{-i\theta P}$ at energy norm $g$ takes time $\hbar|\theta|/g$. For $\widetilde H_n=\sum_{a=1}^{M_n}h_a$, a first-order product formula with $L$ slices over physical duration $T$ has error
$$
 \epsilon_{\rm prod}\le \frac{T^2}{2L\hbar^2}
 \sum_{a<b}\|[h_a,h_b]\|.
 \tag{F.10.4b.8c.10}
$$
To keep the actual duration $T$, assign each of the $M_n$ pulses in a slice duration $T/(LM_n)$ and energy $M_nh_a$. This amplification is charged. Unamplified pulses instead take total time $M_nT$ and define a different slower protocol. Gate synthesis adds the sum of its norm errors. Preparation time is the sum of the actual pulse times, placement includes every routed edge, precision includes each $p_j$ and pulse angle, and the resource record retains the full norms in (F.10.4b.8c.7), the gauge energy $\Delta_n r_n^{\rm g}$, all $q_n$ modes and full $2^{e_n}$ carrier. No efficiency bound is assumed.

*Proof.* At a common vertex exactly the earlier/later incidence produces a Pauli anticommutation. This gives $A_{ij}^2=B_i^2=I$, $A_{ij}=-A_{ji}$, endpoint anticommutation and all disjoint commutations. Every edge occurs twice in $\prod_iB_i$, so that product is $I$. The cycle phase makes $S_C$ Hermitian and central. Its $X$-support modulo two is the graph cycle; independent cycle vectors therefore give independent stabilizers without $-I$. Reducing non-base edges by the stated length-three/four cycles leaves the contractible cubical lattice, whose cycles are generated by its square faces. The stabilizer rank is $e_n-(q_n+1)+1$, proving the dimension.

A proper nonempty product of the $B_i$ has the nonzero $Z$ support of a graph cut; every nonidentity cycle stabilizer has nonzero $X$ support. Its trace against the code projector is zero. Fourier inversion on the commuting $B_i$ group shows that every sign assignment with $\prod_ib_i=1$ has rank one on the code. Edge $A$ operators flip the endpoint signs, and connectedness reaches all assignments. Thus this is the irreducible total-even Clifford representation. Adjoining reservoir occupation equal to original parity supplies (F.10.4b.8c.3), rather than discarding the original odd sector.

Direct Majorana expansion gives
$$
 a_i^*a_j+a_j^*a_i=\frac{i}{2}A_{ij}(B_i-B_j),\quad
 i(a_i^*a_j-a_j^*a_i)=-\frac{1}{2}A_{ij}(I-B_iB_j),
$$
which proves the Hamiltonian identity and both hopping signs. Cycle relations prove path independence on the code. All syndrome sectors have equal dimension $2^{q_n}$; every wrong syndrome costs at least $\Delta_n$, while its remaining energies lie in $[-\mathcal H_n,\mathcal H_n]$. Comparing partition functions proves (F.10.4b.8c.6).

For (F.10.4b.8c.8), iterate the interaction-path commutator inequality. Weight a step by $e^{\operatorname{diam}/3}$; the sum of its support-weighted Hamiltonian norms divided by $\hbar$ at an endpoint is at most $\kappa_{n,Y}$. The nested commutator contributes $2^k$, ordered time integrals contribute $|\tau|^k/k!$, and the starting-point sum contributes $|X|$. Summing gives the displayed exponential. The inside/outside interaction picture removes outside terms, and integration of the bound against each crossing term gives (F.10.4b.8c.9). A two-term Duhamel estimate bounds a Lie-product step by half its squared duration times the commutator sum; unitary telescoping over $L$ steps gives (F.10.4b.8c.10). Preparation follows the stated elimination, parity paths and Givens decomposition. The exact encoding transports the geometric and thermal estimates of Theorem F.10.4b.8b. Every nonempty finite box is a witness. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104b8d-regional-source-comparison-with-charged-spectral-branches"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.8d (Regional Source Comparison with Charged Spectral Branches).** The source of Theorem F.10.4b.8c has a cofinal regional even-CAR comparison on compact smooth Cauchy spinors, finite even words, bounded coefficient sums, compact boost windows and finite compositions of bounded self-adjoint even-word control Hamiltonians and general even-word readouts. Regional covers are connected open covers with a connected overlap graph and nonempty open adjacent overlaps. On this grammar the inclusions, overlaps and refinement compose exactly, states are asymptotically compatible, and the Dirac time-slice and causal responses have the quantitative norm limits below. All lattice modes remain in the physical source.

*Proof.* First take $R$ to be a rational coordinate box, or a finite union of such boxes with a connected graph of positive-open overlaps, compactly contained in the half-space. Let $w_R>0$ be the minimum side length among its boxes and a chosen rational overlap box for every edge of a spanning overlap tree. For $a_n<w_R/4$ and $B_n$ containing their closures, the contained-cell graph is connected: every box has a connected rectangular cell core and each selected overlap contains a common core cell. General connected open regions use directed exhaustion by these finite box unions. For these finite-stage regions, let $\mathcal K_n(R)$ span the spinor cells wholly contained in its coordinate image, using one half-open convention on cell faces, and put $\mathfrak A_n(R)=\operatorname{CAR}(\mathcal K_n(R))^+$. The isometry $J_n^m=E_mI_n$ replaces each coarse cell by the normalized sum of its subcells. It satisfies $J_m^kJ_n^m=J_n^k$. The induced CAR inclusions $j_n^m$ are unital isometric *-monomorphisms preserving regions. Their source maps are
$$
 \pi_mj_n^m\pi_n^{-1}:\pi_n\mathfrak A_n(R)\longrightarrow\pi_m\mathfrak A_m(R).
 \tag{F.10.4b.8d.1}
$$
These are maps on represented retained code algebras, with the bounded-collar full-carrier representatives of Theorem F.10.4b.8c. Compression and preparation supply the physical CP response maps. Equality on the code is the declared response equivalence. Operators resolving different gauge syndromes retain their separate full-source state and cost record; (F.10.4b.8d.1) does not assert norm refinement of every raw edge-qubit observable.

A Majorana monomial basis gives

$$
\mathfrak A_n(R)\cap\mathfrak A_n(S)=\mathfrak A_n(R\cap S),
$$

and these abstract code-algebra overlap/inclusion maps commute with refinement. Support-preserving physical overlap tests use connected overlap boxes or their connected components. If $R\cap S$ is disconnected, its cross-component even bilinears use paths in a declared larger connected region, whose support and routing costs are retained; the displayed full-intersection identity then is an abstract code-algebra identity rather than an intersection-local tensor lift. Cell approximation away from the boundary makes their union norm dense in $\operatorname{CAR}(L^2(R,\mathbb C^4))^+$. For a normalized real Majorana $c(h)=a(h)+a(h)^*$, $c(h)^2=I$. If neighboring cover members have a common normalized $h$, then
$$
 c(f)c(g)=[c(f)c(h)][c(h)c(g)].
 \tag{F.10.4b.8d.2}
$$
Following a chain of overlaps and resolving general compact vectors by a partition of unity proves even-algebra cover generation. At sufficiently fine stages every employed open overlap contains cells, giving the finite comparison. For disconnected covers, $c(f)c(g)$ for $f,g$ in different pieces lies in the union's even algebra but not in the algebra generated by the two separate even algebras. The connected-overlap hypothesis is the exact retained cover condition.

Use the Bessel-potential $H^k$ norm defined by the Fourier weight $(1+|p|^2)^{k/2}$. For uniform error bounds fix compact support with $y\le Y_0$, $H^3$ norm bound $M$, word length bound $d$, and coefficient sum $M_0$. The longitudinal characteristic speed in $s$ is one. Commuting up to $k\le3$ derivatives through (F.10.4b.8b-L2), integration by parts in its symmetric principal part gives the loose bound
$$
 \sup_{|s|\le T}\|v(s)f\|_{H^k}
 \le M_T:=M\exp\{100(1+\mu)4^3e^{Y_0+T}T\}.
 \tag{F.10.4b.8d.3}
$$
Indeed nonzero coefficient derivatives equal $e^y$ and are bounded by $e^{Y_0+T}$; their commutator derivative order on $f$ is at most $k$. The sum of the at most $3\,2^k$ Leibniz terms and the mass terms is bounded by the displayed coefficient. The orbit supports are compact by geometric finite propagation. Smooth approximation proves the same estimate for the indicated Sobolev family.

For $a_n\le1$, set
$$
 c_T=M_T\left[\frac{1+2e^{Y_0+T+1}}{6}
 +\frac{(2+\mu)e^{Y_0+T+1}}{2}\right],\quad

 \tag{F.10.4b.8d.4}
$$
Once the orbit and stencil collar lie in $B_n$, (F.10.4b.8b-L5)–(F.10.4b.8b-L7) give vector error at most $e_n(T)$. Word telescoping gives response error at most
$M_0d\max\{1,M\}^{d-1}e_n(T)$.
Matrix coefficients cost their norms. A control $e^{-itB}$ approximated by $e^{-itB_n}$ adds at most $|t|\|B_n-B\|$ in unitary norm, and at most twice that in a unit-norm response. Finite protocol composition adds these errors and those of every free interval. This is a closed error bound for the declared control/readout grammar.

For a thermal integration cutoff $L\ge2\log2$, (F.10.4b.8b-L10)–(F.10.4b.8b-L11) imply
$$
 b_n(L)\le\frac{\pi}{2}a_nc_L+\frac{8M}{\pi}e^{-L/2},\quad
 d_n(L)\le M b_n(L)+a_nM^2/\pi.

Here $d_n$ bounds a covariance entry; the last term is the projection error for the other vector. A normalized $r\times r$ Wick determinant costs at most $r\,r!$ times the maximal entry error. The fixed-$r$-mode trace-norm version uses the actual Gram normalization in Theorem F.10.4b.8b: $\gamma_n\le(a_n/\pi)^2\sum_i\|\nabla f_i\|^2<1/2$ adds at most $4\gamma_n$ to a covariance entry error, and the resulting density-entry bound is multiplied by $2^{3r/2}$. Preparation and gauge-sector errors add their trace bound and $2\eta_n$. Comparing both stages to the same continuum response proves asymptotic state compatibility for (F.10.4b.8d.1), including the explicit representative mismatch.

An executable summable choice is available. Enumerate rational compact regions, a countable dense smooth family and rational compact windows. At stage $k$ retain their first $k$ members. Choose $L_k$ so the thermal tails total at most $2^{-k-4}$; choose $n_k>n_{k-1}$ containing every orbit collar and making each discretization, Gram, preparation and gauge-leakage contribution at most $2^{-k-4}$. All inequalities have explicit finite seminorms, so this is a finite search at each stage. The accumulated tail is bounded by a fixed multiple of $2^{-k}$. Contraction and norm density extend the result pointwise to the closure. Uniformity belongs to the stated bounded smooth families, rather than to arbitrary ultraviolet unit balls. These exact algebra maps and compatible response families satisfy the retained-family F.10.1 comparison.

High-energy and doubler branches have separate quantitative bounds. Finite spectral calculus gives

 \|1_{\{|K_n|>\Lambda\}}E_nf\|
 \le\Lambda^{-1}(\|Kf\|+r_n(f)).

For low-energy Brillouin-edge branches, extend the finite grid vector by zero and use its lattice Fourier transform.  \tag{F.10.4b.8d.7}

The first term is the cell-projection error and the second is the continuum Fourier tail beyond $\pi/(2a_n)$. Apply this to $v(s)f$ and add (F.10.4b.8d.4) to bound the actual evolved lattice vector. The smoothness condition has content. The interpolants converge weakly to zero with norms bounded away from zero. Thus a bounded-boost-energy grammar alone contains noncompatible doubler sequences.
