For the time-slice map, solve the geometric Dirac Cauchy problem. If a smooth cutoff $\chi$ changes from zero to one inside a chosen Cauchy neighborhood, applying the Dirac operator to $\chi\psi$ gives a source there. Write $D=i\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu-m$, $E=G_{\rm ret}-G_{\rm adv}$, and $f=D(\chi\psi)$. Then $G_{\rm ret}f=\chi\psi$ and $G_{\rm adv}f=(\chi-1)\psi$, so $Ef=\psi$. Cauchy uniqueness gives composition and cutoff independence; the conserved Dirac current gives the one-particle isometry. Compact smooth approximation and CAR norm continuity give time-slice density. Their finite representatives are the averaged Cauchy data, with precisely the projection and propagation errors above. This also defines comparison for compact spacetime diamonds and their boosted images, rather than restricting the statement to one coordinate slice.

For spacelike-separated geometric smearings the relevant continuum CAR pairings vanish. Their smooth Cauchy representatives satisfy
$$
 |\langle E_nf,E_ng\rangle|
 =|\langle(I-P_n)f,(I-P_n)g\rangle|
 \le(a_n/\pi)^2\|\nabla f\|\|\nabla g\|.
 \tag{F.10.4b.8d.8}
$$
Moving an even word of length $r$ through another of length $t$ takes $rt$ CAR exchanges and leaves positive final sign. Each finite scalar anticommutator error multiplies the norms of the remaining factors. Thus (F.10.4b.8d.8), and the two evolution errors when a propagated representative is used, give a quantitative vanishing spacelike commutator. Norm density gives the limiting local even algebra. This direct geometric source comparison proves limiting causality on this grammar without identifying the loose LR velocity in (F.10.4b.8c.8) with $c$.

The finite KMS strip width is always $2\pi\rho/c$. State and real-time estimates control both boundaries on compact real intervals. The strip Poisson formula bounds an interior compact set by those boundary errors plus its bounded-kernel tails; enlarge the boundary interval first, then refine. This yields compact uniform closed-strip convergence on the analytic core and by norm approximation on the completed algebra, as required by F.10.3. Compact nonzero smooth spinors, their even number observables and overlapping rational boxes supply explicit nonempty witnesses. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104b8e-a-response-active-clock-on-the-same-retained-source"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.8e (A Response-Active Clock on the Same Retained Source).** Fix a compact proper-time window $0\le\tau\le T_*$ and the independent inputs $\rho,\ell,c,\Omega>0$, with $\Omega T_*<2\pi$. There are finite ordinary clock, readout and control registers on the source of Theorem F.10.4b.8c whose time readout converges to $\tau=\rho s/c$. Their joint control/readout has a nonzero retained response to every fixed smooth local mode occupation, and its source backreaction, timing, preparation and precision costs are the bounds below. The refinement claim concerns prepared clocks and the specified finite responses.

**Independent clock.** Put $L=2^b$ clock levels at the observer worldline $x^1=\rho\cosh s$, $ct=\rho\sinh s$. Their proper-time action and state are
$$
 S_C=\int d\tau\,[i\hbar\langle\psi,\dot\psi\rangle-
 \langle\psi,H_C\psi\rangle],\quad
 H_C=\hbar\Omega\sum_{k=0}^{L-1}k|k\rangle\langle k|
 =\hbar\Omega\sum_{j=0}^{b-1}2^j n_j,
 \quad|u_L\rangle=L^{-1/2}\sum_k|k\rangle.
 \tag{F.10.4b.8e.1}
$$
The binary representation is an ordinary $b$-qubit register. Its calibration frequency $\Omega$ and epoch are source settings independent of the KMS comparison. The metric worldline gives $d\tau=(\rho/c)ds$ directly. Its period $2\pi/\Omega$ is independent of the thermal period $2\pi\rho/c$. The exact clock tick is $2\pi/(L\Omega)$; the state advances by a cyclic pointer step after that proper time. Distributed program clocks at stationary cells $x_i^1>0$ have proper lapse $d\tau_i=(x_i^1/\rho)d\tau$ and independently set proper frequency $\Omega_i=\Omega\rho/x_i^1$, so their reference-time phase is the same $\Omega\tau$. Epoch data are distributed along the finite preparation tree before the input window, with its transmission/gate time and every clock copy charged. A reference-time pulse energy $h_i$ is implemented with local proper energy $(\rho/x_i^1)h_i$. Position/lapse precision enters the frequency-calibration error. These explicit geometric redshifts synchronize the finite control program without using temperature as a clock definition. The admitted program uses prescribed local timed controls. Before the input window, distribute each local switch its finite pulse table, key copy and calibrated local clock; retain every table bit, timer, switch and archive. A switch acts on its own bounded-radius term, so one observer clock is never coupled to the whole Hamiltonian. If pulse $a$ has actual applied peak term $h_a$ and total start/end timing error $\delta\tau_a$, Duhamel gives a complete trace-norm channel error at most $2\sum_a\|h_a\|\delta\tau_a/\hbar$. Add twice the summed timing-failure probability for an unconditional bound. Program transmission, synchronization and position/lapse errors enter this same finite budget. This includes the free-term cancellation and amplification switches in the capture block below.

Use the covariant phase POVM $|\theta\rangle\langle\theta|d\theta/(2\pi)$ with $|\theta\rangle=\sum_ke^{-ik\theta}|k\rangle$. The probability density in $e^{-iH_C\tau/\hbar}|u_L\rangle$ is the Fejer kernel centered at $\Omega\tau$. Integrate this POVM over $M_C$ equal bins to get actual finite effects $E_j$, and report the bin center divided by $\Omega$, unwrapped in the registered window. For $0<\Omega\delta<\pi$ and a window separated from its wrap point,
$$
 \Pr\{|\widehat\tau-\tau|>\delta+\pi/(M_C\Omega)\}
 \le\frac{1}{ L\sin^2(\Omega\delta/2)}.
 \tag{F.10.4b.8e.2}
$$
An epoch shift places a window starting at zero away from the wrap. The finite readout isometry $\psi\mapsto\sum_j\sqrt{E_j}\psi\otimes|j\rangle$ has a full-carrier unitary completion. QR elimination on its padded $LM_C$-dimensional unitary gives a finite $O((LM_C)^2\log^2(LM_C))$ elementary-gate bound before routing; all readout, completion and garbage registers are charged. Clock preparation is $b$ Hadamard gates. Its mean energy and variance are
$\hbar\Omega(L-1)/2$ and $(\hbar\Omega)^2(L^2-1)/12$.
A fractional calibration error $\epsilon_\Omega$ and epoch error $\epsilon_0$ add at most $T_*\epsilon_\Omega+\epsilon_0$ to the time tolerance. Preparation trace error and readout-channel error add their half trace bounds to the failure probability.

**Response-active smooth-mode control.** Let $f$ be a fixed normalized compact smooth spinor and $f_n=E_nf/\|E_nf\|$. Choose an actual number-conserving finite unitary $w_n$ sending $f_n$ to a selected local port mode $e_p$ in the cell adjacent to the registered observer worldline, included in the capture paths once the box contains it. A sequence of at most $q_n-1$ Givens eliminations constructs it. Route each elimination along a spanning-tree path by fermionic swaps and return the route, as in Theorem F.10.4b.8c. Thus $W_n=\Gamma(w_n)$ and $W_n^*$ use at most $O(q_ne_n)$ bounded-radius even gates each. Both halves, their paths and all intermediate source modes are charged.

Capture by $W_n$, apply the genuinely local port-clock pulse
$$
 H_{\rm pulse}=H_C+\lambda Z_0\otimes n_p,
 \qquad \eta=\lambda d_p/\hbar,
 \tag{F.10.4b.8e.3}
$$
for duration $d_p$, and undo $W_n$. Here $Z_0$ is the clock's lowest binary energy bit and $n_p=(I-B_p)/2$ is the local encoded port occupation. Place that bit next to the selected port star; it couples to at most $D$ edge qubits. The other $b-1$ bits have the individual onsite energies in (F.10.4b.8e.1); local gates route them to the finite readout apparatus when needed, with the gate count and duration charged. Thus growing clock dimension creates neither a hidden growing-degree port interaction nor an uncharged carry-edge assumption. During this registered control block the source free terms are switched off; the clock continues evolving throughout. Because $Z_0$ commutes with $H_C$ and the capture acts on the source, the ideal joint effect in the clock interaction picture is exactly
$$
 \exp[-i\eta Z_0\otimes B_{f_n}],\qquad
 B_{f_n}=a^*(f_n)a(f_n).
 \tag{F.10.4b.8e.4}
$$
A dense smooth-mode coupling has therefore been implemented by an actual local transport/pulse/return protocol. It is not inserted as a bounded-radius Hamiltonian term.

For an arbitrary source/reference state and the prepared clock, read the lowest clock bit's $Y$ observable in its known freely rotating frame. Then exactly
$$
 \langle Y_0^{\rm rot}\rangle=\sin(2\eta)\,\langle B_{f_n}\rangle,
 \qquad
 \frac{d}{ d\eta}\langle Y_0^{\rm rot}\rangle\big|_{0}
 =2\langle B_{f_n}\rangle.
 \tag{F.10.4b.8e.5}
$$
This follows by resolving the source projection $B_{f_n}$ into its zero/one sectors and rotating the initial lowest bit $|+\rangle$ about $Z$. Occupied and unoccupied $f_n$ preparations give different responses already at every finite stage. The limiting derivative is the fixed smooth occupation response $2\langle a^*(f)a(f)\rangle$, because
$$
 \|I_nf_n-f\|\le2\|(I-P_n)f\|,
 \qquad
 \|B_{I_nf_n}-B_f\|\le4a_n\|\nabla f\|/\pi
 \tag{F.10.4b.8e.6}
$$
for sufficiently large $n$. Thus the active clock response belongs to the retained smooth grammar, including when $\eta_n\to0$. No clock observable is declared response null.

The joint pulse changes a source or clock marginal by trace norm at most $2|\eta|$. If a full control block has duration $d_n$ and total implemented unitary error $\epsilon_{U,n}$, switching off the finite source Hamiltonian costs at most
$2\|H_n\|d_n/\hbar+2\epsilon_{U,n}$ in a unit-norm source response compared with the freely evolving reference. The same bound holds with the full carrier norm $\mathcal H_n$ when off-code inputs are admitted. This is charged rather than hidden in a change of the physical clock. Given a total rotation-angle budget $A_n$ for capture and return, applying each gate sequentially at norm $g_n$ takes time $\hbar A_n/g_n$. Thus a prescribed capture/return duration $d_n-d_p$ is achieved with $g_n=\hbar A_n/(d_n-d_p)$, with the actual peak energy and every pulse angle included. The middle pulse separately has energy $|\lambda|$ and duration $d_p$.

For a desired response accuracy $\epsilon$, require errors before dividing by $\sin(2\eta)$ to be at most $\epsilon|\sin(2\eta)|/2$. In particular clock-frame phase calibration, preparation, synthesis, capture timing and source comparison errors must meet that budget. Repeating a bounded $Y$ measurement on independent preparations gives source expectation accuracy $\epsilon$ with failure probability at most $\zeta$ using
$$
 N_{\rm rep}\ge \frac{8\log(2/\zeta)}{\epsilon^2\sin^2(2\eta)}.
 \tag{F.10.4b.8e.7}
$$
Every repetition has a fresh clock preparation, source preparation, key/archive and readout/reset record. The low-bit $Y$ readout and full phase-time POVM can be performed on separate identically prepared runs; their joint-output protocol uses separate prepared clock registers, whose dimensions and costs are added. The phase readout is not assumed nondisturbing. This explicitly charges the $\eta^{-1}$ precision and $\eta^{-2}$ sampling cost of a weak active response. Using $2\eta$ in place of $\sin(2\eta)$ adds at most $2\eta^2/3$ for $|\langle B_f\rangle|\le1$.

**Joint convergence and equilibrium record.** Fix the geometry and finite smooth-response list. Choose $\delta_j\downarrow0$, $L_j,M_{C,j}\uparrow\infty$ so the right side of (F.10.4b.8e.2), bin width and calibration errors tend to zero. Choose $\eta_j\to0$, $d_j\to0$ and $n_j\to\infty$ so all source, timing and circuit errors just specified are $o(|\sin2\eta_j|)$, with $\mathcal H_{n_j}d_j/\hbar\to0$. An explicit order is $\eta_j=2^{-j}$, then choose $n_j$ making the retained source errors at most $\eta_j^3$, then choose $d_j$ so $\mathcal H_{n_j}d_j/\hbar\le\eta_j^2$, take $d_{p,j}=d_j/2$, and set $\lambda_j=\hbar\eta_j/d_{p,j}$. Choose capture/return strengths from their angle budgets and tighten preparation, readout and synthesis errors to $o(\eta_j)$. The peak pulse energies generally grow; their small integrated disturbance follows from $\eta_j\to0$, with those growing energies charged. This explicit ordering avoids an assumed free precision or bounded-strength limit.

The total ordinary, unnormalized source response error is bounded by the Theorem F.10.4b.8d error plus
$$
 2|\eta_j|+2\mathcal H_{n_j}d_j/\hbar
 +2\epsilon_{U,j}+\epsilon_{\rm prep,j}
 +\omega_A(\delta_j+\pi/(M_{C,j}\Omega)+T_*\epsilon_{\Omega,j}+\epsilon_{0,j}),
 \tag{F.10.4b.8e.8}
$$
where $\omega_A$ is the actual proper-time modulus of continuity of the fixed retained response. For a smooth word it is bounded by its word-length/product-norm factor times $c\|Kf\|/\rho$ times the time error. Readout failure probability additionally includes (F.10.4b.8e.2), the pulse trace bound and preparation/readout errors. Equation (F.10.4b.8e.8) is the bound on the successful time-readout event. An unconditional expected-response bound adds $2\|A\|P_{\rm fail}$, with $P_{\rm fail}$ bounded as just stated; that term also tends to zero. Dividing the active response by $\sin(2\eta_j)$ with its stricter error budget gives the nonzero limit in (F.10.4b.8e.5).

The equilibrium field reference remains $D_n$ or the charged faithful $\Sigma_n$ of Theorem F.10.4b.8c. The timing state $|u_L\rangle$ is a prepared off-equilibrium state. A reference for the uncoupled field/clock is its product with $Z_C^{-1}e^{-\beta_EH_C}$, whereas the actual timing experiment uses the prepared clock. For an always-on local comparison Hamiltonian $H_n^{\rm all}+H_C+\lambda Z_0n_p$, its Gibbs state differs in trace norm from the uncoupled Gibbs state by at most $2\beta_E|\lambda|$. This follows by differentiating the normalized exponential, applying Schatten Holder to the Duhamel integral, and bounding the two centered terms by $\beta_E|\lambda|$ each. The prepared switched protocol (F.10.4b.8e.3) retains its own state and schedule; it is not assigned this equilibrium state.

All clock/control modules follow declared timelike placement paths. For each module at Rindler radius $r_i=x_i^1$, with rest mass $M_i$ and maximal proper internal/control energy $E_i^{\max}$, the support-force budget is $F_i\le(M_i+E_i^{\max}/c^2)c^2/r_i$. This includes the actual proper clock frequency $\Omega_i=\Omega\rho/r_i$ and all pulse energy assigned to that module. The observer module has $r_i=\rho$. All modules share rapidity $s=c\tau/\rho$, so on the reference window $[0,T_*]$ the summed inertial kinetic-work change is bounded by

$$
\sum_i(M_ic^2+E_i^{\max})[\cosh(cT_*/\rho)-1],
$$

with pulse work, transport, switching and reset/reuse additionally charged by their actual Hamiltonian norms and durations. These prescribed-support finite apparatus costs do not assert a gravitational stress solution for the apparatus. The local chart-clock identity is the same metric identity as Lemma F.10.4b.8.0; the added result is the finite active readout/control realization and its quantitative source comparison. The construction supplies a flat same-source clock certificate. No curved-patch modular identification is used. ∎

<a id="definition-f104b7h-infinite-first-thermal-car-source-and-retained-response"></a>**Definition F.10.4b.7h (Infinite-First Thermal CAR Source and Retained Response).**

###### 3.1 Frozen physical source and geometry

Fix positive computable physical constants $\beta,\hbar,\kappa$ with $\kappa\ge 4\beta$, supplied with certified approximations at requested precision. The parameter $\kappa$ has inverse-energy units and fixes the probe bandwidth; it is specified independently of a desired growth exponent. Define

\[
\alpha=\frac{\pi}{2\kappa\hbar},\qquad
b=\frac{\alpha\beta\hbar}{2}=\frac{\pi\beta}{4\kappa},\qquad
c=\cos b,\qquad s=\frac14.
\]

Thus $0<b\le\pi/16$, and the source-derived leading-edge rate below is $\lambda=2\alpha=\pi/(\kappa\hbar)$. This is strictly below the thermal upper rate $2\pi/(\beta\hbar)$; it is a bandwidth/propagation rate, not a claimed Lyapunov instability.

For $m=1,2,\dots$ take $n=2^m$ identical independent blocks. Each block has one-particle space

\[
\mathfrak h_0=L^2(\mathbb R,dE)\otimes\mathbb C^2_{\rm replica}\otimes\mathbb C^2_{\rm flavor},
\qquad (h_0f)(E)=Ef(E).
\]

The physical source is the ordinary tensor product of $n$ independent $\mathrm{CAR}(\mathfrak{h}_0)$ block systems. This choice registers the standard tensor MPU interface and permits arbitrary entangled inputs across retained block factors. We do not silently identify this tensor product with a globally graded CAR algebra. Within each block the bounded physical observable algebra is $\mathrm{CAR}(\mathfrak{h}_0)$, with

\[
\tau_t(a^*(v))=a^*(e^{ith/\hbar}v),\qquad
\omega_\beta(a^*(v)a(w))=\langle w,Rv\rangle,
\qquad R=(1+e^{\beta h})^{-1}.
\]

Here $a$ is antilinear and $a^*$ is linear. Within each block the state is the gauge-invariant quasifree state with this covariance. The complete state and evolution are their ordinary tensor products. The block and product states are faithful and $\beta$-KMS for this same physical evolution, not for an unrelated modular clock. Its two-point KMS identity is obtained directly from $(1-R)=e^{\beta h}R$; Wick expansion gives the identity on the dense algebra of finite products of energy-analytic fields, and boundedness extends the KMS state to CAR. Finite-dimensional spectral truncations have exactly the Gibbs states of the corresponding $h$, providing an alternative direct proof and the regulator interpretation.

**Faithfulness of the infinite state.** It does not follow merely by taking a limit of faithful finite densities. For this finite-temperature KMS state, let $\mathcal N_\omega=\{A:\omega(A^*A)=0\}$, a closed left ideal. If $A\in\mathcal N_\omega$, put $C=A^*A$. For an entire analytic $B$, KMS gives
\[
\omega(B^*CB)=\omega\!\left(CB\tau_{i\beta\hbar}(B^*)\right)=0.
\]
The last equality follows by Cauchy–Schwarz because $\omega(C^2)\le\|C\|\omega(C)=0$. Hence $AB\in\mathcal N_\omega$. Analytic elements are norm dense, so $\mathcal N_\omega$ is a closed two-sided ideal. The CAR algebra is simple (its standard matrix UHF inductive limit), as is a finite ordinary tensor product of these CAR algebras. Since $\omega(I)=1$, the ideal cannot be the full algebra and therefore is zero. Thus the actual infinite state is faithful. This proves the needed fact for every fixed $n$, with no uniform finite-density eigenvalue assertion.

The two-sided $E$ spectrum is an algebraic free-fermion energy variable, not an unstable bosonic oscillator. Particle-hole transformation on the negative-energy half-line identifies the vacuum implementation with positive excitation Hamiltonian $d\Gamma(|h|)\ge 0$, after subtracting the filled-sea energy. The finite-temperature state is not a trace-class density matrix on the continuous vacuum Fock space. Its KMS state and automorphism exist nonetheless; in its thermal representation the implementing Liouvillian has the usual two-sided spectrum. The infinite-carrier limit is taken before arbitrary late time. No finite regulator is asserted to mix irreversibly for all times.

Specify the fixed normalized spectral wavepacket

\[
w(E)=\frac{\kappa c}{\pi}\cosh(\beta E/2)\operatorname{sech}(\kappa E),\qquad f(E)=\sqrt{w(E)}.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.1.1}
\]

The identity

\[
\int_{\mathbb R}\operatorname{sech}(\kappa E)e^{-iEt/\hbar}\,dE
=\frac\pi\kappa\operatorname{sech}(\alpha t)
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.1.2}
\]

and its analytic continuation show $\int w=1$. A fixed delay cell has duration $\ell=(\log 2)/\alpha$; the source geometry has $m+2$ cells per line. Thus

\[
T_n=(m+2)\ell=\alpha^{-1}\log(4n),\qquad
 g_n=e^{iT_nh/\hbar}f.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.1.3}
\]

This registers the actual geometry, rather than retrospectively relabeling a freely chosen delay as system size. There are n independent lines/blocks and their probe separation increases by one fixed cell when their number doubles. The total delay-line length is O(n log n). The physical clock is t in $\tau_{t}$; there is no omitted preparation or start-time translation in the theorem.

###### 3.2 Actual bounded observables and retained degrees

Write $C(v)=a(v)+a^*(v)$. For a normalized vector, $C(v)$ is a Hermitian unitary. In block $j$ and replica $r=1,2$ set

\[
F_{jr}=f\otimes e_{jr,1},\qquad
G_{jr}=g_n\otimes(se_{jr,1}+\sqrt{1-s^2}e_{jr,2}).
\]

Define the even bounded probes

\[
A_j=iC(F_{j1})C(F_{j2}),\qquad
B_j=iC(G_{j1})C(G_{j2}),\qquad
A_n=\prod_{j=1}^n A_j,\quad B_n=\prod_{j=1}^n B_j.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.2.1}
\]

Every $A_j$, $B_j$, $A_n$ and $B_{n}$ is a nonzero Hermitian unitary, hence a contraction. The even block probes commute across blocks. The flavor rotation $s$ prevents coincident self-probe contact.

Within each block retain the indicated four-dimensional one-particle span. The formal direct-sum bookkeeping space is

\[
S_n=\operatorname{span}\{F_{jr},G_{jr}:1\le j\le n,\ r=1,2\}.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.2.2}
\]

For every pair the Gram off-diagonal is $s\langle f,g_n\rangle$, of modulus at most $s=1/4$. Each Gram matrix has eigenvalues in $[3/4,5/4]$. Thus the bookkeeping dimension $\dim S_n=4n$ is exact, with uniform conditioning. The actual complete retained algebra is the ordinary tensor product of $n$ block algebras $\mathrm{CAR}(S_{n,j})\cong M_{16}$, hence is the entire matrix algebra $M_{16}^{\otimes n}\cong M_{2^{4n}}$. We register

\[
N_{\rm eff}=4n.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.2.3}
\]

**Operational non-padding witness.** The retained response defined below is the identity channel at physical time zero. It can prepare and distinguish $2^{4n}$ mutually orthogonal states. Any exact smaller-dimensional carrier reproducing this entire service would have to distinguish that many states perfectly, so its dimension is at least $2^{4n}$. This establishes an actual retained-mode count; it is not an attained minimum for the full microscopic source or a claim that its reservoir has only $4n$ modes.

All n blocks occur in both actual product observables and in the retained-response channel. This is not a one-mode pulse padded with spectator modes. The reservoir is infinite and is not counted as a finite retained carrier.

<a id="theorem-f104b7h1-same-normalization-kms-otoc-and-strict-analytic-disk"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.7h.1 (Same-Normalization KMS OTOC and Strict Analytic Disk).**

###### 3.3 Quarter-density-equivalent KMS definition and exact evaluation

For energy-analytic X,Y define

\[
\mathcal P(X,Y;t)=
\omega_\beta\bigl(
X(t-3i\beta\hbar/4)Y(-i\beta\hbar/2)
X(t-i\beta\hbar/4)Y\bigr),
\]

\[
\mathcal Q(X)=\omega_\beta(X(-i\beta\hbar/2)X),\qquad
\mathcal D(X,Y)=\mathcal Q(X)\mathcal Q(Y).
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.3.1}
\]

For every finite Gibbs regulator these are exactly $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^{1/4}X(t)\rho^{1/4}Y\rho^{1/4}X(t)\rho^{1/4}Y)$ and $\lVert\rho^{1/4}X\rho^{1/4}\rVert_2^{2}\lVert\rho^{1/4}Y\rho^{1/4}\rVert_2^{2}$. The equality follows by moving the powers of $e^{-\beta H/4}$ through the trace; there is no new or rescaled denominator. Equation (F.10.4b.7h.3.1) is therefore the quarter-density-equivalent infinite-source object.

At complex time $\alpha_z(C(f))$ means analytic continuation of $\alpha_t(C(f))$; since $a$ is antilinear it is not $C(e^{izh/\hbar}f)$. Explicitly it is $a(e^{i\bar z h/\hbar}f)+a^*(e^{izh/\hbar}f)$. All fields used here are bounded analytic elements throughout the required products. Indeed $w(E)$ decays as $\exp[-(\kappa-\beta/2)|E|]$; $C(f)$ extends in norm to imaginary times $|\operatorname{Im} z|<\hbar(\kappa/2-\beta/4)$. Since $\kappa\ge 4\beta$ this width exceeds $\beta\hbar$, more than the largest shift in (F.10.4b.7h.3.1) on the open quarter strip. Products and their KMS expectations are holomorphic there.

The scalar field correlation is

\[
G(t)=\omega_\beta(C(e^{ith/\hbar}f)C(f))
=c\operatorname{sech}(\alpha t+ib).
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.3.2}
\]

To check it directly, the two annihilation/creation contractions give

\[
G(t)=\int w(E)[(1-R(E))e^{-iEt/\hbar}+R(E)e^{iEt/\hbar}]dE.
\]

Evenness of $w$ and $R(-E)=1-R(E)$ combine them into twice the first term. Substituting (F.10.4b.7h.1.1) cancels $\cosh(\beta E/2)$, and (F.10.4b.7h.1.2) gives (F.10.4b.7h.3.2). In particular $G(-i\beta\hbar/2)=c$.

Put

\[
x=\alpha(t-T_n),\qquad
S(x)=\operatorname{sech}^2(x+ib/2)+\operatorname{sech}^2(x-ib/2).
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.3.3}
\]

For a single replica, Wick's rule on the four fields in (F.10.4b.7h.3.1) gives

\[
P_{\rm odd}(t)=s^2c^2\operatorname{sech}^2(x+ib/2)
-c^2+s^2c^2\operatorname{sech}^2(x-ib/2)
=c^2[-1+s^2S(x)].
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.3.4}
\]

The middle contraction has a minus sign. For the two-replica even probes, regrouping the eight fermion fields gives six inter-replica transpositions and hence positive sign. The four factors $i$ contribute $i^{4}=1$. Thus $P_j=P_{\mathrm{odd}}^{2}$. The half-temperature pair $Q(A_j)=Q(B_j)=c^{2}$. Factorization of the even block factors yields exactly

\[
\boxed{D_n=c^{4n}>0,\qquad
P_n(t)=c^{4n}[1-s^2S(\alpha(t-T_n))]^{2n},\qquad
F_n(t)=\frac{P_n(t)}{D_n}=[1-s^2S(\alpha(t-T_n))]^{2n}.}
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.3.5}
\]

The disconnected lower bound $c^{(4n)}$ is tracked explicitly; it is exponentially small. This matters for finite approximation of P/D and cannot be discarded.

###### 3.4 Global analytic disk for exactly P/D

For $z$ with $|\operatorname{Im} z|<\beta\hbar/4$, let $x=\alpha(z-T_n)$. Then $|\operatorname{Im} x|<b/2$. Each $q_\pm=\operatorname{sech}^{2}(x\pm ib/2)$ has imaginary argument in $(-b,b)$. Since

\[
|\arg\cosh(u+iv)|\le|v|\quad (|v|<\pi/2),
\]

we have $|\arg q_\pm|\le 2b$ and $|q_\pm|\le\sec^{2}b$. Consequently

\[
\operatorname{Re}S\ge\cos(2b)(|q_+|+|q_-|)\ge\cos(2b)|S|,
\qquad |S|\le2\sec^2b.
\]

It follows that

\[
|S|^2\le\frac{2\sec^2b}{\cos(2b)}\operatorname{Re}S.
\]

Since $s^{2}=1/16<\cos(2b)\cos^{2}b$ for $b\le\pi/16$,

\[
|1-s^2S|^2=1-2s^2\operatorname{Re}S+s^4|S|^2<1
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.4.1}
\]

at every finite interior point. Thus $|F_n(z)|<1$ on the entire open horizontal strip, in particular the requested right half-strip. On real time $S$ is positive and $S\le 2\sec^{2}(b/2)$, so $0<s^{2}S<1$ and $0<F_n(t)<1$. There is no finite real-time unit-circle contact. $F_{n}$ approaches 1 only as $t\to\pm\infty$. No finite recurrence theorem is evaded by an illegal interchange of limits: the source here already has continuous spectrum.

<a id="theorem-f104b7h2-connected-value-derivative-and-logarithmic-first-threshold"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.7h.2 (Connected Value, Derivative and Logarithmic First Threshold).**

###### 3.5 Explicit value and logarithmic-derivative errors

Set $\lambda=2\alpha$ and

\[
u=e^{2x}=\frac{e^{\lambda t}}{16n^2},\qquad
R(u)=\frac{S(x)}{8cu}-1.
\]

The exact rational identity

\[
S(x)=4u\left[\frac{e^{ib}}{(1+ue^{ib})^2}+\frac{e^{-ib}}{(1+ue^{-ib})^2}\right]
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.5.1}
\]

implies, for $0<u<1$,

\[
|R(u)|\le a(u):=\frac{2u+u^2}{c(1-u)^2},\qquad
|\dot R(u)|\le\frac{2\lambda u}{c(1-u)^3}.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.5.2}
\]

Here and below a dot denotes the physical-time derivative. For $u\le 1/32$ and $c\ge\cos(\pi/16)>31/32$, the convenient weaker bounds are

\[
a(u)\le3u,\qquad |\dot R(u)|\le3\lambda u.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.5.3}
\]

Define $X=s^{2}S=S/16$ and $v=2nX$. Then

\[
v=\frac{c}{16n}e^{\lambda t}(1+R),\qquad
h_n=1-F_n=1-(1-X)^{2n}.
\]

For $0\le X\le 1$, elementary Bernoulli/exponential inequalities give

\[
v-v^2/2\le h_n\le v.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.5.4}
\]

If $v<1$, $h_n/v=1+R_B$ with $-v/2\le R_B\le 0$. Therefore, with the explicit leading prefactor $a_n=c/(16n)$,

\[
h_n(t)=a_ne^{\lambda t}(1+r_n(t)),\qquad
|r_n(t)|\le a(u)+(1+a(u))v/2.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.5.5}
\]

For the derivative, exact differentiation gives

\[
(\log h_n)'=\frac{X'}X\,\frac{2nX(1-X)^{2n-1}}{1-(1-X)^{2n}}.
\]

The second factor lies between $(1-X)^{2n-1}$ and 1. Hence its distance from 1 is at most $(2n-1)X\le v$. Using (F.10.4b.7h.5.2), provided $a(u)<1$,

\[
\left|(\log h_n)'-\lambda\right|
\le\frac{2\lambda u}{c(1-u)^3[1-a(u)]}+\lambda v.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.5.6}
\]

This is the required derivative control at the connected scale; it is not inferred from a value-only approximation.

Fix any $0<\delta<1$. For

\[
0\le t\le(1-\delta)\lambda^{-1}\log n,
\]

we have $u\le(1/16)n^{-1-\delta}\le 1/32$ and $v\le(c/16)n^{-\delta}(1+3u)$. Thus uniformly on this whole interval,

\[
|r_n|\le\tfrac14 n^{-\delta},\qquad
\left|\frac{r_n'}{1+r_n}\right|\le\tfrac14\lambda n^{-\delta}.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.5.7}
\]

The displayed constants are conservative: substitute $u\le n^{-1-\delta}/16$, $n\ge 2$, $c\le 1$ and $a\le 3u$ into (F.10.4b.7h.5.5)–(F.10.4b.7h.5.6). The second bound uses $1-3u\ge 29/32$.

In particular any growing-window origin $s_n\to\infty$ with $s_n=o(\log n)$ gives the required nonempty late growing window and vanishing value/derivative errors. For example $s_n=\lambda^{-1}\sqrt{\log n}$.

At $t=0$, (F.10.4b.7h.5.5) yields $h_n(0)=a_n(1+O(1/n))$; more explicitly $|h_n(0)/a_n-1|\le 1/(4n)$. In actual retained-degree units,

\[
a_n=\frac{c}{4N_{\rm eff}},\qquad
\frac{7c}{32N_{\rm eff}}\le h_n(0)\le\frac{9c}{32N_{\rm eff}}
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.5.8}
\]

for $n\ge 2$. (These bounds follow already from relative error $\le 1/8$; they are intentionally loose.) If the prefactor convention insists on $a_n^{\mathrm{exact}}=h_n(0)$, divide $1+r_n(t)$ by $1+r_n(0)$. The value error then is at most $(|r_n(t)|+|r_n(0)|)/(1-|r_n(0)|)$, and the logarithmic-derivative bound is unchanged. Thus the exact-start prefactor is also supplied.

The disconnected error is identically zero if $d_n=D_n$: $v_n^{\mathrm{disc}}=0$ and $(v_n^{\mathrm{disc}})'=0$. With direct comparator $a_n e^{\lambda t}$, the connected relative error is exactly $r_{n}$ from (F.10.4b.7h.5.5); no epidemic source is asserted or required.

###### 3.6 Fixed positive threshold in physical time

First, the same explicit estimates (F.10.4b.7h.5.5)–(F.10.4b.7h.5.6) may be used with $\delta=0$. They give

\[
\left|(\log h_n)' -\lambda\right|\le\lambda/4,
\qquad h_n'\ge(3\lambda/4)h_n,
\qquad 0\le t\le\lambda^{-1}\log n.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.6.0}
\]

Thus there is an actual uniform positive lower growth rate through the threshold window, in addition to the asymptotically exact rate on the growing early windows. This lower bound is source-derived and is not a saturation claim.

Let $t_n=\lambda^{-1}\log n$. Then $u=1/(16n)\le 1/32$. Equations (F.10.4b.7h.5.2)–(F.10.4b.7h.5.3) give $1+R\ge 1-3/32=29/32$. Consequently

\[
v(t_n)=\frac{c}{16}(1+R)\ge\frac{29c}{512}>\frac1{32}.
\]

Since $h_n\ge 1-e^{-v}$,

\[
h_n(t_n)>1-e^{-1/32}>\frac1{64}=:q_*.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.6.1}
\]

Thus the first threshold time satisfies

\[
\boxed{t_{*,n}(1/64)\le\lambda^{-1}\log n
=\lambda^{-1}\log N_{\rm eff}-\lambda^{-1}\log4.}
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.6.2}
\]

There is also a matching lower logarithmic scale. For any $0\le t\le t_n$, $u\le 1/(16n)$, so $h_n(t)\le v(t)\le[c/(16n)]e^{\lambda t}[1+3/(16n)]$. Consequently any first passage to $q_*=1/64$ obeys

\[
t_{*,n}(1/64)\ge\max\{0,\lambda^{-1}(\log n-\log5)\}.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.6.3}
\]

Together (F.10.4b.7h.6.2)–(F.10.4b.7h.6.3) give $\Theta(\log N_{\mathrm{eff}})$ for large $n$. The small-$n$ source may already exceed this deliberately conservative threshold at $t=0$; no strictly positive first passage is asserted for every $n$.

There is no uncounted physical source-start delay. The delayed packet separation $T_{n}$ is part of the source geometry at $t=0$; the actual product OTOC has the nonzero seed (F.10.4b.7h.5.8) at that same physical origin. The collective product reaches a fixed deficit before the center of the single-block pulse because $O(n)$ small block deficits accumulate.

A sharper optional asymptotic is available: for any fixed real y,

\[
h_n(\lambda^{-1}[\log n+y])\longrightarrow
1-\exp[-(c/16)e^y],
\]

with $O_y(1/n)$ error and matching derivative convergence, by (F.10.4b.7h.5.1) and $\log(1-X)=-X+O(X^{2})$. This is a fixed-threshold theorem directly from the same source, not an extrapolation of the early vanishing window.

<a id="theorem-f104b7h3-complete-retained-channel-mixing-with-polynomial-prefactor"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.7h.3 (Complete Retained-Channel Mixing with Polynomial Prefactor).**

##### 4 Complete retained response and a common finite-source refinement

The response protocol uses the same Hamiltonian, temperature, packets and complement as the OTOC protocol. It replaces all retained modes by an arbitrary input, performs one autonomous evolution, and returns the entire retained output with any reference. There are no intermediate interventions. Write $\tau_n$ for the actual retained KMS marginal and $\mathcal R_{\tau_n}(X)=\operatorname{Tr}(X)\tau_n$. For one block below, write $S_{n,0}$ for its four-dimensional retained one-particle space, $P$ for its projection, $Q=I-P$, and $C=(1+e^{\beta h})^{-1}$ for the physical covariance. The global channel is the ordinary product of the block channels.

The proved bounds are
\[
 d_{\mathrm{resp},n}(t):=\tfrac12\|\Phi_{n,t}-\mathcal R_{\tau_n}\|_\diamond
 \le\min\{1,600n e^{-\alpha(t-T_n)}\},\qquad t\ge T_n,\tag{F.10.4b.7h.R1}
\]
\[
 t_{\rm mix}(\varepsilon)\le T_n+\alpha^{-1}\log(600n/\varepsilon)
 =\alpha^{-1}[2\log n+\log(2400/\varepsilon)],\quad 0<\varepsilon<1.\tag{F.10.4b.7h.R2}
\]
For $t<T_n$, $2400n^2e^{-\alpha t}\ge600n>1$. Thus (F.10.4b.7h.R1) and the trivial half-diamond bound give the all-time bound stated in Section 1. This is a deterministic exponential error tail with an explicit prefactor and zero ideal floor; no fictitious random passage process is introduced.

For the common finite regulator and a declared horizon $T_n\le t\le R$, the same proof gives
\[
 d_{\mathrm{resp},n,M}(t)\le
 \min\{1,600n e^{-\alpha(t-T_n)}+\zeta_{n,M}(R)\},
\quad\zeta_{n,M}(R)=300n\left[2Q_\Lambda+\frac{(R+T_n)\Delta E}{2\hbar}\right].\tag{F.10.4b.7h.R3}
\]
The finite comparator is its own exact retained Gibbs marginal, identified with the same logical retained algebra. Complete convergence to the continuum channel and equilibrium is proved below. No finite-regulator all-time decay is asserted.

At time zero $\Phi_{n,0}$ is identity. Choosing an eigenvector of $\tau_n$ with minimum eigenvalue gives $d_{\rm resp,n}(0)\ge1-16^{-n}$, since its trace-distance from $\tau_n$ is $1-p_{\min}$ and $p_{\min}\le16^{-n}$. Thus the channel starts a uniform positive distance from the limiting replacer.

The full protocol class includes arbitrary retained inputs, arbitrary reference entanglement, final instruments/POVMs, and their complete outcome records. It excludes access to the omitted reservoir and interventions during the autonomous interval. Keeping an earlier measurement can preserve input information, so the theorem does not quantify over such different protocols. CPTP postprocessing of the returned output/reference cannot increase its bound.

###### 4.1 Independent-input assignment, including the graded split

Since $S_{n,0}$ is finite-dimensional, the usual Klein/Jordan–Wigner split is an explicit algebra isomorphism

\[
 \operatorname{CAR}(S_{n,0}\oplus S_{n,0}^\perp)
 \cong\mathcal B(\mathcal F(S_{n,0}))\otimes\operatorname{CAR}(S_{n,0}^\perp),
\]

under which

\[
 a(f_S)\longmapsto a_S(f_S)\otimes I,
 \qquad
 a(f_E)\longmapsto P_S\otimes a_E(f_E),
 \quad P_S=(-1)^{N_S}.
\]

Let $\omega_E$ be the restriction of the global KMS state to $\operatorname{CAR}(S_{n,0}^\perp)$. It is even and gauge invariant. Define the assignment

\[
 \mathcal A(\sigma)=\sigma\otimes\omega_E                       \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R4}
\]

in this displayed tensor factorization. For arbitrary finite references use $\mathcal A\otimes\mathrm{id}$ and leave the reference untouched. This is a CPTP preparation/assignment map: it prepares the specified fixed environment state and embeds an independently supplied retained density matrix. Equivalently, begin with the global KMS preparation, trace out/discard its retained factor, and insert the independently supplied input.

This operation preserves the **entire** original complement marginal. For an even complement monomial the split contains no $P_S$; for an odd monomial its $\omega_E$ expectation is zero. Thus its expectation after (F.10.4b.7h.R4) is the KMS complement expectation for every $\sigma$. In particular there is no dependence of that marginal on the supplied input. There is generally nonzero equilibrium system–complement covariance before the reset; it is deliberately removed. We never claim that the coupled KMS state initially equals a product of its marginals.

The block channel is

\[
 \Phi_t(\sigma)=\bigl(\mathcal A(\sigma)\circ\alpha_t\bigr)|_{\operatorname{CAR}(S_{n,0})},
\]

with the Schrödinger/Heisenberg convention fixed by the displayed formula. Reversing the convention changes the sign of $t$ but not any absolute overlap bound below. The limiting state $\tau$ is the actual KMS restriction to $\operatorname{CAR}(S_{n,0})$, with covariance $C_0=P C P|_{S_{n,0}}$; the replacer is $\mathcal R_\tau(\sigma)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma)\tau$.

For the ordinary block-tensor source the global assignment is the genuine product of block environment preparations and the global channel is $\Phi_t^{\otimes n}$, even when the retained input is entangled across blocks. This is an ordinary finite-matrix tensor statement, not a graded-product assumption.

**Parity scope.** In the manuscript's formal qubit/Hilbert source host, CAR is an encoded matrix algebra, so arbitrary density matrices and the full ordinary diamond norm are admitted. If instead an actual-fermion parity-superselection rule is imposed, restrict preparations to parity-admissible inputs and parity-compatible references; the same bound still holds because it was proved on a larger mathematical input class. Realizing arbitrary parity-coherent logical inputs then needs a specified parity-reference/encoding service and its modes and controls must be charged. No unregistered parity resource is used to justify physical arbitrary-fermion preparations. The formal encoded-qubit service is the nominated branch.

###### 4.2 General complete-channel mixing lemma

**Complete-channel lemma.** Let `S` be a `k`-dimensional complex one-particle subspace, `C` an even gauge-invariant quasi-free covariance commuting with `U_t`, and use assignment (F.10.4b.7h.R4). Suppose

\[
 \delta I\le C_0\le(1-\delta)I,\qquad 0<\delta\le1/2.
\]

Write $V:S\to\mathcal H$ for the inclusion, $X=P U_t V$, and $x=\lVert X\rVert$. If $x\le\delta/6$, then

\[
 \|\Phi_t-\mathcal R_\tau\|_\diamond
 \le (8+24/\delta)k x.                                        \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R5}
\]

**Proof.** Put

\[
 Y=Q U_t V,\quad R=(I-X^*X)^{1/2},\quad Z=Y R^{-1}.
\]

Since $Y^*Y=I-X^*X$, $Z$ is an isometry with range in the environment. Moreover

\[
 \|Z-U_tV\|\le x+1-\sqrt{1-x^2}\le x+x^2\le\tfrac32x.         \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R6}
\]

The overlap $(U_tV)^*Z=R$ is positive. Principal-angle rotations in the span of $U_tS$ and $ZS$ give a one-particle unitary $W_1$, identity off a subspace of dimension at most $2k$, sending $U_tV$ to $Z$. Its Hermitian logarithm has eigenvalues in $[-\arcsin x,\arcsin x]$. Its finite-rank CAR implementation is an even unitary $W=\exp(i\,d\Gamma(K))$, and the safe estimate

\[
 \|W-I\|\le2k\arcsin x
\]

follows by summing the absolute one-particle eigenangles. Conjugation by $W$ changes any full channel, also after arbitrary reference amplification, by at most $2\lVert W-I\rVert$. This replaces the evolved output embedding $U_tV$ by $Z$ at diamond cost at most $4k\arcsin x\le 8kx$.

All output modes in the replaced embedding lie in $S^\perp$. The even environment state makes the expectation of each odd output monomial zero and each even output monomial a scalar independent of the input. Hence the replaced channel is exactly a replacer with gauge-invariant quasi-free covariance

\[
 D=Z^*CZ.
\]

Stationarity $U_t^*CU_t=C$ and (F.10.4b.7h.R6) give

\[
 \|D-C_0\|\le2\|Z-U_tV\|\le3x.                              \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R7}
\]

Thus $\delta I/2\le D\le(1-\delta/2)I$. For any covariance $B$ strictly between zero and one, its finite-mode density matrix is

\[
 \rho_B=\frac{e^{-d\Gamma(K_B)}}{\operatorname{Tr}e^{-d\Gamma(K_B)}},
 \qquad K_B=\log(I-B)-\log B.
\]

The resolvent integral for the logarithm yields $\lVert\log A-\log B\rVert\le a^{-1}\lVert A-B\rVert$ when both operators are at least $aI$. Consequently

\[
 \|K_D-K_{C_0}\|\le(4/\delta)\|D-C_0\|.
\]

Interpolate linearly between the two many-body modular Hamiltonians. The Duhamel derivative of a normalized Gibbs density has trace norm at most twice the norm of the Hamiltonian derivative: Hölder's inequality bounds $\lVert\rho^u L\rho^{1-u}\rVert_1\le\lVert L\rVert$, and the normalization derivative contributes at most another $\lVert L\rVert$. Therefore

\[
 \|\rho_D-\rho_{C_0}\|_1
 \le2\|d\Gamma(K_D-K_{C_0})\|
 \le\frac{8k}{\delta}\|D-C_0\|
 \le\frac{24k}{\delta}x.                                     \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R8}
\]

The diamond norm between two replacers is exactly the trace norm between their replacement states. Combining (F.10.4b.7h.R8) with the rotation estimate proves (F.10.4b.7h.R5). All rotations occur in finite-dimensional one-particle spaces, so no infinite second-quantization norm or implementability assumption was used. ∎

###### 4.3 All constants for the nominated packets

The retained covariance has an `n`-independent spectral floor. In each replica its unorthonormalized covariance form has diagonal `1/2` and cross term of modulus at most `s/2`; the same holds for its complementary covariance `I-C`. Therefore, using the upper Gram bound `1+s`,

\[
 \delta=\frac{1-s}{2(1+s)}=\frac3{10}                         \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R9}
\]

works for every delay. This uses only $w(E)=w(-E)$, $C(E)+C(-E)=1$, and Cauchy–Schwarz, not a product assumption across $S$ and its complement.

For real `u`,

\[
 |\operatorname{sech}(u+ib)|
 \le c^{-1}\operatorname{sech}u,
 \qquad |m(t)|\le\operatorname{sech}(\alpha t)
 \le2e^{-\alpha|t|}.
\]

The compression of $U_t$ in one replica has raw matrix entries $m(t)$, $s\,m(t-T_n)$, and $s\,m(t+T_n)$, up to conjugation. Gram orthonormalization gives

\[
 x\le\frac{|m(t)|+s\max\{|m(t-T_n)|,|m(t+T_n)|\}}{1-s}
 \le\frac{2(1+s)}{1-s}e^{-\alpha(t-T_n)}
 =\frac{10}{3}e^{-\alpha(t-T_n)},\quad t\ge T_n.              \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R10}
\]

For one block $k=4$, (F.10.4b.7h.R5) gives half-diamond distance at most $176x$ when $x\le\delta/6=1/20$. When $x>1/20$, the trivial half-diamond bound one is smaller than $176x$. Thus the useful global statement is

\[
 \tfrac12\|\Phi_t-\mathcal R_\tau\|_\diamond
 \le\min\{1,176x\}\quad\text{for every }x\in[0,1].           \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R11}
\]

For ordinary product channels, telescoping their difference and using that every channel has diamond norm one proves

\[
 \tfrac12\|\Phi_t^{\otimes n}-\mathcal R_\tau^{\otimes n}\|_\diamond
 \le n\tfrac12\|\Phi_t-\mathcal R_\tau\|_\diamond.
\]

Combining this with (F.10.4b.7h.R10) gives coefficient $1760/3<600$ and proves (F.10.4b.7h.R1). This argument includes every retained matrix entry and arbitrary cross-block/reference entanglement. There is no exponentially large matrix-basis prefactor.

###### 4.4 Same finite Hamiltonian/state resources

The OTOC experiment prepares the global KMS/Gibbs state and evaluates the quarter-density word of that state. The response experiment prepares that **same** state, performs the declared retained reset (F.10.4b.7h.R4), then uses the **same** autonomous Hamiltonian. These are different preparation protocols on the same source. A reset state is not required to be globally stationary. The source state, Hamiltonian, packet choices, temperature, time units, and available complement resource remain identical.

In particular the response equilibrium $\tau$ is a marginal of the original global KMS state. It need not equal a Gibbs state of a naively projected local Hamiltonian $P h P$. No Gibbs property of that artificial subsystem Hamiltonian enters the proof.

The full environment is response-active and remains a declared component of the source. Only the output metric is coarse. Retained effective size and total source resources are separate entries; see Construction F.10.4b.7h.8.

<a id="construction-f104b7h4-one-positive-finite-gibbs-regulator-and-thermal-pair-comparison"></a>**Construction F.10.4b.7h.4 (One Positive Finite-Gibbs Regulator and Thermal Pair Comparison).**

###### 4.5 Finite Gibbs regulator and its response floor

Choose a symmetric partition of $[-\Lambda,\Lambda]$ into $M$ cells $I_j$ of width at most $\Delta E$, with symmetric energy midpoints $E_j$. Define

\[
 q_j=\int_{I_j}w(E)dE,\quad Z_\Lambda=\sum_jq_j=1-Q_\Lambda,
 \quad f_j=\sqrt{q_j/Z_\Lambda},\quad (g_n)_j=e^{iT_nE_j/\hbar}f_j.
\]

Each block now has `4M` finite complex source modes. For `n` blocks use the positive Hamiltonian

\[
 H^+_{n,M}
 =\sum_{\text{blocks,flavors},j:E_j\ge0}E_j n_j
  +\sum_{\text{blocks,flavors},j:E_j<0}|E_j|(1-n_j).             \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R12}
\]

Equivalently it is $d\Gamma(h_M)$ plus the explicitly recorded scalar

\[
 E_{\rm ref}=4n\sum_{E_j<0}|E_j|.
\]

Its ground energy is zero. This scalar does not affect the Heisenberg evolution or normalized Gibbs state,

\[
 \rho_{n,M}=e^{-\beta H^+_{n,M}}/\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H^+_{n,M}},
 \qquad C_M=(1+e^{\beta h_M})^{-1}.
\]

The state is faithful at every finite regulator. Its minimum many-body Gibbs eigenvalue is at least $2^{-4nM}\exp(-\beta E_{\max})$ with $E_{\max}=4n\sum|E_j|\le 4nM\Lambda$. We use the actual retained covariance floor (F.10.4b.7h.R9), rather than pretending this global minimum is uniform.

Use the four retained packet vectors and their Gram orthonormalization exactly as above, with finite sums replacing integrals. Symmetry gives occupation $1/2$ and hence the same $\delta=3/10$ exactly. Prepare the complement marginal of this finite Gibbs state and reset the retained factor exactly as in (F.10.4b.7h.R4).

Put $a_0=\kappa-\beta/2>0$. Since

\[
 w(E)\le\frac{2\kappa c}{\pi}e^{-a_0|E|},
\]

one has

\[
 Q_\Lambda\le\frac{4\kappa c}{\pi a_0}e^{-a_0\Lambda},
 \quad
 L_\Lambda:=\int_{|E|>\Lambda}|E|w(E)dE
 \le\frac{4\kappa c}{\pi}e^{-a_0\Lambda}
       \left(\frac\Lambda{a_0}+\frac1{a_0^2}\right).             \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R13}
\]

Let $m_M(u)=\sum(q_j/Z_\Lambda)e^{iuE_j/\hbar}$. Conditioning on the spectral interval changes a bounded expectation by at most $2Q_\Lambda$; replacing energies in a cell by its midpoint changes a phase by at most $|u|\Delta E/(2\hbar)$. Hence

\[
 |m_M(u)-m(u)|\le2Q_\Lambda+\frac{|u|\Delta E}{2\hbar}.        \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R14}
\]

For $0\le t\le R$, the three arguments $t,t\pm T_n$ have modulus at most $R+T_n$. Repeating the raw-matrix and Gram estimate gives

\[
 x_M(t)\le\frac{10}{3}e^{-\alpha(t-T_n)}
       +\frac53\left[2Q_\Lambda+
               \frac{(R+T_n)\Delta E}{2\hbar}\right].          \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R15}
\]

Apply (F.10.4b.7h.R11) to the finite source and telescope the ordinary channels. Since $176(5/3)<300$, this proves (F.10.4b.7h.R3). Every ingredient is on the same finite positive Hamiltonian and faithful Gibbs state. There is no irreversible full-state mixing assertion.

For $0<\zeta<\varepsilon$, the certified finite-window mixing time is

\[
 t\ge T_n+\alpha^{-1}\log\frac{600n}{\varepsilon-\zeta},
 \qquad t\le R.                                             \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R16}
\]

The regulator is chosen first to make this interval nonempty and the floor small. Fixing the regulator and letting $t\to\infty$ invalidates the finite-window floor estimate and produces recurrences, as required by the finite-carrier obstructions.

###### 4.6 Common thermal pair approximation, including derivatives

The quarter-density source derivation uses the scalar pair contraction

\[
 G(q)=2\int w(E)(1-C(E))e^{-iEq/\hbar}\,dE,
\]

at imaginary differences in $-\beta\hbar\le\operatorname{Im}q\le 0$. For the OTOC half-strip $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le\beta\hbar/4$, its cross differences are $(z-T_n)-i\beta\hbar/4$ and $(z-T_n)-3i\beta\hbar/4$; same-probe differences include $-i\beta\hbar/2$. Use the **same** finite Gibbs source, defining

\[
 G_M(q)=2\sum_j(q_j/Z_\Lambda)(1-C(E_j))e^{-iE_jq/\hbar}.
\]

If $q=u+iv$ with $-\beta\hbar\le v\le 0$, the multiplier

\[
 \phi_q(E)=(1-C(E))e^{-iEq/\hbar}
\]

obeys $|\phi_q(E)|\le 1$: for positive $E$ the imaginary exponential is at most one; for negative $E$, its growth is canceled by $1-C(E)\le e^{\beta E}$. Also

\[
 |\partial_E\phi_q(E)|\le\beta+|u|/\hbar.
\]

Indeed its logarithmic real derivative is $\beta C(E)+v/\hbar\in[-\beta,\beta]$ and its imaginary derivative is $-u/\hbar$. For $|u|\le L$, exact cell weights therefore give

\[
 \boxed{|G_M(q)-G(q)|\le4Q_\Lambda+\Delta E(\beta+L/\hbar).}   \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R17}
\]

Let $\mu_1=\int|E|w(E)\,dE$, finite and bounded by $4\kappa c/(\pi a_0^2)$. If $Q_\Lambda\le 1/2$, differentiating with respect to $u$ and estimating the omitted tail and normalization yields

\[
 \boxed{|\partial_uG_M(q)-\partial_uG(q)|
 \le\frac{2L_\Lambda+4Q_\Lambda\mu_1}{\hbar}
 +\frac{\Delta E}{\hbar}
       [1+\Lambda(\beta+L/\hbar)].}                           \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R18}
\]

For the cell error, differentiate $E\phi_q(E)$ and use $|E_j|\le\Lambda$. These two estimates are uniform on the full closed thermal pair strip, not just on the real axis. They cover $c_M=G_M(-i\beta\hbar/2)\to c$ and its resulting disconnected normalization $D_{n,M}=c_M^{4n}$ as well as every Wick contraction in the finite quarter-density word.

For fixed $n$ the algebraic KMS state is obtained as $\Lambda\to\infty$, $\Delta E\to 0$. A concrete common-space embedding sends spectral basis vector $e_j$ to $f(E)1_{I_j}(E)/\sqrt{q_j}$. The specific diagonal grids below need not be nested. Their displayed isometries into the common one-particle space and their logical Gram-frame identifications are the comparison maps. Increasing cutoffs and decreasing cell widths give strong approximation of $L^2$ because $f>0$ almost everywhere. A nested dyadic grid could alternatively be used at fixed $n$, but no exact nesting of the chosen diagonal is asserted. Covariances and dynamics are not falsely asserted to intertwine exactly across regulators: (F.10.4b.7h.R14), (F.10.4b.7h.R17), (F.10.4b.7h.R18), and strong convergence of midpoint multiplication provide the comparison. Wick's determinant/Pfaffian formula then proves every fixed-degree packet-word convergence. The finite response certificate (F.10.4b.7h.R3) was proved directly. Complete channel convergence, beyond fixed-degree correlation convergence, is proved in the next refinement theorem.

<a id="theorem-f104b7h5-common-regulator-normalized-c1-and-connected-scale-bounds"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.7h.5 (Common-Regulator Normalized C1 and Connected-Scale Bounds).**

###### 4.7 Exact normalized $C^1$ control on one common finite-Gibbs regulator

Use precisely the spectral cells of (F.10.4b.7h.R12)–(F.10.4b.7h.R18). Let $a=\kappa-\beta/2>0$. Truncate $E$ to $[-\Lambda,\Lambda]$ and partition symmetrically into equal cells $I_{j}$ of width $\Delta E$ with midpoint $E_{j}$. Set

\[
q_j=\int_{I_j}w(E)dE,\quad Q_\Lambda=\int_{|E|>\Lambda}w(E)dE,
\quad Z_\Lambda=1-Q_\Lambda,\quad
f_j=\sqrt{q_j/Z_\Lambda},\quad (g_n)_j=e^{iE_jT_n/\hbar}f_j.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.10.1}
\]

Use four flavors per block and the exact finite Hamiltonian $h_M=\operatorname{diag}(E_j)$, the same $\beta$-Gibbs covariance $R_M=(1+e^{\beta h_M})^{-1}$, the same flavor rotations, and the same ordinary tensor block construction. This supplies an actual finite Gibbs source with the actual normalized probes.

Its basic two-point function and quarter constant are

\[
G_M(q)=2\sum_j\frac{q_j}{Z_\Lambda}(1-R(E_j))e^{-iE_jq/\hbar},\qquad
c_M=G_M(-i\beta\hbar/2)>0.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.10.2}
\]

For the closed KMS pair strip $-\beta\hbar\le\operatorname{Im} q\le 0$ and $|\operatorname{Re} q|\le L$, both $|G(q)|\le 1$ and $|G_M(q)|\le 1$. For the finite function this follows directly by grouping symmetric energies $\pm E$: its maximum modulus at fixed imaginary part is bounded by the weighted average of $\cosh[(\beta/2+\operatorname{Im} q/\hbar)E]/\cosh(\beta E/2)$, which is at most 1. This bound uses the actual Gibbs weights and symmetry, not a finite-strip disk assumption on the four-point function.

Let $\mu_1=\int|E|w(E)dE$, $J_\Lambda=\int_{|E|>\Lambda}|E|w(E)dE$, and $\Gamma=2\mu_1/\hbar$. The envelope $w(E)\le(2\kappa/\pi)e^{-a|E|}$ gives explicit constants

\[
Q_\Lambda\le C_Qe^{-a\Lambda},\quad
J_\Lambda\le C_Q(\Lambda+a^{-1})e^{-a\Lambda},\quad
\mu_1\le C_Q/a,\qquad C_Q=4\kappa/(\pi a).
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.10.3}
\]

For $Q_\Lambda\le 1/2$ define

\[
\epsilon_0=4Q_\Lambda+\Delta E\,(\beta+L/\hbar),
\]

\[
\epsilon_1=\frac{2J_\Lambda+4Q_\Lambda\mu_1}{\hbar}
+\frac{\Delta E}{\hbar}[1+\Lambda(\beta+L/\hbar)].
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.10.4}
\]

Then uniformly on that closed pair strip,

\[
|G_M-G|\le\epsilon_0,\qquad |G_M'-G'|\le\epsilon_1,
\qquad |c_M-c|\le\epsilon_0.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.10.5}
\]

Proof: write $\varphi_q(E)=(1-R(E))e^{-iEq/\hbar}$. On the stated strip, $|\varphi_q(E)|\le 1$ and $|\partial_E\varphi_q(E)|\le\beta+|\operatorname{Re} q|/\hbar$. The latter follows by differentiating: the real logarithmic term $\beta R(E)+\operatorname{Im} q/\hbar$ lies in $[-\beta,\beta]$, and the imaginary term has modulus $|\operatorname{Re} q|/\hbar$. Tail removal and normalization cost at most $4Q_\Lambda$ in $2\int w\varphi$. Midpoint replacement on exact cell weights costs at most $\Delta E\sup|\varphi'|$. Differentiation in physical time inserts $-iE/\hbar$. The tail costs $2J_\Lambda/\hbar$, normalization at most $4Q_\Lambda\mu_1/\hbar$, and $|\partial_E(E\varphi)|\le 1+\Lambda(\beta+L/\hbar)$ gives the last term. This proves both bounds, including the derivative at its actual source scale.

For $z$ in the closed quarter strip $|\operatorname{Im} z|\le\beta\hbar/4$, put

\[
K_+(z)=G(z-T_n-i\beta\hbar/4),\qquad
K_-(z)=G(-z+T_n-i\beta\hbar/4),
\]

and use the identical definitions with $G_{M}$. The symmetric finite Gibbs source obeys the same KMS reversal identity, so finite Wick evaluation gives exactly

\[
B_M(z)=1-\frac{s^2}{c_M^2}[K_{M,+}(z)^2+K_{M,-}(z)^2],
\quad F_{n,M}(z)=B_M(z)^{2n},\quad D_{n,M}=c_M^{4n}.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.10.6}
\]

The corresponding infinite $B$ is $1-s^{2}S$. This is an exact finite quarter-density trace formula, not a prescribed finite approximation to the infinite answer. For $0\le\operatorname{Re} z\le H$ use $L=H+T_n$ in (F.10.4b.7h.10.4).

Assume $\varepsilon_0\le c/2$ and $\varepsilon_1\le\Gamma$. Since $c\ge 31/32$, $c_M\ge c/2$, $|K|,|K_M|\le 1$, $|K'|\le\Gamma$ and $|K_M'|\le 2\Gamma$, elementary differentiation of (F.10.4b.7h.10.6) yields the conservative uniform bounds

\[
|B_M-B|\le3\epsilon_0,\qquad
|B_M'-B'|\le6\Gamma\epsilon_0+2\epsilon_1.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.10.7}
\]

For detail, the difference of the two square sums is at most $4\varepsilon_0$, while $|c_M^{-2}-c^{-2}|\le 8\varepsilon_0/c^{4}$. The difference of their derivatives is at most $8\Gamma\varepsilon_0+4\varepsilon_1$; the true square-sum derivative has modulus at most $4\Gamma$. Division by $c_{M}^{2}$ and multiplication by $s^{2}=1/16$ give (F.10.4b.7h.10.7). Also $|B'|\le\Gamma$, and the infinite disk gives $|B|\le 1$. Thus $|B_M|\le 1+3\varepsilon_0$ and the telescoping power identity proves

\[
|F_{n,M}-F_n|\le6n\epsilon_0 e^{6n\epsilon_0},
\]

\[
|F_{n,M}'-F_n'|
\le e^{6n\epsilon_0}[24\Gamma n^2\epsilon_0+4n\epsilon_1].
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.10.8}
\]

These estimates hold on the entire specified compact quarter strip. They do not assert any global finite-mesh disk condition.

On the real interval $0\le t\le\lambda^{-1}\log n$, the source theorem gives $h_n\ge h_n(0)\ge 1/(32n)$, and $|h_n'/h_n|\le 5\lambda/4$. Therefore

\[
\left|\frac{h_{n,M}}{h_n}-1\right|
\le192n^2\epsilon_0e^{6n\epsilon_0}=:\eta_n.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.10.9}
\]

When $\eta_n\le 1/2$, $h_{n,M}>0$ and

\[
\left|\frac{h_{n,M}'}{h_{n,M}}-\frac{h_n'}{h_n}\right|
\le e^{6n\epsilon_0}
[1536\Gamma n^3\epsilon_0+256n^2\epsilon_1+480\lambda n^2\epsilon_0].
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.10.10}
\]

This follows by putting the derivative difference over $h_{n,M}\ge h_n/2$ and bounding the denominator correction using (F.10.4b.7h.10.9). It controls both connected values and their logarithmic derivatives, not merely an error at disconnected scale.

The disconnected normalization is also tracked without hiding its small size:

\[
\left|\frac{D_{n,M}}{D_n}-1\right|
\le\exp(8n\epsilon_0/c)-1,
\qquad D_n=c^{4n},\quad D_{n,M}=c_M^{4n}.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.10.11}
\]

An exponentially tiny D does not force exponential precision in this special source because its exact source-derived Wick factorization cancels it before comparison. One must use (F.10.4b.7h.10.6); an arbitrary absolute-error estimate on P would not have this property.

###### One explicit common diagonal sequence

Take

\[
H_n=\frac4\alpha\log(2400n),\quad L_n=H_n+T_n,
\quad\Lambda_n=\frac{12}{a}\log(4n),
\]

\[
M_n=2\left\lceil\kappa\Lambda_n n^8\right\rceil,
\qquad\Delta E_n=2\Lambda_n/M_n\le\kappa^{-1}n^{-8}.
\tag{F.10.4b.7h.10.12}
\]

The integer $M_{n}$ is even, so the grid is symmetric. Equations (F.10.4b.7h.10.3)–(F.10.4b.7h.10.4) are explicit computable bounds at every n. They imply

\[
\epsilon_0=O_{\beta,\kappa,\hbar}(n^{-8}\log n),\qquad
\epsilon_1=O_{\beta,\kappa,\hbar}(n^{-8}(\log n)^2).
\]

Consequently the connected relative error in (F.10.4b.7h.10.9) is $O(n^{-6}\log n)$, and the logarithmic-derivative error in (F.10.4b.7h.10.10) is $O(n^{-5}(\log n)^{2})$. The preliminary small-error inequalities hold for every sufficiently large $n$ with a threshold computed from (F.10.4b.7h.10.3)–(F.10.4b.7h.10.4); any finitely many earlier regulators can be further refined without changing the sequence's asymptotics. The additional error is smaller than the required original $O(n^{-\delta})$ early-window error for every fixed $0<\delta<1$. The strict positive gap in (F.10.4b.7h.6.1) preserves the $q=1/64$ threshold for sufficiently large regulated sources on the same horizon.

There are four flavors times $M_{n}$ energy cells per block and $n$ blocks: $4nM_n=O(n^9\log n)$ finite fermionic modes, with diagonal energies bounded by $\Lambda_n=O(\log n)$. Exact cell weights and their square-root preparation parameters are computable from the declared parameters and may be evaluated with certified quadrature to additional polynomial precision; such parameter rounding must be budgeted in the same contraction errors, not called exact. This is a conservative finite-horizon formal realization count, not an efficient hardware proposal. The infinite KMS source supplies the global disk and all-time mixing. Every fixed finite simulator retains recurrence outside its declared horizon.

<a id="theorem-f104b7h6-compact-horizon-complete-channel-refinement"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.7h.6 (Compact-Horizon Complete-Channel Refinement).**

###### 4.8 Complete channel refinement on every compact horizon

Correlation convergence alone is not used as a substitute for complete channel convergence. The following finite, deliberately conservative estimate supplies it explicitly.

Embed each finite spectral mode into the common continuum space by $e_j\mapsto f\,1_{I_j}/\sqrt{q_j}$, as above. Let $V_M,V:\mathbb{C}^4\to\mathcal H$ be the finite and continuum orthonormal retained frames obtained by their positive Gram inverse square roots. Set

\[
 e=5\left(\sqrt{2Q_\Lambda}+\frac{T_n\Delta E}{2\hbar}\right),
 \qquad
 e_R=e+\frac{R\Delta E}{2\hbar}+\beta\Delta E.                 \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R21}
\]

The abstract input and output algebra is always $\operatorname{CAR}(\mathbb{C}^4)=M_{16}$ through these frames. Thus both channels have exactly the same logical domain/codomain, rather than implicitly identifying nonidentical physical packet modes. Then

\[
 \boxed{\sup_{0\le t\le R}
 \tfrac12\|\Phi_{n,M,t}-\Phi_{n,t}\|_\diamond
 \le\min\{1,2^{28} n e_R\}.}                                \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R22}
\]

This estimate includes arbitrary parity-coherent formal inputs and arbitrary reference amplification. Its large numerical constant is fixed, independent of `n`, the delay and the regulator. It is used for refinement, not the sharper mixing prefactor.

**Proof.** The embedded finite `f_M` is the normalized restriction of `f` to the cutoff interval. Thus

\[
 \|f_M-f\|\le\sqrt{2Q_\Lambda},\qquad
 \|g_M-g\|\le\sqrt{2Q_\Lambda}+T_n\Delta E/(2\hbar).
\]

For one replica the raw two-column frame difference has norm at most $\sqrt{2}$ times the latter bound. Both Gram matrices have lower bound $g_0=1-s$. The resolvent formula gives

\[
 \|G_M^{-1/2}-G^{-1/2}\|
 \le\frac{\|G_M-G\|}{2g_0^{3/2}}.
\]

Consequently the orthonormal frame difference is at most $2\sqrt{2}\,g_0^{-3/2}$ times the raw-vector bound; this is less than the coefficient five in (F.10.4b.7h.R21). The two replicas are orthogonal, so $\lVert V_M-V\rVert\le e$.

Extend the midpoint Hamiltonian to the common ambient one-particle space as multiplication by $E_j$ inside cell $I_j$, and by the original $E$ outside the cutoff interval. Denote its unitary and covariance by $U_M(t)$ and $C_M^{\mathrm{ext}}$. This extension is used only for a comparison: the extra modes are invariant and decoupled from every embedded finite source mode. Hence it gives exactly the same finite response on the declared finite source. Pointwise Lipschitz estimates give

\[
 \|U_M(t)-U_t\|\le t\Delta E/(2\hbar),\qquad
 \|C_M^{\mathrm{ext}}-C\|\le\beta\Delta E/8.
\]

Write $X=V^*U_tV$, $Y=(I-VV^*)U_tV$, and similarly $X_M,Y_M$. Then

\[
 \|X_M-X\|\le2e+t\Delta E/(2\hbar)=:\varepsilon_X,
\]
\[
 \|Y_M-Y\|\le3e+t\Delta E/(2\hbar)=:\varepsilon_Y.             \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R23}
\]

Use the eight Majoranas associated with $v_j$ and $iv_j$; multiply each ordered product by its usual unit-modulus phase to obtain the fixed Hermitian unitary monomial basis of $M_{16}$. These phases do not change any norm estimate. In the Klein split, each evolved Majorana is the sum of an input Majorana linear combination and $P_S$ times an environment Majorana. Every summand has norm at most one. Expand a basis monomial of length at most eight into at most $2^8$ such products. After putting its input/parity factors on the left, its environment expectation is zero for odd degree. For even degree it is the quasi-free Wick sum. There are at most $7!!=105$ pairings, each with at most four contractions; every contraction has modulus at most one.

Each input-field coefficient changes by at most $\varepsilon_X$. Each environment Majorana contraction changes by at most

\[
 \varepsilon_c=4\varepsilon_Y+2\|C_M^{\mathrm{ext}}-C\|
 \le12e+4t\Delta E/(2\hbar)+\beta\Delta E/4.                 \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R24}
\]

The factor four follows by writing a Majorana contraction as the sum of its creation–annihilation and annihilation–creation pairings and using the vector errors twice in each. Product telescoping now bounds the change in the channel adjoint on any basis monomial by

\[
 2^8(8\varepsilon_X+420\varepsilon_c)
 \le2^{21}e_R.                                             \tag{F.10.4b.7h.R25}
\]

No independence or Gaussianity of the retained input was assumed; only the fixed bath is quasi-free. For a Hermitian unitary basis $\Gamma_a$ of $M_d$, $\operatorname{Tr}\Gamma_a\Gamma_b=d\,\delta_{ab}$, an arbitrary amplified input $Z$ satisfies

\[
 (\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})(Z)
 =\frac1d\sum_a\Gamma_a\otimes
   \operatorname{Tr}_S[(\Delta^*(\Gamma_a)\otimes I)Z].
\]

Trace-norm duality bounds each partial trace by $\lVert\Delta^*(\Gamma_a)\rVert\,\lVert Z\rVert_1$, while $\lVert\Gamma_a\rVert_1=d$. Thus the diamond norm is at most $d^2$ times the largest adjoint-basis bound. With $d=16$, (F.10.4b.7h.R25) gives per-block full diamond at most $2^{29}e_R$. Ordinary tensor telescoping and the half-diamond convention prove (F.10.4b.7h.R22). ∎

The equilibrium replacements converge as well. Their retained covariances differ by at most $2e+\beta\Delta E/8$; both have the exact floor $\delta=3/10$. The same logarithm/Duhamel argument gives a one-block state trace bound $(4k/\delta)(2e+\beta\Delta E/8)$, $k=4$, and the ordinary $n$-block state bound is at most $n$ times this. Therefore every regulator is compared with the same logical infinite channel and equilibrium, and two regulators can be compared by the sum of their errors.

At fixed `n`, (F.10.4b.7h.R22) vanishes on every fixed compact horizon. Along the common sequence (F.10.4b.7h.10.12), $\sqrt{Q_\Lambda}=O(n^{-6})$ and the mesh terms are $O(n^{-8}\log n)$, so $e_R=O(n^{-6})$ and the complete $n$-block channel error is $O(n^{-5})$ on its logarithmic horizon. The finite mixing floor (F.10.4b.7h.R3) is $O(n^{-7}\log n)$ on that same sequence. The exact physical packet retentions vary with `n`; no false projective consistency across different delays is asserted. Across regulators at the same `n`, the displayed frame identifications are the explicit response maps. Arbitrary fixed finite post-output instruments, including complete outcomes, inherit (F.10.4b.7h.R22) by CPTP contractivity.

<a id="proposition-f104b7h7-actual-sampled-channel-gap-and-clock-scope"></a>**Proposition F.10.4b.7h.7 (Actual Sampled-Channel Gap and Clock Scope).**

###### 4.9 Actual sampled-channel spectral-gap datum

In the proved all-time bound, set $M_n^{\rm mix}=2400n^2$. This is distinct from the number $M_n$ of spectral cells in (F.10.4b.7h.10.12). In this subsection write $\mathcal R_n=\mathcal R_{\tau_n}$ and $\rho_n^{\rm ret}=\tau_n$; $M_n^{\rm mix}$ is the mixing prefactor, while $\vartheta_n$ is a sampled physical duration. Choose

\[
\vartheta_n=\alpha^{-1}\log(4\max\{1,M_n^{\rm mix}\}),\qquad
T_n^{\rm samp}=\Phi_{n,\vartheta_n}.
\]

When $M_n^{\rm mix}\ge1$, this is exactly $\vartheta_n=\alpha^{-1}\log(4M_n^{\rm mix})$. In all cases the stated choice gives $\|T_n^{\rm samp}-\mathcal R_n\|_\diamond\le1/2$. The actual finite-dimensional CPTP channel $T_n^{\rm samp}$ has a unique invariant state $\sigma_n$, its eigenvalue 1 is simple, and every other eigenvalue obeys

\[
|\lambda|\le1/2.
\]

Thus its absolute discrete-channel spectral gap is at least 1/2. More generally choose $\vartheta_n(\delta)=\alpha^{-1}\log(2\max\{1,M_n^{\rm mix}\}/\delta)$, $\delta\in(0,1)$. The raw diamond error is at most $\delta$, giving gap at least $1-\delta$ and $\|\sigma_n-\rho_n^{\rm ret}\|_1\le\delta$.

**Proof.** On every traceless complex matrix $X$, $\mathcal R_n(X)=0$, hence

$$
\|T_n^{\rm samp}X\|_1\le\delta\|X\|_1.
$$

A finite-dimensional CPTP map has an invariant density matrix. Differences between invariant matrices are traceless, so $\delta<1$ gives uniqueness. Every eigenvector with eigenvalue $\lambda\ne 1$ has zero trace, because trace preservation gives $(\lambda-1)\operatorname{Tr}X=0$; therefore $|\lambda|\le\delta$. A traceless eigenvector at 1 is impossible, and a nontrivial Jordan block at 1 is excluded by power boundedness of a CPTP map. Finally $\sigma_n-\rho_n^{\rm ret}=(T_n^{\rm samp}-\mathcal R_n)(\sigma_n)$, giving the invariant-state distance bound. ∎

Choosing, for example, $\delta_n=1/(2n)$ gives invariant-state trace error at most $1/(2n)$, a gap at least $1-1/(2n)$, and still $\vartheta_n(\delta_n)=O(\log n)$ when $M_n^{\rm mix}=K n^2$. This gives a literal spectral-gap record for the **actual sampled boundary channel**. Its physical duration $\vartheta_n=O(\log n)$ is part of the certificate: the dimensionless per-application gap is not a uniform physical generator rate. Repeated application of this channel means repeated uses of the declared preparation/evolution/readout service, with a fresh or reset environment for each use; it is not the same as one uninterrupted evolution to time kϑ_n. No physical repetition is needed merely to certify the spectrum of the actual one-shot channel. If repeated service is claimed, charge its resets and preparation explicitly. The independently proved one-shot all-time bound (F.10.4b.7h.R1) and its all-time extension remain the physical tail certificate.

Optional mathematical iteration estimate: with the invariant replacement $\mathcal R_{\sigma_n}$,
$\|(T_n^{\rm samp})^k-\mathcal R_{\sigma_n}\|_\diamond\le2\delta^k$. The proof iterates the diamond contraction on inputs with zero system partial trace. This must not be asserted for $\Phi_{n,k\vartheta_n}$ without a semigroup theorem.

### F.10.4c Reflection-Positivity Gate for Lorentzian Reconstruction

<a id="theorem-f104b7d-refining-open-carrier-growth-and-passage-certificate"></a>**Theorem F.10.4b.7d (Refining Open-Carrier Growth and Passage Certificate).** On $N\ge2$ qubits, with $n_i=|1\rangle\langle1|_i$, take $H=0$ and the two-body GKLS jumps
$$
L_{ij}=\sqrt{\lambda/(N-1)}\,n_i\sigma_j^+\quad(i\ne j),\qquad\lambda>0.
$$
Start in one infected computational-basis site. The diagonal algebra is invariant, and the infected count $K_t$ has rates
$$
k\longrightarrow k+1\quad\text{at }b_k=\lambda k(N-k)/(N-1),\qquad K_0=1.
$$
Put $m_N(t)=\mathbb EK_t$, $g_N=m_N/N$ and $A_N(t)=2(e^{\lambda t}-1)/(N-1)$. Whenever $A_N(t)<1$,
$$
1-A_N(t)\le m_N(t)e^{-\lambda t}\le1,\qquad
0\le\lambda-(\log m_N)'\le\frac{\lambda A_N(t)}{1-A_N(t)}.
\tag{F.10.4b.7d.1}
$$
Thus on $0\le t\le(1-\delta)\ln N/\lambda$, for each fixed $0<\delta<1$, $g_N=N^{-1}e^{\lambda t}(1+r_N)$ with uniform errors $r_N=O(N^{-\delta})$ and $r_N'/(1+r_N)=O(\lambda N^{-\delta})$.

For $m=\lceil qN\rceil\ge2$, $0<q<1$, let $\tau_m=\inf\{t:K_t\ge m\}$. With $H_0=0$ and $H_k=\sum_{j=1}^k1/j$,
$$
\mathbb Ee^{\theta\tau_m}=\prod_{k=1}^{m-1}\frac{b_k}{b_k-\theta},\quad \theta<\min_{k<m}b_k,
\qquad
\mathbb E\tau_m=\frac{N-1}{\lambda N}(H_{m-1}+H_{N-1}-H_{N-m}).
\tag{F.10.4b.7d.2}
$$
The mean is $(\ln N+\ln(q/(1-q))+\gamma)/\lambda+o(1)$, where $\gamma$ is the Euler--Mascheroni constant, and
$$
\Pr(\tau_m>\mathbb E\tau_m+s)
\le\exp\!\left[-\theta s+\frac{\theta^2\pi^2}{12\lambda^2(1-q)^2(1-\theta/\lambda)}\right],\quad0<\theta<\lambda.
\tag{F.10.4b.7d.3}
$$
Full absorption instead has mean $2(N-1)H_{N-1}/(\lambda N)\sim2\ln N/\lambda$. Its centered upper-tail bound is (F.10.4b.7d.3) with the quadratic term replaced by $\theta^2\pi^2/[3\lambda^2(1-\theta/\lambda)]$. The diagonal-sector spectral gap is $\lambda$, and distance in total variation from the all-infected state is exactly $\Pr(\tau_N>t)$.

*Proof.* A jump is nonzero on a diagonal configuration exactly when $i$ is infected and $j$ susceptible. Each susceptible site then flips at rate $\lambda k/(N-1)$, proving the count reduction and diagonal invariance. The generator gives
$$
m_N'=\lambda m_N-\frac\lambda{N-1}\mathbb E[K_t(K_t-1)].
$$
Thin the births of a Yule process with rates $\lambda k$ to couple $K_t\le Y_t$. Its moment equations give $\mathbb EY_t=e^{\lambda t}$ and $\mathbb E[Y_t(Y_t-1)]=2e^{\lambda t}(e^{\lambda t}-1)$. Variation of constants yields
$$
1-\frac{2(e^{\lambda t}-1-\lambda t)}{N-1}\le m_N(t)e^{-\lambda t}\le1.
$$
Dividing the moment equation by this positive lower bound, weakened to $1-A_N$, proves (F.10.4b.7d.1) and the derivative remainder.

Successive holding times are independent exponentials of rates $b_1,\ldots,b_{m-1}$. Their transform gives (F.10.4b.7d.2), since $b_k^{-1}=(N-1)(1/k+1/(N-k))/(\lambda N)$. Harmonic asymptotics prove its stated leading term. For $k<m$, $b_k\ge\lambda$ and $b_k\ge\lambda(1-q)k$, so $\sum_{k<m}b_k^{-2}\le\pi^2/[6\lambda^2(1-q)^2]$. The power series inequality $-\ln(1-x)-x\le x^2/[2(1-x)]$ gives the centered log transform bound and Chernoff gives (F.10.4b.7d.3). At $m=N$,
$$
\sum_{k<N}b_k^{-2}\le\frac2{\lambda^2}\sum_{k<N}\left(k^{-2}+(N-k)^{-2}\right)\le\frac{2\pi^2}{3\lambda^2},
$$
which proves the full-absorption bound. Likewise $-\ln(1+x)+x\le x^2/2$ gives the lower-tail bound $\Pr(\tau_m<\mathbb E\tau_m-s)\le\exp[-\theta s+\theta^2\sum_{k<m}b_k^{-2}/2]$ for every $\theta>0$. The count generator is upper triangular with eigenvalues $0,-b_1,\ldots,-b_{N-1}$ and minimum nonzero magnitude $\lambda$. Absorption is the only way to reach the limiting point mass, so the asserted variation distance is exact. ∎

<a id="definition-f104c1-finite-pu-reflection-positivity"></a>**Definition F.10.4c.1 (Finite PU Reflection Positivity).** Let $\mathfrak A_E$ be a finite Euclidean history algebra, $\Theta$ an antilinear reflection involution, and $\mathfrak A_+$ its positive-time subalgebra. A normalized linear functional $\Omega_E$ is reflection positive when
$$
\Omega_E(\Theta(F)F)\ge0\qquad(F\in\mathfrak A_+).
\tag{F.10.4c.1}
$$

<a id="theorem-f104c2-finite-reflection-positivity-reconstruction-gate"></a>**Theorem F.10.4c.2 (Finite Reflection-Positivity Reconstruction Gate).** Assume Definition F.10.4c.1, $\Theta(1)=1$, and a Euclidean time step $a>0$. Suppose the linear transfer map $T_E$ preserves $\mathfrak A_+$ and the null space of the form $\langle F,G\rangle_{\mathrm{OS}}=\Omega_E(\Theta(F)G)$, and its induced quotient operator is a positive contraction with spectrum in $(0,1]$. Then the quotient is a finite Hilbert space with a unit vector $[1]$, a nonnegative Hamiltonian
$$
H_{\mathrm{OS}}=-\frac{\hbar}{a}\log T_{\mathrm{OS}},
$$
and unitary evolution $U(t)=e^{-itH_{\mathrm{OS}}/\hbar}$. These data alone do not construct an observable representation, a cyclic vacuum or a local QFT. Those conclusions require a representation and correlation-identification certificate; a vacuum also requires $T_E1-1$ to be null.

Conversely, suppose a Euclidean history realization of a finite Hilbert-space branch supplies a linear map $V:\mathfrak A_+\to\mathcal H$, a unit vector $V1$, and $H\ge0$, with
$$
\Omega_E(\Theta(F)G)=\langle VF,VG\rangle,\qquad
VT_E=e^{-aH/\hbar}V.
$$
If the finite subspace $\operatorname{ran}V$ is invariant under $e^{-aH/\hbar}$, these data satisfy the positivity and transfer hypotheses above. The converse concerns this correlation-preserving realization.

*Proof.* Positivity of the diagonal of the sesquilinear form gives Hermitian symmetry by polarization. Applying positivity to $F+zG$ gives Cauchy--Schwarz. Thus every null vector is orthogonal to every vector, so the quotient by the null space is a Hilbert space. Normalization gives $\|[1]\|^2=1$. Null-space preservation makes $T_{\mathrm{OS}}$ well defined. The finite spectral theorem applied to its eigenvalues $0<q\le1$ gives Hamiltonian eigenvalues $-(\hbar/a)\log q\ge0$ and unitary $U(t)$. If $T_{\mathrm{OS}}[1]=[1]$, then $H_{\mathrm{OS}}[1]=0$. No representation or cyclicity assertion follows from a vector-space quotient alone.

For the converse, the displayed Gram identity proves reflection positivity and identifies the null space with $\ker V$. The intertwining relation preserves that kernel and identifies the quotient transfer with the restriction of $e^{-aH/\hbar}$ to $\operatorname{ran}V$. An invariant subspace of this finite self-adjoint operator is reducing; its restricted eigenvalues lie in $(0,1]$. This proves all the stated finite reconstruction claims. ∎

<a id="corollary-f104c3-reflection-positivity-as-a-correlation-preserving-gate"></a>**Corollary F.10.4c.3 (Reflection Positivity as a Correlation-Preserving Gate).** A Euclidean history functional violating (F.10.4c.1) has no positive-norm Hilbert-space realization with $\Omega_E(\Theta(F)G)=\langle VF,VG\rangle$ for all retained positive-time histories.

*Proof.* Such a realization would give $\Omega_E(\Theta(F)F)=\|VF\|^2\ge0$, contradicting the assumed violation. ∎

<a id="corollary-f104c4-källén-lehmann-spectral-gate-for-ppi-observable-two-point-functions"></a>**Corollary F.10.4c.4 (Källén--Lehmann Spectral Gate for PPI-Observable Two-Point Functions).** Assume a scalar Wightman branch with a positive Hilbert metric, a unique normalized invariant vacuum $\Omega$, a strongly continuous translation representation $U(a)=e^{iP\cdot a}$, and forward-cone spectrum. Use signature $(+---)$ in the spectral formulas below. Let $O=O^\dagger$ be a local scalar operator-valued tempered distribution on a common invariant domain containing $\Omega$, with its vacuum expectation subtracted. For a non-Hermitian field use the adjoint-paired two-point function. Retain the scalar Källén--Lehmann theorem and its time-ordered distributional extension on this branch, including an admissible subtraction/contact prescription.

The positive mass measure $\rho_O$ is supported on $s\ge0$. Choose a spacelike point $p_0^2<0$ and an integer $N\ge0$ with
$$
\int_0^\infty (1+s)^{-N-1}\rho_O(ds)<\infty.
$$
With the convention that the free scalar response is $(p^2-s+i0)^{-1}$, the subtracted response is
$$
G_O^F(p^2)=P_{N-1}(p^2)
+(p^2-p_0^2)^N\int_0^\infty
\frac{\rho_O(ds)}{(s-p_0^2)^N(p^2-s+i0)}.
\tag{F.10.4c.4.1}
$$
The polynomial $P_{N-1}$ belongs to the declared contact prescription; for an unsubtracted branch use $N=0$, $P_{-1}=0$. An isolated positive mass atom gives a positive-residue pole and, with the particle-sector certificate, a stable one-particle contribution. A missing pole in one field is not a completeness or PPI-nullity test.

*Proof.* Smearing is essential: for every test function $f$, the spectral theorem supplies the positive measure
$$
\mu_f(B)=\langle O(f)\Omega,E(B)O(f)\Omega\rangle\ge0.
$$
These measures are supported in the forward cone. The scalar Källén--Lehmann theorem identifies their common covariant two-point distribution by a positive mass-shell measure. Vacuum subtraction removes the separate zero-momentum vacuum contribution. The retained time-ordering and subtraction theorem supplies the dispersion representation; positivity and temperedness alone do not specify its contact extension. For nonreal $p^2$, the stated integrability condition controls the subtracted large-$s$ kernel, which is of order $s^{-N-1}$; the real-axis expression is its distributional boundary value. A mass atom contributes its coefficient times $(p^2-m^2+i0)^{-1}$, proving the residue statement. The existence and hypotheses of the spectral/dispersion import remain part of the QFT branch certificate, beyond the finite Hilbert-space construction of Theorem F.10.4c.2. ∎

<a id="corollary-f104c5-no-finite-dimensional-källén-lehmann-spectral-weight"></a>**Corollary F.10.4c.5 (No Finite-Dimensional Källén--Lehmann Spectral Weight).** Assume the scalar Wightman branch of Corollary F.10.4c.4 on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, with the translations part of a strongly continuous unitary representation of the proper orthochronous Poincaré group or its covering group. Then every vacuum-subtracted smeared field annihilates the vacuum, $O(f)\Omega=0$, and the Källén--Lehmann measure vanishes, $\rho_O=0$. No mass atom, pole or continuum survives. A nonzero Källén--Lehmann measure therefore requires an infinite-dimensional representation space, and no Poincaré-covariant finite quotient of the reflection-positive reconstruction of Theorem F.10.4c.2 supplies one.

*Proof.* Theorem F.0k gives $U(a)=I$, so the joint spectral measure $E$ of $P$ is the point mass $E(\{0\})=I$. For each test function $f$ the positive measure $\mu_f(B)=\langle O(f)\Omega,E(B)O(f)\Omega\rangle$ is therefore $\|O(f)\Omega\|^2\delta_0$. The scalar Källén--Lehmann representation of Corollary F.10.4c.4 writes $\mu_f$ as $\int\rho_O(ds)\,|\hat f|^2\,dm_s$, where $m_s$ is the Lorentz-invariant measure on the forward shell $\{p^2=s,\ p^0\ge0\}$. With at least one spatial dimension, every $m_s$, including the forward light-cone measure for $s=0$, assigns zero mass to the origin. Hence $\|O(f)\Omega\|^2=\mu_f(\{0\})=0$. Choose $f$ with $\hat f$ nowhere zero, for example a Gaussian. The total mass $\int\rho_O(ds)\int|\hat f|^2dm_s$ of $\mu_f$ equals $\|O(f)\Omega\|^2=0$, and since every inner integral is strictly positive, $\rho_O=0$. ∎
