\langle O_1\cdots O_k\rangle
=\int_{\mathcal F_{\mathrm{reg}}}
\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma_\phi^{\otimes k}
O_1\otimes\cdots\otimes O_k\right)\nu(d\phi).
\tag{F.10.4e.3}
$$
Thus a regular field coordinate parametrizes the retained extremal states. A redundant parametrization need not give a unique parameter measure; the state-space de Finetti measure remains the intrinsic object.

*Proof.* Theorem F.10.4e.2 gives the mixture on the state space. Boundedness permits its trace pairing with $O_1\otimes\cdots\otimes O_k$. The pushforward identity then changes that integral to the displayed parameter integral. If the parametrization is a Borel isomorphism onto its image, $\nu=(\sigma^{-1})_*\mu$ is the unique lift. Without such an identification, existence and any uniqueness of a lift are separate data. ∎

<a id="definition-f104e5-quantum-lan-field-certificate"></a>**Definition F.10.4e.5 (Quantum LAN Field Certificate).** Let $\{\sigma_\phi\}_{\phi\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{reg}}}$ be a faithful finite-dimensional regular family supporting an extremal component of Theorem F.10.4e.2, let $\phi_0\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{reg}}$, and write local coordinates as
$$
\phi_N(u)=\phi_0+\frac{u}{\sqrt N},
\qquad
u\in K\Subset T_{\phi_0}\mathcal F_{\mathrm{reg}}.
\tag{F.10.4e.4}
$$
The associated finite experiment is
$$
\mathcal E_N(K)
=
\left\{
\sigma_{\phi_N(u)}^{\otimes N}:u\in K
\right\}.
\tag{F.10.4e.5}
$$
A quantum LAN field certificate at $\phi_0$ is a tuple
$$
\mathfrak L_{\phi_0}
=
(\mathcal G_{\phi_0},\mathcal I_{\phi_0},\Omega_{\phi_0},\Theta_N,\Xi_N,\epsilon_N)
\tag{F.10.4e.6}
$$
such that:

1. $\mathcal G_{\phi_0}(K)=\{G_u:u\in K\}$ is a Gaussian experiment with finitely many canonical modes and identifiable tangent coordinates. It may have classical and quantum parts; finite mode count does not assert finite Hilbert-space rank. The matrix $\mathcal I_{\phi_0}\ge0$ acts on the identifiable tangent quotient, and $\Omega_{\phi_0}$ specifies the commutators of the quantum canonical coordinates.

2. Use root fidelity $F$ and require the overlap normalization
$$
F(G_u,G_v)=
\exp\!\left[-\frac18(u-v)^T\mathcal I_{\phi_0}(u-v)\right].
\tag{F.10.4e.7}
$$
For a classical--quantum experiment, the state norms below are predual norms and the channels act on normal states; on matrix or trace-class states this is the ordinary trace norm.

3. $\Theta_N$ and $\Xi_N$ are CPTP channels satisfying the two-sided deficiency bounds
$$
\sup_{u\in K}
\left\|
\Theta_N(\sigma_{\phi_N(u)}^{\otimes N})-G_u
\right\|_1
\le\epsilon_N,
\tag{F.10.4e.8}
$$
$$
\sup_{u\in K}
\left\|
\Xi_N(G_u)-\sigma_{\phi_N(u)}^{\otimes N}
\right\|_1
\le\epsilon_N,
\tag{F.10.4e.9}
$$
with $\epsilon_N\to0$;

4. For every unbounded polynomial moment retained in the comparison, the certificate supplies finite-experiment and Gaussian probe identifications, bounded cutoffs transported by $\Theta_N^*$, and uniform tail bounds on compact $u$-sets. For each cutoff the bounded-probe comparison error tends to zero; the expectation errors from removing the cutoffs tend uniformly to zero in both experiments. Quantum canonical moments use Weyl, equivalently symmetric, ordering. These conditions are required moment by moment to the prescribed finite order; bounded two-sided deficiency alone does not imply them.

The branch is called a PU-LAN field branch when every retained extremal component admits such a certificate on each compact coordinate patch.

<a id="theorem-f104e6-gaussian-normal-form-of-certified-mpu-fields"></a>**Theorem F.10.4e.6 (Gaussian Normal Form of Certified MPU Fields).** On a PU-LAN field branch, write $\rho_{N,u}=\sigma_{\phi_N(u)}^{\otimes N}$. The following statements hold uniformly for $u$ in a retained compact coordinate set.

1. Every Gaussian bounded probe $B$ is simulated on the finite experiment by $\Theta_N^*B$, and every finite bounded probe $A_N$ is simulated on the Gaussian experiment by $\Xi_N^*A_N$, with expectation error at most $\epsilon_N$ for unit-norm probes. A common limiting probe requires the corresponding probe identification.
2. The Gaussian experiment has vanishing connected cumulants of order at least three for its canonical linear coordinates, with Weyl ordering in the quantum part. Finite-experiment moments and cumulants of a prescribed finite order converge to these values when clause 4 of the certificate holds for all moments involved. Nonlinear functions of Gaussian coordinates need not be Gaussian.
3. The overlap determines
$$
-\log F(G_u,G_v)=\frac18(u-v)^T\mathcal I_{\phi_0}(u-v),
\qquad
\left.\nabla_v^2[-\log F(G_u,G_v)]\right|_{v=u}
=\frac14\mathcal I_{\phi_0}.
\tag{F.10.4e.10}
$$
Equivalently, the Hessian of $-4\log F$ is $\mathcal I_{\phi_0}$. The Gaussian covariance equals $\mathcal I_{\phi_0}^{-1}$ only on an independently certified efficient commuting submodel with nonsingular information matrix; the noncommuting response retains its separate form $\Omega_{\phi_0}$.

*Proof.* Duality and (F.10.4e.8) give
$$
|\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{N,u}\Theta_N^*B)-\operatorname{Tr}(G_uB)|
\le\|B\|\,\epsilon_N.
$$
Likewise, (F.10.4e.9) gives
$$
|\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{N,u}A_N)-\operatorname{Tr}(G_u\Xi_N^*A_N)|
\le\|A_N\|\,\epsilon_N.
$$
For a classical--quantum experiment these are the corresponding state/observable dual pairings. They prove the bounded operational comparison and do not identify observables on different spaces without the channels.

For each polynomial moment in clause 4, insert its bounded cutoff. The two tail errors vanish uniformly, and the intervening bounded-probe error tends to zero by the channel comparison; taking these limits proves convergence of that moment. For Gaussian canonical coordinates the Weyl characteristic function has the form $\exp(i\ell^Tm-\ell^TV\ell/2)$. Its logarithm is quadratic, so all Weyl-ordered connected cumulants of order at least three vanish. A cumulant of any prescribed finite order is a finite polynomial in moments up to that order, which proves its convergence under the same certificates. Differentiating the overlap quadratic gives $\mathcal I_{\phi_0}/4$ for $-\log F$, and $\mathcal I_{\phi_0}$ for $-4\log F$. Neither this calculation nor the channel bounds identify the covariance with the inverse Fisher matrix outside the separately certified commuting submodel. ∎

<a id="corollary-f104e7-gaussian-overlap-gate-for-flavor-and-field-profiles"></a>**Corollary F.10.4e.7 (Gaussian Overlap Gate for Flavor and Field Profiles).** A Gaussian overlap kernel imported from a PU-LAN certificate must use its root-fidelity normalization: the Hessian of $-\log F$ is $\mathcal I_{\phi_0}/4$, or equivalently the Hessian of $-4\log F$ is $\mathcal I_{\phi_0}$. Use in a field, flavor or packet-profile sector also requires an identification with the certified tangent coordinates and probes. Equality of a Hessian by itself is not a LAN certificate.

*Proof.* Theorem F.10.4e.6 gives the normalized quadratic and the channel-mediated probe comparisons. De Finetti supplies a mixture of extremal states but neither these local comparison channels nor their Gaussian overlap normalization. Thus a sector lacking the LAN and identification certificates retains the Gaussian kernel as an additional branch input. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104e8-explicit-commuting-lan-with-square-root-deficiency-rate"></a>**Theorem F.10.4e.8 (Explicit Commuting LAN with Square-Root Deficiency Rate).** Fix $0<a\le1/2$, $p_0,p=p_0+t/\sqrt n\in[a,1-a]$, $|t|\le T$, and set $v=p(1-p)$, $v_0=p_0(1-p_0)$, $v_*=a(1-a)$. On $\rho_{n,t}=\operatorname{diag}(1-p,p)^{\otimes n}$ measure the computational basis, count $K$, and output $X=(K-np_0+U)/\sqrt n$, with independent $U$ uniform on $[-1/2,1/2)$. Denote this normal CPTP channel by $\Theta_n$. Its parameter-independent inverse comparison $\Xi_n$ rounds $np_0+\sqrt nX$, clips to $[0,n]$, and prepares the uniform bit-string mixture of that count. Then $\Xi_n\Theta_n\rho_{n,t}=\rho_{n,t}$. For $G_t=N(t,v_0)$ both full predual-norm errors are at most
$$
B_n=\min\left\{2,\sqrt{2\left[C_{a,T}/n+L_{n,a}\beta_{n,a}\right]}\right\}=O_{a,T}(n^{-1/2}),
\tag{F.10.4e.11}
$$
where
$$
\beta_{n,a}=\min(1,2e^{-na^2/2}),\quad
L_{n,a}=n\ln(1/a)+1/a+\tfrac12\ln(2\pi n),
$$
$$
C_{a,T}=\frac5{24v_*}+\frac1{2a^2}+\frac1{12}
+\frac{(1-2a)^2T^2}{4v_*^2}.
$$
The Gaussian information is $\mathcal I=1/v_0$ and root fidelity is $F(G_t,G_s)=e^{-(t-s)^2/(8v_0)}$. This commuting family has a separately efficient estimator $(K-np_0)/\sqrt n$, of variance $v$, and covers every faithful Bernoulli base locally. Its likelihood remainder and all prescribed finite polynomial moments satisfy clause 4 of Definition F.10.4e.5.

*Proof.* The disjoint jitter cells round back to their counts; conditional on a count the original bit strings are uniform. Thus the exact inverse holds and contraction transfers the forward error to the reverse channel. Let $S=K/n$, $\Delta=S-p$ and $D(s\Vert p)=s\ln(s/p)+(1-s)\ln((1-s)/(1-p))$, including its continuous endpoints. Since its fourth derivative in $s$ is positive,
$$
D(s\Vert p)\ge\frac{(s-p)^2}{2v}+\frac{(2p-1)(s-p)^3}{6v^2}
$$
on all of $[0,1]$. Centered Bernoulli moments give $\mathbb E\Delta^2=v/n$, $\mathbb E\Delta^3=v(1-2p)/n^2$, so $n\mathbb ED(S\Vert p)\ge1/2-(1-2p)^2/(6nv)$. Convexity gives $0\le D(s\Vert p)\le\ln(1/a)$.

On $A=\{a/2\le S\le1-a/2\}$, Robbins's factorial bound (1955), $\ln m!=(m+1/2)\ln m-m+\tfrac12\ln(2\pi)+r_m$ with $0<r_m<1/(12m)$, gives
$$
H(K)\ge n\mathbb E[D(S\Vert p)1_A]+\tfrac12\ln(2\pi n)\Pr(A)
+\tfrac12\mathbb E[\ln(S(1-S))1_A]-\frac1{12n}.
$$
No factorial is evaluated at zero. A centered Bernoulli log moment generating function has second derivative at most $1/4$, so Chernoff gives $b:=\Pr(A^c)\le\beta_{n,a}$. For $f(s)=\ln(s(1-s))$, $f''\ge-8/a^2$ on this interval. Taylor's lower bound, $\mathbb E\Delta=0$, $|\Delta|\le1$ and $|f'(p)|\le1/a$ yield
$$
\tfrac12\mathbb E[f(S)1_A]\ge\tfrac12\ln v-b/a-2v/(na^2).
$$
Here the truncated linear term costs $b/a$; it is not replaced by zero. Removing the divergence tail costs $n\ln(1/a)b$, and the prefactor costs $\tfrac12\ln(2\pi n)b$. Consequently
$$
H(K)\ge\tfrac12\ln(2\pi e n v)-E_{n,a,p},\quad
E_{n,a,p}=\frac{(1-2p)^2}{6nv}+\frac{2v}{na^2}+\frac1{12n}+L_{n,a}\beta_{n,a}.
$$
The jittered density has differential entropy $H(K)-\frac12\ln n$, mean $t$ and variance $v+1/(12n)$. Direct integration against $G_t$ therefore gives
$$
D(\Theta_n\rho_{n,t}\Vert G_t)
\le E_{n,a,p}+\frac1{24nv_0}
+\frac12\left(\frac v{v_0}-1-\ln\frac v{v_0}\right).
$$
The last term is at most $(v-v_0)^2/[4\min(v,v_0)^2]$, by its second derivative $1/(2v^2)$, and $|v-v_0|\le(1-2a)T/\sqrt n$. Using $v\le1/4$ gives $C_{a,T}/n+L_{n,a}\beta_{n,a}$. To obtain the full-$L^1$ bound without importing a limit theorem, partition at $\{q\ge g\}$. Log-sum bounds $D(q\Vert g)$ below by the binary relative entropy of its masses $\alpha,\gamma$. Its second derivative in $\alpha$ is $1/[\alpha(1-\alpha)]\ge4$, so it is at least $2(\alpha-\gamma)^2=\|q-g\|_1^2/2$. This proves (F.10.4e.11), including $n=1$ and empty central events.

For the likelihood record, choose $a_0>0$ with $p_0\in[2a_0,1-2a_0]$ and $T/\sqrt n\le a_0$. With $Z_n=(K-np_0)/\sqrt n$, Taylor expansion of the two scalar logarithms gives
$$
\log\frac{dP_{n,t}}{dP_{n,0}}=tZ_n/v_0-t^2/(2v_0)+R_n,
\quad \sup_{|t|\le T}|R_n|\le\frac{T^2|Z_n|/(4a_0^2)+T^3/(6a_0^3)}{\sqrt n}.
$$
The linear and quadratic terms follow by substituting $K=np_0+\sqrt nZ_n$; the remainder uses $|\log(1+x)-x+x^2/2|\le2|x|^3/3$ at $|x|\le1/2$. The same Bernoulli Chernoff argument gives $\Pr(|X|>T+y)\le2e^{-2(y-1/2)^2}$ for $y\ge1$, uniformly in $n,t$. The Gaussian obeys a stronger bound. Layer-cake integration proves uniform integrability of every fixed polynomial order. Bounded cutoffs $x^d1_{|x|\le L}$ are transported by $\Theta_n^*$, and their bounded error is at most $L^dB_n$; their two tails vanish uniformly. This proves the moment and likelihood assertions. Gaussian integration gives root fidelity. The count score is $(Z_n-t)/v$, so its Fisher information is $1/v$ and the unbiased count estimator attains the Cauchy--Schwarz Cramér--Rao bound. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104e9-explicit-noncommuting-fixed-spectrum-qubit-lan"></a>**Theorem F.10.4e.9 (Explicit Noncommuting Fixed-Spectrum Qubit LAN).** Fix $1/2<\mu<1$, $q=1-\mu$, $r=2\mu-1$, $p=q/\mu$, $\nu=q/r$ and $|u|\le M$ in $\mathbb R^2$. Set
$$
\rho_{n,u}=\left[U_n(u)\operatorname{diag}(\mu,q)U_n(u)^*\right]^{\otimes n},\qquad
U_n(u)=e^{i(u_x\sigma_x+u_y\sigma_y)/\sqrt n}.
$$
On Fock space let $N=a^*a$, $Q=(a+a^*)/\sqrt2$, $P=(a-a^*)/(i\sqrt2)$, $D(\alpha)=e^{\alpha a^*-\bar\alpha a}$ and
$$
\tau=(1-p)\sum_{k\ge0}p^k|k\rangle\langle k|,\quad
\alpha_u=\sqrt r(-u_y+iu_x),\quad G_u=D(\alpha_u)\tau D(\alpha_u)^*.
$$
There are parameter-independent normal CPTP channels $\Theta_n,\Xi_n$ whose two full trace-norm errors are at most
$$
\epsilon_n=\min\left\{2,\frac{4M}{\sqrt r}
\left[\frac\mu r\sqrt{\frac{(1-r^2)B_1}{n}}+\frac{\sqrt{B_3}}n\right]
+\frac{2q}r e^{-nr^2/2}\right\},
\tag{F.10.4e.12}
$$
where $A=rM^2$, $B_1=1+\nu+A$ and
$$
B_3=A^3+(9\nu+6)A^2+(18\nu^2+24\nu+7)A+6\nu^3+12\nu^2+7\nu+1.
$$
The rate is compact-uniform $O(n^{-1/2})$, including compact base-spectrum intervals in $(1/2,1)$. The Gaussian mean, covariance and commutator are
$$
m_u=\sqrt{2r}(-u_y,u_x),\quad V=(2r)^{-1}I_2,\quad[Q,P]=iI,
\qquad F(G_u,G_v)=e^{-r^2|u-v|^2/2}.
\tag{F.10.4e.13}
$$
Thus $\mathcal I=4r^2I_2$. Every prescribed finite Weyl polynomial moment has transported probes and compact-uniform cutoff tails, and the family has a state-weighted operator-log remainder of order $n^{-1/2}$.

*Proof.* We construct the channels rather than import a LAN convergence theorem. The spin-block construction is the one used by Guţă and Kahn (2006). Let $J_z=\frac12\sum_i\sigma_z^{(i)}$ and $J_\pm=\sum_i(\sigma_x^{(i)}\pm i\sigma_y^{(i)})/2$. The commutators $[J_z,J_\pm]=\pm J_\pm$ and $[J_+,J_-]=2J_z$ decompose the finite space into spin ladders. Starting at a highest-weight vector of weight $j$, repeated lowering has squared norms $k!(2j)(2j-1)\cdots(2j-k+1)$; its normalized ladder has basis $|j,j-k\rangle$, $0\le k\le2j$. Its orthogonal complement is invariant, so iteration gives a fixed unitary $S_n$ and
$$
(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}=\bigoplus_j\mathcal H_j\otimes\mathbb C^{d_j},\qquad
d_j=\binom{n}{n/2-j}-\binom{n}{n/2-j-1}.
$$
The multiplicity follows by subtracting the dimensions of adjacent nonnegative $J_z$ weight spaces; out-of-range binomial coefficients vanish. Here $j$ runs from $0$ or $1/2$ to $n/2$. Put $L=2j$ and $a_j=n/2+j$. Directly writing the product state as $(\mu q)^{n/2}e^{\ln(\mu/q)J_z}$ gives
$$
S_n\rho_{n,u}S_n^*=\bigoplus_jw_n(j)\rho_{j,u}\otimes I_{d_j}/d_j,
$$
$$
\tau_j=\frac{1-p}{1-p^{L+1}}\sum_{k=0}^Lp^k|j,j-k\rangle\langle j,j-k|,
\quad\rho_{j,u}=e^{2i(u_xJ_x+u_yJ_y)/\sqrt n}\tau_j e^{-2i(u_xJ_x+u_yJ_y)/\sqrt n},
$$
$$
w_n(j)=d_j\mu^{a_j}q^{n-a_j}\frac{1-p^{L+1}}{1-p}.
$$
These weights are normalized and independent of $u$. With $b_{n,\mu}(a)=\binom{n}{a}\mu^aq^{n-a}$,
$$
w_n(j)=b_{n,\mu}(a_j)\frac\mu r\frac{L+1}{a_j+1}(1-p^{L+1})\le\frac\mu r b_{n,\mu}(a_j).
$$
Cauchy--Schwarz on the binomial variance and the identity $p^{2a-n+1}b_{n,\mu}(a)=p b_{n,q}(a)$ imply
$$
\sum_jw_n(j)|L/n-r|\le\frac\mu r\frac{\sqrt{1-r^2}}{\sqrt n},\qquad
\sum_jw_n(j)p^{L+1}\le\frac qr e^{-nr^2/2}.
\tag{F.10.4e.14}
$$
The second inequality uses the Bernoulli Chernoff estimate above on $a\ge n/2$.

Let $V_j|j,j-k\rangle=|k\rangle$ and $P_L=\sum_{k=0}^L|k\rangle\langle k|$. The forward channel applies $S_n$, pinches the blocks, traces multiplicities and embeds each block with $V_j$. Define the CPTP compression/reset
$$
C_j(\omega)=V_j^*P_L\omega P_LV_j+\operatorname{Tr}((I-P_L)\omega)|j,j\rangle\langle j,j|.
$$
The reverse prepares $\bigoplus_jw_n(j)C_j(\omega)\otimes I_{d_j}/d_j$ and conjugates by $S_n^*$. Both are normal CPTP on all inputs. If $e_j=\|V_j\rho_{j,u}V_j^*-G_u\|_1$, convexity gives the forward error at most $\sum_jw_ne_j$; contraction of $C_j$ gives the same reverse bound because it inverts the block embedding exactly.

The zero-extended finite generator on Fock space is, with $c=u_x+iu_y$ and $s=L/n$,
$$
H_{n,j}=c a^*\sqrt{(L-N)_+/n}+\bar c\sqrt{(L-N)_+/n}\,a,
\qquad H_\infty=\sqrt r(ca^*+\bar ca).
$$
The boundary lowering coefficient vanishes on $|L+1\rangle$, so this is the exact block generator extended by zero. The inequalities $|\sqrt x-\sqrt r|\le|x-r|/\sqrt r$ and $|(s-k/n)_+-r|\le|s-r|+k/n$ give, by the two weighted shifts,
$$
\|(H_{n,j}-H_\infty)\psi\|
\le\frac{2M}{\sqrt r}\left[|s-r|\|(N+1)^{1/2}\psi\|+n^{-1}\|(N+1)^{3/2}\psi\|\right].
\tag{F.10.4e.15}
$$
The thermal coherent-state mixture is $\tau=\int|z\rangle\langle z|e^{-|z|^2/\nu}d^2z/(\pi\nu)$: angular integration kills unequal powers and radial $\gamma$ integration gives $(1-p)p^k$. Displacement shifts $z$. Conditional on $z$, the number law is Poisson with mean $|z|^2$. Expanding complex Gaussian moments gives, for $0\le t\le1$,
$$
\operatorname{Tr}D(t\alpha_u)\tau D(t\alpha_u)^*(N+1)\le B_1,\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}D(t\alpha_u)\tau D(t\alpha_u)^*(N+1)^3\le B_3.
$$
In detail $\mathbb E|Z+\beta|^{2\ell}=\sum_{k=0}^\ell\binom{\ell}{k}^2k!\nu^k|\beta|^{2(\ell-k)}$; for a Poisson variable $K$, $\mathbb E(K+1)^3=\lambda^3+6\lambda^2+7\lambda+1$. These identities give precisely the displayed constants.

Apply Duhamel to the thermal purification $\Psi=\sqrt{1-p}\sum_kp^{k/2}|k,k\rangle$ and the first-factor generators. The displaced purifications have finite third number moment, so (F.10.4e.15) is integrably bounded along the path. The oscillator field is self-adjoint; displaced number vectors are polynomials applied to a coherent vector and lie in every needed number domain. Finite sums in the purifying factor justify differentiation first, and this bound passes the integral to the full vector. The norm difference of the two purified unitaries is at most $(2M/\sqrt r)(|s-r|\sqrt{B_1}+\sqrt{B_3}/n)$. Pure-state trace distance is at most twice vector distance. The embedded initial thermal truncation has exact distance $2p^{L+1}$ from $\tau$. Thus
$$
e_j\le2p^{L+1}+\frac{4M}{\sqrt r}\left(|L/n-r|\sqrt{B_1}+\sqrt{B_3}/n\right).
$$
Averaging with (F.10.4e.14) proves (F.10.4e.12).

Normal ordering and the coherent-state Gaussian integral give characteristic function $\exp(it\cdot m_u-|t|^2/(4r))$, proving the Gaussian data. For root fidelity, rotate the displacement difference $\delta$ to a real quadrature. Measuring $Q$ bounds quantum root fidelity above by the normal affinity $e^{-r|\delta|^2/2}$. This measurement bound follows by inserting the measurement resolution in $\operatorname{Tr}(\sqrt\rho\sqrt\sigma U)$ and applying Hilbert--Schmidt Cauchy--Schwarz, then refining finite partitions. A matching lower bound uses the thermal purification: its joint displacement overlap is
$$
\langle\Psi|D_a(\delta)D_b(\beta)|\Psi\rangle
=\exp\left[-\frac{2\nu+1}2(|\delta|^2+|\beta|^2)+2\sqrt{\nu(\nu+1)}\operatorname{Re}(\delta\beta)\right].
$$
To check it, the two annihilators $(a-\sqrt p\,b^*)/\sqrt{1-p}$ and $(b-\sqrt p\,a^*)/\sqrt{1-p}$ are canonical and annihilate $\Psi$. Normal ordering in them gives squared displacement parameters $(\delta-\sqrt p\bar\beta)/\sqrt{1-p}$ and $(\beta-\sqrt p\bar\delta)/\sqrt{1-p}$, yielding the formula. Choose $\beta=2\sqrt{\nu(\nu+1)}\bar\delta/(2\nu+1)$. Trace-norm duality bounds this purification overlap by the root fidelity and gives $e^{-r|\delta|^2/2}$. Both bounds coincide and $|\alpha_u-\alpha_v|^2=r|u-v|^2$, proving (F.10.4e.13).

For the remainder put $b=\frac12\ln(\mu/q)$, $\bar Z_n=n^{-1}\sum_i\sigma_z^{(i)}$ and $\Delta_n=(2b/\sqrt n)(\sum_i\sigma_y^{(i)},-\sum_i\sigma_x^{(i)})$. Exact Pauli rotation and sine/cosine remainders give
$$
\log\rho_{n,u}-\log\rho_{n,0}
=u\cdot\Delta_n-2b|u|^2\bar Z_n+R_n^{\mathrm{op}},\qquad
\|R_n^{\mathrm{op}}\|\le\frac{4bM^3}{3\sqrt n}+\frac{2bM^4}{3n}.
$$
Under any $\rho_{n,v}$ with $|v|\le M$, product variance and its rotated mean give $\|\bar Z_n-rI\|_{2,\rho_{n,v}}\le n^{-1/2}+2rM^2/n$. Replacing $\bar Z_n$ by $rI$ therefore has an additional error at most $2bM^2(n^{-1/2}+2rM^2/n)$. This is an ordinary operator-log record; its quadratic coefficient $4br$ is distinct from the fidelity information $4r^2$.

To prove the moment record, for each integer $h\ge1$ let $S(a,b)$ denote Stirling numbers of the second kind and define
$$
m_h=\sum_{\ell=0}^h S(h+1,\ell+1)\ell!\nu^\ell,
\quad B_h=\sum_{\ell=0}^h S(h+1,\ell+1)\sum_{k=0}^\ell\binom{\ell}{k}^2k!\nu^kA^{\ell-k},
\quad C_h=\max\{m_he^{Mh2^h},B_h\},\quad C_0=1.
$$
The falling-factorial expansion of $(K+1)^h$ and the preceding Gaussian moment formula bound the target number moment by $B_h$. A geometric law conditioned on $k\le L$ has increasing moments at most $m_h$. Along the finite block unitary, the off-diagonal coefficient is at most $M\sqrt{k+1}$. For $f_k=(k+1)^h$, $f_{k+1}-f_k\le h2^{h-1}(k+1)^{h-1}$. The commutator derivative and $2\sqrt{f_kf_{k+1}}|\psi_k\psi_{k+1}|\le f_k|\psi_k|^2+f_{k+1}|\psi_{k+1}|^2$ give $|\partial_t\langle(N+1)^h\rangle|\le Mh2^h\langle(N+1)^h\rangle$. Gronwall proves the conditional bound $C_h$ for every block and therefore for the forward output.

For a Weyl polynomial $W$ of degree $d$, let $K_W$ be the sum over its word coefficients of their absolute values times $2^{e/2}(e+1)^{e/2}$ for word length $e$. Expanding $Q,P$ into shifts proves $W^*W,WW^*\le K_W^2(N+1)^d$ as forms. Let the bounded target probe be $P_LWP_L$, transported by $\Theta_n^*$, and the uncut finite probe be $S_n^*[\bigoplus_j V_j^*WV_j\otimes I_{d_j}]S_n$. The latter has exactly the forward-output expectation; it is not a product of adjoint-transformed linear probes. For either output state, Markov and Hilbert--Schmidt Cauchy--Schwarz give
$$
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(I-P_L)\le C_h/(L+2)^h,\qquad
|\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(W-P_LWP_L)|\le2K_W\sqrt{C_dC_h}/(L+2)^{h/2}.
$$
Here split $W-P_LWP_L=(I-P_L)W+P_LW(I-P_L)$ and use both form bounds. The full moment error is consequently at most
$$
K_W(L+1)^{d/2}\epsilon_n+4K_W\sqrt{C_dC_h}/(L+2)^{h/2}.
\tag{F.10.4e.16}
$$
Taking $n\to\infty$ and then $L\to\infty$ proves clause 4 for every retained finite order. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104e10-correlated-three-coordinate-qubit-lan-certificate"></a>**Theorem F.10.4e.10 (Correlated Three-Coordinate Qubit LAN Certificate).** Fix a known base $\mu_0\in(1/2,1)$ and compact parameters $|t|\le T$, $|u|\le M$. Put $\mu=\mu_0+t/\sqrt n$, $q_0=1-\mu_0$, $r_0=2\mu_0-1$, $v_0=\mu_0q_0$ and
$$
\rho_{n,t,u}=\left[U_n(u)\operatorname{diag}(\mu,1-\mu)U_n(u)^*\right]^{\otimes n},\qquad
\Gamma_{t,u}(x)=g_t(x)G_{0,u},
$$
where $g_t=N(t,v_0)$ and $G_{0,u}$ is the base-spectrum oscillator of Theorem F.10.4e.9. The classical--quantum predual norm is $\int\|H(x)\|_1dx$. Define
$$
\delta=\min\{(\mu_0-1/2)/2,(1-\mu_0)/2\},\quad
\mu_\pm=\mu_0\pm\delta,\quad r_\pm=2\mu_\pm-1,\quad q_+=1-\mu_-,
\quad\nu_*=q_+/r_-,\quad D_*=\mu_+/r_-.
$$
For $n\ge\max\{1,\lceil(T/\delta)^2\rceil\}$, use Theorem F.10.4e.9's fixed Schur transform and block maps, and let $\Pi_j$ project onto its $j$-th direct summand. Let $c_n=\lceil n/2\rceil$, $a=n/2+j$, and let $\kappa_a(x)$ be the uniform density on
$$
I_a=[(a-n\mu_0-1/2)/\sqrt n,(a-n\mu_0+1/2)/\sqrt n).
$$
The forward channel retains the block label jointly with its quantum state:
$$
\Theta_n(A)(x)=\sum_{a=c_n}^n\kappa_a(x)V_j\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{mult}}(\Pi_jS_nAS_n^*\Pi_j)V_j^*.
\tag{F.10.4e.17}
$$
Round $n\mu_0+\sqrt n x$ and clip to $[c_n,n]$; let $E_a$ be that partition of the real line, including unbounded endpoint cells. The reverse channel is
$$
\Xi_n(H)=S_n^*\left[\bigoplus_{a=c_n}^n
\left\{\int_{E_a}C_j(H(x))dx\right\}\otimes I_{d_j}/d_j\right]S_n.
\tag{F.10.4e.18}
$$
Both channels are parameter-independent normal CPTP, and $\Xi_n\Theta_n\rho_{n,t,u}=\rho_{n,t,u}$ exactly. They have two-sided compact-uniform deficiency bounded by
$$
\varepsilon_n=\min\{2,B_n+J_n+Q_n+Z_n\}=O_{\mu_0,T,M}(n^{-1/2}),
\tag{F.10.4e.19}
$$
where $B_n$ is (F.10.4e.11) with $a=(1-\mu_0)/2$ and $p_0=\mu_0$, once $T/\sqrt n\le a$; use the bound $2$ otherwise. The other terms are
$$
J_n=\min\{2,(r_-\sqrt n)^{-1}+2q_+/(r_-n)+D_*e^{-nr_-^2/2}\},
$$
$$
Q_n=\min\left\{2,\frac{4M}{\sqrt{r_-}}\left[\frac{D_*\sqrt{B_{1,*}}}{\sqrt n}+\frac{\sqrt{B_{3,*}}}n\right]+\frac{2q_+}{r_-}e^{-nr_-^2/2}\right\},
\quad
Z_n=\min\{2,[2/(\mu_-r_-)+2M/r_-]T/\sqrt n\}.
$$
Here $B_{1,*},B_{3,*}$ are the nonnegative polynomials in Theorem F.10.4e.9 evaluated at $\nu_*$ and $A_*=r_+M^2$. The Gaussian canonical covariance and commutator on $(X,Q,P)$ are
$$
V=\operatorname{diag}(v_0,(2r_0)^{-1},(2r_0)^{-1}),\qquad
\Omega=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&0\\0&0&1\\0&-1&0\end{pmatrix},
$$
$$
F(\Gamma_{t,u},\Gamma_{s,v})
=\exp[-(t-s)^2/(8v_0)-r_0^2|u-v|^2/2],\qquad
\mathcal I=\operatorname{diag}(1/v_0,4r_0^2,4r_0^2).
\tag{F.10.4e.20}
$$
The experiment has all prescribed finite mixed classical--Weyl moment records and a compact-uniform state-weighted operator-log remainder of order $n^{-1/2}$. It covers every faithful nondegenerate qubit base and compact local coordinate patch.

*Proof.* The forward operations are Schur conjugation, pinching, partial trace, conditional embedding and jittering. The reverse integrates a classical partition, applies the CPTP compression/reset and prepares a maximally mixed multiplicity. Thus both act on all normal input states. The actual forward model is
$$
\Theta_n\rho_{n,t,u}(x)=\sum_aw_\mu(j)\kappa_a(x)\sigma_{\mu,j,u},\qquad
\sigma_{\mu,j,u}=V_j\rho_{\mu,j,u}V_j^*.
$$
Every jitter cell rounds to its original block and $C_j(\sigma_{\mu,j,u})=\rho_{\mu,j,u}$. This proves the exact model inverse without asserting an inverse on discarded cross-block coherences or multiplicity states. Contraction bounds the reverse deficiency by the joint forward deficiency.

Let $b_\mu(a)=\binom{n}{a}\mu^a(1-\mu)^{n-a}$ and $r=2\mu-1$, $q=1-\mu$, $p=q/\mu$. The exact spin-weight ratio is
$$
\frac{w_\mu(j)}{b_\mu(a)}=R_\mu(a)(1-p^{2a-n+1}),\quad
R_\mu(a)=\frac{\mu(2a-n+1)}{r(a+1)},\quad
R_\mu(a)-1=\frac{a-n\mu+q}{r(a+1)}.
$$
Extend $w$ by zero below $c_n$. Cauchy--Schwarz for the first numerator and the tilted-binomial identity in (F.10.4e.14) for the second give
$$
\sum_{a=0}^n|w_\mu(a)-b_\mu(a)|
\le\frac{\sqrt{n\mu q}+q}{r(c_n+1)}+\frac\mu r e^{-nr^2/2}\le J_n.
$$
The omitted lower binomial tail and the tilted upper tail are both bounded by $e^{-nr^2/2}$, also at odd $n$, since the omitted integers lie below $n/2$. Jittering is a contraction, so the forward classical marginal differs from $g_t$ by at most $J_n+B_n$.

Theorem F.10.4e.9's block estimate holds at the actual $\mu$. Its constants are bounded by the starred constants and its spin average by $D_*/\sqrt n$, giving quantum error $Q_n$ against $G_{\mu,u}$. Differentiating the geometric probabilities gives $\sum_k|\partial_\mu[(1-p)p^k]|\le2/(\mu r)$, so $\|\tau_\mu-\tau_0\|_1\le2|\mu-\mu_0|/(\mu_-r_-)$. Displacement by $\zeta$ changes a thermal state of parameter $r$ by at most $2|\zeta|/\sqrt r$: on its purification use $\|(e^{iK}-I)\Psi\|\le\|K\Psi\|$ with field variance $|\zeta|^2/r$, followed by partial trace. Since $|\sqrt r-\sqrt{r_0}|\le|\mu-\mu_0|/\sqrt{r_-}$, changing the thermal state and displacement to the fixed base costs at most $Z_n$.

Insert the comparison state $q_{n,t}(x)G_{0,u}$, with the actual classical marginal. Its quantum difference is exactly the actual spin-weighted average of conditional trace distances and is bounded by $Q_n+Z_n$. Its remaining difference from $\Gamma$ is the classical $L^1$ distance bounded by $B_n+J_n$. This proves (F.10.4e.19) with all finite correlations retained. The entropy rate of Theorem F.10.4e.8 is the square-root-rate term; no $n^{-1/4}$ loss is required. The product Gaussian characteristic function and root affinity give (F.10.4e.20).

Here is a quantitative remainder record. Put $a_0=(1-\mu_0)/2$, $b_0=\frac12\ln(\mu_0/q_0)$, $b_+=\frac12\ln(\mu_+/(1-\mu_+))$, $v_*=\mu_+(1-\mu_+)$,
$$
K_z=\sum_i(I+\sigma_z^{(i)})/2,\quad Z=(K_z-n\mu_0I)/\sqrt n,\quad
\Delta_t=Z/v_0,\quad(\Delta_x,\Delta_y)=\frac{2b_0}{\sqrt n}(\sum_i\sigma_y^{(i)},-\sum_i\sigma_x^{(i)}).
$$
Then
$$
\log\rho_{n,t,u}-\log\rho_{n,0,0}
=t\Delta_t+u_x\Delta_x+u_y\Delta_y-\left[t^2/(2v_0)+2b_0r_0|u|^2\right]I+R_n,
$$
and uniformly in both $(t,u)$ and the evaluation state $\rho_{n,s,v}$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\|R_n\|_{2,\rho_{n,s,v}}\le{}&\frac{T^2(1/2+T+r_+M^2/\sqrt n)/(4a_0^2)+T^3/(6a_0^3)}{\sqrt n}
+\frac{4b_+M^3}{3\sqrt n}+\frac{2b_+M^4}{3n}\\
&+\frac{T(M+2r_+M^2)}{v_*\sqrt n}
+2M^2\left[b_+\left(\frac{1+2T}{\sqrt n}+\frac{2r_+M^2}{n}\right)+\frac{r_0T}{2v_*\sqrt n}\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.10.4e.21}
$$
To prove it, split the log difference into the unrotated spectral change and the rotation of the log at $\mu$. Theorem F.10.4e.8's scalar Taylor bound gives $[T^2|Z|/(4a_0^2)+T^3/(6a_0^3)]/\sqrt n$. Under the evaluation product state, $\operatorname{Var}Z\le1/4$ and $|\mathbb EZ|\le T+r_+M^2/\sqrt n$, proving its first term. The sine/cosine bounds of Theorem F.10.4e.9 give the next two terms. The difference $|b_\mu-b_0|\le T/(2v_*\sqrt n)$ multiplies $2F_u$, where $F_u=(u_x\sum\sigma_y-u_y\sum\sigma_x)/\sqrt n$ has standard deviation at most $M$ and mean magnitude at most $2r_+M^2$, giving the next term. Finally $\|n^{-1}\sum\sigma_z-r_0I\|_2\le(1+2T)/\sqrt n+2r_+M^2/n$; separating $b_\mu\bar Z-b_0r_0I$ proves the last term. This establishes (F.10.4e.21) by the triangle inequality.

For the mixed moments use Theorem F.10.4e.9's constants $C_h$ with $\nu_*,A_*$; its proof was conditional in every block, so the same bound holds at every classical coordinate of the forward output. The weight domination $w_\mu\le D_*b_\mu$ gives
$$
\Pr(|X|>y)\le2D_*e^{-2(y-T-1/2)^2},\qquad y>T+1/2,
$$
also for the target. For $k\ge1$ set
$$
A_k=D_*2^{k-1}\left[(T+1/2)^k+k2^{-k/2}\Gamma(k/2)\right],\quad A_0=1,
$$
$$
A_k(R)=2D_*\left[R^ke^{-2(R-T-1/2)^2}+k\int_R^\infty y^{k-1}e^{-2(y-T-1/2)^2}dy\right],
\quad A_0(R)=2D_*e^{-2(R-T-1/2)^2}.
$$
Layer cake gives $\mathbb E|X|^k\le A_k$ and its tail at most $A_k(R)$; the centered binomial integral is $k2^{-k/2}\Gamma(k/2)$. Conditional number control gives $\mathbb E[|X|^k(N+1)^h]\le A_kC_h$, despite finite correlations.

For $F(x,Q,P)=\sum_kx^kW_k(Q,P)$ use cutoff $1_{|x|\le R}\sum_kx^kP_LW_kP_L$ and its exact adjoint transport. Its finite uncut probe is the block-diagonal matrix with $j$-block
$$
\sum_k\left[\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}\left(\frac{a-n\mu_0+z}{\sqrt n}\right)^k dz\right]V_j^*W_kV_j\otimes I_{d_j}.
$$
For degrees $d_k$ and word constants $K_k$ as in Theorem F.10.4e.9, the two experiment tails and bounded error sum to at most
$$
\varepsilon_n\sum_kR^kK_k(L+1)^{d_k/2}
+2\sum_kK_k\sqrt{C_{d_k}}A_k(R)
+4\sum_kK_k\sqrt{C_{d_k}C_h}A_k/(L+2)^{h/2}.
$$
Indeed the classical tail uses the conditional polynomial bound; the number tail uses the two conditional Cauchy--Schwarz estimates already proved. Taking $n\to\infty$ first, then $R,L\to\infty$, proves every retained finite mixed moment. Cumulants are finite polynomials of these moments, with limiting higher canonical Weyl cumulants zero because the joint characteristic function is quadratic.

Every faithful nondegenerate qubit base is a known unitary conjugate of the stated diagonal base. The three tangent derivatives $\sigma_z,r_0\sigma_y,-r_0\sigma_x$ are independent, so the inverse-function theorem gives a regular full-dimensional chart. Conjugating the finite channels covers each orientation with the same estimates, and every compact tangent set fits some $T,M$. Constants are uniform on compact interior spectrum intervals. This proves coverage of the declared family. ∎

Theorems F.10.4e.8--F.10.4e.10 populate Definition F.10.4e.5 on the faithful commuting and faithful nondegenerate-qubit families, with the remainder and polynomial-uniform-integrability records. The spectral coordinate is the independently efficient commuting submodel. The two rotational SLDs have commutator $8ir_0^2\sigma_z$, so their symmetric covariance identity alone does not certify a simultaneous classical estimator. A maximally mixed component requires a distinct chart; pure endpoints and other retained families require their corresponding admission and LAN records.

Finite oscillator approximation is quantitative. For $\mathcal R_L\omega=P_L\omega P_L+\operatorname{Tr}((I-P_L)\omega)|0\rangle\langle0|$, purification and the two-dimensional pure-state distance formula give $\|\omega-\mathcal R_L\omega\|_1\le2\sqrt t+t\le4\sqrt t$, where $t=\operatorname{Tr}\omega(I-P_L)$. The number bounds therefore give error at most $\min\{2,4\sqrt{C_h}/(L+2)^{h/2}\}$, also after integrating the correlated classical record. Its retained oscillator dimension is $L+1$. A discrete replacement of the continuous classical Gaussian has full measure-norm distance $2$; a finite-resolution implementation must instead specify its probe algebra and comparison norm. Qubit code-corner embedding records faithfulness on the retained qubit algebra, not on the full $M_8$ carrier.

<a id="definition-f104e11-clocked-finite-register-lan-source"></a>**Definition F.10.4e.11 (Clocked Finite-Register LAN Source).** Fix the Hilbert/Born and normalized-instrument branch of Proposition 4, Definition 27 and Theorem 28a. The source below uses the three-qubit MPU substrate of Section 7.1.3 and Theorem 7.6s. Its data factor is $Q_M$; $Q_P,Q_I$ start in their registered ready states. Fix a rational base $\mu_0\in(1/2,1)$, positive rational compact bounds $T,M$, a pulse duration $\tau_g$ in seconds, and a detector scale $v_{\mathrm d}$ in volts. The explicit nonempty instance is $\mu_0=3/4$, $T=M=1$ and every integer $n\ge64$. Other rational bases use Theorem F.10.4e.10's lower bound on $n$. The retained preparation family is
$$
\sigma_{n,t,u}=e^{i(u_x\sigma_x+u_y\sigma_y)/\sqrt n}
\operatorname{diag}(\mu_0+t/\sqrt n,1-\mu_0-t/\sqrt n)
e^{-i(u_x\sigma_x+u_y\sigma_y)/\sqrt n},
\qquad |t|\le T,\quad |u|\le M.
\tag{F.10.4e.22}
$$
The preparation port owns $(t,u)$. Comparison-channel controllers receive $n,\mu_0,T,M$ and the declared precision, and have no return path to that port. The source prepares $n$ independent copies by preparing
$\sqrt\mu|00\rangle+\sqrt{1-\mu}|11\rangle$, applying the displayed rotation to its first qubit, and placing its purifying qubit in the source archive. The spectral preparation is a two-level rotation; the data rotation is generated during a preparation slot by $-\hbar(u_x\sigma_x+u_y\sigma_y)/(\tau_g\sqrt n)$. Thus the actual rotational drive coordinates are $u_x/(\tau_g\sqrt n),u_y/(\tau_g\sqrt n)$ in inverse seconds. Population, $t,u,X,Q,P$ are dimensionless. A registered detector of a bounded self-adjoint matrix $B$ returns the eigenvalue times $v_{\mathrm d}$; its mean voltage is $v_{\mathrm d}\operatorname{Tr}(\rho B)$. This fixes detector units without identifying a register-emulated oscillator with a mechanical displacement. The $\sqrt n$-rescaled tangent derivatives at the base of (F.10.4e.22) are $\sigma_z,r_0\sigma_y,-r_0\sigma_x$, and are independent. The commuting subfamily has $u=0$; the fixed-spectrum subfamily has $t=0$. A maximally mixed base and a larger single-site retained algebra are outside this source census.

A finite source program is a bounded decision tree of ready-register allocation, independent fair-bit preparation, one-, two- and three-qubit unitary pulses, computational-basis instruments, classical control, and archive transfer. Every branch ends with an output or an explicit failure symbol. The tree is padded to a fixed number of service slots. An instrument is armed at its designated slot. Its perspective/control label is the current tree node, and its normalized perspective kernel is the deterministic successor selected by that instrument outcome; a terminal node follows its padded self-loop. On a line of $W$ active or archive MPU sites, a logical qubit occupies $Q_M$ and the other two factors remain in the code's ready state. A pulse $U$ is generated on its nominated factors by $H_U=-\hbar\operatorname{Arg}(U)/\tau_g$, with eigenphases in $[-\pi,\pi]$, and is extended by zero on the complement of their code. Hence $e^{-iH_U\tau_g/\hbar}=U$, $\|H_U\|\le\pi\hbar/\tau_g$, and the ideal code is invariant. SWAP routing places every primitive on at most three adjacent sites. Registers have zero Hamiltonian between pulses. Basis instruments are the registered projective instruments of Definition 27; a retained copy of each private instrument record and every displaced quantum subsystem belongs to the archive. An apparent discard is this specified partial trace in the public response map. A slot used again is first swapped with a fresh ready register, and its former state is archived. No archive erasure or cyclic renewal is promised.

The source includes the following independently fixed service account. For a complete padded word record its allocated site count $R$, program bits $B_{\rm prog}$, fresh ready logical qubits $r$, fair bits $b_{\rm rnd}$, pulse slots $G$, instrument/readout slots $D$, duration $\mathcal T$, and every archive allocation. Compilation and stored coefficient tables are part of setup, with their actual finite compilation duration $\tau_{\rm set}$ recorded. Ready-source, fair-source and program-write service slots each have duration $\tau_g$, as do pulse and instrument slots; hence $\mathcal T=\tau_{\rm set}+\tau_g(r+b_{\rm rnd}+G+D+B_{\rm prog})$. A fair-source slot owns preparation; any additional gates or readouts used to consume it are charged in $G,D$. Each source has positive, finitely specified prices $e_{\rm set},e_{\rm ready},e_{\rm rnd},e_g,e_d,e_{\rm prog}$ in joules, controller power $P_c$ in watts and per-site maintenance power $p_c$ in watts, fixed before responses. Independent service supplies debit
$$
E_{\rm svc}=e_{\rm set}+r e_{\rm ready}+b_{\rm rnd}e_{\rm rnd}
 +G e_g+D e_d+B_{\rm prog}e_{\rm prog}+(P_c+Rp_c)\mathcal T.
\tag{F.10.4e.23}
$$
The ready-source price owns its consumed low-entropy states; the fair-source price owns its independent normalized preparations. All $3R$ qubits, including inactive code factors, and all stored program and archive bits are charged. Pulse action is a separate resource, at most $\pi\hbar G$. On the ideal degenerate-register, cyclic-pulse model the net register work of each pulse is zero; (F.10.4e.23) is the controller/source service debit, rather than a heat inferred from gate count. The returned resource is the full displayed vector together with this explicitly supplied service law. For the finite compiler, $G$ counts individual controlled Euler/phase exponentials with generator norm at most one, and the exact reversible $X$, CNOT, Toffoli and SWAP pulses. An arbitrary unitary macro is expanded into those factors before its slots, program, action and service debit are counted. Every positive price tuple is admitted; no price is selected by a LAN outcome or used to assert a resource optimum. A source with cyclic archive reset must add its actual complete-side-information instrument and Definition-28 account. The finite consumed-source branch already supplies a complete account for every operation admitted here.

Finite-precision source members replace the reference preparations and controls by certified trace/diamond approximants. A known initial ready-state error is charged to the preparation budget. For example, independent ready qubits of excited population $g$ give full input trace error at most $2rg$. Such states can be supplied by finite-gap Gibbs qubits, $g=(1+e^{\Delta/(k_BT_b)})^{-1}$; a SWAP transfers the old state, with all correlations, to the consumed source/archive. Its actual energy change is retained if that preparation mechanism is chosen. Pure ready states instead name a consumed pure-state resource. These are alternative source declarations, not a claim of finite-resource exact thermal erasure.

<a id="theorem-f104e12-two-way-finite-resolution-mpu-lan-interface"></a>**Theorem F.10.4e.12 (Two-Way Finite-Resolution MPU LAN Interface).** On Definition F.10.4e.11's source, let $\rho=\sigma_{n,t,u}^{\otimes n}$ and $\Gamma=\Gamma_{t,u}$ be the experiment of Theorem F.10.4e.10, with its unchanged ideal deficiency $\varepsilon_n$. For every positive tolerance there are a finite cell algebra, an oscillator cutoff, source programs for both comparison channels, and a complete source-to-carrier response map with that tolerance. The assertion includes the commuting and fixed-spectrum subfamilies with the channel modifications below.

Fix a rational $R_0>T+1$ large enough to contain all closed jitter cells $\overline I_a$ in its interior. Partition $[-R_0,R_0]$ into finitely many intervals of maximum width $h$, including every endpoint of every $I_a$ and every finite boundary of the reverse partition $E_a$. Choose every additional boundary rational, so all endpoints are algebraic. Add the two unbounded tail cells. Let $\mathcal P=\{C_1,\ldots,C_m\}$ be this partition. Each cell lies in one $E_a$ up to null endpoints. For an integer $L\ge0$ put $d=L+1$ and
$$
\mathcal A_{\mathcal P,L}=\bigoplus_{c=1}^m M_d,\qquad
\mathcal QH=\left(\int_{C_c}\mathcal R_L(H(x))\,dx\right)_{c=1}^m,
\quad \Gamma_{\mathcal P,L}=\mathcal Q\Gamma.
\tag{F.10.4e.24}
$$
The pairing is $\sum_c\operatorname{Tr}(H_c B_c)$, the observable norm is $\max_c\|B_c\|$, and the state-difference norm is $\sum_c\|H_c\|_1$. For differences of normalized states it is twice the supremum, over effects, of the absolute outcome-probability difference. The map $\mathcal R_L$ is the cutoff/reset channel already defined after Theorem F.10.4e.10, with its output regarded as an $M_d$ matrix. On every bounded cell set $k_c=1_{C_c}/|C_c|$; on each tail choose the unit-rate exponential density translated to the boundary and supported in that tail. Define the normal comparison identification
$$
\mathcal J(H_c)(x)=\sum_c k_c(x)\iota_L H_c\iota_L^*,
\qquad \mathcal Q\mathcal J=\operatorname{id},
\tag{F.10.4e.25}
$$
where $\iota_L$ includes the first $d$ number states. This is a density-valued response identification. The actual finite source output is the cell label and the finite quantum register.

The exact finite channels are
$$
F=\mathcal Q\Theta_n,
\qquad
R(H_c)=S_n^*\left[\bigoplus_a
\left\{\sum_{c:C_c\subset E_a}C_j(\iota_LH_c\iota_L^*)\right\}
\otimes I_{d_j}/d_j\right]S_n=\Xi_n\mathcal J(H_c).
\tag{F.10.4e.26}
$$
All maps are defined on every input state, including inputs outside the statistical family. Write
$$
\kappa_L=\min\{2,4\sqrt{C_s}/(L+2)^{s/2}\},\quad
\chi_{h,R_0}=h\sqrt{2/(\pi v_0)}
 +4\exp[-(R_0-T)^2/(2v_0)],\qquad s\ge1,
\tag{F.10.4e.27}
$$
where $C_s$ is the uniform number-moment constant of Theorem F.10.4e.10. Then
$$
\|F\rho-\Gamma_{\mathcal P,L}\|_1\le\varepsilon_n,
\qquad
\|R\Gamma_{\mathcal P,L}-\rho\|_1\le\varepsilon_n+\kappa_L,
\qquad
\|\mathcal JF\rho-\Gamma\|_1\le\varepsilon_n+\kappa_L+\chi_{h,R_0}.
\tag{F.10.4e.28}
$$
The finite norm in the first comparison has zero cell error: cell probabilities are exact integrals. Oscillator truncation also vanishes from that first comparison because both experiments use the same channel $\mathcal Q$. These facts do not remove its separate cutoff and cell/tail debits when a full normal response is requested.

Here is a separated implementation account. Let $\eta_{\rm prep}$ bound the aggregate ready/input preparation error, let $\eta_{\rm rnd}$ bound all finite-sampler kernel errors in full $\ell^1$, and let
$\eta_{\rm gate}=2G2^{-b}+\sum_g\eta_g$ bound angle rounding and residual encoded diamond errors. For each implementation step, suppose its output, also with any untouched reference, has code-complement probability at most $\lambda_g$, and its code-compressed channel has the stated encoded error. Set $\eta_{\rm leak}=4\sum_g\sqrt{\lambda_g}$ and
$\eta_{\rm impl}=\eta_{\rm prep}+\eta_{\rm rnd}+\eta_{\rm gate}+\eta_{\rm leak}$.
For the forward source add its own $\eta_{\rm impl}^{F}$ to the first and third bounds in (F.10.4e.28); for the reverse source add $\eta_{\rm impl}^{R}$ to the second. A subsequently approximated detector of norm at most $K$ adds its registered detector error and multiplies the preceding state bound by $K$. At no stage is a weaker probe error relabeled as full trace or measure norm.

*Proof.* The source state is obtained by the stated two-qubit preparation followed by partial trace. Its tensor powers are the retained extremal components of Definition F.10.4e.1: for each fixed one-site state, all copy numbers give the consistent product family. The LAN sequence changes that one-site state with $n$ as prescribed by its local experiment. The code map $V|z\rangle=|z,0,0\rangle$ is used together with the source preparations, pulses, instruments and archives, rather than as a substitute for them. For an arbitrary state on the full physical carrier, use the total decoder
$\mathcal D(\omega)=V^*P\omega PV+\operatorname{Tr}((I-P)\omega)|0\rangle\langle0|$,
with the tensor-product code projector $P=VV^*$. Its Kraus operators are $V^*P$ and $|0\rangle\langle e|$ for an orthonormal basis of the complement, so it is CPTP. Extend every encoded source program with this specified failure/reset branch; its complementary input and flags go to the charged archive. Induction over the complete finite decision tree proves normalization for every state and preserves the Born law on the nominated family. Pullback of each retained effect is its channel adjoint, which proves the source-to-carrier response equality on every finite protocol. The reference source has zero leakage.

To construct $F$, perform the fixed $S_n$, read the block $a=n/2+j$ without reading its ladder coordinate, transfer the multiplicity register to the archive, and use $V_j$ on the ladder. Compress/reset that ladder at $L$. Conditional on the same retained $a$, sample $c$ with
$$
p(c\mid a)=\int_{C_c}\kappa_a(x)\,dx=\sqrt n\,|C_c\cap I_a|.
$$
These nonnegative probabilities sum to one. In particular the exact model output is
$$
(F\rho)_c=\sum_a w_\mu(j)p(c\mid a)\mathcal R_L(\sigma_{\mu,j,u}).
$$
Every nonzero term has its original $a$, and a bounded cell with positive forward probability identifies that $a$. The source keeps its conditional oscillator state. Multiplying a separately prepared spin marginal by a separately prepared oscillator marginal would change this formula.

The quantum steps have explicit Kraus representations. For each $j$ and multiplicity basis vector $z$, the low-ladder Kraus operator is

$$
P_L V_j(I_{\mathcal H_j}\otimes\langle z|)\Pi_jS_n.
$$

For each ladder index $k>L$, add
$|0\rangle\langle j,j-k|\otimes\langle z|\,\Pi_jS_n$.
Multiply the operators for cell $c$ by $\sqrt{p(c\mid a)}$ and attach its orthogonal classical output label. Their adjoint products sum to identity because the cell probabilities, spin projections, ladder projections and multiplicity basis each resolve their corresponding identity. The reverse reads $c$, obtains its $a$, applies the Kraus compression/reset $C_j$ to the oscillator register, prepares the uniform multiplicity state, and applies $S_n^*$. For its multiplicity preparation the Kraus index has amplitude $1/\sqrt{d_j}$ for each of the $d_j$ basis states. This proves CPTP normalization on all inputs and gives (F.10.4e.26). The source can retain every dilation index privately while the public map is exactly the channel stated.

Contractivity of $\mathcal Q$ proves the first bound. Because the partition refines every $E_a$, integration of $\mathcal J\mathcal QH$ over an $E_a$ is exactly the integral of $\mathcal R_LH$ over that set, included back into Fock space. Consequently
$R\mathcal Q\Gamma=\Xi_n(\mathcal R_L\Gamma)$,
with the classical coordinate left unchanged. The accepted cutoff estimate and contraction give the second bound. The same observation gives $RF\rho=\rho$ whenever $L\ge n$; for arbitrary $L$, its model-return error is at most $\kappa_L$, using the conditional finite-output moment bound. No inverse is asserted on cross-block coherences or nonuniform multiplicity inputs discarded by $\Theta_n$.

For a Gaussian density $g_t$, cell averaging on a bounded interval $C$ gives
$$
\int_C\left|g_t(x)-|C|^{-1}\int_Cg_t(y)dy\right|dx
\le |C|\int_C|g_t'(z)|dz.
$$
Indeed express the difference as the average of $g_t(x)-g_t(y)$, integrate $|\int_y^xg_t'|$, and bound the measure of pairs whose segment meets a fixed $z$ by $|C|^2$. Summing and using
$\int|g_t'|=\sqrt{2/(\pi v_0)}$ bounds the bounded-cell contribution. On a tail, the original density and its replacement have equal mass, hence their full-$L^1$ difference is at most twice that mass. Chernoff's bound for $N(t,v_0)$ gives total tail mass at most $2e^{-(R_0-T)^2/(2v_0)}$. This proves $\chi_{h,R_0}$. The target is the product $g_tG_{0,u}$; oscillator cutoff costs at most $\kappa_L$. Thus
$\|\mathcal J\mathcal Q\Gamma-\Gamma\|_1\le\chi_{h,R_0}+\kappa_L$.
Apply $\mathcal J$ to the first bound and use the triangle inequality to prove the third.

For comparison with representative-point probes, retain a separate explicit norm. Let $\|B(x)\|\le1$ and $\|B(x)-B(y)\|\le K_B|x-y|$ on $[-R_0,R_0]$, using any representative of each bounded cell and arbitrary norm-one tail representatives. Pairing a state with these representatives incurs at most $K_Bh+2\Pr(|X|>R_0)$, before the oscillator debit. This is a bounded-Lipschitz response estimate. For all measurable bounded probes the density-identification comparison in (F.10.4e.28) has the full normal predual norm. The actual atomic readout measure has full measure-norm distance exactly $2$ from a continuous Gaussian: its finite support has probabilities one and zero, respectively. This provides an exact separating event at every finite resolution.

We give a finite compiler so the interfaces do not rely on an unpriced Schur oracle. The highest-weight construction in Theorem F.10.4e.9 computes $S_n$ from finite matrices and ladder normalizations; all entries are algebraic for this fixed representation. QR elimination expresses any $P\times P$ unitary in at most $P(P-1)/2$ two-level rotations and $P$ diagonal phases: zero the subdiagonal entries column by column using a unitary on the two selected rows, and undo the elimination. A two-level rotation between binary words of width $w$ is reduced to a multiply-controlled single-qubit rotation by a Gray path of at most $w$ bit changes and the inverse path. A control on at most $w-1$ specified bits is computed into at most $w$ ready scratch bits by a Toffoli chain, used once, and uncomputed. Negative controls are conjugated by $X$. A general controlled one-qubit unitary is an allowed two-qubit pulse. These operations require fewer than $64w^2$ one-, two- or three-qubit primitives per two-level factor for $w\ge1$. Thus $64w^2P^2$ is a valid bound, including phases. Bringing at most three operand qubits together in a line and returning them uses at most $6W$ adjacent swaps, so multiplication by $6W+1$ covers locality routing. Choose the active/archive workspace $W$ before compiling routes. Program storage is a separate bank; after routing is compiled its actual $B_{\rm prog}$ bits are allocated there. Thus $R$ includes both banks and there is no circular rule determining workspace from its own unrolled program size. Each scratch, route and controller bit is reserved and charged.

For completeness, a finite CPTP map $M_{d_1}\to M_{d_2}$ with Kraus operators $K_\alpha$ has the isometry
$W\psi=\sum_\alpha K_\alpha\psi\otimes|\alpha\rangle$,
since $\sum K_\alpha^*K_\alpha=I$. Extend an orthonormal basis of its image to an orthonormal basis of its finite output space. This extends $W$ to a unitary with ready ancillas and realizes the channel by archive transfer. Padding $d_1,d_2$ to powers of two, at most $d_1d_2$ Kraus operators are needed: the positive matrix with blocks $\Phi(|i\rangle\langle j|)$ has that size, and its spectral decomposition supplies such a Kraus family by reshaping its vectors. A unitary dimension $P=d_1d_2^2$ therefore suffices, with $w=\log_2P$, plus the preceding compiler scratch. This proves a finite bound for every block, reset, detector and type-preparation subroutine, even when a more efficient implementation is unused. Padding complement inputs by a declared ready-output channel makes the construction total. It also prepares every finite $\Gamma_{\mathcal P,L}$ by purifying its positive normalized matrix; its preparation port owns the parameters and is isolated from the comparison controller.

All non-dyadic classical distributions have a finite-sampler implementation. For a probability vector on $J$ symbols choose integers $N_i$ with sum $2^B$ by flooring $2^Bp_i$ and adding one to the largest remainders until the sum is correct. Then $|N_i/2^B-p_i|<2^{-B}$, and its full-$\ell^1$ error is at most $J2^{-B}$. A retained $B$-bit uniform word and cumulative lookup realize that integer law with no rejection or omitted probability. Source bits are fresh and independent; the word and every lookup scratch bit are archived. The channel sampling tables here have algebraic probabilities (and rational uniform type probabilities), so their integer counts can be computed with certified algebraic comparison. If a source instead supplies probabilities through certified rational approximants, first normalize a positive rational vector, charge its independently bounded full-$\ell^1$ error, and apply the integer construction to that vector. The same construction prepares uniform multiplicities and, on the commuting branch, uniform bit-string types. State comparison, including an untouched quantum reference, contracts the conditional kernel error. Telescoping across all draws proves the stated $\eta_{\rm rnd}$; the table description contains every block's distribution, not merely the branch selected in one run. For the varying-spectrum reverse map the cell determines $a$, so it samples no independent spin label.

The finite programs expand each controlled one-qubit unitary into its phase and three Euler exponentials, counting those factors individually in $G$; the conservative $64w^2$ bound includes them. Each rounded factor is $e^{i\theta A}$ with $\|A\|\le1$. Rounding its angle by at most $2^{-b}$ changes its unitary by at most $2^{-b}$, by integrating $iAe^{\mathrm{itA}}$. The fixed reversible controls are exact reference primitives. Any separate imperfect implementation of them is included in $\eta_g$. For two unitaries, expansion of $U\rho U^*-V\rho V^*$ bounds the diamond norm by $2\|U-V\|$. Telescoping proves $2G2^{-b}$ and the sum of residual channel errors. Preparation errors contract and sum. To justify the leakage term, let $P$ be the code projector and $\lambda=\operatorname{Tr}((I-P)\omega)$. Purify $\omega$ and project the purification; the two-vector trace-distance formula, followed by partial trace, gives $\|\omega-P\omega P\|_1\le2\sqrt\lambda$. The decoder adds a positive trace-$\lambda$ ready term. Therefore $\|\omega-V\mathcal D(\omega)V^*\|_1\le2\sqrt\lambda+\lambda\le4\sqrt\lambda$. The argument works with every untouched reference. Applying it before each channel telescoping step proves $\eta_{\rm leak}$ under the expressly complete leakage premise. A leakage probability without that comparison is not assigned a diamond norm. If a public leakage flag is additionally retained, its own classical mismatch, at most $2\lambda$ per flag, is added separately.

For the commuting construction use the basis/count channel of Theorem F.10.4e.8, include all its count-cell boundaries in $\mathcal P$, set $L=0$, and use uniform type preparation on the reverse. This realizes both commuting channels with zero oscillator debit. For the fixed-spectrum construction use Theorem F.10.4e.9's Schur/block forward channel and its reverse block distribution $w_n(j)$, whose finite sampler has the same charged error rule. Its public classical algebra is trivial; its block record remains in the private archive. Its cell/tail debit is zero. For the full varying-spectrum construction the preceding proof retains the correlated label throughout. These alternatives use exactly the parameter-independent ideal channels owned by their respective theorems.

Finally choose $n$ with $\varepsilon_n$ below its assigned budget, then a finite $L$ with $\kappa_L$ below its budget, finite $R_0,h$ with $\chi_{h,R_0}$ below its budget, and finite sampler/angle/ready precision with their sum below the remaining budget. The accepted bounds and all compiler counts are explicit and finite. Ideal source members have $\eta_g=\lambda_g=0$; other members supply their stated residuals. Every bound is uniform on the retained compact parameter set. The total resource vector is obtained by counting the actual padded program, with a separate entry for $S_n,S_n^*$, block extraction, ladder compression, cell lookup, type/multiplicity preparation, detector, routing, scratch and archive transfer. Substitution of these counts into the source's pre-existing law (F.10.4e.23) proves its cost for every admitted word. No minimization over a different hardware class is part of this owner. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104e13-normal-response-refinement-of-the-finite-lan-interface"></a>**Theorem F.10.4e.13 (Normal-Response Refinement of the Finite LAN Interface).** Let $\mathcal P_m$ be nested finite interval partitions, each containing all earlier boundaries, with bounded-cell mesh tending to zero on every compact interval and tails escaping to infinity. Include the finitely many jitter/reverse boundaries of each selected sample size $n_m$ before constructing $\mathcal P_m$. Let $L_m\uparrow\infty$. For the algebras and maps of (F.10.4e.24)--(F.10.4e.25), coarse merging and $\mathcal R_{L_m}$ define CPTP restriction maps $q_{m\leftarrow m+1}$ with
$$
q_{m\leftarrow m+1}\mathcal Q_{m+1}=\mathcal Q_m,
\qquad
\|\mathcal J_m\mathcal Q_mH-H\|_1\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
\|H\|_1=\lim_m\|\mathcal Q_mH\|_1
\tag{F.10.4e.29}
$$
for every normal trace-class-valued integrable density $H$, also every difference of two such states. Thus the finite response quotients identify the full continuous-register normal experiment and its original predual norm. They supply no finite atomic full-TV approximation.

Every bounded normal probe $B(x)$ has the finite representative $B_m=\mathcal J_m^*B$, with $\|B_m\|\le\|B\|$ and
$$
\langle\mathcal Q_mH,B_m\rangle\longrightarrow\langle H,B\rangle.
\tag{F.10.4e.30}
$$
Effective finite probes are compiled by Theorem F.10.4e.12. General bounded measurable probes belong to the normal completion specified by (F.10.4e.29)--(F.10.4e.30); an arbitrary uncomputable probe is not asserted to have a finite program. Choose $n_m\to\infty$ and finite implementation budgets so that $\varepsilon_{n_m},\kappa_{L_m},\chi_{h_m,R_m},\eta_{\rm impl,m}$ all tend to zero. Then both directions of the declared LAN comparison, every retained bounded normal response, and every prescribed finite mixed-moment record are realized by this refining finite-source family. The continuous protocol retained here is this explicit normal-response completion.

*Proof.* The oscillator channels obey $\mathcal R_L\mathcal R_{L'}=\mathcal R_L$ for $L'\ge L$, since all population above $L$ ends in $|0\rangle$ and no lost coherence is recreated. Merging nested cells gives the first identity. These maps contract full-$\ell^1$ trace norm, so $\|\mathcal Q_mH\|_1$ is nondecreasing and bounded above by $\|H\|_1$.

To prove convergence, first take $H(x)=f(x)A$ with $f$ continuous and compactly supported and $A$ a matrix on finitely many number states. For sufficiently large $m$ there is no oscillator truncation of $A$, its support lies between the tail boundaries, and on each intersecting cell the average of $f$ differs from $f$ by at most its modulus of continuity at the mesh. Integrating over a fixed compact enlargement proves convergence in $L^1(\mathbb R;\mathcal T_1)$. Finite linear combinations of such functions are dense: approximate a Bochner integrable trace-class function by a finite simple function, approximate each of its trace-class values by finite matrices, and approximate the indicators of its finite-measure sets in scalar $L^1$ by continuous compactly supported functions. The last scalar approximation follows by finite unions of intervals and continuous ramps at their endpoints; regularity of Lebesgue measure supplies those unions. Each $\mathcal J_m\mathcal Q_m$ is a contraction, so a three-term triangle inequality extends convergence to every $H$. Finally
$\|H\|_1\le\|H-\mathcal J_m\mathcal Q_mH\|_1+\|\mathcal Q_mH\|_1$
proves the norm identity. Dual pairing proves (F.10.4e.30), uniformly for norm-one probes once a fixed state's reconstruction error is specified. The finite representatives average $P_{L_m}B(x)P_{L_m}$ against $k_c$, rather than evaluating an arbitrary measurable $B$ at a point.

Finite adaptive decision protocols on the comparison output are contractions to their complete classical--quantum record; diamond control of the implementations also permits untouched reference registers and finite ancillary instruments. A word with several supplied comparison calls has the sum of their declared channel errors by telescoping. There is no uncharged uniform guarantee for unboundedly many calls. The normal experiment fixes all single-call and every fixed finite-call responses. The density-identification error in (F.10.4e.28) tends to zero on the chosen diagonal, proving the complete bounded-response assertion.

For an explicitly retained mixed Weyl polynomial use the bounded cutoff and transported probes in Theorem F.10.4e.10. Add the corresponding finite implementation error times that cutoff's norm; refine its finite classical coefficients and matrix entries until their separate detector error tends to zero. For a fixed cutoff the preceding bounded-response theorem applies. The two uncut expectation tails are the same $A_k(R)$ and $C_s/(L+2)^s$ bounds already proved in Theorem F.10.4e.10. First make those tails small, then choose $n$ and source precision for that cutoff. A diagonal selection works for every prescribed finite list of moments. This proves its clause-4 records without inferring unbounded-moment convergence from bounded deficiency. The limiting covariance and root-fidelity information remain those of (F.10.4e.20), with inverse-information covariance on the commuting efficient submodel. ∎

### F.10.4f Predictive Nuclearity Species Bound

<a id="definition-f104f1-pu-phase-space-nuclearity-datum"></a>**Definition F.10.4f.1 (PU Phase-Space Nuclearity Datum).** On a regular AQFT branch satisfying the continuum bridge hypotheses of Theorem F.0 and Theorem F.10.2, let $\mathfrak A(O)$ be the local algebra of a relatively compact causal region $O$, let $\Omega_*$ be the cyclic PCE/KMS vector of the faithful equilibrium state, and let $H\ge0$ be the positive generator of the retained time evolution. For $\beta>0$, define the local phase-space map
$$
\Theta_{\beta,O}:
\mathfrak A(O)\to\mathcal H,
\qquad
\Theta_{\beta,O}(A)=e^{-\beta H}A\Omega_*.
\tag{F.10.4f.1}
$$
A finite MPU approximation of this datum is a triple
$$
(\mathfrak A_h(O),H_h,\Omega_h)
$$
with corresponding map
$$
\Theta_{\beta,O}^{(h)}(A)=e^{-\beta H_h}A\Omega_h.
\tag{F.10.4f.2}
$$
The branch has PU phase-space capacity bound $C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta)$ when the finite approximants, represented on their finite GNS Hilbert spaces, satisfy, uniformly in $h$,
$$
\operatorname{rank}\Theta_{\beta,O}^{(h)}
\le
\exp(C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta)),
\qquad
\lVert\Theta_{\beta,O}^{(h)}\rVert\le1.
\tag{F.10.4f.3}
$$
Here $\lVert\cdot\rVert_1$ denotes the Banach-space nuclear norm of a map from the local $C^*$-algebra, with its operator norm, to the GNS Hilbert space. A PU phase-space capacity certificate must provide an explicit nuclear decomposition
$$
\Theta_{\beta,O}^{(h)}(A)
=
\sum_{r=1}^{R_h}\varphi_{h,r}(A)\,\xi_{h,r}
$$
satisfying
$$
\sum_{r=1}^{R_h}\|\varphi_{h,r}\|\,\|\xi_{h,r}\|
\le
\exp(C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta)).
\tag{F.10.4f.5}
$$

<a id="theorem-f104f2-necessary-modular-nuclearity-bound"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.2 (Necessary Modular Nuclearity Bound).** Suppose the finite maps have the certified decompositions (F.10.4f.5), their domains and codomains are related to the limiting local algebra and GNS Hilbert space by contractive comparison maps, and the transported representing tensors admit a weakly convergent subnet in $\mathfrak A(O)^*\widehat\otimes_\pi\mathcal H$ whose represented map is the pointwise-weak limit $\Theta_{\beta,O}$. Then
$$
\lVert\Theta_{\beta,O}\rVert_1
\le
\exp(C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta)).
\tag{F.10.4f.4}
$$

*Proof.* Let $T_h$ denote the transported representing tensor of the certified finite decomposition. Contractivity of the comparison maps gives
$$
\|T_h\|_\pi\le
\sum_r\|\varphi_{h,r}\|\,\|\xi_{h,r}\|
\le e^{C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta)}.
$$
By the assumed weak convergence of a subnet, its limit $T$ represents $\Theta_{\beta,O}$. The closed ball of a Banach space is weakly closed, so
$$
\|\Theta_{\beta,O}\|_1\le\|T\|_\pi
\le e^{C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta)}.
$$
No inequality involving the limit inferior of the minimal finite nuclear norms is inferred from arbitrary chosen representations.

For completeness, finite rank and the Hilbert target do provide the required finite nuclear bound. Use the Hilbert inner product linear in its second slot. Choose an orthonormal basis $(e_r)_{r=1}^{R_h}$ of the range and put $\varphi_{h,r}(A)=\langle e_r,\Theta_{\beta,O}^{(h)}A\rangle$. Then
$$
\Theta_{\beta,O}^{(h)}A=\sum_{r=1}^{R_h}\varphi_{h,r}(A)e_r,\qquad
\sum_r\|\varphi_{h,r}\|\le R_h\|\Theta_{\beta,O}^{(h)}\|
\le e^{C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta)}.
$$
These finite estimates do not imply weak compactness of the transported projective-tensor ball or identify its limiting map; those continuum hypotheses remain independent. ∎

<a id="definition-f104f3-split-nuclear-mpu-realization-certificate"></a>**Definition F.10.4f.3 (Split-Nuclear MPU Realization Certificate).** Let a retained AQFT branch satisfy the nuclearity bound (F.10.4f.4), Hadamard-PCE and reflection-positivity gates, the split property, and the local PU-LAN certificate. For a relatively compact region $O$ and $0<\delta<1$, a realization certificate records
$$
\mathfrak R_{\delta,O}
=(O_-\Subset O\Subset O_+,\mathcal N_O,\mathcal B_{\delta,O},
\pi_{\delta,O},\iota_{\delta,O},\omega_{\delta,O},C_{\delta,O}).
\tag{F.10.4f.6}
$$
Its requirements are:
1. $\mathfrak A(O_-)\subset\mathcal N_O\subset\mathfrak A(O_+)$ is a split inclusion with a type-I intermediate factor.
2. $\mathcal B_{\delta,O}$ is a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra with state $\omega_{\delta,O}$.
3. The interfaces $\pi_{\delta,O}:\mathfrak A(O)\to\mathcal B_{\delta,O}$ and $\iota_{\delta,O}:\mathcal B_{\delta,O}\to\mathfrak A(O_+)$ are UCP.
4. Choose error allocations $\delta_0,\delta_{\mathrm{impl}}\ge0$ with $\delta_0+\delta_{\mathrm{impl}}\le\delta$. On the retained test core $\mathcal T_O$,
$$
|\omega(A)-\omega_{\delta,O}(\pi_{\delta,O}A)|
\le\delta_0\|A\|.
\tag{F.10.4f.7}
$$
5. On the same core,
$$
\|A-\iota_{\delta,O}\pi_{\delta,O}A\|_\omega
\le\delta_0\|A\|.
\tag{F.10.4f.8}
$$
6. The induced finite phase-space map approximates $\Theta_{\beta,O}$ to error $\delta_0$ in the declared test norm for every $\beta$ in the retained window.
7. All carrier, ancilla and interface costs obey
$$
C_{\delta,O}\le C_0|\partial O|\,P(\log(1/\delta))
+C_1\operatorname{Vol}_{\mathrm{active}}(O)
+C_2C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta),
\tag{F.10.4f.9}
$$
where the nonnegative polynomial $P$ and all constants are branch data.
8. The record supplies a code-corner embedding into $(\mathbb C^8)^{\otimes N}$ and finite circuits for the retained interfaces. The ideal code algebra is invariant. All circuit and leakage errors in the state, GNS and phase-space comparisons of items 4--6 are separately bounded by $\delta_{\mathrm{impl}}$ in their respective norms. A leakage probability alone is not identified with any of these norm errors. All implementation costs are included in $C_{\delta,O}$.

<a id="theorem-f104f4-finite-pce-realization-from-a-split-nuclear-certificate"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.4 (Finite-PCE Realization from a Split-Nuclear Certificate).** If these certificates exist for every retained $O$ and $0<\delta<1$, each pair admits a finite MPU realization with
$$
|\omega(A)-\omega_{\mathcal N_{\delta,O}^{\mathrm{MPU}}}(A)|
\le\delta\|A\|\qquad(A\in\mathcal T_O),
\tag{F.10.4f.10}
$$
and
$$
C_{\mathrm{PCE}}(\mathcal N_{\delta,O}^{\mathrm{MPU}})\le C_{\delta,O}.
\tag{F.10.4f.11}
$$
The cost is finite at each positive tolerance; this assertion supplies no uniform cost bound as $\delta\downarrow0$.

*Proof.* Write $\mathcal B_{\delta,O}=\bigoplus_\alpha M_{n_\alpha}$ and $m=\sum_\alpha n_\alpha$. Choose $N$ with $8^N\ge m$ and an isometry $V:\mathbb C^m\to(\mathbb C^8)^{\otimes N}$. The map $j_0(B)=VBV^*$ faithfully represents the algebra in the corner with identity $VV^*$. A finite state with density $D$ becomes $VDV^*$; no extension of the algebra to the unused complement is required. Item 8 supplies the physical interfaces and their errors, which are not consequences of this dimension count. The triangle inequality combines the abstract error $\delta_0$ and implementation error $\delta_{\mathrm{impl}}$ to prove (F.10.4f.10), and gives the analogous GNS and phase-space bounds. Items 7--8 charge every implementation resource to $C_{\delta,O}$, proving the cost inequality. The polynomial in $\log(1/\delta)$ may diverge as the tolerance decreases, so no tolerance-uniform bound follows. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104f5-exact-finite-energy-nuclearity-norm-and-species-bound"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.5 (Exact Finite Energy-Nuclearity Norm and Species Bound).** Let $\mathcal K=\mathcal K_O\otimes\mathcal K_c$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space with inner product linear in its second slot, let $\mathfrak A_h(O)=B(\mathcal K_O)\otimes I_c$, and let
$$
H_h=H_O\otimes I_c+I_O\otimes H_c,
\qquad
\Omega_h=\Omega_O\otimes\Omega_c,
$$
with $H_O,H_c$ self-adjoint, $\Omega_O,\Omega_c$ unit vectors and $H_c\Omega_c=0$. For $\beta>0$ put $Z_O(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H_O}$, and let $E_{\min}$ be the least eigenvalue of $H_O$. Then the finite phase-space map (F.10.4f.2) satisfies
$$
\lVert\Theta^{(h)}_{\beta,O}\rVert_1=Z_O(\beta),
\qquad
\operatorname{rank}\Theta^{(h)}_{\beta,O}=\dim\mathcal K_O,
\qquad
\lVert\Theta^{(h)}_{\beta,O}\rVert=e^{-\beta E_{\min}}.
\tag{F.10.4f.12}
$$
The infimum defining the nuclear norm is attained by the energy-eigenbasis decomposition below. Consequently:

1. a decomposition satisfying (F.10.4f.5) exists exactly when $\log Z_O(\beta)\le C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta)$, and the norm condition in (F.10.4f.3) holds exactly when $H_O\ge0$;
2. if $\mathcal K_O=\bigotimes_{s=1}^{N}\mathcal K_s$ and $H_O=\sum_sH_s$, with $H_s$ acting on the $s$-th factor, then $Z_O=\prod_sZ_s$. If each $H_s$ has the eigenvalue $0$ and at least one further eigenvalue in $[0,E_*]$, counted with multiplicity, then (F.10.4f.5) forces the species bound
$$
N\le\frac{C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta)}{\log\!\left(1+e^{-\beta E_*}\right)};
\tag{F.10.4f.13}
$$
3. along a sequence of such approximants, one $h$-independent $C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta)$ admits decompositions satisfying (F.10.4f.5) for every $h$ exactly when $\sup_h\log Z_{O,h}(\beta)<\infty$. In particular, an unbounded number of species obeying the hypothesis of item 2 with one fixed $E_*$ excludes every uniform capacity certificate at every $\beta>0$.

*Proof.* The map $V\xi=\xi\otimes\Omega_c$ is an isometry, $A\mapsto A\otimes I_c$ is an isometric identification of the domains, and $e^{-\beta H_c}\Omega_c=\Omega_c$. Hence $\Theta^{(h)}_{\beta,O}(A\otimes I_c)=V\Theta_O(A)$ with $\Theta_O(A)=e^{-\beta H_O}A\Omega_O$. Composition with the contractions $V$ and $V^*$ increases neither nuclear norms nor ranks, and $V^*V=I$, so it suffices to treat $\Theta_O$.

Let $(e_j)$ be an orthonormal eigenbasis of $H_O$ with eigenvalues $E_j$. Then
$$
\Theta_O(A)=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}\,\langle e_j,A\Omega_O\rangle\,e_j.
\tag{F.10.4f.14}
$$
The functional $A\mapsto\langle e_j,A\Omega_O\rangle$ has norm $\lVert e_j\rVert\,\lVert\Omega_O\rVert=1$, attained at $A=|e_j\rangle\langle\Omega_O|$, so (F.10.4f.14) has nuclear sum $Z_O(\beta)$. Conversely, let $\Theta_O=\sum_r\varphi_r(\cdot)\xi_r$ be any nuclear decomposition, finite or absolutely summable, and define the contraction $S:\mathcal K_O\to B(\mathcal K_O)$ by $S\xi=|\xi\rangle\langle\Omega_O|$. Then $\Theta_O(S\xi)=e^{-\beta H_O}\xi$, so
$$
Z_O(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}(\Theta_O\circ S)=\sum_r\varphi_r(S\xi_r)\le\sum_r\lVert\varphi_r\rVert\,\lVert\xi_r\rVert.
$$
Hence $\lVert\Theta_O\rVert_1=Z_O(\beta)$, attained by (F.10.4f.14). The map $A\mapsto A\Omega_O$ is onto $\mathcal K_O$ and $e^{-\beta H_O}$ is invertible, which gives the rank. Finally $\lVert\Theta_O(A)\rVert\le\lVert e^{-\beta H_O}\rVert\,\lVert A\rVert$, with equality at $A=|e_{\min}\rangle\langle\Omega_O|$ for a lowest eigenvector $e_{\min}$; thus $\lVert\Theta_O\rVert=e^{-\beta E_{\min}}$.

Item 1 follows because the finite-dimensional infimum is attained, and $e^{-\beta E_{\min}}\le1$ exactly when $E_{\min}\ge0$. For item 2, $e^{-\beta H_O}=\bigotimes_se^{-\beta H_s}$ and the trace is multiplicative on tensor products. The two displayed eigenvalues give $Z_s(\beta)\ge1+e^{-\beta E_*}$, and taking logarithms in $\prod_sZ_s(\beta)\le e^{C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta)}$ gives (F.10.4f.13). Item 3 is item 1 applied uniformly in $h$, and item 2 gives $\log Z_{O,h}(\beta)\ge N_h\log(1+e^{-\beta E_*})$. ∎

Theorem F.10.4f.5 identifies the finite nuclear norm of Definition F.10.4f.1 with the local partition function on product-vacuum approximants. The weak-limit hypotheses of Theorem F.10.4f.2 and the positive-tolerance realization costs of Theorem F.10.4f.4 keep their stated scope.

<a id="theorem-f104f6-entangled-energy-nuclearity-and-an-interacting-tensor-limit"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.6 (Entangled Energy-Nuclearity and an Interacting Tensor Limit).** Let $A=\mathbb C^d$, $C=\mathbb C^r$, $r\le d$, and
$$
\Omega=\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}\sqrt{p_j}\,e_j\otimes f_j,\quad p_j>0,\quad\sum_jp_j=1,
\qquad H(e_i\otimes f_j)=E_{ij}e_i\otimes f_j.
$$
For real $E_{ij}$ and $\beta>0$, the map $T(B)=e^{-\beta H}(B\otimes I)\Omega$ from the operator-norm matrix algebra to the Hilbert space has exact Banach nuclear norm and rank
$$
\nu(T)=\sum_{i,j}\sqrt{p_j}e^{-\beta E_{ij}},\qquad\operatorname{rank}T=dr.
\tag{F.10.4f.15}
$$
Here $\nu$ denotes the nuclear norm denoted $\|\cdot\|_1$ in Definition F.10.4f.1. In particular $E_{ij}=E_i$ gives the factor $(\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H_A})\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt{\rho_A}$, and the maximally entangled zero-Hamiltonian case gives $d^{3/2}$.

For an infinite interacting example fix $0<r_0<1$, $\beta\ge\beta_0>0$, $p_j=(1-r_0^2)r_0^{2j}$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)\otimes\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)$ and $E_{ij}=(i-j)^2$. The resulting normalized $\Omega$ is cyclic and separating for the left algebra, $H\ge0$ and $H\Omega=0$. Put
$$
C_0=1+2\sum_{k\ge1}e^{-\beta_0k^2},\quad S=\frac{\sqrt{1-r_0^2}}{1-r_0},\quad
\ell_n=\sqrt{1-r_0^{2n}},\quad m=\lfloor n/2\rfloor,
$$
$$
D_n=C_0Sr_0^m+\frac{S e^{-\beta_0(n-m)^2}}{1-e^{-\beta_0}}.
$$
For the normalized $n\times n$ corner approximants, transported by compression on the domain and corner inclusion on the Hilbert target, their representing tensors satisfy
$$
\|U-U_n\|_\pi\le D_n+(\ell_n^{-1}-1)C_0S\longrightarrow0,
\qquad \nu(T_n)\le\frac{C_0}{1-r_0},
\tag{F.10.4f.16}
$$
uniformly for $\beta\ge\beta_0$. Thus they populate the analytic tensor-convergence premises of Theorem F.10.4f.2.

*Proof.* The coordinate functionals $\varphi_{ij}(B)=\langle e_i,Be_j\rangle$ have norm one, so the positive coefficient expansion gives the upper bound in (F.10.4f.15). The map sending $\sum x_{ij}e_i\otimes f_j$ to $\sum x_{ij}|e_i\rangle\langle e_j|$ is a contraction into operator norm, since operator norm is bounded by Hilbert--Schmidt norm. Composing any nuclear representation of $T$ with it and taking the finite trace gives the positive coefficient sum as a lower bound. Every coefficient is nonzero, so all $dr$ independent outputs occur.

For the infinite model, every matrix unit applied to $\Omega$ gives a nonzero scalar multiple of $e_i\otimes f_j$, proving cyclicity. All $p_j>0$ imply separatingness. The positive diagonal Hamiltonian is self-adjoint on its square-summability domain and annihilates $\Omega$. Every column heat sum is at most $C_0$, giving absolute projective convergence of
$$
U=\sum_{i,j\ge0}\sqrt{p_j}e^{-\beta(i-j)^2}\varphi_{ij}\otimes(e_i\otimes f_j).
$$
Its coefficients agree with the spectral action on $(B\otimes I)\Omega$, so it represents $T$. The finite tensor is $\ell_n^{-1}$ times the square truncation. Terms with $j\ge m$ cost at most $C_0Sr_0^m$; among the remaining terms outside the square one has $i\ge n$, so $i-j\ge n-m$ and the Gaussian-series tail is at most $e^{-\beta_0(n-m)^2}/(1-e^{-\beta_0})$. This proves the missing-tail bound $D_n$. Normalization gives the other term in (F.10.4f.16), and $\ell_n\ge\sqrt{1-r_0^2}$ gives its uniform finite norm bound. Finite-corner trace tests also prove that the infinite nuclear norm equals its full positive coefficient sum. ∎

On a fixed bandwidth-$b$ core, write $P_n$ for the first $n$ levels, $\rho_n=P_n\rho P_n/(1-r_0^{2n})$, and
$$
\pi_n(A)=P_nAP_n,\qquad
\iota_n(B)=B\oplus\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_nB)I_{P_n^\perp},\qquad E_n=\iota_n\pi_n.
$$
Both maps are UCP, and for $n>b$,
$$
|\omega(A)-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_n\pi_nA)|\le2r_0^{2n}\|A\|,
\qquad\|(A-E_nA)\Omega\|\le(r_0^{n-b}+2r_0^n)\|A\|.
\tag{F.10.4f.17}
$$
Indeed the state tail has mass $r_0^{2n}$. Writing $Q_n=I-P_n$, the operator difference is $Q_nAP_n+AQ_n-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_nP_nAP_n)Q_n$; the last two terms each cost $r_0^n\|A\|$, while bandwidth confines the first to input indices at least $n-b$. This proves the bound. The heat-map error is bounded by (F.10.4f.16). A sufficient cutoff grows as $O(b+\ln(1/\delta))$; circuit and complete PCE costs still require the interfaces of Definition F.10.4f.3.

<a id="theorem-f104f7-literal-rank-and-unsmeared-core-obstructions"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.7 (Literal Rank and Unsmeared-Core Obstructions).** Let $S_h:X\to Y$ be linear maps into a Hausdorff locally convex space whose continuous dual separates points. If $\operatorname{rank}S_h\le R<\infty$ and $S_hx\to Sx$ weakly for every $x$, then $\operatorname{rank}S\le R$. Consequently the literal regulator-independent rank bound in (F.10.4f.3), under the comparison maps of Theorem F.10.4f.2, excludes an infinite-dimensional faithful local algebra with limiting map $A\mapsto e^{-\beta H}A\Omega$ at finite $\beta>0$ and $H\ge0$.

In the infinite example of Theorem F.10.4f.6, every finite-rank linear $E:A\to A$ additionally satisfies
$$
\sup_{\|A\|\le1}\|(A-EA)\Omega\|\ge\sqrt{p_0}.
\tag{F.10.4f.18}
$$
Thus uniform nuclearity and tensor convergence do not discharge the full-unit-ball form of (F.10.4f.8).

*Proof.* For any $R+1$ domain vectors and $R+1$ continuous functionals, the corresponding matrix of pairings with $S_h$ has determinant zero. Passing to the limit preserves zero determinant. If the limit had $R+1$ independent images, continuous coordinate functionals on their finite-dimensional span, extended to $Y$ by Hahn--Banach, would give an identity pairing matrix, a contradiction. Comparison maps cannot increase rank. Faithfulness makes $A\mapsto A\Omega$ injective. Spectral calculus gives $\ker e^{-\beta H}=0$ because $e^{-2\beta E}>0$ at every finite spectral value. Their composition on an infinite-dimensional algebra has infinite rank, proving the first obstruction.
