For the second take $A_k=|e_k\rangle\langle e_0|$, of norm one. Their images $A_k\Omega=\sqrt{p_0}e_k\otimes f_0$ are orthogonal with common norm. All $(EA_k)\Omega$ lie in one finite-dimensional subspace. Bessel's inequality makes the distances of these orthogonal vectors from that subspace tend to $\sqrt{p_0}$, proving (F.10.4f.18). Every factorization through a finite-dimensional algebra has finite rank. The bandwidth-core bounds (F.10.4f.17) and accuracy-dependent approximation ranks retain their different quantifiers. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104f8-implementation-specific-nuclearity-window"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.8 (Implementation-Specific Nuclearity Window).** Let $M\subset B(\mathcal H)$ have a cyclic separating unit vector $\Omega$, and let $U(t)=e^{\mathrm{itL}}$ normalize $M$ and fix $\Omega$ for every real $t$. Its modular conjugation satisfies $JLJ=-L$. Hence $L\ge0$ forces $L=0$; a finite-positive-temperature KMS state for the resulting identity dynamics is tracial.

Positive implementers of a nontrivial faithful Gibbs dynamics nevertheless exist when vector fixing is not imposed. Let $K\ge0$ be a nonscalar finite Hamiltonian, $\rho=e^{-bK}/Z(b)$, $b>0$, and represent the algebra on its Hilbert--Schmidt space by left multiplication with $\Omega=\sqrt\rho$. Both
$$
H_+X=KX,\qquad LX=KX-XK
$$
implement $\alpha_t(A)=e^{\mathrm{itK}}Ae^{-itK}$. Here $H_+\ge0$, $L\Omega=0$, and $H_+\Omega\ne0$. The state is $b$-KMS. At real heat parameter $s$, the exact finite nuclear norms are
$$
\nu(T_s^+)=\frac{Z(s)Z(b/2)}{\sqrt{Z(b)}},\qquad
\nu(T_s^L)=\frac{Z(s)Z(b/2-s)}{\sqrt{Z(b)}}.
\tag{F.10.4f.19}
$$
For $Ke_j=\varepsilon j e_j$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)$, use the unitized compact algebra and its left representation, with $q=e^{-b\varepsilon}$ and $\rho=\sum_j(1-q)q^j|e_j\rangle\langle e_j|$. Then $T_s^+$ is nuclear exactly for $s>0$, while $T_s^L$ is nuclear exactly for $0<s<b/2$, with norms
$$
\nu(T_s^+)=\frac{\sqrt{1-q}}{(1-e^{-s\varepsilon})(1-e^{-b\varepsilon/2})},\qquad
\nu(T_s^L)=\frac{\sqrt{1-q}}{(1-e^{-s\varepsilon})(1-e^{-(b/2-s)\varepsilon})}.
\tag{F.10.4f.20}
$$
At $s=0$ both maps are bounded and noncompact; the canonical map is also bounded and noncompact at $s=b/2$. Outside the respective closed intervals the finite-matrix-core maps have no bounded extensions.

*Proof.* On the Tomita core $M\Omega$, $S_0(A\Omega)=A^*\Omega$ commutes with $U(t)$ by normalization and vector invariance. The inverse group preserves the same core, so graph closure gives $USU^*=S$. Uniqueness of $S=J\Delta^{1/2}$ then gives $UJU^*=J$. Antiunitarity yields $Je^{\mathrm{itL}}J=e^{-itJLJ}$; uniqueness of the generator proves $JLJ=-L$, including domains. Its real spectrum is symmetric. Positivity therefore forces zero; the KMS boundary relation for the identity flow becomes $\omega(AB)=\omega(BA)$. These are the standard-implementation facts of Dereziński, Jakšić and Pillet (2003), Theorem 2.10 and Proposition 2.14 in their author preprint.

For the Gibbs model the two unitary groups are $X\mapsto e^{\mathrm{itK}}X$ and $X\mapsto e^{\mathrm{itK}}Xe^{-itK}$, so direct conjugation gives the same algebra automorphism. Trace cyclicity gives $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A\alpha_{ib}(B))=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho BA)$; finite matrices are analytic and the bounded-strip condition follows by three-lines. On the unitized compact oscillator algebra, finite matrix units and the identity form a dense analytic subalgebra; norm approximation and the same strip bound prove KMS for the full algebra. The Gibbs vector is cyclic because matrix-unit images span Hilbert--Schmidt space and separating because $\sqrt\rho$ has dense range.

On matrix units, the two heat maps have positive coefficients $Z(b)^{-1/2}e^{-sE_i-bE_j/2}$ and $Z(b)^{-1/2}e^{-sE_i-(b/2-s)E_j}$. The coordinate decomposition and contraction/trace proof of Theorem F.10.4f.6 give (F.10.4f.19). In the oscillator the convergent geometric sums give (F.10.4f.20); finite-corner traces give the matching lower bounds. Their coefficient summability also proves that every $A\Omega$ lies in the spectral domain of $e^{-sL}$ in the claimed open window. At $s=0$, images of $E_{i0}$ are orthogonal of common nonzero length; at $s=b/2$ the canonical images of $E_{0j}$ have that property. The endpoint expressions are $A\sqrt\rho$ and $\sqrt\rho A$, both contractions. Nuclear operators are compact by truncating their summable representations, so the endpoints are not nuclear. For $s<0$, images of $E_{i0}$ grow exponentially; for canonical $s>b/2$, images of $E_{0j}$ grow exponentially. This excludes bounded extensions.

Writing either convergent coefficient array as $cx^iy^j$, its normalized $n$-corner tensor obeys
$$
\|U-U_n\|_\pi\le\frac c{(1-x)(1-y)}
\left[x^n+y^n+(1-q^n)^{-1/2}-1\right].
$$
This follows by summing outside the square and paying normalization. It is uniform on $s\ge s_0>0$ for $H_+$ and on $0<s_0\le s\le s_1<b/2$ for $L$. It proves the corresponding tensor-limit premises; both finite ranks are $n^2$. ∎

The implementing automorphism alone does not fix the numerical nuclearity bound: replacing $H$ by $H+cI$ multiplies the map and its nuclear norm by $e^{-sc}$ while preserving that automorphism. An implementation and energy origin are therefore part of a phase-space datum. The interacting example in Theorem F.10.4f.6 also needs its own clock identification: for $A=|e_0\rangle\langle e_1|\otimes I$ and $B=I\otimes|f_0\rangle\langle f_1|$,
$$
\|[e^{\mathrm{itH}}Ae^{-itH},B]\|=2|\sin t|.
$$
The phases on complementary indices $0,1$ are $e^{-it},e^{it}$, proving this formula. Thus that Hamiltonian does not normalize the fixed left algebra. Its analytic tensor estimates hold, while a KMS interpretation must specify the invariant algebra and implementing clock. Definition F.10.4f.1 does not itself require $H\Omega_*=0$, so the canonical-positive obstruction applies when that extra vector-fixing premise is supplied.

<a id="proposition-f104f9-finite-minor-witness-for-the-literal-capacity-route"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.9 (Finite Minor Witness for the Literal Capacity Route).** Retain (F.10.4f.3) unchanged, fix $O$ and a finite positive heat parameter, and put $R=\lfloor e^{C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta)}\rfloor$. Under the contractive comparison maps and pointwise weak limit in Theorem F.10.4f.2, Theorem F.10.4f.7 refutes the conjunction of this rank cap and a faithful infinite-dimensional limiting local phase-space map. This conclusion applies to the exact rank, rather than a nuclear norm or an accuracy-dependent rank.

A concrete separating minor is available in Theorem F.10.4f.6. Set $r_0=1/2$, $\beta=\log 2$ in that theorem's energy units, $d=R+1$, $A_k=|e_k\rangle\langle e_0|$ and $f_i(\xi)=\langle e_i\otimes f_0,\xi\rangle$, for $0\le i,k<d$. Then
$$
[f_i(\Theta A_k)]_{i,k<d}
=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}2^{-k^2}\right)_{k=0}^{R},
\qquad
\det[f_i(\Theta A_k)]
=\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)^d
2^{-R(R+1)(2R+1)/6}>0.
\tag{F.10.4f.21}
$$
For $R=4$ this determinant is $9\sqrt3/2^{35}$. The same witness has a typed positive-Gibbs version in Theorem F.10.4f.8: $b\varepsilon=\log4$ and $s\varepsilon=\log2$ give entries $(\sqrt3/2)2^{-k}$ and determinant $(\sqrt3/2)^d2^{-R(R+1)/2}$, equal to $9\sqrt3/2^{15}$ when $R=4$. Every rank-at-most-$R$ transported map $S$ has maximum entry error on this finite list at least $(\sqrt3/2)2^{-R^2}/(R+1)$ in the interacting example, and at least $(\sqrt3/2)2^{-R}/(R+1)$ in the positive-Gibbs example.

*Proof.* In the interacting example, $A_k\Omega=(\sqrt3/2)e_k\otimes f_0$ and its energy is $k^2$. In the positive-Gibbs example the represented energy of $e_k\otimes f_0$ is $\varepsilon k$. These facts give the displayed diagonal matrices. For every transported finite map of rank at most $R$, the same $(R+1)$-square pairing matrix has determinant zero. Its entries converge individually under the stipulated pointwise weak convergence, whereas the displayed determinant is positive. For the quantitative statement, write $M$ for the positive diagonal witness and $N$ for the pairing matrix of $S$. Choose a unit vector in $\ker N$. Then $\min_iM_{ii}\le\|M-N\|\le d\max_{i,k}|M_{ik}-N_{ik}|$. Thus each family supplies a finite witness and a positive finite-test error threshold for the accepted obstruction. The first witness uses the analytic interacting family; its clock identification keeps the separate restriction in Theorem F.10.4f.8. The second uses that theorem's specified positive implementer. For a general faithful local algebra the source-bound conclusion follows directly from Theorem F.10.4f.7. ∎

<a id="definition-f104f10-charged-positive-gibbs-register-successor"></a>**Definition F.10.4f.10 (Charged Positive-Gibbs Register Successor).** The successor replaces the regulator-independent exact rank requirement by accuracy-dependent finite ranks $n(\delta)^2$, and chooses a fixed bandwidth test set. Equation (F.10.4f.3) remains the antecedent of the literal route in Proposition F.10.4f.9.

Fix $\varepsilon>0$ in energy units, inverse energy-temperature $b>0$, bandwidth $w\in\mathbb N_0$, and a heat window $s\ge s_0>0$, with $s,b$ in inverse energy units. Let
$$
\mathcal A=\mathcal K(\ell^2(\mathbb N_0))+\mathbb CI,
\quad Ke_j=\varepsilon j e_j,
\quad q=e^{-b\varepsilon},\quad y=\sqrt q,
\quad\rho=(1-q)\sum_{j\ge0}q^j|e_j\rangle\langle e_j|.
$$
The algebra acts by left multiplication on Hilbert--Schmidt operators; $\Omega=\sqrt\rho$. The represented time group is $\alpha_t(A)=e^{itK/\hbar}Ae^{-itK/\hbar}$, with $t$ in seconds; the temperature is $T=1/(k_Bb)$, and the imaginary physical-time period is $\hbar b$. Use the positive represented energy $H_+X=KX$, with energy origin $\inf\sigma K=0$. The phase-space map is $T_s^+(A)=e^{-sK}A\sqrt\rho$. The retained test set $\mathcal T_w$ consists of contractions $A\in\mathcal A$ with $A_{ij}=0$ for $|i-j|>w$; each finite protocol declares its bandwidth before choosing the cutoff. Products use their actual summed bandwidth. The union over finite bandwidths contains the finite matrix algebra and the identity.

For a dyadic cutoff $n=2^k>w$, put $P_n=\sum_{j<n}|e_j\rangle\langle e_j|$,
$$
\rho_n=\frac{P_n\rho P_n}{1-q^n},\quad
\pi_n(A)=P_nAP_n,\quad
\iota_n(B)=B\oplus\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_nB)I_{P_n^\perp},\quad
E_n=\iota_n\pi_n.
$$
The finite source is a labelled binary register, grouped three qubits to each $\mathbb C^8$ carrier, with Gibbs preparations, the channels below, diagonal clock gates, contraction-access circuits, and retained success and readout registers. Its index source has $m=2^\ell\ge n$ levels and Hamiltonian $K_m=\varepsilon\sum_{r<\ell}2^r|1\rangle\langle1|_r$. At each accuracy the default source size is $m=2n$; a larger supplied source is charged at its actual $\ell$ and duration. Every physical source parameter and requested clock or heat query has a finite computable description and a certified precision-production routine covered by the same computation and storage budget below. The analytic heat bound covers all real $s\ge s_0$; a uniformly priced family of queries additionally obeys this production bound. The source-to-carrier map is the binary basis isometry on every named register, tensor the identity on spectators. It transports all instruments by conjugation and keeps every declared classical outcome label.

Contraction access is an explicit input of this source class. For every admitted test $A$ and precision $p$, a supplied, verified compiler produces a unitary block circuit whose ideal successful block is $P_nAP_n$ and whose implemented successful block differs by at most its certified gate-error sum. Each requested reference-vector preparation or readout has its own such circuit record. The compiler's computation, program, working memory, gate list, parameters and verification are charged. The class fixes constants $a,d$ in advance and admits inputs only when their complete production and circuit records have at most $a(n+1)^d(p+1)^d$ elementary operations and bits. This is a finite-register access condition on the chosen source. A bare matrix-entry oracle or an unspecified preparation supplies no admitted input. The class is nonempty: the matrix units $|e_0\rangle\langle e_0|$ and $|e_0\rangle\langle e_1|$ when $w\ge1$, their bounded-size fixed sums with supplied contraction dilations, and scalar contractions have direct controlled-swap and rotation compilers with this bound. It also admits directly supplied finite gate circuits with their full production records.

The primitive service supplies CNOT, reversible classical gates, and controlled one-qubit rotations or phases. A $p$-bit calibrated logical control has code-restricted coherent error at most $2^{-p}$, at most $a_g(p+1)^{d_g}$ charged primitive pulse uses, and duration at most $\tau_0 a_g(p+1)^{d_g}$. Its parameter production and stored control bits are also charged. The counter $G$ below counts these primitive uses, so the precision-dependent service cost is included in the fixed tariff. Classical compilation has a fixed clock and per-step tariff; no computational work is free. Fix in advance the prices for clean qubits, gate uses, parameter bits, memory-qubit-ticks, record-bit-ticks, communication bits, compiler/checker steps and ready-state renewal. All have positive finite values in a nominated service-cost unit. A reset swaps the spent register with a paid clean register and moves the displaced state into the paid archive for the protocol's declared finite holding interval. The source owns preparations, clocks, control and archives; the query service owns probe circuits and their records. Retained output memory has a declared owner and holding interval. A finite protocol fixes its number of calls, records and samples; an accuracy-dependent sampling or storage request pays its actual additional count.

For a run let $Q$ count allocated qubits, $G$ elementary gate uses, $B$ stored control bits, $L$ communicated bits, $J$ compiler/checker steps, $Q_{\rm clean}$ clean qubits, $Q_{\rm reset}$ ready-state renewals, and $W_q,W_c$ the actual qubit-tick and retained-record-bit-tick totals, including archives. The complete source cost is the fixed linear tariff
$$
C=\kappa_qQ+\kappa_gG+\kappa_bB+\kappa_lL+\kappa_jJ
 +\kappa_{\rm clean}Q_{\rm clean}+\kappa_{\rm reset}Q_{\rm reset}
 +\kappa_{mq}W_q+\kappa_{mc}W_c.
\tag{F.10.4f.22}
$$
The execution clock has tick $\tau_0$ and is distinct from the represented evolution label $t$. The duration is the sum of actual serial primitive durations, compiler/checker ticks and the declared holding intervals. The response map sends the compiled phase circuit to $\alpha_t$ at its labelled $t$; identifying this label with elapsed microscopic evolution is an additional clock comparison. Parallel execution may reduce that sum and retains every occupied-memory charge. The source records counts before discarding any auxiliary state. The retained infinite responses are the state functional, GNS vector and heat vector for each admitted final test, together with the finite circuits' declared classical records; a different infinite-process response requires its own comparison. Thermal work identifications, a regional net and a geometric area tariff enter through their separately nominated source data.

<a id="theorem-f104f11-simultaneous-gibbs-register-bounds-and-circuits"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.11 (Simultaneous Gibbs Register Bounds and Circuits).** Definition F.10.4f.10 has the following properties.

1. The state is faithful and $b$-KMS for $\tau\mapsto\alpha_{\hbar\tau}$. It is invariant as a state under the represented time group. The implementer $e^{itH_+/\hbar}$ fixes neither $\Omega$ nor its ray for all real $t$. The canonical implementer $LX=KX-XK$ fixes $\Omega$ and has both energy signs. With $x_0=e^{-s_0\varepsilon}$ and $K_0=\sqrt{1-q}/[(1-x_0)(1-y)]$, the positive map is nuclear for every $s>0$, uniformly bounded in nuclear norm on $s\ge s_0$. Its finite ranks are $n^2$.
2. Both interfaces are UCP. For every $A\in\mathcal T_w$, their simultaneous errors satisfy
$$
\begin{aligned}
|\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_n\pi_nA)|&\le2q^n,\\
\|(A-E_nA)\sqrt\rho\|_2&\le y^{n-w}+2y^n,\\
\sup_{s\ge s_0}\|T_s^+-T_{s,n}^+\pi_n\|_{\infty\to2}
&\le K_0\bigl[x_0^n+y^n+(1-q^n)^{-1/2}-1\bigr].
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.10.4f.23}
$$
The finite heat target is included into the infinite Hilbert--Schmidt space by zero extension. The third bound also holds in projective-tensor norm and on the entire algebra unit ball. For each fixed $w,b,\varepsilon,s_0$ and $0<\delta_0<1$, a dyadic cutoff $n=O(w+\log(1/\delta_0))$ makes all three bounds at most $\delta_0$.
3. The source has explicit finite circuits for $\rho_n$, for the Schrödinger duals of compression and recovery between $M_n$ and every supplied $M_m$, and for the unnormalized positive heat response. If $e$ is the sum of coherent gate and access errors in the chosen circuit realization, the additional errors in state, GNS and heat-map comparisons are respectively at most $2e,2e,e$, with each budget taken over the gates participating in that comparison. Code leakage is included in the coherent error. The implementation-channel bounds hold with the complete declared record retained, relative to the ideal finite circuits. Their composition adds the participating per-call coherent errors. For a single contraction success/failure readout, the infinite instrument has success probability $p(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A^*A)$ and its ideal finite circuit has $p_n(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_n(\pi_nA)^*\pi_nA)$. Their complete binary-record measure-norm distance is at most $2q^{n-w}$, and the implemented circuit adds at most $2e$. The same bound holds for the joint-success versus failure record of positive heat damping after $A$. A more detailed or sequential infinite record uses its actual effect-comparison term below; bandwidth alone does not identify the composed effects. At fixed protocol length and holding intervals, polynomial charged access yields a cost polynomial in $\log(1/\delta)$ on the default $m=2n$ source, with $\delta_0+2e\le\delta$. Larger input sources, additional samples and longer record retention contribute their actual cost in (F.10.4f.22).

*Proof.* The algebra, state and represented positive energy are the oscillator instance of Theorem F.10.4f.8, so that theorem supplies the KMS and nuclearity statements with the present units. Directly, $H_+\Omega$ has a nonzero $j=1$ component. Ray invariance for every real $t$ would require $e^{it\varepsilon j/\hbar}$ to be independent of $j$ on the positive weights of $\Omega$, which fails for $j=0,1$. The canonical operator has eigenvalue $\varepsilon(i-j)$ on $|e_i\rangle\langle e_j|$, annihilates $\Omega$, and has both signs. Matrix units show finite rank $n^2$ because every coefficient is nonzero.

Compression is UCP with the corner's own identity. The scalar state in the complementary block makes $\iota_n$ UCP and unital; its range lies in $\mathcal A$, because it differs from a scalar identity by a finite-rank operator. The state tail has mass $q^n$, giving the first bound. With $Q_n=I-P_n$ and $c_A=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_nP_nAP_n)$,
$$
A-E_nA=Q_nAP_n+AQ_n-c_AQ_n.
$$
The second and third terms applied to $\sqrt\rho$ each have Hilbert--Schmidt norm at most $y^n$. Bandwidth makes the first vanish on input indices below $n-w$, so its norm is at most $\sqrt{\sum_{j\ge n-w}(1-q)q^j}=y^{n-w}$. This proves the GNS estimate uniformly on the admitted test set.

The positive heat coefficients are $\sqrt{1-q}\,x^iy^j$, with $x=e^{-s\varepsilon}$. The discarded square has total coefficient sum at most $K_0(x_0^n+y^n)$, and finite-state normalization adds at most $K_0[(1-q^n)^{-1/2}-1]$. This is the projective-tensor estimate, which dominates the operator-to-Hilbert norm. If $q^n\le1/2$, the normalization term is at most $2q^n$. Set $z=\max(x_0,y)<1$. It suffices to choose an integer
$$
n_*\ge\max\left\{w+1,\ w+\frac{\log(3/\delta_0)}{-\log y},\
\frac{\log(4K_0/\delta_0)}{-\log z},\
\frac{\log(2/\delta_0)}{-\log q}\right\},
$$
and take the least dyadic $n\ge n_*$. Then $n<2n_*$ except at the exact dyadic endpoint, all three errors are at most $\delta_0$, and the asserted cutoff follows for fixed positive $b,\varepsilon,s_0$ and fixed bandwidth.

The finite Gibbs purification has an explicit product circuit. Write the level $j$ in binary as $\sum_{r<k}2^r j_r$. The identity
$$
\sum_{j<n}q^j=\prod_{r<k}(1+q^{2^r})
$$
gives
$$
\Omega_n=\bigotimes_{r<k}
\frac{|00\rangle+y^{2^r}|11\rangle}{\sqrt{1+q^{2^r}}}.
\tag{F.10.4f.24}
$$
For each pair apply $R_y(2\arctan(y^{2^r}))$ to its first qubit, then CNOT to its second. This uses $k$ rotations and $k$ CNOTs. Keeping both registers supplies the stated GNS vector; tracing the second supplies $\rho_n$. Its discarded register belongs to the source's charged archive.

The dual of compression is the isometric insertion $J_{n,m}(\sigma)=\sigma\oplus0$, implemented by adjoining zero high bits. The dual of the finite recovery block is
$$
R_{n,m}(\sigma)=P_n\sigma P_n+\operatorname{Tr}(Q_n\sigma)\rho_n.
\tag{F.10.4f.25}
$$
Here the output corner is identified with $M_n$ and $Q_n$ is inside $M_m$. A reversible comparator computes the flag $f=[j\ge n]$ on the input index. When $f=0$, swap the low $k$ input bits into a fresh output register. The remaining input and all ancillary bits are zero on this branch. When $f=1$, leave the entire input index in the environment and prepare (F.10.4f.24) on the fresh output and a purifying register. Retain the flag. The environment is identical for every low-index input and orthogonal between the two flag branches and between distinct high input indices. Partial trace therefore preserves every low-block coherence, removes all low/high coherences, and replaces the high block by its trace times $\rho_n$. This proves (F.10.4f.25) on every matrix unit and hence every input, including inputs entangled with an external reference. The comparator, swaps and controlled preparation require $O(\ell+k)$ elementary reversible and controlled gates using work qubits. Their environments, work qubits and flags are individually included in the resource counters. The finite dual's Heisenberg action is exactly $B\mapsto B\oplus\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_nB)I_{m-n}$; its formulas are compatible for all $m\ge n$ with the prescribed infinite scalar extension.

For the heat map, prepare $\Omega_n$, apply the admitted contraction block circuit to its first register, and retain that circuit's success flag. For each level bit $j_r$ of the first register, condition a fresh flag rotation on $j_r=1$, with cosine $x^{2^r}$. The block in which every heat flag is zero multiplies $|j\rangle$ by $\prod_r x^{2^rj_r}=x^j$. The joint successful block is exactly $e^{-sK_n}(P_nAP_n)\sqrt{\rho_n}$. All failure flags remain part of the instrument. The retained linear heat response is this unnormalized vector; conditional normalization would define a different response map. There is no uncharged repeat-until-success step. The finite represented-clock circuit uses the product of the diagonal phases $e^{it\varepsilon2^r/\hbar}$ on the first register. Parameter production for $s,t$ is included in the source input and its compilation tariff; any uniformly priced parameter range or algorithm must satisfy the charged-access condition.

Every finite source register has a binary basis isometry into $\lceil Q/3\rceil$ eight-dimensional carriers. Extend each gate by the identity on unused code levels. Ideal code invariance is then exact, and the binary conjugation preserves the complete record law. The implementation statement uses the supplied gate calibrations, rather than deducing an error norm from the embedding dimension. If $V_j$ is an ideal gate isometry and $\widehat V_j$ its implementation, telescoping a product of contractions gives
$$
\|\widehat V-V\|\le\sum_j\|\widehat V_j-V_j\|=:e.
$$
A code-block error $\eta_j$ and leakage probability bounded uniformly by $\lambda_j$ supply the sufficient summand $\eta_j+\sqrt{\lambda_j}$, by orthogonal projection onto the code and its complement. The primitive coherent bound already includes both. For normalized input vectors, the two resulting pure-state density operators differ in trace norm by at most $2e$. Partial trace and a fixed readout contract this bound, also with reference and outcome registers retained. A telescoping composition of channels adds these implementation errors, including under common adaptive processing. This is a comparison with the ideal finite instrument, including its retained outcome registers.

For the infinite-versus-finite contraction readout, write
$$
a=\sum_{j<n}(1-q)q^j\|P_nAe_j\|^2,\quad
d=\sum_{j<n}(1-q)q^j\|Q_nAe_j\|^2,\quad
u=\sum_{j\ge n}(1-q)q^j\|Ae_j\|^2.
$$
Then $p(A)=a+d+u$ and $p_n(A)=a/(1-q^n)$. Contractivity gives $0\le a\le1-q^n$ and $0\le u\le q^n$. Bandwidth gives $0\le d\le q^{n-w}-q^n$, since $Q_nAe_j=0$ for $j<n-w$. Hence
$$
-q^n\le p(A)-p_n(A)
=d+u-\frac{q^n}{1-q^n}a\le q^{n-w}.
$$
A Bernoulli record has full measure-norm distance $2|p-p_n|$, proving the bound $2q^{n-w}$. Replacing $A$ by the contraction $e^{-sK}A$ preserves its bandwidth and obeys $\pi_n(e^{-sK}A)=e^{-sK_n}\pi_n(A)$; this proves the stated joint heat-success bound. These records include failure with its full probability. Internal failure flags need their actual effects if distinguished further. At the cutoff already chosen, $y^{n-w}\le\delta_0/3$ gives $2q^{n-w}\le2\delta_0^2/9\le\delta_0$.

More generally let a nominated infinite instrument and its finite source instrument have complete finite-outcome POVMs $(F_a)$ and $(F_{n,a})$, respectively. Put
$$
\Delta_n=\sum_a\left|\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\rho_n[F_{n,a}-P_nF_aP_n]\bigr)\right|.
$$
The complete record laws satisfy the effect-comparison bound
$$
\|\mathbb P_\rho-\mathbb P_{\rho_n,n}\|_1\le2q^n+\Delta_n.
$$
Indeed, first measure $(F_a)$ in the normalized corner state $\rho_n\oplus0$; contraction of the exact state-norm difference bounds this change by $2q^n$. The difference from that law to the actual finite law is exactly the displayed sum $\Delta_n$, so the triangle inequality proves the claim. The term is zero when every finite effect is the compressed infinite effect. For instrument products, this equality must be proved or the term evaluated from their actual effects. A general circuit-access record supplies no automatic vanishing estimate for $\Delta_n$. The contraction calculation above gives a complete admitted case directly, without such an assumption.

For a Heisenberg channel, expanding $\widehat V^*(B\otimes I)\widehat V-V^*(B\otimes I)V$ bounds its completely bounded norm by $2e\|B\|$. Applying it to the fixed $\Omega$ proves the GNS implementation bound. The independently prepared purification has vector error at most its gate sum; multiplication by contraction access and the heat successful block and telescoping add their respective gate sums. Projection onto the successful flags is contractive, so the unnormalized heat-vector error is at most $e$. This establishes the three norm comparisons separately.

The scalar infinite extension of the recovery channel differs by at most the finite preparation's trace error in operator norm. Thus the finite-source Heisenberg bound just proved extends uniformly to the same $E_n$ comparison; no infinite unpriced channel is executed. Access to an infinite test is its admitted compiler's finite corner record. Arbitrary unknown infinite states or uncharged infinite matrix queries are outside Definition F.10.4f.10's source.

Choose $\delta_0\le\delta/2$ and make every comparison's coherent sum at most $\delta/4$. If the compiled gate count is $G(n,p)\le a'(n+1)^{d'}(p+1)^{d'}$, increase $p$ until $G(n,p)2^{-p}\le\delta/4$. The exponential decrease guarantees termination; $p=O(\log(1/\delta)+\log(n+1))$ for fixed source constants. Compilation, gates, bits, clean registers, renewals and memory-time all have polynomial counts under the stated access and holding-time conditions. Equation (F.10.4f.22), with prices fixed before the protocol, therefore gives the claimed polynomial cost. Additional work is priced by the same counters. The construction proves an upper bound for every admitted compiler and finite protocol satisfying those budgets; it asserts no cost minimum and makes no free-service comparison. ∎

A shift $K\mapsto K+cI$ leaves the Gibbs state and algebra automorphism unchanged and multiplies the positive heat map by $e^{-sc}$. The canonical $L$ is unchanged. Definition F.10.4f.10 fixes $c=0$; any other origin is a different represented heat datum. Vector, ray and state invariance have different force even in finite dimension: for $K=\operatorname{diag}(0,\varepsilon)$, $L+\varepsilon I$ is positive and implements the same nontrivial KMS dynamics, while $(L+\varepsilon I)\Omega=\varepsilon\Omega$. Its ray is invariant and its vector is not fixed. Theorem F.10.4f.8's positive/vector-fixing obstruction therefore retains its exact vector and energy-origin premises. Its canonical window $0<s<b/2$ belongs to $L$; the successor uses $H_+$ and its window $s>0$.

<a id="theorem-f104f12-sharp-properly-infinite-unit-ball-gns-width"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.12 (Sharp Properly-Infinite Unit-Ball GNS Width).** Let $M\subset N\subset B(\mathcal H)$ be unital von Neumann algebras with the same identity, let $\Omega\in\mathcal H$ be a unit vector, and set $\omega(A)=\langle\Omega,A\Omega\rangle$. Assume that $M$ is properly infinite: it contains isometries $s,t$ with $s^*s=t^*t=1$ and $s^*t=0$. For a bounded linear finite-rank map $E:M\to N$ put
$$
\epsilon_\omega(E)=\sup_{A\in M,\ \|A\|\le1}\|(A-E(A))\Omega\|.
$$
Then $\epsilon_\omega(E)\ge1$. The bound is sharp even when $E$ is required to be normal, unital, completely positive and state preserving:
$$
\inf_{\substack{E:M\to N\ \text{finite rank, normal UCP}\\
\omega\circ E=\omega}}\epsilon_\omega(E)=1.
\tag{F.10.4f.12.1}
$$
More quantitatively, let $d=\dim\operatorname{span}\{E(A)\Omega:A\in M\}$. For every integer $m>d$, one of the $m$ contractions $v_j=t^{j-1}s$, $1\le j\le m$, has
$$
\|(v_j-E(v_j))\Omega\|\ge\sqrt{1-d/m}.
\tag{F.10.4f.12.2}
$$

Consequently, if the retained test set in (F.10.4f.8) is the complete unit ball of a properly infinite regional algebra, no factorization through a finite-dimensional algebra meets that GNS error bound at any $\delta_0<1$. This conclusion allows the finite rank to depend arbitrarily on the requested accuracy. Its response norm is the unsmeared norm $A\mapsto\|A\Omega\|$; it imposes no lower bound on the energy-damped map $A\mapsto\|e^{-\beta H}A\Omega\|$ or on a separately restricted test set such as Definition F.10.4f.10's bandwidth class.

*Proof.* Since $s^*t=0$, its adjoint is $t^*s=0$, and $s^*t^ks=0$ for every $k\ge1$. Cancellation of the isometric powers of $t$ therefore gives $v_j^*v_k=\delta_{jk}1$. Thus the vectors $v_j\Omega$ are orthonormal, without any cyclicity, separatingness or energy assumption on $\Omega$.

Let $F=\operatorname{span}\{E(A)\Omega:A\in M\}$ and let $P_F$ be its orthogonal projection. The space is finite-dimensional. For an orthonormal basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $F$, Bessel's inequality gives
$$
\sum_{j=1}^m\|P_Fv_j\Omega\|^2
=\sum_{a=1}^d\sum_{j=1}^m|\langle e_a,v_j\Omega\rangle|^2\le d.
$$
Some $j\le m$ has $\|P_Fv_j\Omega\|^2\le d/m$. Since $E(v_j)\Omega\in F$,
$$
\|(v_j-E(v_j))\Omega\|^2
\ge\operatorname{dist}(v_j\Omega,F)^2
=1-\|P_Fv_j\Omega\|^2\ge1-d/m.
$$
This proves (F.10.4f.12.2). Taking $m\to\infty$ proves $\epsilon_\omega(E)\ge1$.

The rank-one map $E_0(A)=\omega(A)1$ factors through $\mathbb C$, is normal UCP, and preserves $\omega$. For every contraction $A$,
$$
\|(A-E_0(A))\Omega\|^2
=\omega(A^*A)-|\omega(A)|^2\le1.
$$
Together with the lower bound, this proves (F.10.4f.12.1). If $E=\iota\pi$ factors through a finite-dimensional algebra, its range is finite-dimensional; applying the result to that $E$ proves the stated certificate obstruction. Heat damping and restrictions of the test domain change the map or the supremum used in the argument, so the asserted lower bound has exactly the displayed unsmeared unit-ball domain. ∎

<a id="definition-f104f13-regional-massive-vacuum-datum"></a>**Definition F.10.4f.13 (Regional Massive Vacuum Datum).**

Write $\mathfrak h=L^2(\mathbb R^d,dp)$, $\omega(p)=\sqrt{m^2+{|p|}^2}$, $H=d\Gamma(\omega)$, and $\Omega$ for the common-field Fock vacuum. Let $B\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded ball and $O=D(B)$ its causal development. Use the Fourier normalization of Definition F.10.4c.7. Put

$$
K_s=\overline{\omega^s\widehat{C_c^\infty(B;\mathbb C)}}^{\,L^2},\qquad s=\pm\tfrac12,
\quad Jf(p)=\overline{f(-p)}.
\tag{F.10.4f.13.1}
$$

The closed real localization space is

$$
K_B=\tfrac12(1+J)K_{-1/2}+\tfrac12(1-J)K_{1/2}.
\tag{F.10.4f.13.2}
$$

Its two summands are real-orthogonal, so the sum is closed. The time-slice construction Theorem F.10.4c.19 identifies, on this same Hilbert space,

$$
\mathfrak A(O)={\{W(h):h\in K_B\}}^{\prime\prime},\qquad
\Theta_{\beta,O}(A)=e^{-\beta H}A\Omega.
\tag{F.10.4f.13.3}
$$

Indeed smooth Cauchy data supported in $B$ give the vectors $2^{-1/2}(\omega^{-1/2}\widehat g+i\omega^{1/2}\widehat k)$. The cutoff-in-time construction in (F.10.4c.19.3) represents each such solution by a spacetime test inside $D(B)$, and conversely finite propagation sends the latter tests to such Cauchy data. Closure in the one-particle norm gives strong convergence of Weyl operators. This proves equality of the represented von Neumann algebras, including the vacuum representation. There is no tensor-product assumption across the spatial boundary.

**Computable local nuclearity data.**

Choose a real $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ equal to one on a neighborhood of $\overline B$. In momentum variables let $D=1+{|p|}^2-\Delta_p$. Its eigenvalues, with multiplicity, are $\lambda_\alpha=1+d+2|\alpha|$, $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^d$. Fix an integer $k>d/2$ and set

$$
Z_k={\left[\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^d}\lambda_\alpha^{-2k}\right]}^{1/2},
\quad
k_{\beta,s}(p,q)={(2\pi)}^{-d/2}e^{-\beta\omega(p)}{\omega(p)}^s
\widehat\chi(p-q){\omega(q)}^{-s},
$$
$$
B_{\beta,s,k}={\left[\int_{\mathbb R^{2d}}{|D_q^k k_{\beta,s}(p,q)|}^2\,dp\,dq\right]}^{1/2},
\quad K_{\beta,s}=Z_kB_{\beta,s,k},\quad q_\beta=e^{-\beta m}.
\tag{F.10.4f.14.1}
$$

Every quantity is finite. Effective descriptions of $m,\chi$ with their derivative and Fourier-tail enclosures make these explicit convergent-integral bounds.

<a id="theorem-f104f14-regional-massive-energy-nuclearity"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.14 (Regional Massive Energy Nuclearity).** For every $\beta>0$, $\Theta_{\beta,O}$ is nuclear and

$$
\nu(\Theta_{\beta,O})\le
\prod_{s=\pm1/2}{\det(1-|e^{-\beta\omega}E_s|)}^{-2}
\le \exp\left[\frac{2(K_{\beta,-1/2}+K_{\beta,1/2})}{1-q_\beta}\right],
\tag{F.10.4f.14.2}
$$

where $E_s$ is the orthogonal projection onto $K_s$. Its operator norm is one.

*Proof.* The multiplier-conjugated localization operator $L_s=\omega^s\chi\omega^{-s}$ is bounded. In Fourier variables its kernel has the same form as (F.10.4f.14.1), with the heat factor omitted. The inequalities $\omega(p)/\omega(q)\le1+|p-q|/m$ and its inverse bound the ratio of the half-powers by ${(1+|p-q|/m)}^{1/2}$. Schur's test applies because $\widehat\chi$ is Schwartz. On the dense defining set of $K_s$, $L_sv=v$; hence $L_sE_s=E_s$.

The operator $T_s=e^{-\beta\omega}L_s$ has kernel $k_{\beta,s}$. Every derivative in $q$ has polynomially bounded factors in $p,q$, multiplied by a Schwartz derivative of $\widehat\chi(p-q)$ and by $e^{-\beta\omega(p)}$. Substituting $u=p-q$ proves square integrability even after applying $D_q^k$. Integration by parts on Schwartz vectors gives $T_sD^k$ as the Hilbert–Schmidt kernel $D_q^k k_{\beta,s}$. Thus

$$
T_s=(T_sD^k)D^{-k},\qquad {\|T_s\|}_1\le B_{\beta,s,k}Z_k.
$$

The factorization extends from the Schwartz core by the bounded Hilbert–Schmidt factors. Consequently $e^{-\beta\omega}E_s=T_sE_s$ is trace class with trace norm at most $K_{\beta,s}$ and norm at most $q_\beta<1$.

Apply the bosonic nuclearity theorem of Buchholz–Jacobi in the precise formulation of Lechner–Sanders, Theorem 3.2: (F.10.4f.13.2) supplies its real-subspace decomposition, $J$ commutes with the heat multiplier, and the preceding estimates supply its two trace-class strict contractions. This gives the determinant bound. For every eigenvalue $0\le t\le q_\beta$, $-\log(1-t)\le t/(1-q_\beta)$; summing proves the second inequality. Finally $\|\Theta A\|\le\|A\|$, while $\Theta(1)=\Omega$. ∎

This is a bound on the full unit ball of the actual local von Neumann algebra. The global heat operator itself is not trace class in infinite volume; the proof uses localization before taking its trace ideals.

<a id="proposition-f104f14a-a-hyperfinite-factor-with-a-noncompact-energy-map"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.14a (A Hyperfinite Factor with a Noncompact Energy Map).** Algebraic hyperfiniteness alone does not imply nuclearity of $A\mapsto e^{-\beta H}A\Omega$. There is a hyperfinite finite-factor example for which this map is noncompact for every $\beta>0$.

*Proof.* Let $\mathfrak R$ be the von Neumann algebra obtained by taking the strong closure of the increasing finite matrix algebras $M_2(\mathbb C)^{\otimes n}$ in the GNS representation of their consistent normalized product trace $\tau$. Its trace-preserving conditional expectation $E_n$ onto the first $n$ matrix factors is also the $L^2$ orthogonal projection. The finite tensor words are dense in this GNS space, so $E_nX\to X$ in $L^2$. If $X$ is central, $E_nX$ commutes with that full finite matrix algebra and is therefore $\tau(X)I$ for every $n$; hence $X=\tau(X)I$. This proves the factor property. The normalized trace is faithful and the algebra contains matrix algebras of arbitrarily large size, so it is the hyperfinite $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor, with trace vector $\Omega$. Set $H=0$ on $L^2(\mathfrak R,\tau)$. For each $n$, let $u_n$ be Pauli $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ in factor $n$, with identity in the other factors. Then

$$
 \|u_n\|=1,\qquad \tau(u_n)=0,\qquad
 \langle u_m\Omega,u_n\Omega\rangle=\tau(u_m^*u_n)=\delta_{mn}. \tag{F.10.4f.14a.1}
$$

Thus the unit ball has images $e^{-\beta H}u_n\Omega=u_n\Omega$ separated by distance $\sqrt2$. The energy map is not compact. A nuclear map has a representation $T=\sum_k\varphi_k\otimes\xi_k$ with $\sum_k\|\varphi_k\|\|\xi_k\|<\infty$; its finite partial sums converge in operator norm, so it is compact. Hence this map is not nuclear. $\square$

This is an algebraic factor and a specified Hamiltonian, without an assertion of a relativistic local net. Theorem F.10.4f.14 proves nuclearity for its actual massive local source through its heat-localization trace-class estimates; those dynamical hypotheses distinguish that source from the present example.

**Projective tensors and quantitative tails.**

Here is the exact imported coefficient statement used below. The bosonic construction underlying Lechner–Sanders, proof of Theorem 3.3, equations (3.16)–(3.17), supplies a positive trace-class strict contraction $T$ and an occupation basis $(\xi_\mu)$ with

$$
\Theta_{b,O}(A)=\sum_\mu\varphi_\mu(A)\xi_\mu,
\qquad \varphi_\mu(A)=\langle\xi_\mu,e^{-bH}A\Omega\rangle,
\qquad \|\varphi_\mu\|\le c_\mu:=\prod_j(\mu_j+1)t_j^{\mu_j},
\tag{F.10.4f.15.1}
$$

where $(t_j)$ are the eigenvalues of the output-side joint compact majorant fixed explicitly in Proposition F.10.4f.16, and $\|T\|\le q:=e^{-bm}<1$. Zero eigenvalues carry no positive occupations. The basis/majorant is an admissible one in that coefficient construction, with the output-side compatibility checked in Proposition F.10.4f.16; an arbitrary spatial-mode or lattice basis is not substituted. The functionals are normal, as is immediate from their displayed vacuum-matrix-element formula. We use this established coefficient lemma as an imported analytic theorem. The localization proof in Theorem F.10.4f.14 verifies its free-field hypotheses here.

Put

$$
\mathcal Z(t)=\prod_{j\ge1}{(1-t_j)}^{-2},\qquad
\mathcal Z_J(t)=\prod_{j\le J}{(1-t_j)}^{-2},
\quad
\Lambda_{J,L}=\{\mu:\operatorname{supp}\mu\subset\{1,\ldots,J\},\ |\mu|\le L\}.
$$

<a id="proposition-f104f15-regional-projective-nuclear-tails"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.15 (Regional Projective Nuclear Tails).** The tensor

$$
U_b=\sum_\mu\varphi_\mu\otimes\xi_\mu
\in{\mathfrak A(O)}^*\widehat\otimes_\pi\mathcal H
\tag{F.10.4f.15.2}
$$

converges absolutely. For $1<z<q^{-1}$ its finite truncation obeys

$$
{\|U_b-U_{b;J,L}\|}_\pi\le
\mathcal Z(t)-\mathcal Z_J(t)+z^{-(L+1)}\mathcal Z_J(zt)=:\mathcal D_{J,L},
\tag{F.10.4f.15.3}
$$

and has rank at most $\binom{J+L}{L}$. In particular

$$
\mathcal Z(t)-\mathcal Z_J(t)
\le\mathcal Z(t)\frac{2\sum_{j>J}t_j}{1-q},\qquad
\mathcal Z_J(zt)\le\exp\left[\frac{2z\operatorname{Tr}T}{1-zq}\right].
\tag{F.10.4f.15.4}
$$

*Proof.* The single-coordinate sum is $\sum_{r\ge0}(r+1)t^r={(1-t)}^{-2}$. Tonelli and $\sum t_j<\infty$ give $\sum_\mu c_\mu=\mathcal Z(t)<\infty$. Terms using a mode above $J$ sum to $\mathcal Z-\mathcal Z_J$. For the remaining terms of degree above $L$, $1\le z^{|\mu|-(L+1)}$ gives the second term in (F.10.4f.15.3). The number of retained multiindices is the stars-and-bars count. Finally $1-e^{-x}\le x$ and $-\log(1-t)\le t/(1-q)$ give (F.10.4f.15.4). ∎

Proposition F.10.4f.16 supplies an explicit eigenvalue-tail enclosure for this majorant. That enclosure belongs to its occupation basis; the lattice's unrelated global momentum cutoff has the separate comparison in Theorem F.10.4f.17. Bounds uniform for $\beta\ge b$ follow by applying $e^{-(\beta-b)H}$ to every output vector: this is a contraction, so the same projective tail works throughout the half-line.

<a id="proposition-f104f16-explicit-regional-spectral-tails"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.16 (Explicit Regional Spectral Tails).** The majorant in (F.10.4f.15.1) can be chosen with output-side operators

$$
A_s=|E_se^{-b\omega}|={(e^{-b\omega}E_se^{-b\omega})}^{1/2},\qquad q=e^{-bm},
$$
$$
P(t)=\mathbf1_{(t,\infty)}(A_{-1/2})\vee\mathbf1_{(t,\infty)}(A_{1/2}),
\qquad T=\int_0^qP(t)\,dt.
\tag{F.10.4f.16.1}
$$

For every integer $k>d$, let $B_k=B_{b,-1/2,k}+B_{b,1/2,k}$, $S=K_{b,-1/2}+K_{b,1/2}$, $J_M=\binom{M+d}{d}$, and $c_d=d^{d-1}/(d-1)!$. Then

$$
\operatorname{Tr}T\le S,\qquad
\sum_{j>2J_M}t_j\le B_k\sum_{r>M}\binom{r+d-1}{d-1}{(1+d+2r)}^{-k}
\le\frac{B_kc_d}{k-d}{(M+1)}^{d-k}.
\tag{F.10.4f.16.2}
$$

In particular a full-regional tensor approximation of rank at most $\binom{2J_M+L}{L}$ has projective error at most

$$
\frac{2B_kc_d}{(1-q)(k-d)}
\exp\left(\frac{2S}{1-q}\right){(M+1)}^{d-k}
+z^{-(L+1)}\exp\left(\frac{2zS}{1-zq}\right),\quad 1<z<q^{-1}.
\tag{F.10.4f.16.3}
$$

*Proof.* The projections $P(t)$ are nested as $t$ decreases and commute with $J$. Spectral integration gives $\|T\|\le q$, $[T,J]=0$, and

$$
T^r=\int_0^q r t^{r-1}P(t)\,dt\ge A_s^r\qquad(r>0).
$$

Right-continuous choices at the countably many eigenvalue thresholds have no effect on these integrals. Each $P(t)$ has rank at most the sum of the two spectral-projection ranks. Thus $T$ is compact, its positive eigenvalues are dominated by the decreasing merge of the eigenvalues of $A_{-1/2}$ and $A_{1/2}$, and its trace is at most the sum of their traces. After the largest $2J$ entries of that merge, its tail is no larger than the sum of each individual tail after $J$ entries.

This output-side orientation is material. In Buchholz–Jacobi's original proof, equations (2.14)–(2.20), the one-particle forms are precisely $|E_s e^{-b\omega}|$; the passage to the occupation coefficient estimate uses $T^2\ge A_s^2$ and commutation with $J$. The present spectral-join majorant has those properties, so it is an admissible choice for the coefficient construction in (F.10.4f.15.1). Equality of singular values with the adjoints $e^{-b\omega}E_s$ is used for bounds; it is not used to identify their eigenvectors.

Theorem F.10.4f.14 gives $e^{-b\omega}E_s=(T_sD^k)D^{-k}E_s$, with $\|T_sD^k\|\le B_{b,s,k}$. The singular-value ideal inequality therefore yields $s_j(A_s)\le B_{b,s,k}{\lambda_j(D)}^{-k}$. The first $J_M$ Hermite eigenvectors have total degree at most $M$, which gives the series in (F.10.4f.16.2). Finally $\binom{r+d-1}{d-1}\le c_d{(r+1)}^{d-1}$ and $1+d+2r\ge r+1$; comparison with $\int_{M+1}^\infty x^{d-1-k}dx$ proves its last bound. Insert (F.10.4f.16.2) into (F.10.4f.15.3)–(F.10.4f.15.4), using $\operatorname{Tr}T\le S$, to obtain (F.10.4f.16.3). ∎

Thus a requested tail error determines finite $M,L$ directly from localization integrals, the mass and the heat parameter. No unquantified compactness modulus is needed. Computing the corresponding eigenvectors and a near-budget finite nuclear decomposition is a separate production problem from this analytic rank/tail bound.

The source nominations below retain their own local parameters and scopes. The final full-regional theorem uses the complete-ball weighted computational class, positive collars and heat window, fixed original physical clock, the permitted same-nominated-cutoff coarse nuclear ceiling and the complete finite-service/query tariff. Earlier component limitations remain attached to their original routes. The localized-flip and projection-free constructions supply the later full-regional conjunction on this nomination.

**Common-lattice transport.**

Retain $J_n,I_n,Q_n,H_n,R_n,\delta_n,a_n$ from Definitions F.10.4c.7 and F.10.4c.10. Let $\rho_n^{\rm cell}=\sqrt d\delta_n/2$. Fix a heat window $\beta\ge\beta_0>0$ and put $b=\beta_0/3$. Discard the finite initial segment until $\rho_n^{\rm cell}\le m$. For $q$ in the cell centered at $p$,

$$
\omega(q)\le\omega(p)+\rho_n^{\rm cell}\le(\pi/2+1)\omega_n(p)<3\omega_n(p).
\tag{F.10.4f.17.1}
$$

The second inequality uses $2|\sin(a_np_j/2)|/a_n\ge2|p_j|/\pi$ throughout the Brillouin zone, and $\omega_n\ge m$.

Define on its initial multiplication domain

$$
r_{n,\beta}=J_ne^{-\beta\omega_n}J_n^*e^{b\omega},\qquad
R_{n,\beta}=\mathbf1_{\{N\le R_n\}}\Gamma(r_{n,\beta}).
\tag{F.10.4f.17.2}
$$

<a id="theorem-f104f17-common-lattice-regional-tensor-transport"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.17 (Common-Lattice Regional Tensor Transport).** These operators extend to contractions, and, for every $A\in\mathfrak A(O)$,

$$
\pi_n(A)=I_n^*AI_n,\qquad
I_ne^{-\beta H_n}\pi_n(A)\Omega_n=R_{n,\beta}\Theta_{b,O}(A).
\tag{F.10.4f.17.3}
$$

Furthermore $R_{n,\beta}\to e^{-(\beta-b)H}$ strongly, uniformly on compact heat windows. Hence

$$
U_{n,\beta}:=(1\otimes R_{n,\beta})U_b
\longrightarrow (1\otimes e^{-(\beta-b)H})U_b=:U_\beta
\quad\text{in projective norm},
\tag{F.10.4f.17.4}
$$

uniformly on compact heat windows, with ${\|U_{n,\beta}\|}_\pi\le\mathcal Z(t)$. A finite quantitative bound is

$$
{\|U_{n,\beta}-U_\beta\|}_\pi
\le2\mathcal D_{J,L}+
\sum_{\mu\in\Lambda_{J,L}}c_\mu
\|(R_{n,\beta}-e^{-(\beta-b)H})\xi_\mu\|.
\tag{F.10.4f.17.5}
$$

*Proof.* The cell rows of $e^{-\beta\omega_n}J_n^*e^{b\omega}$ have disjoint supports. Their squared norms are $\delta_n^{-d}\int_{C_{n,p}}e^{-2\beta\omega_n(p)+2b\omega(q)}dq\le1$ by (F.10.4f.17.1). This proves contractivity, including the extension across the initially unbounded multiplier. Second quantization and particle truncation preserve it. On every particle sector, multiplication by $e^{-bH}$ cancels $e^{b\omega}$ before averaging, giving the bounded-operator identity

$$
R_{n,\beta}e^{-bH}=I_ne^{-\beta H_n}I_n^*.
$$

Since $I_n\Omega_n=\Omega$, (F.10.4f.17.3) follows. This verifies the maps on the *represented algebra and its actual vacuum*, rather than on formal symbols.

On a compactly supported smooth one-particle vector, cell averaging converges in $L^2$, lattice dispersion converges uniformly on its compact support, and the exponential multipliers converge uniformly for $\beta$ in a compact interval. Thus $r_{n,\beta}\to e^{-(\beta-b)\omega}$ strongly on a dense set, and contractivity extends it to every vector. Tensor products give the same assertion on each fixed particle sector. The particle cutoff tends to infinity, giving the Fock-space statement. Truncate (F.10.4f.15.2), use convergence on its finitely many outputs, and bound the omitted terms by twice their nuclear sum. This proves (F.10.4f.17.4)–(F.10.4f.17.5). ∎

**Exact finite-domain boundary.** $\pi_n$ is normal UCP into the common source matrix algebra. Its image of $\mathfrak A(O)$ is an operator system; it need not be a subalgebra. The generated matrix algebra may be the whole global register. Theorem F.10.4f.17 therefore proves the tensor-limit premise for the transported regional-test maps in (F.10.4f.17.3). It gives no nuclear bound on the entire global matrix algebra before restriction. An exact finite local net or a uniform bound for that enlarged domain requires its own construction. Proposition F.10.4f.18 and Theorems F.10.4f.19–F.10.4f.21 instead supply actual finite local algebras for one explicitly retained local mode.

**An entangled local canonical mode.**

Fix real $g\in C_c^\infty(B)$ with ${\|g\|}_{L^2}=1$. Define

$$
A_g=\langle\widehat g,\omega^{-1}\widehat g\rangle,\quad
B_g=\langle\widehat g,\omega\widehat g\rangle,\quad
\nu_g=\tfrac12\sqrt{A_gB_g},\quad s_g={(B_g/A_g)}^{1/4},
$$
$$
q_g=\phi(\omega^{-1/2}\widehat g/\sqrt2),\quad
p_g=\phi(i\omega^{1/2}\widehat g/\sqrt2),\quad
Q=s_gq_g,\quad P=s_g^{-1}p_g,\quad c=(Q+iP)/\sqrt2.
\tag{F.10.4f.18.1}
$$

The Weyl operators of $Q,P$ belong to $\mathfrak A(O)$ by Definition F.10.4f.13. They obey the regular one-mode CCR. Let

$$
M_g={\{e^{i(uQ+vP)}:u,v\in\mathbb R\}}^{\prime\prime}\subset\mathfrak A(O).
$$

<a id="proposition-f104f18-entangled-local-canonical-mode"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.18 (Entangled Local Canonical Mode).** There is a concrete factorization $\mathcal H\simeq\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)\otimes\mathcal H_c$ with $M_g=B(\ell^2)\otimes1$. Its vacuum restriction is

$$
\rho_g=(1-\eta)\sum_{j\ge0}\eta^j|j\rangle\langle j|,
\qquad \eta=\frac{\nu_g-1/2}{\nu_g+1/2}\in(0,1).
\tag{F.10.4f.18.2}
$$

The vacuum has infinite Schmidt rank across this local factor and its commutant. The physical Hamiltonian $H$ couples the factor to its complement; replacing its heat map by $e^{-\beta\varepsilon c^*c}$ changes the datum.

*Proof.* The CCR normalization gives $[q_g,p_g]=i$ on the finite-particle Schwartz core. Its two vacuum variances are $A_g/2,B_g/2$, and the symmetrized covariance is zero. Thus the rescaled variances are both $\nu_g$. Strict Cauchy–Schwarz gives $A_gB_g>1$: equality would make $\omega$ constant on the nonzero support of $\widehat g$ in $L^2$, whereas every level set of $\omega$ has Lebesgue measure zero. Hence $\nu_g>1/2$.

For a direct factorization put

$$
u=(s_g\omega^{-1/2}+s_g^{-1}\omega^{1/2})\widehat g/2,
\qquad v=(s_g\omega^{-1/2}-s_g^{-1}\omega^{1/2})\widehat g/2.
\tag{F.10.4f.18.3}
$$

Direct calculation gives $\langle u,v\rangle=0$, ${\|u\|}^2=\nu_g+1/2$, ${\|v\|}^2=\nu_g-1/2$, and $c=a(u)+a^*(v)$. Set $f_1=u/\|u\|$, $f_2=v/\|v\|$, choose $r>0$ with $\cosh r=\|u\|$, and put $b_j=a(f_j)$. Then

$$
c=\cosh r\,b_1+\sinh r\,b_2^*,\qquad
 d=\cosh r\,b_2+\sinh r\,b_1^*.
\tag{F.10.4f.18.4}
$$

These are two commuting canonical annihilators. A two-mode squeezing unitary implements this finite-dimensional Bogoliubov transformation. It can be defined directly by its usual exponential on the analytic finite-occupation core, or by the disentangled series in Propositions F.10.4f.22–F.10.4f.24 and Corollary F.10.4f.25. The Fock factorization over $\operatorname{span}\{f_1,f_2\}\oplus{\{f_1,f_2\}}^{\perp}$ therefore gives $M_g=B(\mathcal F(\mathbb C c))\otimes1$. In the $c,d$ number basis the equations $b_1\Omega=b_2\Omega=0$ recursively give

$$
\Omega=\sqrt{1-\eta}\sum_{j\ge0}{(\sqrt\eta)}^j|j_c,j_d\rangle\otimes\Omega_\perp,
\qquad \eta=\tanh^2r.
\tag{F.10.4f.18.5}
$$

The normalized square-summable solution is unique. Taking the partial trace gives (F.10.4f.18.2) and its infinite positive Schmidt list.

For the coupling statement, $i[H,p_g]=-q_{(-\Delta+m^2)g}$, with the harmless sign changed if the opposite Heisenberg convention is chosen. The function $(-\Delta+m^2)g$ is not proportional to $g$: Fourier transformation would again force an $L^2$ function onto a level set. Choose real $h\in C_c^\infty(B)$ perpendicular to $g$ but with $\langle h,(-\Delta+m^2)g\rangle\ne0$. The observable $p_h$ commutes with both $q_g,p_g$ yet does not commute with $q_{(-\Delta+m^2)g}$. Therefore the physical infinitesimal evolution leaves the one-mode factor. In particular an additive self-adjoint implementation $H_g\otimes1+1\otimes H_c$ on this factorization is impossible, since it would normalize the factor. All identities can first be differentiated between analytic finite-field vectors. ∎

The complement in Proposition F.10.4f.18 contains the commuting mode $d$ and all remaining field modes. It is the actual commutant of a local subfactor, not a replacement product vacuum. The underlying spatial lattice of (F.10.4c.7.6) also retains its cross-boundary nearest-neighbor terms.

**State-exact finite local interfaces.**

Write $P_n=\sum_{j<n}|j_c\rangle\langle j_c|$, $Q_n^g=1-P_n$, and $t_n=\eta^n$. Here $Q_n^g$ is a local-mode projection, distinct from the global lattice projection $Q_n$ of Theorem F.10.4f.17. Define

$$
\mathcal B_n=M_n\oplus\mathbb C,\qquad
j_n(B,z)=(B\oplus zI_{P_n^\perp})\otimes1\in M_g,
$$
$$
\pi_n^g(A)=\left(P_nAP_n,\ t_n^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_gQ_n^gAQ_n^g)\right),
\qquad E_n^g=j_n\pi_n^g,
\tag{F.10.4f.19.1}
$$

where in (F.10.4f.19.1) $A$ denotes its one-mode representative. The finite state is

$$
\omega_n(B,z)=\operatorname{Tr}(P_n\rho_gP_nB)+t_nz.
\tag{F.10.4f.19.2}
$$

<a id="theorem-f104f19-state-exact-local-finite-interfaces"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.19 (State-Exact Local Finite Interfaces).** $j_n$ is a unital faithful normal $*$-homomorphism; $\pi_n^g$ and $E_n^g$ are normal UCP; $\omega_n\pi_n^g=\omega$ on all of $M_g$. On the fixed bandwidth-$w$ core

$$
\mathcal T_{g,w}=\{A\in M_g:\|A\|\le1,\ \langle i|A|j\rangle=0\text{ for }|i-j|>w\}
$$

and $n>w$,

$$
\|(A-E_n^gA)\Omega\|\le\eta^{(n-w)/2}+2\eta^{n/2}=:\gamma_{n,w},
\quad
\|e^{-\beta H}(A-E_n^gA)\Omega\|\le\gamma_{n,w}\quad(\beta\ge0).
\tag{F.10.4f.19.3}
$$

The union of finite bandwidths contains every finite matrix and the identity and is strong-operator dense in $M_g$.

*Proof.* Both summands of $\pi_n^g$ are completely positive and send the identity to their identities. The second is a state on the high block. $j_n$ is visibly a unital representation, so the assertions about positivity and normality follow. Since $\rho_g$ is block diagonal, (F.10.4f.19.2) gives exact state preservation. Write $P=P_n,Q=Q_n^g$ and $a=t_n^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_gQAQ)$. Then

$$
A-E_n^gA=QAP+AQ-aQ.
$$

The last two terms have vacuum norms at most $\sqrt{t_n}$ each. Bandwidth makes $QAP|j\rangle=0$ for $j<n-w$, so the first norm is at most $\eta^{(n-w)/2}$. Contraction of $e^{-\beta H}$ proves the heat bound without factorizing $H$. Strong density follows from $P_nAP_n\to A$ strongly and strongly in adjoint. ∎

For interfaces formally defined on all of $\mathfrak A(O)$, choose a normal state $\sigma$ on $\mathcal H_c$ and the normal UCP map $\mathcal E_g=\mathrm{id}\otimes\sigma:B(\mathcal H)\to M_g$ in the displayed factorization. Then $\pi_n^g\mathcal E_g$ has the required full domain and agrees with (F.10.4f.19.1) on the retained core. The recovery $j_n$ has range in $\mathfrak A(O)\subset\mathfrak A(O_+)$. State preservation is asserted on $M_g$, where $\mathcal E_g$ is the identity; no vacuum-preserving conditional expectation from the full regional algebra onto $M_g$ is assumed.

The actual vacuum net is split for every positive double-cone collar. This is the free-field split conclusion of Buchholz–Wichmann; alternatively Lechner–Sanders' quasi-free Hadamard modular nuclearity theorem and the modular-nuclearity split implication apply to this Minkowski vacuum. Thus one can choose a type-I factor $\mathfrak A(O)\subset\mathcal N\subset\mathfrak A(O_+)$. The finite recovery above lies in the smaller concrete $M_g$; it does not require a circuit for an unspecified split unitary.

**One positive finite Hamiltonian for a heat window.**

Fix $0<\beta_0\le\beta_1<\infty$ and $\lambda>0$. Let $\mathcal K_n=\operatorname{HS}(\mathbb C^n)\oplus\mathbb C$, $D_n^g=n^2+1$, with left representation $L_n(B,z)(X,a)=(BX,za)$ and cyclic state vector

$$
\chi_n=(\sqrt{P_n\rho_gP_n},\sqrt{t_n}).
$$

There is an isometry $V_n:\mathcal K_n\to\mathcal H$ satisfying

$$
V_nL_n(B,z)\chi_n=j_n(B,z)\Omega,
\qquad V_n\chi_n=\Omega.
\tag{F.10.4f.20.1}
$$

Explicitly $V_nE_{ij}=|i_c,j_d\rangle\otimes\Omega_\perp$ and the final scalar basis vector goes to $Q_n^g\Omega/\sqrt{t_n}$. Orthogonality of the Schmidt vectors proves that it is an isometry.

Put $A_\lambda=\lambda{(H+\lambda)}^{-1}$ and

$$
\mathcal K_{n,L}^{\rm Krylov}=\operatorname{span}\{A_\lambda^jV_nx:x\in\mathcal K_n,\ 0\le j\le L\},
\quad A_{n,L}=P_{n,L}A_\lambda|_{\mathcal K_{n,L}^{\rm Krylov}},
$$
$$
H_{n,L}=\lambda(A_{n,L}^{-1}-1).
\tag{F.10.4f.20.2}
$$

The compression $A_{n,L}$ is strictly positive on this finite-dimensional space: $A_\lambda$ has zero kernel, so every nonzero quadratic form is positive; compactness of the finite unit sphere gives a positive minimum. It is at most one. Thus $H_{n,L}\ge0$ and $H_{n,L}\Omega=0$.

For an explicit uniform approximation bound set

$$
M=e^{\beta_1\lambda},\quad B=\frac9{\beta_0\lambda},\quad
r=\log(1+{(2B)}^{-1}),\quad b_*=r^{-1},\quad c_*=\frac{\log4}{4\sqrt{b_*}},
$$
$$
\epsilon_L=8M\left(\frac{\sqrt L}{c_*}+\frac1{c_*^2}\right)e^{-c_*\sqrt L},\qquad L\ge\lceil16b_*\rceil.
\tag{F.10.4f.20.3}
$$

<a id="theorem-f104f20-coupled-positive-finite-heat-register"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.20 (Coupled Positive Finite Heat Register).** There is a finite global register, a faithful regional representation of $\mathcal B_n$ on it, a normalized vacuum, a positive Hamiltonian fixing that vacuum, and an isometric output comparison $J_{n,L}$ to the common field such that

$$
\sup_{\beta_0\le\beta\le\beta_1}\sup_{\|(B,z)\|\le1}
\left\|J_{n,L}e^{-\beta H_{n,L}}\rho_{n,L}(B,z)\Omega_{n,L}
-e^{-\beta H}j_n(B,z)\Omega\right\|\le2\epsilon_L.
\tag{F.10.4f.20.4}
$$

Padding if needed, its Hilbert dimension is at most $(L+2)(n^2+1)$. The map from this finite regional algebra to its finite vacuum representation has nuclear norm at most

$$
\nu(\Theta_{\beta,O})+2(n^2+1)\epsilon_L.
\tag{F.10.4f.20.5}
$$

Consequently $n=O_{g,w}(\log(1/\delta))$, $L=O_{\beta_0,\beta_1,\lambda}(\log^2(1/\delta))$ suffice for uniform retained-core GNS/heat error $\delta$ and an added nuclear budget $\delta$. The dimension is $O(\log^4(1/\delta))$ on these fixed data.

*Proof: polynomial estimate.* On $[0,1]$ define $f_\beta(x)=\exp[-\beta\lambda(x^{-1}-1)]$, with $f_\beta(0)=0$. For real $x>0$, the disk $|z-x|\le x/2$ has $\operatorname{Re}(1/z)\ge2/(9x)$. Cauchy's estimate, followed by maximizing $x^{-k}e^{-2\beta_0\lambda/(9x)}$, gives

$$
{\|f_\beta^{(k)}\|}_\infty\le M B^k{(k!)}^2.
$$

All derivatives extend by zero at $x=0$. For $F_\beta(\theta)=f_\beta((1+\cos\theta)/2)$, Faà di Bruno and $|\partial_\theta^j(1+\cos\theta)/2|\le1$ give

$$
{\|F_\beta^{(k)}\|}_\infty\le2M r^{-k}{(k!)}^2.
$$

Here is a bound for the combinatorial sum: after using $\ell!\le k!$ once, its remaining generating function is ${[1-B(e^z-1)]}^{-1}$; at $z=r$ its value is two. Positivity of its coefficients gives the stated $2r^{-k}$ bound.

Integration by parts $k$ times in the periodic Fourier coefficient therefore bounds the $j$th Chebyshev coefficient by $4M b_*^k{(k!)}^2j^{-k}$. For $j\ge16b_*$ choose $k=\lfloor\sqrt{j/(4b_*)}\rfloor$. Using $k!\le k^k$ gives a bound $4Me^{-c_*\sqrt j}$. Sum the tail by the integral $\int_L^\infty e^{-c_*\sqrt x}dx$. The degree-$L$ Chebyshev truncation $p_{\beta,L}$ satisfies ${\|f_\beta-p_{\beta,L}\|}_{C[0,1]}\le\epsilon_L$, uniformly on the heat window.

*Proof: finite Hamiltonian and representation.* For $x\in\mathcal K_n$ and $0\le j\le L$,

$$
A_{n,L}^{\,j}V_nx=A_\lambda^jV_nx.
$$

Induction uses the definition of the Krylov space at each intermediate step. The two polynomial actions consequently agree on $V_n\mathcal K_n$. Spectral calculus and the uniform polynomial bound give

$$
\|e^{-\beta H_{n,L}}V_nx-e^{-\beta H}V_nx\|\le2\epsilon_L\|x\|.
$$

The two terms are compared by the inclusion of the Krylov space into $\mathcal H$.

If its dimension is not a multiple of $D_n^g$, add fewer than $D_n^g$ inert dimensions and extend the output isometry into orthogonal field vectors. Give the padding Hamiltonian zero. On the resulting space choose a unitary identifying the subspace $V_n\mathcal K_n$ with $\mathcal K_n\otimes|0\rangle$ inside $\mathcal K_n\otimes\mathbb C^h$. Conjugate $L_n\otimes1_h$ by this unitary. This is the faithful finite regional representation $\rho_{n,L}$ and it satisfies $\rho_{n,L}(B,z)V_n\chi_n=V_nL_n(B,z)\chi_n$. The vacuum is $V_n\chi_n=\Omega$. The full source algebra is the matrix algebra of this finite register; its vector state has the whole register as its cyclic representation. Its regional subalgebra need not be cyclic by itself. This proves (F.10.4f.20.4), including the algebra and vacuum identifications.

The exact map $(B,z)\mapsto e^{-\beta H}j_n(B,z)\Omega$ is the restriction of the regional nuclear map along a norm-one $*$-homomorphism, so its nuclear norm is at most $\nu(\Theta_{\beta,O})$. The difference in (F.10.4f.20.4) is a map on $M_n\oplus\mathbb C$. Expand it in its $n^2$ matrix-coordinate functionals and scalar coordinate, each of norm one. Each output error is at most $2\epsilon_L$. This gives nuclear norm at most $2(n^2+1)\epsilon_L$, proving (F.10.4f.20.5). Combine (F.10.4f.19.3) and (F.10.4f.20.4) for the retained core. Choose the constants so that both $\gamma_{n,w}$ and $2(n^2+1)\epsilon_L$ fit their allocations. The displayed growth orders follow directly from (F.10.4f.19.3) and (F.10.4f.20.3). ∎

This construction retains the physical coupling through the actual resolvent $A_\lambda$ and its matrix elements. Its finite Hamiltonian is neither the Gibbs number operator of (F.10.4f.18.2) nor a compression that discards the complementary Schmidt sector.

**Local-core tensor convergence.**

<a id="theorem-f104f21-local-algebra-projective-tensor-limit"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.21 (Local-Algebra Projective Tensor Limit).** Choose $L=L(n)\to\infty$ with $(n^2+1)\epsilon_{L(n)}\to0$. Transport the finite phase-space maps of Theorem F.10.4f.20 to $M_g$ by $\pi_n^g$ and to $\mathcal H$ by $J_{n,L}$. Their representing tensors can be chosen to converge in projective norm to a representing tensor of $\Theta_{\beta,O}|_{M_g}$, uniformly for $\beta\in[\beta_0,\beta_1]$. Their finite nuclear budgets are bounded independently of $n$ by (F.10.4f.20.5).

*Proof.* A normal functional on $M_g=B(\ell^2)\otimes1$ is a trace-class matrix $\sigma$. The predual of $E_n^g$ sends it to

$$
{(E_n^g)}_*\sigma=P_n\sigma P_n+\operatorname{Tr}(Q_n^g\sigma)\rho_{\rm tail,n},
\quad \rho_{\rm tail,n}=t_n^{-1}Q_n^g\rho_gQ_n^g.
$$

Thus

$$
{\|\sigma-{(E_n^g)}_*\sigma\|}_1
\le{\|\sigma-P_n\sigma P_n\|}_1+|\operatorname{Tr}(Q_n^g\sigma)|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{F.10.4f.21.1}
$$

Restrict the normal coefficient functionals of (F.10.4f.15.1) to $M_g$. Equation (F.10.4f.21.1), absolute summability, and dominated convergence prove $(E_n^{g*}\otimes1)U_\beta\to U_\beta$ in projective norm. Uniformity follows by writing every $U_\beta$ using the single tensor at $b=\beta_0$ and output contraction $e^{-(\beta-b)H}$.

Replace the exact finite output map $e^{-\beta H}j_n(\cdot)\Omega$ by the register map of Theorem F.10.4f.20. The matrix-coordinate expansion in that proof gives projective norm error at most $2(n^2+1)\epsilon_L$, also after the contractive precomposition $\pi_n^g$. This tends to zero. The pre-transport nuclear budgets are (F.10.4f.20.5). At each finite stage the target is finite-dimensional; its tensor can be represented by finitely many coordinate functionals. If a specified finite decomposition sum is needed within an extra $\varepsilon>0$ of the displayed budget, truncate a summable nuclear representation and express its residual in a target basis; a tail smaller than $\varepsilon/\sqrt{\dim\mathcal H_{n,L}}$ suffices by Cauchy–Schwarz. ∎

For a finite occupation truncation $\Lambda$ in (F.10.4f.15.1), a completely explicit error ledger is twice its projective tail, plus the finitely many trace-class errors (F.10.4f.21.1) of the retained coefficient matrices, plus $2(n^2+1)\epsilon_L$. The source-dependent coefficient matrices are part of that ledger. Proposition F.10.4f.16 supplies the analytic spectral-tail enclosure. Producing the associated eigenbasis and a near-budget explicit nuclear decomposition is a separate certificate-production demand; the efficient matrix/interface compiler in Propositions F.10.4f.22–F.10.4f.24 and Corollary F.10.4f.25 does not price those spectral certificate artifacts. Their convergence is proved, rather than inferred from boundedness of a projective-tensor ball.

Theorem F.10.4f.21 supplies the actual finite-algebra weak-subnet predicate, strengthened to norm convergence, on $M_g$. Theorem F.10.4f.17 supplies the full-regional transported-test predicate. The two domains are stated separately: their combination does not replace $M_g$ by the complete algebra $\mathfrak A(O)$ in Theorem F.10.4f.21.

**Finite matrix production and source costs.**

<a id="proposition-f104f22-finite-gaussian-matrix-production"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.22 (Finite Gaussian Matrix Production).**

Let $F=\operatorname{span}\{f_1,f_2\}$ from (F.10.4f.18.3) and define the two-by-two contraction

$$
{C(t)}_{ab}=\langle f_a,e^{-t\omega}f_b\rangle,\qquad t\ge0.
\tag{F.10.4f.22.1}
$$

If $S$ sends the $b$-occupation basis to the $c,d$ basis, then

$$
\langle i_c,j_d|e^{-tH}|k_c,l_d\rangle
=\langle i,j|S^*\Gamma(C(t))S|k,l\rangle.
\tag{F.10.4f.22.2}
$$

To verify (F.10.4f.22.2), compare exponential vectors in $\Gamma(F)$: compression of $\Gamma(e^{-t\omega})$ to $\Gamma(F)$ has kernel $\exp\langle z,C(t)w\rangle$, hence is exactly $\Gamma(C(t))$. Taking coefficients proves equality on every particle sector. Squeezing acts entirely in $\Gamma(F)$, while the other modes are initially vacuum. The high-tail vector in (F.10.4f.20.1) is $(\Omega-\sum_{j<n}\sqrt{(1-\eta)\eta^j}|j_c,j_d\rangle)/\sqrt{t_n}$, so the same formula supplies every heat-matrix entry of $V_n$.

The resolvent moments needed for (F.10.4f.20.2) are

$$
V_n^*A_\lambda^rV_n=
\frac{\lambda^r}{(r-1)!}\int_0^\infty t^{r-1}e^{-\lambda t}V_n^*e^{-tH}V_n\,dt
\quad(r\ge1),
\tag{F.10.4f.22.3}
$$

and the zeroth moment is the identity. This is spectral calculus followed by the scalar $\gamma$ integral. The integrand has norm at most the $\gamma$ density, giving a direct certified integration tail. The largest moment needed for the degree-$L$ Krylov data is $2L+1$.

For numerical production, squeezing itself has a controlled finite occupation tail. Put $a=\sqrt\eta=\tanh r$. Up to the sign fixed by the direction of $S$, its disentangling is

$$
S=\exp(\pm a b_1^*b_2^*)
{(\cosh r)}^{-(N_1+N_2+1)}\exp(\mp a b_1b_2).
\tag{F.10.4f.22.4}
$$

On $|i,j\rangle$ the last series terminates at $\min(i,j)$ and the first raises both indices. The matrix entries are therefore finite sums at every named output pair. For $i,j<n$ and a nonnegative common increase $v$, their absolute value is at most

$$
e^n\eta^{v/2}{(v+2n)}^n.
\tag{F.10.4f.22.5}
$$

Indeed the lowering coefficient is at most $n^l/l!$, whose sum is at most $e^n$, and the raising factorial ratio is at most ${(v+2n)}^n$. All omitted powers of $a$ and $\cosh r$ have magnitude at most one. If $P_{\le K}^{(2)}$ is the two-mode total-number cutoff and $v_0=\lfloor K/2\rfloor-n\ge0$, choose $v_0+2n\ge4n/|\log\eta|$. The ratio of consecutive squared majorants is at most $\sqrt\eta$, so

$$
\|(1-P_{\le K}^{(2)})S P_{<n,<n}\|
\le \frac{n e^n\eta^{v_0/2}{(v_0+2n)}^n}{\sqrt{1-\sqrt\eta}}.
\tag{F.10.4f.22.6}
$$

The extra $n$ is the square root of the $n^2$ input dimension. Thus $K=O_\eta(n\log(n+1)+p)$ suffices for error $2^{-p}$. The scalar tail basis in (F.10.4f.20.1) multiplies the required accuracy by at most $\eta^{-n/2}$ and an additional polynomial in $n$; this increases $p$ by $O_\eta(n+\log n)$.

On $P_{\le K}^{(2)}$, $\Gamma(C(t))$ is a finite block matrix preserving total number. Its entries follow by expanding ${(C_{11}z_1+C_{21}z_2)}^i{(C_{12}z_1+C_{22}z_2)}^j$ with the usual factorial normalization. Thus the entire matrix-production problem consists of the four one-particle integrals (F.10.4f.22.1), finite sums, and the one-dimensional integral (F.10.4f.22.3). It does not require a many-dimensional integration over an unpriced infinite field state.

<a id="proposition-f104f23-effective-regularized-gaussian-compiler"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.23 (Effective Regularized Gaussian Compiler).**

A convenient fixed profile is

$$
g(x)=Z^{-1/2}\prod_{j=1}^d\exp\left[-\frac1{1-{(x_j/a)}^2}\right]
\mathbf1_{\{|x_j|<a\}},\qquad a\sqrt d<\operatorname{rad}(B),
\tag{F.10.4f.23.1}
$$

where $Z$ is its squared $L^2$ norm. The extension is smooth. For the one-dimensional unnormalized bump $h$, Cauchy's estimate on the disk of radius $(1-x^2)/8$ gives

$$
{\|h^{(k)}\|}_\infty\le32^k{(k!)}^2.
\tag{F.10.4f.23.2}
$$

In fact $\operatorname{Re}(1/(1-z^2))\ge1/[4(1-x^2)]$ on that disk; optimize the resulting ${(1-x^2)}^{-k}e^{-1/[4(1-x^2)]}$ bound. Scaling and products give explicit derivative enclosures for (F.10.4f.23.1). Integration by parts, choosing $k$ proportional to $\sqrt{|p|}$, gives a bound $C e^{-c\sqrt{|p|}}$ for $\widehat g$ with positive computable $C,c$. The same estimate with polynomial prefactors covers the two vectors in (F.10.4f.18.3). Consequently their energy moments, and the derivatives of (F.10.4f.22.1), have bounds $M_0A_0^k{(k!)}^2$ with computable constants depending on the fixed profile and mass.

These estimates give a finite precision-production algorithm. Truncate each momentum integral where the explicit stretched-exponential tail is below its allocation. Its radius is $O(p^2)$ for $p$ bits. On finite intervals use composite Gaussian quadrature. For a function with derivative bound $M A^k{(k!)}^2$, a subinterval width at most ${(8Ak)}^{-1}$ and Gaussian order $k$ give an error bounded by a constant times $M$ times the interval length times $4^{-k}$: use the order-$2k$ Hermite-interpolation remainder and positive Gaussian weights. Hence $k=O(p+\log M+\log(1+T))$ suffices on an interval of length $T$. Normalization, the finitely many matrix coefficients, and the $\gamma$ integral (F.10.4f.22.3) use the same operations. The $\gamma$ tail is cut at a computable $T=O_\lambda(r+p)$ by the elementary exponential Markov bound.

After the two-mode cutoff (F.10.4f.22.6), products have degree at most $K$. More explicitly, if each factor obeys $|f^{(j)}|\le M_0A_0^j{(j!)}^2$, Leibniz and $\binom{j+K-1}{K-1}\le2^{j+K}$ bound a product by ${(2M_0)}^K{(2A_0)}^j{(j!)}^2$. Thus the derivative-scale constant stays bounded independently of $K$, while the logarithm of the prefactor is $O(K\log(1+M_0))$. The factorial coefficients in (F.10.4f.22.2) add $O(K\log(K+1))$ to that logarithm. On $[0,T]$, the gamma-density factor has derivative scale at most $r+\lambda+1$ and prefactor with logarithm $O(r\log(T+2)+T)$. The factor $t_n^{-1/2}$ adds $O(n)$. In particular the quadrature scale itself, as well as the logarithm of its prefactor, is polynomial in $n,K,r,p$. Fourier evaluations on the momentum box have derivative scale polynomial in its radius and in $T$; the bump and exponential formulas give these enclosures directly. This proves finite computable matrix production. It also isolates the parameters controlling the production cost; a polynomial-time assertion additionally counts the arithmetic, quadrature, orthogonalization and control precision described next.

**Thresholded bases and controlled energy ceiling.**

The exact Krylov space in (F.10.4f.20.2) has at most $M_n=(L+1)(n^2+1)$ generators of norm at most one. Its abstract definition does not give a free exact-rank decision. At finite tolerance, start with the known orthonormal image of $V_n$, use certified Gram entries from (F.10.4f.22.3), and greedily retain another generator only when its residual norm is certified above a threshold $\theta$. Stop when all residuals are certified at most $2\theta$. Overlapping thresholds, for example accepting a certified squared residual above $\theta^2$ and stopping below $4\theta^2$, avoid equality decisions. Every retained pivot has squared residual at least $\theta^2$. Its Gram matrix $G$ therefore satisfies the conservative lower bound

$$
\lambda_{\min}(G)\ge\theta^{2M_n}M_n^{-M_n}
\qquad(0<\theta<1).
\tag{F.10.4f.23.3}
$$

This follows from the determinant product of Gram–Schmidt residuals and $\lambda_{\max}(G)\le M_n$. Enclosing entries to a precision polynomially smaller than this bound certifies each pivot and the resulting orthonormal coordinates. The number of *bits*, rather than the inverse bound itself, is $O(M_n\log(1/\theta)+M_n\log M_n)$.

Let $P$ be the retained-span projection and $A_P=P A_\lambda|_{\operatorname{ran}P}$. Each omitted generator has distance at most $2\theta$. For a unit $x\in\mathcal K_n$, Cauchy–Schwarz over the $D_n^g$ basis vectors gives

$$
\|(1-P)A_\lambda^jV_nx\|\le2\sqrt{D_n^g}\theta\quad(0\le j\le L).
$$

The recursion for $P A_\lambda^jV_n-A_P^jV_n$ then bounds the $j$th moment mismatch by $2(j+1)\sqrt{D_n^g}\theta$. Chebyshev coefficients of $f_\beta$ have magnitude at most two. The absolute monomial-coefficient sum of $T_j(2x-1)$ is at most $7^j$, by its three-term recurrence. Therefore replacing the exact Krylov space by this retained span adds at most

$$
4{(L+1)}^2 7^L\sqrt{D_n^g}\theta
\tag{F.10.4f.23.4}
$$

to the window error. Choose $\theta$ to put (F.10.4f.23.4) inside its declared allocation. Its logarithm is $O(L+\log D_n^g+\log(1/\delta))$, so the bit precision required by (F.10.4f.23.3) remains polynomial in $\log(1/\delta)$.

The finite inverse in (F.10.4f.20.2) can also be regularized at a controlled energy ceiling. Replace $A_P$ by $A_P\vee a_0 I$ with

$$
a_0=\min\left\{\tfrac12,\frac{\beta_0\lambda}{\beta_1\lambda+\log(1/\varepsilon_{\rm cap})}\right\}.
\tag{F.10.4f.23.5}
$$

For $0<\varepsilon_{\rm cap}<1$, functional calculus changes every heat filter on the retained window by at most $\varepsilon_{\rm cap}$, because the modification occurs below $a_0$, where both filters are bounded by $e^{\beta_1\lambda-\beta_0\lambda/a_0}$. The vacuum eigenvalue one is untouched, and the resulting positive finite Hamiltonian has

$$
\|H_{\rm cap}\|\le\lambda/a_0=O_{\beta_0,\beta_1,\lambda}(\log(1/\varepsilon_{\rm cap})).
\tag{F.10.4f.23.6}
$$

This prevents a small Gram or resolvent eigenvalue from becoming an unpriced energy requirement. Finite spectral calculus can be performed with interval errors; the square-root inequality controls the positive-part operation and inversion is bounded on $[a_0,1]$. Taking the matrix-entry precision high enough separately controls the resulting operator error. In finite arithmetic enforce the exact vacuum eigenvector by replacing a computed compression $A'$ with $|\chi\rangle\langle\chi|+(1-|\chi\rangle\langle\chi|)A'(1-|\chi\rangle\langle\chi|)$ in its finite source coordinates, then clip its remaining spectrum to $[a_0,1]$. The exact compression already fixes $\chi$, so this repair has a controlled matrix-norm error; preparation of the declared $\chi$ is charged separately. The preceding estimates give an explicit finite stopping criterion for every precision refinement.

<a id="proposition-f104f24-charged-gaussian-core-interfaces"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.24 (Charged Gaussian Core Interfaces).**

The computational test class supplies, before cutoff selection, a fixed bandwidth, a contraction certificate, and a matrix-entry producer whose complete computation/program/working-memory cost for indices below $m$ and accuracy $2^{-p}$ is bounded by a fixed polynomial in $m,p$. All input-description bits are charged. For the scalar component of (F.10.4f.19.1), truncating its normalized geometric tail after $v$ terms gives error at most $\eta^v$; choose $v=O_\eta(p)$ and query the diagonal producer through index $n+v$. The finite contraction dilation is then produced from the certified corner matrix by finite matrix arithmetic. Entry uncertainty is paid explicitly, with a harmless certified norm rescaling if needed. Fixed rational matrix units, their supplied fixed finite sums, and the identity form a nonempty admitted class. Analytic (F.10.4f.19.3) covers every banded contraction; the polynomial tariff below covers this computationally admitted subclass, in the same charged-access sense as F.10.4f.10.

A finite source record lists $g,m,n,L$, the chosen heat window, the moments (F.10.4f.22.3) and their enclosures, the pivot/Gram certificate, $\theta,a_0$, the represented algebra and vacuum matrix, and the actual finite matrices for the requested interfaces. In this resource branch choose $n$ as the next dyadic cutoff, which preserves its $O(\log(1/\delta))$ size. The finite state's $M_n$ component is a truncated geometric law; its preparation is the binary product preparation of F.10.4f.11, with an additional tail-label amplitude $\sqrt{t_n}$. The Schrödinger dual of (F.10.4f.19.1), between any two supplied finite cutoff sources, is a comparison of the level index followed by an exact low-corner transfer or the declared tail-state preparation. This is a finite measure/reset channel retaining its flag and environment. The default larger cutoff is $2n$, so its tail block is another shifted dyadic truncated geometric law. A larger supplied source pays its actual dimension, preparation and duration; a nondyadic block uses ordinary finite amplitude preparation with at most its dimension in controlled rotations. Code-corner embeddings place these finite registers into three-qubit MPU carriers.

For a finite contraction $B$, use its Halmos dilation. For the positive heat operation use the Halmos dilation of $e^{-\beta H_{\rm cap}}$; the finite source also has the single Hamiltonian $H_{\rm cap}$ for the whole window. A unitary extension of the regional representation and the retained-span basis change are finite dense unitaries. QR uses at most $D(D-1)/2$ two-level factors for dimension $D$. Use Proposition F.10.4c.22's algebraic pulse construction with this successor's fixed service interval $\tau_0>0$ and $H_{\rm cap}$: $H_0=4\pi\tau_0^{-1}I+H_{\rm cap}$, endpoint-compensated logarithm $\|G\|\le2\pi$, and the cubic switching function. Then $\sup\|C\|\le3\pi/\tau_0$, $\int\|C\|\le2\pi$, and total generator norm is at most $\|H_{\rm cap}\|+7\pi/\tau_0$. This supplies a positive calibrated realization including its endpoint phase and fixed service clock. The lattice interval $\tau_n=4^{-n}$ is not used for this compiler. There are no discarded unsuccessful events. Every preparation, comparator, basis change, control, flag, archive, and readout has a named service entry.

If the implemented preparation purification has vector error $e_{\rm prep}$ and the participating coherent gate errors sum to $e_{\rm gate}$, complete fixed finite records differ from their ideal finite circuits in trace norm by at most $2(e_{\rm prep}+e_{\rm gate})$. For a Heisenberg interface the completely bounded norm error is at most $2e_{\rm gate}$, which also bounds its error on $\Omega$; the unnormalized heat-vector error is at most $e_{\rm prep}+e_{\rm gate}$.
