Add these separately to (F.10.4f.19.3), (F.10.4f.20.4), (F.10.4f.23.4) and (F.10.4f.23.5). Every uniform finite-map perturbation $e_{\rm reg}$ from thresholding, capping, matrix/basis production or coherent implementation contributes at most $(n^2+1)e_{\rm reg}$ to the nuclear/projective norm by the coordinate decomposition in Theorem F.10.4f.20. Allocate their total below $\delta/[8(n^2+1)]$ when a nuclear/tensor budget $\delta$ is requested. This adds at most $\delta/8$ to the ideal (F.10.4f.20.5)/Theorem F.10.4f.21 ledger and preserves the polynomial parameter growth. These are source-implementation comparisons, including leakage amplitudes. An infinite-versus-finite sequential record additionally uses its actual composed effects; a bandwidth bound on the individual operators alone does not identify those effects. For a nominated finite POVM, the effect-mismatch sum is the one in F.10.4f.11, with the present finite state.

Use the positive fixed tariff (F.10.4f.22). The record includes matrix-production arithmetic and checker steps, all parameter bits, allocated and clean qubits, gate uses, control energy/strength, communicated bits, flags, and the actual memory/record holding times. A repeated service swaps in a paid ready register and archives the displaced one. Sampling to statistical error $\delta$ with confidence $1-\zeta$ costs its actual $O(\delta^{-2}\log(1/\zeta))$ trials, independently of the norm approximation.

For fixed $d$, positive rational $m,a,\beta_0,\beta_1,\lambda$, the profile (F.10.4f.23.1), fixed $w$, a fixed finite number of calls, efficiently supplied rational query parameters, the computational test class just defined and bounded declared holding intervals, Propositions F.10.4f.22–F.10.4f.23 reduce the regularized finite compiler to a number of bounded-precision arithmetic operations polynomial in $n,L,K,p$, where all these parameters are polynomial in $\log(1/\delta)$. The quadrature dimensions are the fixed $d$ momentum variables and one Laplace variable; the field occupation is handled by finite two-mode matrices. Dense QR, the bit precision from (F.10.4f.23.3), and the capped energy (F.10.4f.23.6) preserve a polynomial upper bound. Under the same calibrated finite-precision service tariff as F.10.4f.11, this gives

$$
C_{\rm core}(\delta)\le C_g\,P_g(\log(1/\delta))
\tag{F.10.4f.24.1}
$$

for a nonnegative polynomial obtained by composing those explicit finite loops and the nominated service polynomial. The constants include the fixed profile's enclosures, mass, bandwidth, heat window, prices, circuit count and holding intervals. They exclude no controller or matrix-production work. Equation (F.10.4f.24.1) concerns the norm-accurate fixed finite interface, not an accuracy-dependent sampling archive.

<a id="corollary-f104f25-fixed-core-geometric-cost"></a>**Corollary F.10.4f.25 (Fixed-Core Geometric Cost).**

For this geometric comparison define the regional area entry by the Cauchy-base boundary, $|\partial O_R|:=|\partial B_R|$ for $O_R=D(B_R)$. Keep one fixed centered profile of support radius $r_*>0$ in the concentric balls $B_R$ with $R\ge2r_*$. Its matrices and costs are independent of unused additional volume. Translated profiles have the same quantum matrices up to covariance; arbitrary location/address production and label bits pay their actual additional cost. The uniform tariff here uses the fixed-center family. With $S_*:=|\partial B_{2r_*}|>0$,

$$
C_{\rm core}(\delta)\le (C_g/S_*)\,|\partial B_R|\,P_g(\log(1/\delta)).
\tag{F.10.4f.25.1}
$$

This is an explicit instance of the geometric *upper-bound form* in (F.10.4f.9), for the retained one-mode core, with $C_1=C_2=0$. The resource being represented has fixed spatial resolution and fixed number of canonical modes. A source that retains a number of independent modes growing with region size, shrinks the collar, or seeks the full regional algebra requires the resulting mode-count, covariance-conditioning, nuclear-tail and compilation bounds. Equation (F.10.4f.25.1) supplies no area-law claim about those larger tasks. The service clock and encoded field coordinates retain the distinct source-clock comparison stated in Proposition F.10.4c.22 and F.10.4f.11.

<a id="theorem-f104f26-faithful-thermal-semibounded-clock-obstruction"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.26 (Faithful Thermal Semibounded-Clock Obstruction).** Let $M\subset B(\mathcal H)$ be a von Neumann algebra, let $\alpha$ be a strongly continuous one-parameter automorphism group of $M$, and let $\varphi$ be a faithful normal $b$-KMS state for $\alpha$, with $0<b<\infty$. Suppose a strongly continuous unitary group $U(t)=e^{\mathrm{itK}}$ on $\mathcal H$ implements $\alpha$, and $K$ is bounded below. Then $M$ is semifinite. In particular a nonzero type-III algebra under these hypotheses admits no such implementer. No assumption that $U(t)$ fixes the state vector is needed.

*Proof.* Araki–Zsidó's Borchers implementation theorem, Theorem 2.14, produces a positive injective contraction $h\in M$ with

$$
\alpha_t(x)=h^{-it}xh^{it},\qquad x\in M.
$$

The unitary group $h^{-it}$ is strongly continuous by spectral calculus. Its generator $-\log h$ is nonnegative and affiliated with $M$. This is a continuous implementing group inside the algebra; the conclusion is stronger than separate innerness of each automorphism.

For the physical KMS convention $\varphi(A\alpha_{ib}(B))=\varphi(BA)$, uniqueness of modular dynamics gives $\sigma_s^\varphi=\alpha_{-bs}$. The opposite KMS convention reverses this sign, with no effect on the argument. Consequently the modular group of the faithful normal state is implemented by the strongly continuous unitary group $h^{ibs}$ inside $M$.

Pedersen–Takesaki, Theorem 7.4, identifies existence of such an inner continuous modular implementation with semifiniteness. To spell out its applicable direction: if $\sigma_s^\varphi=\operatorname{Ad}(a^{is})$ for a strictly positive affiliated $a$, then $a$ lies in the centralizer and the faithful normal semifinite weight $\varphi(a^{-1/2}\,\cdot\,a^{-1/2})$ has trivial modular group. It is a faithful normal semifinite trace. Thus $M$ is semifinite, proving the theorem. ∎

A generator bounded above is likewise excluded on a type-III algebra: apply the implementation theorem to the reversed flow and reverse the resulting inner group back. Hence every implementing generator of a faithful normal finite-temperature type-III KMS dynamics is unbounded in both directions.

<a id="proposition-f104f30-effective-local-gaussian-matrix-exhaustion-and-retained-core-interfaces"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.30 (Effective Local Gaussian Matrix Exhaustion and Retained-Core Interfaces).**

#### 1. Frozen source and dimensionless canonical coordinates

Use the source of Appendix F, Definitions F.10.4c.7 and F.10.4c.10 and Theorems F.10.4c.17–19:

$$
\begin{aligned}
H &= d\Gamma(\omega),\quad \omega(p) = \sqrt{m^{2}+|p|^{2}},\quad m>0, \\
H_{\mathrm{Fock}} &= \Gamma_s(L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{3},dp)),\quad \Omega = \Omega_{\mathrm{Fock}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The regional algebra for a Cauchy base B is generated by the local real Cauchy data. For a diamond B is a bounded ball; for a wedge B can be its open half-space base. Fix a positive computable reference energy $\mu_{0}$. It only makes oscillator coordinates dimensionless and does not replace H or rescale time.

Choose real $L^{2}$-orthonormal $g_1,g_2,\ldots$ in $C_c^\infty(B)$, with span dense in $H_0^{1}(B)$. Set

$$
\begin{aligned}
Q_j &= \sqrt{\mu_0}\, \phi(g_j),\quad P_j = \pi(g_j)/\sqrt{\mu_0}, \\
[Q_i,P_j] &= i \delta_{ij},\quad [Q_i,Q_j]=[P_i,P_j]=0.
\end{aligned}
$$

For either a bounded ball or a half-space, choose strictly increasing computable balls $B_{l}$ with closures contained in $B$ and union $B$. Enumerate $b_{l}$ times all real coordinate monomials, where $b_{l}$ is a fixed computable Gevrey-2 bump positive throughout $B_{l}$ and zero outside. These functions belong to $C_c^\infty(B)$, including in the bounded-ball case. Every finite subset is linearly independent: on the shell outside the largest preceding ball only the polynomial multiplying the outermost bump survives, and hence it vanishes identically; induction handles the remaining balls. Their span is $H_0^{1}$-dense: a compactly supported smooth $f$ lies in some $B_l$, $f/b_l$ extends smoothly by zero near that ball's boundary, and polynomial $C^{1}$-approximation followed by multiplication by $b_{l}$ approximates $f$ in $H^{1}$. Certified Gram–Schmidt therefore has a strictly positive pivot at every step and terminates without an exact-zero decision. All normalization constants and derivative/Fourier-tail enclosures are computable. There is no claim that the resulting $L^{2}$ orthogonal projections converge in $H^{1}$ at a uniform rate.

Let $M_{r}$ be the von Neumann algebra of the first r canonical pairs. Finite-dimensional regular CCR representation gives

$$
\begin{gathered}
M_{r}\cong B(\ell^{2}(\mathbb{N}_0^r))\otimes I_{\mathrm{complement}}, \\
M_r\subset M_{r+1}\subset A(D(B)).
\end{gathered}
$$

The regular CCR identification can also be obtained by extending the finite nondegenerate real symplectic span to a symplectic basis of the finite complex one-particle space generated by its positive/negative-frequency packets. This uses finite linear algebra, rather than an infinite split unitary. At most 2r complex packets are needed.

Density of the Cauchy data in $H_0^{1}$ implies density in the one-particle Cauchy norm $H^{-1/2}\oplus H^{1/2}$. Strong continuity of Weyl operators then gives

$$
\Bigl(\bigcup_r M_r\Bigr)'' = A(D(B)).
$$

For an unbounded half-space use compactly supported data throughout; the same union generates the wedge algebra. No sharp spatial tensor-product factorization of the whole field is assumed.

#### 2. A genuinely nested finite-algebra exhaustion

In each fixed canonical oscillator let $P_{n}$ project onto levels 0,…,n−1 and define

$$
B_n = B(P_n \ell^{2}) \oplus \mathbb{C} I_{P_n^\perp}.
$$

The inclusion $B_n\subset B_{n+1}$ sends $(b,c)$ to $(b\oplus c,c)$. In particular it is unital; it is not a nonunital Hilbert-space corner inclusion. For $r,n$ define

$$
B_{r,n} = \bigotimes_{j=1}^r B_n \subset M_r.
$$

Adding a mode tensors with the identity and increasing $n$ uses the displayed inclusions. Consequently $B_j:=B_{j,j}$ is an increasing sequence of finite-dimensional unital algebras. More general cofinal increasing integer pairs work as well. Its dimensions are

vector-space dimension $d_j=(j^{2}+1)^j$,
minimal faithful representation dimension $a_j=(j+1)^j$.

For fixed r, the strong closure of ∪_n $B_{r,n}$ is $M_{r}$: finite matrix units and identity occur in every oscillator. Thus

$$
\Bigl(\bigcup_j B_j\Bigr)'' = A(D(B)).
$$

The vacuum is separating for each region by the scalar Reeh–Schlieder/locality argument. Hence $\omega|_{B_j}$ is faithful. In the actual finite GNS Hilbert space $H_j=B_j\Omega$, the vector $\Omega$ is cyclic and separating and $\dim H_j=\dim B_j$. This is exactly the exhaustion hypothesis used by the finite Tomita theorem, with no abstract hyperfiniteness assumption remaining.

The norm closure is a particular AF subalgebra. Its strong closure is the full local von Neumann algebra. These are not interchangeable assertions.

#### 3. Actual vacuum covariance and its effective matrix entries

Order $R=(Q_1,\ldots,Q_r,P_1,\ldots,P_r)$. The centered covariance $V_{r}$ has blocks

$$
\begin{aligned}
X_{ab} &= (\mu_0/2)\langle g_a,\omega^{-1}g_b\rangle, \\
Y_{ab} &= \frac{1}{2\mu_0}\langle g_a,\omega g_b\rangle, \\
V_r &= \operatorname{diag}(X,Y).
\end{aligned}
$$

The real symmetrized QP block vanishes. All entries are ordinary convergent three-dimensional momentum integrals. The source Fourier convention is retained. Effective Gevrey profile descriptions, positive mass bounds and their Fourier-tail enclosures make these entries computable by finite quadrature. No local Gibbs Hamiltonian is identified with H.

Here is a direct coefficient producer that avoids exact Williamson eigenvector choices. Let $A_r=V_r+I/2$ and, for independent complex variables $z$ and $\bar z$, put

$$
v(z,\bar z)=((z+\bar z)/\sqrt{2},(z-\bar z)/(i \sqrt{2})).
$$

The Gaussian Husimi generating identity is

$$
\begin{aligned}
G(z,\bar z)&=\det(A_r)^{-1/2} \\
&\quad \exp\Bigl(\bar z\cdot z - \frac{1}{2}v(z,\bar z)^{\mathsf T} A_r^{-1}v(z,\bar z)\Bigr) \\
&= \sum_{m,n} (\rho_r)_{mn}\, \bar z^m z^n / \sqrt{m!\, n!}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\rho_{r}$ is the **actual** vacuum density on $M_r$'s defining oscillator representation. This identity follows by convolving its Gaussian Wigner function with the vacuum Gaussian and expanding coherent vectors. Therefore a named matrix entry is a finite Taylor coefficient of an explicit quadratic exponential. Multivariate coefficient recursion, finite matrix inversion and a positive square root produce it with certified error. Degenerate covariance eigenvalues cause no decision problem. The finite input profiles, mass and $\mu_{0}$ remain the only source data.

#### 4. Explicit occupation tails, including displaced tests

For a Gaussian state with covariance $V_{r}$ and mean $d\in\mathbb{R}^{2r}$, define

$$
M_z = ((1+z)/2)\, I + (1-z)V_r.
$$

For $z>1$ sufficiently close to one,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{r,d}\, z^{N}) &= \det(M_z)^{-1/2} \\
&\quad \exp((z-1)d^{\mathsf T} M_z^{-1}d/2), \\
N&=\sum_j(Q_j^{2}+P_j^{2}-1)/2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.10.4f.30.4.1}
$$

One derivation evaluates the overlap with the normalized thermal Gaussian for $0<z<1$ and analytically continues its nonnegative-coefficient generating series up to its first positive singularity. The uncertainty inequality gives $\lambda_{\min}(V_r)\ge 1/(4\lVert V_r\rVert)$, so a negative real singularity cannot precede that positive boundary in modulus. Formula (F.10.4f.30.4.1) is also the quadrature-coordinate version of the Gaussian moment-generating formula in Cardin and Quesada (2022, Section III, equations (28)–(30)). This citation supplies the finite Gaussian identity; the cutoff and source conclusions here are proved separately.

Choose a certified rational $\bar v\ge\max(1/2,\lVert V_r\rVert)$, and

$$
z = 1 + 1/[2(\bar v+1)].
$$

Then $M_z\ge I/2$ and $z$ lies inside that convergence interval. It follows that

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{r,d}\, \mathbf{1}_{N\ge K}) &\le C_r(d)\, z^{-K}, \\
C_r(d)&=2^r \exp((z-1)\lVert d\rVert^{2}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.10.4f.30.4.2}
$$

Indeed $z^N\ge z^K$ on the retained tail, $\det(M_z)^{-1/2}\le 2^r$, and $M_z^{-1}\le 2I$. Thus a tail allocation $\varepsilon$ is achieved by

$$
K \ge [\log C_r(d)+\log(1/\varepsilon)]/\log z.
\tag{F.10.4f.30.4.3}
$$

The constants retain r, the actual covariance conditioning and the displacement size. They are not claimed uniformly bounded as r grows.

For a mode-box cutoff $P_{<K}^{\otimes r}$, its complement is contained in $\{N\ge K\}$; (F.10.4f.30.4.2) bounds its probability as well. For fixed $r$ and bounded $d$, $K=O_r(\log(1/\varepsilon))$.

#### 5. Effective faithful state blocks on the nested algebras

The direct-sum blocks of $B_{r,n}$ are indexed by subsets S⊂{1,…,r}: modes in S lie in their n-dimensional low corner and modes outside S carry the scalar tail block. The actual density in block S is

$$
\begin{aligned}
(D_S)_{a b} &= \sum_{k_j\ge n,\ j\notin S} (\rho_r)_{(a,k),(b,k)}, \\
0&\le a_j,b_j<n \text{ for } j\in S.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.10.4f.30.5.1}
$$

The family $D_{S}$ is positive and has $\Sigma_{S}$ Tr $D_{S}=1$. Faithfulness inherited from $\Omega$ separating makes every $D_{S}$ strictly positive, including every scalar block.

To compute all blocks, choose $K\ge n$ and restrict each tail summation to $n\le k_j<K$. All omitted block matrices are positive. The sum of their traces is at most $\operatorname{Tr}\rho_r(1-P_{<K}^{\otimes r})$, hence at most $C_r(0)z^{-K}$. Consequently their total trace-norm error is bounded by that same quantity. Add the missing trace mass to the all-tail scalar block to obtain a normalized finite state; this increases the total error by at most another $C_r(0)z^{-K}$. Taylor-coefficient arithmetic errors are budgeted separately, followed, if necessary, by finite positive-part clipping and normalization with their explicitly computed matrix-norm errors.

This is a finite stopping algorithm for the complete actual state restriction. It does not approximate an unknown split density. A crude dense implementation uses at most $K^{2r}$ Gaussian density entries, plus finite block sums. This dependence is part of the cost ledger.

Since $D_{S}>0$, continued interval refinement eventually certifies a positive lower bound $\lambda_{j}$ for every finite state block. The standard finite GNS model is

$$
\begin{gathered}
H_j=\bigoplus_S\mathrm{HS}(\mathbb{C}^{n^{|S|}}),\\
\chi_j=\bigoplus_S\sqrt{D_S},\\
L_j(b)X=bX,\\
\Delta_{j}X=D_S X D_S^{-1},\quad J_j X=X^*\quad\text{on each block}.
\end{gathered}
$$

These are actual faithful finite modular data. Finite logarithms can be computed after $\lambda_{j}$ is certified. No lower bound uniform in j, no cheap precision bound in j and no physical-time identification of log $\Delta_{j}$ follows from faithfulness alone.

#### 6. Explicit two-sided GNS recovery for Weyl tests

Fix $r$ and write a Weyl operator in these modes as $W=\prod_{i=1}^r W_i$; different mode factors commute. For one oscillator and an arbitrary normal tail state $\sigma$, define the UCP map

$$
\begin{aligned}
E_{i,n}(A)&=P_n A P_n + \sigma(Q_n A Q_n)Q_n, \\
Q_n&=I-P_n,
\end{aligned}
$$

where $\sigma$ is normalized on $Q_{n}$. A concrete choice is the level-$n$ vector state. Its range is $B_{n}$, and $\lVert E_{i,n}(A)\rVert\le\lVert A\rVert$. Write

$$
t_i=\omega(Q_n),\quad u_i=\omega(W_i^*Q_n W_i).
$$

The exact decomposition $A-E(A)=QAP+AQ-\sigma(QAQ)Q$ gives, for $A=W_i$,

$$
\lVert(W_i-E_{i,n}W_i)\Omega\rVert\le\sqrt{u_i}+3\sqrt{t_i}.
\tag{F.10.4f.30.6.1}
$$

The same estimate holds for $W_i^*$ with the displaced mean reversed. Formula (F.10.4f.30.4.2), applied to the two-dimensional marginal covariance of mode $i$, computes both tails. For $\lVert d_i\rVert\le R_i$ the resulting bound is uniform.

Set $W_n=\prod_i E_{i,n}(W_i)\in B_{r,n}$. Telescoping, commutation between different mode factors, and contractivity imply

$$
\begin{gathered}
\lVert(W-W_n)\Omega\rVert\le\sum_i[\sqrt{u_i}+3\sqrt{t_i}],\\
\lVert(W^*-W_n^*)\Omega\rVert\le\text{the same displacement-uniform bound.}
\end{gathered}
\tag{F.10.4f.30.6.2}
$$

For clarity, the factors from other modes commute with the i-th difference; their contractions can be moved to the left before taking the vector norm. No vacuum product assumption enters (F.10.4f.30.6.2).

On a fixed finite-mode displacement ball the right side is at most

$$
4 \sum_i \sqrt{C_i(R_i)}\, z_i^{-n/2}.
\tag{F.10.4f.30.6.3}
$$

Thus an explicit $n=O_{r,V,R}(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ gives simultaneous vector and adjoint-vector error $\varepsilon$. Finite Weyl words reduce to one displacement and a known phase. Finite sums with a declared coefficient $\ell^{1}$ bound acquire that factor; normalization uses a declared positive cancellation floor. The heat-vector error on any $\beta\ge 0$ is no larger, because $e^{-\beta H}$ is a contraction. The vacuum expectation error is bounded by the vector error.

All members of the countable local Weyl generating core involving the first r enumerated Cauchy functions lie exactly in $M_{r}$. Consequently (F.10.4f.30.6.2) gives **effective Tomita graph recovery** on that generating core:

$$
W_n\Omega\to W\Omega\quad\text{and}\quad S_j W_n\Omega=W_n^*\Omega\to W^*\Omega.
$$

For response vectors given by other fixed local Weyl words, the same proof uses the displaced Gaussian marginal and its explicitly bounded mean. This gives a computable strong-star comparison on every fixed finite list of such response vectors.

For arbitrary smooth data not lying in the first $r$-mode span, the omitted spatial-mode approximation is an additional error. A computable residual modulus for the chosen compact spatial test family must be supplied; density of the union alone is not a uniform mode selector. Neither an arbitrary $L^{2}$ projection nor a pointwise scalar tail estimate is silently promoted to that modulus.

#### 7. Full-domain UCP interfaces and nuclear budgets

The finite type-I factor $M_{r}$ has a global tensor representation. For an explicit state choice, extend its finite symplectic frame within the at-most-$2r$ complex packet space to a full symplectic basis, use a canonical vacuum on the complementary finite canonical coordinates, and use the original Fock vacuum on the orthogonal packet complement. Finite symplectic Gram–Schmidt and finite matrix-function enclosures compute the resulting complementary Gaussian state $\sigma_{c}$. Its normal partial-state expectation $E_r=\mathrm{id}\otimes\sigma_c$ is UCP on $B(H)$ and is the identity on $M_{r}$. Its value on a supplied Weyl test is computed by the finite symplectic projection and this Gaussian characteristic function; arbitrary unspecified operators are not assumed to come with a free access oracle. Therefore composing it with the tensor of the cutoff maps $E_{i,n}$ gives a normal UCP map

$$
\pi_{r,n}: A(O)\to B_{r,n}.
$$

Its recovery is the actual unital inclusion $B_{r,n}\subset M_r\subset A(O)\subset A(O_+)$. On the retained finite-mode tests, $E_{r}$ has no effect and (F.10.4f.30.6.2) controls the GNS, state and heat comparisons. The finite state is the actual restriction from Section 5. This construction does **not** claim $E_{r}$ or the cutoff maps preserve the vacuum on the entire regional algebra.

A genuine type-I collar A(O_-)⊂N⊂A(O_+) is supplied by the already proved same-net split theorem. Its abstract existence meets the split inclusion entry; the implemented interfaces above do not use an unspecified unitary for N. This distinction is already permitted by the original one-mode source route. No claim is made here of an effective circuit for a chosen full collar split unitary.

Let $j:B_{r,n}\to A(O)$ be the actual inclusion. The exact finite-domain heat map

$$
\Theta^B_\beta(b)=e^{-\beta H}j(b)\Omega
$$

has nuclear norm at most the **same full-regional** nuclear bound $N_{\beta,O}$ from F.10.4f.14, because restriction along a norm-one *-homomorphism does not increase nuclear norm. This bound is uniform in $r,n$. If a finite-source heat map differs from $\Theta^B_\beta$ by at most $e$ in operator norm on $B_{r,n}$, its nuclear norm differs by at most

$$
\dim(B_{r,n})\, e = (n^{2}+1)^r e,
\tag{F.10.4f.30.7.1}
$$

using an Auerbach basis. Thus a uniform finite budget is obtained by explicitly paying this dimension factor in the source error.

This is a pre-transport nuclear bound on actual finite algebras, rather than a bound only on an operator-system image. It does not imply projective convergence on the full unrestricted regional input algebra through the particular $E_{r}$ above. The earlier collar/Schmidt construction retains its separate full-regional projective theorem.

#### 8. Effective comparison with the original finite registers

Let $V_j:H_j\to H$ be the actual finite GNS isometry $V_j L_j(b)\chi_j=j(b)\Omega$. Its finite Gram matrix is computed from the genuine state $D_{S}$. The vectors entering it can be approximated effectively in the original Fock representation, not merely specified by abstract GNS labels.

One explicit method uses Weyl inversion. In one oscillator,

$$
\lvert a\rangle\langle b\rvert=(1/\pi)\int_{\mathbb{C}}\langle b\vert D(\alpha)\vert a\rangle D(-\alpha)\,d^{2}\alpha.
\tag{F.10.4f.30.8.1}
$$

The coefficient is a Gaussian times a known finite polynomial. The integral is a weak/strong-vector integral; no false operator-norm continuity of $D(\alpha)$ is assumed. Its norm tail is bounded by the integral of the absolute Gaussian-polynomial coefficient. Products treat $r$ modes, and each tail projector is identity minus finitely many diagonal matrix units. Thus every $B_j\Omega$ is approximated by finite quadrature of explicit local coherent vectors with certified Gaussian radial tails. Their one-particle packets are finite combinations of $\omega^{\pm1/2}\hat g_i$, with effective Fourier tails. Ordinary coherent-state occupation tails and original momentum-cell comparison then compute $I_k^*V_j$ and their errors.

Write $Q_k=I_kI_k^*$. The original source has $Q_k\to I$ strongly and $Q_k\Omega=\Omega$. For fixed $j$, certify

$$
G_{j,k}=V_j^*Q_kV_j,\qquad \lVert I-G_{j,k}\rVert<\eta^{2}<1.
$$

Finite certified search terminates. Set

$$
W_{j,k}=I_k^*V_j G_{j,k}^{-1/2}.
$$

Then $W_{j,k}$ is an exact isometry, $W_{j,k}\chi_j=\Omega_k$, and the polar error has the prior certificate's bound. Complete its finite representation on the orthogonal complement by the all-tail character of $B_{j}$. This gives a unital faithful finite representation in the unchanged original register, with exact vacuum state on $B_{j}$. The original $H_{k}$ and rounded query clocks are retained. Actual heat-vector errors are computed on the finitely many input basis vectors and pay (F.10.4f.30.7.1). For a heat interval $[b,B]$, finite interval subdivision and the standard heat Lipschitz estimate away from zero give a uniform finite stopping test; the strong convergence $Q_k\to I$ of the original source ensures termination.

Choose increasing $k_{j}$ and demand each new stage meet all earlier finitely many retained query/error allocations. This yields one common original subsequence for the countable query list. It is a certified search, not a claim of a small or uniform source index. Its representations are not asserted to be the norm-coherent region embeddings required by F01.

#### Effective geometric-boost cross-pairings

For finite basis vectors $b\Omega$ and $c\Omega$ constructed above, all pairings $\langle b\Omega,U(\Lambda_s)c\Omega\rangle$ are computable uniformly for $s$ in a named compact rapidity interval. Expand matrix units by (F.10.4f.30.8.1), expand tail projectors by identity minus their finite low sums, and use the scalar Weyl vacuum kernel for each resulting product. The kernel depends only on finitely many packet Gram entries $\langle h_a,U_1(\Lambda_s)h_b\rangle$. The original positive mass and compact rapidity interval give computable smooth boost-coordinate maps and polynomially bounded Jacobian derivatives. Gevrey packet tails bound their momentum integrals, while the Gaussian-polynomial Weyl-inversion coefficients bound the remaining displacement integrals.

All finite basis vectors $b\Omega$ are in the domain of every fixed power of the scalar boost generator. At the one-particle level this follows because $\omega^{\pm1/2}\hat g_i$ are Schwartz and the boost generator is a first-order differential operator with smooth polynomially bounded coefficients. Differentiating a coherent vector produces a finite field polynomial applied to that vector; at each fixed derivative order its norm is bounded by a polynomial in the displacement variables and finitely many one-particle boost derivatives. These bounds remain integrable against the Gaussian-polynomial coefficients in (F.10.4f.30.8.1). Dominated differentiation therefore computes each fixed boost moment, in particular $\lVert K b\Omega\rVert$ and $\lVert K^{2}b\Omega\rVert$, with $K$ normalized by the credited same-wedge Bisognano–Wichmann formula. The same argument applies to a finite Weyl test or a finite linear combination of such vectors.

Consequently the target norms and cross-pairings required by the finite modular grid/graph selectors are actual effective scalar quantities on these finite retained families. Uniformity over all regional unit vectors, a mode-independent cost bound and compatibility of different bounded-diamond modular actions are not claimed.

#### 9. Effective finite near-budget nuclear certificates

There is a useful way to avoid the remaining infinite spectral-eigenbasis oracle for **finite-source** nuclear certificates. A map $T:B\to\mathbb{C}^D$ with computable finite matrices admits an effective finite-decomposition search below any strict known nuclear upper bound. No algorithm for the exact minimum is needed.

Enumerate finite rational tensors $\sum_l\varphi_l\otimes\xi_l$. On a finite direct sum $B=\bigoplus M_{d_s}$, the norm of a functional is $\sum_s\lVert F_s\rVert_1$, computable by finite singular-value enclosures. Compute each tensor's cost $\sum_l\lVert\varphi_l\rVert\lVert\xi_l\rVert$ and its matrix residual $T-T_{\mathrm{candidate}}$. Expand the residual in the fixed matrix-coordinate functionals; their norms are one, so the sum of the output residual norms is an explicit projective-norm upper bound. Accept when candidate cost plus residual cost is below $N+\varepsilon$, where $N$ is a certified strict upper enclosure for $N_{\beta,O}+\dim(B)e$, including the finite-source heat error $e$ from (F.10.4f.30.7.1), and $\varepsilon>0$. The original continuum bound $N_{\beta,O}$ alone is not substituted for the finite-source bound.

Finite rational tensors are dense, and $\nu(T)\le N$; the strict $\varepsilon$ margin guarantees termination. The resulting decomposition includes the residual correction and is a genuine finite representation of the computable finite map, with coefficient-error enclosures if only finite output precision is requested. This produces a finite near-budget certificate without assuming computability of the full collar's Schmidt basis or the original infinite majorant's eigenvectors.

This search can be extremely expensive. Its actual enumeration, arithmetic, stored coefficients and precision are charged. Effectivity does not imply a polynomial tariff.

#### 10. Formal compilation, costs, and remaining owner clauses

Every produced finite matrix/state/channel has a finite Stinespring or purification dilation. Dense QR and two-level synthesis give a finite encoded circuit; Gray-code decomposition and ancillary controlled gates reduce it to one- and two-carrier operations, with nearest-neighbor routing if that service model is selected. A conservative count for an arbitrary $D$-dimensional unitary is $O(D^{2}(\log D)^{3})$ two-qubit operations after line routing. Preparation, reset flags, storage, classical matrix production and nuclear-certificate enumeration are separate charged entries. Operator-norm gate error $\varepsilon_{g}$ contributes at most $2\varepsilon_g$ to the induced channel distance; errors telescope across the actual gate list. This is a formal finite compilation statement, not a claim of a hardware experiment.

For each **fixed** number of retained modes and fixed computable Gevrey profiles, the state-entry and Weyl-cutoff part has cutoff $K,n=O(\log(1/\delta))$, with dense finite work growing at least as the displayed powers $K^{2r}$ and $(n^{2}+1)^r$. One must also charge the source-index search, near-budget nuclear decomposition search, Gram conditioning and every control/holding-time term. No proof here bounds those combined costs by one fixed polynomial in $\log(1/\delta)$ uniformly in $r$, shrinking collars or arbitrary regional families.

The original F14 cost condition is

$$
C_{\delta,O}\le C_0|\partial O|P(\log(1/\delta))+C_1\mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{active}}(O)+C_2C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta).
$$

This inequality is not established merely because all steps terminate. The retained-mode growth, spatial approximation modulus, covariance and Gram conditioning, nuclear-certificate production complexity, and source/control-clock identification must be bounded in this exact inequality. Local PU-LAN and Hadamard-PCE/reflection admission also remain separate source predicates. No stronger requirement for an actual laboratory run is added.

The positive result of Proposition F.10.4f.30 is therefore an effective actual matrix exhaustion, explicit Gaussian state and strong-star graph producers, retained-core UCP comparisons, original-register polar access, and finite near-budget nuclear-certificate production. Full F01/F14 closure lies outside Proposition F.10.4f.30.

<a id="proposition-f104f310-effective-bounded-resolvent-majorant-and-j-real-blocks"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.31.0 (Effective Bounded-Resolvent Majorant and J-Real Blocks).**

##### 1. The new majorant

Fix $b>0$, $q=\exp(-bm)<1$ and the original output-side positive compact operators

$$
\begin{aligned}
&A_s=|E_s \exp(-b \omega)|=(\exp(-b \omega) E_s \exp(-b \omega))^{1/2}, \\
&s=-1/2,+1/2,\qquad \lVert A_s\rVert\le q.
\end{aligned}
$$

They commute with the original conjugation $J$. Write $B_s=A_s^2$. Choose the explicit slack $q'=(1+q)/2$ and define

$$
\begin{aligned}
R_s&=(I-B_s/q'^{2})^{-1}, \\
R&=R_-+R_+-I, \\
C&=I-R^{-1}, \\
T&=q' C^{1/2}, \\
c&=q'/\sqrt{q'^{2}-q^{2}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1.1}
$$

All inverses in (1.1) are bounded with known condition bounds. There are no spectral joins, equality decisions about eigenspaces, or inverses of local modular polarizers.

##### Theorem F.10.4f.31.0.1

T is positive compact, commutes with J, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
&T^{2}\ge A_s^{2} \text{ for both } s, \\
&\lVert T\rVert\le q'<1, \\
&\operatorname{Tr} T\le c(\operatorname{Tr} A_-+\operatorname{Tr} A_+).
\end{aligned}
\tag{1.2}
$$

**Proof.** $R_s\ge I$, hence $R\ge R_s\ge I$. Order reversal under inversion gives $R^{-1}\le R_s^{-1}=I-B_s/q'^2$. Thus $C\ge B_s/q'^2$, proving the domination. Also $0\le C\le I$, proving the contraction estimate.

Further,

$$
\begin{aligned}
0\le C=(R-I)R^{-1}&\le R-I \\
&=\sum_s B_s(q'^{2} I-B_s)^{-1} \\
&\le(B_-+B_+)/(q'^{2}-q^{2}).
\end{aligned}
$$

Square-root monotonicity gives

$$
T\le c\, (A_-^{2}+A_+^{2})^{1/2}.
$$

The last positive square root is the absolute value of the column $x\to(A_-x,A_+x)$. Its trace norm is at most $\operatorname{Tr}A_-+\operatorname{Tr}A_+$, by the triangle inequality for the two column summands. This proves (1.2), trace class, and compactness. Every function and algebraic operation in (1.1) commutes with $J$. No commutation between $A_-$ and $A_+$ was used. ∎

The original imported bosonic coefficient construction uses precisely a positive $J$-real strict contraction with $T^2\ge A_s^2$; this is the output-side criterion checked in the frozen F.10.4f.16. Therefore it applies to (1.1). This is not the invalid replacement $T=A_-+A_+$ with a possibly noncontractive norm.

##### 2. Explicit tails and the new capacity ceiling

Use the original localization constants $B_{b,s,k}$, $S=K_{b,-1/2}+K_{b,1/2}$, the three-dimensional Hermite eigenvalues $\lambda_{j}$ and their multiplicities. They give

$$
\begin{aligned}
a_{s,j}&:=s_j(A_s)\le B_{b,s,k}\, \lambda_j^{-k}, \\
\operatorname{Tr} A_-+\operatorname{Tr} A_+&\le S.
\end{aligned}
$$

Let $t_{j}$ be the decreasing eigenvalues of the new T. For every $j\ge 1$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
t_{2j-1}&\le c[a_{-,j}+a_{+,j}], \\
t_{2j}&\le c[a_{-,j}+a_{+,j}].
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.1}
$$

Indeed approximate each $A_{s}$ by its first $j-1$ singular terms. Their column has rank at most $2(j-1)$, and its residual norm is at most $a_{-,j}+a_{+,j}$. Singular-value monotonicity from $T^2\le c^2(A_-^2+A_+^2)$ proves (2.1). Consequently

$$
\sum_{j>2J} t_j \le 2c \sum_s \sum_{j>J} a_{s,j}.
\tag{2.2}
$$

This deliberately conservative factor two is kept. For $J=\binom{M+3}{3}$, $k>3$ and the original $c_{3}$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{j>2J} t_j \\
&\le 2c\, [B_{b,-1/2,k}+B_{b,1/2,k}]\, c_3/(k-3) \\
&\qquad (M+1)^{3-k}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.3}
$$

The bosonic occupation coefficient bound is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{coefficient norm} &\le c_\mu=\prod_j (\mu_j+1)\, t_j^{\mu_j}, \\
Z_{\mathrm{new}}&=\prod_j (1-t_j)^{-2} \\
&\le \exp[2c S/(1-q')].
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.4}
$$

Thus the old tail argument now yields

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_{J,L}&\le Z_{\mathrm{new}} \cdot 2 \sum_{j>J}t_j/(1-q') \\
&\quad +z^{-(L+1)} \exp[2z\, cS/(1-zq')], \\
1&<z<1/q'.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.5}
$$

All selectors follow explicitly from (2.3)-(2.5). For instance $z=(1+1/q')/2$ is admissible. The old ceiling $\exp[2S/(1-q)]$ is not claimed for this new tensor. The new fixed-region value $\log Z_{\mathrm{new}}$ is a proved same-source capacity upper bound and is independent of the requested approximation accuracy.

##### 3. Why the required regional projections are actually computable

For a ball $B$ and $s=\pm1/2$, the defining dense generators of $K_{s}$ are $\omega^{s}$ times Fourier transforms of smooth compactly supported profiles in $B$. Its Hilbert orthogonal complement has the effective dense set

$$
\omega^{-s} \text{ times Fourier transforms of smooth profiles supported outside } \operatorname{closure}(B).
\tag{3.1}
$$

To verify density rather than only inclusion, $x\in K_s^\perp$ means the distribution $f=\omega^s x$, in $H^{-s}$, vanishes in $B$. Dilate $f$ slightly outwards about the ball center, giving a support gap; dilation tends strongly to the identity in $H^{-s}$. Truncate at large radius and mollify within the support gap. These smooth exterior functions approximate $f$ in $H^{-s}$, and applying $\omega^{(-s)}$ proves (3.1). The same approximation handles complex and real parts. No half-order boundary $\delta$ is introduced.

All finite inner products of explicit Gevrey bump generators and their massive multipliers are computable with the prior Fourier-tail/quadrature enclosures. Choose computably described dense lists ($u_{j}$) in $K_{s}$ and ($v_{j}$) in $K_s^\perp$. For a computable $x$, let $P_{N}$ and $Q_{N}$ be the finite orthogonal span projections. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert E_s x-P_N x\rVert^{2} \\
&\le\lVert x\rVert^{2}-\lVert P_N x\rVert^{2}-\lVert Q_N x\rVert^{2} \to 0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.2}
$$

The right side has computable interval bounds. Increase the two finite lists and arithmetic precision until its upper enclosure is below $\epsilon^{2}$. Near-dependent list entries are handled by certified thresholded Gram-Schmidt, retaining a dense subsequence; exact equality need not be decided. Equation (3.2) is a verified stopping certificate, not an appeal to an unspecified limiting modulus. It proves that $E_{s}$ acts effectively on computable vectors. It gives no polynomial runtime bound as $\epsilon$ decreases.

##### 4. Effective compactness, without an eigenvector-gap oracle

The original kernel factorization supplies, for every $k$ and Schatten exponent $p$ with $kp>3$,

$$
\exp(-b \omega)E_s=(K_s D^{k})D^{-k}E_s,
$$

where $K_{s}$ is the explicit localized heat-kernel operator and $D$ is the original Hermite operator. Truncating the middle $D^{-k}$ at a finite Hermite head gives a finite-rank representation with known $S_{p}$ residual, bounded by the corresponding convergent Hermite series. Its finite output and input vectors are computable; application of $E_{s}$ is certified by (3.2).

Hence $B_s=A_s^2$ has effective finite-rank approximants in every $S_{p}$. Algebraic products preserve these explicit ideal bounds. The inverses in (1.1) can be approximated by their convergent geometric series with ratio at most $q^2/q'^2<1$; multiplying their tail by the compact $B_{s}$ factor gives an explicit ideal-norm tail, rather than multiplying the infinite-rank identity by a small number and calling it trace class. The same argument applies to $R^{-1}$, since $R$ is bounded between $I$ and an explicit scalar multiple of $I$. Thus $C$ has effective $S_{1/2}$ finite-rank approximants.

When a finite self-adjoint approximation is not positive, take its positive part. Its negative eigenvalues are bounded in absolute value by the singular values of its error from the true positive $C$; this follows from the variational principle. It therefore has a controlled $S_{1/2}$ error, with an explicit harmless quasi-triangle constant. The trace square-root inequality already proved in the canonical collar component then gives a certified $S_{1}$ error for $T=q'\sqrt{C}$. In short, (1.1) is a genuine finite-rank/vector approximation algorithm for the actual new majorant. Every projection search, retained vector, matrix operation and precision refinement is included in its operation record.

##### Exact finite spectral blocks instead of unstable labelled eigenvectors

Do not demand a uniformly continuous individual eigenbasis. Given an error allocation, choose positive spectral thresholds separated from the spectrum by rational gaps, certifying those gaps with the effective operator-norm finite-rank approximants. Such choices can be found by finite search because a compact operator has only finitely many eigenvalues above any positive lower cutoff. Its spectral projectors on these intervals are computable by a resolvent contour or polynomial approximation with the certified gap.

The projector ranks are finite and become certified when an approximating projector is within norm less than one of a known finite-rank projector. Project rational dense vectors into each block and use certified Gram-Schmidt to obtain a computable orthonormal frame for that exact finite spectral subspace. Every interval endpoint is strictly outside the spectrum; exact equal-eigenvalue decisions are avoided.

Round the new majorant upward on each retained spectral block to its upper endpoint, leaving the omitted low spectrum unchanged. Denote this operator $\bar{T}$. It commutes with $T$ and $J$, remains a strict contraction if endpoints are selected below $q''=(1+q')/2$, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\bar{T}^{2}\ge T^{2}\ge A_s^{2}, \\
&\operatorname{Tr}\bar{T}\le cS+\eta_{\mathrm{round}},
\end{aligned}
$$

provided the total rank times the block-width budget is at most $\eta_{\mathrm{round}}$. The head frames are now *exact eigenvectors of $\bar{T}$*, including any degenerate blocks. Their coefficients are computable reals and vectors; a requested finite numerical output includes explicit approximation enclosures. This is an actual admissible majorant and coefficient basis, not an arbitrary basis substituted into the old lemma.

Use $q''$, $cS+\eta_{\mathrm{round}}$ and the inherited low-spectrum tail in (2.4)-(2.5). The finite occupation head, its actual output Fock vectors and its coefficient functionals

$$
\phi_\mu(A)=\langle\xi_\mu,\exp(-b H_{\mathrm{phys}})A\, \Omega\rangle
$$

are now specified effectively. On supplied computable retained Weyl data the functionals are computed from finite symmetric-tensor overlaps and the source Gaussian characteristic function. An arbitrary unspecified operator A is not given a free numerical evaluation oracle.

##### 5. Exactly what this closes, and its complete production ledger

This supplies a constructive same-source output-side nuclear majorant, explicit quantitative tails, computable finite head vectors, and an admissible occupation representation with a proved (looser) capacity ceiling. It eliminates the exact spectral-join and individual-eigenvector-selection obstacle from this producer. It also proves termination of the scalar regional projection subroutine rather than labeling it an external input.

The following costs remain explicit and cannot be inferred small from rank or determinant estimates:

1. number of primal/dual regional-projection candidates and their Gram precisions in (3.2);
2. finite-rank Hermite quadrature, bounded-resolvent evaluations, spectral-block searches and all vector coefficients;
3. the number of occupations, $H=\binom{J+L}{L}$, if the finite tensor is fully expanded;
4. physical coherent preparation or access to each produced packet/function, all interfaces and any output-state/circuit synthesis;
5. source transport, physical clock comparison, control/storage/holding and every archived complete record.

A generating formula for a finite occupation sum is a legitimate succinct mathematical description. It is not evidence that enumerating that sum or physically accessing all its coefficients has zero cost. The all-inclusive polynomial tariff of F14 remains unproved for this producer. Conversely, its missing cost theorem is no longer a missing existence/effectivity theorem for the output spectral data. The source, gate, cost and implementation clauses stay separately typed.

<a id="proposition-f104f311-structured-correlated-gaussian-preparation-and-complete-flags"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.31.1 (Structured Correlated Gaussian Preparation and Complete Flags).**

##### 1. Frozen owner and inputs

The owner is Definition F.10.4f.3, items1–8. Item 7 requires

$$
C_{\delta,O} \le C_0 |\partial O|\, P(\log(1/\delta)) + C_1 \operatorname{Vol}_{\mathrm{active}}(O) + C_2 C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta),
$$

with **one polynomial and constants as branch data**. Item 8 separately requires code-corner embeddings, finite interface circuits, invariant ideal code algebras, and separate implementation bounds for state, GNS and phase-space norms. Qubit count alone is not its cost. F.10.4f.24 already provides a fixed-mode compiler with a changed, separately typed service clock; Proposition F.10.4f.31.1 does not identify that clock with the original lattice clock.

Use the actual canonical local coordinates of Proposition F.10.4f.30, Sections 1–6:

$$
\begin{aligned}
R&=(Q_1,\ldots,Q_r,P_1,\ldots,P_r),\quad [Q_i,P_j]=i\delta_{ij}, \\
V&=\operatorname{diag}(X,Y), \\
X_{ab}&=(\mu_0/2)\langle g_a,\omega^{-1}g_b\rangle, \\
Y_{ab}&=(1/(2\mu_0))\langle g_a,\omega g_b\rangle, \\
\omega(p)&=\sqrt{m^{2}+|p|^{2}},\quad m>0.
\end{aligned}
$$

The $g_i$ are the actual orthonormal local profiles, not spectral modes substituted for them. The Gaussian density $\rho_V$ is exactly the vacuum restriction to their type-I mode factor. Its restriction to $B_{r,n}$ is the faithful block state $D=(D_S)_S$ proved there. The physical Hamiltonian remains $d\Gamma(\omega)$, coupled to the complementary modes; none of the Gaussian preparation gates below is asserted to be that physical evolution.

The retained family for the positive circuit theorem is fixed before choosing its numerical tolerance: a fixed $r$, these exact first $r$ profiles, a fixed displacement radius $R$, and, when sums or protocols are requested, fixed bounds on term count, coefficient sum, cancellation floor, and protocol length. This is a bounded strong-star compact Weyl family, **not** the norm-dense linear span of all Weyl operators. The estimate does not hold uniformly on the union of all such families. Passing to a spatially richer compact family may require $r=r(O,\delta)$, and its residual modulus is a separate cost/input. All formulas retain that dependence. No tolerance-dependent deletion of tests from a fixed declared family is allowed.

Fix a certified $v\ge\max(1/2,\lVert V\rVert)$. Its uncertainty inequality implies

$$
V \ge (4v)^{-1} I.
\tag{1.1}
$$

For example, the Robertson inequality for unit vectors $x$ and $-Jx$ gives $\langle x,Vx\rangle\langle Jx,VJx\rangle\ge 1/4$, hence (1.1). This uses the vacuum-variance convention $I/2$.

A source-specific, directly computable upper bound avoids an unexplained covariance oracle. Put

$$
\Lambda_r^{2} = \lVert(\langle\nabla g_a,\nabla g_b\rangle)_{a,b\le r}\rVert.
$$

Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert X\rVert &\le \mu_0/(2m), \\
\lVert Y\rVert &\le \sqrt{m^{2}+\Lambda_r^{2}}/(2\mu_0), \\
v &= \max\bigl(1/2,\ \mu_0/(2m),\ \sqrt{m^{2}+\Lambda_r^{2}}/(2\mu_0)\bigr)
\end{aligned}
\tag{1.2}
$$

is valid. Indeed $\lVert\sum c_i g_i\rVert_2=\lVert c\rVert_2$; Cauchy–Schwarz for the positive operator $\omega$ gives $\langle f,\omega f\rangle\le\lVert f\rVert_2\lVert\omega f\rVert_2$. Thus $\kappa(V)\le 4v^2$. No geometric upper bound on $\Lambda_r$ for the prior Gram–Schmidt enumeration is inserted by assumption.

##### 2. A gap-free formula for an actual Gaussian purification

Let $J$ be the real symplectic matrix on the $r$ modes, $A=V^{1/2} J V^{1/2}$, and $Z=\operatorname{diag}(I_r,-I_r)$. Define

$$
\begin{aligned}
F &= [I + (1/4) A^{-2}]^{1/2}, \\
C &= V^{1/2} F V^{1/2}, \\
\Gamma &= \begin{bmatrix} V & C Z \\ Z C & Z V Z \end{bmatrix}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.1}
$$

The ordering in the doubled space is system $(Q,P)$ followed by ancillary $(Q,P)$. $A$ is invertible real skew-symmetric. Its positive singular values are the symplectic eigenvalues $\nu_i\ge 1/2$; consequently $0\le F\le I$. Formula (2.1) is well-defined even when some symplectic eigenvalues coincide or equal $1/2$.

##### Lemma 2.1

$\Gamma$ is a pure covariance on $2r$ modes, its system marginal is $V$, and

$$
\lVert\Gamma\rVert \le 2v,\qquad \Gamma \ge (8v)^{-1} I.
\tag{2.2}
$$

**Proof.** In a Williamson frame $V=S D S^{\mathsf T}$, with $S J S^{\mathsf T}=J$ and $D=\operatorname{diag}(\nu_1,\dots,\nu_r,\nu_1,\dots,\nu_r)$, one has

$$
C=S\, (D^{2}-I/4)^{1/2}\, S^{\mathsf T}.
$$

For verification without presuming that matrix square roots commute with congruence: choose an orthogonal $O$ with $A=O D J O^{\mathsf T}$ and $S=V^{1/2} O D^{-1/2}$. Then $F=O(I-D^{-2}/4)^{1/2}O^{\mathsf T}$, which proves the displayed expression for $C$. Pairing each Williamson mode with an ancillary copy produces the usual two-mode pure covariance with entries $\nu_i$ and $\sqrt{\nu_i^2-1/4}$, and ancillary momentum reversal $Z$ gives (2.1). Equivalently direct multiplication yields $\Gamma(J\oplus J)\Gamma=(J\oplus J)/4$. This proves purity and the marginal assertion. Since $\lVert C\rVert\le v$, the norm of the two-by-two operator block matrix is at most $2v$; purity implies the reciprocal symplectic bound in (2.2). ∎

This formula needs inverses of $V$ and $A$, whose smallest singular values are bounded by (1.1) and $1/2$, respectively. The only potentially non-Lipschitz operation is the positive square root of $I+A^{-2}/4$ at zero; it is continuous with a square-root modulus. Thus a demand for an inverse minimum symplectic-eigenvalue **gap** is artificial here. It does not follow that the original profile integrals are cheaply computable: their actual production cost is still charged.

##### Lemma 2.2: a bounded-energy Gaussian gate list

A purification with covariance $\Gamma$ can be produced from vacuum by at most $G\le 10(2r)^2$ one- and two-mode Gaussian primitives. At every intermediate ideal step its centered covariance has norm at most

$$
w=2v.
\tag{2.3}
$$

**Proof.** The positive matrix $T=(2\Gamma)^{1/2}$ is symplectic. A positive symplectic matrix has a Bloch–Messiah decomposition $T=K D K^{\mathsf T}$, with $K$ orthogonal symplectic and reciprocal diagonal entries of $D$. The initial $K^{\mathsf T}$ fixes vacuum, so first apply the $2r$ single-mode squeezers $D$, then a passive interferometer $K$. All squeezer covariance eigenvalues are at most $\lVert T\rVert^2/2=\lVert\Gamma\rVert\le 2v$; applying them one at a time preserves this bound. A passive gate preserves the covariance norm, including when the interferometer is split into pair rotations and phase shifts. Ordinary complex Givens elimination on $U(2r)$ supplies fewer than a quadratic number of those primitives. The conservative displayed constant covers phase gates. ∎

Only the finite covariance is synthesized. This is not a factorization of the scalar physical Hamiltonian and does not change its coupling or clock.

##### 3. Finite compression with complete failure records

Set

$$
\begin{aligned}
z&=1+1/[2(w+1)], \\
t_K&=4 z^{-K}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.1}
$$

For any ideal one- or two-mode marginal encountered in Lemma 2.2, the Gaussian occupation estimate from the prior exhaustion gives

$$
\Pr(\text{one of those occupations} \ge K) \le t_K.
\tag{3.2}
$$

Indeed the event is contained in $N_1+N_2\ge K$, and the two-mode moment bound is $4z^{-K}$; the one-mode estimate is smaller. The bound applies to both the input and output of each primitive because (2.3) holds at both steps.

Let $P$ be the cutoff $0,\dots,K-1$ on the participating one or two modes and $U$ the ideal primitive. Its compression $A_U=PUP$ is a contraction on dimension at most $K^2$. Implement its Halmos dilation on that finite space with a fresh success/failure bit. Read and keep the bit, retain the failure environment, and perform no postselection. All branches continue as a trace-preserving instrument; after a failure any fixed padded continuation may be used and remains in the record.

##### Theorem 3.1: complete-record approximation

There is such a finite instrument whose complete dephased-flag record, including the final purification register and retained environments, differs in trace norm from the ideal Gaussian purification with all success bits zero by at most

$$
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{trunc}} \le 8G \sqrt{t_K} = 16G\, z^{-K/2}.
\tag{3.3}
$$

Thus

$$
K \ge [2/\log z]\, \log(16G/\varepsilon_{\mathrm{trunc}})
\tag{3.4}
$$

suffices. One may increase `K` to at least `n+1` for the subsequent cutoff interface. In particular,

$$
K=O(n+(v+1) \log(G/\varepsilon_{\mathrm{trunc}})).
\tag{3.5}
$$

**Proof.** Embed the truncated finite space in the full oscillator space. If $\psi$ is an ideal intermediate vector, then

$$
\lVert(PUP-U)\psi\rVert \le \lVert(I-P)\psi\rVert+\lVert(I-P)U\psi\rVert \le 2\sqrt{t_K}.
$$

The first inequality follows by writing the difference as $PU(P-I)\psi+(P-I)U\psi$; no operator-norm approximation of the infinite unitary is claimed. Contractive telescoping gives for the unnormalized all-success final vector $\eta$

$$
e:=\lVert\eta-\psi_{\mathrm{final}}\rVert \le 2G\sqrt{t_K}.
$$

Its probability is $\lVert\eta\rVert^2$. The sum of the probabilities of all failure records is exactly $1-\lVert\eta\rVert^2\le 2e$, because the complete finite instrument is trace preserving. In the success block

$$
\bigl\lVert\, |\eta\rangle\langle\eta|-|\psi_{\mathrm{final}}\rangle\langle\psi_{\mathrm{final}}|\, \bigr\rVert_1 \le 2e.
$$

Failure blocks are orthogonal to the ideal all-success flag record and have total trace at most `2e`. Adding gives `4e`, proving (3.3). This is a comparison of complete instruments, not a renormalized success amplitude. ∎

There is a separate coherent-dilation vector estimate, useful when a GNS/unnormalized-vector implementation error is requested. Before the flags are dephased, let $\Psi_{\mathrm{impl}}$ be the normalized full finite-dilation vector, and compare with $\psi_{\mathrm{final}}\otimes|\text{all success}\rangle$ in the common oscillator/flag embedding. Their overlap is $\langle\psi_{\mathrm{final}},\eta\rangle$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert\Psi_{\mathrm{impl}}-\psi_{\mathrm{final}}\otimes|\text{all success}\rangle\rVert^{2} \\
&=2-2\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{\mathrm{final}},\eta\rangle\le 2e, \\
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{vec}} &\le 2\sqrt{2G}\, z^{-K/4}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.8}
$$

Thus one may impose the additional selector

$$
K \ge [4/\log z]\, \log(2\sqrt{2G}/\varepsilon_{\mathrm{vec}}).
\tag{3.9}
$$

Coherent finite-gate errors add at most `e_gate` to this vector bound. Applying the cutoff-channel isometry below preserves it; tracing/dephasing contracts the corresponding state distance. This is a vector comparison in the explicitly chosen Gaussian purification and flag representation. Identifying it with the original scalar register's physical response still uses the separately charged GNS/polar/source comparison. A small recorded failure probability alone was not used as a vector-error identity.

The chosen finite binary code support, including the interface ancillas, is invariant under the finite Halmos unitaries. Unused binary-carrier levels can carry identity. This support statement alone does not assert that every preparation unitary normalizes the regional direct-sum algebra or discharges the full original source code-invariance predicate. Leakage out of the ideal infinite Gaussian occupations is already represented by the explicit failure record; hardware/code leakage has its own implementation error, not just its probability.

##### Finite primitive synthesis and its costs

Each one/two-mode compression has at most $K^4$ entries. Each is a coefficient of a Gaussian coherent-state kernel in at most four variables. Fixed-variable coefficient recursion to degree at most $4K$, factorial scaling, and finite arithmetic produce all these entries with precision polynomial in $K$ and the requested bit precision, **given certified primitive parameters**. A conservative coefficient bit budget is polynomial in $K$, parameter-bit length, and $\log(G/\varepsilon_{\mathrm{gate}})$; cancellations are handled by absolute interval bounds, not by a presumed relative-error condition number.

After a certified contraction rescaling, matrix square roots give its finite Halmos unitary. Square-root continuity permits squared input-error allocations; it does not introduce an inverse spectral-gap oracle. A dense $2K^2$-dimensional unitary has $O(K^4)$ two-level factors. Standard binary Gray-code synthesis gives the conservative bound

$$
N_{\mathrm{gates}} \le c\, G K^{4} (1+\log K)^{3}
\tag{3.6}
$$

for one/two-qubit operations with unrestricted qubit connectivity. Nearest-neighbor routing multiplies this by at most a linear factor in the number of live/archived qubits if no better layout is supplied. This is intentionally not a native optical-gate tariff. All rotations must be compiled to the nominated finite-precision service set, adding its actual synthesis cost.

If the coherent errors in these finite unitary dilations sum to $e_{\mathrm{gate}}$, their complete instrument channel error in diamond norm is at most $2e_{\mathrm{gate}}$. Classical flags may be retained or communicated rather than discarded; both their storage and communication cost are charged. No replacement of complete records by successful branches occurs.

The quantum workspace, before counting the compiler's classical work, is

$$
O(r \log K+G) \text{ qubits},
\tag{3.7}
$$

including the purification modes and archived binary Gaussian-compression flags. The cutoff channel below adds $O(r\log K)$ environment bits. Routing, control strengths/energies, actual durations, clean-ancilla supply, readout, and record holding are additional tariff entries; (3.6) alone is not $C_{\delta,O}$.

##### 4. Exact finite-algebra restriction without an exponential density listing

For one oscillator define the Schrödinger channel to $h_n=\mathbb{C}^n\oplus\mathbb{C}|\mathrm{tail}\rangle$ by the isometry

$$
\begin{aligned}
|j\rangle &\mapsto |j\rangle|0\rangle &&\text{if } j<n, \\
|j\rangle &\mapsto |\mathrm{tail}\rangle|j+1\rangle &&\text{if } j\ge n.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.1}
$$

Tracing its environment erases low/high cross terms, keeps the low matrix, and sends all high diagonal mass to the scalar tail label. Tensor this over the $r$ modes, denoting the channel by $C_n^{\otimes r}$. The output density is block diagonal for $(M_n\oplus\mathbb{C})^{\otimes r}$. Its blocks are exactly the $D_S$ sums in Section 5 of the prior exhaustion.

Consequently applying (4.1) to the system half of the Gaussian purification prepares the **actual restricted state**, rather than a substitute state. On finite input levels $<K$, a comparator, conditional level transfer, and retained reset environment implement (4.1) with reversible arithmetic polynomial in $r\log K$; (4.1) is injective and extends to a finite unitary. Its actual gate synthesis and flag/storage costs are paid.

Trace-norm contractivity gives

$$
\lVert D_{\mathrm{impl}}-D\rVert_1 \le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{trunc}} + 2e_{\mathrm{gate}} + \varepsilon_{\mathrm{param}} + \varepsilon_{\mathrm{cut}},
\tag{4.2}
$$

where $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{param}}$ is the actual certified purification-parameter error, and $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cut}}$ covers finite implementation of (4.1). The exact ideal $D$ remains faithful. If the implemented approximate density must itself be faithful, mix a paid probability $a>0$ of the maximally mixed state on $(\mathbb{C}^{n+1})^{\otimes r}$. This adds at most $2a$ in trace norm and gives every block eigenvalue at least $a/(n+1)^r$. It is an implementation perturbation; it is not claimed equal to the exact vacuum restriction. Preparing this extra product mixture does not require listing $(n^2+1)^r$ numbers.

A certificate for $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{param}}$ can be obtained without eigenvector-gap assumptions. If $\Gamma'$ is the pure covariance of the implemented ideal Gaussian parameter list and $\lVert\Gamma'-\Gamma\rVert\le\xi$, then, with $m_{\mathrm{aux}}=2r$ and (2.2),

$$
\begin{aligned}
\bigl\lVert\, |\psi_{\Gamma'}\rangle\langle\psi_{\Gamma'}|-|\psi_\Gamma\rangle\langle\psi_\Gamma|\, \bigr\rVert_1 \\
&\le 2 \sqrt{8 r v \xi}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.3}
$$

To verify this sufficient bound, Gaussian overlap is $|\langle\psi_{\Gamma'},\psi_\Gamma\rangle|^2=\det(\Gamma+\Gamma')^{-1/2}$. Since $\det(2\Gamma)=1$ and $\lVert(2\Gamma)^{-1/2}(\Gamma'-\Gamma)(2\Gamma)^{-1/2}\rVert\le 4v\xi$, the determinant is at most $(1+4v\xi)^{4r}$. Thus the squared overlap is at least $(1+4v\xi)^{-2r}\ge 1-8rv\xi$; the pure-state trace-norm formula gives (4.3). A negative last lower bound is harmless; one can take the minimum with the trivial distance 2. The unknown overall purification phase does not matter.

##### 5. The actual retained Weyl interface has tensor-size circuits

Let the retained test be $W=\prod_{i=1}^r W_i$, with each canonical displacement bounded by $\lVert d_i\rVert\le R$. Retain exactly the normal UCP cutoff of the prior exhaustion, using the level-$n$ tail state:

$$
E_{i,n}(A)=P_n A P_n+\langle n|A|n\rangle(I-P_n).
$$

Set $B_i=(P_n W_i P_n,\langle n|W_i|n\rangle)\in M_n\oplus\mathbb{C}$ and $B(W)=\bigotimes_i B_i$. Each $B_i$ is a contraction on $\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$. A local Halmos dilation implements it with the complete success/failure instrument; the product has $r$ such dilations. Compression entries are one-mode displaced-oscillator coefficients, hence can be computed by the same fixed-variable recursion. The scalar value requires level $n$, explaining $K\ge n+1$ above. The circuit and matrix-production costs are polynomial in $r,n,R$ and logarithmic numerical precision, rather than in the dimension of the full tensor-product algebra. Put

The already proved source-GNS and adjoint-GNS estimates give

&\lVert(W^{*}-j(B(W))^{*})\Omega\rVert \le 4r \sqrt{C_R}\, z_0^{-n/2}.

Thus

$$
n \ge [2/\log z_0]\, \log(4r \sqrt{C_R}/\delta_{\mathrm{core}})
\tag{5.2}
$$

is an explicit uniform selector. Heat contraction makes (5.1) valid after $\exp(-\beta H)$ for every $\beta\ge 0$; it does not simulate that heat operation. A finite Weyl word is a phase times one displacement. Sums have their declared coefficient $\ell^1$ factor and cancellation-floor factor; linear-combination circuit synthesis also pays the number of terms and its preparation costs.

These are the same finite-mode retained tests and actual state as before. For a test whose data is outside the first `r`-mode span, spatial residual error must still be supplied. There is no assertion of operator-norm Weyl continuity, no arbitrary unit-ball GNS approximation, and no finite-register clock substitution.

For a protocol of $q$ declared finite instruments, a state-preparation trace error $e_{\mathrm{state}}$ and complete-instrument diamond errors $e_1,\dots,e_q$ give full joint-record trace error at most

$$
e_{\mathrm{state}} + \sum_{j=1}^{q} e_j.
\tag{5.3}
$$

This follows by CPTP contraction and telescoping on system, environments and classical registers. It does **not** follow that the infinite physical protocol is approximated merely because its individual Weyl contractions satisfy (5.1). That additional comparison needs its actual composed effects and the original-source dynamics, exactly as in F.10.4f.24.

##### 6. What the quantum bound does and does not price

For these structured state/interface operations the explicit bound has the form

$$
\begin{aligned}
C_{\mathrm{struct}} &\le Q_{\mathrm{cov}}(r,p) + Q_{\mathrm{dec}}(r,p,v) \\
&\quad + \operatorname{Poly}(r,K,n,p,R) \times \text{service/routing tariff} \\
&\quad + \text{charged preparation, archive and holding costs}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6.1}
$$

Here `p` is the certified working bit precision, including the coefficient and square-root error allocations. `Q_cov` is the actual cost of the covariance integrals on the actual profiles. `Q_dec` is the cost of producing and checking the symplectic/passive gate parameters of Lemma 2.2 to the residual (4.3). Formula (2.1) removes an exact eigenbasis or a minimum symplectic-gap oracle; it does not license writing zero in either ledger entry. The finite-dimensional decompositions are computable and their residuals are checkable. Proposition F.10.4f.31.1 does not assert a uniform bit-complexity theorem for the exact prior profile enumeration or its chosen decomposition implementation.

For supplied covariance/gate certificates and polynomially priced finite-precision gates, the **quantum circuit size and its local matrix arithmetic** are one fixed polynomial in $r,v,n,R,\log(1/\varepsilon)$; the exponent does not grow with $r$. This is the improvement over the previous $K^{2r}$ state listing and arbitrary whole-register QR. Equations (1.2), (3.4), and (5.2) exhibit every analytic parameter on which that statement depends.

The following are not included in that partial bound and cannot be hidden in its constant:

1. A spatial approximation selector $r=r(O,\delta)$ for the actual retained compact test family, including shrinking collar dependence and profile derivatives $\Lambda_r$.
2. Original-register polar transport $W_{j,k}$, its Gram certificates, output matrix production, conditioning, source-index selection, and synthesis. A structured Gaussian state preparation does not make this generally non-Gaussian polar map cheap.
3. The actual original physical heat and real-time instrument, including source-clock/light-cone and control-energy comparison. The Gaussian gates here are encoded services; their parameters are not the time variable of $d\Gamma(\omega)$.
4. Producing an explicit near-budget nuclear tensor. The finite rational enumeration from the prior theorem remains effective without a polynomial bound. A nuclear-norm bound is not a cheap certificate producer.
5. Actual selected-service durations, endpoint phases, resets, warm/clean carriers, flags, complete archives and memory holding. Unlimited-cost real arithmetic or infinitely precise analog gates are not primitive services.
6. Local PU-LAN, Hadamard-PCE cost admission, and physical source adoption. Mathematical Hadamardness/reflection positivity or a finite Gaussian density does not prove these resource predicates.

Even if $r,v$ were bounded by a polynomial in $\log(1/\delta)$ for a fixed region and $Q_{\mathrm{cov}},Q_{\mathrm{dec}}$ had the corresponding bound, obtaining one constant times **area**, plus the allowed active-volume and capacity terms, over an unbounded regional/collar family would still require its spatial tariff comparison. Polynomial dependence on volume is not automatically the linear-volume term in F14.

##### 1. Stable local coordinates

Fix a cube $Q=(0,l)^3$ with closure inside the time-zero base of $O$. Let

$$
\begin{aligned}
&g_j(x)=(2/l)^{3/2} \prod_{a=1}^{3} \sin(\pi j_a x_a/l)\, 1_Q(x), \\
&j \in \mathbb{N}^{3},\qquad \lambda_j=\pi^{2} |j|_2^{2}/l^{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

These are exactly orthonormal in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$, lie in $H_0^1(Q)$ after zero extension, and satisfy

$$
\langle\operatorname{grad} g_j,\operatorname{grad} g_k\rangle=\lambda_j \delta_{jk}.
$$

They need not be $C^\infty$ across the boundary of $Q$. This is harmless and is stated explicitly: approximation by $C_c^\infty(Q)$ in $H^1$ gives approximation in both required massive $H^{\pm1/2}$ Cauchy norms. Their Weyl operators therefore belong to the original local algebra $A(O)$. The free-space operator $\omega=(m^2-\Delta)^{1/2}$ is never replaced by the Dirichlet square root on $Q$.

For $1\le j_a\le F$ let $P_F$ be the real $L^2$ orthogonal projection, $r=F^3$, and use the canonical local coordinates from the previous exhaustion with reference scale $\mu>0$. Their actual covariance is

$$
\begin{aligned}
V_F&=\operatorname{diag}(X_F,Y_F), \\
(X_F)_{jk}&=(\mu/2)\langle g_j,\omega^{-1}g_k\rangle, \\
(Y_F)_{jk}&=(1/(2\mu))\langle g_j,\omega g_k\rangle.
\end{aligned}
$$

The source uncertainty relation and the diagonal gradient matrix give

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert V_F\rVert &\le v_F := \max\bigl(1/2,\ \mu/(2m),\ \sqrt{m^{2}+3 \pi^{2} F^{2}/l^{2}}/(2\mu)\bigr), \\
V_F &\ge (4v_F)^{-1} I,\qquad \operatorname{condition}(V_F)\le 4v_F^{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1.1}
$$

Thus the covariance norm is $O(F)$, and no Gram pivot or unexplained profile-enumeration conditioning is hidden. The exact finite Gaussian state is faithful because the original vacuum is separating for $A(O)$; its finite algebra restriction is likewise faithful.

##### 2. One fixed compact retained core, selected before accuracy

Fix $a>0$, $0<\alpha\le 1$, $R>0$, a maximum word length $\ell$, a finite sum count $q$, and a normalization floor $\eta>0$. The real Cauchy profiles obey the fixed ellipsoid bound

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_j \exp(2a |j|_\infty^{\alpha})\, (1+\lambda_j) \\
&\qquad (|g_j^{\mathrm{coeff}}|^{2}+|k_j^{\mathrm{coeff}}|^{2}) \le R^{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.1}
$$

Call the associated Weyl-word/sum family $G(Q,a,\alpha,R,\ell,q,\eta)$. Sums have coefficient $\ell^1$ norm at most one and are divided only by a certified norm at least $\eta$. Include adjoints and the identity. This family is fixed independently of $\delta$. It is compact in the two Cauchy norms. It has infinitely many independent spatial directions. Its generated local Weyl algebra is not finite-dimensional: every finite sine direction occurs with sufficiently small nonzero amplitude, and powers/rescaling generate its entire one-parameter Weyl group. The union of these directions is dense in the cube's real local Cauchy spaces. A compact retained set need not itself be a linear norm-dense unit ball.

For an effective tariff, use the following charged input convention, parallel to the admitted computational class in F.10.4f.24. A requested member supplies its coefficients through a certified producer whose complete description, arithmetic, communication and working-memory cost for the first $F^3$ coefficients at $p$-bit absolute accuracy is bounded by one fixed polynomial in $F,p$. Its envelope certificate is part of the query. Arbitrary unbounded descriptions or a free infinite oracle are not admitted. This is a restriction of the paid access grammar, not a claim about every possible description of every point of (2.1).

Let

$$
C_m=\sqrt{(m^{-1}+m+1)/2},\qquad U=C_m\, \ell R.
$$

For a word's summed Cauchy data, its original one-particle packet h and truncated packet $h_{F}$ satisfy

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert h\rVert &\le U,\qquad \lVert h-h_F\rVert \le e_F:=U \exp(-a F^{\alpha}), \\
\lVert h_F\rVert &\le U+e_F.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.2}
$$

Indeed the omitted $H^1$ norm squared is at most $(\ell R)^2\exp(-2aF^{\alpha})$, and the two free-space Cauchy multipliers are bounded by $C_{m}$ from this $H^1$ norm. The sum/normalization factor is at most $1/\eta$. A sufficient selector is

$$
F=\max\bigl(1,\lceil[a^{-1} \log_+(U/\epsilon_{\mathrm{sp}})]^{1/\alpha}\rceil\bigr).
\tag{2.3}
$$

In particular $r=O(\log(1/\delta)^{3/\alpha})$, unlike the fixed finite Sobolev core, whose required mode count is polynomial in $1/\delta$. The earlier Sobolev lower bound is respected.

##### 3. The actual full-domain UCP map and the spatial error

The finite regular CCR factor $M_{F}$ generated by these canonical pairs is type I and has a tensor decomposition $H=K_F\otimes K_{F}'$. Use the actual vacuum marginal on its commutant as a normal state $\sigma_{c}$. Define

$$
E_F=\mathrm{id}_{B(K_F)} \otimes \sigma_c.
$$

This is a full-domain normal UCP map on $B(H)$ onto $M_{F}$. For real Cauchy data, the $L^2$ residuals are symplectically orthogonal to the retained coordinates. Therefore the Weyl factors commute and

$$
E_F(W(h))=\exp(-\lVert h-h_F\rVert^{2}/2)\, W(h_F).
\tag{3.1}
$$

This equality uses the actual Gaussian vacuum characteristic function on the commuting residual Weyl factor. It does not assume that the joint vacuum on $M_{F}$ and its commutant is a product, nor that $E_{F}$ preserves its correlations.

The original Weyl vacuum estimate gives

$$
\lVert[W(h)-E_F W(h)]\Omega\rVert \le (1+U+e_F)e_F+e_F^{2}/2.
\tag{3.2}
$$

It also holds for adjoints. The first term compares $W(h)$ and $W(h_F)$; the second uses $1-\exp(-x)\le x$. Weyl-word phases are calculated from the actual finite/free-space symplectic form and included as controlled phases.

Apply the previous mode cutoff with a specified level-n tail state:

$$
\begin{aligned}
E_{i,n}(A)&=P_n A P_n+\langle n|A|n\rangle\, (1-P_n), \\
\pi_{F,n}&=\Bigl(\bigotimes_i E_{i,n}\Bigr) E_F, \\

$$

Both interfaces are normal UCP; $\iota$ is the actual unital inclusion. The exact finite state is $\omega_{F,n}=\omega$ composed with $\iota$, not a product of individual marginals. No canonical collar unitary is needed for these retained interfaces. The already proved same-net split factor independently supplies the required collar inclusion.

Let $R_{d}$ be the fixed bound on the canonical displacement coordinates of a summed retained word. One may take a fixed conservative multiple of $\sqrt{\mu+\mu^{-1}}\,\ell R$, according to the source Weyl normalization. Set

z_F&=1+1/[2(v_F+1)], \\

The prior Gaussian occupation proof applies to the actual marginals, including their correlations, and gives

&\le \bigl[ (1+U+e_F)e_F+e_F^{2}/2+e_{\mathrm{occ}} \bigr]/\eta.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.3}
$$

The vacuum expectation error is bounded by the same quantity. Applying $\exp(-\beta H_{\mathrm{phys}})$ contracts this vector bound for every $\beta\ge 0$. Thus (3.3) gives the declared retained test norm for the physical heat-map comparison uniformly on any retained window. It does not assert full-regional projective convergence of these particular $E_{F}$ maps.

For example choose $\epsilon_{\mathrm{sp}}\le\min(1,\eta\delta_0/[8(2+U)])$ and

n=\bigl\lceil[2/\log z_F]\, \log(8r \sqrt{C_d}/(\eta \delta_0))\bigr\rceil.
\tag{3.4}
$$

Then (3.3) is at most $\delta_{0}$. Every cutoff and covariance constant is now explicitly controlled as r grows.

##### 4. An efficient producer of the actual free-space covariance

Here is a direct algorithm, not a Dirichlet-covariance substitution. For real f,g in L2 put

$$
\begin{aligned}
K(f,g)&=\langle f,\omega^{-1}g\rangle \\
&=\pi^{-1/2} \int_{\mathbb{R}} \exp(y/2-m^{2} \exp(y)) \\
&\qquad \langle f,\exp(\exp(y) \Delta)g\rangle\, dy.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.1}
$$

For $g_{j}$ and their first distributional derivatives, these are products of one-dimensional sines/cosines on (0,l). Because $g_{j}$ vanishes at the boundary, its first distributional derivatives have no boundary $\delta$. Integration in momentum gives the exact identity

$$
\begin{aligned}
\langle g_j,\omega g_k\rangle \\
&=m^{2} K(g_j,g_k)+\sum_{a=1}^{3} K(\partial_a g_j,\partial_a g_k).
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.2}
$$

The free heat kernel is a product, so each three-dimensional heat pairing in (4.1) is a product of three one-dimensional pairings.

##### 4.1 Certified outer sinc rule

For $\lVert f\rVert\lVert g\rVert\le B$, the integrand of (4.1) is analytic in $|\operatorname{Im} y|<\pi/2$. On the lines $\operatorname{Im} y=\pm d$, $d=\pi/4$, its integrated absolute value is at most

$$
B/[m \sqrt{\cos d}].
$$

This follows from $\lVert\exp(\exp(y+id)\Delta)\rVert\le 1$ and the elementary $\gamma$ integral. The usual rectangular-contour proof of the trapezoidal rule (integrate the cotangent sampling kernel, close at real endpoints and use the decaying tails) consequently gives the explicit conservative bound

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Bigl|K-h \sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}} f(kh)\Bigr| \\
&\le 4B/[m \sqrt{\cos d}\,(\exp(2\pi d/h)-1)].
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.3}
$$

The omitted left integral is at most 2B exp(-T_-/2)/sqrt(pi); the discrete left tail is bounded by

$$
h B \exp(-(N_-+1)h/2) / [\sqrt{\pi}(1-\exp(-h/2))].
$$

For the right discrete tail use monotonicity after $m^2\exp(y)\ge 1$ and the positive bound $\exp(y/2-m^2\exp(y))$; its integral is $B m^{-1}\operatorname{erfc}(m\exp(y/2))$, and the first omitted sample adds the stated elementary integrand bound times $h$. These formulas directly select $h,N_-,N_+$ for any allocation $\epsilon$. They give

$$
\begin{aligned}
h^{-1}&=O(p+\log(1+B)), \\
N_-+N_++1&=O((p+\log(1+B))^{2}),
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.4}
$$

at $p$ bits for fixed $m$. Extremely large $t=\exp(kh)$ values are skipped once their explicit positive bound is below the remaining tail allocation. Thus needed $t$ satisfy $t=O((p+\log(1+B))/m^2)$, whereas $\log(1/t_{\min})=O(p+\log(1+B))$.

No equality or rank-decision oracle enters the stopping criteria. All exponential/square-root constants may be enclosed outward by ordinary rational intervals.

##### 4.2 Efficient one-dimensional heat pairings

For $a,b$ each a normalized sine or cosine with frequency at most $\pi F/l$, set, for $0\le z\le l$,

$$
C_{ab}(z)=\int_0^{l-z} a(x+z)\,b(x)\, dx.
$$

Product-to-sum makes $C_{ab}$ a finite sum of trigonometric terms and z times trigonometric terms. If two frequencies coincide, use the limiting linear formula directly; otherwise the nonzero frequency denominator is at least pi/l. No small uncontrolled divisor appears. The exact heat pairing is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\langle a,\exp(t \Delta)b\rangle \\
&=\pi^{-1/2} \int_0^{l/(2\sqrt{t})} \exp(-u^{2}) \\
&\qquad [C_{ab}(2\sqrt{t}\,u)+C_{ba}(2\sqrt{t}\,u)]\, du.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.5}
$$

Truncate $u$ at $U_p=\sqrt{p\log 2+\log(C(1+B)(p+2))}$, with a conservative fixed $C$ sufficient for the Gaussian tail allocation. Since $|C_{ab}|\le\lVert a\rVert\lVert b\rVert$, the omitted absolute tail is explicitly bounded by $B\operatorname{erfc}(U_p)$. The remaining interval length is at most $U_{p}$. Its integrand is an entire exponential-trigonometric polynomial of fixed structural size. Its frequency is at most $2\pi F\sqrt{t}/l$, with $t$ bounded as in Section 4.1.

To make the complexity assertion elementary, rescale the remaining interval to $[0,1]$ and enclose its Taylor polynomial. For a term $z^{j}\exp(-Az^2+iB_0z)$, $j\le 1$, the circle $|z|\le 2$ has modulus at most $2\exp(4A+2|B_0|)$. Cauchy's estimate gives a uniform degree-$N$ remainder at most $4\exp(4A+2|B_0|)\,2^{-N}$. Here $A\le U_p^2=O(p+\log(1+B))$ and $|B_0|\le CF\sqrt{t}\,U_p$. Consequently degree

$$
N=O(p+\log(1+B)+F \sqrt{t}\, U_p)
\tag{4.6}
$$

suffices. Coefficients are obtained by the finite quadratic-exponential recursion and integrated exactly as polynomial coefficients. Precision must exceed the target bits plus $O(N+F\sqrt{t}U_p)$; this controls cancellation absolutely. This is polynomial in $F,p$ for fixed $m,l$. An interval implementation may instead use equivalent high-order Gaussian quadrature.

There are $r^{2}$ covariance entries, four negative-power pairings per $Y$ entry, $O(p^2)$ outer samples and three fixed-dimensional heat factors per sample. Derivative norms have $B=O(F^2)$. Equations (4.3)-(4.6), elementary interval arithmetic, and (4.2) therefore produce $V_{F}$ to entry error $2^{-p}$ in a number of bit operations and working bits bounded by a fixed polynomial in $F,p$. Operator error at most $\xi$ follows by assigning entry error $\xi/(2r)$. This includes the actual matrix production and its checker, without exponentially long density output.

norm at most $2v_F$ and at most $G\le 40r^2$ elementary one/two-mode Gaussian primitives. A repeated symplectic eigenvalue needs no inverse eigenvalue gap. Numerical output is validated by its reconstructed covariance, not by claimed convergence of individual eigenvectors.
