##### 6. Code, errors, and the scoped complete service ledger

There is an explicit full-matrix code variant that avoids confusing support invariance with normalization of a regional direct-sum algebra. Let $a_F=(n+1)^r$, let $B_0=(M_n\oplus\mathbb{C})^{\otimes r}$ act on $\mathbb{C}^{a_F}$, and let $\mathrm{Zpin}:M_{a_F}\to B_0$ be central-block pinching. Replace the finite certificate algebra by

For a fixed maximum number $q_{\mathrm{call}}$ of retained operations and bounded holding intervals, the ledger contains:

A conservative logical gate count is

\tag{6.1}
$$

before finite-set synthesis and routing. Space is $O(r\log K+q_{\mathrm{call}}G)$ plus the explicitly polynomial arithmetic workspace; line routing costs at most their sum as an additional multiplicative factor. All these quantities are polynomial in $F,p,n,K$. The previous finite-precision tariff charges every listed item by a fixed nonnegative polynomial in these quantities and their bits; bounded holding intervals and sequential gate duration multiply polynomial quantities and preserve that property.

For accuracy $\delta$, Sections 1-5 give

$$
\begin{aligned}
&F=O(\log(1/\delta)^{1/\alpha}),\quad r=F^{3},\quad v_F=O(F), \\
&n,K=\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta)),\quad p=\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta)).
\end{aligned}
\tag{6.2}
$$

<a id="lemma-f104f312a-purification-precision-and-total-code-completion"></a>**Lemma F.10.4f.31.2a (Purification Precision and Total-Code Completion).**

##### 1. Covariance precision is propagated through the purification

In the Gevrey producer, $\xi$ in the Gaussian overlap estimate means error in the **doubled pure covariance Gamma**, not error directly in V. The following explicit modulus supplies that missing precision allocation.

Let $V,V'$ be physical covariances with norms at most $s\ge 1$ and let $\eta=\lVert V-V'\rVert$. Their uncertainty relation gives $V,V'\ge(4s)^{-1}I$. Set $B=V^{1/2}$, $A=BJB$, $F=[I+A^{-2}/4]^{1/2}$, $C=BFB$, with primes for $V'$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert B-B'\rVert&\le\sqrt{s}\, \eta, \\
\lVert A-A'\rVert&\le 2s \eta, \\
\lVert A^{-1}\rVert,\ \lVert A'^{-1}\rVert&\le 2, \\
\lVert A^{-1}-A'^{-1}\rVert&\le 8s \eta, \\
\lVert A^{-2}-A'^{-2}\rVert&\le 32s \eta, \\
\lVert F-F'\rVert&\le\sqrt{8s \eta}, \\
\lVert C-C'\rVert&\le 2s \eta+s \sqrt{8s \eta}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The square-root estimate for B uses its positive spectral lower bound; the one for F is the operator square-root Holder inequality and requires no minimum symplectic gap above 1/2. The real skew A has singular values equal to the symplectic eigenvalues, which are at least 1/2, proving its inverse bound. The other inequalities follow by the two-factor product identities.

For the doubled pure covariance this yields

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert\Gamma(V)-\Gamma(V')\rVert \\
&\le(1+2s)\eta+s \sqrt{8s \eta}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1.1}
$$

Consequently target pure-covariance error $\xi$ is attained by

$$
\eta\le\min\{1,\ \xi/[2(1+2s)],\ \xi^{2}/(32s^{3})\}.
\tag{1.2}
$$

A computed symmetric covariance $\hat V$ with $\lVert\hat V-V\rVert\le\epsilon$ becomes a physical covariance by adding $\epsilon I$: $\hat V+\epsilon I\ge V$ in the uncertainty-matrix order. Its error is at most $2\epsilon$. Use $s=v_F+1$ and choose $\epsilon\le\eta/2$ and $\epsilon\le 1/2$. Entry precision $\epsilon/(2r)$ suffices. The added inflation, its parameter bits and its actual Gaussian preparation perturbation are charged. Equations (1.1)-(1.2) show that the input bit budget stays polynomial in $r,\log v_{F}$ and $\log(1/\xi)$, as needed by the growing-mode tariff.

##### Same-phase vector error

For two pure Gaussian covariances $\Gamma,\Gamma'$ with $\lVert\Gamma-\Gamma'\rVert\le\xi$ and the norm/inverse bounds in the structured compiler, the squared overlap satisfies

$$
|\langle\psi,\psi'\rangle|^{2}\ge 1-8r s \xi.
$$

After aligning their overlap to be real and nonnegative,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert\psi-\psi'\rVert&\le 4\sqrt{r s \xi}, \\
\bigl\lVert\, |\psi\rangle\langle\psi|-|\psi'\rangle\langle\psi'|\, \bigr\rVert_1&\le 2\sqrt{8r s \xi}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1.3}
$$

The vector bound follows from $2(1-F)\le 2(1-F^2)$, $F=|\langle\psi,\psi'\rangle|$. It is not deduced by treating trace distance as an identity for a fixed arbitrary phase.

The ideal purification (2.1) in the structured compiler is the standard vectorization $\sqrt{\rho_V}$. Choosing its vacuum coefficient positive identifies its phase. Two exact such purifications have the positive overlap $\operatorname{Tr}(\sqrt{\rho_V}\sqrt{\rho_{V'}})$. In a numerical Gaussian synthesis whose residual pure covariance is validated but whose phase is otherwise unspecified, explicitly compute the complex Gaussian overlap and apply its inverse phase before claiming the vector comparison. This is a finite determinant/Gaussian-kernel calculation on the doubled finite covariance. The overlap is bounded away from zero once $8rs\xi\le 1/2$; its argument can then be enclosed without a vanishing-overlap decision. The chosen finite Gaussian gate list fixes its own metaplectic phase, and that phase is included in this calculation. Its determinant arithmetic and final controlled phase are charged.

One can also avoid covariance-to-phase inference by charging the individual finite Gaussian primitive parameter errors directly in the coherent gate sum. Either implementation must use one of these actual phase certificates. To allocate errors $e_{\mathrm{vec,param}}$ and $e_{\mathrm{tr,param}}$ in (1.3), it suffices to take

$$
\xi\le\min\{1/(16rs),\ e_{\mathrm{vec,param}}^{2}/(16rs),\ e_{\mathrm{tr,param}}^{2}/(32rs)\}.
$$

This fixes the V-to-Gamma and same-phase parameter-error entries of the main Gaussian ledger.

##### 2. Spectral-block selection preserves the polynomial head rank

The clustered spectral producer must not let an unbounded degeneracy silently inflate the head rank. Let $T$ be the new positive trace-class majorant with $\operatorname{Tr}T\le S_T$ and an explicit analytic tail selector. For desired omitted trace $\epsilon>0$ choose $J$ with

$$
\sum_{j>J}t_j\le\epsilon/2.
$$

Choose a threshold $\theta$ in [epsilon/(4J),epsilon/(2J)] outside the spectrum, certifying its positive distance with the effective finite-rank operator-norm approximants. Such a threshold exists and can be found by the specified finite search. Its discarded trace obeys

$$
\sum_{t_j<\theta}t_j\le J \theta+\sum_{j>J}t_j\le\epsilon,
$$

and its retained rank satisfies

$$
\operatorname{rank} 1_{(\theta,\infty)}(T)\le S_T/\theta\le 4 S_T J/\epsilon.
\tag{2.1}
$$

All multiplicities are included. In particular the rank remains polynomial in 1/epsilon at fixed geometry because the earlier fixed-k Hermite tail selector makes J polynomial in 1/epsilon. A tight degeneracy requires keeping its entire block; (2.1) already prices it.

For spectral rounding on this head use the known rank upper bound $\bar R=\lceil 4S_T J/\epsilon\rceil$ and total interval-width budget $\eta_{\mathrm{round}}/\bar R$. This makes the total trace increase at most $\eta_{\mathrm{round}}$. Interval endpoints stay strictly below $q''<1$ and outside the spectrum. The head remains the same subspace, so subdividing spectral blocks does not increase its rank. All interval searches/precision costs remain charged, with no efficiency claim beyond the analytic rank bound.

The occupation cutoff $L=O(\log(1/\delta))$ and polynomial head-rank bound now imply explicitly

$$
\log H=\log\binom{J_{\mathrm{head}}+L}{L}=O(\log^{2}(1/\delta)),
$$

for the canonical Sobolev proof. This fills the head-rank step needed to preserve its final logarithmic-cube carrier estimate.

##### 3. The invariant code includes its auxiliary matrix factors

The signal algebra $\tilde B=M_{a_F}$, $a_F=(n+1)^r$, is not invariant as $\tilde B\otimes I$ under a unitary that entangles signal and ancillary registers. The invariant ideal code used by the implementation certificate is therefore defined explicitly as the **total** finite algebra

$$
B_{\mathrm{total}}=\tilde{B} \otimes M_{d_{\mathrm{aux}}},
$$

including every preparation, environment, failure-flag and working register touched by the retained finite circuits. This is a full matrix algebra on its code corner. Its faithful C8 embedding is the binary carrier embedding of that total space. Every compiled ideal unitary preserves this corner and its full algebra.

Extend all certificate maps, rather than silently changing the algebra. For a specified auxiliary density $\sigma_{\mathrm{aux}}$, define

$$
\begin{aligned}
\pi_{\mathrm{total}}(A)&=\tilde{\pi}(A) \otimes I_{\mathrm{aux}}, \\
\iota_{\mathrm{total}}(B)&=\tilde{\iota}[(\mathrm{id} \otimes \sigma_{\mathrm{aux}})(B)], \\
\omega_{\mathrm{total}}&=\tilde{\omega} \otimes \sigma_{\mathrm{aux}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.1}
$$

They are UCP, $\omega_{\mathrm{total}}=\omega$ composed with $\iota_{\mathrm{total}}$, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
\iota_{\mathrm{total}}\, \pi_{\mathrm{total}}&=\tilde{\iota}\, \tilde{\pi}, \\
\omega_{\mathrm{total}}\, \pi_{\mathrm{total}}&=\tilde{\omega}\, \tilde{\pi}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the mathematical retained state/GNS/heat errors are unchanged. The finite-domain nuclear bound survives contractive UCP precomposition. There is no asserted injective original-net representation of every added auxiliary matrix entry; the original F14 interfaces are UCP. No F01 faithful local-net embedding is inferred.

If faithfulness of the entire finite state is required, choose

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\sigma_{\mathrm{aux}}=(1-\epsilon_{\mathrm{aux}})|\mathrm{ready}\rangle\langle\mathrm{ready}|+\epsilon_{\mathrm{aux}} I/d_{\mathrm{aux}}, \\
&0<\epsilon_{\mathrm{aux}}<1.
\end{aligned}
$$

Then $\omega_{\mathrm{total}}$ is faithful. The finite preparation is a paid mixture of the ready state and a maximally mixed product state. Relative to the clean-ancilla circuit, its trace-norm implementation perturbation is at most $2\epsilon_{\mathrm{aux}}$. A purification can be chosen with overlap at least $\sqrt{1-\epsilon_{\mathrm{aux}}}$, giving vector perturbation at most $\sqrt{2\epsilon_{\mathrm{aux}}}$. Choose $\epsilon_{\mathrm{aux}}$ inside the respective state and vector allocations; its mixing flag and environment are retained and already included in the total carrier. Additional ancillas used solely to purify this preparation can equivalently be included once in a larger total code at the outset; no recursive uncharged environment is needed because the prepared density, rather than its purification, is the finite state in the certificate.

All auxiliary dimensions, preparation costs, finite-map dimension factors, pulse/holding durations and memory are those of $B_{\mathrm{total}}$, not merely those of the signal algebra. Since the structured construction uses polynomially many auxiliary qubits, $\log\dim(B_{\mathrm{total}})$ remains polynomial in $\log(1/\delta)$ on the Gevrey branch. The canonical construction retains its actual, potentially much larger circuit/auxiliary cost and still makes no all-inclusive polynomial claim.

<a id="lemma-f104f312b-correlated-retained-output-cut-and-inflation-safe-selectors"></a>**Lemma F.10.4f.31.2b (Correlated Retained Output Cut and Inflation-Safe Selectors).**

##### 1. Three objects with distinct types

Write S for the signal register, A for every finite work, purification, restriction-environment and failure-flag register touched by the compiled finite circuit, and

where $\sigma_{A}$ is any explicitly specified finite density (strictly positive when desired). These UCP maps and the state are exact mathematical data. If a complete record is dephased, its complete trace-norm distance is at most 2 $e_{\mathrm{prep}}$, by trace-norm contractivity of that same record channel. A classical mixture can be handled by a charged purification/comparison flag. All phase conventions are those proved in the precision completion. ##### 2. The retained state and GNS comparisons

Definition F.10.4f.3 item 4 tests $\omega_{\mathrm{total}}$ only on $\pi_{\mathrm{total}}(x)$, for $x$ in the retained core. For the declared finite sums, apply the triangle inequality with their actual coefficient l1 bound (at most 1/eta). Apply the same argument to adjoints. ##### 3. What exactly is invariant

The code-corner embedding is of $B_{\mathrm{total}}$ itself as the full matrix algebra of its finite total corner. For the polynomial-bit tariff, all fixed numerical branch data (mass, lengths, reference frequency, Gevrey constants, normalization and protocol bounds) must admit polynomial-time certified precision routines. The map $V_{\mathrm{sig}}$ in the output-cut proof is isometric on the full GNS space of $(B_{\mathrm{signal}},\omega_{\mathrm{signal}})$ into the correlated purification's signal-cyclic space. Its next comparison with the original net is only on the earlier retained algebra

##### 2. Gate-by-gate invariant total code

After computing sufficient cutoffs $n_{\mathrm{req}},K_{\mathrm{req}}$, choose

<a id="lemma-f104f312d-computational-core-and-complete-instrument-domain"></a>**Lemma F.10.4f.31.2d (Computational Core and Complete-Instrument Domain).**

##### 1. What the frozen target actually permits

The broader regional realization requires full-regional finite-algebra, expanded-mode/collar geometric, LAN/Hadamard-cost, microscopic-clock and explicit nuclear-certificate records. Definition F.10.4f.3 specifies estimates on a declared retained test core $T_{O}$, a finite algebra and full-domain UCP maps. - a genuine growing-mode example, with infinitely many fixed spatial directions;
- not an enlargement of, or a uniform recovery theorem for, the previously selected Sobolev family;
- not by itself a discharge of the whole original target row.

The full-domain typing of the new $\pi$ is important but insufficient to change that last distinction. An input map defined on $A(O)$ is not automatically accurate on every point of its unit ball or on the old Sobolev family.

##### 2. Why accuracy-dependent smoothing cannot repair the product route

Fix the original smooth compact Sobolev family with $s>1/2$ and a support set containing a cube. Let $S_{\delta}$ be any preprocessing/smoothing map, including nonlinear or source-dependent choices. Suppose its output is ultimately recovered in an r(delta)-canonical-mode factor $M_{r}$, and suppose the complete operation $E_{\delta}$ satisfies the required uniform original GNS estimate

$$
\sup_{A\in T_{\mathrm{Sob}}} \lVert(A-E_\delta A)\Omega\rVert \le\delta.
$$

The previously proved basis-independent carrier theorem applies directly to $E_\delta$'s *final recovery range*, independent of what $S_{\delta}$ does internally. It gives

$$
r(\delta)\ge c\, \delta^{-3/(s+1/2)}.
\tag{2.1}
$$

For the faithful product algebra $(M_n\oplus\mathbb{C})^{\otimes r}$, even $n=1$ requires at least $r$ binary carriers. Under the original positive allocated-carrier tariff,

$$
C_\delta\ge c'\, \delta^{-3/(s+1/2)}.
\tag{2.2}
$$

Thus no smoothing, increasing Gevrey envelope, accuracy-dependent basis, compressed matrix-description format or improved Gaussian synthesis can transport the product-route polylogarithmic cost to that original fixed Sobolev family. This is an exact conditional consequence of the proved width theorem, not a claim that approximation by smooth functions is impossible. Smoothing can approximate it, but its required final mode census already violates this tariff.

This deduction also applies if one assigns two errors, a smoothing error delta/2 and a Gevrey compiler error delta/2: the triangle inequality would imply the antecedent above, so the same lower bound follows. Omitting the smoothing cost cannot avoid the carrier lower bound. Allowing active volume or capacity to acquire an unrecorded inverse-tolerance term changes the original fixed-region cost predicate.

The non-product canonical collar route is outside this theorem's faithful-product premise and remains a genuine possible route. The new bounded-resolvent nuclear producer and canonical-frame algorithm work toward that route without claiming that this exclusion settles it.

##### 3. Finite-list and complete-record scope

A finite list of predetermined local profiles admits a finite-dimensional span, so the fixed-mode theorem covers its spatial truncation exactly. Enlarging to the new Gevrey compact family covers an infinite-dimensional accuracy-dependent spatial resolution with one explicit modulus. Neither statement says that all profiles from the old Sobolev family have uniformly short descriptions.

For a fixed-length protocol consisting of retained Weyl unitaries, include every prefix displacement in the declared radius before selecting F,n. The original vacuum after each ideal prefix is a displaced Gaussian with that bounded mean. The same occupation and spatial estimates therefore apply at every prefix. If a finite contraction B approximates the ideal unitary U on such a vector $\psi$ by e, its complete Halmos dilation V obeys

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert V\psi-U\psi \otimes |\mathrm{success}\rangle\rVert^{2} \\
&=2-2 \operatorname{Re}\langle U\psi, B\psi\rangle \le 2e.
\end{aligned}
$$

Here the success overlap is the actual one, and the failure branch is kept. Contractive telescoping through $q_{\mathrm{call}}$ such dilations gives vector error at most $q_{\mathrm{call}}\sqrt{2e}$, and complete-record trace error at most twice that. Choosing $e\le\delta_{\mathrm{impl}}^2/(8q_{\mathrm{call}}^2)$ preserves the Gevrey polylogarithmic selectors. This supplies complete finite Weyl-unitary records with all failure flags; it is stronger than a success-conditioned response comparison.

For general sequential instruments, one must compare the actual composed effects or provide Stinespring control on the complete retained prefix family. A list of individual vacuum expectation errors is not such a theorem. No unrestricted instrument-completeness claim is inserted into the new producer. A requested expanded protocol class retains its actual effect/tail/description costs.

<a id="proposition-f104f313-actual-local-scalar-parity-qubit-lan-binding"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.31.3 (Actual Local Scalar Parity-Qubit LAN Binding).**

##### 1. The literal prerequisite

Definition F.10.4e.5 begins with a faithful **finite-dimensional** regular state family supporting a de Finetti extremal component. Its four clauses require: an identified finite-mode Gaussian tangent experiment; the root-fidelity normalization; parameter-independent two-way normal CPTP comparisons; and separate transported/cutoff polynomial-moment records. Theorems F.10.4e.8–e.10 prove such certificates for specified qubit families. Definition e.11 and Theorems e.12–e.13 supply their actual finite source, units, compilers and normal-response completion.

The source binding below therefore uses a true $M_{2}$ factor. Exact normal Gaussian copy mixing alone has a different source type and is proved separately in Proposition F.10.4f.31.3a.

##### 2. An exact qubit factor in the original local scalar algebra

Choose one nonzero real localized canonical profile from the actual local-mode factor of the original massive scalar construction. The same construction may use a fixed smooth compactly supported profile when smooth-state insertions are also required. Its vacuum covariance is $V=\operatorname{diag}(x,y)$, with $x,y>0$ and $\nu=\sqrt{xy}>1/2$. Strict inequality follows without a numerical eigenvalue-gap assumption: the actual vacuum is separating for the local algebra, hence its density on this type-I mode factor is faithful; a one-mode Gaussian with $\nu=1/2$ would be pure and not faithful.

The local canonical squeeze

$$
Q'=s Q,\qquad P'=P/s,\qquad s=(y/x)^{1/4}
$$

has covariance $\nu I_2$. In its actual local oscillator representation the vacuum marginal is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\tau_p&=(1-p) \sum_{n\ge 0} p^{n} |n\rangle\langle n|, \\
p&=(\nu-1/2)/(\nu+1/2) \in (0,1).
\end{aligned}
$$

The unitary occupation relabeling

$$
J |2k+b\rangle = |b\rangle \otimes |k\rangle,\quad b=0,1,
$$

gives the exact identity

$$
\begin{aligned}
J \tau_p J^{*}&=\operatorname{diag}(\mu,1-\mu) \otimes \tau_{p^{2}}, \\
\mu&=1/(1+p)=1/2+1/(4\nu).
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.1}
$$

For a,b in {0,1}, the strong sums

$$
e_{ab}=\sum_{k\ge 0}|2k+a\rangle\langle 2k+b|
$$

are matrix units with $e_{00}+e_{11}=I$. They define a normal faithful unital embedding $\beta:M_2\to M_{\mathrm{mode}}\to A(O)$. The actual scalar vacuum restricted through $\beta$ is exactly $\operatorname{diag}(\mu,1-\mu)$. In particular $\sigma_{z}$ maps to oscillator parity; $\sigma_{x}$ and $\sigma_{y}$ exchange adjacent even/odd number levels, with the indicated phase.

Equation (2.1) factors this single oscillator marginal after a specified local Gaussian change of coordinates. It neither factors the full scalar vacuum against the mode commutant nor proves independence of different spatial regions.

##### 3. The declared local family and independently supplied copies

Retain the fixed-spectrum, two-dimensional local family

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sigma_z&=U_z \operatorname{diag}(\mu,1-\mu)\, U_z^{*}, \\
U_z&=\exp[i(z_x \sigma_x+z_y \sigma_y)].
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.1}
$$

At the base its derivatives are $r\sigma_y,-r\sigma_x$, where $r=2\mu-1=1/(2\nu)>0$. They are independent, so this is a faithful regular local chart. Its original-field realization is the family of global states

$$
\omega_z(A)=\omega(\beta(U_z)^{*} A\, \beta(U_z)).
\tag{3.2}
$$

Restriction of (3.2) to $\beta(M_2)$ is exactly (3.1). The family outside this finite subalgebra is not asserted to have the same statistical experiment or the same Fisher information.

For $N$ copies, the source explicitly supplies $N$ independently prepared instances with the same parameter $z=u/\sqrt{N}$. These may be $N$ experimental replicas or $N$ separately nominated preparations. Their joint retained state is $\sigma_{u/\sqrt{N}}^{\otimes N}$. This is not a cloning operation and is not inferred from clustering, split inclusions, or the original spatial vacuum. The parameter port owns $u$; comparison controllers receive only $N$, the fixed base and accuracy, with no parameter side channel.

Every fixed state $\sigma_{z}$ defines the exchangeable extremal product component $\sigma_z^{\otimes k}$, so the finite-dimensional/de Finetti premise is populated on this declared family. A mixture over this family is a separately specified mixture of those components.

##### 4. The exact LAN tuple and scalar probe identification

Consume Theorem F.10.4e.9 at the actual $\mu$. Write $q=1-\mu$, $r=2\mu-1$, $p=q/\mu$ and $\nu_L=q/r$. The Gaussian tangent experiment is

$$
\begin{aligned}
G_u&=D(\alpha_u)\, \tau_p\, D(\alpha_u)^{*}, \\
\alpha_u&=\sqrt{r}\,(-u_y+i u_x), \\
V_G&=(2r)^{-1} I_2,\qquad [Q_G,P_G]=i I, \\
I_{\mathrm{LAN}}&=4 r^{2} I_2.
\end{aligned}
$$

Its root fidelity is $\exp[-r^2|u-v|^2/2]$, exactly $\exp[-(u-v)^T I_{\mathrm{LAN}}(u-v)/8]$. The parameter-independent normal CPTP channels $\Theta_N,\Xi_N$ are the existing spin/Schur, ladder and multiplicity-preparation channels, with their full trace-norm compact-uniform error

$$
\begin{aligned}
\epsilon_N \le \min\bigl(2, \\
&\quad (4M/\sqrt{r})\bigl[(\mu/r)\sqrt{(1-r^{2})B_1/N}+\sqrt{B_3}/N\bigr] \\
&\quad +(2q/r)\exp(-N r^{2}/2)\bigr),
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.1}
$$

where $A=rM^2$, $B_1=1+\nu_L+A$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}
B_3&=A^{3}+(9\nu_L+6)A^{2}+(18\nu_L^{2}+24\nu_L+7)A \\
&\quad +6\nu_L^{3}+12\nu_L^{2}+7\nu_L+1.
\end{aligned}
$$

There is also an exact identification of the Gaussian target with the same original local mode. From (2.1), $q/\mu=p$ and $(2r)^{-1}=\nu$. Thus its thermal state $\tau_{p}$ is exactly the squeezed-frame vacuum marginal we started with, not a different covariance. The target $G_{u}$ is its actual local Weyl displacement $D(\alpha_u)$. The defining oscillator representation gives a normal *-isomorphism of every bounded Gaussian output probe into $M_{\mathrm{mode}}$ inside $A(O)$; undo the fixed squeeze when writing it in the original $Q,P$ coordinates. Both sides of the LAN diagram are therefore identified response algebras of the same scalar source, while their experiment sizes and independent-copy supplies remain different. No full-field/commutant statistical equivalence is asserted.

The actual bounded scalar probe corresponding to a finite-experiment observable $B_{N}$ is $\beta^{\otimes N}(B_N)$. This is a norm-preserving *-homomorphism and preserves its expectation exactly in the retained source states. Thus the two directions are genuine identified local scalar responses, rather than equality of a covariance/Hessian without channels.

The prescribed finite polynomial moment records, transported bounded cutoffs, and their tails are exactly those proved in e.9 and realized in e.12–e.13. No unbounded moment convergence is inferred from trace norm alone. On another compact chart of the same orbit, first apply the fixed base conjugation; the same certificate applies.

This establishes all four clauses of Definition e.5 for the declared local qubit family. It does not certify every family of states on $A(O)$, every change of the scalar covariance, or every extremal family a larger F14 branch might choose to retain.

##### 5. Actual finite source, base precision and complete records

The reference source e.11 explicitly chose rational $\mu_{0}$. The actual $\mu$ in (2.1) need not be rational. No historical extension is assumed. The finite construction extends directly as follows. Compute the actual $x,y$ and hence $\mu$ to certified precision; find rational compact bounds $1/2<\mu_-<\mu<\mu_+<1$. This terminates for the fixed profile. The finite preparation coefficients, block probabilities and Gaussian cutoff matrices are now computed by rational interval arithmetic. The fixed Schur matrix depends on $N$, not on $\mu$. Every occurrence of $\mu$ in the error constants is bounded by these certified compact bounds.

For a numerical base $\hat{\mu}$, the single-qubit base densities differ in trace norm by $2|\mu-\hat{\mu}|$. Applying the same local rotation and telescoping $N$ products costs at most $2N|\mu-\hat{\mu}|$. Choose this below its allocation. On a certified compact base interval the Gaussian thermal/displacement comparison has the explicit Lipschitz constants already proved in e.10. Thus its additional base error is also separately allocated. Choosing the approximation bits costs $O(\log(N/\epsilon))$ beyond the actual fixed covariance-production bits. Neither equality of irrational parameters nor an exact sampling oracle is needed.

The occupation relabeling on a dyadic number cutoff is simply separation of the least significant bit and a shift of the remaining address. The local squeeze is a one-mode Gaussian primitive; its cutoff implementation and the actual one-mode source preparation have the complete vector/trace/flag bounds of the structured producer of Proposition F.10.4f.31.1. For a Gaussian number tail above 2K, the mass is $p^{(2K)}$; a cutoff/reset comparison costs at most 4 $p^{K}$ in trace norm, and retaining its coherent flag uses the corresponding square-root allocation. Bounded local qubit rotations preserve each pair {2k,2k+1}, so they add no new occupation tail beyond this fixed pair cutoff.

Supply $N$ independent actual copies at per-copy source error at most $\epsilon_{\mathrm{src}}/N$. All preparation purifiers, mode remainders, block/multiplicity labels, fair words, sampler scratch and failure flags are archived or retained in the specified public comparison. The original field vacuum's correlations with its unmeasured commutant are not replaced by product correlations in an asserted full-field comparison: the source identification here is precisely the $\beta(M_2)$ response algebra.

The admitted source-native rail compiler realizes the finite qubit preparation and e.12 comparison circuits. Every dimension, finite coefficient table and QR/controlled-rotation list is counted. The existing conservative finite compiler bound may be used; no free Schur, state-preparation or continuous detector oracle is inserted. Dephasing/partial trace of a private archive occurs only in the nominated public response channel and does not remove its physical storage charge.

##### 6. Cost, mode growth and the remaining exact boundary

Let $R_{\mathrm{alloc}},B_{\mathrm{prog}},r_{\mathrm{ready}},b_{\mathrm{random}},G,D,T_{\mathrm{set}}$ denote the actual counters of the compiled program, now including the scalar marginal preparation, squeeze/occupation interface and all $N$ copies. Its physical account is e.11's fixed positive service law, or the more detailed admitted rail ledger with its actual source-independent reference frequency. In particular

$$
\begin{aligned}
T_{\mathrm{elapsed}}&=T_{\mathrm{set}}+\tau_g(r_{\mathrm{ready}}+b_{\mathrm{random}}+G+D+B_{\mathrm{prog}}), \\
E_{\mathrm{service}}&=e_{\mathrm{set}}+r_{\mathrm{ready}}\, e_{\mathrm{ready}}+b_{\mathrm{random}}\, e_{\mathrm{random}} \\
&\quad +G e_g+D e_d+B_{\mathrm{prog}}\, e_{\mathrm{prog}}+(P_c+R_{\mathrm{alloc}}\, p_c)T_{\mathrm{elapsed}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Occupied/idle rail energy, pulse action, timing/angle precision and every holding interval are added as in Definition F.10.4f.31.6. There are at least N supplied data qubits and their independent-copy preparation costs. Neither a Gaussian limit nor a partial trace makes these costs disappear. This constructs finite physical service data for the local LAN family; it does not give a polylogarithmic total cost in its LAN error.

For $r_{\mathrm{modes}}$ exact Williamson modes of an actual covariance $\lVert V\rVert\le v$, each parity qubit has $r_i=1/(2\nu_i)\ge 1/(2v)$, while $\nu_{L,i}=\nu_i-1/2\le v$. Tensor the fixed-spectrum certificates and add their errors. Formula (4.1) then has a uniform upper bound

$$
\begin{aligned}
\epsilon_{\mathrm{total}} &\le r_{\mathrm{modes}}\, C(v,M)/\sqrt{N} \\
&\quad +4 r_{\mathrm{modes}}\, v \exp[-N/(8v^{2})],
\end{aligned}
\tag{6.1}
$$

with an explicit nonnegative polynomial upper bound $C$ obtained from (4.1), replacing $r^{-1/2}$ by $\sqrt{2v}$, $\mu/r$ by $2v$, $\nu_{L}$ by $v$ and $A$ by $M^2$. Rounding this to a polynomial in $1+v+M$ is harmless. A sufficient $N$ is the maximum of a constant multiple of $[r_{\mathrm{modes}}C(v,M)/\epsilon]^2$ and $8v^2\log(16r_{\mathrm{modes}}v/\epsilon)$.

This fixed-spectrum bound needs no lower bound on the small thermal occupation $p_{i}$: approaching a pure base does not make (6.1) blow up. A varying-spectrum chart does require its own endpoint control and is not covered by this assertion. The exact Williamson frame identifies the mathematical subalgebras; numerical frame production and the summed covariance/purification errors retain the producer's gap-free validation and actual cost. Any physical common-original-register frame transport remains a separate interface obligation.

Consequently growing retained Gaussian modes admit a family-specific LAN construction with all copy/conditioning dependence exposed. At a required LAN tolerance $\epsilon=\delta$, this construction's chosen copy count is generally polynomial in $1/\delta$, rather than in $\log(1/\delta)$; the positive supply cost must be included if that LAN experiment is part of the F14 service being priced. A prerequsite existence certificate is not permission to omit that experiment's requested execution cost.

The proved local qubit source has the original scalar vacuum as its exact base restriction and has actual scalar probe identifications. Its finite realization has the admitted independent service clock. The still-missing common microscopic field clock/light-cone comparison is not supplied by the LAN theorem. Nor does existence of this selected chart prove coverage of an unstated larger retained extremal-family census.

<a id="proposition-f104f313a-exact-correlated-gaussian-copy-concentration-and-its-source-domain"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.31.3a (Exact Correlated Gaussian Copy Concentration and Its Source Domain).**

Let $\rho_{V,d}$ be a normal $r$-mode Gaussian state with covariance $V$ and mean $d$, with one fixed actual local-mode covariance $V$. For $N$ independently supplied copies, consider

$$
\rho_{V,d/\sqrt{N}}^{\otimes N}.
$$

Choose a real orthogonal $N$-by-$N$ matrix $O$ whose first row is $(1,\dots,1)/\sqrt{N}$, and apply the passive copy-index symplectic transformation $S=O\otimes I_{2r}$. It preserves $I_{N}\otimes V$ exactly and transforms the mean $(d/\sqrt{N},\dots,d/\sqrt{N})$ to $(d,0,\dots,0)$. Gaussian characteristic functions therefore give the exact state identity

$$
\begin{aligned}
U_O\, \rho_{V,d/\sqrt{N}}^{\otimes N}\, U_O^{*} \\
&=\rho_{V,d} \otimes \rho_{V,0}^{\otimes(N-1)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.10.4f.31.3a.1}
$$

No product approximation to correlations inside $V$ is made. The forward normal CPTP channel conjugates by $U_{O}$ and traces the last $N-1$ copies. The reverse adjoins $N-1$ independent copies of the actual $\rho_{V,0}$ and conjugates by $U_O^*$. Both channels are parameter independent and have zero deficiency on this experiment. Ancillary supply in the reverse direction is an actual state resource.

An explicit concentration circuit uses $N-1$ beam splitters per original mode. At step $k$ combine the previously collected amplitude $\sqrt{k-1}\,d/\sqrt{N}$ with $d/\sqrt{N}$, using cosine $\sqrt{(k-1)/k}$ and sine $1/\sqrt{k}$. It leaves collected amplitude $\sqrt{k}\,d/\sqrt{N}$ and zero in the released port. Thus there are exactly $r(N-1)$ pair mixers, apart from ordering/routing. Applying the same real mixing to every original mode preserves all correlations in $V$. Full covariance norm stays $\lVert V\rVert$, and the total displacement norm stays $\lVert d\rVert$. The growing-mode Gaussian compiler consequently gives finite cutoff/flag implementations with actual gate, routing, record and covariance-precision bounds. Preparing $N$ copies to per-copy trace error $\epsilon/N$ gives total input trace error at most $\epsilon$; coherent purifications use their separate summed vector allocations. Add all $r(N-1)$ gate/dilation errors and retain every flag. Ancilla/rail supply, duration and holding charges scale with the actual $N$ and cannot be replaced by a one-copy cost.

Canonical linear observables and every prescribed finite Weyl-ordered polynomial are transported exactly by this linear transformation. Gaussian moment tails follow from the fixed covariance and bounded mean; number cutoffs have the earlier exponential moment bounds. These facts give a complete exact normal Gaussian-shift statistical equivalence, not merely a characteristic-function limit.

It is not, by itself, a certificate under the literal starting premise of Definition F.10.4e.5. Its single-copy state family acts on an infinite-dimensional oscillator algebra, whereas that definition starts from a faithful finite-dimensional family. A tolerance-dependent oscillator cutoff produces an approximation to (F.10.4f.31.3a.1), but changes the single-copy family as the tolerance changes; it does not retroactively make the fixed source family finite-dimensional. Proposition F.10.4f.31.3 supplies the genuine finite-dimensional chart instead, and its Gaussian limit is exactly this same local thermal covariance.

Equation (F.10.4f.31.3a.1) is useful when the branch separately retains normal Gaussian experiments. It supplies no new acceptance or family substitution, no spatial iid claim, and no microscopic field-clock identification.

<a id="proposition-f104f314-smooth-hadamard-parity-states-and-positive-field-controls"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.31.4 (Smooth Hadamard Parity States and Positive Field Controls).**

##### 1. A finite complex packet space controls the full field state

Choose the local canonical mode of Proposition F.10.4f.31.3 from real smooth compact Cauchy profiles, for example the explicit Gevrey-two bumps in the Hadamard protocol note. Let $E$ be the complex span of its original one-particle $Q$ and $P$ packets. Then $\dim_{\mathbb{C}}(E)\le 2$. The packets and every element of $E$ have all momentum moments. Choose a computable orthonormal basis $e_1,\dots,e_d$ by the finite packet Gram matrix; any small fixed Gram pivot is retained in its actual precision/cost constants.

The original scalar Fock space and vacuum factor as

$$
\begin{aligned}
F(h)&=F(E) \otimes F(E_\perp), \\
\Omega&=\Omega_E \otimes \Omega_{E_\perp}.
\end{aligned}
$$

This is the genuine complex-orthogonal Fock factorization. It is not the generally false assertion that the local canonical mode factorizes from its local commutant. The local mode algebra is contained in $B(F(E))\otimes I$, since its fields involve only the packets in $E$. Hence every bounded parity-qubit unitary $\beta(U)$ acts there, and

$$
\beta(U)\Omega=\psi_U \otimes \Omega_{E_\perp}.
\tag{1.1}
$$

The same statement holds for any fixed finite collection of these local modes, with $E$ its finite complex packet span. The span includes both actual $Q$ and $P$ packets, not just a putative annihilation mode. Thus every creation/annihilation component of the finite Bogoliubov frame is included. The real field also contains the complex-conjugate negative-frequency waves; these are explicitly retained in the kernels in §3. This lemma concerns the scalar factor. If the common source additionally contains an independent charged/Dirac factor, the operation is $\beta(U)\otimes I$ on that factor: both its particle and sea/antiparticle covariances are unchanged, rather than omitted or approximated. No nontrivial Dirac operation is claimed by the scalar proof.

##### 2. Finite moments survive the parity-qubit operation

Complete the local canonical coordinates inside the finite E to a symplectic frame, adding its actual finite complementary coordinates. This is a finite-dimensional symplectic linear-algebra operation. In the resulting defining oscillator representation the original vacuum is a finite-mode pure Gaussian, with a finite covariance and exponential number tails. Let $N_{\mathrm{can}}$ be the sum of all these canonical number operators, including the complementary ones.

The parity-qubit rotation mixes only $|2k\rangle$ and $|2k+1\rangle$ in the chosen local coordinate and acts identically on the complementary coordinates. Within each such block, the weights $(N_{\mathrm{can}}+1)^m$ have ratio at most $2^m$. Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert(N_{\mathrm{can}}+1)^{m} \beta(U) \psi\rVert \\
&\le 2^{m} \lVert(N_{\mathrm{can}}+1)^{m} \psi\rVert
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.1}
$$

for every integer $m\ge 0$ and every vector in the stated domain, uniformly over $U\in U(2)$. This follows block by block from its unitary norm, and extends by summing the orthogonal blocks. For several independently rotated local modes replace $2^m$ by the corresponding finite product, or use their total bounded occupation change.

Let $N_{E}$ be the ordinary number operator in the orthonormal complex frame E. A finite Bogoliubov change of coordinates writes each $N_{E}$ as a quadratic polynomial in the canonical creation/annihilation operators. Repeated ladder bounds give, for each integer m,

$$
\lVert(N_E+1)^{m} \psi\rVert\le C_m \lVert(N_{\mathrm{can}}+1)^{m} \psi\rVert,
\tag{2.2}
$$

with explicit finite $C_{m}$ obtained from that fixed symplectic matrix and the finitely many quadratic monomials. One can expand the $m$-th power, use $\lVert a_i\psi\rVert\le\lVert N_{\mathrm{can}}^{1/2}\psi\rVert$ and $\lVert a_i^*\psi\rVert\le\lVert(N_{\mathrm{can}}+1)^{1/2}\psi\rVert$, and shift the number weight by at most $2m$ after each monomial. This gives an elementary conservative $C_{m}$. Applying (2.1)–(2.2) to the Gaussian vacuum shows that every $\psi_{U}$ has all number moments, uniformly in the retained qubit chart.

All physical field-energy moments, not merely local number moments, are controlled. For each integer m define

$$
B_m=\max\Bigl(1, \max_{1\le k\le m} \lVert\omega^{k} P_E\rVert^{1/k}\Bigr).
$$

These are finite, computably bounded packet norms because $E$ is spanned by smooth packets with all momentum moments. On the $n$-particle space with every input leg in $E$, expand $(\sum_{i=1}^n\omega_i)^m$. There are $n^{m}$ ordered terms. If an index occurs $k$ times, its factor $\omega^k P_E$ has norm at most $B_m^k$. Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert H_0^{m} \psi_n\rVert&\le\hbar^{m} n^{m} B_m^{m} \lVert\psi_n\rVert, \\
\lVert H_0^{m} \psi_U\rVert&\le\hbar^{m} B_m^{m} \lVert N_E^{m} \psi_U\rVert.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.3}
$$

The output legs need not remain in $E$; the displayed $\omega^k P_E$ norms control their full one-particle Hilbert-space norm. Taking finite-particle approximants and using closedness proves the domain statement. Hence every source vector is in the domain of every power of the actual physical $H_{0}$, uniformly on the retained qubit chart with the explicit moment constants from (2.1)–(2.2). If an untouched independent Dirac/other free-vacuum factor is present, its renormalized positive Hamiltonian annihilates its unchanged vacuum, so the same estimate controls the total physical energy.

No lower bound on an infinite-dimensional polarizer is used. This is a fixed finite packet-space calculation with actual matrix/covariance constants.

##### 3. Exact smoothness of the two-point difference

Let $f_i(x)$ be the positive-frequency classical wave corresponding to $e_{i}$. It is smooth, with all local derivatives bounded by the weighted Fourier integrals used in the Hadamard note. Decompose the scalar field into these finitely many oscillator components and the $E_{\mathrm{perp}}$ field. By (1.1), the latter remains in its original vacuum and has zero one-point function. All altered two-point coefficients are therefore finite sums built from

$$
\begin{aligned}
N_{ij}&=\langle\psi_U,a_i^{*} a_j \psi_U\rangle, \\
M_{ij}&=\langle\psi_U,a_i a_j \psi_U\rangle,
\end{aligned}
$$

multiplying $f_i(x)\overline{f_j(y)}$, their conjugates, $f_i(x)f_j(y)$, and their conjugates. The vacuum terms are unchanged. Cauchy–Schwarz bounds every $N_{ij},M_{ij}$ by the finite first number moments, for example

$$
\begin{aligned}
|N_{ij}|&\le\sqrt{\langle n_i\rangle\langle n_j\rangle}, \\
|M_{ij}|&\le\sqrt{\langle n_i+1\rangle\langle n_j\rangle}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus

$$
\omega_{U,2}-\omega_{\mathrm{vac},2}
$$

is an actual finite-rank smooth kernel on spacetime, uniformly controlled by the retained finite frame and chart. Its localized $H^m$ bounds follow from Leibniz' rule and the explicit $f_{i}$ derivative bounds. Consequently the original field states used by the local qubit LAN source satisfy the Hadamard two-point wavefront condition. They need not be quasifree; this is a direct smooth-difference proof, not an invocation of a quasifree-only theorem on a non-Gaussian state. It supplies exactly the two-point regularity needed by the point-split quadratic observables. Any stronger higher-correlation or quasifree-source predicate retains its own scope.

The source base is the unchanged vacuum. The N-copy experiments use independent copies of these actual states as explicitly declared previously; their local Hadamard regularity is not a spatial iid assertion.

##### 4. Explicit positive bounded field controls and finite comparison

For a desired local qubit unitary $U=\exp(iK)$, choose Hermitian $K$ on $\mathbb{C}^2$ with $\lVert K\rVert\le\pi$ and a smooth monotone switching function $a(t)$ from 0 to 1 in a fixed duration $T$. Let

$$
\begin{aligned}
K_t&=\exp[-iH_0(t-T)/\hbar]\, \beta(K) \exp[iH_0(t-T)/\hbar], \\
H_{\mathrm{drive}}(t)&=H_0-\hbar a'(t)K_t+\hbar |a'(t)|\, \lVert K\rVert I.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.1}
$$

The perturbation is bounded and $H_{\mathrm{drive}}(t)\ge 0$. Its interaction-picture non-scalar generator is one fixed conjugate of $\beta(K)$; the exact final state is $\beta(U)\Omega$ up to the explicitly integrated scalar phase. The drive norm-action is at most $\hbar$ ||K||, its peak bounded-control norm is $\hbar$ ||K|| ||a'||_infinity, and its scalar offset has the same bound. The elapsed duration and its actual holding costs are T. Its final field energy is finite and bounded explicitly by

\tag{4.2}
$$

using that $\psi_{U}$ lies in $F(E)$ and the $E_{\mathrm{perp}}$ vacuum. The packet matrix $P_E\omega P_E$ is finite and computable. A cyclic control account must retain this energy increase, its source/controller debit and the scalar phase. The large bare field Hamiltonian is not assigned a bounded operator norm.

For the finite retained implementation, express the actual finite symplectic frame from §2 as a Gaussian circuit on $d$ modes, truncate it with its actual covariance/occupation bounds, apply $U$ to the least significant occupation bit of the designated local mode, then undo the frame circuit if an $E$-basis output is wanted. All complementary Gaussian modes and failure flags are kept. This gives a structured finite preparation of the actual vector $\psi_{U}$ in the explicit isometric $F(E)$ comparison, with coherent error supplied by the same finite Gaussian compiler. This is stronger than merely matching the qubit marginal. The elementary qubit operation changes no pair index, so its complete record and occupation tails are controlled by (2.1). All frame arithmetic, covariance data, ancillas, quantum/classical controls, physical rail slots and holding energy are charged.

At fixed smooth packet data this source comparison uses finitely many modes and the same polynomial-in-log-accuracy structured service bounds. The formal continuum drive (4.1) and its retained finite circuit are explicit mathematical data. Their claimed equality of retained source responses is through the stated packet Fock embedding. A demanded original microscopic-lattice control or common-clock transport is still a further theorem, not supplied by this continuum construction.

Together, this lemma makes the declared local parity-qubit LAN family compatible with the smooth two-point Hadamard resource subrecord. It neither asserts that every retained F14 state is such a finite-packet state nor resolves the full canonical Sobolev tariff.

<a id="proposition-f104f315-paid-displacement-sobolev-bridge-and-complete-sampler-records"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.31.5 (Paid Displacement–Sobolev Bridge and Complete Sampler Records).**

##### 1. The exact owner and a necessary distinction

Definition K.10.4a chooses the Hadamard-subtracted remainder $r_U=\omega_2-H_U$ and the localized Sobolev norms $N_{j,m}=\lVert Q_j r_U\rVert_{H^m}$. Its functional is the weighted sum of $N/(1+N)$, with value infinity if any required norm is infinite. Theorem K.10.4b expressly calls this a continuum regularity criterion and requires an independent protocol-to-Sobolev-complexity bridge before giving it a physical PCE-cost interpretation.

In Proposition F.10.4f.31.5 use the displacement convention $W(h)=\exp[a^*(h)-a(h)]$. Choose $h=i\kappa$ with $\kappa$ in the original real localized field subspace, so $W(h)=\exp[i(a^*(\kappa)+a(\kappa))]$ is exactly a local Weyl operator. The harmless fixed $i$ and field normalization are included when converting the original Cauchy-profile coordinates; they never enlarge the localization region. With smooth compact Cauchy profiles its classical mean has smooth compact Cauchy data.

For every Hadamard state the functional is at most $\sum_{j,m\ge 1}2^{-j-m}=1$. Consequently it cannot alone provide a uniform upper bound on the physical work of preparation. Here is an explicit same-field demonstration. Let $h$ be a nonzero smooth localized scalar one-particle packet with $E_h=\langle h,\omega h\rangle$ finite and positive. The coherent state $W(Ah)\Omega$ is Hadamard for every real $A$, while its field energy above vacuum is

$$
\Delta E= \hbar A^{2} E_h.
\tag{1.1}
$$

This is unbounded in $A$. If a centered quasifree state is required, average these states with $A$ replaced by $AZ$, $Z$ a standard real normal variable. Its Weyl characteristic function is Gaussian, its two-point difference is a smooth rank-one kernel, and its expected energy is again $\hbar A^{2}E_h$. Thus the example lies in the centered quasifree class too.

The resource implication is precise: a complete cyclic-drive work account preparing these states from vacuum must supply (1.1), or charge that energy to its consumed preparation resource. No inequality $E_{\mathrm{preparation}}\le C\,C_{\mathrm{Had}}$, or $\le C(1+C_{\mathrm{Had}})$, holds uniformly over this family with fixed $C$. This rejects a missing normalization shortcut, not finite-cost admissibility of each fixed state. A valid quantitative bridge must also retain amplitude, profile/derivative, precision and protocol data.

##### 2. An explicit smooth computational profile class

For a fixed cube choose the real compactly supported bump

$$
\begin{aligned}
b(x)&=\prod_{a=1}^{3} \exp[-1/(u_a(1-u_a))], \\
u_a&=x_a/l \in (0,1),
\end{aligned}
$$

and zero elsewhere, with an optional fixed normalization. Its derivatives satisfy a certified Gevrey-two bound. In one dimension use the complex circle of radius $d/8$, $d=\min(u,1-u)$. There $\operatorname{Re}[1/(z(1-z))]\ge 1/(4d)$; Cauchy's estimate and maximization of $d^{(-k)}\exp[-1/(4d)]$ give

\lVert b_1^{(k)}\rVert_\infty \le 32^{k} (k!)^{2},

with rescaling $l^{(-k)}$ and fixed product/normalization constants in three dimensions. All derivatives tend to zero at the boundary. Repeated integration by parts therefore gives stretched-exponential sine coefficients $|b_j|\le C\exp[-c\sqrt{|j|_\infty}]$ after optimization of the derivative order. The constants can be weakened outward and chosen rational. Multiplication by the fixed polynomial Sobolev weights does not spoil this decay.

Hence a fixed finite set of such profiles belongs to the previously proved computational Gevrey spectral class with $\alpha=1/2$ and sufficiently small positive $a$. Its coefficient production by certified Gevrey quadrature uses a polynomial in $\log(1/\epsilon)$ number of samples/operations; the derivative bound supplies the quadrature remainder. One elementary implementation uses composite Taylor quadrature of order $k$ on a uniform mesh with mesh width proportional to $k^{-2}$, and $k$ proportional to $\log(1/\epsilon)$: each cell's remainder is bounded by $C^{k}k!\,h^{k}$, which is exponentially small for that mesh, and there are polynomially many cells. All polynomial/trigonometric factors used to form sine coefficients have their actual frequency bounds included. Function values, exponentials and normalization are computed with certified polynomial-bit arithmetic. The growing-mode covariance producer then applies without treating a profile oracle as free.

Let h be the one-particle packet of fixed smooth Cauchy data chosen from this finite set. Since the mass is positive and the Cauchy data are smooth and compactly supported, h has all momentum moments. Define explicit weighted integrals

$$
\begin{aligned}
M_d(h)&=(2\pi)^{-3/2} \int (1+\omega(p))^{d} \\
&\qquad \omega(p)^{-1/2}|h(p)|\, dp.
\end{aligned}
$$

Repeated integration by parts with the preceding derivative bounds gives finite, effective upper bounds for every $M_{d}$. These bounds, rather than mere membership in C-infinity, are part of the branch data.

The smooth Klein-Gordon mean $\phi_{h}$ of $W(h)\Omega$ obeys, on every spacetime compact and for $|\alpha|\le d$,

|\partial^{\alpha} \phi_h| \le\sqrt{2}\, M_d(h),
\tag{2.1}
$$

up to the fixed field/Fourier units. Both time derivatives $\omega$ and spatial derivatives p are bounded by the retained (1+omega) weight. For an amplitude-bounded finite list of such packets all corresponding constants are explicit finite numbers.

This is a genuine smooth subset of the Gevrey spectral test family. The full sine-spectral family in the earlier producer contains nonflat boundary profiles and is not asserted to create Hadamard displaced states. Its vacuum approximation theorem does not need that stronger assertion.

##### 3. A protocol-to-Sobolev upper certificate

Fix the local Hadamard reference once on the Minkowski branch. One may use the actual vacuum bidistribution as a state-independent Hadamard reference on each retained normal neighborhood. If a different fixed parametrix is retained, include its known smooth difference $s_U=\omega_{\mathrm{vac},2}-H_U$ and its separately certified seminorms; none is discarded.

In the coherent case $\phi_{h}$ is the first moment and (3.1) is the full two-point function, not the connected covariance. In the centered mixture it is the covariance itself.

Choose, for example, properly supported multiplication cutoffs $Q_j=\chi_j$ with compact base support covering $U\times U$. Such order-zero operators are elliptic in every nonzero cotangent direction wherever $\chi_{j}$ is nonzero, so they meet K.10.4a. N_{j,m}(r_U) \le N_{j,m}(s_U)+A^{2} C_{j,m,h},

where one usable $C$ is obtained by summing all derivatives of $\chi_j\phi_h(x)\phi_h(y)$ up to total order $m$, bounding each factor by its displayed sup norm, and multiplying by $\sqrt{\operatorname{Vol}(\operatorname{supp}\chi_j)}$. The finite binomial sums, Fourier units and $H^m$ convention are recorded directly. Equation (3.2) is an effective all-order regularity certificate and proves the Hadamard property on every finite retained neighborhood cover.

The same branch record contains the paid profile generator, actual covariance-production program, amplitude bound, pulse data of §4, finite probe list/precision and all compiled-service counters of §5. Equations (3.2), (4.2) and (5.1) relate those actual protocol data to the Sobolev and physical-resource quantities. No numerical identification of a saturated Sobolev functional with joules is made.

If the value of the bounded functional is itself requested to additive error $\epsilon$, only $j,m\le J$ need numerical evaluation, with $J$ chosen so $2^{1-J}\le\epsilon/2$; the rest is bounded by its geometric weights once (3.2) certifies finiteness. There is no finite-response test that decides this regularity property for arbitrary undisclosed states.

##### 4. An explicit positive physical field-drive module

This paragraph supplies mathematical physical control data rather than invoking a preparation oracle. Write $H_0=\hbar\,d\Gamma(\omega)$. Choose a fixed smooth monotone shape $s$ on $[0,1]$ with $s(0)=0,s(1)=1$ and $s'$ zero at the endpoints. Put $a(t)=A\,s(t/T)$. For target final packet $h$, set

$$
\begin{aligned}
h_t&=\exp[i \omega(T-t)]h, \\
H_A(t)&=H_0+i \hbar a'(t)[a^{*}(h_t)-a(h_t)] \\
&\quad +\hbar a'(t)^{2} \lVert\omega^{-1/2}h\rVert^{2} I.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.1}
$$

The linear field perturbation is infinitesimally form bounded relative to $H_{0}$. Completing the square in the annihilation field proves $H_A(t)\ge 0$ as a quadratic form and defines its self-adjoint realization. The scalar offset is recorded, not omitted. In the $H_{0}$ interaction picture the non-scalar drive is $a'(t)$ times one fixed Weyl generator, so its propagator is exactly the desired Weyl displacement, with the known integrated scalar phase. At the final time it produces $W(Ah)\Omega$ up to that recorded phase. The Cauchy supports of $h_{t}$ remain in the finite causal enlargement of the initial smooth support over duration $T$, by the actual Klein-Gordon propagation. The pulse need not preserve one fixed smaller region for all times.

The source record is explicit:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{elapsed time}&=T, \\
\int |a'|\, dt&=|A|, \\
\int a'^{2}\, dt&=(A^{2}/T) \int_0^1 |s'|^{2}, \\
\text{peak scalar offset}&\le\hbar A^{2} \lVert s'\rVert_\infty^{2} \\
&\qquad \lVert\omega^{-1/2}h\rVert^{2}/T^{2}, \\
\text{final field energy}&=\hbar A^{2} E_h.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.2}
$$

Because the drive and its offset vanish at the endpoints, the net field work is its final energy increase. The controller's nonnegative operating debit, waveform production, timing and profile-control costs must additionally be charged. On a number cutoff K, the linear-drive norm is at most a fixed multiple of $\hbar$ |a'| ||h||sqrt(K+1); its integrated norm and finite-sector Duhamel precision are therefore explicit. There is no bounded full-Fock operator-norm claim.

Equation (4.1) is an actual continuum field control Hamiltonian with the original physical $H_{0}$ and explicit support. It does not prove that the earlier microscopic lattice/rail controls converge to it on the original common clock. That remains the separate source-transport theorem. The finite retained response simulator in §5 uses the admitted rail module and charges its own service clock.

##### 5. Finite paid preparation and probes

For fixed $|A|\le A_{\max}$, the coherent displacement is one of the retained smooth Weyl calls. The spatial/covariance/Gaussian compiler applies with the enlarged fixed displacement bound, providing state, coherent-vector, retained-interface and complete-record errors, with dyadic cutoffs and the precision supplements listed in Theorem F.10.4f.31.7 §5. &\le C_{\mathrm{branch}}\, P(\log(1/\epsilon)),

under the already nominated polynomial finite-precision tariff. The constants include (4.2), all amplitude/profile seminorm bounds, and fixed T. For the centered quasifree Gaussian-amplitude family, no unpriced continuous random number is necessary. Supply two independent $B$-bit uniform words. At dyadic midpoints $U_B,V_B$ in $(0,1)$, compute

Couple them with exact independent uniform $U,V$ in their cells. Monotonicity of $f(u)=\sqrt{-2\log u}$, summing its cell oscillations outside the first cell, and direct integration on that first cell give

The cosine difference contributes at most $2\pi\,2^{-B}\,\mathbb{E}f(U)$, another finite constant times $2^{-B}$. Thus $\mathbb{E}|Z-Z_B|$ has the same bound. Coherent vectors are Lipschitz along a fixed Weyl ray, so the full field-state trace error is at most

$$

with the fixed Weyl normalization absorbed in $C$. Elementary log/square-root/trigonometric routines at $p$ bits add their separately bounded amplitude error. Choose $B,p=O(\log(1/\epsilon)+\log(1+A_{\max}))$; all $2B$ fair bits and arithmetic records are retained. The largest sampled amplitude is $O(A_{\max}\sqrt{B+1})$, so the displacement/occupation cutoffs and physical control costs remain polynomial in $\log(1/\epsilon)$ for fixed $A_{\max}$. This is a complete finite dyadic sampler, not postselection or rejection with omitted tails. Its continuous limit is the centered quasifree state in §§1–3. Every finite protocol ends with its actual retained fair words and control history.

This gives a nonempty actual smooth-state branch with both explicit Sobolev regularity and finite paid approximants, including a direct positive field-drive module. Its use closes a **specified smooth-displacement finite-protocol Hadamard admissibility subrecord**. A full F14 owner still must identify this as its retained state/probe census, supply the original-register/clock transport where demanded, and include any broader canonical, LAN and preparation work. For a retained finite fair-word record, the ideal comparison keeps the same cell label $R_B=\lfloor 2^B U\rfloor,\lfloor 2^B V\rfloor$, together with the deterministic numerical arithmetic history for that label, and conditionally averages the exact field displacement over $U,V$ in that cell. <a id="definition-f104f316-positive-finite-precision-rail-services-and-full-source-ledger"></a>**Definition F.10.4f.31.6 (Positive Finite-Precision Rail Services and Full Source Ledger).**

The actual structured finite circuit can be physically represented on that admitted source without expanding an entire exponential-dimensional register into one rail per global basis vector:

1. Encode each three-qubit $\mathbb{C}^8$ carrier as one excitation in eight positive equal-frequency rails. Its full matrix units are quadratic rail couplings. A one-carrier unitary uses the source's drift-compensated logarithm pulse.
2. A controlled binary phase between two carriers is a finite sum of the admitted positive cross-Kerr couplings between their designated bit-value rail projectors. At most sixteen rail-pair terms are required for two selected bits. Local basis changes and these phases realize the one/two-qubit gate list of the structured compiler, with a constant number of source primitives per logical elementary gate. Swaps provide the already charged routing.
3. Fresh one-excitation pointer pairs implement the binary instrument flags. Their outcome and failure stores are retained. A pointer readout is not silently replaced by an unrecorded trace or free reset. The exact finite restriction channel retains its prescribed environment registers.
4. Choose one positive independent reference frequency $\nu$ and a fixed slot $L>3\pi/(2\nu)$, in $\hbar=1$ units. For every bounded-size gate, the source's endpoint-compensated control has logarithm norm at most $\pi$, integrated norm at most $\pi$ and peak norm below $\nu$. The total quadratic rail generator stays nonnegative. Its source-clock record is the supplied reference oscillator, and all endpoint phase/drift compensation services are retained.

There are $O(Q)$ occupied rail blocks for $Q$ encoded qubits, a constant number of rails per block, and $O(N_{\mathrm{gate}})$ fixed-size pulse/control records. Constant overhead preserves the structured polynomial gate/space bounds. Sequential elapsed service time is at most a constant times $L\,N_{\mathrm{gate}}$ plus the actual preparation/readout intervals. Baseline energy is proportional to the actual number of live signal/pointer blocks; integrated holding cost is that live count times the actual elapsed/holding intervals. Controls, communicated bits, parameter installation, classical arithmetic, archives, detector actions and any reset have the nominated positive service charges. Transferred work and stored energy changes are not counted twice.

For a Hamiltonian-control error $E(t)$, the coherent gate error is bounded by $\int\lVert E(t)\rVert\,dt/\hbar$. Preparation, detector and pointer errors remain distinct. These feed the state/GNS/heat norm ledger of the Gaussian producer, not merely a failure probability.

This is a formal physical realization theorem on an already admitted source class. It supplies the actual finite service clock and complete finite instruments. It does not identify that service clock with the original scalar translation/refinement clock, establish spatial locality in the emergent diamond geometry, or prove a program-minimal tariff. The existing calibrated service source does not grant those additional statements. Their original-source comparison is a separate mathematical construction still required for full F14 closure.

##### Explicit elapsed-time, baseline and precision ledger

A particularly simple registered service choice takes every signal, pointer and code rail at the same fixed positive reference frequency $\nu$ and every elementary service slot of length $L=4\pi/\nu$. Free evolution on each one-excitation group is then exactly identity at each endpoint. This is a choice of formal admitted source parameters; it is not inferred from field transition probabilities.

For a local $U(8)$, choose a Hermitian logarithm $K$ with $\exp(-iK)=U$ and $\lVert K\rVert\le\pi$. With $s(t)=3(t/L)^{2}-2(t/L)^{3}$, install the quadratic rail matrix $\nu I+s'(t)K$. Its minimum eigenvalue is at least $\nu-3\pi/(2L)>0$ on the full Fock space. Its control norm action is at most $\pi$, peak norm at most $3\pi/(2L)$, peak derivative norm at most $6\pi/L^{2}$ and integrated derivative norm at most $3\pi/L$.

For a controlled binary phase, use the admitted positive cross-Kerr Hamiltonian $\kappa(t)n_a n_b$ with $\int\kappa=\theta\in[0,2\pi]$. Its exact action on the two one-excitation code groups is the desired phase on their selected basis pair. A negative desired phase is represented modulo $2\pi$ by a nonnegative $\theta$; no negative unbounded quartic interaction is used. The cubic pulse has peak $\kappa\le 3\pi/L$, integrated $\kappa\le 2\pi$, peak derivative $\le 12\pi/L^{2}$ and integrated absolute derivative $\le 6\pi/L$. A selected bit projector in a $\mathbb{C}^8$ code is the sum of four rail-occupation projectors, so the product of two such bit projectors uses sixteen positive rail-pair cross-Kerr phases. They commute, but counting sixteen sequential slots is a conservative valid tariff. Each individual group's total excitation commutes with every local quadratic and cross-Kerr service. The tensor code remains invariant on all input states and spectator extensions.

Let $N_{\mathrm{phys}}$ be the actual number of local quadratic, rail-pair Kerr, pointer, swap, preparation and readout service slots after compilation. Let $Q_{\mathrm{live}}$ be the largest number of live or archived one-excitation code/pointer groups, including environments. With separately recorded preparation/readout durations $T_{\mathrm{extra}}$ and a bounded declared post-service holding interval $H_{\mathrm{post}}$, record

$$
\begin{aligned}
T_{\mathrm{elapsed}}&=L N_{\mathrm{phys}}+T_{\mathrm{extra}}, \\
\text{carrier/group time} &\le Q_{\mathrm{live}}(T_{\mathrm{elapsed}}+H_{\mathrm{post}}), \\
\text{stored baseline energy time} &\le\hbar \nu\, Q_{\mathrm{live}}(T_{\mathrm{elapsed}}+H_{\mathrm{post}}), \\
\text{quadratic control action} &\le\pi \hbar N_{\mathrm{quad}}, \\
\text{Kerr control action} &\le 2\pi \hbar N_{\mathrm{Kerr}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

All these quantities, all allocated idle rails, the actual parameter/program bits, arithmetic working memory, readout/communication and archive costs are charged. Constant overhead from eight rails per carrier and sixteen Kerr terms per inter-carrier controlled phase preserves the polynomial counts. A direct alternative uses one n-rail group per truncated oscillator and a polynomial two-qudit synthesis; the binary C8 construction suffices here and incurs no global $n^{r}$ rail group.

For ideal closed signal gates the free endpoint energy is $\hbar\nu$ times the exactly conserved total excitation number. Their net signal work is therefore zero, by the source's exact work identity. This does not declare controller installation, drive storage, preparation, detector use or resetting free. Preparing each occupied ready group supplies its actual baseline energy $\hbar\nu$; pointer and archive storage are separate records. Work transferred into a stored baseline is not added a second time under another name. Transient control energy and its actual duration have the displayed bounds.

For coherent error budget $e_{\mathrm{gate}}$ choose, conservatively,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\delta_H &\le \hbar e_{\mathrm{gate}}/[4 \max(1,N_{\mathrm{phys}})L], \\
\delta_\nu &\le e_{\mathrm{gate}}/[4 \max(1,Q_{\mathrm{live}})(T_{\mathrm{elapsed}}+H_{\mathrm{post}})], \\
\delta_{\mathrm{time}} &\le \hbar e_{\mathrm{gate}}/[4 \max(1,N_{\mathrm{phys}})\, H_{\mathrm{code,max}}].
\end{aligned}
$$

These are uniform code-Hamiltonian, reference-frequency and per-slot timing error allocations; $H_{\mathrm{code},\max}$ includes the actual live baseline and active control bound. Duhamel and the triangle inequality sum their coherent contributions to at most the allocated $e_{\mathrm{gate}}$ after any additional compiler errors are included. The number of parameter bits is $O(\log(1/e_{\mathrm{gate}})+\log N_{\mathrm{phys}}+\log Q_{\mathrm{live}}+\log(1+T_{\mathrm{elapsed}}+H_{\mathrm{post}})+\log(1+H_{\mathrm{code},\max}))$. It is polynomial in $\log(1/\delta)$ on the Gevrey branch. Pointer, detector, preparation and leakage amplitudes have their own allocations. Public elapsed-time/clock records retain their actual enclosures and are not hidden inside a trace-distance claim.

The polynomial tariff conclusion consumes exactly the already nominated fixed finite-precision source-service pricing law. It follows because the **actual** rail count, gate count, pulse bounds, installed bits, elapsed/holding intervals and classical work above are polynomial, rather than because the word “gate” has been assigned a cost independent of physical accuracy. This completes the finite-service source ledger at its declared scope. The scalar continuum clock and geometric source comparison remain separate, as stated above.

11 October 2026 UTC. Additive literal correction to Definition F.10.4f.31.6.

The bound $\nu I+s'(t)K\ge[\nu-3\pi/(2L)]I>0$ is a bound on the finite one-particle rail coefficient matrix. Its bosonic second quantization is nonnegative on full Fock space and has vacuum energy zero. It is not bounded below on full Fock space by that strictly positive scalar. On the invariant one-excitation rail code it has the stated positive lower bound.

Likewise, every finite operator-norm, norm-action, peak-strength, variation and perturbation bound used for quadratic and cross-Kerr gates is on the explicitly nominated invariant finite rail code (or a finite union of nominated code sectors when expressly included). The full-Fock quadratic and Kerr generators are generally unbounded. Their nonnegativity, self-adjoint realization and code invariance justify the finite-sector restrictions; no bounded full-Fock norm is claimed.

The service schedule, complete occupied-rail/holding-energy ledger and finite-sector Duhamel error bounds are unchanged by this domain clarification.

<a id="theorem-f104f317-one-smooth-growing-state-probe-protocol-family"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.31.7 (One Smooth Growing State–Probe–Protocol Family).**

##### 1. Exact branch declaration

Fix the original massive scalar vacuum net, physical Hamiltonian $H=d\Gamma(\omega)$, $\omega=(m^{2}-\Delta)^{1/2}$, physical units and a positive compact heat window. Fix a cube $Q$ compactly contained in the time-zero base of every retained fixed-center diamond $O_R$, $R\ge R_*>0$. Fix positive rational parameters $a,\rho_0,R,\mu$ and finite word/protocol lengths. All other fixed constants have certified polynomial-time digit producers. The same old split factor may be used for each specified collar; its effective construction is unchanged.

The profile family below is fixed before accuracy. It is not the old compact Sobolev family and is not the complete old sine ellipsoid. No smoothing operation on that old family is claimed.

Let $b$ on $(0,1)^3$ be the $L^2$-normalized product $\exp[-1/(u_i(1-u_i))]$, extended by zero. Its normalization and all integrals below have certified polynomial-bit routines. Choose disjoint cubes $Q_j=c_j+(0,\rho_j)^3$ inside $Q$, with

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho_j&=\rho_0 j^{-2}, \\
(c_j)_1&=x_0+2\rho_0 \sum_{k<j} k^{-2}, \\
(c_j)_2&=(c_j)_3=y_0.
\end{aligned}
$$

Choose $\rho_{0}$ and $x_0,y_0$ so their compact closure, including the single accumulation point, lies strictly inside $Q$. For example bound the first-coordinate series by 2. Define

$$
g_j(x)=\rho_j^{-3/2}\, b((x-c_j)/\rho_j).
$$

These are smooth, real, exactly $L^2$-orthonormal. Their gradient inner products are diagonal, and $\lVert\nabla g_j\rVert^{2}=D_b\rho_j^{-2}$, with the fixed effective constant $D_b=\lVert\nabla b\rVert^{2}$. Set $\lambda_j=D_b\rho_0^{-2}j^{4}$.

The admitted real Cauchy pairs (f,k) are

$$
\begin{aligned}
&f=\sum_j c_j^{f} g_j,\quad k=\sum_j c_j^{k} g_j, \\
&\sum_j \exp(2aj)(1+\lambda_j)(|c_j^{f}|^{2}+|c_j^{k}|^{2})\le R^{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
$$

A supplied member includes a certified coefficient producer whose complete description, arithmetic, communication, working-memory and envelope-checking costs through $j\le r$ at $p$ bits are bounded by one fixed polynomial in $r,p$. The analytic ellipsoid includes points without such short programs; they are not given free access. This computational subclass is nonempty and infinite dimensional: every rational finite sequence with the displayed certified envelope is admitted, as are explicitly generated infinite exponentially decreasing sequences. Its fixed finite supports are not a fixed-rank restriction.

Let $h(f,k)$ be the original one-particle Cauchy map, with its original Weyl units. A fixed constant $C_{m}$ gives

$$
\lVert h\rVert\le U,\quad \lVert h-h_r\rVert\le U \exp(-ar),
\tag{2}
$$

where $h_{r}$ uses $j\le r$ and $U=C_m R$ (enlarged for the fixed word length). This follows from the disjoint-support $H^1$ form and the original massive $H^{\pm 1/2}$ bounds. The canonical symplectic form of retained and omitted pairs is exactly zero.

##### Smoothness at every boundary, including the accumulation point

For a multi-index of order s, the bump estimate gives

$$
