Write $N_E=d\Gamma(P_E)$, $K_{\mathrm{perp}}=d\Gamma(P_{E^\perp}AP_{E^\perp})$ as a nonnegative quadratic form, and $C_E=\lVert A^{1/2}P_E\rVert^{2}<\infty$. Splitting the annihilation-amplitude norm into its $E$ and $E^\perp$ pieces gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
K&\le 2 C_E N_E+2 K_\perp, \\
K_\perp&\le 2 K+2 C_E N_E,\quad N_E\le K.
\end{aligned}
$$

The finite Bogoliubov change between $E$-number and the completed canonical frame gives effective form inequalities $N_E+1\le c(N_{\mathrm{can}}+1)$ and $N_{\mathrm{can}}+1\le c'(N_E+1)$. A parity-qubit rotation $B$ mixes only adjacent occupations in one canonical coordinate; hence $B^*(N_{\mathrm{can}}+1)B\le 2(N_{\mathrm{can}}+1)$, uniformly $U\in U(2)$. Therefore

$$
B^{*}(N_E+1)B\le C_B(N_E+1),\quad C_B=2cc'.
$$

Because $B$ acts only on $F(E)$, it commutes with $K_{\mathrm{perp}}$. Combining the displayed inequalities yields the explicit uniform form bound

$$
B^{*} K B \le[2 C_E C_B+4+4 C_E]\, K+2 C_E C_B.
$$

All constants are computable from the fixed smooth packet Gram and symplectic matrices; no variable-profile pivot is used. Iterating this bound with the Weyl inequality above for the fixed maximum prefix length gives an effective uniform $E_{K}$ for every retained ideal prefix, including its adjoint test. These are closed-form/closed-quadratic-form inequalities, so finite-particle proofs extend by closure to their stated domains. There is no assertion of a uniform finite-register approximation on the much larger physical-H-energy-only ball.

The original projection estimate is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert(I-Q_n)\psi\rVert&\le q_n \lVert K^{1/2}\psi\rVert, \\
q_n^{2}&=3d_n^{2}/\pi^{2}+a_n^{2}/\pi^{2}+1/(R_n+1)=O(4^{-n}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
$$

The original sampled smooth-packet bound, original $H_{n}$ dynamics, rounding $|[t]_n-t|\le\tau_n/2$, and complete-instrument telescoping therefore give

$$
e_{\mathrm{original}}(n)\le C_{\mathrm{family}}\, 2^{-n}
\tag{2}
$$

in coherent vector norm for the declared fixed-length complete protocol, with the corresponding factor-two trace norm. The constant includes the actual finite test/time/seminorm budgets and every ideal prefix. The source preparation, readout, finite coefficient and pulse errors have their own additional allocations as in F.10.4c.22.

For a compressed parity unitary B, a direct proof avoids treating it as a Weyl operator: on a prefix $\psi$ the success difference

$$
Q_n B Q_n \psi-B \psi
$$

has norm at most $\lVert(I-Q_n)B\psi\rVert+\lVert(I-Q_n)\psi\rVert$. Its complete Halmos failure amplitude is bounded by the same projection quantities. Equation (1) applies to both ideal prefixes. This gives (2) for the enlarged grammar as well. The contraction matrix itself is computed and paid as stated above.

For actual real-time output comparison, the source relation is

$$
I_n \exp(-i[t]_n H_n)\, I_n^{*} \psi \to \exp(-itH)\psi
$$

with the original $K$-regular estimate. One may equivalently compare after $\mathrm{Enc}_n/\mathrm{Dec}_n$ and include its lost-mass flag. The refined scalar carrier provides an additional commuting diagram with its explicit original subcode and separate $O(2^{-n})$ error; it supplies no favorable original tariff. These formulas identify the comparison map and the original physical clock. They do not identify the encoded momentum/control graph with the original emergent spatial chart.

Combining (2) with the local common-family compiler's error $e_{\mathrm{local}}$ gives an actual **two-source response comparison through the same field** of size at most $e_{\mathrm{original}}+e_{\mathrm{local}}$, in the respective vector/complete-record norms. This is stronger than an unlabelled equality of marginal covariances. It still does not prove that a physical map between the two finite sources can be executed with the local compiler's tariff. A direct finite comparison is computable; its input size, matrix production, source preparation and dilation costs must be added.

##### 3. A fixed smooth test already detects the momentum-cell floor

##### Cell lemma

Let $h\in C^1(\mathbb{R}^3;\mathbb{C})$ have a derivative that is not identically zero. There is a compact rectangular box $B$, a complex phase $z$ of modulus one, a coordinate (say $p_1$), and $b>0$ such that

$$
\partial_1 \operatorname{Re}(z\, h(p))\ge b \text{ on } B.
$$

For all sufficiently fine cubic cell grids of width d, the union of cells entirely inside B has volume at least Vol(B)/2. Let $P_{d}$ be the L2 projection onto their full cell-indicator grid (with any additional cells elsewhere). For a cell C inside B, Fubini and the variance identity in its first coordinate give

$$
\int_C |h-\operatorname{average}_C h|^{2} \ge (b^{2}d^{2}/12) \operatorname{Vol}(C).
$$

Indeed, for fixed transverse coordinates, $|f(x)-f(y)|\ge b|x-y|$; the identity $\operatorname{Var}(f)=(1/(2d^{2}))\int\int|f(x)-f(y)|^{2}$ gives $b^{2}d^{2}/12$. Allowing the full-cell mean only adds the nonnegative variance of the transverse conditional means. Summing proves

$$
\lVert(I-P_d)h\rVert \ge b \sqrt{\operatorname{Vol}(B)/24}\, d=:c_h d.
\tag{3}
$$

This is a first-order **lower** bound for the fixed piecewise-constant comparison basis. Arbitrarily high smoothness does not raise its approximation order. It is not a Kolmogorov-width lower bound for all possible finite bases.

Choose a nonzero single smooth bump direction from the common family, with sufficiently small fixed amplitude to satisfy its envelope. Its original one-particle packet $h_*$ is Schwartz, nonzero and therefore nonconstant. The box/derivative data above can be certified by effective interval search. One completely explicit nondegeneracy choice puts the bump in $x_{1}>0$: for its real-field packet proportional to $\omega^{-1/2}\hat{g}$,

$$
\partial_1 h_*(0) \text{ is a nonzero imaginary multiple of } \int x_1 g(x)\, dx.
$$

Continuity then supplies B and b with computable positive rational lower bounds. The fixed original first-mode squeeze changes neither smoothness nor existence of such a packet. This test and its coherent output belong to the common family.

The one-particle component of its coherent vector is

$$
P_1 W(h_*)\Omega=i \exp(-\lVert h_*\rVert^{2}/2)\, h_*.
$$

Since $Q_n$'s one-particle image is exactly the original cell space, (3) implies

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert(I-Q_n)W(h_*)\Omega\rVert \\
&\ge\exp(-\lVert h_*\rVert^{2}/2)\, c_h d_n \\
&\ge c_*\, 4^{-n}
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
$$

for all sufficiently large n. The last inequality uses

$$
d_n=2\pi/(4^{n}+4^{-n})\ge\pi\, 4^{-n}.
$$

No occupation-tail estimate is used for this lower bound. It already occurs in particle number one and survives every larger occupation cutoff.

Every vector in the original code's $I_{n}$ image has distance at least (4) from this ideal output. With ancillas and complete record flags, project the compared target onto the same original source subspace: the same lower bound holds. Consequently, an actual original-register vector realization with error at most $\delta$ through **this $I_n$ comparison** requires

$$
4^{n}\ge c_*/\delta.
\tag{5}
$$

A weaker expectation-only comparison, a new decoder whose range is not $I_n H_n$, or a newly compressed interface need not satisfy this premise. Equation (5) is not asserted for them.

##### 4. What is forced if the whole original code is physically allocated

The original source-control record explicitly allocates $\lceil\log_2 D_n\rceil$ source qubits. Even an optimal exact binary encoding of the **whole** $H_{n}$ requires that many. Since

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\binom{M+R}{R}=\prod_{j=1}^{R} (M+j)/j \ge(M/R)^{R}, \\
&M_n=(16^{n}+1)^{3}\ge 4^{6n},\quad R_n=4^{n},
\end{aligned}
$$

one gets the exact simple bound

$$
\log_2 D_n\ge 10n\, 4^{n}.
\tag{6}
$$

Thus a fixed positive per-qubit (or per-C8-carrier) allocation price $\kappa$ gives, using (5),

$$
C_{\text{full original}}(\delta)\ge c\, \kappa\, \delta^{-1}\log(1/\delta)
\tag{7}
$$

for small $\delta$. Controllers, clocks, nuclear producers, routing, holding, readout and any autonomous history can only add nonnegative costs. This is a lower bound even when the matrix program has a very short description and the clock compilation is perfect. Global one-rail-per-basis-vector realization is still more expensive.

This excludes a particular proposed way of proving the geometric inequality: requiring the physically allocated **entire unchanged original register**, compared through $I_{n}$ at error $\delta$, while claiming that its complete carrier cost is bounded by a fixed-region polynomial in $\log(1/\delta)$.

##### Mandatory qualifications

1. Abstractly embedding the original register in a common carrier is not physical allocation of all its basis states. If only an accessible corner is physically supplied, (6) is not automatically its paid width. A new corner producer, state/interface/heat error theorem, clock comparison and tariff may avoid (7); these are constructive mathematical tasks, not forbidden possibilities.
2. The contradiction uses fixed physical $|\partial O|$, active volume, capacity, service prices, reference length and nonnegative polynomial coefficients, all independent of $\delta$. If a different geometry expression divides by a stage microscopic length $\ell_0=a_n$, a term $\operatorname{Vol}(O)/a_n^{3}$ already dominates (6); then (7) does **not** contradict that different bound. An accuracy-dependent capacity or active-volume convention likewise changes the conclusion. No microscopic denominator is silently held fixed or silently varied.
3. Literal F.10.4f.9 names fixed branch constants, $|\partial O|$, active volume and $C_{\mathrm{PU}}(O,\beta)$. On the fixed-center common family these quantities are fixed as $\delta$ varies. The common family's separate local-service area bound uses exactly this convention. Proposition F.10.4f.31.8 makes no claim about a different owner whose geometric units have other quantifiers.
4. The lower bound does not show that the canonical Sobolev approach is impossible, that every smooth-core source costs inverse accuracy, or that every original-source response comparison requires allocating $H_{n}$. It defeats this **specified full-register implementation route** and identifies what any cheaper route must replace explicitly.
5. The proof assumes no globally optimal programs, additional adopted premises or historical calibration.

##### 5. What the endpoint-clock result changes

A positive autonomous perfect-transfer history Hamiltonian realizes a finite gate word at prescribed endpoints with abstract clock dimension O(gate count). Its parameter bits, norm and holding extension can be polynomial. This avoids incorrectly transferring the all-time packet compiler's inverse-accuracy resource selector to a finite-endpoint problem.

It does not reduce the required data-code dimension in (6) when that entire original code is supplied. Nor does circuit universality of time-dependent quadratic/positive-Kerr pulses prove an exact polynomial static implementation of the history's gate-conditioned exchange blocks. The companion endpoint-clock theorem and static-source obstruction keep those two issues distinct. There is no unconditional claim that autonomy itself makes every endpoint computation expensive.

##### 6. Resulting decision for the common certificate

Completed: one smooth common census; same-family UCP/state/two-sided-GNS/physical-heat test bounds; actual correlated finite preparation with parity states; local finite-dimensional LAN charts; explicit Hadamard-Sobolev bridge; same-family full-regional nuclear tensors and split data; an effective original-register comparison with the original physical clock; a polynomial complete tariff for the specified local finite services; and the route-specific lower bound above.

Still not proved: one **complete** geometric tariff simultaneously paying the required original-input/heat/nuclear producers and their physical comparison on a compressed same-field source; an admitted polynomial static endpoint source if autonomy is demanded; and emergent spatial source-locality identification where required. The remaining issue is an explicit producer/source-and-cost conjunction, rather than disconnected LAN or Hadamard entries.

<a id="theorem-f104f319-structured-original-dispersion-finite-heat-source"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.31.9 (Structured Original-Dispersion Finite Heat Source).**

##### 1. Inputs, exact local interfaces and the required finite output vectors

Take the fixed smooth common family in Theorem F.10.4f.31.7, with the precision supplements of its section 5. At accuracy $\delta$ choose its growing local mode count $r$, occupation level $n$, exact local algebra $B_0=(M_n\oplus\mathbb{C})^{\otimes r}$, full-domain $\pi$ and local inclusion $\iota_0$. These local algebra and UCP objects are unchanged. The exact restricted state from that proof is denoted $\omega_{\delta,\mathrm{ref}}$ below; the final assembled certificate uses the actual ideal finite-source state, with its separately proved small discrepancy.

Let $C:\mathbb{R}^{2r}\to h_R$ be its real canonical packet column map. Normalize the real Hilbert symplectic form so

$$
C^{\mathsf T} J_h C=J_r,
$$

where $J_h,J_r$ are norm-one orthogonal complex structures. Fixed convention factors can be absorbed once into $C$. Its norm $M$ is bounded by a fixed polynomial in $r$, because its vacuum covariance has norm $v_r=O(1+r^{2})$. The finite complex span of its columns has dimension at most $2r$. The fixed first parity mode is among them.

For a retained source state and query, the required exact phase-space vector is

$$
\exp(-\beta H)\, \iota_0(b)\, \psi,\quad b=\pi(A),\quad H=d\Gamma(\omega).
$$

After the common spatial truncation, all its canonical operations and source vectors act in the Fock space over the complex span of C. The omitted smooth displacement tails have the already proved same-phase vector allocation. The commutant outside that **complex** span is genuinely vacuum; this is not a product assertion about the local CCR commutant.

We use a finite Gaussian canonical-coordinate change, with its complementary coordinates included, followed by local pair rotations, displacements and occupation restriction. All purifiers, reset flags and complete failure records remain. A uniform version permits any contraction $b\in B_0$: after cutting off the input Gaussian/prefix preparation in every canonical coordinate, $b$ maps a low block within levels $<n$ and acts as a scalar on a high block. Thus it does not increase any canonical occupation beyond $\max(n,K_{\mathrm{in}})$. Including the finite complementary Gaussian coordinates gives a total canonical number ceiling

$$
K_{\mathrm{tot}}\le d \max(n,K_{\mathrm{in}}),\quad d\le 2r,
$$

on the finite prepared approximation, uniformly in $\lVert b\rVert\le 1$. Its vector error from the exact $\iota_0(b)\psi$ is at most the separately allocated preparation error, by contractivity. The fixed-length efficient query circuit is required only for the declared word grammar, not for an arbitrary dense supplied $b$.

The construction below prices this common finite vector source and the physical heat output. It does not infer a short program from the total Hilbert-space dimension.

##### 2. Stable packet production without an inverse near-pure eigenvalue

##### 2.1 Momentum cut and thresholded frame

Let $P_{\Lambda}$ be multiplication by the indicator of $[-\Lambda,\Lambda]^3$ in the original momentum representation. For the disjoint smooth bumps and their $\omega^{\pm 1/2}$ columns, their explicit Gevrey-two Fourier tails give

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert(I-P_\Lambda)C\rVert &\le C_{\mathrm{poly}}(r,\Lambda) \\
&\qquad \exp[-c \sqrt{\rho_r \Lambda}].
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\rho_{r}$ is a fixed multiple of $r^{-2}$, choosing $\Lambda$ polynomial in $r$ and $p$ makes this at most $2^{-p}$. The optional fixed first-mode squeeze changes only fixed constants. Every momentum integral is still an integral of the original free-space $\omega$, not a Dirichlet covariance.

Use certified thresholded Gram-Schmidt on the at most $2r$ columns of $P_{\Lambda}C$. Retain a column when its residual is certified above $\theta$ and stop when all omitted residuals are certified $\le 2\theta$, using overlapping decision intervals. Let $q_1,\dots,q_d$ be the exact orthonormal frame described by the selected computable columns and their Gram matrix, and $Q$ its projection. Then

$$
\lVert(I-Q)P_\Lambda C\rVert\le 2 \sqrt{2r}\, \theta.
$$

Every retained pivot is $\ge\theta$. After first scaling all columns by their known norm bound, the usual determinant estimate gives an inverse Gram lower bound with logarithm $O(d\log(1/\theta)+d\log(d+1))$. Thus precision **bits** are polynomial. No exact rank decision or inverse smallest thermal occupation is used. Exact frame vectors are computable linear combinations; finite numerical outputs have certified enclosures.

Put $C_0=Q P_\Lambda C$ and $e=\lVert C_0-C\rVert$. We now correct its small symplectic error exactly within the produced frame. Write

$$
\begin{aligned}
&J_0=C_0^{\mathsf T} J_h C_0,\quad B=J_r^{-1}J_0, \\
&R=B^{-1/2},\quad D=C_0 R.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
$$

Choose $e$ so $\lVert B-I\rVert<1/8$. The inverse square root is its real convergent power series about $I$. Since $B^T J_r=J_r B$, the same identity holds for every real analytic function of $B$. Consequently

$$
\begin{aligned}
R^{\mathsf T} J_0 R&=R^{\mathsf T} J_r B R=J_r RBR=J_r, \\
D^{\mathsf T} J_h D&=J_r.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
$$

Also $\lVert R-I\rVert\le C\lVert B-I\rVert$ and $\lVert D-C\rVert\le C(1+M)^3 e$. These bounds have explicit convergent-series constants; choosing generous outward rational constants is sufficient. $D$ is an exact canonical frame in the finite momentum-cutoff space. Its fields are implementation/comparison fields, not a redefinition of the original local fields or $\iota$.

All matrix square roots in (1) use the near-identity gap, so the polynomial-bit statement does not depend on a complex Gram eigenvalue close to zero. In particular covariance eigenvalues close to the pure value 1/2 cause no inverse-precision energy or unbounded basis search.

##### 2.2 A polynomial-norm symplectic completion

Let $D^\sharp=J_r^{-1}D^T J_h$, so $D^\sharp D=I$, and $P=DD^\sharp$. Then $\lVert P\rVert\le\lVert D\rVert^{2}$. The real symplectic complement $L=\ker D^\sharp$ is the range of $I-P$. On an ordinary orthonormal basis of $L$, let $J_{L}$ be the restricted skew form.

Writing $P_{L}$ for the ordinary orthogonal projection onto $L$, the skew operator is $J_L=P_L J_h|_L$. Its inverse is explicitly $J_L^{-1}x=-(I-P)J_h x$ for $x\in L$: $P_L J_h D=0$ makes the correction vanish after applying $P_L J_h$, and the remaining term is $x$. Equivalently, for $x,y\in L$, $(I-P)(-J_h y)$ is its form-dual vector, with the sign changed consistently if the opposite $J$ convention is used. Hence

$$
\lVert J_L^{-1}\rVert\le\lVert I-P\rVert\le 1+\lVert D\rVert^{2}.
\tag{3}
$$

An orthonormal basis for $L$ is found from the full-row-rank matrix $D^T J_h$; its nonzero singular values are bounded below by $1/\lVert D\rVert$ because $D$ is canonical. Polar decomposition of $J_{L}$ and the positive factor $|J_L|^{-1/2}$ produce canonical complementary pairs with norm at most $\sqrt{1+\lVert D\rVert^{2}}$. Orthogonal complex-pair choices can use a largest-coordinate pivot; their finite-dimensional lower bounds are polynomial in $d$. This yields a symplectic completion $S$ with

$$
\lVert S\rVert+\lVert S^{-1}\rVert\le C(1+M),
\tag{4}
$$

up to a conservative polynomial enlargement. The norm argument applies equally to the exact original frame C in its actual finite complex span, before any momentum cut. Thus original target occupation-cutoff vectors have the same polynomial completion/number bounds even if their complex Gram matrix is ill-conditioned; algorithmic frame production is only needed for D. Every operation uses a displayed spectral or pivot bound. No inverse of a nearly pure complex-packet Gram matrix occurs. A finite Bloch-Messiah/Gaussian circuit for S is produced with the gap-free reconstruction and phase conventions.

##### 2.3 Why replacing the frame controls the actual operators and cutoff outputs

For completeness, a near-frame metaplectic comparison gives a uniform error beyond raw Weyl coefficients. Join $C$ to $D$ by $C_t^{\mathrm{raw}}=C+t(D-C)$, and correct its skew form by the same analytic formula (1), obtaining a canonical $C_{t}$ with $C_0=C,C_1=D$. For sufficiently small $\lVert D-C\rVert$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert C_t\rVert&\le 2(M+1), \\
\lVert\dot{C}_t\rVert&\le 8(M+1)^{2}\lVert D-C\rVert.
\end{aligned}
$$

Set $P_t=C_t C_t^\sharp$ and $A_t=\dot{C}_t C_t^\sharp$. The real finite-rank operator

$$
K_t=A_t-A_t^{\sharp}+P_t A_t^{\sharp} P_t
\tag{5}
$$

is symplectic-skew and satisfies $K_t C_t=\dot{C}_t$. The identity follows from differentiation of $C_t^\sharp C_t=I$; in particular $P_t A_t P_t=-P_t A_t^\sharp P_t$. Its norm is bounded by a conservative $512(M+1)^8\lVert D-C\rVert$, and its support lies in the fixed finite complex span of $C,D$. Solve $S_t'=K_t S_t$, $S_0=I$. Then $S_1 C=D$, and $\lVert S_t\rVert,\lVert S_t^{-1}\rVert$ are bounded by $\exp(\int\lVert K_t\rVert)$.

The finite-mode metaplectic implementer $U_{t}$ has a quadratic generator. Elementary ladder bounds give

$$
\lVert H_{K_t}\xi\rVert\le C(d+1)\lVert K_t\rVert\, \lVert(N+1)\xi\rVert,
$$

with its normal-ordering scalar retained. A Bogoliubov change with bounded $S_{t}$ similarly bounds $\lVert(N+1)U_t\xi\rVert$ by $C(d+1)\exp(C\int\lVert K_t\rVert)\lVert(N+1)\xi\rVert$. Duhamel therefore gives a polynomial constant $C_{\mathrm{frame}}$ such that

$$
\lVert(U_1-I)\xi\rVert\le C_{\mathrm{frame}} \lVert D-C\rVert\, \lVert(N+1)\xi\rVert.
\tag{6}
$$

The phase is fixed by the continuous metaplectic path, not inferred from a covariance alone. This implementer is used to prove the comparison; the algorithm may directly synthesize the finite D-frame rather than physically run (5).

It intertwines every canonical field, its number spectral projections, parity matrix units and bounded local functional calculus. Thus it controls the **whole** occupation-cutoff algebra as well as the raw Weyl/pair words. For a contraction $b$, compare $U_{1}b\psi$ to $b\psi$ using (6), and $U_1\psi$ to $\psi$ for the input; finite occupation approximations from Section 1 supply the required uniform number moment. Approximation residuals cost at most twice their vector norm under two unitaries. This makes near-frame error a separately allocated polynomially controlled implementation error on every retained vector and, if requested, uniformly over the finite $B_0$ unit ball. It is not an unjustified coefficient estimate for a potentially large cutoff polynomial.

##### 3. Physical-particle tails after correlated preparation and recovery

The local canonical cutoff is different from a cutoff in the original complex Fock particle number. Both are controlled explicitly.

Let $U_{S}$ be the Gaussian coordinate change of Section 2, with $d$ modes and $\lVert S\rVert^{2}\le w$, a polynomial in $r$. Let $\xi$ be any unit vector supported on canonical total number $\le K_{\mathrm{tot}}$, with arbitrary spectator flags. For $s=1$,

&\le\lVert\exp(tN/2)U_S \exp(-N/2)\rVert_2^{2}.

The squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm is the number generating function of the squeezed thermal state, times $\operatorname{Tr}\exp(-N)$. Its covariance norm is at most $(w/2)\coth(1/2)$. Choose

\exp(t)-1\le 1/[2(w \coth(1/2)+1)].

&\le\exp(K_{\mathrm{tot}})[2/(1-\exp(-1))]^{d}=:M_{\mathrm{phys}}.

For spectators this is an operator bound on the signal factor, not a product-state assumption. Here $t^{-1}=\mathrm{poly}(r)$, and $\log M_{\mathrm{phys}}=\mathrm{poly}(r,n,K_{\mathrm{in}})$. Therefore

is below $\eta$ with a polynomial $L$ in $r,n,K_{\mathrm{in}},\log(1/\eta)$. This covers every correlated cutoff/recovery vector of Section 1, not merely coherent input vectors. Exact target vectors add their separately bounded source/occupation approximation residual.

The Gaussian state and frame circuits can themselves be truncated using the coherent Gaussian/flag bounds. All their finite occupation cutoffs, phase corrections, covariance inflation and ancillary environments are charged. Equations (7)-(8) do not replace those synthesis errors by a marginal trace-distance assertion.

##### 4. Bounded-energy one-particle Krylov source

The produced $q$-frame lies in $h_\Lambda=P_\Lambda h$. On that Hilbert space,

$$
m\le\omega\le E:=\sqrt{m^{2}+3\Lambda^{2}}.

Set $A=\omega/E$, a positive contraction, and let $P_0$ be projection onto $\operatorname{span}\{q_i\}$. For degree $L_{K}$, form the Krylov vectors $A^j q_i$, $0\le j\le L_K$. Their norms are at most one. An exact Krylov space would preserve every required moment through degree $L_{K}$.

The uniform polynomial approximation used here is elementary. On $[0,1]$, truncate the exponential Taylor series for $\exp(-z E x)$, where either $z=\beta\in[0,B]$ or $z=it$ with $|t|\le T$. Its remainder is at most $\exp(|z|E)(|z|E)^{L_K+1}/(L_K+1)!$. Taking $L_K$ to be a sufficiently large fixed multiple of $E(B+T)+p+1$ makes this $\le 2^{-p}$, by $n!\ge(n/e)^n$. As in the original thresholded Krylov proof, induction gives the vector mismatch of compressed $j$th moments at most $2(j+1)\sqrt{d}\,\theta_K$. The absolute coefficient sum of the chosen exponential polynomial is at most $\exp(E(B+T))$. Therefore its additional error is at most

$$
2(L_K+1)\sqrt{d}\, \theta_K \exp(E(B+T)).
\tag{9}
$$

Choose $\theta_{K}$ to put (9) in its allocation. Its negative logarithm is polynomial in $p,r$. There are at most $d(L_K+1)$ generators; the determinant/pivot bound gives polynomially many matrix bits, not an inverse-gap-sized physical parameter.

Let

$$
h_{\mathrm{fin}}=P \omega P \text{ on } \operatorname{ran} P,\quad J_{\mathrm{fin}}\colon \operatorname{ran} P\to h_\Lambda\to h.
$$

It is an actual positive finite matrix, $mI\le h_{\mathrm{fin}}\le EI$. Its norm is independent of Gram conditioning. Finite numerical production keeps that positive spectral interval by outward-error inflation/clipping; Duhamel charges the actual matrix error separately. Every moment is an integral of $\bar{q}_i$ times $(\omega/E)^j$ times $q_{k}$ on the finite momentum box. Analytic-strip quadrature applies after extending conjugate Fourier factors as their reflected analytic transforms. The normalization coefficients may have large magnitude, but their logarithms are polynomial by the pivot bound; this enlarges quadrature order and arithmetic bits polynomially. No dense many-particle integration occurs.

For every v in the original q-frame and the retained beta/time windows,

$$

\lVert J_{\mathrm{fin}} \exp(-it h_{\mathrm{fin}})v-\exp(-it \omega)v\rVert&\le e_1\lVert v\rVert.

The exact polynomial part intertwines up to (9), and the two functional-calculus remainders supply the remaining errors. This gives the actual original physical time t. It does not call $\beta$ a physical unitary waiting time.

##### 5. Second quantization and the complete heat flag

On l-particle inputs in the q-frame, contractions tensor-telescope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\lVert\Gamma_l(J_{\mathrm{fin}} \exp(-\beta h_{\mathrm{fin}})) \\
&\qquad -\Gamma_l(\exp(-\beta \omega))\rVert\le l\, e_1,

It proves a permitted retained-core theorem, not the broader regional realization named by the target. The full-domain definition of $\pi$ does not change its approximation domain. The old canonical Sobolev choice is unchanged and has no transferred polylogarithmic producer bound.
2. **Expanded-mode/collar geometric costs.** Growing r within the fixed compact smooth computational core is paid here. Uniform recovery on expanding regional mode sets, shrinking collars, or geometry that changes the localization constants requires corresponding estimates. A fixed inner split factor and fixed-support cost divided by the containing region's area do not prove those broader scalings.
3. **Near-budget nuclear-certificate production.** The effective producer of Proposition F.10.4f.31.0 uses a declared looser determinant ceiling. The original target retains a near-budget production requirement. One must construct and price a verifiable finite/on-demand coefficient producer with an evaluated budget and a certified tail at that original ceiling. A compressed generator plus an analytically summed tail may suffice if it supplies the requested certificate; physical enumeration of every tensor term is not presumed mandatory. An unevaluated infinite formula, effectivity alone, or the new heat circuit does not establish its production tariff. This is a separate production question.
4. **Microscopic-clock/source scope.** The actual scalar-register comparison and original clock are explicit; the new fixed-service source has a complete tariff. Any original requirement that physically deploys the whole microscopic source, demands its complete input channel, or couples its carrier inventory to the geometric budget still needs the corresponding record. The present theorem's comparison-only route is not a claim that those larger physical services are free.
5. **Broader LAN/Hadamard domains.** The gates and finite preparation costs are discharged for every state/chart in the same declared smooth family. If the owner retains additional families or an executed LAN comparison at an accuracy-dependent sample count, those genuinely additional states/services require their own bounds and costs. They are not an open gap inside the theorem above.

The original fixed-rank and unrestricted full-unit-ball GNS obstructions remain valid. The new family changes neither negative result. A requested owner-bound verification record can quote the proved theorem and its actual tests.

<a id="theorem-f104f3111-complete-smooth-ball-profiles-and-actual-covariance-producer"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.31.11 (Complete Smooth Ball Profiles and Actual-Covariance Producer).**

##### 1. Exact construction on the actual retained ball

Fix spatial dimension $d$ ($d=3$ in the scalar branch), a center $c$ and a radius $R>0$. Geometry has certified digit producers. Write $B=B(c,R)$. For $z=(x-c)/R$ in the unit ball, put

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=z/\sqrt{1-|z|^{2}},\quad u=1+|y|^{2}, \\
z&=y/\sqrt{u},\qquad J(y)=u^{(d+2)/2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

$J$ is the determinant of $dy/dz$: its tangential eigenvalues are $\sqrt{u}$, and its radial eigenvalue is $u^{3/2}$. Define the unitary map from $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^d,dy)$ onto $L^{2}(B,dx)$ by

$$
(U_R h)(x)=R^{-d/2} J(y)^{1/2} h(y).
$$

Let $H_{n}$ be the physicists' Hermite polynomial, $H_0=1$, $H_1=2y$, $H_{n+1}=2yH_n-2nH_{n-1}$, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
&h_\alpha(y)=\pi^{-d/4} \prod_i \bigl[H_{\alpha_i}(y_i)/\sqrt{2^{\alpha_i} \alpha_i!}\bigr] \exp(-|y|^{2}/2). \\
&g_\alpha^{R}=U_R h_\alpha \text{ on } B, \text{ and zero outside its closure.}
\end{aligned}
$$

Order $\alpha$ in graded lexicographic order, beginning $\alpha=0$; write $g_j$, $j\ge 1$, $K_j=|\alpha_j|$. There are $\binom{K+d}{d}$ modes through total degree $K$. In particular $K_j\le j$, and $K_j=O_d(j^{1/d})$. No eigenvalue sorting, eigenvector selection, degeneracy test, Gram pivot or spectral gap oracle occurs.

The $g_{j}$ are real and exactly $L^{2}$-orthonormal, and form a complete basis of $L^{2}(B)$. The zero extensions are $C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}^d)$, supported in the closed ball: explicitly each is a finite sum of powers of $(1-|z|^{2})$, polynomial factors in $z$, and $\exp[-|z|^{2}/(2(1-|z|^{2}))]$. Every derivative vanishes at the sphere. They are not claimed individually to lie in $C^\infty_c(B)$, whose support must stay a positive distance from the boundary. Section 4 proves the correct local-net inclusion by inner approximation.

The elementary Hermite identities used below agree with the DLMF (National Institute of Standards and Technology n.d., §§18.3 and 18.9). All additional transformation and complexity estimates are proved here. Completeness can also be checked without a spectral theorem: orthogonality to every polynomial times $\exp(-|y|^{2}/2)$ makes the entire Gaussian-weighted Fourier transform vanish to all orders at zero, hence vanish identically; Fourier uniqueness then gives zero.

This is a coordinate/profile construction. If an auxiliary operator is desired, $U_R(-\Delta_y+|y|^{2})U_R^{-1}$ has these eigenfunctions and known eigenvalues $2|\alpha|+d$. It is NOT the physical scalar Hamiltonian or the free-space one-particle operator $\omega=(m^{2}-\Delta_x)^{1/2}$. All covariances and heat maps retain the original $\omega$.

##### 2. Polynomial H1 bounds on entire low-mode subspaces

For $R=1$ direct differentiation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
T_i&=U_1^{-1} \partial_{x_i} U_1 \\
&=\sqrt{u}\,[\partial_{y_i}+y_i(y\cdot\operatorname{grad}_y)+(d+2)y_i/2].
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.1}
$$

The Hermite ladder identities are

$$
\begin{aligned}
y_i h_\alpha&=\sqrt{\alpha_i/2}\, h_{\alpha-e_i}+\sqrt{(\alpha_i+1)/2}\, h_{\alpha+e_i}, \\
\partial_i h_\alpha&=\sqrt{\alpha_i/2}\, h_{\alpha-e_i}-\sqrt{(\alpha_i+1)/2}\, h_{\alpha+e_i}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently any word of l multiplications/derivatives has norm at most

$$
[2(K+d+l)]^{l/2}
$$

on the entire total-degree $\le K$ Hermite subspace. This is a subspace operator estimate, not merely a bound on individual columns.

Since $\lVert D_z y\rVert\le u^{3/2}$, (2.1) gives

$$
\lVert\operatorname{grad} U_1 h\rVert \le \lVert u^{3/2} \operatorname{grad} h\rVert + ((d+2)/2)\lVert\sqrt{u}\,y h\rVert.
$$

Squaring the polynomial weights and expanding $u^{3}$ and $u|y|^{2}$ expresses each norm square as a finite positive sum of squared norms of ladder words of length at most four. The sum of coefficients of $u^{3}$ is $(d+1)^{3}$; that of $u|y|^{2}$ is $d(d+1)$. For example the explicit generous constant $C_d=10(d+4)^3$ suffices to conclude

$$
\lVert\operatorname{grad} U_R h\rVert \le R^{-1} C_d (K+d+4)^{2} \lVert h\rVert.
\tag{2.2}
$$

Thus the gradient Gram matrix of the first r profiles satisfies

$$
G_r \le R^{-2} C_d^{2}(K_r+d+4)^{4} I.
$$

It need not be diagonal. No step in Theorem F.10.4f.31.11 replaces it by a diagonal matrix.

For the actual massive free-space covariance and a fixed canonical scale $\mu$, the positive and negative blocks obey

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert Y_r\rVert &\le (2\mu)^{-1} \sqrt{m^{2}+R^{-2} C_d^{2}(K_r+d+4)^{4}}, \\
\lVert X_r\rVert &\le \mu/(2m).
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.3}
$$

Here concavity/Cauchy–Schwarz gives $\langle f,\omega f\rangle\le\lVert f\rVert\sqrt{m^2\lVert f\rVert^2+\lVert\nabla f\rVert^2}$, and $\omega^{-1}\le m^{-1}$. Hence the full covariance norm is polynomial in $r$ and $R^{-1}$. The uncertainty relation gives the familiar inverse-polynomial lower bound $V_r\ge(4\lVert V_r\rVert)^{-1}I$. Any fixed first-pair canonical squeeze changes only fixed constants. There is no fictitious Dirichlet vacuum.

##### 3. Derivative, Gevrey and exponential Fourier-tail bounds

There is an effective $C_{d}\ge 1$ such that, for every ordered spatial derivative of length s,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert\partial^{s} g_\alpha^{R}\rVert_2 \\
&\le R^{-s} C_d^{s+1}(s!)^{2}(K+4s+d+1)^{2s}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.1}
$$

An explicit coefficient-majorant algorithm proves and can compute this bound. Compose (2.1) $s$ times in normal order. The coefficients of derivative order $b$ are symbols of growth at most $2s+b$. The starting first-order coefficients $\sqrt{u}(\delta_{ij}+y_i y_j)$ have growth 3 and the zeroth-order coefficient $(d+2)y_i\sqrt{u}/2$ has growth 2. Their $q$th derivatives obey $C_d^{q+1}q!(1+|y|)^{\mathrm{order}-q}$; these follow by differentiating $u^{1/2}$ and $u\ge 1$. In a composition term, each derivative falling on a coefficient reduces growth by one; a derivative retained on $h$ raises $b$ by one. This proves growth $2s+b$ by induction. The product of the derivative factorials is $\le s!$, and the Leibniz placements and term count are bounded by $C_d^s s!$. Thus the sum of coefficient majorants is $\le C_d^{s+1}(s!)^{2}$. Replace a growth weight $(1+|y|)^{2s+b}$ by its positive multinomial majorant. Ladder-word length is at most $(2s+b)+b\le 4s$, which proves (3.1), enlarging $C_d$. This argument is valid for every vector in the degree $\le K$ subspace, not only basis vectors. Fixed Sobolev embedding order $q>d/2$ adds $q$ derivatives to (3.1), and supplies the corresponding sup norm bound. Boundary flatness justifies use of global zero-extension Sobolev norms.

In particular there are effective fixed constants, depending on d,a,R, such that the coefficient class in Section 5 is uniformly Gevrey four:

$$
\lVert\partial^{s} f\rVert_\infty+\lVert\partial^{s} k\rVert_\infty \le A B^{s}(s!)^{4}.
\tag{3.2}
$$

To verify the factorial index rather than hide an index-dependent constant, insert (3.1), $K_j\le j$ and the coefficient bound $E e^{-aj}(j+1)^{-3}$. The sum of $e^{-aj}(j+4s+C)^{2s+C}$ is at most $C_a^{s+1}(s!)^{2}$ times a fixed polynomial in $s$. This follows from the $\gamma$ integral for $\sum e^{-aj}j^n$, or from $(j+4s+C)^n\le 2^n[j^n+(4s+C)^n]$. The fixed extra polynomial and Sobolev shift are absorbed into $B^s$. The original two factorials in (3.1) give (3.2). At $s=0$ enlarge $A$ separately.

A particularly convenient certified Fourier cutoff does not require optimizing Gevrey constants. Let p be requested precision bits, let K bound all retained Hermite degrees, and fix the finite polynomial momentum weight of the desired tail. Choose

$$
\begin{aligned}
s&=C[p+\log(r+2)+\log(2+R+R^{-1}+m+m^{-1})] + C_{\mathrm{weight}}, \\
P&=C_{d,\mathrm{weight}} \max(1,R^{-1})\, (s+K+d+1)^{4}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.3}
$$

Plancherel, (3.1), factorial $\le s^s$, and the inequality on $\{|\xi|>P\}$, $|\xi|^{-s}\le P^{-s}$, show that the squared weighted Fourier tail of every retained column is $\le 2^{-p}$ after increasing the computable constants. Replacing $s$ by $s+\text{the fixed weight}$ covers $\omega^{\pm 1}$, physical energy moments and the fixed momentum derivatives needed by the compiler. Coordinate multiplication for momentum derivatives is bounded on this fixed ball and is handled by the same finite derivative-majorant calculation. Polynomial factors from $r$ simultaneous columns are covered by $\log(r+2)$. The cutoff $P$ is polynomial in $r,p$ and the declared geometric scales; it is not exponential in the profile index.

##### 4. The full local Cauchy topology and the same regional net

For $\phi\in C^\infty_c(B)$, $U_R^{-1}\phi$ is a smooth compactly supported function of $y$, hence Schwartz. Its Hermite coefficients decay faster than every power of total degree: repeated application of $-\Delta_y+|y|^{2}$ and the eigenvalue $2|\alpha|+d$ proves this directly. Combining that decay with (3.1) proves convergence of its Hermite partial sums after $U_{R}$ in every fixed global $H^s_x$ norm. Thus the finite span of the $g_{j}$ approximates every $C^\infty_c(B)$ in $H^1$, and therefore in the physical $H^{+1/2}$ and $H^{-1/2}$ Cauchy norms.

Conversely each $g_{j}$ has flat boundary jets. Multiplying it by a smooth inner cutoff that equals one away from a collar of width $\epsilon$ produces $C^\infty_c(B)$ functions converging to $g_{j}$ in $H^s$ for every fixed $s$. Powers of $\epsilon^{-1}$ from cutoff differentiation are beaten by the $\exp(-c/\epsilon)$ flat tail. This proves $g_{j}$ belongs to the closure of the original local test-function space; it does not silently identify $H_0^{1/2}$ with some different trace convention. Define the local Cauchy space as precisely the closure of $C^\infty_c(B)$ in the original free-space Cauchy norm. Both inclusions now hold.

Strong continuity of Weyl operators in that one-particle norm implies

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{vonNeumann}\{ W(h(f,k)) : f,k \text{ finite linear combinations of } g_j \} \\
&= A(D(B)),
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.1}
$$

for the same original free scalar time-zero/diamond net. The real symplectic form remains the original $L^{2}$ pairing. The first $r$ profile pairs are exactly canonical, and their omitted pairs commute symplectically. Their regular finite-mode type-I factors $M_{r}$ are increasing, and their union generates the whole regional algebra in the von Neumann sense.

Equation (4.1) is a density/generation result. It is NOT uniform approximation of the regional operator unit ball by bounded-rank UCP maps, nor a uniform GNS recovery statement, nor a complexity bound for approximating an arbitrarily supplied local observable. It also does not prove convergence of a particular state-nonpreserving conditional expectation on every regional vector from density alone.

##### 5. One effective growing smooth Cauchy envelope

Fix $a>0$ and $E>0$, and admit the real coefficient pairs satisfying

$$
\sum_{j\ge 1} e^{2aj}(j+1)^{6} [|c_j^{f}|^{2}+|c_j^{k}|^{2}] \le E^{2}.
\tag{5.1}
$$

A supplied member must carry a coefficient and envelope certificate whose description, arithmetic, communication and storage through index r and precision p cost one specified polynomial in r,p. The analytic ellipsoid alone does not supply such programs. Finite rational coefficient data with a certified strict margin give nonempty examples in every finite mode sector.

Using $\lVert g_j\rVert_{H^1}\le C_{d,R}(j+1)^{2}$, Cauchy–Schwarz gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert f-f_r\rVert_{H^{1}}+\lVert k-k_r\rVert_{H^{1}} \\
&\le C_{d,R,a}\, E\, e^{-ar}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5.2}
$$

Indeed the remaining sum is bounded by $E$ times the square root of $\sum_{j>r}e^{-2aj}(j+1)^{-2}$. This avoids the invalid diagonal-gradient argument. The same bound holds in the original one-particle Cauchy norm, with its actual mass/units constant. Thus $r=O(\log(1/\delta))$ suffices for the declared envelope, the covariance ceiling is polynomial in $r$, and all common-family occupation, word-prefix, smooth-difference/Hadamard and finite-service arguments can be re-run with these substituted constants.

The envelope is not all local Cauchy data at one fixed E. Nevertheless it supplies nonzero small multiples of every basis direction, and their Weyl operators generate (4.1); integer powers permit arbitrary amplitudes for generation. That generation argument is not a free finite-service circuit for unbounded amplitudes, word lengths or arbitrary full-regional tests. Each actual service retains its specified amplitude and word/program costs.

##### 6. A certified polynomial-bit actual-covariance producer

The following is an interval algorithm, not an empirical quadrature assertion. For fixed d and fixed derivative/weight orders, its arithmetic operations and precision lengths are bounded by one polynomial in r,p and the displayed geometric scales.

For direct waveform/profile access at a rational $x$, first decide membership in the rational ball (or enclose the computable geometry to the requested support/error margin). Outside the ball return zero. Inside, put $t=1-|z|^{2}$. Differentiating the explicit finite Hermite formula bounds a spatial jet of order $b$ by $\exp[-1/(C t)+C_d(K+b+1)\log((K+b+2)/t)]$ times explicit $R$ factors. If $t^{-1}$ exceeds a sufficiently large fixed polynomial in $K,b,p$ and the geometric scales, this majorant certifies every requested jet entry below $2^{-p}$ and zero may be returned with that error. Otherwise all rational/algebraic arguments have polynomial magnitude and bit length. Truncated $d$-variate power-series arithmetic through order $b$ computes the jet of the explicit formula in polynomially many operations ($d$ fixed); coefficient bit lengths and the extra cancellation precision are polynomial in $K,b,p$ and input bit length. Exact boundary points have the certified zero jet. Thus polynomial-bit production includes spatial profiles and finite jets, not only integral values. For nonrational geometry, a finite input description must provide the stated certified digit routine; no exact boundary-decision oracle is needed, since an uncertainty interval wholly inside the small-tail collar can return the same zero enclosure. Points away from that collar are classified by a finite precision comparison.

First evaluate Fourier columns in y variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\hat{g}_\alpha^{R}(\xi)&=(2\pi)^{-d/2} R^{d/2} \exp(-i \xi\cdot c) \\
&\qquad \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} u^{-(d+2)/4} h_\alpha(y) \\
&\qquad \exp[-i R\, \xi\cdot y/\sqrt{u}]\, dy.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6.1}
$$

Hermite polynomial coefficients are exact integers from the finite recurrence, of bit length O((K+1)log(K+2)). Factorials and normalization constants have ordinary certified polynomial-time integer and elementary-function algorithms. A crude uniform coefficient majorant gives

$$
|h_\alpha(y)| \le \exp[C_d(K+1)\log(K+2)]\,(1+|y|)^{K} \exp(-|y|^{2}/2).
$$

Consequently truncation to $[-T,T]^d$ with $T=C_d(K+p+1)$ makes the $L^1$ tail, with every fixed polynomial derivative/weight factor, smaller than $2^{-p}$. The deliberately loose linear $T$ avoids dependence on a sharp oscillator asymptotic; Gaussian tail integrals are bounded by integration by parts. $T$ remains polynomial. Allocation for many Fourier evaluations uses extra precision bits, or a uniform bound at the required outer-quadrature nodes.

On a fixed complex tube $|\operatorname{Im}y|<\eta_d$, $\operatorname{Re}(1+\sum y_i^{2})\ge 1-\eta_d^{2}>1/2$. The chosen square root and powers of $u$ are single-valued analytic there. On that tube with $|\operatorname{Re}y|\le\sqrt{d}\,T+1$, the logarithm of an absolute integrand majorant is bounded by

$$
C_d[(K+1)\log(K+T+2)+T^{2}+R|\xi|+p+1].
$$

This follows directly from the finite Hermite polynomial, Gaussian, and analytic coordinate map; even the cruder polynomial-in-$T$ bound for $y/\sqrt{u}$ is adequate. Split the real $y$-box into constant-size cubes strictly inside this tube. On each, integrate the Taylor polynomial in $d$ variables exactly and use the geometric Cauchy remainder. Taylor order polynomial in $p,K,T,R|\xi|$ suffices; there are $O((1+T)^d)$ cubes and $O(\mathrm{order}^d)$ coefficients per cube. Coefficients are generated by truncated power-series arithmetic for multiplication, square root/inverse powers and exponential. Increase working precision by the logarithm of the displayed absolute majorant and the polynomial operation count. Outward-rounded interval arithmetic then certifies the requested absolute error. Fixed dimension is essential; no dimension-free assertion is made.

For the covariance use exactly

$$
\begin{aligned}
X_{jk}&=(\mu/2) \int \overline{\hat{g}_j(\xi)}\, (m^{2}+|\xi|^{2})^{-1/2}\, \hat{g}_k(\xi)\, d\xi, \\
Y_{jk}&=(1/(2\mu)) \int \overline{\hat{g}_j(\xi)}\, (m^{2}+|\xi|^{2})^{1/2}\, \hat{g}_k(\xi)\, d\xi.
\end{aligned}
$$

Truncate $\xi$ using (3.3). Products' tails are controlled by Cauchy–Schwarz with the weighted column tails. In a fixed strip of width less than $m/(4\sqrt{d})$, the physical $\omega$ powers are analytic with a certified nonzero denominator. Continue the real conjugate Fourier factor as $\hat{g}_j(-\xi)$. The compact support gives the strip bound $|\hat{g}_j(\xi+i\eta)|\le C R^{d/2}\exp(R|\eta|+|c\cdot\eta|)$, using $\lVert g_j\rVert_1\le\operatorname{vol}(B)^{1/2}$. The common translation phases cancel in covariance products, so no artificial center-dependent covariance cost is needed. Constant-size outer cells, Taylor or Gaussian quadrature of order polynomial in $p,\log P,R$ and $m^{-1}$, and calls to (6.1) at polynomially many nodes certify every entry. If the selected cubature uses derivatives, the same $y$-integral with bounded powers of $x$ supplies them. Entry error $\le\epsilon/(2r)$ certifies the $2r$-by-$2r$ operator error.

All truncation radii, node counts, recurrence degrees, intermediate bit lengths and precision allocations are polynomial. No statement here relies on exact covariance diagonalization; the existing regularized symplectic/metaplectic compiler is to be used. Exact orthogonality and canonical commutators are mathematical identities of the defining profiles, not floating-point declarations.

##### 7. Geometry, collar and full-certificate boundaries

This construction works directly on balls, so cubes need not replace the retained ball geometry. For ellipsoids one can compose with a fixed affine map and charge its singular values. Different radii give different bases; no unproved nested-basis compatibility across balls is asserted. For each ball separately the same original net is recovered by (4.1).

Radius scaling is explicit: $s$ derivatives cost $R^{-s}$, $H^1$ grows as $R^{-1}$, Fourier cutoffs and physical covariances carry $R^{-1}$, and Fourier evaluation carries $R$ and the requested frequency. Bounds are polynomial in these numerical scales and in certified digit costs, not automatically polynomial in the bit length of an arbitrarily enormous or tiny geometric number. Fixed $R$ in a declared compact positive range gives uniform constants. A lower bound $R\ge R_*$ controls inverse-radius constants only; it does not by itself control every large-$R$ physical or compiler resource or convert a volume cost into an area cost.

Approximating a flat profile by an interior-supported one is effective: the explicit formula bounds an $\epsilon$ collar by a polynomial in $\epsilon^{-1},K$ times $\exp[-c/\epsilon]$. Taking $\epsilon^{-1}$ polynomial in $K+p$ yields a $p$-bit Sobolev approximation with polynomial seminorm/cutoff costs for fixed derivative order. This numerical support collar is not the split inclusion's geometric collar. A split factor between $B_{R}$ and $B_{R+\ell}$, its canonical frame/repair producer, a full expanded nuclear tensor and their $\ell$-dependent tariffs remain separate records. No uniform shrinking-collar area law follows from this basis.

Accordingly Theorem F.10.4f.31.11 replaces the disjoint-bump span of Theorem F.10.4f.31.7 by an effective complete smooth growing local core with polynomial input covariance costs. To assert any larger F14 finite-algebra/heat/geometric result, substitute it into the common/heat compiler as in Theorem F.10.4f.31.12, prove the nominated full-domain comparisons on their actual declared test sets, and include every retained split, nuclear-certificate, source, LAN sample, protocol, collar and microscopic-clock cost. The unrestricted-GNS and original fixed-rank obstructions remain unchanged.

<a id="theorem-f104f3112-complete-ball-heat-and-source-transfer"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.31.12 (Complete-Ball Heat and Source Transfer).**

##### 1. Branch and geometric quantifiers

Fix one actual ball $B=B(c,R)$, with $0<R<\infty$, the original mass $m>0$ and free-space $\omega=(m^{2}-\Delta)^{1/2}$, positive heat window $[\beta_0,\beta_1]$, bounded physical-time and holding windows, fixed profile envelope, fixed word/protocol lengths and the nominated finite-precision positive rail-service law. Geometry and fixed constants have the certified digit producers specified in the profile proof. Constants below may depend on $R$, $R^{-1}$, $m$, $m^{-1}$, the declared collars and these fixed data.

The primary region is $O=D(B)$. Any ambient containing diamonds may also be retained, with the same fixed supported input family; full-net generation below refers to this original $O$, not automatically to every larger ambient region. Choose a fixed split collar $O_-\subset\subset O\subset\subset O_+$ and its same-net type-I intermediate factor. Literal F.10.4f.3 does not demand that the canonical finite-mode factor equal this split factor. Newly executing an entire canonical split-unitary producer is a separate priced service if requested.

One may let $R$ range over a declared compact interval $[R_{\min},R_{\max}]$ with uniform supplied constants and fixed positive collar bounds. The estimates are then uniform after retaining both $R_{\min}^{-1}$ and $R_{\max}$. A lower bound $R\ge R_*$ alone does not control every large-$R$ Fourier-production cost. No variable-radius or shrinking-collar area law is inferred from a fixed-ball theorem.

Use the complete real orthonormal basis $g_{j}$ of `Theorem F.10.4f.31.11`, obtained by pulling the Hermite basis through $y=z/\sqrt{1-|z|^{2}}$, $z=(x-c)/R$. The finite span is dense in the original regional Cauchy topology, and every $g_{j}$ is globally smooth and flat on the sphere. Individual supports may touch the sphere; membership in the original local space is proved by inner-cutoff approximation, not by falsely claiming $g_{j}$ belongs to $C_c^\infty(B)$.

Declare, before accuracy, the computational envelope

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\sum_j \exp(2aj)(j+1)^{6} (|c_j^{f}|^{2}+|c_j^{k}|^{2})\le E^{2}, \\
&f=\sum_j c_j^{f} g_j,\quad k=\sum_j c_j^{k} g_j.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use the same uniformly polynomial coefficient-program requirement, same fixed first-mode parity embedding, fixed finite-dimensional z charts at each supplied classical h, same bounded-length Weyl/parity source states and prefixes, and same finite l1-normalized tests with norm floor $\eta$. This is a new explicitly declared branch. The old Sobolev core and the disjoint-bump branch of Theorem F.10.4f.31.10 keep their original definitions and costs.

##### 2. Exact substitution ledger

The following are the only profile inputs used by the common/heat compiler of Theorems F.10.4f.31.7 and F.10.4f.31.9. Each is available for the new basis with the displayed replacement, so no diagonal-gradient or fictitious vacuum step remains.

##### 2.1 Canonical commutation and spatial tail

The profiles are exactly L2-orthonormal. Their real Cauchy pairs therefore have the same canonical symplectic form and the retained/omitted pairs commute symplectically. The profile proof gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert f-f_r\rVert_{H^{1}}+\lVert k-k_r\rVert_{H^{1}}&\le C_{R,a,d}\, E \exp(-ar), \\
\lVert h-h_r\rVert&\le C_{m,R,a,d}\, E \exp(-ar).
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
$$

This bound is proved by Cauchy--Schwarz on the weighted coefficients and individual H1 upper bounds. The gradient Gram is not diagonal, and no diagonal identity is used.

Consequently the exact full-domain conditional expectation onto the actual r-mode CCR factor still sends a retained word to

$$
E_r(A)=\exp(i \theta) \exp(-\lVert h_{\mathrm{tail}}\rVert^{2}/2)\, A_r.
$$

The residual Weyl operator commutes with every retained pair/parity operation. The exact same spatial source/prefix and two-sided vector estimates follow from (1), with the original Weyl phase included.

##### 2.2 Actual covariance and canonical completion

Let $K_{r}$ be the largest retained Hermite total degree. The whole-subspace estimate is

$$
\lVert\operatorname{grad} f_r\rVert\le R^{-1} C_d(K_r+d+4)^{2}\lVert f_r\rVert.
$$

Thus the physical free-space covariance has

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert V_r\rVert&\le v_r:=\max\bigl(\mu/(2m), \\
&\qquad (2\mu)^{-1} \sqrt{m^{2}+R^{-2} C_d^{2}(K_r+d+4)^{4}}\bigr), \\
V_r&\ge(4v_r)^{-1} I.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
$$

A fixed first-pair squeeze changes only fixed constants. This is a polynomial bound in $r$ and the declared geometric scales, since $K_r\le r$. It is a bound on the entire low-mode subspace, not a columnwise estimate multiplied without justification. The independent exact checks include nonzero off-diagonal gradient entries.

<a id="proposition-f104f3113-power-mean-nuclear-coefficients-and-evaluated-budgets"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.31.13 (Power-Mean Nuclear Coefficients and Evaluated Budgets).**

##### 1. Original datum and exact budget being approached

Keep the frozen regional massive scalar datum, a fixed ball B, $b>0$, the original conjugation J, and

$$
\begin{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}

&=2 \sum_{k\ge 1} [\operatorname{Tr} A_-^{k}+\operatorname{Tr} A_+^{k}]/k.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
$$

It is the first upper bound in F.10.4f.14.2, and $\Gamma_0\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{trace}}:=2S/(1-q)$. ##### 2. Power-mean majorant

For any even integer $p\ge 2$, put

$$
X_p=A_-^{p}+A_+^{p},\quad T_p=X_p^{1/p},\quad q_p=2^{1/p}q.
\tag{2}
$$

Take $p\ge p_0$, where $p_{0}$ is an explicit even integer with $2^{1/p_0}q\le\sqrt{q}<1$. All powers can be computed from the original positive $B_s=A_s^{2}$, as $X_p=B_-^{p/2}+B_+^{p/2}$.

<a id="proposition-f104f31131"></a>**Proposition F.10.4f.31.13.1.** $T_{p}$ is a positive J-real trace-class strict contraction, and

$$
T_p^{2}\ge A_s^{2},\quad \lVert T_p\rVert\le q_p\le\sqrt{q},\quad \operatorname{Tr} T_p\le S.
\tag{3}
$$

For every integer $1\le k\le p$,

$$
\operatorname{Tr} T_p^{k} \le \operatorname{Tr} A_-^{k}+\operatorname{Tr} A_+^{k}.
\tag{4}
$$

**Proof.** $X_p\ge A_s^p$, and the power $2/p$ is operator monotone, giving $T_p^{2}\ge A_s^{2}$. The norm estimate is immediate. For positive $X,Y$ and $0<r\le 1$, trace subadditivity gives $\operatorname{Tr}(X+Y)^r\le\operatorname{Tr}X^r+\operatorname{Tr}Y^r$. Applying it to $X=A_-^p,Y=A_+^p,r=k/p$ proves (4), including (3)'s trace claim.

For completeness, the trace inequality is proved by regularizing finite matrices and integrating

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d}{dt} \operatorname{Tr}(X+tY)^{r}&=r \operatorname{Tr}[Y(X+tY)^{r-1}] \\
&\le r\, t^{r-1}\operatorname{Tr} Y^{r}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The inequality uses operator antitonicity of $x^{r-1}$, whose exponent lies in $[-1,0]$. Integrate from 0 to 1, then pass to positive trace-ideal limits; finite spectral approximations and positivity justify this passage. $J$-reality is preserved by sums and functional calculus. QED.

The imported bosonic coefficient theorem consumes precisely $T^{2}\ge A_s^{2}$, $J$-reality and $\lVert T\rVert<1$. Thus it applies to $T_{p}$. This is a valid same-source nuclear tensor; no arbitrary basis is inserted into that theorem.

##### 3. Exponentially small excess over the original determinant

Write $\Gamma_p=2\operatorname{Tr}[-\log(I-T_p)]$. Terms of its power series through $p$ are bounded by (4). For $k>p$, $\operatorname{Tr}T_p^k\le S q_p^{k-1}$. Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Gamma_p &\le \Gamma_0 + \Delta_p, \\
\Delta_p &= 2S q_p^{p}/[(p+1)(1-q_p)] \\
&= 4S q^{p}/[(p+1)(1-q_p)].
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
$$

In particular $\Delta_p\le 4Sq^p/[(p+1)(1-\sqrt{q})]$. An explicit even $p=O(\log(1/\epsilon))$ at fixed $b,m,S$ makes $\Delta_p\le\epsilon/4$. For example take $p\ge p_0$ and

$$
p\ge\max\bigl(0,\log(16 \max(1,S)/(\epsilon(1-\sqrt{q})))/(-\log q)\bigr).
$$

This is stronger than estimating $\Gamma_{p}$ merely by $2S/(1-q_p)$, whose excess would only decay like $1/p$. The low trace powers retain the original determinant information and remove that artificial inverse-precision degree.

No noncommutative product A_-A_+ is assumed positive or commuting. The construction is continuous for fixed finite p and avoids an exact decision about whether two spectral subspaces coincide.
