Finite linear sums are evaluated termwise with their fixed $\ell^1$ envelope. A state $\psi=V\Omega$ is handled by evaluating $A V$, whose word length is still bounded by the declared census. The abstract coefficient functional exists on the entire regional algebra, with its original norm bound; numerical evaluation is promised only on supplied computable inputs. An arbitrary regional operator or arbitrary enormous dense finite matrix is not given a free numerical access oracle.

##### 7. Exact producer record and unresolved tariff

A request specifies the ball/collar localization datum, b, the original budget interpretation, a log-budget tolerance $\epsilon$, a projective tail tolerance $\delta$, an optional finite coefficient query list and its error tolerance. The finite record outputs:

1. $p$, $q_p$, $q_\star$ and the verified scalar inequalities (5),(11),(12), or the analytic exact trace-ceiling slack (13);
2. the evaluated interval for $\Gamma_{0}$ and the final rational outward budget $\Gamma_{\mathrm{cert}}$;
3. head spectral intervals/ranks, exact computable block-frame descriptors with requested finite enclosures, $J,L$ and the evaluated omitted projective bound;
4. a multiindex decoder and the explicit coefficient algorithm, plus any requested evaluated coefficients and their error intervals;
5. every regional-projection search counter, kernel quadrature, matrix/root/block precision, vector descriptor, arithmetic, memory, output and optional physical-access cost.

This is a terminating producer, not a formula awaiting unspecified spectral information. If the full tensor is requested, it runs the decoder over all binom(J+L,L) indices and pays that enumeration. If only a certified generator and tail are requested, its actual finite construction plus the requested on-demand queries are paid instead.

Two resource gaps remain visible. First, the primal/dual $E_{s}$ routine has no polynomial-logarithmic worst-case search bound. Second, the existing fixed-k Hermite tail selectors may give ranks polynomial in 1/delta; a Gevrey optimization can improve the analytic rank bound only after its derivative constants are proved and does not automatically accelerate $E_{s}$. Thus this result establishes an evaluated near-original-budget certificate and effective on-demand production. It does not yet establish that its complete physical production tariff fits the geometric polynomial-logarithmic inequality when this nuclear producer is actually executed as part of the nominated service.

A possible next route is a boundary-adapted fractional elliptic or extension-PDE solver on the ball. Smooth heat inputs can acquire boundary power/log singularities under $E_{s}$, so convergence of a plain flat smooth basis need not be exponential. Any weighted Jacobi/spherical-harmonic or geometric hp claim must prove its coercivity, boundary asymptotics, conditioning, error rate and explicit collar/heat-window dependence. None of those is supplied by the mere existence of a complete smooth profile basis.

##### 8. Relation to the original representing tensor

The new majorant changes a coefficient basis and its upper bound, not the phase-space map. In a Hilbert target, two absolutely convergent projective tensors representing the same map $A\to\Theta_b(A)$ are equal: apply increasing finite-rank orthogonal target projections. Each projected tensor is determined by its finitely many coefficient functionals, and these projections converge in projective norm on every absolutely summable tensor. Thus the finite heads above approximate the same original representing tensor, with their newly certified tails, even though their computable majorant differs from the spectral join.

This does not identify $\Gamma_{\mathrm{cert}}$ with the old spectral-join determinant or with the minimal nuclear norm. The established budgets are precisely (12) and, where selected, (13). No program minimality, historical acceptance or full tensor enumeration is added as a prerequisite.

<a id="lemma-f104f3114-gevrey-hermite-schatten-heads-and-exact-block-precision"></a>**Lemma F.10.4f.31.14 (Gevrey Hermite–Schatten Heads and Exact Block Precision).**

##### 1. A computational cutoff does not change the original budget

Keep the original ball $B$, $E_s$, $A_s=|E_s\exp(-b\omega)|$, $b>0$, $s=\pm 1/2$ and the original capacity/budget record. Choose an auxiliary real Gevrey-two function $\chi_{G}$ equal to one on a neighborhood of the closed ball and supported in a fixed larger ball. Record

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\lVert\partial^{\alpha}\chi_{G}\rVert_{\infty} \\
&\quad\le A_{\chi}B_{\chi}^{|\alpha|}(|\alpha|!)^{2},
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
$$

with $A_\chi,B_\chi\ge 1$ and a certified containing radius/center. These constants include the chosen localization collar; they are not uniform under an unpriced shrinking collar.

Such a cutoff is explicit. Use the flat step $w(t)=\exp(-1/t)$ for $t>0$ and zero otherwise, $\chi(t)=w(t)/(w(t)+w(1-t))$, and compose its constant extensions with the quadratic radial coordinate between two fixed radii. On the transition interval the denominator is at least $\exp(-2)$; the usual Cauchy estimate on a disk proportional to $t$ followed by optimizing $t$ proves Gevrey order two for $w$. Product/reciprocal differentiation and the quadratic chain rule give effective constants in (1). All radius, inverse collar and digit costs are retained.

Put

$$
L_{s}=\omega^{s}\chi_{G}\,\omega^{-s},\quad T_{s}=\exp(-b\,\omega)L_{s}.
$$

Since $L_s E_s=E_s$ on the original closed localization space,

$$
\exp(-b\,\omega)E_{s}=T_{s}E_{s}.
\tag{2}
$$

This auxiliary factorization changes neither $E_{s}$ nor $A_{s}$, their determinant, the physical heat map, nor any already nominated coarser trace ceiling. It only gives a stronger computational approximation bound. Its cutoff is not substituted into the old capacity record.

##### 2. A factorial bound for the actual kernel derivatives

In three momentum dimensions the kernel is

$$
\begin{aligned}
k_{b,s}(p,q) &= (2\pi)^{-3/2}\exp(-b\,\omega(p)) \\
&\quad \omega(p)^{s}\,\hat{\chi}_{G}(p-q)\,\omega(q)^{-s}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Let $D_q=1+|q|^{2}-\Delta_q$ and

$$
B_{b,s,k}=\lVert D_{q}^{k}k_{b,s}\rVert_{L^{2}(dp\,dq)}.
$$

<a id="lemma-f104f31141"></a>**Lemma F.10.4f.31.14.1.** Effective constants $A,C\ge 1$, depending only on the fixed mass, heat/localization data and (1), satisfy

$$
B_{b,s,k}\le A\,C^{k}(k!)^{12},\quad k\ge 0.
\tag{3}
$$

The same constants cover both s signs. They can be chosen by the positive coefficient majorants below; no spectral data or projection routine occurs in them.

**Proof and majorant accounting.** Normal-order each word in the $k$ factors of $1+\sum q_i^{2}-\sum\partial_i^{2}$. Each resulting term is $c_{\alpha,\beta}q^\alpha\partial^\beta$ with $|\alpha|+|\beta|\le 2k$. Counting commutator contractions gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum|c_{\alpha,\beta}| &\le C_{3}^{k+1}(2k)! \\
&\le {C'_{3}}^{k+1}(k!)^{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
$$

One explicit way to validate the count is to expand the 7 choices per factor, replace each square by its two first-order symbols, and overcount all choices of derivative/multiplication contractions by (2k)!. The finite number of normal monomials is polynomial in k and is absorbed into a geometric constant.

The massive multiplier is analytic in a fixed complex tube of width proportional to $m$. Cauchy's estimate gives, for all $|\gamma|\le 2k$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&|\partial^{\gamma}\omega(q)^{-s}| \\
&\quad\le C_{m}^{|\gamma|+1}|\gamma|!\,(1+|q|)^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
$$

This contributes at most another ${C_m'}^{k+1}(k!)^{2}$. The outer factor $\omega(p)^s$ is at most a fixed multiple of $(1+|p|)^{1/2}$.

Write $u=p-q$ and use

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(1+|q|)^{2k+1/2} \\
&\quad\le (1+|p|)^{2k+1}(1+|u|)^{2k+1}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The p factor then has the heat-weighted bound

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\lVert\exp(-b\,\omega(p))(1+|p|)^{2k+3/2}\rVert_{2} \\
&\quad\le A_{b}C_{b}^{k}(k!)^{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
$$

It follows by radial integration against $\exp(-2b|p|)$; the square root of the resulting $\Gamma(4k+\text{constant})$ is bounded by a geometric constant times $(k!)^{2}$. Fixed polynomial factors in $k$ are absorbed in $C_{b}$.

The remaining Fourier term is bounded by

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\lVert(1+|u|)^{2k+1}\partial^{\gamma}\hat{\chi}_{G}(u)\rVert_{2}, \\
&|\gamma|\le 2k.
\end{aligned}
$$

Plancherel and multinomial expansion reduce it to a geometric-in-$k$ sum of $\lVert\partial^\alpha(x^\gamma\chi_G)\rVert_2$, $|\alpha|\le 2k+1$. Leibniz differentiation costs at most a factor $(2k)!$ times geometric constants and the support radius to power $2k$; (1) costs $((2k+1)!)^{2}$. Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\lVert(1+|u|)^{2k+1}\partial^{\gamma}\hat{\chi}_{G}\rVert_{2} \\
&\quad\le A'_{\chi}{C'_{\chi}}^{k}(k!)^{6}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
$$

The two factorial powers in (4), the two in (5), the two in (6), and the six in (7) give twelve. Leibniz binomial coefficients and the finite-dimensional normal-ordering sums grow at most geometrically after these displayed factorials, so they do not add a hidden k-dependent exponent. Integrating in p,u has unit Jacobian and factors the two displayed L2 majorants; the triangle inequality finishes (3).

All constants are computable from these scalar estimates. If a single coarse formula is preferred, increase every scale to

$$
\begin{aligned}
G &= 2+m+m^{-1}+b^{-1}+|\mathrm{center}|+R_{\mathrm{support}} \\
&\quad +A_{\chi}+B_{\chi}+\operatorname{Vol}(\operatorname{support}\chi_{G})^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The elementary multinomial, $\Gamma$ and Cauchy estimates above are dominated, in $d=3$ and $|s|\le 1/2$, by $A=C=2^{200}G^{200}$ after harmless enlargement of $G$ to include the explicitly chosen tube factor. This intentionally loose choice is not used as a sharp physical tariff. QED.

##### 3. Stretched-exponential intrinsic spectral tails

The original factorization on the Schwartz core extends to

$$
\begin{aligned}
F_{s} &:= \exp(-b\,\omega)E_{s}=(T_{s}D^{k})D^{-k}E_{s}, \\
\lVert T_{s}D^{k}\rVert &\le B_{b,s,k}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Hermite levels have eigenvalues $\lambda_\alpha=4+2|\alpha|$ and cumulative rank $J_M=\binom{M+3}{3}$. Singular-value ideal inequalities and (3) give

$$
\begin{aligned}
s_{J_{M}+1}(A_{s}) &= s_{J_{M}+1}(F_{s}) \\
&\le A\,C^{k}(k!)^{12}(M+1)^{-k}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
$$

Choose $k=\lfloor c(M+1)^{1/12}\rfloor$, with $c>0$ small enough that $C k^{12}/(M+1)\le 1/2$. Since $k!\le k^k$, (8) is at most $A\,2^{-k}$. Adjusting the finite initial segment gives effective $A_1,c_1>0$ with

$$
s_{j}(A_{s})\le A_{1}\exp(-c_{1}j^{1/36}).
\tag{9}
$$

The counting exponent 36 is three spatial dimensions times factorial exponent 12. It is a deliberately conservative bound.

Consequently, for $0<a\le 1$, explicit integral comparison of the sum with $y=j^{1/36}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{j>J}s_{j}(A_{s})^{a}
&\le A_{1}^{a}C_{36}(a\,c_{1})^{-36} \\
&\qquad \exp[-(a\,c_{1}/2)J^{1/36}].
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
$$

For example bound $y^{35}\exp(-a c_{1}y/2)$ by $(70/(e a c_1))^{35}$ before integrating the remaining exponential. All inverse-$a$ factors are shown; constants are not asserted uniform as $a$ tends to zero.

To make $(10)\le\eta$ it suffices that

$$
J^{1/36}\ge C\,a^{-1}[\log(1/\eta)+\log(1/a)+1],
\tag{11}
$$

with fixed branch constants included in $C$. For the power-mean producer $a=1/p$ and $p=O(\log(1/\epsilon))$, this head rank is polynomial in $p$ and the requested precision bits. Root tolerances that require another factor $p$ in the bit budget still give polynomial head ranks. The old fixed-$k$ inverse-accuracy rank estimate was not an inherent analytic obstruction.

The power-mean majorant inherits the trace tail by its proved merge inequality. At a positive spectral threshold $\tau$, (9) also bounds the number of eigenvalues above $\tau$ polynomially in $\log(1/\tau)$. Thus cluster-inclusive block production need not use the coarse rank bound $S/\tau$. Choosing $\tau$ proportional to the desired omitted trace divided by a polynomial-log head count retains a polynomial-log rank even when a threshold falls inside a degenerate cluster. The whole cluster is included and explicitly paid.

##### 4. Constructive finite-rank heads and the remaining projection calls

Let $P_{M}$ project onto the Hermite levels $\le M$. The finite-rank operator

$$
F_{s,M,k}=(T_{s}D^{k})P_{M}D^{-k}E_{s}
\tag{12}
$$

has rank at most $J_{M}$ and, whenever $ka>3$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\lVert F_{s}-F_{s,M,k}\rVert_{S_{a}}^{a} \\
&\quad\le B_{b,s,k}^{a}\,c_{3}/(ka-3)\,(M+1)^{3-ka}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
$$

This is the original tail inequality with its k dependence retained. Take M+1 at least 2C $k^{12}$. Its right side is at most

$$
A^{a}c_{3}/(ka-3)\,(M+1)^{3}\,2^{-ka}.
\tag{14}
$$

A certified elementary selector increases $k$ until (14) is below the requested $\eta$, always setting $M=\lceil 2C k^{12}\rceil$. The logarithm of the polynomial prefactor is $O(\log k+\log(1/a))$ at fixed branch data, so a choice

$$
k=O(a^{-1}[\log(1/\eta)+\log(1/a)+1]^{2})
$$

already suffices. Hence this selector, $J_{M}$ and its scalar arithmetic are polynomial in $a^{-1}$ and precision bits. This slightly looser squared-log choice avoids an implicit logarithm in a stopping rule.

The finite output columns are explicit:

$$
\begin{aligned}
u_{\alpha} &= (T_{s}D^{k})h_{\alpha},\quad |\alpha|\le M, \\
F_{s,M,k} &= \sum_{\alpha}\lambda_{\alpha}^{-k}\,|u_{\alpha}\rangle\langle E_{s}h_{\alpha}|.
\end{aligned}
$$

The output-side positive matrix needed for $A_s^{2}$ is therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
B_{s,M,k} &= F_{s,M,k}F_{s,M,k}^{*} \\
&= \sum_{\alpha,\beta}\lambda_{\alpha}^{-k}\lambda_{\beta}^{-k}
\langle h_{\alpha},E_{s}h_{\beta}\rangle\,|u_{\alpha}\rangle\langle u_{\beta}|.
\end{aligned}
\tag{15}
$$

In fact $D^k P_M D^{-k}=P_M$, so (12) is exactly $F_{s,M}=T_s P_M E_s$, independent of $k$. Compute the direct columns $v_\alpha=T_s h_\alpha$ and put $V=T_s P_M$; then (15) is simply $B_{s,M}=V G^s V^*$. The $k$-dependent differentiated columns are only a tail-proof device. Their large Hermite eigenweights need not be created and cancelled numerically. Thus every unknown regional quantity in this finite head is in the finite Hermite moment matrix

$$
G^{s}_{\alpha,\beta}=\langle h_{\alpha},E_{s}h_{\beta}\rangle.
\tag{16}
$$

It is a positive contraction. The output functions $u_{\alpha}$ and their Gram matrices use only the original heat multiplier, explicit Gevrey cutoff, Hermite polynomials and fixed-dimensional integrals. They do not call an arbitrary spectral-packet oracle. Conjugation-real Hermite phase conventions and real block-frame conventions are retained.

The log norms of $T_s D^k$, intermediate derivatives and Hermite coefficients are $O(k\log(k+1)+M\log(M+1))$ plus declared geometric scales. Their quadrature truncations and precision lengths are polynomial in these quantities: heat controls $p$ tails, the Gevrey Fourier bound controls $p-q$ tails, and fixed-dimensional Gevrey interval quadrature handles the remaining explicit integrals. Explicitly, for a retained integrand with derivative bound $A_0B_0^n(n!)^{2}$, choose Taylor order $n=O(P+\log A_0)$ and cell width $h\le 1/(C B_0(n+1)^{2})$. The Taylor remainder including its factorial denominator is then geometrically small in $n$. The truncated domains, $B_{0}$ and $\log A_{0}$ are polynomial in the selected degrees, precision and fixed geometric scales. Fixed dimension makes both the number of cells and coefficients polynomial. Near a flat-step endpoint, jets are certified as negligible once the inverse distance exceeds a polynomial in $n,P$; elsewhere ordinary truncated power-series arithmetic has polynomial bit cost. This is a constructive rate for the Gevrey quadrature, not an analytic-strip assertion about a nonanalytic cutoff. The cutoff itself is supplied with the explicit derivative/finite-jet producer from Section 1. A finite Taylor/interval differentiation implementation has polynomially many coefficients because the integration dimensions and physical space dimension are fixed.

The only unresolved primitive is obtaining (16), uniformly through degree $M$ and the requested bits, with a proved polynomial cost. The terminating primal/dual projection routine computes these entries but supplies no such rate. A norm-$\eta$ approximation to $E_s h_\beta$ gives each moment to $\eta$, since $\lVert h_\alpha\rVert=1$; splitting matrix/operator budgets over $J_{M}$ and the known column norms costs only polynomially many additional bits. Numerical moment matrices are symmetrized and their positive-contraction interval is certified; all repairs are charged.

For even power $p$, $X_{p}$ uses powers of $B_s=A_s^{2}$, so no preliminary inverse or labelled square-root basis is needed. Schatten-product bounds, the trace-root inequality and polynomial-log ranks propagate (13) through the power-mean construction. Its $p$-dependent root accuracy is explicitly retained. Finite-dimensional spectral interval gaps can be selected by the polynomial-rank pigeonhole construction. Once a positive separating gap $g$ is certified, approximate the exact compact operator by a finite matrix in operator norm $O(\eta g)$, then use the finite matrix spectral projector; the Davis--Kahan projector estimate gives error $O(\eta)$. A cluster is kept whole, without requiring individual eigenvector gaps. Certified finite-matrix diagonalization to a residual uses polynomial arithmetic in matrix dimension and $\log(1/(\eta g))$; it does not sample a contour or iterate a polynomial for $O(1/g)$ steps. Refining these finite matrix projectors supplies the exact block descriptor and requested finite vector enclosures. Thus a small gap costs extra bits and the already selected analytic head refinement, not an unrecorded inverse-gap loop.

##### 5. Conditional complete classical producer tariff

Here is a precise, narrower missing hypothesis than an unspecified efficient projection oracle:

**Hermite projection-moment service.** For the actual ball, original mass, $s=\pm 1/2$, $M$ and bit request $P$, produce certified entries (16), $|\alpha|,|\beta|\le M$, with complete arithmetic, memory, parameter and geometric cost bounded by a fixed polynomial in $M,P$ at fixed branch geometry. Only these supplied Hermite columns are required.

If this service is proved, (12)--(16), the power-mean root/block algorithm of Proposition F.10.4f.31.13 and the fixed-word on-demand overlap algorithm give a polynomial-logarithmic **classical** near-original-budget nuclear producer, with an evaluated determinant, fixed exact block descriptors, explicit coefficient values and a certified projective tail. Full tensor enumeration still has its actual combinatorial output cost if requested. Optional physical packet preparation/access is charged separately; no physical source cost is inferred from a classical matrix description.

The exact equations for that service are Lemma F.10.4f.31.14a: $E_+$ is a screened half-order Dirichlet variational projection on $B$, and $E_-$ is identity minus the corresponding exterior projection. Their energy errors are precisely the required $L^2$ projection errors. For Hermite inputs the forcing has explicit analytic seminorms: multiplication of a Hermite Gaussian by $\omega^{1/2}$ in momentum has Gaussian tails, so every spatial derivative and finite complex-strip norm follows from elementary Gaussian moments. The logarithms of their constants are polynomial in $M$ and the requested bits. A solver theorem must quantify its dependence on those constants, rather than merely say 'analytic forcing'.

Massless interior preconditioning has the explicit finite condition bound in that common lemma. It does not by itself prove fast kernel application, and it fails uniformly on the unbounded exterior. Massive exterior truncation, boundary-adapted approximation, quadrature and conditioning still require their own proved rates. The available massless cuboid hp results do not directly supply them for the original massive ball/exterior geometry.

All bounds here are at fixed mass/heat/localization geometry, or with their displayed numerical scales carried in the constants. A polynomial in inverse collar or large radius is not automatically the original area-plus-active-volume tariff. No owner-wide closure, old Sobolev cost transfer, or unrequested autonomous-clock claim follows.

<a id="lemma-f104f3114a-exact-screened-variational-projections-and-interior-preconditioning"></a>**Lemma F.10.4f.31.14a (Exact Screened Variational Projections and Interior Preconditioning).**

Let $\omega=(m^2-\Delta)^{1/2}$, $m>0$, on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$, with unitary Fourier transform. Let $K_s(B)$ be the closed $L^2$ span of $\omega^s C_c^\infty(B)$, $s=\pm 1/2$, and $E_{s}$ its orthogonal projection. All spaces below are complexified if necessary; real conjugation commutes with every construction.

#### 1. Both signs reduce to a positive-order Dirichlet variational problem

For an open set $D$, define $V(D)$ as the closure of $C_c^\infty(D)$ in the norm $\lVert\omega^{1/2}u\rVert_2$. This is a Hilbert space; it is the supported half-order space with the closure convention kept explicit at the critical exponent. Define

$$
a_{m}(u,v)=\langle\omega^{1/2}u,\omega^{1/2}v\rangle.
$$

For every $x\in L^2$ there is a unique $u_{D}\in V(D)$ such that

$$
a_{m}(u_{D},v)=\langle x,\omega^{1/2}v\rangle\quad\text{for every } v\in V(D).
\tag{F.10.4f.31.14a.1}
$$

The functional has norm at most $\lVert x\rVert$, so this is the Riesz theorem without any added regularity assumption. The isometry $u\to\omega^{1/2}u$ has closed range $K_+(D)$; (F.10.4f.31.14a.1) is precisely the equation for its orthogonal projection. Consequently

$$
E_{+}(B)x=\omega^{1/2}u_{B}.
\tag{F.10.4f.31.14a.2}
$$

Proposition F.10.4f.31.0, Section 3, gives the exterior-density identity

$$
K_{-}(B)^{\perp}=K_{+}(\mathbb{R}^{3}\setminus\operatorname{closure}(B)).
$$

For the ball this theorem includes dilation away from its boundary, truncation and mollification in the half-order distribution norm; it is not an assertion that a sharp indicator is bounded on $H^{1/2}$. It follows that

$$
E_{-}(B)x=x-\omega^{1/2}u_{\mathrm{ext}},
\tag{F.10.4f.31.14a.3}
$$

where $u_{\mathrm{ext}}$ solves (F.10.4f.31.14a.1) in V(R3 minus closure(B)). Thus the negative-sign projection need not be implemented by inverting a first-kind negative-order operator. It can use the same positive-order screened Dirichlet equation on an exterior domain. The exterior problem and its costs remain distinct from the interior problem.

When $x$ is smooth enough, the right side of (F.10.4f.31.14a.1) is the distribution pairing with $\omega^{1/2}x$ restricted to $D$. For arbitrary $x\in L^2$ equation (F.10.4f.31.14a.1), rather than an unproved $L^2$ forcing formula, defines it.

#### 2. Exact Galerkin and residual certificates

Let $V_{N}$ be any finite-dimensional subspace of $V(D)$, and let $u_{N}$ solve (F.10.4f.31.14a.1) on $V_{N}$. Orthogonality gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\lVert\omega^{1/2}(u_{D}-u_{N})\rVert_{2} \\
&\quad=\min_{v\in V_{N}}\lVert\omega^{1/2}(u_{D}-v)\rVert_{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.10.4f.31.14a.4}
$$

For an arbitrary approximate vector $w\in V(D)$, define the residual $r_w(v)=\langle x,\omega^{1/2}v\rangle-a_m(w,v)$. Its norm in the dual of $(V(D),a_m)$ is exactly

$$
\lVert r_{w}\rVert_{V(D)^{*}}=\lVert\omega^{1/2}(u_{D}-w)\rVert_{2}.
\tag{F.10.4f.31.14a.5}
$$

If $r_{w}$ is represented by an $L^2$ function $g$ on $D$, then $a_m(v,v)\ge m\lVert v\rVert_2^2$ gives the computable upper bound

$$
\lVert r_{w}\rVert_{V(D)^{*}}\le m^{-1/2}\lVert g\rVert_{L^{2}(D)}.
\tag{F.10.4f.31.14a.6}
$$

The L2 representation in (F.10.4f.31.14a.6) is a hypothesis to check for the chosen trial functions; it is not automatic for arbitrary energy-space functions. Equations (F.10.4f.31.14a.4)-(F.10.4f.31.14a.6) control the actual L2 projection output, for both (F.10.4f.31.14a.2) and (F.10.4f.31.14a.3), and need no inverse tiny Gram eigenvalue if a stable variational solver is supplied. They do not by themselves bound approximation dimension or quadrature cost.

#### 3. Elementary interior massless preconditioner estimate

For the ball of radius $R$ and $u$ supported there, put $a_0(u,u)=\int|p|\,|\hat{u}(p)|^2\,dp$. By Cauchy-Schwarz and the unitary Fourier convention,

$$
\lVert\hat{u}\rVert_{\infty}^{2}\le|B_{R}|\,\lVert u\rVert_{2}^{2}/(2\pi)^{3}.
$$

Choose $\rho>0$ by $|B_R|\,|B_\rho|/(2\pi)^3=1/2$; explicitly $\rho^3=9\pi/(4R^3)$. Then the Fourier mass outside $|p|\le\rho$ is at least half the total, and

$$
a_{0}(u,u)\ge\rho\,\lVert u\rVert_{2}^{2}/2.
\tag{F.10.4f.31.14a.7}
$$

Density extends this to $V(B)$. Since $0\le\sqrt{m^2+t^2}-t\le m$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&a_{0}(u,u)\le a_{m}(u,u)\le\kappa\,a_{0}(u,u), \\
&\kappa=1+2m/\rho.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.10.4f.31.14a.8}
$$

This proves an explicit condition bound $O(1+mR)$ for the massless Dirichlet inverse as a screened interior preconditioner. On the Hilbert space with inner product $a_{0}$, the represented operator $A_0^{-1}A_m$ is self-adjoint with spectrum in $[1,\kappa]$. Exact preconditioned Richardson iteration with step $2/(1+\kappa)$ contracts in both $a_{0}$ and $a_{m}$ norms by

$$
q=(\kappa-1)/(\kappa+1).
\tag{F.10.4f.31.14a.9}
$$

For $m>0$ this gives $O(\kappa\log(1/\epsilon))$ exact operator iterations at fixed initial energy error. Inexact applications add their actual residual errors through the geometric sum. Polynomial-logarithmic total runtime still requires a certified sufficiently fast application of the massless inverse, the screened operator, and all quadratures. Equation (F.10.4f.31.14a.9) is not that application theorem.

#### 4. Exterior limitation

The interior constant cannot be reused on the full exterior. Choose a fixed normalized smooth compact bump supported in an annulus away from zero and dilate it to scale $L$, so that for all sufficiently large $L$ its support is outside $B_{R}$. Its massless energy is $c/L$ while its screened energy is at least $m$. Hence $a_m/a_0\ge mL/c$ tends to infinity. There is no uniform finite $\kappa$ for this exterior massless preconditioner.

A truncated exterior domain inside a ball of radius L regains (F.10.4f.31.14a.7)-(F.10.4f.31.14a.9) with L replacing R. To turn that observation into a polylogarithmic algorithm requires a proved massive exterior truncation error, boundary-compatible approximation rates, and explicit conditioning/quadrature bounds. No exponential spatial tail for arbitrary computable inputs is assumed here.

<a id="theorem-f104f3115-paid-projection-free-production-under-the-original-coarse-ceiling"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.31.15 (Paid Projection-Free Production under the Original Coarse Ceiling).**

##### 1. Exact original clause and branch nomination

The frozen Appendix F, in the paragraph `Computable local nuclearity data` immediately before F.10.4f.14, permits choosing a real $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ equal to one on a neighborhood of the closed retained ball $B$. It imposes no requirement that this computational localization cutoff fit a previously fixed narrow split collar. Formula F.10.4f.14.1 then defines

$$
K_{b,s}=Z_{k}B_{b,s,k},\quad S_{b}=K_{b,-1/2}+K_{b,+1/2},
$$

from that chosen cutoff and the actual original massive kernel. The proof of F.10.4f.14 establishes $\lVert T_s\rVert_1\le K_{b,s}$ for $T_s=\exp(-b\omega)\omega^s\chi\omega^{-s}$, before multiplying by $E_{s}$. Thus this bound applies directly to the explicit kernel operator, not only to its inaccessible projected version.

We nominate $\chi$ once as follows, before accuracy. Fix the actual ball $B(c,R)$, mass $m>0$, and compact positive heat interval $b\in[b_0,b_1]$. Fix one real Gevrey-two bump $\chi_{0}$ with

$$
\begin{aligned}
&0\le\chi_{0}\le 1,\quad \chi_{0}=1\text{ on } |x|\le 1, \\
&\operatorname{support}\chi_{0}\subset\{|x|\le 2\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The explicit radial flat-step construction and certified derivative bounds are those of the Gevrey-head theorem. Define

$$
\chi_{L}(x)=\chi_{0}((x-c)/L).
$$

Choose $L>R$ with the quantitative bounds below. This wide **computational** localization radius is recorded as branch data. It is not the split collar, and it is not replaced by the physical region's radius in the ledger. Set the original $S_{b}$ using this same nominated $\chi_{L}$ and one original allowed fixed integer $k>3/2$, for example $k=2$. The original coarse log ceiling is then exactly

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{old}}(b)=2S_{b}/(1-q_{b}),\quad q_{b}=\exp(-bm).
\tag{1}
$$

Every occurrence of $S_{b}$ below is this original same-cutoff quantity. The original intrinsic product determinant involving $E_{s}$ is a separate, generally tighter bound.

##### 2. A quantitative conjugated-cutoff norm

For $a=\omega(p)$, $d=\omega(q)$ and $s=\pm 1/2$,

$$
|a^{s}d^{-s}-1|\le|a-d|/(2m)\le|p-q|/(2m).
\tag{2}
$$

For $s=+1/2$ this follows from $|\sqrt{a/d}-1|=|a-d|/[\sqrt{d}(\sqrt{a}+\sqrt{d})]$; the negative case exchanges $a,d$. The lower bound $a,d\ge m$ gives the denominator $2m$.

The kernel of $\omega^s\chi_L\omega^{-s}-\chi_L$ is therefore Schur-bounded by

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(2\pi)^{-3/2}\int|u|\,|\hat{\chi}_{L}(u)|\,du/(2m) \\
&\quad= C_{\chi}/(mL), \\
&C_{\chi}:=[2(2\pi)^{3/2}]^{-1} \\
&\quad\int|v|\,|\hat{\chi}_{0}(v)|\,dv.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
$$

This uses both Schur row and column bounds, uniformly in the other momentum variable. Translation contributes only a phase, and dilation gives the factor $L^{-1}$. In particular it is the norm of multiplication by $\chi_{L}$, at most one, plus a commutator estimate; it is not the generally larger $L^1$ norm of the whole Fourier transform.

The constant is explicitly bounded without an absolute-Fourier quadrature oracle:

$$
C_{\chi}\le\lVert(1-\Delta)^{2}\chi_{0}\rVert_{2}/(16\sqrt{\pi}).
\tag{4}
$$

Cauchy--Schwarz and Plancherel prove this because $\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}|v|^{2}/(1+|v|^{2})^4\,dv=\pi^{2}/8$. The derivative bounds and fixed support give a certified rational upper constant $C_0\ge C_\chi$. Thus

$$
\lVert\omega^{s}\chi_{L}\,\omega^{-s}\rVert\le 1+C_{0}/(mL).
\tag{5}
$$

Let $q_0=\exp(-b_0m)$, and set

$$
c=1+(1-q_{0})/(2(1+q_{0}))=(3+q_{0})/(2(1+q_{0}))<2.
$$

Choose, with outward certified rounding,

$$
L\ge\max(2R,\,m^{-1},\,2C_{0}(1+q_{0})/(m(1-q_{0}))).
\tag{6}
$$

Then $(5)\le c$. For every retained $b$, $q=q_b\le q_0$ and

$$
r=cq<1,\quad c(1+q)<2.
\tag{7}
$$

In particular this is available for every fixed positive heat window, not only for large $\beta$. As $b_{0}$ tends to zero, the needed $L$ can grow like $1/(b_0m^{2})$; that dependence is recorded and no uniform small-$\beta$ geometric bound is claimed.

##### 3. Explicit-kernel majorants, with no regional projection call

Keep the original $A_s^{2}=\exp(-b\omega)E_s\exp(-b\omega)$. Since $L_s E_s=E_s$,

$$
A_{s}^{2}=T_{s}E_{s}T_{s}^{*}\le T_{s}T_{s}^{*}.
$$

Define

$$
C_{s}=(T_{s}T_{s}^{*})^{1/2}.
$$

These are positive J-real operators, produced from explicit kernels. Equations (5)--(7) and the original factorization give

$$
\begin{aligned}
&C_{s}^{2}\ge A_{s}^{2},\quad\lVert C_{s}\rVert\le r<1, \\
&\operatorname{Tr}C_{-}+\operatorname{Tr}C_{+}=\lVert T_{-}\rVert_{1}+\lVert T_{+}\rVert_{1}\le S_{b}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
$$

No $E_{s}$ occurs in the computation of $T_sT_s^*$. Its finite Hermite head is simply $T_s P_M T_s^*$, so the finite Gram matrix that obstructed the original tight producer is the identity.

For even $p\ge 2$ let

$$
\begin{aligned}
U_{p} &= (C_{-}^{p}+C_{+}^{p})^{1/p} \\
&= [(T_{-}T_{-}^{*})^{p/2}+(T_{+}T_{+}^{*})^{p/2}]^{1/p}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
$$

The power-mean proof of Proposition F.10.4f.31.13 applies with $r$ in place of $q$. Thus $U_p^{2}\ge A_s^{2}$, $U_p$ is $J$-real, $\operatorname{Tr}U_p\le S_b$, and $\lVert U_p\rVert\le r_p=2^{1/p}r<1$ once $p$ is large enough. It is therefore an admissible majorant for the **original** bosonic nuclear coefficient theorem on the full regional algebra.

##### 4. Exact admission under the old coarse ceiling

Let $f(t)=-\log(1-t)/t$. Its nonnegative series gives

$$
f(r)\le 1+r/[2(1-r)].
\tag{10}
$$

The product determinant of $C_-,C_+$ has log at most $2S_b f(r)$. By (7),

$$
\begin{aligned}
d(q,c) &:= 1/(1-q)-[1+r/(2(1-r))] \\
&= q[2-c(1+q)]/[2(1-q)(1-r)]>0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
$$

For $b=b_0$ and the exact $c$ in Section 2, this simplifies to $q_0/[4(1-r_0)]$. For a fixed interval $b\in[b_0,b_1]$, a positive uniform lower bound is obtained from $q_1=\exp(-b_1m)>0$ and $q_{0}<1$. Consequently the old coarse ceiling has explicit slack over this projection-free kernel determinant.

As in Proposition F.10.4f.31.13,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&2\operatorname{Tr}[-\log(I-U_{p})] \\
&\quad\le 2S_{b}f(r)+2S_{b}r_{p}^{p}/[(p+1)(1-r_{p})].
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
$$

Choose a sufficiently large even $p$ so the last term uses at most one quarter of the positive slack $2S_b\,d(q,c)$. Since $r_p^p=2r^p$, this is an effective exponentially convergent scalar selection. The factor $S_{b}$ cancels in the relative choice, so $p$ may be fixed once for the branch and heat window, independently of the requested tensor accuracy $\delta$. This is not an inverse-$\delta$ root order.

Round the retained exact $J$-real spectral blocks of $U_{p}$ upward, as in the producer of Proposition F.10.4f.31.13, with total trace increment small enough that the resulting log-determinant increment is at most another quarter of the slack. Low spectrum is retained when asserting domination. This yields a valid same-source occupation tensor under the original exact ceiling $\exp(\Gamma_{\mathrm{old}}(b))$.

##### Numerical inequalities are actually certified

The kernel integrals defining $S_{b}$ are explicitly evaluated with enclosures. Refine $[S_{\mathrm{lo}},S_{\mathrm{hi}}]$ and $[q_{\mathrm{lo}},q_{\mathrm{hi}}]$ until, with $r_{\mathrm{hi}}=c\,q_{\mathrm{hi}}<1$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
G &= 2S_{\mathrm{lo}}/(1-q_{\mathrm{lo}}) \\
&\quad -2S_{\mathrm{hi}}[1+r_{\mathrm{hi}}/(2(1-r_{\mathrm{hi}}))]>0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
$$

Strict inequality (11) guarantees termination; the chosen compact branch gives fixed scalar precision bounds. The kernel is nonzero, so a positive $S_{\mathrm{lo}}$ is reached; its explicit nonzero smooth kernel patch also gives a direct lower witness if desired. No comparison to zero at a limiting singular datum is required.

Allocate at most G/4 each to the power-mean excess, upward spectral rounding and numerical/budget enclosures. The output rational log budget can then be taken as

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Gamma_{\mathrm{cert}} &= 2S_{\mathrm{hi}}[1+r_{\mathrm{hi}}/(2(1-r_{\mathrm{hi}}))]+3G/4 \\
&< 2S_{\mathrm{lo}}/(1-q_{\mathrm{lo}})\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{old}}(b).
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
$$

All constants, computed intervals and slack checks are recorded. Thus the producer does not merely announce an infinite determinant or allow an unquantified overshoot of the old budget. The original scalar $S_{b}$ is itself priced: at $d=3$ and the nominated $k=2$,

$$
Z_{2}^{2}=(\zeta(2)-\zeta(3))/32.
$$

This follows by summing Hermite-level multiplicity $(n+1)(n+2)/2$ against $(4+2n)^{-4}$. The $\zeta(3)$ value has a direct polynomial-bit producer: Euler-transform the alternating series $\eta(3)=(3/4)\zeta(3)$. Its $k$th difference $d_k=\sum_{j=0}^k(-1)^j\binom{k}{j}/(j+1)^3$ is a positive number at most one, by $a_n=(1/2)\int_0^1 x^{n-1}(-\log x)^{2}\,dx$. The Euler-transformed summands therefore have remainder at most $2^{-K}$ after $K$ terms, each computable by $K$ finite rational binomial sums with polynomial bit lengths. $\zeta(2)=\pi^{2}/6$ and square roots use certified elementary arithmetic. The fixed-order kernel integrals $B_{b,s,2}$ use the explicit Gevrey quadrature and Fourier tails of Section 5. Thus evaluating the actual original $K$ and $S$ to precision $P$ has polynomial bit cost; no slowly converging naive Hermite series is assigned a free oracle.

This result does **not** approximate the intrinsic product determinant of A_-,A_+ to arbitrary relative or additive accuracy. That tighter task retains its Hermite regional-projection interface. The positive result here is an explicit producer satisfying the original coarser ceiling (1) on the declared permitted-cutoff branch.

##### 5. Polynomial-logarithmic head and coefficient production

The Gevrey-head proof of Lemma F.10.4f.31.14 applies directly to $T_{s}$, with the same actual nominated $\chi_{L}$. Its kernel satisfies $B_{b,s,k}\le A C^k(k!)^{12}$, and

##### 6. Actual finite physical access services

If the requested nuclear record also includes finite physical packet access, that service is supplied rather than inferred from its matrix description. Its nominated inputs are a retained occupation index $|\mu|\le L_{\mathrm{occ}}$ and/or a bounded-length supplied word, with the complete query/record grammar already used by the heat certificate. No arbitrary full-regional operator input port is added.

The retained spectral packets are computable combinations of polynomially many explicit kernel columns, with the root/block precision already proved. There is also an exact tail certificate for **arbitrary vectors of a rounded block**, not merely eigenvectors of the unrounded operator. If the block lies above $\tau>0$ and $\lVert e\rVert=1$, then

$$
\begin{aligned}
e &= U_{p}^{p}U_{p}^{-p}e=\exp(-b\,\omega)v, \\
\lVert v\rVert &\le 2c^{2}q\,r^{p-2}\tau^{-p}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{15}
$$

Indeed expand $U_p^p$ as $\sum_s(T_sT_s^*)^{p/2}$, peel off the left $\exp(-b\omega)$, and bound $L_sL_s^*$, the next heat factor and the remaining powers by $c^{2}$, $q$ and $r^{p-2}$. The inverse is only on the retained spectral block and has norm at most $\tau^{-p}$. Thus

$$
\lVert 1_{\omega>E}\,e\rVert\le 2c^{2}q\,r^{p-2}\tau^{-p}\exp(-bE).
\tag{16}
$$

Energy/momentum cutoff $E=O([p\log(1/\tau)+\log(1/\delta)+\text{constant}]/b)$ suffices. This is polynomial in precision bits and all displayed branch parameters; an inverse-accuracy momentum lattice is unnecessary.

Spatial tails can be recorded too. For a fixed complex momentum shift $|\eta|\le m/(8\sqrt{3})$, the kernel of $T_{s}$ evaluated at $p+i\eta$ is analytic. The shifted Fourier cutoff is the transform of $\exp(\eta\cdot x)\chi_L(x)$. Its weighted Fourier $L^1$ norm is bounded by a fixed-order Sobolev norm on its compact support, as in (4). The massive multiplier ratio has the same polynomial Schur bound on this smaller strip, and the shifted heat factor has a uniform bound $\exp(Cbm)$ times its real-axis bound. Therefore a directly computable constant $A_{\mathrm{shift}}$ has

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert(T_{s}w)(p+i\eta)\rVert_{L^{2}(dp)} &\le A_{\mathrm{shift}}\lVert w\rVert_{2}, \\
\log A_{\mathrm{shift}} &\le \operatorname{poly}(L,m,m^{-1},b,b^{-1},\text{cutoff constants}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
$$

Only fixed-order derivatives of $\exp(\eta\cdot x)\chi_L$ enter this Schur bound; their exponential factor has logarithm $O(Lm)$, not an inverse-precision parameter. Since $e=\sum_s T_s w_s$ with $\lVert w_s\rVert\le c\,q\,r^{p-2}\tau^{-p}$, the $L^2$ strip/weighted-Fourier identity gives exponential spatial tails. Applying shifts $\pm a$ along each coordinate, $a=m/(8\sqrt{3})$, yields

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\lVert 1_{|x|>X}\,\check{e}(x)\rVert \\
&\quad\le\sqrt{6}\,[2A_{\mathrm{shift}}\,c\,q\,r^{p-2}\tau^{-p}] \\
&\qquad\exp(-aX/\sqrt{3}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
$$

This identity follows first for smooth decaying inputs by contour shift and then for all $L^2$ inputs by bounded continuation; (17) provides the limit bound. The center and actual cutoff support are already included in $A_{\mathrm{shift}}$. A spatial comparison radius polynomial in $p\log(1/\tau)$, precision bits and the displayed geometry therefore suffices. If finite spatial-access regions are requested, their real size, tests and interface cost are recorded rather than identified with the smaller original ball. No source rail-graph locality theorem is inferred from this tail estimate.

The large raw tail prefactor is not a large physical-energy assertion. Since $\lVert e\rVert=1$, combine each bound with the bound one. For example a tail at most $\min(1,A_e\exp(-bE))$ gives, by the layer-cake formula, every fixed energy moment bounded by a fixed polynomial in $1+b^{-1}\log_+(A_e)$. The same argument applies to (18). Here $\log A_e=O(p\log(1/\tau)+\log A_{\mathrm{shift}})$, so all fixed energy, spatial and momentum-derivative moments are polynomial in the selected precision parameters. The physical regularizer used in the original register comparison therefore has an explicit polynomial-logarithmic bound on each retained occupation packet, after including its particle count and the polynomial number of modes.

Every exact output occupation vector $\xi_{\mu}$ is itself Hadamard in the stated two-point sense: its two-point difference is a finite sum of products of the smooth positive-frequency waves of the $e_{j}$, weighted by the finite occupations. Smoothness follows directly from the all-order energy moments just proved. Finite superpositions, complete finite flag mixtures and the nominated finite occupation-code intermediate states have the same finite-packet smooth-difference proof, with their actual particle/mode factors included. This is a direct assertion about the prepared packet states, not an inference from vacuum Hadamardness. It adds no new unknown statistical chart to the retained LAN family.

Retaining the low-spectrum tail in the mathematical majorant does not require physically storing all its modes. The finite coefficient/source response uses the certified head; its omitted contribution is the already allocated projective error.

##### Explicit polynomial-size packet frame

Energy and spatial tails alone do not supply an efficient amplitude-loading circuit. Here the explicit kernel supplies the missing finite coefficient vector. Write $D_p=1+|p|^{2}-\Delta_p$, and let $P_{M}$ be its Hermite-level projector through total degree $M$. There are computable branch constants $A_{\mathrm{out}},C_{\mathrm{out}}\ge 1$ such that

$$
\lVert D_{p}^{k}T_{s}\rVert_{\mathrm{HS}}\le A_{\mathrm{out}}C_{\mathrm{out}}^{k}(k!)^{6}.
\tag{19}
$$

To prove (19), normal-order $D_p^k$ as in the input-side lemma. Its coefficient sum contributes $C^k(k!)^{2}$. Derivatives of the full analytic factor $\exp(-b\omega(p))\omega(p)^s$ in a fixed strip of width proportional to $m$ have the Cauchy bound $C^{n+1}n!\exp(-b\omega(p)/2)(1+|p|)^{1/2}$, with the fixed $\exp(Cbm)$ factor absorbed into $A_{\mathrm{out}}$. This contributes another $(k!)^{2}$ for $n\le 2k$. The $p$-monomials then have heat moments bounded by $C^k(k!)^{2}$, exactly as in that lemma.

Unlike the input-side derivative bound, no growing Fourier weight is needed. With $u=p-q$, the undifferentiated $q$ multiplier obeys $|\omega(q)^{-s}|\le C(1+|p|)^{1/2}(1+|u|)^{1/2}$. The remaining $u$ norm is bounded by $\lVert(1+|u|)\partial^\gamma\hat{\chi}_L(u)\rVert_2$, $|\gamma|\le 2k$. Plancherel bounds this by a geometric multiple of $\lVert x^\gamma\chi_L\rVert_{H^1}$. Differentiating $x^\gamma$ only once costs at most $2k$ and the fixed support radius to power $2k$; the fixed $H^1$ cutoff norm is already known. Thus this factor grows geometrically in $k$ and adds no factorial power. Leibniz binomial factors are geometric. Integrating in $p,u$ and summing gives precisely the six factorial powers in (19). The constants include the center, $L$, $m$, $b$ and the fixed cutoff norms, with polynomial logarithmic majorants in those displayed scales. A looser exponent twelve would also suffice for the following tariff.

Put $B_{\mathrm{packet}}=2r^{p-1}\tau^{-p}$. Uniformly for every unit vector $e$ in the entire retained spectral head $\operatorname{Ran}1_{[\tau,\infty)}(U_p)$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
e &= \sum_{s}T_{s}w_{s},\quad\sum_{s}\lVert w_{s}\rVert\le B_{\mathrm{packet}}, \\
\lVert(I-P_{M})e\rVert &\le B_{\mathrm{packet}}A_{\mathrm{out}}C_{\mathrm{out}}^{k}(k!)^{6}(M+1)^{-k}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{20}
$$

Indeed $w_s=T_s^*(T_sT_s^*)^{p/2-1}U_p^{-p}e$, so $\lVert w_s\rVert\le r^{p-1}\tau^{-p}$. The Hermite eigenvalue bound and (19) then prove (20) for the whole head, not just a chosen basis. Take $k\ge\log_2(B_{\mathrm{packet}}A_{\mathrm{out}}/\epsilon)+1$ and $M+1\ge 2C_{\mathrm{out}}k^6$ (enlarging $k$ to at least one). Since $k!\le k^k$, $(20)\le\epsilon$. The Hermite rank $\binom{M+3}{3}$ is polynomial in $p\log(1/\tau)+\log(1/\epsilon)$ and the displayed fixed branch constants.

Let E be the isometry whose columns are the exact J-real head-frame packets and $C_{M}$ the finite coefficient matrix of $P_{M}$ E in the conjugation-real Hermite convention. Equation (20) gives

$$
\lVert I-C_{M}^{*}C_{M}\rVert\le\epsilon^{2}.
$$

The corrected matrix $C_M(C_M^*C_M)^{-1/2}$ is therefore an isometry and differs from $E$, after the Hermite output embedding, by $O(\epsilon)$. It has no small Gram pivot or small success probability. Its entries are produced by the exact spectral-block descriptor: approximate the block projector in operator norm using the explicit finite kernel matrices, project a certified finite $J$-real orthonormal block frame, and correct its near-identity Gram. All needed $\langle h_\alpha,T_s h_\beta\rangle$ and finite-kernel column overlaps are explicit fixed-dimensional Gevrey quadratures covered by the head algorithm of Lemma F.10.4f.31.14. Matrix-entry budgets absorb both finite ranks; projector accuracy absorbs the certified block gap. Refinements keep the exact descriptor fixed. Thus the coefficient matrix itself, not just a norm or tail formula, is computed in polynomial time and storage.

Complete this finite isometry to a finite unitary and synthesize its passive one-particle basis rotation by polynomially many Givens rotations. On the sector with total occupation at most $L_{\mathrm{occ}}$, each two-mode block has polynomial dimension and its explicit square-root occupation matrix elements are computable; its complete finite-code circuit is compiled using the physical rail service of Definition F.10.4f.31.6. No postselection with probability $\tau^{p}$ and no piecewise-constant spatial lattice are used.

The computational Hermite span also has a priced embedding into the original physical one-particle space. Hermite ladder bounds give a uniform polynomial energy moment on all levels $\le M$, and Gaussian tails give a momentum cutoff polynomial in $M$ and the requested bits. Apply the bounded-energy Krylov/matrix compiler of Theorem F.10.4f.31.9 to the original $\omega$ on this momentum-cut span, allocating its finite-frame Gram correction and all one-particle defects. The relevant Gaussian/massive integrals have the same explicit polynomial quadrature production. Its finite global output isometry is separate from the exact local UCP recovery. <a id="theorem-f104f3116-localized-flip-actual-finite-algebra-and-regional-tensor-limit"></a>**Theorem F.10.4f.31.16 (Localized Flip, Actual Finite Algebra and Regional Tensor Limit).**

##### 1. Exact localized rotation and the localizing UCP map

Fix concentric $O=D(B_R)$ and $O_+=D(B_{R+\ell})$, with $m,\ell>0$. Choose $0<\tau<\ell/2$, real compact Gevrey-two $f$ with support in $(-\tau,\tau)$ and integral one, and $0\le\chi\le 1$ equal to one on $B_{R+\tau}$, supported in $B_{R+\ell-\tau}$. On two identical original scalar fields let

$$
Q=\int f(t)\chi(x)\,{:}[\pi_{1}\phi_{2}-\phi_{1}\pi_{2}]{:}(t,x)\,dt\,dx.
$$

With $[\phi_j,\pi_k]=i\delta_{jk}$ this sign gives $[Q,\phi_1]=-i\phi_2$. Thus $U=\exp(i\pi Q/2)$ obeys

$$
U(A\otimes I)U^{*}=I\otimes A,\quad A\in A(O).
\tag{1}
$$

Only this one-way relation is needed; the reverse $O(2)$ rotation includes a sign. No global parity is silently added. The primary local-current theorem of Morsella and Tomassini (2008, Appendix A, Proposition A.2 and equation (3.3)) proves essential self-adjointness, localization of the current exponential in $A(O_+)\otimes A(O_+)$, and its exact local symmetry. The neutral-field specialization is their cited D'Antoni--Longo construction. Our quantitative kernel proof also verifies the bounded-number/HS-pair hypotheses. The result applies to the full bounded local algebra: the field commutator integrates to the Weyl rotation on the common analytic domain, and normal unitary conjugation extends it to the generated von Neumann algebra.

Let $V_0\psi=\psi\otimes\Omega$, $V=UV_0$, and $\Xi=V\Omega=U(\Omega\otimes\Omega)$. Define

$$
L(B)=V^{*}(I\otimes B)V,\quad B\in B(H).
\tag{2}
$$

Then $L$ is normal UCP, $L(A)=A$ for every $A\in A(O)$, and $L(B(H))\subset A(O_+)$. ##### 1. Explicit quadratic kernels

Write $F(v)=\int f(t)\exp(itv)dt$ and use the original unitary spatial Fourier convention. For the pinned charge $Q=\int f\chi\,{:}(\pi_{1}\phi_{2}-\phi_{1}\pi_{2}){:}$ and $U_{t}=\exp(itQ)$, the number matrix has off-diagonal species entries $A_{12}=+i a$ and $A_{21}=-i a$, where

$$
\begin{aligned}
a(p,q) &= (2\pi)^{-3/2}/2\,\Bigl[\sqrt{\omega_{p}/\omega_{q}}+\sqrt{\omega_{q}/\omega_{p}}\Bigr] \\
&\quad \hat{\chi}(p-q)\,F(\omega_{p}-\omega_{q}),
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
$$

and a symmetric two-species pair kernel whose 12 entry is

$$
\begin{aligned}
b_{12}(p,q) &= -i(2\pi)^{-3/2}/2\,\Bigl[\sqrt{\omega_{q}/\omega_{p}}-\sqrt{\omega_{p}/\omega_{q}}\Bigr] \\
&\quad \hat{\chi}(p+q)\,F(\omega_{p}+\omega_{q}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
$$

The 21 entry is its transpose; the diagonal species entries vanish. The displayed spatial Fourier convention and $F(v)=\int f(t)\exp(itv)dt$ fix these phases; the number kernel is read with $a_{i}^{*}(p)a_{j}(q)$, and the pair kernel with $a_{i}^{*}(p)a_{j}^{*}(q)$. Direct substitution gives $[Q,\phi_{1}]=-i\phi_{2}$, hence the positive one-way transfer under $U_{\pi/2}$. The number operator matrix is Hermitian and the pair matrix is symmetric.

The ratio estimate and Schur's test bound the number kernel by a computable constant $C_{A}$. The pair kernel is Hilbert--Schmidt because compact Gevrey time smearing gives

$$
|F(v)|\le C\exp(-c\,|v|^{1/2}),
$$

and $\omega_{p}+\omega_{q}$ controls both momenta. All fixed-order mixed kernel derivatives have explicit bounds from the same formulas. On finite-particle vectors,

$$
\lVert Q\psi\rVert\le C_{Q}\lVert(N+1)\psi\rVert,
\tag{3}
$$

by the bounded-number and Hilbert--Schmidt-pair creation estimates. Iteration on a vector with at most $n$ particles costs at most $C_{Q}^{k}\prod_{j<k}(n+2j+1)$. Finite-particle vectors consequently are analytic for $Q$ on a nonzero interval depending on $n$; their dense union gives essential self-adjointness. The free-field local-current theorem supplies the exact localization and rotation identity with the specified spacetime support. The charge is not an instantaneous spatial rotation: omitting time smoothing would lose the Hilbert--Schmidt pair estimate in three dimensions.

##### 2. One fixed weighted analytic space controls the noncompact number kernel

Bounds at each Sobolev order followed by exponentiating their constants would not suffice. Instead use a single fixed weighted analytic norm. Choose a mass-controlled strip width $\eta_0<m/16$ and $a>0$. Let

$$
\begin{aligned}
w_{a}(p) &= \exp[a(1+|p|^{2})^{1/8}], \\
\lVert v\rVert_{G} &= \sup_{|\eta_{i}|\le\eta_{0}}\lVert w_{a}(p)v(p+i\eta)\rVert_{L^{2}(dp)},
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
$$

with the usual analytic-strip interpretation and closure of analytic rapidly decreasing vectors. For Hilbert--Schmidt columns use the same norm with values in the input Hilbert space. Decrease $\eta_{0}$ by a fixed factor whenever Cauchy derivatives are taken. All numbers $a,\eta_{0}$ and norm majorants are chosen and recorded before accuracy.

The number kernel acts boundedly on $G$. To see this, shift its input and output variables by the same $i\eta$. The cutoff argument $p-q$ stays real. The mass square root is analytic and comparable to its real value in this strip; its half-power ratio is bounded by $C_{m}(1+|p-q|/m)^{1/2}$. The time factor is bounded by $\lVert f\rVert_{1}\exp(C\tau m)$, since its imaginary argument is uniformly bounded. Finally

$$
w_{a}(p)/w_{a}(q)\le\exp(Ca|p-q|^{1/4}).
$$

The Gevrey Fourier estimate for $\chi$ has decay $\exp(-c_{\chi}|p-q|^{1/2})$, which absorbs this weaker weight and the fixed ratio power. Both Schur row and column integrals are finite with computable scalar bounds, uniformly in $\eta$. Contour shift on decaying analytic vectors, followed by the $L^2$ bound and closure, proves boundedness on (4). It does not assume that the number kernel is compact.

The pair kernel maps unweighted $L^2$ into $G$ in Hilbert--Schmidt norm. Shift only its output $p$. The Fourier cutoff picks up at most the fixed compact-support exponential $\exp(R_{\mathrm{support}}|\eta|)$. The time Fourier transform at $\omega(p+i\eta)+\omega(q)$ retains Gevrey decay in $\omega_{p}+\omega_{q}$, with a fixed strip prefactor. This decay absorbs $w_{a}(p)$, both ratio powers and the six-dimensional integration measure. Thus

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert A\rVert_{G\to G} &\le M_{A}, \\
\lVert B\rVert_{L^{2}\to G;\mathrm{HS}} &\le M_{B}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
$$

The same conclusions hold for conjugates, transposes and adjoints in the doubled real-linear equation. Their scalar bounds use the displayed cutoff derivative/support and mass constants. This is a quantitative finite integral estimate, not an unbounded-order energy assumption.

##### 3. Evolved Bogoliubov coefficients and factorial heads

Let $A_{t},B_{t}$ be the bounded number and Hilbert--Schmidt pair blocks of the symplectic evolution generated by $Q$, for $|t|\le\pi/2$. The doubled generator is bounded on $L^2$ plus its conjugate, with norm $M_{0}$. Hence its propagator has norm at most $\exp(M_{0}|t|)$. Duhamel in the equation for $B_{t}$, using the free number evolution on $G$ and (5), yields

$$

<a id="definition-f104g1-uniform-recursive-heat-kernel-audit"></a>**Definition F.10.4g.1 (Uniform Recursive Heat-Kernel Audit).** Let $\{L_h\}_{h\downarrow0}$ be finite local generators on a bounded region $O$, with symmetric-sector heat kernels $p_t^{(h)}(x,y)$ relative to declared reference measures. The window specifies its cutoff relative to the mesh and its upper time bound; no estimate outside that window is asserted. A two-sided on-diagonal scaling $p_t(x,x)\asymp t^{-q}$ gives spectral dimension $d_s=2q$ under the retained scaling definition. A volume/walk-dimension normalization gives $q=d_v/d_w$ only with its separate volume and kernel certificate. Thus $t^{-4/d_w}$ uses $d_v=4$, whereas $d_s=4$ uses $q=2$ on that two-sided scaling branch. A one-sided upper bound alone establishes neither dimension identity.

2. the finite forms are uniformly Markovian, conservative, tight on the local $L^2$ realization, and local on the audited window. They converge on the core in the Mosco-core sense: for canonical finite reconstructions $f_h,g_h$ of $f,g\in\mathcal C_O$,
$$
\mathcal E_h(f_h,g_h)\to\mathcal E_O(f,g),
\tag{F.10.4g.2}
$$
and the same core supplies the liminf and recovery sequences needed for the local finite-form compactness theorem;

3. if a horizon or scattering branch contains trapped predictive sets $\mathcal T_x(h)$ and dual update-frequency trapped sets $\mathcal T_p(h)$, the finite fractal-uncertainty audit holds:
$$
\left\|
\Pi_{\mathcal T_x(h)}
\mathcal F_h^{-1}
\Pi_{\mathcal T_p(h)}
\mathcal F_h
\right\|
\le
C h^{\beta_{\mathrm{FUP}}}.
\tag{F.10.4g.3}
$$

The exponent $\beta_{\mathrm{FUP}}$ is part of the audit certificate. It must either be derived from stated branch regularity data, such as doubling, porosity, or Frostman-type bounds for the trapped sets, or recorded as branch-supplied data under Convention P.14.1e.

<a id="theorem-f104g2-heat-kernel-audit-for-local-generator-tightness"></a>**Theorem F.10.4g.2 (Heat-Kernel Audit for Local Generator Tightness).** Retain Definition F.10.4g.1 with a complete varying-space Mosco liminf/recovery and limiting-form identification certificate. To use its scalar $L^2$ diffusion in Theorem F.0, additionally supply the identification with the observable generators $\mathcal D_h^*$ on the declared common local Banach realization; scalar heat-kernel convergence alone is not this operator-norm identification.

Assume the $\mathcal D_h^*$ are closed densely defined generators on that realization, with the stated common graph cores, and the coherent derivations $B_hA=i[H_h,A]$ extend from those cores in the graph norm to all of $D(\mathcal D_h^*)$, where they obey
$$
\|B_hA\|\le a\|\mathcal D_h^*A\|+b\|A\|,
\qquad 0\le a<1,
$$
uniformly, with $b\ge0$. Retain compatible self-adjoint Hamiltonians, their strong-resolvent and core-commutator convergence, and the corresponding limiting domain conditions. Assume the full sums and limiting sum are maximally dissipative. Require a Trotter--Kato certificate on the same Banach realization: convergence at some $\lambda>0$ of the full resolvents on a dense set, the uniform contraction-resolvent bound, and identification of the limiting resolvent with that of $\overline{\mathcal D_{\mathrm{cont}}^*+i[H_{\mathrm{cont}},\cdot]}$. Then the applicable relative-bounded perturbation and Trotter--Kato theorems give strong semigroup convergence on bounded positive-time intervals to the generator
$$
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cont}}^*
=\overline{\mathcal D_{\mathrm{cont}}^*+i[H_{\mathrm{cont}},\cdot]}.
\tag{F.10.4g.4}
$$
The exact source theorem and its varying-space or common-space hypotheses remain part of the convergence certificate.

For the trapped-set conclusion, require $\mathcal F_h$ to be unitary and the two indicated $\Pi$ to be orthogonal projections. Put $P_h=\Pi_{\mathcal T_x(h)}$, $Q_h=\mathcal F_h^{-1}\Pi_{\mathcal T_p(h)}\mathcal F_h$, and $\varepsilon_h=Ch^{\beta_{\mathrm{FUP}}}$. Every unit vector satisfies
$$
\|(I-P_h)\psi\|+\|(I-Q_h)\psi\|\ge1-\varepsilon_h.
$$
Thus no normalized family becomes asymptotically supported in both trapped projections. This is a localization obstruction; decay, leakage and removal by PCE require their own dynamical or response certificate.

*Proof.* For $A=\mathcal D_h^*$ and $B=B_h$, the relative estimate implies
$$
(1-a)\|Ax\|\le\|(A+B)x\|+b\|x\|,
\quad
\|(A+B)x\|\le(1+a)\|Ax\|+b\|x\|.
$$
Hence the two graph norms are equivalent, so completeness of the graph norm of $A$ makes $A+B$ closed on $D(A)$. This does not say that $B$ alone is closed on that domain. Maximal dissipativity supplies the contraction semigroups. The declared full-resolvent convergence, uniformly bounded at $\lambda$, extends from its dense test set to the common space; the applicable Trotter--Kato theorem then supplies semigroup convergence. Its continuum applicability is an imported certificate, not a consequence of the finite commutator estimate.

For localization,
$$
\|\psi-P_hQ_h\psi\|
\le\|(I-P_h)\psi\|+\|P_h(I-Q_h)\psi\|
\le\|(I-P_h)\psi\|+\|(I-Q_h)\psi\|.
$$
Since $\|P_hQ_h\|\le\varepsilon_h$, the triangle inequality gives the claimed lower bound. In particular, an exact common unit vector is impossible once $\varepsilon_h<1$. No evolution operator occurs in this argument, so it establishes no decay or leakage rate. ∎

<a id="definition-f104g3-local-bochner-mosco-certificate"></a>**Definition F.10.4g.3 (Local Bochner-Mosco Certificate).** A local Bochner-Mosco certificate on a bounded operational region $O$ is a finite record

$$
\mathfrak B^{BM}_{O}
=
(\mathcal C_O,\Gamma_h,\Gamma_{2,h},K_h,N_h,\mathfrak B_h,\mathfrak C_h,\mathfrak R_h,\mathfrak H_h,\nu_O)
$$

such that:

1. $\mathcal C_O$ is the retained radius-2 polynomial test core used by Theorem D.6e, restricted to $O$ and closed under the carré-du-champ operations required on that core.
2. $\Gamma_h$ and $\Gamma_{2,h}$ are the finite carré-du-champ and iterated carré-du-champ forms of the local finite generator on $\mathcal C_O$.
3. The finite forms are uniformly Markovian, conservative, local on the audited window, and Mosco-core convergent as in Definition F.10.4g.1.
4. The radius-2 Bakry-Émery defect $\mathfrak B_h$ of Theorem D.6e tends to zero on the cover of $O$ with limiting parameters $K_h\to K$ and $N_h\to4$.
5. The finite-core and recovery defects $\mathfrak C_h$ and $\mathfrak R_h$ of Theorem D.6e tend to zero on the same retained core.
6. The local Euclidean-rigidity defect $\mathfrak H_h$ is recorded when the regular-manifold upgrade is invoked; otherwise the output is only the retained metric-measure RCD branch.
7. On the declared local realization and varying-space identifications, all hypotheses of Theorem C.6c are supplied: complete full-support length metric-measure spaces with quadratic Cheeger energy, Sobolev-to-Lipschitz and integrability properties; global generator-domain $\mathrm{BE}(K_h,4)$ inequalities; and Mosco, heat-flow, and carré-du-champ test convergence sufficient to pass those inequalities to the limit. The candidate-form identification and both Mosco inequalities required by Theorem D.6e are included.
8. The heat-kernel audit has spectral dimension $d_s=4+o(1)$ on the same macroscopic window. The declared normalization satisfies $\mu=\mathcal H^4$ on the limiting local realization, as required for strict noncollapse in Theorem C.6c.

<a id="corollary-f104g4-local-rcd-gate-from-the-bochner-mosco-certificate"></a>**Corollary F.10.4g.4 (Local RCD Gate from the Bochner-Mosco Certificate).** If $\mathfrak B^{BM}_{O}$ is accepted on a bounded regular region $O$, then every selected Mosco/measured-GH subsequential limit on $O$ satisfies the retained operational version of noncollapsed $\mathrm{RCD}^*(K,4)$, and the limiting Cheeger energy is quadratic. A response-active non-quadratic or Finsler limit fails this gate unless the non-quadratic directions are response-null.

*Proof.* Items 3-5 supply the declared finite-core defects. Item 7 supplies both Mosco inequalities and the candidate Cheeger-form identification used by Theorem D.6e, together with the ambient, generator-domain, and convergence hypotheses of Theorem C.6c. That theorem gives the local $\mathrm{RCD}^*(K,4)$ conclusion, and item 8 supplies its Hausdorff-measure normalization for strict noncollapse. A response-active non-quadratic direction would violate the quadratic Cheeger-energy conclusion; if the direction is response-null, it is removed by the PPI quotient rather than retained as a distinct continuum energy. ∎

<a id="theorem-f104g4a-response-active-finsler-mosco-countermodel"></a>**Theorem F.10.4g.4a (Response-Active Finsler Mosco Countermodel).** Let $\mathbb T^4=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^4$, let $h=n^{-1}$, let $V_h=(h\mathbb Z/\mathbb Z)^4$, and set
$$
\mathcal X_h=
\left(h^2\mathbb Z\cap[-h^{-1},h^{-1}]\right)^{V_h}.
$$
Thus every approximating carrier has finitely many configurations. For $u\in\mathcal X_h$, write
$$
D_{j,h}u(x)=\frac{u(x+he_j)-u(x)}h
$$
and define the finite, translation-invariant, nearest-neighbor propagation cost
$$
\mathcal E_h(u)
=
\frac{h^4}{2}\sum_{x\in V_h}
\left(\sum_{j=1}^4|D_{j,h}u(x)|\right)^2.
\tag{F.10.4g.4a.1}
$$
Embed a configuration as the function $J_hu$ constant with value $u(x)$ on the periodic cube $x+[0,h)^4$. Extend $\mathcal E_h$ by $+\infty$ to all other elements of $L^2(\mathbb T^4)$. In this common space, the weak-liminf and strong-recovery Mosco conditions hold for
$$
\mathcal E(u)=
\begin{cases}
\frac12\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb T^4}
\left(\sum_{j=1}^4|\partial_ju|\right)^2dx,
&u\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb T^4),\\
+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\tag{F.10.4g.4a.2}
$$
This is the Cheeger energy of the flat torus with tangent norm $\ell^\infty$ and cotangent norm $\ell^1$. For $f(x)=\sin(2\pi x_1)$ and $g(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)$,
$$
\mathcal E(f+g)+\mathcal E(f-g)-2\mathcal E(f)-2\mathcal E(g)
=2\int|\partial_1f\,\partial_2g|\,dx=32.
\tag{F.10.4g.4a.3}
$$
For every pair with $u,v,u+v,u-v\in\mathcal X_h$, retain the finite response
$$
\mathfrak r_h(u,v)=
\bigl(\mathcal E_h(u),\mathcal E_h(v),
\mathcal E_h(u+v)+\mathcal E_h(u-v)-2\mathcal E_h(u)-2\mathcal E_h(v)\bigr).
\tag{F.10.4g.4a.4}
$$
It is a sum of radius-one terms. On the finite Hilbert space with basis indexed by these pairs, its coordinates are diagonal self-adjoint observables and the basis readout is a normalized PVM. The response distinguishes this nonquadratic energy from every quadratic energy.

*Proof.* Suppose $J_hu_h\rightharpoonup u$ in $L^2$ and the liminf of the energies is finite. Pass to a subsequence attaining that liminf with bounded energies. Let $G_{j,h}$ be constant on each cube with value $D_{j,h}u_h(x)$. Since
$$
\mathcal E_h(u_h)=\int\Phi(G_h)\,dx,\qquad
\Phi(\xi)=\tfrac12\|\xi\|_1^2\ge\tfrac12\|\xi\|_2^2,
$$
the four gradients have a weakly convergent $L^2$ subsequence. For a smooth periodic test function $\varphi$, discrete summation by parts gives
$$
\int G_{j,h}\varphi\,dx
=-h^4\sum_xu_h(x)
\frac{\bar\varphi_h(x)-\bar\varphi_h(x-he_j)}h,
$$
where $\bar\varphi_h(x)$ is the average of $\varphi$ on the cube at $x$. The piecewise-constant difference of these averages converges uniformly to $\partial_j\varphi$. Weak convergence and boundedness of $J_hu_h$ identify the gradient limit as $\partial_ju$. Thus $u\in W^{1,2}$, and weak lower semicontinuity of the integral of the convex continuous function $\Phi$ gives the liminf bound.

For smooth periodic $u$, round its grid samples to $h^2\mathbb Z$. Each value error is at most $h^2/2$, hence each forward-difference error is at most $h$. The amplitude cutoff is inactive for sufficiently small $h$. Uniform convergence of the differences gives energy convergence and $J_hu_h\to u$ strongly. Smooth approximation in $W^{1,2}$ and a diagonal choice give recovery for every finite-energy $u$; for an infinite-energy $L^2$ function, smooth $L^2$ approximation supplies a strong configuration approximation and the upper bound is automatic. The continuity estimate
$$
|\Phi(\xi)-\Phi(\eta)|
\le C(\|\xi\|_2+\|\eta\|_2)\|\xi-\eta\|_2
$$
justifies the energy convergence under the smooth $W^{1,2}$ approximation.

For the Cheeger identification, the local metric slope of a smooth function is the dual norm $\|\nabla u\|_1$. Mollification and convexity give smooth recovery, while the preceding weak lower-semicontinuity argument gives the relaxation lower bound; hence its relaxed squared-slope energy is $\mathcal E$. Finally, $\int_0^1|2\pi\cos(2\pi x)|\,dx=4$, so the displayed gap is $2\cdot4^2=32$. Quantized samples of $f,g$ and their sums and differences satisfy the amplitude constraint for small $h$, and their energies converge by the same difference estimate. Their finite response therefore tends to the nonzero gap, proving response activity. ∎

Theorem F.10.4g.4a gives a response-active Finsler/nonquadratic alternative. It shows that quadratic-RCD rigidity does not hold unconditionally; Corollary F.10.4g.4 remains valid on branches carrying its stronger Bochner-Mosco certificate.

<a id="definition-f104g5-coherent-hamiltonian-handling-certificate"></a>**Definition F.10.4g.5 (Coherent Hamiltonian Handling Certificate).** Let $H_{n,O}$ be the coherent Hamiltonian part of the local generator on $O$. A coherent Hamiltonian handling certificate is a finite record

$$
\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{coh}}(O)
=
(H_{n,O}^{\mathrm{res}},V_{n,O}^{\mathrm{null}},\Theta_O,\Psi_O,\mathfrak h_{\mathrm{coh}})
$$

where $H_{n,O}^{\mathrm{res}}$ acts on response-active classes, $V_{n,O}^{\mathrm{null}}$ acts only on response-null classes, and $H_{n,O}=H_{n,O}^{\mathrm{res}}+V_{n,O}^{\mathrm{null}}$ before passage to the retained local quotient. The indicator $\Theta_O$ is accepted only with one of the following witnesses:

1. Retention witness: $\Theta_O=1$, the operators $H_{n,O}^{\mathrm{res}}$ are self-adjoint on compatible local Hilbert spaces, and they converge in local strong-resolvent form to a self-adjoint finite-energy-density operator $H_{\mathrm{cont},O}^{\mathrm{res}}$. The witness also supplies the common algebraic graph core $\mathcal C_O$ used in Theorem F.10.4g.2 and constants $a<1$, $b<\infty$, independent of $n$, such that
$$
\|[H_{n,O}^{\mathrm{res}},A]\|
\le
a\|\mathcal D_{n,O}^*A\|+b\|A\|
\qquad
(A\in\mathcal C_O),
$$
and, for every convergent core sequence $A_n\to A$,
$$
[H_{n,O}^{\mathrm{res}},A_n]
\longrightarrow
[H_{\mathrm{cont},O}^{\mathrm{res}},A].
$$
2. Cancellation witness: $\Theta_O=0$ and $H_{n,O}^{\mathrm{res}}$ is removed by an explicit response-null identification or by an accepted defect-filling datum $D$ satisfying $[H_{n,O}^{\mathrm{res}}]+\partial D=0$ in the finite obstruction complex.

If neither witness is supplied, the coherent Hamiltonian part of the AQFT bridge remains open on $O$.

<a id="corollary-f104g6-closure-of-the-coherent-hamiltonian-handling-gate"></a>**Corollary F.10.4g.6 (Closure of the Coherent-Hamiltonian Handling Gate).** Assume $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{coh}}(O)$ is accepted on each bounded operational region of the retained cover and that the heat-kernel/Mosco, closed-generator, maximal-dissipativity, and full-generator resolvent/Trotter--Kato hypotheses of Theorem F.10.4g.2 hold on the same regions. The coherent certificate supplies the separate Hamiltonian-handling entries of that theorem. On the retention branch,

$$
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cont}}^*
=
i[H_{\mathrm{cont},O}^{\mathrm{res}},\cdot]+\mathcal D_{\mathrm{cont},O}^*.
$$

On the cancellation branch,

$$
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cont}}^*
=
\mathcal D_{\mathrm{cont},O}^*.
$$

No coherent term is silently discarded: it is either transported by an accepted convergence witness, removed by an accepted response-null or defect-filling witness, or left as an open bridge condition.

*Proof.* The retention witness supplies self-adjoint strong-resolvent convergence, the common graph core, the uniform relative bound with constant $a<1$, and convergence of the commutators on every convergent core sequence. Together with the stated full-generator stability and resolvent hypotheses, these data permit application of Theorem F.10.4g.2 to identify the limiting sum. The cancellation witness removes the response-active coherent term either by the response quotient or by exact defect filling in the obstruction complex. If neither witness is present, the hypotheses of this corollary are absent and no closure is asserted. ∎

<a id="proposition-f104g7-gkls-response-does-not-canonically-split-coherent-and-dissipative-parts"></a>**Proposition F.10.4g.7 (GKLS Response Does Not Canonically Split Coherent and Dissipative Parts).** On a finite matrix carrier, write the one-channel Schrödinger-picture generator as
$$
\mathcal L_{H,L}(\rho)
=-i[H,\rho]
+L\rho L^\dagger
-\frac12\{L^\dagger L,\rho\}.
\tag{F.10.4g.7.1}
$$
For every $c\in\mathbb C$, the transformation
$$
L'=L+cI,
\qquad
H'=H+\frac{1}{2i}\bigl(\bar cL-cL^\dagger\bigr)
\tag{F.10.4g.7.2}
$$
obeys $\mathcal L_{H',L'}=\mathcal L_{H,L}$ on the full matrix algebra. The response generator therefore does not canonically determine its coherent/dissipative decomposition.

The ambiguity is nonempty already on a qubit. With $H=0$, $L=\sigma_x$, and $c=i$, equation (F.10.4g.7.2) gives
$$
L'=\sigma_x+iI,
\qquad
H'=-\sigma_x\ne H,
\qquad
\mathcal L_{H',L'}=\mathcal L_{H,L}.
\tag{F.10.4g.7.3}
$$

*Proof.* Expanding the dissipator after $L\mapsto L+cI$ cancels the $|c|^2$ terms and adds
$$
\frac12[\bar cL-cL^\dagger,\rho].
$$
The Hamiltonian increment in (F.10.4g.7.2) contributes the negative of this commutator, proving equality for every matrix $\rho$. Substitution gives (F.10.4g.7.3). Proposition F.10.12h independently checks equality on the four matrix units, which form a basis of $M_2(\mathbb C)$, and rejects the opposite Hamiltonian-sign mutation. ∎

Thus a traceless-jump, orthogonality, minimal-noise, or comparable gauge can define a representative when included as additional branch data. Definition F.10.4g.5 must carry that gauge choice when it transports separate coherent and dissipative pieces to the continuum; the carrier and convergence records required there remain independent of the finite noncanonicity result.

<a id="proposition-f104g8-exact-gauge-fixed-qubit-dephasing-certificate"></a>**Proposition F.10.4g.8 (Exact Gauge-Fixed Qubit Dephasing Certificate).** On $M_2(\mathbb C)$ fix the normalized traceless Pauli basis $F_j=\sigma_j/\sqrt2$ and the traceless-Hamiltonian gauge. For $\omega\in\mathbb R$ and $\gamma\ge0$, the Heisenberg generator
$$
\mathcal L^*(A)
=
i\left[\frac\omega2\sigma_z,A\right]
+
\gamma(\sigma_zA\sigma_z-A)
\tag{F.10.4g.8.1}
$$
has the gauge-fixed GKLS record
$$
H=\frac\omega2\sigma_z,
\qquad
C=\operatorname{diag}(0,0,2\gamma)
\tag{F.10.4g.8.2}
$$
in the ordered basis $(F_x,F_y,F_z)$. It generates the explicit completely positive unital semigroup
$$
\Phi_t^*(\sigma_z)=\sigma_z,
\qquad
\Phi_t^*(\sigma_x+i\sigma_y)
=e^{(-2\gamma+i\omega)t}(\sigma_x+i\sigma_y).
\tag{F.10.4g.8.3}
$$
Under the constant refinement system $M_2\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}M_2$, set
$$
H_{n,O}^{\mathrm{res}}=H,
\quad
V_{n,O}^{\mathrm{null}}=0,
\quad
\Theta_O=1,
\quad
\Psi_O=\operatorname{id},
\quad
\mathcal C_O=M_2(\mathbb C).
\tag{F.10.4g.8.4}
$$
The coherent operators, dissipators, common cores, and semigroups then have identically zero convergence defect, and the relative bound in Definition F.10.4g.5 holds with $a=0$ and $b=|\omega|$. Hence (F.10.4g.8.1)--(F.10.4g.8.4) explicitly populate the finite-carrier and separate-convergence slots of that definition on this branch.

*Proof.* Substituting $L=\sqrt\gamma\,\sigma_z$ into the GKLS formula gives the dissipative term in (F.10.4g.8.1); in the normalized basis its only nonzero Kossakowski entry is $2\gamma$. Direct evaluation on the Pauli basis gives (F.10.4g.8.3), which is a phase rotation composed with dephasing and is completely positive and unital. Identity embeddings make every comparison difference zero, and $\|[H,A]\|\le2\|H\|\|A\|=|\omega|\|A\|$ gives the declared relative bound. ∎

This finite certificate fixes a representative because the basis and gauge are declared data. It does not make the split canonical from the full response generator, nor does it provide a nonconstant continuum approximation.

<a id="proposition-f104g9-nonconstant-dyadic-gauge-fixed-dephasing-sequence"></a>**Proposition F.10.4g.9 (Nonconstant Dyadic Gauge-Fixed Dephasing Sequence).** Fix $d\ge1$, $\omega\in\mathbb R$, $\gamma\ge0$, and real sequences $\omega_n\to\omega$ and $\gamma_n\to\gamma$ with $\gamma_n\ge0$. Let $\Lambda_n=2^{-n}\{0,\ldots,2^n-1\}^d\subset[0,1)^d$, with physical mesh $a_n=2^{-n}$, so that $\Lambda_n\subset\Lambda_{n+1}$ and $0\in\Lambda_n$. Put $\mathfrak A_n=\bigotimes_{x\in\Lambda_n}M_2(\mathbb C)$, let $\mathfrak A_n(O)$ be the subalgebra of the sites in $\Lambda_n\cap O$, and let $j_n^m(A)=A\otimes I_{\Lambda_m\setminus\Lambda_n}$ for $m\ge n$. In the traceless-Hamiltonian, traceless-jump gauge, with jump operators $\sqrt{\gamma_n}\,\sigma_z^{(x)}$, define
$$
\mathcal L_n^*=i[H_n,\cdot\,]+\mathcal D_n^*,
\qquad
H_n=\frac{\omega_n}2\sigma_z^{(0)},
\qquad
\mathcal D_n^*(A)=\gamma_n\sum_{x\in\Lambda_n}\bigl(\sigma_z^{(x)}A\sigma_z^{(x)}-A\bigr).
\tag{F.10.4g.9.1}
$$
Let $\mathfrak A_\infty$ be the inductive-limit $C^*$-algebra, with canonical embeddings $j_n$ and local core $\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{loc}}=\bigcup_nj_n(\mathfrak A_n)$. Define $H=\frac\omega2\sigma_z^{(0)}$ and $\mathcal D^*$ by the same formula with $\gamma$ and $\Lambda_\infty=\bigcup_n\Lambda_n$; on $\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ the sum is finite. Then:

1. the maps $j_n^m$ are coherent, region-preserving, unital isometric $*$-monomorphisms, the algebras are nonconstant with $\dim\mathfrak A_n=4^{2^{nd}}$, and $a_n\to0$;
2. for $A\in\mathfrak A_n$ supported on $F\subset\Lambda_n$ and $m\ge n$,
$$
\bigl\|j_n^m(i[H_n,A])-i[H_m,j_n^mA]\bigr\|\le|\omega_n-\omega_m|\,\|A\|,
\qquad
\bigl\|j_n^m(\mathcal D_n^*A)-\mathcal D_m^*(j_n^mA)\bigr\|\le2|\gamma_n-\gamma_m|\,|F|\,\|A\|,
\tag{F.10.4g.9.2}
$$
so the coherent and dissipative parts separately satisfy (F.0.1) on $\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{loc}}$, with limits $i[H,\cdot]$ and $\mathcal D^*$. For $A=\sigma_x^{(0)}$ both differences are nonzero whenever $\omega_n\ne\omega_m$ and $\gamma_n\ne\gamma_m$;
3. let $T_t$ act on the algebra of each finite site set $F$ by $\operatorname{Ad}e^{\mathrm{itH}}\circ\bigotimes_{x\in F}e^{t\gamma(\operatorname{Ad}\sigma_z^{(x)}-\mathrm{id})}$. Then $T_t$ extends to a strongly continuous semigroup of unital completely positive contractions of $\mathfrak A_\infty$, whose generator is the closure of $\mathcal L^*=i[H,\cdot\,]+\mathcal D^*$ on the core $\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{loc}}$. For $A=j_n(A_n)$ supported on $F$ and $t\ge0$,
$$
\bigl\|j_n(e^{t\mathcal L_n^*}A_n)-T_tA\bigr\|\le t\bigl(|\omega_n-\omega|+2|\gamma_n-\gamma|\,|F|\bigr)\|A\|,
\tag{F.10.4g.9.3}
$$
and the coherent groups $\operatorname{Ad}e^{itH_n}$ and dephasing semigroups $e^{t\mathcal D_n^*}$ converge separately in the same way, with the respective terms of (F.10.4g.9.3);
4. on $O=[0,1)^d$, the entries $H_{n,O}^{\mathrm{res}}=H_n$, $V_{n,O}^{\mathrm{null}}=0$, $\Theta_O=1$, $\Psi_O=(j_n)_n$ and $\mathcal C_O=\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ populate the retention witness of Definition F.10.4g.5 in its bounded form, with $a=0$ and $b=\sup_n|\omega_n|$: $j_n(H_n)\to H$ in norm, and $[H_n,A_n]\to[H,A]$ for every convergent core sequence $A_n\to A$. The relative bound uses no part of $\mathcal D_n^*$, and every uniformly bounded, norm-convergent sequence of self-adjoint coherent parts meets the relative-bound and commutator-convergence conditions in this form.

*Proof.* Item 1 follows from $\Lambda_n\subset\Lambda_m$, $|\Lambda_n|=2^{nd}$ and the tensor-product form of $j_n^m$. For item 2, a dephasing term at a site outside $F$ annihilates $A\otimes I$, and $H_m-H_n=\frac{\omega_m-\omega_n}2\sigma_z^{(0)}$; since $\|[\sigma_z^{(0)},A]\|\le2\|A\|$ and $\|\sigma_z^{(x)}A\sigma_z^{(x)}-A\|\le2\|A\|$, the differences are $\frac{\omega_n-\omega_m}2\,i[\sigma_z^{(0)},A]$ and $(\gamma_n-\gamma_m)\sum_{x\in F}(\sigma_z^{(x)}A\sigma_z^{(x)}-A)$, which gives (F.10.4g.9.2). For $A=\sigma_x^{(0)}$ they equal $-(\omega_n-\omega_m)\sigma_y^{(0)}$ and $-2(\gamma_n-\gamma_m)\sigma_x^{(0)}$. The traceless-gauge GKLS record of a matrix-algebra generator is unique (Gorini, Kossakowski and Sudarshan 1976), so $H_n$ and $\mathcal D_n^*$ are the gauge-fixed coherent and dissipative parts of $\mathcal L_n^*$.

For item 3, the superoperators $i[H_n,\cdot]$ and $\operatorname{Ad}\sigma_z^{(x)}-\mathrm{id}$ commute pairwise, because $H_n$ is diagonal and commutes with every $\sigma_z^{(x)}$. Hence $e^{t\mathcal L_n^*}$ is the displayed product with $(\omega_n,\gamma_n)$; it leaves each $\mathfrak A_n(F)$ invariant, fixes the factors outside $F$, and is unital completely positive. The same formula with $(\omega,\gamma)$ defines $T_t$ on $\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ compatibly with every $j_n^m$. ##### 1. Scope and source

and the coherent part is $\theta H_{n}$, $\theta=1/3$. For the full evolution take $\beta=\theta$ and

for its supplied dissipative part take $\beta=0$. Let $G=\sum_{j=1}^{p}G_{j}$. Thus $G$ is exactly $L_{n}$ or $D_{n}$ in the fixed gauge, not a different gauge recovered from source response. The coherent part $B_{n}$ is separately realized by its calibrated finite Hamiltonian and, if desired, by the same product construction without collision contacts.

For these self-adjoint $h_{j}$ the supplied jump is normal and its norm has the exact formula $v_{j}^{2}=\kappa_{j}\lVert h_{j}\rVert^{2}+c^{2}/\kappa_{j}$. The local norms are $m$ or $J$, so for rational source parameters every $v_{j}^{2}$, $g_{j}$, $C$, $Q$ and selector bound below is explicitly rational; the square-root pulse amplitudes are algebraic.
