##### 2. One actual jump, one fresh environment

For a source operator $L$ and a fresh environment qubit in $|0\rangle$, define the self-adjoint block matrix

$$
V_L = \begin{bmatrix}0&L^*\\L&0\end{bmatrix}
$$

in the environment order $0,1$. It has norm $\lVert V_{L}\rVert=\lVert L\rVert=:v$. The collision unitary is

$$
U_L(\delta)=\exp(-i\sqrt{\delta}\, V_L).
$$

Its reduced Heisenberg channel is

$$
\Phi_\delta(A)=\langle 0|U_L(\delta)^*(A\otimes I)U_L(\delta)|0\rangle.
$$

Every $\Phi_{\delta}$ is UCP. A direct expansion gives

$$
\Phi_\delta(A)=A+\delta D_L(A)+R_\delta(A).
\tag{2.1}
$$

Indeed $V_{L}$ is odd under environment parity $\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, while $A\otimes I$ and the ready expectation are even, so all odd commutator orders vanish. The second order is

$$
\begin{aligned}
&-(\delta/2)\langle 0|[V_L,[V_L,A\otimes I]]|0\rangle \\
&=\delta[L^*AL-(L^*LA+AL^*L)/2].
\end{aligned}
$$

This is the actual supplied L, including its imaginary scalar. That scalar is physically present in the contact Hamiltonian; the coherent term c i[h,·] is produced by the interference terms in (2.1). It has not been dropped and re-added under a new label.

At every matrix amplification, for $\delta v^{2}\le 1$,

$$
\lVert R_{\delta}\rVert_{\mathrm{cb}}\le\sum_{k\ge 2}(2\sqrt{\delta}v)^{2k}/(2k)!\le(2/3)e^{2}\delta^{2}v^{4}.
$$

Since $\lVert D_{L}\rVert_{\mathrm{cb}}\le 2v^{2}$,

$$
\lVert e^{\delta D_{L}}-I-\delta D_{L}\rVert_{\mathrm{cb}}\le 2e^{2}\delta^{2}v^{4}.
$$

Consequently the convenient rational bound

$$
\lVert\Phi_{\delta}-e^{\delta D_{L}}\rVert_{\mathrm{cb}}\le 24\delta^{2}v^{4}
\tag{2.2}
$$

holds whenever $\delta v^{2}\le 1$. Also

$$
\lVert\Phi_{s}-I\rVert_{\mathrm{cb}}\le 8s v^{2}\quad\text{for } 0\le s\le\delta,\ \delta v^{2}\le 1.
\tag{2.3}
$$

The bound 8 follows from $e<3$ and $2+(2/3)e^{2}<8$. The numerical constants are slack; no small unrecorded parameter is hidden in them.

##### 3. One local step and one full cycle

Set $v_{j}=\lVert L_{j}\rVert$ and $b_{j}=2\beta\lVert h_{j}\rVert$. Chronologically apply the $j$th collision first and its coherent unitary second. Write $C_{j,\delta}=\exp(\delta\beta i[h_{j},\cdot])$ for the Heisenberg coherent channel. The resulting Heisenberg map is $\Psi_{j,\delta}=\Phi_{j,\delta}\circ C_{j,\delta}$: maps on final observables compose in the reverse of their chronological Schrödinger order. Both factors are contractions. Duhamel's two-factor product bound gives

$$
\lVert\Psi_{j,\delta}-e^{\delta G_{j}}\rVert_{\mathrm{cb}}\le\delta^{2}[24v_{j}^{4}+4\beta\lVert h_{j}\rVert v_{j}^{2}].
\tag{3.1}
$$

Here the extra term uses $(1/2)\lVert[\beta i[h_{j},\cdot],D_{L_{j}}]\rVert_{\mathrm{cb}}\le 4\beta\lVert h_{j}\rVert v_{j}^{2}$. This estimate uses no spectral assumption on $h_{j}$.

Use chronological order $j=1,\dots,p$ for a cycle, so its Heisenberg map is $\Psi_{\delta}=\Psi_{1,\delta}\circ\dots\circ\Psi_{p,\delta}$. For the simplified actual generators one may use

$$
\begin{aligned}
g_j&=2(\beta+c)\lVert h_j\rVert+2\kappa_j\lVert h_j\rVert^{2}, \\
S&=\sum g_j, \\
C&=\sum_j[24v_j^{4}+4\beta\lVert h_j\rVert v_j^{2}]+\sum_{j<k}g_jg_k.
\end{aligned}
$$

The many-factor contraction product bound and (3.1) give

$$
\lVert\Psi_{\delta}-e^{\delta G}\rVert_{\mathrm{cb}}\le C\delta^{2}.
\tag{3.2}
$$

After r cycles with fresh environments,

$$
\lVert\Psi_{\delta}^{r}-e^{r\delta G}\rVert_{\mathrm{cb}}\le rC\delta^{2}.
\tag{3.3}
$$

Freshness is a concrete finite resource: one environment M8 cell, with a nominated qubit subspace and six retained unused levels, is allocated to each jump contact. No used environment is reset or contacted again. Measurement is unnecessary during the dynamics; all environment registers can remain quantum archives.

##### 4. The physical schedule, including every partial cycle

Choose integer $r$ and $\delta=T/r$. Divide each physical cycle of duration $\delta$ into $2p$ consecutive slots, each of duration

$$

For the $j$th collision use a fixed smooth monotone ramp $f(u)=3u^{2}-2u^{3}$, $u\in[0,1]$, and the actual physical code Hamiltonian

$$
H_{\mathrm{col}}(s)=\hbar\sqrt{\delta}\, f'(s/\tau)V_{L_j}/\tau,\qquad 0\le s\le\tau.
$$

Its exact propagator at time $s$ is $\exp(-i\sqrt{\delta}f(s/\tau)V_{L_{j}})$, and at the slot end it is $U_{L_{j}}(\delta)$. For the coherent slot use

$$
H_{\mathrm{coh}}(s)=\hbar\delta\beta f'(s/\tau)h_j/\tau.
$$

Its endpoint is $\exp(-i\delta\beta h_{j})$. For $\beta=0$ this is a declared idle slot. No target evolution is first performed and then followed by uncounted pulse time: these $2p$ slots are the entire physical $\delta$ interval.

Add one predeclared constant scalar baseline $E_{\mathrm{base}}$ I throughout [0,T], with

$$
E_{\mathrm{base}}=\hbar\nu+3p\hbar \max_j\{v_j/\sqrt{\delta},\ \beta\lVert h_j\rVert\},\qquad \nu>0.
$$

Since $\max f'=3/2$, this makes every total code Hamiltonian positive. For this run the preinstalled free code matrix is $E_{\mathrm{base}}I$; every contact Hamiltonian pulse vanishes at its endpoints, so consecutive slots meet continuously at that same baseline and no instantaneous source-energy quench is omitted. The coherent Hamiltonian $\theta H_{n}$ is the separately calibrated retained generator obtained in the displayed collision limit, not a claim that the instantaneous contact Hamiltonian equals $\theta H_{n}$. During a partial collision slot the reduced channel is $\Phi_{\delta f^{2}}$; during a partial coherent slot it is the unitary channel with parameter $\delta f$. Previously used environments never return. Thus the partial-cycle reduced source map $F_{s}$, $0\le s<\delta$, is a composition of complete or partial fresh-environment channels. Put

$$
Q=\sum_j(2\beta\lVert h_j\rVert+8v_j^{2}).
$$

Equation (2.3), the unitary Duhamel bound and telescoping give

$$
\lVert F_{s}-I\rVert_{\mathrm{cb}}\le\delta Q.
\tag{4.1}
$$

At arbitrary physical time $t=k\delta+s$, $k$ full cycles occur before the partial current cycle. The implemented Heisenberg source channel is therefore $\Psi_{\delta}^{k}\circ F_{s}$. In particular, $\lVert\Psi_{\delta}^{k}F_{s}-e^{k\delta G}e^{sG}\rVert_{\mathrm{cb}}$ is at most $\lVert\Psi_{\delta}^{k}-e^{k\delta G}\rVert_{\mathrm{cb}}+\lVert F_{s}-e^{sG}\rVert_{\mathrm{cb}}$, by complete contractivity. Using $\lVert e^{sG}-I\rVert_{\mathrm{cb}}\le sS$ yields

&\quad\le\delta[TC+Q+S].
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.2}
$$

This is convergence throughout the physical clock window, not only at one chosen final time. It also supplies every fixed finite set of readout times. Complete interventions chosen at cycle boundaries have the usual telescoping diamond error, including arbitrary retained reference systems. If an intervention is required at another exact timestamp, install the grid to include that timestamp when possible, or supply its explicit clock/rounding error and corresponding continuity estimate; a changed timestamp is not declared response-null.

An effective selector for any $\varepsilon>0$ is

$$
r\ge\lceil T \max\{\max_j v_j^{2},\ (TC+Q+S)/\varepsilon\}\rceil,\qquad r\ge 1.
\tag{4.3}
$$

Then $\delta v_{j}^{2}\le 1$ and (4.2) is $\le\varepsilon$. All pulse amplitudes, rail coefficients, environment counts and precision budgets are finite at the selected regulator. In particular,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sup\lVert H_{\mathrm{col}}\rVert&\le 3p\hbar v_j/\sqrt{\delta}, \\
\sup\lVert H_{\mathrm{coh}}\rVert&\le 3p\hbar\beta\lVert h_j\rVert.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.4}

The $1/\sqrt{\delta}$ escalation is explicit. Because $v_{j}$ contains $c/\sqrt{\kappa_{j}}$, its large outer-site value also increases $r$ and costs; it is not replaced by the smaller norm of the simplified generator when estimating the physical contact.

###### 6.1 A valid positive intrinsic local certificate

Use precisely the fixed-mesh M8 source. At each $x\in\mathbb Z^d$ retain $\mathbb C^8=\mathbb C^2_{\rm act}\otimes\mathbb C^4_{\rm spec}$, with the spectator factor intact. Let $m>2dJ>0$ and

For expanding stages $\Lambda_n$, put $U_n=U\cap\Lambda_n$, embed its Hilbert space isometrically by the declared vacuum on missing sites, and extend its Hamiltonian by identity tensor factors on those sites. \[
 L_Z=\sqrt{\kappa_Z}h_Z+i\frac{c_0}{\sqrt{\kappa_Z}}I_Z,

Their dissipator is $\mathcal D_U=c_0\delta_U+K_U$, where

 \|\theta\delta_U A\|\le\tfrac12\|\mathcal D_U A\|+\gamma\|A\|.\tag{F.10.4g.10.4}

This holds uniformly in stages and finite regions. The full matrix algebra is its own common algebraic graph core. All generators are bounded and all local limits eventually exact. The matrices obey
\[
0\le H_U\le(m+dJ)|U|I,
\]
with vacuum and fully filled energies $0$ and $m|U|$, so there is a finite per-site energy bound and actual response-active extensivity as the region grows. These are real finite-region retention data. Their finite supplied jump/control realization is covered by Theorem F.10.4g.10.

For $U\subset V$, the Hilbert and observable inclusions are explicit and coherent. The Hamiltonians, however, do not intertwine under those inclusions: an excitation at a boundary site of $U$ hops into $V\setminus U$. ###### 6.2 Exact coherent conditional-expectation compatibility

Let $i_U^V(A)=A\otimes I$ and let $E_U^V$ be normalized partial trace on all outside M8 factors. For every $A\in\mathcal A(U)$,
\[
 E_U^V\delta_Vi_U^V(A)=\delta_UA.\tag{F.10.4g.10.5}
\]
Every crossing coherent bond has a traceless outside $s^\pm$ factor, and all fully outside terms commute with $A$. This proves (F.10.4g.10.5) directly. It is a projected identity. It is not $\delta_Vi_U^V=i_U^V\delta_U$.

###### 6.3 An explicit boundary noise term

Take one crossing active bond $xy$, with $x\in U$, $y\notin U$, and suppress unaffected sites/spectators. For every $A\in M_2$,
\[
 E_x^{xy}D_{h_{xy}}(A\otimes I)
 =\frac{J^2}{2}\big(D_{s^+}+D_{s^-}\big)(A),\tag{F.10.4g.10.6}
\]
where $D_L(A)=L^*AL-\tfrac12\{L^*L,A\}$.

*Proof.* Multiplying the two terms of $h_{xy}$ gives
\[
 E(h_{xy}(A\otimes I)h_{xy})
 =\frac{J^2}{2}(s^+As^-+s^-As^+),\qquad E(h_{xy}^2)=\frac{J^2}{2}I.
\]
Insert these identities in the dissipator and use $s^+s^-+s^-s^+=I$. ∎

Therefore compressing the actual dissipative generator of a larger region gives
\[
 E_U^V\mathcal D_V i_U^V
 =\mathcal D_U+
 \sum_{xy\text{ crossing}}\frac{\kappa_{xy}J^2}{2}
 (D_{s_x^+}+D_{s_x^-}).\tag{F.10.4g.10.7}
\]
The additional term is not zero. On $N_x$, a single edge contributes $(\kappa_{xy}J^2/2)(I-2N_x)$. One can explicitly declare this as a boundary bath, but then that bath is part of the local source record; it is not the original intrinsic truncation, and does not by itself remove dynamical memory from compression.

###### 6.4 The compressed coherent evolution is not a semigroup

With just the same crossing XX bond and the commuting on-site mass terms, let
\[
\Phi_t(A)=E_x^{xy}\big(e^{itH_{xy}}(A\otimes I)e^{-itH_{xy}}\big),
\qquad Z_x=N_x-\tfrac12 I.
\]
Exact two-site evolution gives
\[
 \Phi_t(Z_x)=\cos^2(Jt)Z_x.\tag{F.10.4g.10.8}
\]
Indeed the one-excitation sector rotates with off-diagonal coupling $-J$, and the partial trace removes the crossing coherences; $N_y$ is replaced by $I/2$. Consequently
\[
 \Phi_s\Phi_t(Z_x)=\cos^2(Js)\cos^2(Jt)Z_x
 \ne \cos^2(J(s+t))Z_x
\]
for suitable $s,t>0$. Equivalently the first derivative at zero is zero while the second derivative on $Z_x$ is $-2J^2Z_x$. A finite-dimensional semigroup with zero generator on this invariant one-dimensional subspace would be constant there. This is already the accepted coherent branch, so separate Hamiltonian handling cannot be recovered from the compression shortcut.

Nothing here requires an exact global/regional intertwining axiom. The calculations show directly what the proposed projection method supplies and what it fails to supply.

### F.10.5 Golay Self-Duality and Finite-Resolution Haag Duality

<a id="definition-f105a-golay-pauli-carrier"></a>**Definition F.10.5a (Golay-Pauli Carrier).** Let
$$
V_{24}:=\mathbb F_2^{24}\oplus\mathbb F_2^{24}
$$
with symplectic form
$$
\omega((x,z),(x',z'))=x\cdot z'+x'\cdot z
\quad\text{in }\mathbb F_2.
$$
Let $\mathcal W(V_{24})$ be the finite Weyl-Pauli algebra generated by $W(v)$, $v\in V_{24}$, with
$$
W(v)W(w)=(-1)^{\omega(v,w)}W(w)W(v).
$$
For any subspace $S\le V_{24}$, let $\mathfrak A(S)$ be the unital $*$-algebra generated by $\{W(s):s\in S\}$.

<a id="lemma-f105b-finite-symplectic-commutant"></a>**Lemma F.10.5b (Finite Symplectic Commutant).** In the full matrix representation of the finite Weyl--Pauli algebra,
$$
\mathfrak A(S)'=\mathfrak A(S^{\perp_\omega})
\tag{F.10.5.1}
$$
exactly. Their common center is $\mathfrak A(S\cap S^{\perp_\omega})$; no quotient by that center is taken.

*Proof.* The Weyl matrices form a linear basis, and $\mathfrak A(S)$ is their span over $s\in S$. Conjugation by $W(s)$ multiplies $W(v)$ by $(-1)^{\omega(s,v)}$. Thus, for $X=\sum_vc_vW(v)$, the equations $W(s)XW(s)^*=X$ force $c_v=0$ whenever some $s\in S$ has $\omega(s,v)=1$. The surviving indices are precisely $S^{\perp_\omega}$, proving the exact commutant identity. Intersecting its basis span with the span over $S$ gives the stated center. ∎

<a id="theorem-f105c-finite-symplectic-complement-duality-on-the-marked-carrier"></a>**Theorem F.10.5c (Finite Symplectic-Complement Duality on the Marked Carrier).** Let a finite operational region $R$ be represented by a subspace $S_R\le V_{24}$ and assume its operational complement is represented by
$$
S_{R^c}=S_R^{\perp_\omega}.
$$
Then
$$
\mathfrak A(R)'=\mathfrak A(R^c).
\tag{F.10.5.2}
$$
If, in addition, every allowed truncated-subcarrier duality defect is represented by a nonzero element of an embedded extended Golay stabilizer code, then each such defect has marked support weight at least $8$.

*Proof.* Lemma F.10.5b and the complement hypothesis give
$$
\mathfrak A(R)'
=
\mathfrak A(S_R^{\perp_\omega})
=
\mathfrak A(S_{R^c})
=
\mathfrak A(R^c).
$$
For the conditional support statement, the extended binary Golay code has minimum Hamming weight $8$, so every nonzero element of the assumed defect code has support at least $8$. No weight conclusion follows for defects outside that code. ∎

<a id="corollary-f105d-continuum-haag-duality-under-a-commutant-comparison-certificate"></a>**Corollary F.10.5d (Continuum Haag Duality under a Commutant-Comparison Certificate).** Retain the compatible-family quotient and represented net of Theorems F.10.1--F.10.2. At each finite stage require $S_{R^c}=S_R^{\perp_\omega}$, so Theorem F.10.5c gives exact finite duality. For a represented limiting diamond algebra $\mathfrak A(\mathcal O)\subset B(\mathcal H)$, additionally assume:
1. complementary local representatives commute in the quotient, giving $\mathfrak A(\mathcal O')\subseteq\mathfrak A(\mathcal O)'$;
2. every operator in $\mathfrak A(\mathcal O)'$ is a strong-operator limit of a uniformly bounded net of represented complementary compatible families, with all declared boundary errors tending to zero, and $\mathfrak A(\mathcal O')$ is the corresponding von Neumann closure.
Then
$$
\mathfrak A(\mathcal O)'=\mathfrak A(\mathcal O').
$$

*Proof.* Item 1 is one inclusion. Item 2 places every element of the commutant in the strong-operator closed complementary algebra, proving the reverse inclusion. The compatible-family quotient removes norm-null families but does not by itself preserve commutants or provide item 2. Finite Golay duality and vanishing boundary errors therefore remain inputs to, rather than substitutes for, the commutant-comparison certificate. ∎

### F.10.6 Predictive Markov-Blanket Locality

<a id="definition-f106a-predictive-markov-boundary"></a>**Definition F.10.6a (Predictive Markov Boundary).** Fix a retained state and a complete class of interior and exterior protocols. In the classical finite branch, a boundary variable $B_R$ is sufficient when
$$
\Pr(E_{\bar R}\mid X_R,B_R)=\Pr(E_{\bar R}\mid B_R)
\tag{F.10.6.1}
$$
on the support of the conditioning law, for every retained protocol outcome.

For the quantum statement, require a registered realization by three independent finite tensor factors $R,B_R,\bar R$, with a normalized density matrix and channels representing the complete retained protocol class. Then the boundary is quantum Markov when
$$
I(R:\bar R\mid B_R)_\rho=0.
\tag{F.10.6.2}
$$
A gauge-split common center must first be represented as classical data in such a realization. If both local protocol algebras can read its label, that accessible label is retained in both local records, for example by classical copies. Coarsening the boundary register does not erase those interior or exterior records. All comparisons of sufficient boundary data use the same retained local protocols and state. A sufficient boundary is PCE-minimal under coarsening when no strict coarsening remains sufficient for that class.

<a id="theorem-f106b-locality-as-boundary-conditional-independence"></a>**Theorem F.10.6b (Locality as Boundary Conditional Independence).** On a finite branch:

1. In the classical case, (F.10.6.1) is equivalent to conditional independence
$$
X_R\perp E_{\bar R}\mid B_R
$$
for every exterior protocol outcome.
2. In the quantum finite-algebra case, (F.10.6.2) is equivalent to the existence of a completely positive trace-preserving recovery map
$$
\mathcal R_{B_R\to B_R\bar R}
$$
such that
$$
\rho_{R B_R\bar R}
=
(\operatorname{id}_R\otimes\mathcal R_{B_R\to B_R\bar R})(\rho_{R B_R}).
\tag{F.10.6.3}
$$
3. If $B_R$ is coarsest in the preorder of sufficient boundary data—meaning that for every sufficient $B'_R$ there is a classical stochastic map or quantum channel $B'_R\to B_R$ preserving all exterior protocol distributions—then every sufficient boundary datum factors through $B_R$ up to operational equivalence. PCE-minimality under strict coarsening alone does not imply this coarsest property.

*Proof.* In the classical branch, conditional independence $X_R\perp E_{\bar R}\mid B_R$ is defined by
$$
\Pr(X_R,E_{\bar R}\mid B_R)
=
\Pr(X_R\mid B_R)\Pr(E_{\bar R}\mid B_R).
$$
Whenever $\Pr(X_R,B_R)>0$, division by $\Pr(X_R\mid B_R)$ gives (F.10.6.1). Conversely, multiplying (F.10.6.1) by $\Pr(X_R\mid B_R)$ gives the displayed factorization. This proves (1).

For the quantum branch, Definition F.10.6a supplies finite tensor factors and a normalized density matrix. The finite-dimensional equality theorem of Hayden, Jozsa, Petz and Winter (2004), on these factors and the supports of their marginals, gives a CPTP recovery channel when $I(R:\bar R\mid B_R)_\rho=0$; full rank is not required. This is the retained external Markov theorem. Conversely, exact recovery by a channel on $B_R$ and data processing give
$$
I(R:B_R)_\rho\ge I(R:B_R\bar R)_\rho
\ge I(R:B_R)_\rho.
$$
The second inequality is partial trace. Equality and the chain rule therefore give $I(R:\bar R\mid B_R)_\rho=0$. This proves item 2 on its registered finite tensor-product domain.

For (3), let $B'_R$ be another sufficient boundary datum. By the stated coarsest hypothesis, there is a classical stochastic map or quantum channel $B'_R\to B_R$ preserving every exterior protocol distribution. Hence $B'_R$ factors through $B_R$ up to operational equivalence. PCE-minimality under strict coarsening is not used for this implication and, by itself, would not supply the factorization. ∎

<a id="corollary-f106c-predictive-shielding-without-surplus-boundary-labels"></a>**Corollary F.10.6c (Predictive Shielding Without Surplus Boundary Labels).** For the specified finite state and protocol class, Equations (F.10.6.1) and (F.10.6.2) are respectively classical and quantum Markov-shielding conditions. Boundary labels that alter no conditional exterior protocol distribution are response-null under PPI/PCE. These state-dependent shielding conditions do not by themselves imply algebraic microcausality or channel no-signaling.

*Proof.* Theorem F.10.6b gives the conditional-independence and recovery characterizations. The response quotient removes labels that change none of the stated protocol distributions. Algebraic commutation and no-signaling require their independent operator and channel hypotheses. ∎

<a id="corollary-f106d-markov-recovery-at-a-gauge-split-boundary-center"></a>**Corollary F.10.6d (Markov Recovery at a Gauge-Split Boundary Center).** On a finite quantum-algebra branch, assume $B_R=Z_{\partial R}$ is the common center of a locally complete finite gauge-split datum and exterior protocols are generated by $\mathfrak A_{\bar R}$. Then the following are equivalent:

1. the restricted state satisfies
$$
I(R:\bar R\mid Z_{\partial R})_\rho=0;
\tag{F.10.6.4}
$$

2. there exists a CPTP recovery channel such that
$$
\rho_{RZ_{\partial R}\bar R}
=
(\operatorname{id}_R\otimes\mathcal R_{Z_{\partial R}\to Z_{\partial R}\bar R})
(\rho_{RZ_{\partial R}}).
\tag{F.10.6.5}
$$

The gauge-split hypothesis independently gives the block decomposition (F.10.4d.1)–(F.10.4d.2). The center is PCE-minimal for this state and protocol class if and only if (F.10.6.4) holds and no strict coarsening of $Z_{\partial R}$ still satisfies it for every admissible exterior protocol.

If entropy is measured in nats and
$$
I(R:\bar R\mid Z_{\partial R})_\rho\le\epsilon,
\tag{F.10.6.6}
$$
then a recovery channel exists with
$$
\lVert\rho_{RZ_{\partial R}\bar R}-\widetilde\rho_{RZ_{\partial R}\bar R}\rVert_1
\le
2\sqrt{1-e^{-\epsilon}}
\le
2\sqrt\epsilon.
\tag{F.10.6.7}
$$
Every observable of norm at most one changes in expectation by at most this quantity.

*Proof.* The finite-dimensional equality condition for strong subadditivity, due to Hayden, Jozsa, Petz, and Winter (2004), gives the equivalence of (F.10.6.4) and (F.10.6.5). Theorem F.10.4d.2 gives the block decomposition from local completeness, independently of the state. By Definition F.10.6a, the center is PCE-minimal exactly when it is Markov and every strict coarsening fails the Markov condition for at least one admissible exterior protocol.

For (F.10.6.7), the Fawzi–Renner recoverability theorem gives a channel with fidelity
$$
F(\rho,\widetilde\rho)\ge e^{-\epsilon/2}.
$$
The Fuchs–van de Graaf inequality and $1-e^{-\epsilon}\le\epsilon$ give
$$
\|\rho-\widetilde\rho\|_1
\le
2\sqrt{1-F(\rho,\widetilde\rho)^2}
\le
2\sqrt{1-e^{-\epsilon}}
\le
2\sqrt\epsilon.
$$
Trace duality yields
$$
|\operatorname{Tr}E(\rho-\widetilde\rho)|
\le
\|E\|\,\|\rho-\widetilde\rho\|_1.
$$
∎

<a id="proposition-f106e-gauge-split-center-need-not-be-state-minimal"></a>**Proposition F.10.6e (Gauge-Split Center Need Not Be State-Minimal).** Let $\mathcal H_R$ and $\mathcal H_{\bar R}$ be nonzero finite Hilbert spaces and set
$$
\mathcal H_{\mathrm{phys}}
=
\bigoplus_{z=0}^1
\mathcal H_R\otimes\mathcal H_{\bar R},
$$
$$
\mathfrak A_R
=
\bigoplus_{z=0}^1
B(\mathcal H_R)\otimes I,
\qquad
\mathfrak A_{\bar R}
=
\bigoplus_{z=0}^1
I\otimes B(\mathcal H_{\bar R}).
\tag{F.10.6.8}
$$
This is a locally complete finite gauge-split datum with common center $Z\cong\mathbb C^2$. Under the equal-block identification choose the state
$$
\rho_{RZ\bar R}
=\rho_R\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|_Z\otimes\rho_{\bar R}.
\tag{F.10.6.9}
$$
No faithfulness assumption is imposed. Retain every protocol generated by the two displayed local algebras, including protocols reading the center. The label is nevertheless deterministically zero on this state. In the complete local-record realization of Definition F.10.6a,
$$
I(R:\bar R\mid Z)_\rho=0,\qquad
I(R:\bar R)_\rho=0.
\tag{F.10.6.10}
$$
Consequently the registered two-label boundary and its coarsening $Z\to *$ are both sufficient. If the structural cost is the logarithm of the registered alphabet cardinality, including unused labels, the coarsening reduces that cost from $\ln2$ to $0$. The Shannon entropy of $Z$ is already zero and is not the cost used here.

*Proof.* On each block the algebras in (F.10.6.8) are mutual commutants generating the full block algebra. Their common center remains $\mathbb C^2$ regardless of the state. Only block zero has positive state weight. Every retained local observable therefore acts, for purposes of this state, through its block-zero component. The two components see the product state $\rho_R\otimes\rho_{\bar R}$, and every local copy of the readable central label is the constant zero. Thus both unconditional and boundary-conditioned local records are independent. Replacing the boundary register by a singleton preserves every retained protocol distribution and its shielding property. The strict structural-cost inequality follows from the two registered alphabet sizes. Hence local gauge splitting and Markov sufficiency do not force state-dependent minimality of the common center. ∎

<a id="proposition-f106f-pce-minimal-sufficient-boundaries-need-not-be-unique"></a>**Proposition F.10.6f (PCE-Minimal Sufficient Boundaries Need Not Be Unique).** On the classical finite branch of Definition F.10.6a, let $X_R,E_{\bar R}\in\{0,1\}$ and let the registered boundary $B_R\in\{1,2,3\}$ have the joint law
$$
\Pr(X_R,B_R,E_{\bar R})=\tfrac13\bigl(\delta_{(0,1,0)}+\delta_{(0,2,1)}+\delta_{(1,3,1)}\bigr),
\tag{F.10.6.11}
$$
with the complete interior and exterior readouts $X_R$ and $E_{\bar R}$ as the retained protocol class. Label the five deterministic coarsenings $B'$ of $B_R$ by the partitions of $\{1,2,3\}$. Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
&I(X_R:E_{\bar R}\mid B')=0
\quad\text{for }\{1\}\{2\}\{3\},\ \{1,2\}\{3\},\ \{1\}\{2,3\},\\
&I(X_R:E_{\bar R}\mid B')=\tfrac23\log2
\quad\text{for }\{1,3\}\{2\},
\qquad
I(X_R:E_{\bar R})=\log3-\tfrac43\log2 .
\end{aligned}
\tag{F.10.6.12}
$$
Hence $\{1,2\}\{3\}$ and $\{1\}\{2,3\}$ are both sufficient and PCE-minimal under coarsening, neither is a coarsening of the other, and their only common coarsening is not sufficient. The coarsening family of $B_R$, ordered by coarsening, therefore has no coarsest sufficient member. Both minimal boundaries have alphabet cardinality $2$, block probabilities $(\tfrac23,\tfrac13)$ and Shannon entropy $\log3-\tfrac23\log2$, so neither the registered-alphabet cost nor the boundary entropy selects one of them. The diagonal density matrix of (F.10.6.11) on tensor factors $\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^3\otimes\mathbb C^2$, with coarsenings applied as classical relabeling channels on the middle factor, gives the same values of (F.10.6.2).

*Proof.* On each boundary value the pair $(X_R,E_{\bar R})$ is deterministic, so the finest boundary is sufficient. Given $B_R\in\{1,2\}$, $X_R=0$ is constant, and given $B_R\in\{2,3\}$, $E_{\bar R}=1$ is constant. A constant variable is independent of every variable, so both two-block coarsenings satisfy the conditional independence that Theorem F.10.6b(1) identifies with (F.10.6.1). Given $B_R\in\{1,3\}$, an event of probability $\tfrac23$, the pair is $(0,0)$ or $(1,1)$ with probability $\tfrac12$ each, which gives $\tfrac23\log2>0$. Without conditioning, $\Pr(X_R=1,E_{\bar R}=0)=0$ while $\Pr(X_R=1)\Pr(E_{\bar R}=0)=\tfrac19$, and direct evaluation gives $\log3-\tfrac43\log2>0$. These are all five partitions of a three-element set. The only strict coarsening of either two-block partition is the one-block partition, which fails, so both are PCE-minimal. They are distinct partitions with the same number of blocks, hence incomparable, and every common coarsening of them is the one-block partition. The block probabilities follow from (F.10.6.11). For the diagonal density matrix, every reduced state after a classical relabeling channel is diagonal in a product basis, so each quantum conditional mutual information equals the corresponding classical value. ∎

<a id="theorem-f106g-finite-boundary-selection-exact-refinement-and-spatial-clustering"></a>**Theorem F.10.6g (Finite Boundary Selection, Exact Refinement and Spatial Clustering).**

#### 1. Registered finite selector

Data: a registered ordered finite boundary alphabet $B=\{1,\dots,m\}$, finite complete interior/exterior records $X,E$ and a rational joint law $P(x,b,e)$. Restrict candidates to deterministic coarsenings of this given $B$, as in Proposition F.10.6f.

For a partition $\Pi$, for every block $C\in\Pi$ put $M_{C}(x,e)=\sum_{b\in C}P(x,b,e)$ and $p_{C}=\sum_{x,e}M_{C}(x,e)$. Ignore blocks of zero probability. $\Pi$ is sufficient if and only if every nonzero $M_{C}$ has rank one, equivalently every $2\times 2$ minor vanishes.

Proof. Conditional independence on $C$ is $M_{C}(x,e)/p_{C}=[\sum_{e'}M_{C}(x,e')/p_{C}][\sum_{x'}M_{C}(x',e)/p_{C}]$. A nonnegative nonzero rank-one matrix factors and, after summing, has exactly this normalized outer-product form. The converse is immediate. The minor condition is the standard finite rank-one criterion, valid also with zero rows or columns. ∎

Algorithm: enumerate the Bell-number-many partitions, test those rational equalities, retain the sufficient ones, minimize their number of blocks, then break ties lexicographically by the restricted-growth string in the registered label order. If the registered boundary is sufficient, at least one candidate survives. The output is sufficient and PCE-minimal under strict coarsening: every strict coarsening has fewer blocks and therefore cannot be sufficient. The final tie-break makes the output single-valued.

This is a fully finite exact selection procedure, not an assumption that a coarsest boundary exists. The three-label witness of Proposition F.10.6f has two equal-cost minima; the registered ordering selects the lexicographically smaller string 001, i.e. {1,2}{3}. A relabeling can change the tie-break, so label order is explicit added branch data. Nor is arbitrary refinement compatibility inferred from this rule. In the constructed family below, compatibility is proved independently because there is only one nontrivial two-label partition.

#### 2. Exactly projectively compatible refining Markov carriers

Fix $\kappa>0$, with units inverse length. At ordered spatial positions $x_{0}<\dots<x_{m}$ define a stationary spin law $S_{x}\in\{-1,+1\}$ with $\pi=(1/2,1/2)$ and transition matrix

$$
P_d(s,t)=(1+st\, e^{-\kappa d})/2,\qquad d\ge 0.
$$

The finite law is $\pi(s_{0})\prod_{j=1}^{m}P_{x_{j}-x_{j-1}}(s_{j-1},s_{j})$. Each law at distinct positions is strictly positive. Since $P_{d}=\Pi+e^{-\kappa d}(I-\Pi)$, where $\Pi$ has both rows $\pi$, multiplication gives $P_{d}P_{e}=P_{d+e}$. Hence summing over inserted grid points gives exactly the coarse law.

Use nested dyadic carriers $\Lambda_{n}=2^{-n}\mathbb{Z}\cap[-L_{n},L_{n}]$, with integer $L_{n}$ increasing and $0$ included. Their diagonal density matrices are exactly compatible under partial traces. Both their point counts and their represented spatial extent can grow. For any fixed finite subset, the law is unchanged at all refinements containing it. A direct common realization exists: a fair initial spin followed in either direction by Poisson flips at rate $\kappa/2$; the probability generating function $\mathbb{E}(-1)^{N_{d}}=e^{-\kappa d}$ gives the stated transition. Only these explicitly computed finite laws are needed below.

Take the registered cut boundary $B=S_{0}$, any retained interior record $X$ at finitely many negative positions and any exterior record $E$ at finitely many positive positions. The finite product law factors as

$$
P(X,B,E)=P(B)P(X|B)P(E|B).
$$

Thus $I(X:E|B)=0$ at every $n$. The recovery channel retains/copies the classical $B$ and samples the full exterior conditional law $P(E|B)$. As a quantum channel it first reads $B$ in its registered basis and prepares $|b\rangle\langle b|_{B}\otimes\rho_{E|b}$. This is explicit CPTP, and

$$
\rho_{XBE}=(\mathrm{id}_X\otimes R_{B\to BE})(\rho_{XB})
$$

holds exactly for the entire retained record, not only a selected observable.

The conditional kernels also commute with refinement: summing over newly inserted exterior points uses $P_{d}P_{e}=P_{d+e}$. Therefore the recovery defect and comparison-map defect are identically zero on all refining carriers.

#### 3. Selected boundary minimality and compatibility

Suppose $X$ includes $S_{-a}$ and $E$ includes $S_{b}$, with $a,b>0$. Their connected spin correlation is $e^{-\kappa(a+b)}>0$. Hence deleting $B$ makes these complete records dependent, so the one-block boundary is not sufficient. The binary $B$ has only its identity and one-block coarsenings. The identity is therefore the unique sufficient minimal partition; the selection rule of section 1 returns it.

Its labels and probability law are the same on every carrier, and all coarse/fine maps preserve $S_{0}$. Thus the selected minimal boundary commutes with refinement in this branch. No universal selection uniqueness or covariance under unregistered label changes is asserted.

The finite partition enumerator in Section 1 is restricted to rational input laws. Here the same selection criterion is decided analytically from the explicit binary law and its strictly positive correlation; no exact-equality decision procedure for arbitrary real input probabilities is asserted.

#### 4. Sharp dimension-independent decoupling and spatial clustering

Let $X$ be any finite record at positions $\le a$ and $E$ any finite record at positions $\ge b$, $b>a$, both available on a refining carrier. Then

$$
\begin{gathered}
\lVert\rho_{XE}-\rho_{X}\otimes\rho_{E}\rVert_{1}\le e^{-\kappa(b-a)}, \\
\lvert\operatorname{Cov}(A(X),B(E))\rvert\le e^{-\kappa(b-a)}\lVert A\rVert\lVert B\rVert.
\end{gathered}
$$

The same inequalities hold after arbitrary local classical or quantum channels on the two records. Constants depend on physical separation, not lattice spacing, record sizes or Hilbert-space dimensions.

Proof. Add the endpoint variables $S_{a},S_{b}$ if necessary; consistency permits this without changing the retained marginals. The joint endpoint law is

$$
P(S_a=s,S_b=t)=(1+st\, e^{-\kappa(b-a)})/4.
$$

Its product marginal is $1/4$, so its ordinary $L^1$ difference is precisely $e^{-\kappa(b-a)}$. By the Markov property, the complete left and right records are obtained by a product of conditional sampling channels from $S_{a}$ and $S_{b}$. Applying this product channel to the joint endpoint law gives $P(X,E)$, and applying it to the product law gives $P(X)P(E)$. $L^1$/trace-norm contractivity proves the first inequality. Pairing its difference with $A\otimes B$ proves the second; further local channels preserve the estimate by the same contractivity. Taking $A=S_{a}$ and $B=S_{b}$ attains the correlation bound, so its coefficient and exponent are sharp. ∎

This supplies a separation-dependent decoupling estimate. At physical separation $d$, one can take $\varepsilon(d)=e^{-\kappa d}$ at every regulator. Refinement does not itself force decorrelation at fixed $d$; increasing $d$ does, as a spatial cluster property should require.

Perturbation stability. If a carrier state $\rho_{n}$ is within ordinary trace norm $\delta_{n}$ of the displayed compatible state $\sigma_{n}$ on the complete relevant record, the same registered recovery satisfies

$$
\begin{gathered}
\lVert\rho_{n}-R(\rho_{n,XB})\rVert_{1}\le 2\delta_{n}, \\
\lVert\rho_{n,XE}-\rho_{n,X}\otimes\rho_{n,E}\rVert_{1}\le e^{-\kappa d}+3\delta_{n}.
\end{gathered}
$$

The first follows by inserting $\sigma_{n}=R(\sigma_{n,XB})$ and using contractivity. For the second insert $\sigma_{n,XE}$ and $\sigma_{n,X}\otimes\sigma_{n,E}$; joint-state difference costs $\delta_{n}$ and product-marginal difference costs at most $2\delta_{n}$. These errors are dimension-independent. If $\delta_{n}\to 0$ uniformly on the retained region/record family, exact limiting recovery and the same clustering bound follow. A pointwise error on a smaller record is not silently promoted to that uniform family.

#### 5. Why exact recovery alone does not imply clustering: a faithful countermodel

Fix $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. Let $Z$ be a fair $\pm 1$ boundary bit and, conditional on $Z$, set $X_{i}=Z N_{i}$ at arbitrarily separated labeled spatial sites $i$, where $N_{i}$ are independent spins with $P(N_{i}=-1)=\varepsilon$. Every finite joint law of $(Z,X_{1},\dots,X_{m})$ is strictly positive, hence its diagonal density matrix is faithful. All finite laws are exactly consistent when sites are added.

For any disjoint finite interior and exterior groups, conditioning on $B=Z$ makes them independent. Recovery is exact by copying $Z$ and sampling independent conditional exterior spins. If both groups are nonempty, deleting $B$ fails sufficiency because

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E} X_i&=0, \\
\mathbb{E} X_i X_j&=(1-2\varepsilon)^{2}>0,\qquad i\ne j.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus this binary boundary is also selected minimally by the rule above. Nevertheless its connected correlation is constant at arbitrarily large assigned separation. Measuring one exterior spin gives an explicit detector of the interior spin: $P(X_{j}=X_{i})=[1+(1-2\varepsilon)^{2}]/2>1/2$. No sequence $\eta(d)\to 0$ can bound these correlations uniformly.

Proof. Conditional independence and strict positivity follow directly from $0<\varepsilon<1$. Independent conditional noises give $\mathbb{E}(X_{i}X_{j}|Z)=(1-2\varepsilon)^{2}Z^{2}$. Averaging yields the formulas, proving nonclustering and minimality. ∎

This countermodel establishes nonentailment of spatial clustering from faithfulness, exact Markov sufficiency, exact recovery, consistency and minimal boundary selection alone. Its registered boundary is a shared global label; no geometric localization of that label has been proved. The countermodel makes no geometric localization assumption on that label and does not refute the geometrically specified Markov-chain branch. The exterior detector is **unconditioned**; conditioning on the retained B removes its extra predictive information, exactly as the Definition F.10.6a screening condition requires. Confusing these two detector notions would be an invalid contradiction.

<a id="definition-f106h-incremental-local-record-markov-source"></a>**Definition F.10.6h (Incremental Local-Record Markov Source).** Fix the unchanged P17 ready cell, constructor and task of Theorem C.6c.P17a, and the finite pure-register, local-unitary, projective-record and descriptor-timed edge services and positive tariff of Definition C.6c.4a. The compiler below has its own specified field/terminal-probe interface, separate from the heat-only endpoint decoder. Its length and time units are fixed positive numbers $\ell_*,\tau_*$. Put
$$
a_n=2^{-n},\quad \delta_n=\ell_*a_n,\quad
\eta_n=\tau_*a_n,\quad L_n=n+1,\quad
V_n=a_n\mathbb Z\cap[-L_n,L_n],\qquad
\kappa=\frac{\log2}{\ell_*}.
\tag{F.10.6h.1}
$$
The actual location of $x\in V_n$ is $\ell_*x$. At the completed stage $n$, the only callable communication lanes join nearest neighbors in $V_n$. Their descriptors are $\pm1$. Every earlier lane is retained, held and charged as a dormant owned factor, with no callable input-dependent service. The decoder checks the current stage and edge list before admitting a call. The source-independent schedule and its current-stage access record are explicit; an old preparation record is not an authorization to use its historical edge.

Each location first receives one occurrence of the unchanged 75-bit P17 ready cell. Its exposed $w_x$ is the quantum source/probe factor. Its other 74 factors retain their original core supports. Each site additionally has an explicitly owned persistent classical field bit $S_x\in\{-1,+1\}$ and fresh source/control/record/communication factors allocated by the following finite expansion. $S_x$ is a live nondestructive field port, not an isolated archive. All archival copies have no feedback port. Old core, $w$, field and archive factors are retained when later stages append factors. A previously measured field bit can control a fresh copy; an archived old sampler outcome is never reopened for feedback.

For physical separation $d\ge0$, write
$$
P_d(s,t)=\frac{1+st\,e^{-\kappa d}}2.
\tag{F.10.6h.2}
$$
At the dyadic lengths used here, $e^{-\kappa\ell_*2^{-r}}=2^{-2^{-r}}$ is a positive algebraic number with its specified isolating interval and power equation. All sampler probabilities and square-root amplitudes below therefore have finite exact algebraic descriptions and normalization certificates.

The source is incrementally requested one stage at a time, with public requests $0,1,\ldots$. Before a stage consumes any new private source bit, its compiler emits that stage's finite schedule, coefficient descriptions and complete support/ownership list into fresh owned factors. It never stores a later final-stage choice in an earlier source factor. A finite instance is a prefix ending at any completed stage; its continuation is the next supplied public request. The prepared state $\rho_n$ is the unconditional state at fixed $n$, with a source-independent continuation/stopping schedule. A stopping or stage-selection rule based on private outcomes is a separately retained intervention and conditional state, not one of these $\rho_n$. The fixed compiler program and every earlier stage descriptor remain unchanged. Local outcome controls occupy the same slots on every branch. Code production is source-independent but paid, rather than inferred to be free.

1. **Root and integer skeleton.** At stage zero, prepare a fresh fair field bit $S_0$ by a Hadamard and local projective record service. Create $S_{1}$ and $S_{-1}$, conditionally independently given $S_0$, with transition $P_{\ell_*}$. At each later stage, extend the already created integer skeleton outward from both existing ends to $\pm L_n$, one unit interval at a time, with the same transition. The parent spin is copied along the currently callable nearest-neighbor path inside that unit interval into fresh local controls. At the new integer endpoint prepare and measure the new bit with the given conditional row. No cumulative source history, seed list or root label is sent. Copies and the old and new bit values remain locally recorded on that interval.
2. **Dyadic bridges.** Once the stage's integer skeleton exists, insert all missing dyadic sites, in increasing level and then coordinate order. For an interval $[u,v]$ with its two endpoint spins already available and midpoint $z=(u+v)/2$, prepare and measure $S_z$ with
$$
K_{u,z,v}(r\mid s,t)
=\frac{P_{\ell_*(z-u)}(s,r)P_{\ell_*(v-z)}(r,t)}
       {P_{\ell_*(v-u)}(s,t)}.
\tag{F.10.6h.3}
$$
All denominators are positive. The controls from $u$ and $v$ are carried separately to $z$ by CNOT copies into fresh factors on their respective current nearest-neighbor subpaths; neither control passes the other endpoint. The sampler is a block-controlled two-dimensional real unitary with first column $(\sqrt{K(-1\mid s,t)},\sqrt{K(+1\mid s,t)})$, followed by the local projective record service. Its second column is the normalized orthogonal column. The conditional sampler target and its measured outcome are retained. Additional flip labels, if requested, are the locally computed XOR of the endpoint/target labels, not unrecorded uniform random variables. No independent hidden uniform, rejection loop or unretained success branch is used.
3. **Local qualifying injection.** Once $S_x$ has first been created, execute the original P17 task once at that site with four fresh fair bits $A_{x,1},B_{x,1},A_{x,2},B_{x,2}$. These quadruples are mutually independent over sites and independent of the field samplers. Let $F_{x,j}=A_{x,j}\land B_{x,j}$ and deliver $X_{x,1}=F_{x,1}$, then $X_{x,2}=F_{x,1}\mathbin{\mathrm{XOR}}F_{x,2}$ in the original temporal order. Keep every original P17 gate duration. After freezing the second forecast and before consuming the second source pair, apply $X^{F_{x,1}}$ and then $H^{b_x}$ to the actual exposed $w_x$, where $b_x=(1+S_x)/2$ for $x\ne0$, and $b_0=1$. After consuming the second pair, apply $Z^{F_{x,2}}$. The live local source buffers provide these controls; they are archived only afterwards. The terminal $w_x$ state is
$$
\psi_x(S_x,\lambda_x)
=Z^{F_{x,2}}H^{b_x}X^{F_{x,1}}|0\rangle,
\qquad \lambda_x=(A_{x,1},B_{x,1},A_{x,2},B_{x,2}).
\tag{F.10.6h.4}
$$
The root's quantum injection is deliberately independent of $S_0$. There is no common qualification flag. All forecasts, supplied outcomes, discrepancies, model updates, injection controls and source bits remain at that site's original supports.
4. **Incremental inventory.** Stage $n+1$ allocates fresh hosts at new sites, fresh current-edge lanes and a fresh clock/controller. It appends the record retiring the old edge-access list, without erasing its historical list or using it for feedback. All historical quantum/state and source records remain. Previous clocks freeze at their completed values. The new stage never overwrites an old invoice: it appends its new interval/occurrence ledger and the recomposed cumulative ledger, with their actual distinct timestamps. Every old factor's further holding time is charged over the new interval. No reset or cyclic reuse is assumed.

All field controls in this expansion are already diagonal when copied. Local unitaries and classical Boolean circuits are finite supported matrices from the admitted alphabet; the two-dimensional sampler has the displayed algebraic unitarity certificate. Route copies use the actual current lanes, not a nonlocal gate assigned to the whole parent interval. Each call on a stage-$n$ lane occupies its actual duration $\eta_n$ and implements its gate in the first half, with the completion flag at its endpoint. Local calls, core calls, source measurements and clock updates have their separate positive declared durations. The compiler serializes calls if supports or durations require it; it never compresses the unchanged P17 core into $\eta_n$. A new finite clock is allocated for each stage, and two listed clock X pulses advance each one-hot instruction position. For a stage-$n$ edge call they occupy the second half of its reserved interval, each for $\eta_n/4$, after the first-half gate; their actual supported generators are charged. Factory preparation, descriptor generation, waveform/clock distribution, initialization and synchronization precede the nominated stage and have their own finite resource entries.

**Complete retained regional algebra and interface.** At a completed stage, assign every carrier, local control, live field, clock and archive factor to its actual named location; an edge lane has its two local endpoint factors and a deterministic owned reservation record. Let $\mathcal H_{n,x}$ be the tensor product of the P17 carrier and all auxiliary factors actually present at $x$. Define
$$
\mathcal A_n(U)=\bigotimes_{x\in V_n:\,\ell_*x\in U} B(\mathcal H_{n,x})
\tag{F.10.6h.5}
$$
for the retained spatial regions $U$. All full-carrier matrix factors, including the source/qualification/clock records, are included in this algebra. They are not projected to the scalar spin algebra or removed because they are classical on the prepared state. Static factory/compiler descriptions and global scalar tariff summaries are deterministic records; their copies can be assigned to the root without introducing a random common factor. No input-dependent energy aggregate, private outcome count or random activation-cost summary is collected or broadcast as part of the prepared source; an additional measurement/collection of that kind would be a different paid intervention and a different tested state. Raw input-dependent records remain where the construction put them. Collecting them at a different site is a separately paid protocol, not the definition of a regional restriction.

The state interface retains the entire preparation output and finite terminal local instruments, including the actual $X$- and $Z$-basis measurements of $w_x$, with their complete local output records. Finite algebraic local unitary/instrument descriptions use the admitted supported matrix services and fresh factors. Tensor products of local matrix-unit/Pauli tests determine the full regional density matrix; their linear bounded extension determines its value on all of (F.10.6h.5). No numerical oracle for a noncomputable matrix is supplied. A finite local protocol may adapt to its own outcomes and retain an arbitrary local reference initially independent across the two tested regions. No data-dependent instruction crosses their separation in a test of the prepared state's cluster property. Paid communication is a separately registered intervention, with its full changed state and records.

For the boundary test use the negative and positive sites as the two regions and the full tensor factor at $0$ as the registered physical boundary. On its support, the complete classical boundary alphabet is precisely $(S_0,\lambda_0)$ with deterministic duplicates and deterministic controller fields. The remaining root quantum factor is the state in (F.10.6h.4), depending only on $\lambda_0$. The boundary candidate family consists of deterministic statistics $C=\pi(S_0,\lambda_0)$ of this complete classical alphabet, with all interior and exterior records unchanged. Each candidate supplies **only $C$** as its conditioning datum: its comparison channel measures the classical root label, relabels it by $\pi$ and traces the other root factors in that candidate response. It does not additionally supply an uncoarsened root quantum register or private label as side information. This is the registered deterministic-statistic selector of Theorem F.10.6g; optimization over arbitrary quantum boundary channels is outside the candidate family. The comparison leaves the original physical root factors owned and present in the full source and regional algebra; it does not erase them from the clustering theorem. The minimum-alphabet selector of Theorem F.10.6g is applied using the exact algebraic rank-one test; its finite arithmetic extension to algebraic probabilities uses sign/equality tests for the displayed algebraic numbers. The selected sufficient datum is realized by an actual live copy of $S_0$. The original physical root records are retained in the source even when testing a coarsened boundary statistic.

<a id="theorem-f106i-full-record-refinement-root-cut-minimal-boundary-and-trace-norm-clustering"></a>**Theorem F.10.6i (Full-Record Refinement, Root-Cut Minimal Boundary and Trace-Norm Clustering).** The source of Definition F.10.6h is nonempty at every finite stage and has the following properties.

1. Every site is an occurrence of the unchanged qualifying minimum P17 module executing its actual local forecast/verification/update task and controlling its actual quantum injection. The ready-module original complexity is $C_P=C_{op}=1$. The enlarged source has its own finite literal constructor and resource inventory; its size and later microstates are not assigned that value.
2. The complete source states $\rho_n$, not just their spin marginals, obey exact partial-trace consistency. The embeddings of all old regional matrix algebras are the unital isometric maps $A\mapsto A\otimes I$. They preserve products, inclusions and common locations exactly. Every old record, original timestamp and historical ledger remains a factor of the finer state.
3. At the registered cut through the root site $0$, the selected boundary is exactly $S_0$ up to a relabeling. It is the unique coarsest sufficient partition of the registered supported boundary alphabet and has two labels. Its full-record quantum recovery defect is zero at every stage. The state-specific recovery maps commute with the source restrictions on their complete registered source-state domain, including independent local reference extensions and separate interior/exterior instruments, with the selected classical boundary retained and all output records included.
4. For any finite left/right regional sets $U\subset(-\infty,a]$, $W\subset[b,\infty)$ with physical separation $d=b-a>0$, their complete reduced density matrices satisfy, uniformly in stage and record dimensions,
$$
\|\rho_{n,UW}-\rho_{n,U}\otimes\rho_{n,W}\|_1
\le g(d),\qquad
 g(d)=\begin{cases}
 2,&0<d\le2\ell_*,\\
 e^{-\kappa(d-2\ell_*)},&d>2\ell_*.
 \end{cases}
\tag{F.10.6i.1}
$$
In particular $g(d)\le 2e^{2\kappa\ell_*}e^{-\kappa d}=8e^{-\kappa d}$. For every pair of bounded, possibly noncommuting-within-region observables,
$$
|\rho_n(AB)-\rho_n(A)\rho_n(B)|
\le g(d)\|A\|\|B\|.
\tag{F.10.6i.2}
$$
The same estimate holds for the entire outputs of separate local CPTP instruments on the two regions, including all their records. If an implemented carrier state differs from the complete stated source state by trace norm at most $\epsilon_n$, the same source recovery has defect at most $2\epsilon_n$ and the connected-state bound becomes $g(d)+3\epsilon_n$, by the insertion-and-contractivity argument of Theorem F.10.6g. This perturbation premise concerns the entire retained regional record, not a smaller scalar marginal; the declared ideal source has $\epsilon_n=0$. Beyond the stated regional restriction, these estimates omit no factor belonging to the tested regional algebras: every local qualification, sampler, control and historical source record is retained.

*Proof.* The transition identity $P_dP_e=P_{d+e}$ makes (F.10.6h.3) normalized. Rooted integer growth gives the stationary two-sided Markov law; conditional bridge insertion refines it to the unique law with transition (F.10.6h.2) on the added dyadic positions. Consequently the spin marginal at every stage is exactly that of Theorem F.10.6g, and no sampler success event or hidden normalization is used.

The P17 source quadruples are independent over sites and independent of the field. The original core gives $m=f_1=X_1$ and the pre-outcome forecast $(1+2X_1)/4$. Its Brier risk is $3/16$, the matched fair risk is $1/4$, and the gain $1/16$ exceeds the unchanged margin $1/32$. The original supported model-write, second-forecast-write and verification-ingress null replacements give risk $1/4$. The added $w$ pulses act on the exposed factor and use live source controls nondestructively, so do not change those calculations or the actual predictive loop. The first and second private local flags now also control the displayed physical quantum injection. The old ready descriptor, prefix machine, empty-program exclusion and literal constructor are precisely those of Theorem C.6c.P17a. Thus its attained ready-cell minimum is unchanged. This proves item 1 without a complexity assignment to the complete controller or enlarged graph.

At completed stages every field/source/control/qualification outcome register is diagonal. The only deliberately coherent terminal source factors are the local $w_x$ states in (F.10.6h.4); any unused pure ready factor is likewise locally specified. Conditional on the entire field configuration and all $\lambda_x$, every retained factor is a specified local state and all different factors form a tensor product. A sampler's measured source target equals its output spin. Its copied controls equal its endpoint spins, and any derived flip label is a function of these local labels. Thus there is no unaccounted conditional random seed. Clock, compiler and raw scheduling fields are deterministic. Every archived input-dependent field is the value of its emitted local Boolean circuit. This describes the complete final density matrix, not only the statistics of selected readouts.

In a refinement, the source only uses an old $S_x$ as a control in its already diagonal basis. All resulting targets, messages, sampler factors and their records are fresh. It leaves every old $w_x$, core, source archive, clock and invoice unchanged. A controlled quantum preparation followed by outcome recording can alter off-diagonal test inputs, but the actual old source state is diagonal on every control. Conditional trace preservation therefore leaves the full old source density matrix unchanged, even where it was classically correlated with old $w$ states or with the rest of the carrier. It follows exactly that $\operatorname{Tr}_{n+1\setminus n}\rho_{n+1}=\rho_n$. The algebra inclusions are literal tensor-factor inclusions, not inverses to this state-dependent preparation channel on arbitrary counterfactual inputs. Their coherence, regional isotony and multiplicativity are exact. Old dated resource records retain their old values; the new cumulative cost is a new factor and need not equal them. This proves item 2.

No generation interval crosses zero: zero is an integer endpoint at every dyadic level. Root controls sent in either direction depend only on $S_0$. A bridge's left and right controls meet at its interior midpoint and never deposit the opposite endpoint's value at zero. Thus conditional on $S_0=s$, every negative-site factor and every positive-site factor is generated independently, while the full root factor is obtained from $s$ and the independent local $\lambda_0$. In particular the full source state has the direct classical-block factorization
$$
\rho_{n,-B+}
=\frac12\sum_{s=\pm1}
 \rho_{n,-\mid s}\otimes |s\rangle\langle s|_{B_s}
 \otimes\xi_{n,B'\mid s}\otimes\rho_{n,+\mid s},
\tag{F.10.6i.3}
$$
where $B_s$ is one physical retained field copy and $B'$ includes every other root factor. The apparent $s$-dependence of $\xi$ consists only of redundant copies of $s$; its private $\lambda_0$ and quantum injection are independent of $s$. A CPTP recovery reads the classical $B_s$ nondestructively on this state, keeps all existing root factors, and prepares the complete conditional positive carrier $\rho_{n,+\mid s}$. Formula (F.10.6i.3) gives exact equality with the source state after this channel, and hence zero conditional mutual information for the full independent tensor-factor realization. If only the selected statistic is supplied, the same recovery additionally prepares $B'$ by its explicitly supplied conditional kernel; the original source's $B'$ records are not physically erased to establish the equality.

For minimality, use the actual field reads at $-\ell_*$ and $+\ell_*$. Their conditional means given the complete root label $(s,\lambda_0)$ are both $s/2$. In a coarsened boundary block $C$,
$$
\operatorname{Cov}(S_{-1},S_1\mid C)
=\frac14\operatorname{Var}(S_0\mid C).
\tag{F.10.6i.4}
$$
Every supported label has positive weight. A block mixing the two $s$ values therefore fails the rank-one test. Conversely a partition determining $s$ is sufficient by (F.10.6i.3), since the root's other private labels and quantum state are independent of both sides given $s$. Every sufficient partition refines the binary $S_0$ partition. This proves its unique coarsest property and shows that the registered finite selector returns it. All refinements retain the same $S_0$, and their conditional source states have the same exact partial-trace restrictions. Recovery and restriction consequently commute on these source states. Separate interior/exterior instruments and initially independent local references are included by tensoring their channels and retaining their full outputs; the selected classical boundary is kept. An arbitrary channel erasing that boundary is instead a tested coarsening, not a recovery-preserving operation. This proves item 3 on its stated source-state domain; arbitrary counterfactual coherent field inputs are not substituted for that domain.

For item 4, associate to each output factor its actual source dependence set. The integer update and every later refinement use an interval of physical length at most $\ell_*$. Their source and relay records at $x$ depend only on field spins at distance at most $\ell_*$ from $\ell_*x$. A historical path at an earlier coarser stage has the same physical interval and the same bound. No control carries its sender's preceding history. The host's own coherent $w_x$ and qualification records depend only on $S_x$ and its independent $\lambda_x$. Deterministic allocation, tariff, compiler and clock data add no dependence set. Thus the complete output on $U$ is a CPTP classical-to-quantum decoration of the Markov field in $U^{+\ell_*}$, together with independent local source quadruples. The decoration explicitly includes all historical relay, seed, controller, qualification and quantum factors. Decorations on disjoint source sets have independent ancillary randomness; the source sampling description above supplies their conditional kernels rather than assuming unconditioned sampler coins remain independent after conditioning.

If $d>2\ell_*$, the two enlarged field sets are separated by $d-2\ell_*$. Theorem F.10.6g's full-record Markov estimate is $e^{-\kappa(d-2\ell_*)}$ for their joint-versus-product diagonal states, independently of their numbers of points. Applying the two product decoration channels and trace-norm contractivity gives (F.10.6i.1). The bound $2$ at smaller separation is the universal trace-norm bound for two normalized states. Trace duality gives (F.10.6i.2), and additional local CPTP instruments preserve it. This proves the estimate on the entire matrix algebra (F.10.6h.5), even though several of its factors happen to be diagonal in this state. The conditional states (F.10.6h.4) of different labels do not commute, but the labels $(S_x,\lambda_x)$ that determine them are retained in diagonal registers at the same site. The site-local unitary $V_x=\sum_{s,\lambda}|s,\lambda\rangle\langle s,\lambda|\otimes\bigl(Z^{F_{x,2}}H^{b_x}X^{F_{x,1}}\bigr)^*$, with $b_x$ and $F_{x,j}$ the functions of $(s,\lambda)$ of Definition F.10.6h, therefore maps $\rho_n$ to a state that is diagonal in a product basis, with every $w_x$ in $|0\rangle$. All regional density matrices of the source commute, and items 3 and 4 are the corresponding statements for the classical label law, carried through the local decoration channels. The retained $X/Z$ instruments are noncommuting measurements on this commuting-state source. ∎

<a id="theorem-f106j-paid-geometry-propagation-and-complete-source-comparison"></a>**Theorem F.10.6j (Paid Geometry, Propagation and Complete Source Comparison).** The same incremental source has the following paid link metric, propagation bound, cost-assignment rules and protocol comparison. At completed stage $n$, its chosen paid link-coordinate metric is
$$
d_n(x,y)=\delta_n\,\inf C_{\rm link}(x\leadsto y)
=\ell_*|x-y|.
\tag{F.10.6j.1}
$$
Its current nearest-neighbor graphs fill the real line with mesh $\delta_n$ and expanding domains. Its source-state/refinement, algebra, recovery and clustering statements are therefore uniform statements on these one-dimensional carriers. The cost vector $(E,I_0,B,I,G,J,C_{\rm link},K)$ of the source, the selector and the recovery service is fixed by the assignment rules below over all current and historical resources; its coordinates are not evaluated here, apart from the link charge in (F.10.6j.1) and the edge-call count of a lifted gate in (F.10.6j.2). No equality of the whole invoices at different stages is asserted.

*Proof.* A fresh unknown test qubit, with an arbitrary external reference, is loaded into a paid ready transport factor at $x$ after stage completion. The source permits a sequential path of unconditional qubit-SWAP edge services on current nearest-neighbor lanes, each with its actual duration $\eta_n$ and link charge one. The intermediate ready factors, local preparation, clock, final instrument and every outcome are allocated and charged. A path with $p$ edges transports the unknown qubit and reference exactly, with link charge $p$ and completed-edge latency $p\eta_n$.

Conversely, the only callable inter-site operations are the listed current-edge services. All prepared source factors are independent of the subsequently supplied unknown input, and all historical lanes and archives lack a callable propagation/feedback interface. Induction over the finite circuit's time-ordered ancestry shows that an input-dependent output at another site requires a chain of current-edge calls connecting it to $x$. Every such call has nonnegative additional costs and charges one in the selected coordinate. The minimum number is $|x-y|/a_n$. This proves the matching lower bound and (F.10.6j.1), with arbitrary auxiliary processing, correlated prepared field states and external payload references included. The link coordinate is the explicitly chosen representative of Definition 35, not the infimum of the sum of unrelated preparation and maintenance coordinates.

The completed-edge access convention requires successive calls along an influence path to respect their completion order. Their latency is at least $p\eta_n$, and the displayed SWAP path attains this edge-only bound. Thus its length/latency ratio is $\delta_n/\eta_n=\ell_*/\tau_*$; actual source preparation and terminal readout retain their separate durations. This is the declared endpoint-service cone; microscopic Hamiltonian tails and a relativistic continuum field are outside this statement. The unchanged P17 core durations are not used as transport-clock units.

The current edge's fixed timer law gives $q(1)=1$ for every $n$ and the same price $u_*\alpha_C$. The geometric mark $\delta_n$ in (F.10.6h.1) is the explicit microscopic-length calibration allowed by Definition 35; it does not multiply the tariff, the Hamiltonian, an operator spectrum or a physical clock. In particular the raw charge for a unit physical interval grows as $2^n$ and remains in the invoice. Old unit-charge coarse lanes are dormant, so cannot produce spurious shortcuts in the current metric. A coarse stage-$m$ transport between neighboring old locations is compared at stage $n\ge m$ with $2^{n-m}$ current-edge swaps. They have the same endpoint quantum channel and the same edge-only physical latency $\eta_m$, but their actual raw link charges and the additional supported factors differ and are retained explicitly.

For ownership, each cell's 75 factors belong to that cell occurrence. Its field, sampler, independent qualification source quadruple, coherent injection controls, ready communication targets, local clock and every copied/archive factor receive distinct typed owners at their actual sites. Each lane has its own allocation and a disjoint busy/idle partition. An old lane contributes only its charged dormant intervals after retirement. Lane intervals are excluded from the nonlane bit-time ledger. All setup/factory/code generation and its finite computational transcript, ROM loading, clock preparation/distribution, synchronization, positive-duration gate/read services, source controls, maintained old factors, future-ready stock actually allocated, retirement metadata and final collection actually requested are listed. No zero increment or cancellation against another compiler is used.

The finite emitted word determines the exact quantities $E,I_0,B,I,G,J,C_{\rm link},K$, the actual simultaneous piecewise-constant Hamiltonian $H(t)$, its peak norm and its norm integral. Evaluate the tariff of Definition C.6c.4a on that complete occurrence/interval inventory with its unchanged positive coefficients. Controlled calls reserve the same interval on every branch; the Hamiltonian is the actual controlled operator on its full allocated support. These costs therefore are deterministic source records, not random activation counts silently substituted for the controlled service. Local descriptions/certificates, classical arithmetic and their implementation have their separate paid entries. Where intervals overlap, the recorded norm is the norm of the actual sum of supported generators, not an asserted equality with the sum of their norms.

At a completed stage boundary the old ledger closes over its actual past time interval. Later holding of an old factor belongs to a new interval and owner entry. Additive cumulative coordinates are disjoint sums over these occurrences and intervals; the peak coordinate is the maximum over the union. Old dated invoice factors remain untouched, and the new cumulative invoice records that recomposition. Spatial owner restriction and reassembly are exact partitions of this finite inventory. Under these rules the additive coordinates are exact disjoint sums over occurrences and intervals, so no resource is counted twice, and all original-unit increases along refinement are retained.

The full source response has the explicit branch form used in Theorem F.10.6i: stationary spatial Markov spins, independent local quadruples, their deterministic complete recorded controls and the actual local quantum states (F.10.6h.4). The physical compiler implements each displayed conditional probability by its normalized finite instrument. Induction over its emitted word proves equality of every unnormalized branch state and hence of every finite joint outcome law, including arbitrary external references attached to permitted local or transport inputs. The same induction intertwines adaptive terminal choices with their identical retained local labels. Invalid matrix certificates, unsupported lanes and an archive-feedback request are rejected by the finite source decoder rather than treated as successful protocols. Every physical operation itself is a normalized channel on its full declared carrier; the prepared-state theorem does not rely on a successful-code postselection.

**Actual selector and recovery service.** The boundary selector is also a finite owned computation with its own priced resources. Its supported classical input alphabet has $2\cdot16$ labels $(s,\lambda_0)$; deterministic duplicate fields do not add labels. The algebraic complete side laws are finite explicit sums/products of (F.10.6h.2)–(F.10.6h.4). Classical source labels at each side are retained and determine its remaining conditional quantum state by a local channel. For the registered candidate channel whose output is only $C$, the classical rank-one tests therefore decide sufficiency for the complete interior/exterior quantum output as well: a failed classical test is an actual retained measurement witness, and a passing product law is carried to a product density matrix by the two local channels. Enumerating all partitions and exact algebraic equality tests terminates at each finite stage. More explicitly, its classical probabilities lie in $\mathbb Q(t_n)$ with $t_n=2^{1/2^n}$: clear the positive displayed denominators and reduce numerator polynomials modulo $t_n^{2^n}-2$. This polynomial is irreducible by Eisenstein at $2$ (and is linear for $n=0$), so a zero remainder is exactly equality. Its unique positive root fixes the ordering needed for the sampler certificates. A finite computation trace, its bit workspace, alphabet ordering, chosen partition and two-label boundary copy are compiled into the P17-supported Boolean/memory operations and charged by the same rules; the enumeration ranges over the $\mathrm{Bell}(32)\approx1.28\times10^{26}$ partitions of the alphabet. The analytic proof (F.10.6i.4) supplies the result uniformly without assigning that finite enumerator an unbounded runtime resource for free. The enumeration uses a supplied symbolic source law, not an input-dependent collection of distant private outcomes.

To implement the state-specific quantum recovery, keep the actual left/root carrier and copy the live classical $S_0$ into fresh boundary control. Allocate a fresh right-side response bank, with separately owned ready hosts, sampler/qualification sources, controls, tracks, clocks and archives. Run the conditional right-half integer/bridge compiler with this supplied root value and fresh independent local quadruples, including every earlier-stage logical right-side record. All source/sampler matrices are the same normalized algebraic matrices already supplied above; old coarse logical edge calls are implemented, when needed, by the admitted current-path compilation. Readonly archival copies are not used as inputs. The resulting designated response bank has exactly $\rho_{n,+\mid s}$, including every nominated historical source, quantum and record factor. The root's $B'$ is kept; if the input is only the selected statistic, a separately charged conditional local preparation supplies its stated $\xi_{n,B'\mid s}$.

The bank's historical timestamps and invoice values are explicitly **comparison-output** labels representing the nominated source factor, not claims that an old physical event occurred twice. The recovery implementation retains, in addition, its own actual start/completion times, fresh ownership, full primitive transcript and original-unit resource invoice. Their map to the nominated old source labels is part of the comparison, and the raw new records stay in a distinct physical fibre. Thus zero defect refers to the source-state channel on its displayed designated factors. The total physical recovery apparatus invoice differs from the source invoice, and arbitrary unknown discarded references are outside the recovery statement. The full response of this implementation is the designated recovery state together with that explicitly computed apparatus fibre. Its clocks, coefficient production, controls and all holding/collection intervals are charged by the same inventory rule.

**Full retained-protocol refinement.** A source snapshot inclusion is not used as a substitute for this additional map. Let $m\le n$, and let $\mathcal P$ be any finite admitted stage-$m$ terminal protocol, specified by its finite adaptive tree of local supported matrix instruments, current-edge CNOT/locally controlled SWAP calls, source-independent clock operations and fresh allocation/record commands. It may act on arbitrary old quantum factors; it is not restricted to the diagonal field. Its source-independent finite scheduling skeleton and all conditional branches are supplied before private outcomes. Fresh supports at old locations are assigned the same logical names on both sides.

A local old-site operation is the identical operation on its old factors tensored with the identity on all finer factors. Its new outcome register has the same logical output and location. An old neighboring pair $u,v$ is joined at level $n$ by the unique path $v_0=u,v_1,\ldots,v_k=v$, $k=2^{n-m}$. To realize an admitted two-port gate $G$ whose finite classical controls are local to $u$, move its remote selected qubit $b$ from $v_k$ to a dedicated qubit $t_1$ at $v_1$: apply the adjacent SWAPs in the order $(v_k,v_{k-1}),\ldots,(v_2,v_1)$ on its transport track. Apply $G$ to the original selected qubit/control factors at $u$ and this transported qubit at $v_1$. Undo the transport SWAPs in reverse order. When the control is local to $v$, reverse the orientation. For $k=1$ this is the original gate. All temporary track factors are explicitly allocated at the actual intermediate sites.

Writing the first transport permutation as $W$, the complete word is
$$
W^*\,G_{u,v_1}\,W
=G_{u,v}\otimes I_{\rm track}.
\tag{F.10.6j.2}
$$
The identity holds on the entire carrier, with arbitrary intermediate states and arbitrary external entanglement. It is conjugation by a tensor-factor permutation; a one-way SWAP path alone would not restore intermediate payloads. The word has exactly $2k-1$ paid edge calls. Its ancillary tracks are restored rather than measured, so no hidden data-dependent routing record is erased. Actual deterministic gate/clock/reservation records remain in the fine comparison fibre.

Local instrument channels and their individual unnormalized outcome branches therefore have exactly the old logical action tensored with the identity on the finer source factors. In the following display, $\mathcal P_\alpha$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal P}_\alpha$ denote those logical state/outcome branch channels; the actual newly executed physical clock, tariff and transcript outputs remain in their fully specified separate comparison fibres, so the equation is not an equality of whole physical invoice outputs. Induction over the finite tree, using the same logical outcome labels for every subsequent choice, gives the complete logical channel intertwiner
$$
\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm fine}\,\widetilde{\mathcal P}_{\alpha}(\omega)
=\mathcal P_{\alpha}(\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm fine}\omega)
\tag{F.10.6j.3}
$$
for every complete old logical instrument-outcome label $\alpha$, every input $\omega$ on the full old/fine carrier and every external quantum reference. The original logical output registers are included on both sides. The old physical gate timestamps and invoices are not included in $\alpha$ as if they were the new actual values: they are related by the explicit event-time and cost comparison below. No coarse timestamp is stamped onto a newly executed fine gate. Actual fine source, preparation, track, clock and tariff factors remain on the left and are explicitly described by the emitted word; the displayed partial trace is the registered old-response restriction, not their removal from the full physical state or from the cluster estimate. In particular, on $\rho_n$ this gives every old protocol's law on $\rho_m$. The entire unsimplified routed word, its additional factors and every resource entry are retained in the source comparison fibre.

A gate lifted by (F.10.6j.2) occupies $(2k-1)\eta_n$ of edge service, rather than the old $\eta_m=k\eta_n$; local preparation/readout and clock wrapper durations are added at their actual specified values. The two one-hot clock-update X pulses of an edge call can occupy its second half-slot, each of duration $\eta_n/4$, after the gate's first half-slot. Their supported generators, peak and action are charged. Local and P17 core pulses keep their original durations, with any additional external clock/read wrapper separately scheduled. These choices supply actual finite completion times; the general old/fine comparison is the explicit event-boundary time map of the two emitted words, not an unchanged-clock assertion. Branch lengths can be padded to the supplied finite skeleton with controlled inactive calls, whose lane reservations and holding time are charged. The special ready-payload one-way transport above has its separately stated shorter $k\eta_n=\eta_m$ edge latency.

The compiler records both words and their chronological correspondence, their entire separate vectors, and the difference on each newly allocated factor, gate and maintained interval. It never identifies their raw invoices. Composition of refinements is implemented by retaining the literal successive expansions and adding their actual fibres; the logical identities (F.10.6j.2)–(F.10.6j.3) compose exactly. A directly compiled shorter route can be compared by the same logical identity with a different explicitly retained cost/time fibre. Local half-line protocols lift along paths in that same half-line, so the full local-channel cluster estimate applies to their complete local outputs. A communicating protocol crossing the cut changes the tested state and is a different test from the uncommunicating boundary test.

Finally the exact inclusions and state restrictions of Theorem F.10.6i give an inductive quasi-local matrix algebra and a consistent state on its countable union. Each fixed bounded local observable extends by norm continuity, and the uniform inequalities (F.10.6i.1)–(F.10.6i.2) pass to that completion. The selected boundary and conditional recovery persist on every finite retained record and its compatible completion. The line metric has vanishing mesh and exact current paid-path calibration. A $3+1$ Lorentzian/AQFT promotion is a separate question and is not used in this one-dimensional realization of Theorem F.10.6g. ∎

<a id="proposition-f106k"></a>

<a id="proposition-f106k-exact-clustering-with-a-fixed-boundary-recovery-error"></a>**Proposition F.10.6k (Exact Clustering with a Fixed Boundary-Recovery Error).** On a finite chain of $N\ge3$ bits, take the uniform state on even total parity, represented as a diagonal density matrix $\rho$. Partition the sites into a left interval $A$, an intervening shell $M$ and a right interval $B$, all nonempty.
