Every proper marginal is the product fair-bit state, so every connected correlation between observables on disjoint supports with proper union vanishes. Nevertheless,
$$
I(A:B\mid M)_\rho=\log 2,\qquad
\inf_{\mathcal R:M\to AM}
\frac12\bigl\|\rho_{AMB}-(\mathcal R\otimes\operatorname{id}_B)(\rho_{MB})\bigr\|_1
=\frac12 ,
\tag{F.10.6k.1}
$$
where the infimum includes every CPTP recovery on the shell, with fresh auxiliaries independent of $B$. The same values hold for arbitrarily wide shells.

*Proof.* For each assignment to a proper subset $S$ of sites, exactly $2^{N-|S|-1}$ completions have even total parity. This proves the product law of every proper marginal and hence the correlation statement. The proper-marginal entropies are $S(\rho_{AM})=(|A|+|M|)\log 2$, $S(\rho_{MB})=(|M|+|B|)\log 2$, and $S(\rho_M)=|M|\log 2$, while $S(\rho_{AMB})=(N-1)\log 2$. Their alternating sum gives the conditional mutual information in (F.10.6k.1).

Since $\rho_{MB}=\rho_M\otimes\rho_B$, every recovered state has the form $\omega_{AM}\otimes\rho_B$. Total parity is even with probability $1/2$ in this product because the parity of the fair nonempty block $B$ is unbiased and independent of $AM$. In the target state the probability is one. This test gives the lower bound on half trace distance, including for quantum recovery maps. Appending independent fair bits on $A$ produces the fully uniform state, whose half trace distance from the even-parity state is $1/2$. This attains the bound. ∎

This finite state separates decay of connected correlations from recovery on the same boundary. Thermal or Hamiltonian source hypotheses for a recovering branch require a source-specific estimate.

<a id="theorem-f106l"></a>

<a id="theorem-f106l-a-noncommuting-refining-markov-source-with-evaluated-resource-costs"></a>**Theorem F.10.6l (A Noncommuting Refining Markov Source with Evaluated Resource Costs).** There is a refining one-dimensional P17 source on the locations $V_n$ and with the paid link calibration of Definition F.10.6h. Its regional density operators do not commute, even when compared with their product marginals. At the registered root cut it has a two-label sufficient boundary that is coarsest among finite quantum coarsenings of the physical root. Its exact source-state recovery and boundary selection commute with refinement. The state and its noncommunicating local protocol outputs cluster uniformly. The preparation, selector and recovery are finite physical words in the service alphabet of Definition C.6c.4a, with the tariff and Hamiltonian norms below.

*Proof.* **One source and its full record.** At each level $k\ge0$ supply the newly appearing locations of $V_k$, keeping all earlier hosts, controls, archives and retired lanes. Use the unchanged P17 cell, ready descriptor and qualification task of Theorem C.6c.P17a at each new location. A fair root qubit $S$ is prepared and dephased at level zero, with its basis outcome copied to a retained root record. Both factors are kept. Conditional on $S=b$, $b\in\{0,1\}$, use one signal at each of the two new sites $\pm2^{-k}$, with signal state $\phi_0=|0\rangle$ or $\phi_1=|+\rangle$. At level zero these are the sites $\pm1$. No other sites depend on $S$. Each signal is the exposed payload of its qualified cell. On a fresh neighboring local control first apply a link CNOT from $S$ and then a local controlled-H to the signal. Apply the same link CNOT again to restore the control to its ready zero. Both link calls have their fixed public reservations, and the restored physical control, links and command records remain owned. At the completed stage no classical copy of $S$ remains outside the root. For a coherent input this sequence is an ordinary controlled isometry; on the declared dephased root it implements exactly the two conditional preparations.

At all sites run the original P17 calibration independently. Its two frozen predictions precede the corresponding consumed source bits, and its risk $3/16$ beats the matched fair risk $1/4$ by more than $1/32$. Use separate source qubits, calculation factors and retained outcome records. Qualification never reads $S$ or any signal payload. All other apparatus factors are deterministic or local preparation factors from these independent calibrations. Put the clock, instruction table and local installation input for a deterministic command at the point that executes it. For a link gate use one endpoint. These local words are delivered as source-independent ready inputs. The fixed physical decoder addresses only the current lane bank, and the earlier descriptors and physical lane factors retain their earlier values. Assign every full matrix factor to its physical location, including all occupied and retired communication ports. Local instrument tests include the complete Pauli and matrix-unit dictionary on those factors. The source is incremental: only the new hosts and the two new conditional signals are added at a new level. The control operation reads the diagonal root and leaves its probability and all old conditional factors intact. Taking the partial trace over new factors therefore recovers exactly the old complete state, including both root labels, all earlier preparation histories and archives. Embeddings of regional observables are tensoring with the identity on added factors.

The complete state with left and right half-lines $L,R$ and the physical root factor $B$ has the form
$$
\rho_{LBR}=\frac12\sum_{b=0}^1
\lambda_b\otimes|b\rangle\langle b|_S\otimes\xi_b
                 \otimes\varrho_b .
\tag{F.10.6l.1}
$$
Here $\xi_b$ contains the rest of the root, including its retained copy of $b$, and $\lambda_b,\varrho_b$ include every left/right factor respectively. On each side their only $b$-dependent factors are the corresponding signal payloads. The complete left-right density is genuinely noncommuting on its matrix factors. On the first two signals, whose readouts are actual local ports, its restriction is $\sigma=(P_0\otimes P_0+P_1\otimes P_1)/2$, with $P_b=|\phi_b\rangle\langle\phi_b|$ and $p=(P_0+P_1)/2$. In the computational basis
$$
[\sigma,p\otimes p]_{00,01}=1/32,\qquad
[\sigma,p\otimes I]_{00,10}=1/16 .
\tag{F.10.6l.2}
$$
All remaining factors local to these two sites are independent of $b$. Hence the corresponding commutators on the complete two-site density operators are these nonzero operators tensored with nonzero positive factors. The second comparison uses the left site's density embedded into the two-site algebra. Unitary changes of the two local bases preserve noncommutation.

**Selector and recovery.** The root bit is sufficient by (F.10.6l.1), including after arbitrary separate finite local instruments. Let $\mathcal C$ be any CPTP coarsening from the complete root to a finite system $C$, and put $\gamma_b=\mathcal C(|b\rangle\langle b|_S\otimes\xi_b)$. If $C$ is sufficient on the same complete left and right factors, Theorem F.10.6b gives a channel $\mathcal R_{C\to CR}$ recovering the joint state from $LC$. The left matrices $\lambda_0,\lambda_1$ are linearly independent, since already their first signal marginals are $P_0\ne P_1$ and both have trace one. Applying the two dual linear functionals on their span to the recovery identity gives $\mathcal R(\gamma_b)=\gamma_b\otimes\varrho_b$ for both $b$. Write $f(\alpha,\beta)=\|\sqrt\alpha\sqrt\beta\|_1$ for root fidelity. Its monotonicity follows from the purification characterization of Uhlmann (1976) by an isometric dilation and restriction, and tensor multiplicativity follows from the singular values of a tensor product. Therefore
$$
f(\gamma_0,\gamma_1)\le
f(\gamma_0,\gamma_1) f(\varrho_0,\varrho_1).
$$
The right hand side factor $f(\varrho_0,\varrho_1)\le1/\sqrt2$ by restricting to the first right signal. Thus $f(\gamma_0,\gamma_1)=0$, the two supports are orthogonal, and a projective readout of $C$ returns $S$ exactly. Every sufficient coarsening therefore refines this two-label boundary in the sense of Theorem F.10.6b. Conversely any $C$ with orthogonal supports admits recovery by their nondestructive readout and the displayed conditional preparations. In particular a one-dimensional boundary fails. The selector proof identifies the minimum without a numerical search over candidate channels. Its physical circuit CNOT-copies the actual root bit to its allocated output and retains the rest of the source.

For recovery keep the supplied left and physical root state, use only $S$ as the control, and prepare a new designated right bank with the original right sites, P17 tasks and all required finite source factors. At historical level $k$ the original signal destination $2^{-k}$ is $2^{n-k}$ links away in the currently callable mesh at level $n$. Starting at the root, copy the diagonal control along that current path into fresh qubits, act on the new right signal by controlled-H, and undo the copies in reverse order. This uses $2\cdot2^{n-k}$ link CNOTs and one local pulse. Every historical signal and every right calibration has its own allocated factors. Each historical right endpoint's lane-port and ready bits and each restored control are reproduced as declared ready zeros on the designated bank. The historical right instruction, installation-input and completed-clock bits are prepared at their original locations from exact supplied basis strings, with one local CNOT per bit and the input strings separately owned. Historical root clocks, complete words and source records are kept in the input root factor. The original lane occupation intervals and locations are deterministic comparison labels. They do not authorize any call on those historical lanes. The actual preparation keeps its own start, completion, transcript, resources and restored track factors.

If the input is the selected bit alone, this same right preparation can be used with a separate preparation of the other root factors. Run one independent root P17 calibration, copy the supplied bit into the old root outcome role, and prepare the old deterministic clock, descriptor and lane factors. Each deterministic factor is prepared from a supplied basis string of its precise old completed value by one local CNOT per bit into its fresh designated output. The extra input strings and their copies are accounted below. These are comparison-output copies of the old completed words and clocks, with the actual new clock kept separately. The direct preparation from the bit is normalized on every input because it is implemented by controlled unitaries, fresh states, and complete instruments. On the actual source the input conditioned on $S$ already has product left and right states. Thus the designated complete-state recovery error is zero, and for an input full state within trace norm $\epsilon$ of the stated source the recovery defect is at most $2\epsilon$ by contractivity and the triangle inequality. The conditional states and the identified boundary are compatible under all coarse restrictions. The result concerns the source-state channel and retains the actual apparatus outputs in its comparison fibre.

**Uniform locality.** Non-root $S$-dependent factors lie within physical distance $\ell_*$ of the root. At separation $d>2\ell_*$ two tested regions cannot both contain such a factor or the root. Every other factor is a product decoration, with all within-site correlated calibration records at the same site. The joint density of the regions is then their tensor product. For $d\le 2\ell_*$ the trace-norm defect is at most two. In particular it is bounded by $2e^{2\kappa\ell_*}e^{-\kappa d}$ for the $\kappa$ of Definition F.10.6h. This bound holds for arbitrary retained regional matrix observables and persists under independent local operations, adaptive local records and independent local spectator preparations by trace-norm contraction. It passes to the quasi-local completion by norm continuity. Across the root cut the conditional joint law is product, so no retained exterior detector distinguishes screened interiors after fixing the selected boundary. A communicating intervention is a different test and owns its changed response and routing. Only the current adjacent edges can transmit unknown input. Causal ancestry over their calls gives the paid-path lower bound, and SWAP transport attains it as in Theorem F.10.6j. Its swap-back proof also lifts arbitrary finite older protocols, with the actual fine route and paid comparison outputs, independently of the prepared source law.

**Evaluated tariff.** The following serial compilation fixes one finite version of each service. Its installed finite tables are supplied as ordinary basis ROMs, with descriptions and input words counted. Take $\eta_n=2^{-n}\tau_*$ and use the clock unit and positive rational prices of Definition C.6c.4a. At a new site allocate 30 P17 cells, one for each reserved calibration address of Theorem C.6c.P17a H.8, even if an address names a core bit already inside the active cell. Their entire $2250$ bits are counted. The calibration's prepared source factors and scoring word give 24 local unitary pulses, including four source Hadamards, and six projective records. Its own 66-bit cell ROMs contain 16 ones per cell, loaded by X pulses. Thus each new qualified site contributes 504 local pulses and six record services including its 30 cell ROM loads. Supply these ideal P17 operations at their original positive durations, in units $\tau_*$, chosen common on this source. All pure preparations, including every fresh zero and every later record, are paid allocated resources. Root and neighboring copied-control payloads are additional bits beyond the 30-cell site bank.

Let
$$
v_n=2(n+1)2^n+1,\qquad r_n=(n+1)2^n,\qquad
a_0=3,\quad a_k=v_k-v_{k-1}\ (k\ge1).
$$
Here $v_n$ counts all sites and $r_n$ the sites strictly to the right. Every lane has two ready bookkeeping bits at each endpoint and its allocated-lane record at its outward endpoint. Thus the right side at level $k$ owns $5r_k-2$ such bits, the left owns the same number and the root owns four. Let
$$
\begin{aligned}
d_n&=\sum_{k=0}^n(5r_k-1),\\
h_n&=\sum_{k=0}^n[4+512\mathbf1_{k=0}\beta_k],\\
m_n&=\sum_{k=0}^n \left[255(a_k-\mathbf1_{k=0})+3\right]\beta_k .
\end{aligned}
$$
$d_n$ counts the right-side lane bits and one restored right control per level, all in basis zero. $h_n$ counts deterministic root bits other than the root calibration, supplied bit and its outcome copy. $m_n$ counts deterministic instruction and clock bits at right locations. There are $(a_k-\mathbf1_{k=0})/2$ new right sites at level $k$, with $510$ calibration events at each. Both link calls for the right signal are driven at its right endpoint, so it has three right signal events. The factor $\beta_k$ is the number of fixed instruction and clock bits per main event of the preparation word, computed below from the preparation row without using $h_n,d_n,m_n$. The root's own $510$ calibration and two fair-source events occur at stage zero. Its fresh calibration reproduces the internal data but not the old external instruction tables.
The table gives allocated lanes $e$, descriptor level $l$, other bits $b$, local gates $u$ and record services $j$ before external command overhead, and link uses $q$. Preparation rows are incremental. The selector and the two recovery words act on the indicated stage-$n$ input. Each link use has unit charge.
$$
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
\text{word}&e&l&b&u&j&q\\\hline
\text{preparation at }k&
v_k-1&k&2250a_k+2+2\mathbf1_{k=0}&504a_k+2+\mathbf1_{k=0}&6a_k+\mathbf1_{k=0}&4\\
\text{selector at }n&0&n&1&1&0&0\\
\text{recovery with root}&
r_n&n&2250r_n+(2^{n+1}-1)+d_n+2m_n&
504r_n+n+1+m_n&6r_n&2(2^{n+1}-1)\\
\text{recovery with bit}&
r_n&n&2250(r_n+1)+(2^{n+1}-1)+d_n+1+2h_n+2m_n&
504(r_n+1)+n+2+h_n+m_n&6(r_n+1)&2(2^{n+1}-1)
\end{array}
\tag{F.10.6l.3}
$$
Preparation uses one restored control at each of $\pm2^{-k}$ and at level zero uses the root bit and its record. Recovery allocates the fresh right half-line and a distinct track of length $2^{n-k}$ per right signal. Its calibration cells, independent inputs, and deterministic history-layout labels are assigned to their original locations. A fresh lane set for the recovery service is installed on the same current edge graph. The boundary-bit variant additionally owns the fresh root calibration, its outcome copy and both $h_n$-bit banks. If one tests a combined word with the old prepared state still present, its already owned factors and their further holding intervals are included by the recomposition rule below. Logical recovery labels are the structural names of the output factors and event slots. Each independent recorded calibration outcome is produced anew in the recovered bank.

For clarity, the following fixed-length ROM and clock construction specifies the overhead as explicit functions of any row of (F.10.6l.3). Set
$$
M=u+j+q,\quad
A=\max\!\left(1,\left\lceil\log_2(b+2M+5e+1)\right\rceil\right),
\quad
R=3M(4+3A),\quad
\beta=6(4+3A)+2 .
$$
Use a ready two-bit clock at the location driving each main event. X first initializes its first clock bit. The two local X gates after the main event then turn the first bit off and the second on. Physical slot arming uses the supplied source-independent timed drive. Each event owns three descriptor words: its operation and its two final clock gates. Each word has four opcode bits and three padded $A$-bit address fields. The preinstalled tables occupy exactly $R$ bits, with their $R$ supplied installation-input bits also retained. Thus an event uses $\beta$ local bits from these two inventories and its clock. The fixed finite pulse library is shared by all stages. The registered descriptor timer is the ideal service of Definition C.6c.4a, using the supplied stage-specific positive period $\eta_l$. Every edge descriptor has norm one. The deterministic stage index and clock period are parameters of the physical timed drive recorded by the schedule of its instruction words, independently of the input. The five lane bits of each allocated lane carry no prepared field data. A link call reserves the whole interval $\eta_l$, executes its gate in the first $\eta_l/2$, then its two clock X gates for $\eta_l/4$ each. For local or record events use an interval $3\tau_*$ with three successive unit slots for the main operation and the two clock X gates. The local core operations keep the fixed $\tau_*$ pulse length. The local projective service uses a pointer-copy CNOT during the first half of its main slot and ideal pointer readout with its basis outcome retained during the remainder. The root Hadamard's readout uses its independently allocated pointer, so both factors are retained. Old deterministic timing and ownership records are the installed words, ready port and clock factors with their event-time dictionary. They carry no random outcome-dependent global summary.

Allocate all row factors at its start. Copy each supplied descriptor bit by one local CNOT into its ready table bit in a serial $R\tau_*$ installation interval. Initialize the $M$ first clock bits with one X per clock in a serial $M\tau_*$ interval. The installer uses fixed local bank-to-bank wiring and each supplied tape. It consumes the actual addresses in the finite construction word, given by the location list and repeated circuits above. The finite implementation uses the fixed physical drive and supplied-ready-resource convention of Theorem C.6c.P17a H.8 and Definition C.6c.4a. Its descriptor tapes, timer, and record services are owned source inputs at their registered support and time. Site preparation and loading events have the counted local pulses in (F.10.6l.3), and the word starts with the counted ready stocks. Every newly allocated bit is held through the word, including the command copies and initialized clock bits. Idle ports and parked factors contribute zero generator in the tariff convention. This gives
$$
\begin{split}
B_0&=b+2M+2R+5e,\\
G_0&=u+3M+R,\qquad J_0=j,\qquad K_0=4M+R,\qquad C_0=q,\\
t_0&=R+M+3(u+j)+q\,2^{-l},\\
E_0&=e,\qquad I_{0,0}=e t_0-q\,2^{-l},\qquad I_{\mathrm{bit},0}=B_0t_0 .
\end{split}
\tag{F.10.6l.4}
$$
Here $t_0$ is in units $\tau_*$, $C_0$ is the link charge, and $I_{\mathrm{bit},0}$ is the other-factor bit-time. The clock, ROM and owned lane port bits are other factors. The lane itself has its own busy/idle meter. A projective record service is one $J$ operation and includes its pointer-copy coupling, so that coupling is not an additional $G$ operation. Its Hamiltonian norm is $2\pi\hbar/\tau_*$ during the pointer pulse and zero on the remainder in the ideal readout service convention. Every independent local unitary used is an involution (including controlled-H), with generator $\pi\hbar(I-V)/(2\tau_*)$. During a link gate the corresponding norm is $2\pi\hbar/\eta_l$, and the clock X pulses have norm $4\pi\hbar/\eta_l$. All three kinds of pulse, including the preparation and installation pulses, enter the maximum. With these fixed choices the exact maximum is
$$
\max_t\|H(t)\|=
\begin{cases}
\pi\hbar/\tau_* &q=j=0,\\
2\pi\hbar/\tau_* &q=0,\ j>0,\\
4\pi\hbar\,2^l/\tau_* &q>0.
\end{cases}
\tag{F.10.6l.5}
$$
In the last case this is attained by the first or second clock pulse inside a link interval. Other source supports are idle during an active pulse by the serial schedule. The Hamiltonian action is $\pi\hbar K_0$ on this pulse schedule, since every occupied primitive slot has exactly one nonzero involution pulse, including the pointer coupling inside a $J$ slot. The ideal outcome operation is part of the separately counted record service.

For the preparation through stage $n$, take the sum of all row resources, with the further maintenance terms included:
$$
\begin{split}
E^{\mathrm{prep}}_n&=\sum_{k=0}^n e_k,\qquad
B^{\mathrm{prep}}_n=\sum_{k=0}^n B_{0,k},\\
I^{\mathrm{prep}}_{0,n}
&=\sum_{k=0}^n\left(t_{0,k}\sum_{i=0}^k e_i-q_k2^{-k}\right),\\
I^{\mathrm{prep}}_n&=\sum_{k=0}^n t_{0,k}\sum_{i=0}^k B_{0,i}.
\end{split}
\tag{F.10.6l.6}
$$
$G,J,C_{\rm link},K$ sum directly and the maximum in (F.10.6l.5) is the stage-$n$ maximum. For a selector or recovery on an already prepared carrier, add $E^{\mathrm{prep}}_n t_0$ and $B^{\mathrm{prep}}_n t_0$ to the old-lane and old-factor maintenance entries of (F.10.6l.4), counting the distinct new lanes and factors once. The old and new inventories are then their sums. The three words therefore give the complete evaluated tariff of Definition C.6c.4a in its fixed units and ideal-service resource convention. Source and recovered historical clock records are retained separately from each new actual time. These finite costs may grow with the stage; the recovery, separation and clustering estimates do not depend on that growth. ∎

### F.10.7 Modular-Inclusion Reconstruction of Local Time

<a id="definition-f107a-oriented-half-sided-modular-inclusion-branch"></a>**Definition F.10.7a (Oriented Half-Sided Modular Inclusion Branch).** Let $\mathfrak N=\mathfrak A(D_1)\subset\mathfrak M=\mathfrak A(D_2)$ be von Neumann algebras on one Hilbert space, with a common unit vector $\Omega$ cyclic and separating for each. Use $\sigma_t^{\mathfrak M}=\operatorname{Ad}\Delta_{\mathfrak M}^{it}$ and the orientation
$$
\sigma_{-t}^{\mathfrak M}(\mathfrak N)\subseteq\mathfrak N
\qquad(t\ge0).
\tag{F.10.7.1}
$$
The word future refers to the translation semigroup selected below; it does not identify positive modular parameter with positive physical time.

<a id="theorem-f107b-positive-energy-algebraic-flow-from-modular-inclusion"></a>**Theorem F.10.7b (Positive-Energy Algebraic Flow from Modular Inclusion).** On this branch, the common-vector case of Araki and Zsidó (2005, Theorem 2.1) supplies a strongly continuous group $U(s)=e^{\mathrm{isP}}$ with $P\ge0$, determined by the two modular operators, and $U(s)\mathfrak M U(s)^*\subseteq\mathfrak M$ for $s\ge0$. A geometric action on diamond labels requires its separate covariance certificate.

*Proof.* The vector states on $\mathfrak M$ and $\mathfrak N$ are faithful normal states because $\Omega$ is separating, and their GNS identifications use the same Hilbert space because $\Omega$ is cyclic for both. Their modular groups satisfy the source theorem's negative-modular-half-line hypothesis by (F.10.7.1). The cited common-vector specialization then supplies the positive generator and inclusion-preserving translation group. <a id="theorem-f107e-finite-dimensional-half-sided-modular-triviality"></a>**Theorem F.10.7e (Finite-Dimensional Half-Sided Modular Triviality).** Let $\mathfrak N\subseteq\mathfrak M$ be unital finite-dimensional von Neumann algebras and let $(\sigma_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be an automorphism group of $\mathfrak M$. For the final positive-duration commit, take a fresh record qubit $C$ in $|0\rangle$ and let

H_{\mathrm{commit}}&=\pi(I-U_{\mathrm{commit}})/(2\varepsilon).

Run this constant local Hamiltonian for time $\varepsilon$, from $R-\varepsilon$ to $R$. It exactly implements $U_{\mathrm{commit}}$, and $\lVert H_{\mathrm{commit}}\rVert=\pi/\varepsilon$. Tracing out the pointer leaves a diagonal classical record with probabilities

p(o|b)=(1+ob\kappa_{AB})/2.
\tag{F.10.7f.5}
$$

Thus a retained classical response is already present at time $R$. No zero-duration field measurement or subsequent zero-duration pointer copy is used to claim attainment. Reading a diagonal record is not counted as an additional information-transfer operation. Source dephasing, if the endpoint map is required on arbitrary quantum/reference inputs, can be realized by a source-controlled copy to a fresh local ancilla during $(0,\varepsilon)$: its finite Hamiltonian commutes with the source-bit-controlled field coupling, and discarding that ancilla gives the dephasing of Section 9. Classical input preparation itself is an initial condition, not an unaccounted communication step.

For the actual finite-duration resource ledger, let the dimensionless on-shell temporal Fourier multipliers of $w_{A},w_{B}$ be $W_{A},W_{B}$, and define

E_A&=(1/2)\int|\hat f(q)|^{2}|W_A(|q|)|^{2}\,d^{3}q/(2\pi)^{3}, \\

Both are finite and explicitly determined by the locked smooth windows and f. The source energy after its completed control is exactly

The detector's conditional field displacement has coefficient ±1/2, so the combined coherent branches admit the finite bound

The source coefficient is bounded by $|\lambda|\,\lVert w_{A}\rVert_{\infty}/a$, the receiver coefficient by $\lVert w_{B}\rVert_{\infty}/(2a)$, and the commit and optional source-dephasing Hamiltonians have norm $\pi/\varepsilon$. Include both qubits, any source-dephasing ancilla, the mixed-pointer entropy, every window, and these strength/energy bounds in the ledger. The same cone proof now uses actual spacetime-local operations: source support is in $[0,\varepsilon]\times B_{a}$, receiver support in $[R-2\varepsilon,R-\varepsilon]\times B_{a}(Rn)$, and commit is local at the receiver through $R$. Every fixed positive spacelike margin excludes signaling for sufficiently small $a$; at every null-center displacement the exact fixed response (F.10.7f.5) survives. #### F.10.7f.11 Locked clock domain and explicit conformal/reflected overlap

so h maps $W_{R}$ to the unit diamond. Its inverse is regular on that diamond. The spatial reflection in (F.10.7f.7) preserves the required spacetime orientation of the time-oriented conformal implementation.
