Then for each fixed pair/window the desired right side $C\,\lVert A_n\rVert\,\lVert B_n\rVert\,|X_n|\,\exp[-\mu(d_n-|t|/a_n)]$ is at worst exponentially small in $1/a_{n}$. D5 is superexponentially smaller and hence satisfies it eventually with fixed $\mu>0$, the same physical speed 1, and one common budget diagonal. Inside the geometric cone, the trivial commutator bound gives the same form because $d_{n}-|t|/a_{n}$ is bounded above by $C_{K}$. The finitely many initial stages may be absorbed in the registered constant on that finite budget.

Support cardinality counts actual host blocks carrying the operators, not their internal auxiliary dimension. On a block array of spacing $b_{n}$, $|X_n|=O_K(b_n^{-3})$. Choose $b_{n}$ with $\log(1/b_n)=o(1/a_n)$ so the original support-growth condition holds.

D6 is not true with a sharp Euclidean cone for the ordinary cubic $\ell^{1}$ graph. A concrete geometric candidate is a dense block array of spacing $b_{n}=o(a_{n}^{2})$, with actual links joining centers at distance at most $a_{n}$. Polygonal routing then gives

$$
D \le a_n d_n \le D+O(a_n+D b_n/a_n).
$$

For fixed K this is D6. These links and their clocks/resources must be real registered hardware; unused virtual edges cannot define a favorable metric. The finite source interaction terms must be supported on this actual graph. The required physical routing certificate is a separate condition beyond drawing those edges.

The direct original reading of F.10.2(5) has been independently checked: it requires these inequalities on the same norm-dense compatible representatives, not a new all-UV-unit-ball statement. The latter would generally fail for this high-resolution block source and is not claimed.

#### 6. The actual limiting Hadamard field

For every fixed pair of Cauchy tests f,g,

$$
\omega_n(a^*(P_n f)a(P_n g))=\langle P_n g,C_{\mathrm{vac}} P_n f\rangle \to \langle g,C_{\mathrm{vac}} f\rangle.
$$

With D4 the spacetime two-point tests converge to the genuine Dirac vacuum distribution. Positivity and the CAR relation pass through the actual compatible field-state maps. Thus the identified limit is the known nontrivial Dirac vacuum, with its Hadamard wavefront set and commutator singularity; it is not a smooth zero-field limit.

On each normal neighborhood its Hadamard-subtracted remainder is smooth and the K.10.4a Sobolev quantities are finite. The actual finite preparation above supplies a source-specific finite protocol cost record. No assertion is made that each bare cutoff kernel itself already has the continuum singularity; the finite record identifies its actual source limit/extension. Finite quasifree restrictions and the limiting field belong to one explicitly compared source family.

The selected material crossing ports can be adjoined by the already proved conditional host edges, without changing this field covariance. Their KMS Hamiltonian is the separately realized gN; the field Hamiltonian remains $K_{n}$ and tends to D. Neither is substituted for the other's modular logarithm. The port shrinking-cover theorem can then consume this reference **once the remaining original regional/source gates below are supplied**.

#### 7. Exact remaining realization gates

The construction now fixes the finite field state, actual physical generator, preparation and one common same-clock limit. The remaining initial-reference admission is specifically:

1. A physical local fermion-to-MPU tensor realization on the invariant prepared sector, including actual even regional observable support and faithful code norms. Local Hamiltonian simulation alone is insufficient. In 3D, an unqualified Jordan-Wigner map fails this requirement.
2. A registered physical dense-link geometry/clock with D6 and its real hardware/cost, or another proved graph/geometry comparison satisfying the original spacelike-margin inequality. No metric is renamed to hide a wider microscopic bound.
3. Coherent regional/evolved-slice comparisons, not only the global Cauchy CAR inclusions. Cauchy-local supports above are exact up to the shrinking cell collar. For general spacetime regions the physical instruments, their clock transport and overlap comparisons must be mapped into the same F.10.1 quotient. Finite-Hamiltonian tails must not make every open region's finite algebra the whole apparatus; the retained core and its boundary-error maps must be explicit.

These gates are not F.0's uniform-strength assumption, not full F05 inertial stress tightness, and not a new universal Wightman/autonomy requirement. They are the actual regional/causal source identification named by F.10.1–F.10.2 and K.10.4a. The new estimates supply a concrete route through them, rather than an arbitrary independent vacuum assumption.

<a id="construction-f1012i4-invariant-local-majorana-code-and-faithful-even-responses"></a>**Construction F.10.12i.4 (Invariant Local Majorana Code and Faithful Even Responses).**

#### Result and source scope

A finite cubic-lattice Dirac Hamiltonian has an exact physically local qubit realization on an explicitly prepared invariant code. The construction uses four physical fermion modes and three auxiliary complex modes per spatial site, then a site-block Jordan–Wigner representation. Every encoded Hamiltonian term is supported on one site or the two endpoints of one physical lattice edge. Every even CAR observable in a connected lattice region has a norm-preserving spin representative supported inside that region. The underlying charged/odd CAR fields are reconstructed through the code isometry; they are **not** asserted to be ordinary spin-local operators.

The code input domain, gauge constraints, boundaries, actual source preparation and cost/support ledger are explicit below. Equality is on the code and its declared even operational algebra. There is no claim that arbitrary qubit states, errors leaving the code, or arbitrary qubit channels are equivalent to the fermionic theory.

The primary antecedent is Verstraete and Cirac (2005). That paper uses auxiliary Majoranas to cancel Jordan–Wigner strings and additionally constructs local sector-selecting Hamiltonians. The elementary construction proved here instead uses one auxiliary Majorana per edge endpoint and a paid prepared invariant sector. It claims no local penalty or unique-ground-sector mechanism and so does not import the paper's separate boundary/topological ground-sector statements.

#### 1. Actual finite source Hamiltonian

Let $\Lambda$ be a finite connected subgraph of the cubic lattice $a\mathbb{Z}^{3}$, with degree at most six. Use open boundaries for the main statement. A periodic version is allowed only with its wrap edges and spin structure explicitly registered as physical graph data. At every site $v$ retain four complex CAR modes $c_{v,A}$, $A=1,\dots,4$. With Hermitian Dirac matrices $\alpha_{j}$, $\beta$, $\alpha_{j}^{2}=\beta^{2}=I$, define the actual finite centered-difference one-particle matrix by

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_a(v,v)&=m c^2 \beta, \\
D_a(v,v+a e_j)&=-i \hbar c\, \alpha_j/(2a), \\
D_a(v+a e_j,v)&=D_a(v,v+a e_j)^*.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
$$

Edges leaving the open box are absent. The second-quantized physical source is

$$
\begin{aligned}
H_F&=E_{\mathrm{ref}} I+\sum_v c_v^* m c^2 \beta c_v \\
&\quad+\sum_{(v,w)} [c_v^* T_{vw} c_w+c_w^* T_{vw}^* c_v].
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
$$

The physical time and the actual scalar reference $E_{\mathrm{ref}}$ are the same ones supplied by the Dirac source. Neither a modular Hamiltonian nor a fitted vacuum subtraction replaces them. The encoding works for any registered finite self-adjoint nearest-neighbor quadratic coefficients; it does not change the chosen boundary regulator or remove fermion doublers.

The onsite norm is at most $2|m|c^{2}$. For the centered-difference four-component link, its Fock-space norm is the trace norm of $T_{vw}$, namely $2\hbar c/a$. Thus the physical cutoff strength grows as $1/a$, exactly as in the original regulator. The direct F.10 comparison route must keep its actual physical causal estimate; this construction does not claim a cutoff-independent F.0 interaction norm.

#### 2. Auxiliary Majoranas, boundary completion and the code

Add three complex auxiliary modes per site, equivalently six Majoranas $\eta_{v,r}$, $r=1,\dots,6$. They anticommute with all physical and auxiliary odd modes, are self-adjoint, and obey $\{\eta_{i},\eta_{j}\}=2\delta_{ij}$.

Assign a distinct $\eta_{v,e}$ to every edge incident at $v$. For an oriented undirected edge $e=(v,w)$, define

$$
Q_e=i\, \eta_{v,e}\, \eta_{w,e}.
\tag{3}
$$

Every endpoint Majorana is used once. Consequently

$$
Q_e^*=Q_e,\qquad Q_e^2=I,\qquad [Q_e,Q_f]=0.
\tag{4}
$$

Complete the unused boundary Majoranas into disjoint pairs and give each pair the same $i\eta\eta$ involution, with its orientation fixed in the source record. The total number of unused Majoranas is even. The complete matching contains exactly $3|\Lambda|$ pairs. Boundary pairs need not be neighboring sites: they define preparation/sector constraints, not observation Hamiltonian interactions. Their actual finite preparation routing is counted in Section 8.

The complete commuting set is independent. A product of a nonempty proper subset contains a nonempty set of distinct Majoranas and is not I; the product of all matching pairs is a sign times the auxiliary fermion parity, also not I. Equivalently, an orthogonal Majorana reordering takes the matching to independent canonical pairs. Hence the joint +1 eigenspace on the auxiliary Fock space is one dimensional. Denote its normalized vector by $\chi$ and its projector by $P_{\chi}$. Its parity is fixed by the declared orientations. It is a pure Gaussian/stabilizer state, not a thermal mixed bank supplied at no cost.

Let J be the exact unitary Fock-basis change from the grouped physical/auxiliary ordering to the site-block ordering. Define

$$
\begin{aligned}
W \psi&=J(\psi\otimes\chi), \\
P_{\mathrm{code}}&=W W^*=J(I\otimes P_\chi)J^*.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
$$

Then $W^{*}W=I$ and the code dimension is exactly $2^{4|\Lambda|}$. Both physical parity sectors can be represented; the retained operational algebra is even and preserves them. A selected parity sector or a faithful parity-invariant mixture is fixed by the actual source state. If purifiers are included, their parity/reference data remain explicit.

No gauge term has been added to $H_{F}$. The auxiliary storage Hamiltonian in this witness is explicitly zero during observation. Its preparation, pure input resources and retained qubits are real source entries, not discarded entropy.

#### 3. The exact local self-adjoint spin generator

Before applying $J$, replace every offsite physical quadratic term $h_{e}$ by $h_{e}Q_{e}$, leaving all onsite even terms unchanged:

$$
\begin{aligned}
H_{\mathrm{dress}}&=E_{\mathrm{ref}} I+\sum_v h_v+\sum_e h_e Q_e, \\
H_{\mathrm{spin}}&=J H_{\mathrm{dress}} J^*.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
$$

Here $h_{e}$ and $Q_{e}$ commute, because $h_{e}$ is physical-even and $Q_{e}$ auxiliary-even. Thus every term is self-adjoint. Equations (4) also give $[H_{\mathrm{dress}},Q_{f}]=0$ for every edge and boundary pair. Therefore the code is exactly invariant and

$$
\begin{aligned}
H_{\mathrm{spin}} W&=W H_F, \\
\exp(-it H_{\mathrm{spin}}/\hbar)W&=W \exp(-it H_F/\hbar),\qquad t\in\mathbb{R}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
$$

The complete physical scalar reference appears on both sides. The auxiliary sector has no omitted dynamical or gauge energy.

##### Why the spin interaction is physically local

In site-block Jordan–Wigner notation a global odd Majorana at v is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Gamma_{v,a}&=\Bigl(\prod_{u<v} P_u\Bigr) \gamma_{v,a}, \\
P_u&=\text{product of the seven onsite qubit } Z \text{ operators}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
$$

An even product of odd operators at each individual site contains no intersite Jordan–Wigner string. For example, with e oriented v to w,

$$
\begin{aligned}
(c_{v,A}^* c_{w,B}) Q_e \\
&= -i (c_{v,A}^* \eta_{v,e})(c_{w,B} \eta_{w,e}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
$$

Each parenthesis is onsite-even, so its spin image acts only on its own seven-qubit site block. The Hermitian conjugate has the same support. All onsite even terms are already onsite. Hence $H_{\mathrm{spin}}$ is a sum of one-site and adjacent-two-site matrices, with a bounded number of terms per site and unchanged term norms:

$$
\lVert J h_{e}Q_{e}J^{*}\rVert=\lVert h_{e}\rVert.
\tag{10}
$$

This is exact locality, not a small-string or expectation-only approximation. A two-site term can act on at most fourteen qubits. The original B.4 local-auxiliary support rule permits such fixed finite support. No two-qubit-only interaction promise is made. If that additional hardware restriction is imposed, its actual compiler and time/error ledger must be supplied separately.

At the block-site level, degree is at most six and term incidence is bounded independently of lattice size. A fixed local host ownership enlargement therefore preserves physical support and the original $O(1/a)$ strength, as in the accepted owner host-lift lemma.

#### 4. A faithful local representative for every connected-region even observable

Let R be a connected set of lattice sites, choose a spanning tree $T_{R}$ inside R, and fix its root r. For each v in R set

$$
B_v=\prod_{e\in\text{tree path } r \text{ to } v} Q_e,\qquad B_r=I.
\tag{11}
$$

The $B_{v}$ commute, are involutions, and commute with every physical fermion. Consequently

$$
\tilde c_{v,A}=B_v c_{v,A}
\tag{12}
$$

satisfy the exact CAR on the entire enlarged Fock space. More explicitly, the unitary

$$
U_R=\prod_{v\in R} [(I+B_v)/2+(I-B_v)(-1)^{N_v}/2]
\tag{13}
$$

implements $c_{v,A}\to B_{v}c_{v,A}$, where $N_{v}$ is the total physical occupation at $v$. Every factor in (13) is a commuting self-adjoint unitary. Thus

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Phi_R(A)&=U_R (A\otimes I_{\mathrm{aux}}) U_R^*, \\
E_R(A)&=J \Phi_R(A) J^*
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
$$

is an exact faithful unital *-homomorphism, with $\lVert E_{R}(A)\rVert=\lVert A\rVert$, on the full physical CAR algebra. Its **spin locality conclusion applies to $A\in\mathrm{CAR}_{\mathrm{even}}(R)$**.

To prove that conclusion, expand an even $A$ in even fermionic monomials. For a monomial let $s_{v}$ be its odd/even count at $v$. Multiplication by the $B_{v}$ supplies a tree-edge $Q$ product whose boundary is the set $\{v:s_{v}=1\}$. At each site, the parity of the incident auxiliary Majoranas is therefore $s_{v}$, so physical plus auxiliary parity is even at every site. Equation (8) cancels every intersite string. All tree paths stay in $R$. Thus $E_{R}(A)$ is an ordinary spin operator supported on $R$, including the onsite auxiliary qubits, with no external string.

This argument covers hopping, pairing and arbitrary even finite polynomials, not only number-conserving bilinears. For two test functions f,g in a common normal neighborhood, choose a connected lattice region R inside that neighborhood containing their sampled supports. The finite bilinears c(f)*c(g) and c(f)c(g)* then have actual supported representatives there; the connecting paths are part of that regional choice. Their exact code expectations supply the original quasifree two-point tests.

An odd $c(f)$ need not have a spin-local representative. The underlying charged field is reconstructed using $W$ and the CAR source; the operational spin-local net is its even algebra. For a disconnected support, a charge-pair observable joining two components can require a connecting path. The claimed local representative uses a declared connected neighborhood containing that path. No disconnected-union or odd-locality property is inferred.

#### 5. Operational code quotient, regions and exact responses

Every $E_{R}(A)$ commutes with all $Q$ constraints and preserves the code. On it,

$$
\begin{aligned}
E_R(A) W&=W A, \\
W^* E_R(A) W&=A.
\end{aligned}
\tag{15}
$$

Different spanning trees or different connected containing regions give representatives with the same restriction to the code, although they can differ by order-one operators on other gauge sectors. Define the admitted physical input domain

$$
D_{\mathrm{code}}=\{\rho\ge 0: \operatorname{Tr}\rho=1,\ \rho=P_{\mathrm{code}} \rho P_{\mathrm{code}}\}.
\tag{16}
$$

The retained operational algebra consists of the restrictions $E_{R}(\mathrm{CAR}_{\mathrm{even}}(R))|_{\mathrm{code}}$, or equivalently the quotient of these gauge-preserving representatives by operators annihilating the code. Its norm is

$$
\lVert[O]\rVert_{\mathrm{code}}=\lVert O\vert_{\mathrm{code}}\rVert.
\tag{17}
$$

Equation (15) is an isometric *-isomorphism between this regional algebra and $\mathrm{CAR}_{\mathrm{even}}(R)$. Regional inclusions, overlaps on the same physical CAR subalgebra, and compositions are therefore exact on this actual domain. They are not merely state-dependent equalities in one vacuum.

A local even instrument with Kraus operators $K_{\alpha}$ has the physical implementation $E_{R}(K_{\alpha})$. It preserves the code, and the completeness relation and every sequential response pull back exactly. For every physical source state $\rho_{F}$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho_{\mathrm{spin}}&=W \rho_F W^*, \\
\operatorname{Tr}[\rho_{\mathrm{spin}} E_R(A)]&=\operatorname{Tr}[\rho_F A],
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
$$

with the corresponding exact identities after Hamiltonian evolution (7) and every admitted even local instrument. Faithful finite source restrictions remain faithful in the operational code algebra. They are not faithful on the entire qubit Hilbert space, and no whole-Hilbert CPTP equivalence is asserted.

A parity-preserving channel need not have individually even Kraus operators. For example, a quasifree vacuum-loss comparison can have odd loss Kraus operators while admitting a parity-even fermionic Stinespring unitary on the system plus vacuum ancillary modes. Such a channel is treated by encoding the joint system/ancilla even unitary and the system even observable A tensor I, retaining the actual ancillas and their preparation in the source. The joint code expectation is then exactly the Stinespring channel expectation. This extends the response statement when that actual dilation and its support have been supplied; it does not assert that every Kraus operator is even, nor that an abstract dilation is automatically local. No whole-space qubit loss-channel equivalence is inferred.

The retained responses are genuinely noncommutative. Take two physical modes with faithful diagonal occupations $p$ and $q$, $0<p,q<1$ and $p\ne q$. The even exchange pulse generated by $G=c_{1}^{*}c_{2}+c_{2}^{*}c_{1}$ for dimensionless angle $\pi/2$ exchanges their number expectations. The local $n_{1}$ readout therefore changes from $p$ to $q$, with exact nonzero gap $|p-q|$. Its encoded even pulse and readout have the same gap on the actual code input, at one site for two onsite components or on an adjacent pair for different sites. This is an explicit operational response, not a dimension-only nontriviality claim.

The adjacent-edge term of $H_{\mathrm{spin}}$ need not equal the whole-space tree representative $E_{R}(h_{e})$ when $e$ is not a tree edge. Both preserve the code and have the same restriction $h_{e}$ there. This is why (7), (15) and the stated code norm, rather than a false whole-space equality, are the relevant source comparison.

#### 6. Boundary, topology and parity ledger

For open boundaries the unused auxiliary Majoranas are explicitly paired and prepared. This fixes all auxiliary degrees, leaving no unrecorded boundary factor. There is no penalty Hamiltonian whose locality would need to enforce those boundary choices.

For a periodic graph, every site can use all six auxiliary Majoranas on incident edges. The complete matching still has a unique declared joint sector. The physical wrap couplings and any periodic/antiperiodic signs remain in $T_{vw}$. Preparing this sector is a global finite resource task. It is not claimed to be the unique ground sector of a local spin Hamiltonian; possible topological obstructions to that different claim are irrelevant to (7). A periodic wrap edge is physically local only in the declared torus geometry, not automatically in a Euclidean open-box embedding.

The construction preserves physical fermion parity under all retained even observables and the quadratic Hamiltonian. It does not introduce spin-local odd fields or allow arbitrary parity-changing physical instruments. Ancillary qubit gates used to prepare the encoding are physical spin operations on the simulator; their entire preparation and any parity reference are retained, rather than mistaken for an even CAR observation protocol.

#### 7. Same-field comparison and physical causal bounds

Let $i_{n}^{m}$ be an already proved coherent even CAR comparison for the actual finite Dirac regulators, on its declared regional bounded families. Define its encoded operational comparison by

$$
j_n^m([E_n(A)])=[E_m(i_n^m A)].
\tag{19}
$$

It is exact whenever the source comparison is exact, and inherits its stated defects otherwise, with no norm loss by (17). Actual dynamics errors are identical by (7). For a retained connected region, (14) gives an actual physically supported spin representative with full operator norm equal to the CAR norm.

The UCP convention can be made explicit. If $i_{n}^{m}$ is UCP on the retained even CAR algebras, then (19) is UCP on their operational code algebras. A whole-matrix UCP extension exists: let $C_{n}(O)$ be the compression $W_{n}^{*}OW_{n}$ followed by the physical-parity conditional expectation, and let

$$
L_m(A)=W_m A W_m^*+\omega_m(A)(I-P_{\mathrm{code},m}),
\tag{19a}
$$

where $\omega_{m}$ is any declared state on the target even CAR algebra. Then $L_{m}i_{n}^{m}C_{n}$ is unital completely positive and has exactly the required code restriction. This extension is a mathematical comparison map; its gauge projector need not be region-local, and it is not presented as an actual local preparation channel. The actual local representatives remain (14). Thus the finite source explicitly registers code-domain comparisons. If a separate application insists on unrestricted-qubit local comparison norm, the present theorem does not discharge that stronger premise.

For regional A,B and physical time t,

$$
\lVert[\alpha_{\mathrm{spin},t}(E_{R}(A)),E_{S}(B)]|_{\mathrm{code}}\rVert=\lVert[\alpha_{F,t}(A),B]\rVert.
\tag{20}
$$

Thus any proved physical-mesh/margin Lieb–Robinson or sharper free-propagation estimate for the same CAR source transfers in the admitted code norm with the same constants. A generic unrestricted-spin Lieb–Robinson bound also exists for (6), but may have a larger velocity. This construction does not claim that its coarse bound is the exact relativistic speed c. The parent Dirac analysis must supply the source's actual physical cone/margin estimate, including its fine-lattice/grouped-MPU distance conversion. Off-code errors are outside the claimed exact comparison and require their own control if admitted.

The physical field covariance is unchanged on every encoded two-point test. Hence the supplied CAR continuum/Hadamard comparison transfers with precisely its original fixed-test errors and source state. The encoder does not itself prove that covariance limit, produce a Hadamard parametrix, remove doubling, or prove the initial source has already met every original F.20 gate.

#### 8. Explicit finite preparation and owned resource/support map

Let $p=4|\Lambda|$ and $b=3|\Lambda|$. The following finite preparation works for every supplied finite physical density matrix and, in particular, the actual quasifree state. Its costs can grow with the regulator; no uniform or free preparation claim is made.

##### 8.1 Prepare the actual physical source

For a number-conserving quasifree covariance C, diagonalize it with its actual finite one-particle unitary. Prepare each diagonal occupation probability $\lambda_{j}$ by the retained purification

$$
\sqrt{1-\lambda_j}\,|00\rangle+\sqrt{\lambda_j}\,|11\rangle,
\tag{21}
$$

and apply the corresponding fermionic Gaussian unitary to the physical modes. Keep every purifier. A finite sequence of two-mode Givens rotations implements the unitary with $O(p^{2})$ elementary Gaussian rotations; each has an explicit finite self-adjoint quadratic generator and clock duration. A general quasifree covariance uses the analogous real Majorana plane rotations and the stated parity convention. If coefficients are supplied only to finite precision, retain the actual prepared covariance and its explicit source-state error; do not call the intended continuum state exact at a finite compiler precision.

##### 8.2 Prepare the auxiliary matching state

In the grouped auxiliary ordering, the complete $Q$ matching is a set of $b$ independent commuting Pauli operators. There is a constructive finite Clifford preparation. At step $k$, pick a remaining nontrivial stabilizer, move a nontrivial position to $k$, and use onsite H/S gates to turn all its nontrivial factors into $Z$. CNOTs with target $k$ and controls at its other $Z$ positions reduce it to signed $Z_{k}$. Commutation allows the other generators' $Z_{k}$ factors to be removed by generator-row multiplication. Repeat on the remaining qubits. This uses $O(b^{2})$ Clifford gates and records every final sign. If $C_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is the resulting Clifford, then

$$
\chi=C_{\mathrm{aux}}^*\, |\text{signed computational basis}\rangle.
\tag{22}
$$

The generator-row operations are classical bookkeeping; the recorded Clifford gates are the actual physical preparation. This is deterministic and uses no unrecorded postselection. Pure input qubits and their preparation are owned resources.

##### 8.3 Apply the actual encoding order

Starting from $\rho_{F}\otimes|\chi\rangle\langle\chi|$, apply the finite fermionic mode permutation $J$ to the site-block ordering. Every adjacent fermionic exchange is

$$
\mathrm{FSWAP}=\mathrm{SWAP}\times\mathrm{CZ},
\tag{23}
$$

so $J$ is an explicit finite Clifford circuit. Its occupation-dependent sign is essential; ordinary SWAP alone gives the wrong intertwiner. At most $O((p+b)^{2})$ adjacent ordering exchanges suffice.

All required non-neighboring preparation gates can be compiled using actual ordinary qubit SWAP routing along a fixed connected nearest-neighbor physical graph, then restoring the logical assignment. A gate between endpoints of a path of length $d$ needs at most $2d+1$ neighbor gates up to the fixed gate decomposition. The finite graph diameter $D_{\mathrm{graph}}$ gives a conservative $O(D_{\mathrm{graph}}(p+b)^{2})$ routing bound for the Clifford encoding stages. Purifier and Gaussian-rotation routing is included similarly. Extra temporary routing qubits, if used, stay in the inventory; they are not erased for free. The local observation Hamiltonian afterward remains exactly (6), without those preparation strings.

##### 8.4 Actual drives, clocks and accounting

Each finite gate is supplied by an actual bounded self-adjoint qubit generator over its declared nonzero duration. For an involution $U$ one can use $\pi\hbar(I-U)/(2\tau)$, giving the exact gate up to its registered scalar phase. H, CNOT, SWAP and FSWAP fit this form; phase rotations have their explicit diagonal generators. No frame-change generator is omitted. The storage interaction is switched off during the declared preparation sequence and restored afterward, or its actual driven terms must be included in the compiler instead.

The ledger records: p physical modes, b auxiliary qubits, all purifiers and blanks, every gate, every routing pulse, actual duration, peak control energy, switching work, final physical $H_{F}$ energy including $E_{\mathrm{ref}}$, loaded service/owner flags, retained records and any losses. An ideal cyclic zero-storage pulse has zero net work but nonzero control energy/support; this does not make the blank preparation or encoding free. Restoring $H_{\mathrm{spin}}$ has its actual endpoint energy charge. If an implementation starts from mixed thermal ancillas, its actual purification/reset protocol is an additional charged step; exact pure $\chi$ is not derived from a finite-temperature full-rank state by a unitary alone.

Preparation may occupy the entire finite box and a long pre-observation interval. It is not claimed to be supported in every later small local diamond. The actual field observations and evolution in the admitted interval are local by Sections 3–5. This separation is an owned physical source schedule, not a relabeling of preparation gates as local observations.

#### 9. Unchanged-host lift and deliverable boundary

Attach each seven-qubit encoding block, its retained purifier allocation and preparation wires as explicitly owned local auxiliaries to the unchanged admitted MPU cores. The finite lift uses actual conditional local interactions $P_{Z}\otimes h_{\mathrm{spin},Z}$, physical clock $t$ and independently metered service energy. On the ready-core image it intertwines $H_{\mathrm{spin}}$ exactly, with the service scalar retained. Composing that isometry with $W$ gives the original Dirac source, its even regional responses and physical generator, not a modular surrogate.

Every $h_{\mathrm{spin},Z}$ has the actual one-/two-site support proved above. The host enlargement is fixed at each endpoint and preserves bounded incidence. The aux code input is the actually prepared $P_{\mathrm{code}}$ sector, and every retained observation instrument and Hamiltonian preserves it. Neither the aggregate source nor its gauge code is declared to be a new minimum-complexity MPU.

This supplies the requested finite local spin encoding, physical support, invariant code, exact self-adjoint generator and faithful even responses, with finite owned preparation. The initial regular CAR source, its continuum Hadamard/state comparison, grouped physical cone estimate, and the original regional/clock assembly remain the parent construction's stated inputs.

<a id="construction-f1012i5-actual-history-cost-graph-and-common-metric-form-limit"></a>**Construction F.10.12i.5 (Actual History Cost Graph and Common Metric-Form Limit).**

#### 1. Source and operational calibration

Use the actual finite hosted source and the executed clock/address history of Lemmas 44b.1–44b.6 and Theorems 44b.7–44b.8, with the apparatus/current typing of Lemma 44b.4 and stationary-event markers of Theorem 44b.8. Spatial positions are calibrated host-block addresses, not independent continuum vacuum labels. At actual time $t_{k}$ the actual event instrument writes the clock count and address into a fresh persistent classical metadata register. The field port is, separately, the actual Heisenberg observable $U_{n}(t_{k})^{*}A_{k,j}U_{n}(t_{k})$. An independent clock/completion instrument can write metadata without measuring or copying the field. All addresses, clocks, controllers, old/fresh registers and source preparation remain in the ledger.

Here is an explicit non-reset completion-work representative, which makes the calibration testable. Each enabled comparison service has a degenerate one-bit payload register at each endpoint, a battery with levels $E_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and 0, and a completion flag with levels 0 and $E_{\mathrm{ref}}$. The transfer unitary is a payload SWAP followed by

$$
\lvert E_{\mathrm{ref}}\rangle_{\mathrm{battery}}\lvert 0\rangle_{\mathrm{flag}}\to\lvert 0\rangle_{\mathrm{battery}}\lvert E_{\mathrm{ref}}\rangle_{\mathrm{flag}}.
$$

The last map extends to an energy-conserving SWAP on the two-dimensional one-excitation sector; use the inverse action on $|0\rangle|E_{\mathrm{ref}}\rangle$ and identity on the other sectors. A bounded finite-dimensional pulse generates it in a finite registered duration. It is independent of payload values. #### 3. Cost metric and volume, with explicit comparison maps

Partition $T_{n}$ into half-open cubes $Q_{x}$ of side $b_{n}$ centered at $x$. Let $J_{n}u$ be $u(x)$ on $Q_{x}$, and $P_{n}f(x)=b_{n}^{-4}\int_{Q_{x}}f$. #### 4. Actual graph form: exact normalization and Mosco proof

Signed-permutation symmetry of $S_{n}$ gives

##### 4.1 Weak liminf (including nonsmooth varying functions)

Define $D_{n}u(x)=s_{n}^{-1}\sum_{z}z[u(x+z)-u(x)]$. For any unit vector $v$, Cauchy–Schwarz and (2) give

$$
\lvert v\cdot D_{n}u(x)\rvert^{2}\le s_{n}^{-1}\sum_{z}\lvert u(x+z)-u(x)\rvert^{2}.
$$

Taking the maximizing $v$ yields $\lVert J_{n}D_{n}u\rVert_{2}^{2}\le E_{n}^{G}(u)$. Suppose $J_{n}u_{n}$ converges weakly to $u$ in the varying-space local identifications, with bounded global $L^2$ norm and liminf graph energy finite. Choose a subsequence realizing the liminf. On every fixed compact, $J_{n}D_{n}u_{n}$ has an $L^2$-weakly convergent subsequence. For a smooth compactly supported vector field $\phi$, cell averaging and discrete summation by parts give

$$
b_{n}^{4}\sum_{x}D_{n}u_{n}(x)\cdot P_{n}\phi(x)=-b_{n}^{4}\sum_{x}u_{n}(x)[s_{n}^{-1}\sum_{z}z\cdot(P_{n}\phi(x)-P_{n}\phi(x-z))].
$$

The bracket converges uniformly, and strongly in $L^2$ on a common compact, to $\operatorname{div}\phi$: (2) identifies its first derivative, and the Taylor error is $O(a_{n})\lVert D^{2}\phi\rVert_{\infty}$. $P_{n}$ commutes with translations by $z$. Therefore the weak limit of $J_{n}D_{n}u_{n}$ is the distributional $\nabla u$. Weak lower semicontinuity on increasing compact sets gives

$$
u\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^4),\qquad E(u)\le\liminf E_n^G(u_n).
\tag{4}
$$

Here “$u\in H^{1}$” uses the assumed global $L^2$ bound; the identical localized argument gives $H^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ when only local bounds are retained. The same proof with ordinary weak gradients proves the torus-interpolant liminf. No first-shell isotropy claim substitutes for this argument.

##### 4.2 Strong recovery

For $f\in C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{4})$, regard $f$ as a smooth function on $T_{n}$ once its support is away from the seam and take $u_{n}=P_{n}f$. Taylor expansion, (2), and cell averaging yield

$$
\begin{aligned}
J_n P_n f &\to f \text{ strongly in } L^2, \\
E_n^G(P_n f) &\to \int|\nabla f|^{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
$$

For example the error is bounded by a constant depending on a fixed support and finitely many derivatives times $(a_{n}+b_{n})$; signed symmetry improves the smooth sampling error further. The leading term is exactly $\sum_{z}(\nabla f\cdot z)^{2}/s_{n}=|\nabla f|^{2}$. Dominated Riemann sums handle the cells and the support collar. Density of $C_{c}^{\infty}$ in $H^{1}$, followed by a diagonal choice, gives a strong recovery sequence for every $H^{1}$ function. For functions of infinite energy the recovery inequality is vacuous and $L^2$-density still supplies strong approximants. The same compactly supported $f$ themselves provide recovery for $E_{n}^{T}$.

Consequently both the actual full graph forms $E_{n}^{G}$ and the full flat-interpolant forms $E_{n}^{T}$ Mosco-converge to the SAME closed regular strongly local quadratic form $E$ on the SAME cell/center identifications. Their halves $\mathrm{Ch}_{n}^{G}$ and $\mathrm{Ch}_{n}^{T}$ Mosco-converge to $\mathrm{Ch}=E/2$, the Euclidean Cheeger energy in the one-half convention. Indeed fixed positive scaling multiplies the weak-liminf and strong-recovery inequalities on the same weakly convergent and recovery sequences, and its inverse proves the converse. The half forms prove the D.6e clauses imported by 44a, whose displayed full-energy form is $2\mathrm{Ch}=E$. This is stronger than merely finding an isotropic smooth-test graph limit and does not assert D.6e's global minimizer selection.

The metric limit (1) and energy limit (4)-(5) have the same Euclidean norm and coefficients. In particular the intrinsic metric of E is the limit of the actual cost metrics. Every $T_{n}$ is a complete compact flat four-manifold with full-support volume, regular strongly local quadratic Cheeger energy $\mathrm{Ch}_{n}^{T}=E_{n}^{T}/2$, Sobolev-to-Lipschitz, and the usual generator-domain/integrability properties. On any fixed ball of radius $r$ in a retained compact, $T_{n}$ is eventually exactly Euclidean, since its injectivity radius is $L_{n}/2$. Lifted coordinate functions $y^{i}$ are harmonic. #### 8. Admission boundary and falsifiers

Construction F.10.12i.5 discharges the explicit dense-radius graph metric, calibrated product volume, graph/interpolant common Mosco limit, candidate Cheeger identification, flat global $\mathrm{BE}(0,4)$, same-identification integrated heat/$\Gamma$ passage, and quantitative harmonic-chart input for the declared completion-work representative. Mathematical falsifiers are failure of (1), (2), the weak liminf (4), or use of heat/metric identifications other than the declared cells.

<a id="construction-f1012i9-strict-collar-split-property-of-the-actual-product-source"></a>**Construction F.10.12i.9 (Strict-Collar Split Property of the Actual Product Source).**

For open Cauchy bases C1,C2 with closure(C1) contained in C2, D’Antoni and Hollands (2006, Theorem V.1 and the following even-observable remark) gives a type-I factor $N_{D}$ between the represented inner and outer local algebras. The theorem applies to every quasifree Hadamard state on a globally hyperbolic spin spacetime, so the source-constructed vacuum and the stated smooth finite-prefix extensions meet its state/geometric assumptions.

At cover stage $n$ choose the relevant concentric Cauchy bases with positive collar $\eta_n/8$. This is strictly positive at every finite stage. No uniform positive collar, uniform nuclear index as the collar collapses, or paid physical execution of an abstract split unitary is inferred.

#### Actual product extension

Let I1 be the set of registered point ports in the inner region and I2 those in the outer region, so I1 is a subset of I2. Write $H_{I}$ for the finite tensor product of their actual physical M2 register Hilbert spaces. In the common physical product representation, the inclusions are

$$
\begin{aligned}
&A_D(O_1) \otimes B(H_{I_1}) \otimes I_{I_2\setminus I_1} \\
&\quad \subset N_D \otimes B(H_{I_2}) \\
&\quad \subset A_D(O_2) \otimes B(H_{I_2}).
\end{aligned}
$$

The middle algebra is type I: if $N_{D}$ is spatially $B(K)\otimes I_{L}$, its tensor product with $B(H_{I_2})$ is $B(K\otimes H_{I_2})\otimes I_{L}$. The first inclusion uses identities on the actual additional outer-port factors, and the second is the field split inclusion tensored with those same retained factors. Outside port factors carry their identities throughout. Thus no source factor or response is erased.

The actual prepared state is the already constructed field state tensored with its specified independent material reference; all such factors and their source resources are retained. The factor assertion is representation-theoretic, independent of pretending that a finite grid already has type-III singularities. For the selected finite port algebra alone, the finite type-I property is immediate. The above inclusion additionally supplies the full field-plus-selected-port collar property claimed by the joined branch.

This exact local property occupies the split slot with zero property defect on each admitted strict collar. The separate finite source comparison errors remain their already registered nonzero norm/Gram/input defects. It supplies no sharp-overlap conditional expectation and does not contradict the earlier scoped sharp modular-invariance obstructions.

<a id="construction-f1012i10-paid-cq-coding-and-the-exact-capacity-differential"></a>**Construction F.10.12i.10 (Paid CQ Coding and the Exact Capacity Differential).**

#### 1. The actual channel and its capacity

At one incoming material port prepare either of the actual pure states

$$
\psi_x(r)=\sqrt{1-r}\,|0\rangle+x\sqrt{r}\,|1\rangle,\quad x\in\{+1,-1\},\quad 0<r<1/2.
$$

The complete registered channel is this fixed classical-input encoder $x\to\psi_x(r)$, followed by the two owned SWAP captures. The unrestricted identity quantum wire alone has classical capacity $\log 2$; $h(r)$ below is the capacity of the specified cq input domain. The captures deliver precisely the encoded state to $B$, retaining the spent input/$C$ states and all work resources. Every M2 output observable remains available; the source input-domain restriction is not a quotient of its response algebra. Under the fair prior the $B$ average is $\tau_r=\operatorname{diag}(1-r,r)$ and each conditional entropy is zero. Hence its Holevo information is $h(r)=-r\log r-(1-r)\log(1-r)$. Any other prior changes only the off-diagonal average; dephasing increases entropy to $h(r)$. Thus the fair prior maximizes the Holevo quantity.

The memoryless cq coding theorem identifies this maximum with the asymptotic reliable classical capacity per channel use. It does not identify it with one-use accessible information. Primary sources are Hausladen et al. (1996) and Holevo (1998). The following specialized finite bound supplies an explicit execution approximation rather than appealing only to an asymptotic name.

#### 2. Finite block, code and decoder

Fix $r$, a block size $b$, and $0<\epsilon<h(r)/2$. Write $\ell(r)=\log((1-r)/r)$. Let $P$ be the spectral projector of $\tau_r^{\otimes b}$ onto eigenvalues whose negative log divided by $b$ lies within $\epsilon$ of $h(r)$. The discarded probability $\eta$ satisfies

$$
\eta \le 2\exp[-2b\,\epsilon^2/\ell(r)^2].
\tag{C1}
$$

Indeed the computational-basis number K is Binomial(b,r), and that negative log equals `-log(1-r)+(K/b)ell(r)`. The usual exponential-moment proof of the Bernoulli Hoeffding bound gives C1. Also

$$
P\tau_r^{\otimes b} P \le \exp[-b(h(r)-\epsilon)]\,P.
\tag{C2}
$$

Choose $M$ independent fair sign strings of length $b$ as a random codebook. For codeword $m$ let its normalized tensor-product signal be $\psi_{m}$, put $\phi_m=P\psi_m$, $S_m=|\phi_m\rangle\langle\phi_m|$, $G=\sum_m S_m$, and use the square-root POVM $\Lambda_m=G^{-1/2}S_mG^{-1/2}$, with inverse zero on the kernel and an additional failure effect $I-\sum_m\Lambda_m$. Every codeword has the same computational-basis probabilities, so $q_m=\langle\psi_m|P|\psi_m\rangle=1-\eta$.

For $0\le S\le I$, $T\ge 0$, the Hayashi-Nagaoka inequality at parameter 1 is

$$
I-(S+T)^{-1/2} S(S+T)^{-1/2} \le 2(I-S)+4T.
$$

Its exact domain, generalized-inverse convention and proof are Lemma 2, equation 15 of Hayashi and Nagaoka (2002). Apply it with $S=S_m$ and $T=\sum_{l\ne m}S_l$ to the original normalized signal $\psi_{m}$. Since

$$
1-\langle\psi_m|S_m|\psi_m\rangle=1-q_m^2\le 2\eta,
$$

the first term contributes at most $4\eta$. Conditional on $\psi_{m}$, averaging a distinct independent codeword gives $\mathbb{E}\,S_l=P\tau_r^{\otimes b}P$; C2 bounds its cross term by $\exp[-b(h-\epsilon)]$. Therefore the average over random codebooks of their average decoding error obeys

$$
\mathbb{E}\,P_{\mathrm{error}} \le 4\eta+4(M-1)\exp[-b(h-\epsilon)].
$$

For $M\le\exp[b(h-2\epsilon)]$, at least one finite codebook satisfies

$$
P_{\mathrm{error}} \le 8\exp[-2b\,\epsilon^2/\ell(r)^2]+4\exp[-b\,\epsilon].
\tag{C3}
$$

This uses the conservative coefficient 8 because the PGM is evaluated on the original signals. No unproved projector-first disturbance improvement is used. A strictly padded bound permits finite exhaustive codebook selection with certified matrix arithmetic; efficiency is not claimed. The chosen finite POVM has a finite Naimark realization. It is executed on the actually captured b outputs in their common future using the paid finite ancillary registers, routing and unitary controls. Approximate compiled instruments add their explicitly bounded effect errors to C3.

For example, choose $\epsilon_b=b^{-1/4}$ once below $h(r)/2$ and $M_b=\lfloor\exp[b(h(r)-2\epsilon_b)]\rfloor$. Then the reliable rate tends to $h(r)$, while both terms in C3 vanish. Uniform bounds on a fixed compact $r$-interval within $(0,1/2)$ use its finite maximum $\ell(r)$. They prove uniform values, not convergence of derivatives of discrete finite-code rates.

For completeness, the converse requires no product average for a chosen codebook. Each output marginal has occupation $r$, so its entropy is at most $h(r)$. Entropy subadditivity and the Holevo measurement bound give $I(\text{message}:\text{readout})\le b\,h(r)$. Fano's inequality then bounds every asymptotically reliable rate by $h(r)$.

#### 2. Exact nonzero thermal differential on one common algebra

The bound follows from the displayed explicit formulas: $\lambda$ is bounded above and below by positive $p$-dependent multiples of $1-k$, and $\lambda'$ is $O(1-k)$. <a id="construction-f1012i12-proper-time-material-action-and-actual-incoming-boost-flux"></a>**Construction F.10.12i.12 (Proper-Time Material Action and Actual Incoming Boost Flux).**

Units in the proof are $c=1$; $\hbar$ and $k_{B}$ are retained. The rest energy $m$ is positive and fixed; restoring units replaces $m$ by $mc^{2}$ where it is added to an internal energy.

#### 1. A real source path crossing a fixed horizon

In Minkowski coordinates (t,x,y), $x>0$, take

It crosses the fixed past-horizon patch once at $(-\rho,\rho,y_0)$. At $t=0$ it meets the uniformly accelerated receiver at its instant of rest. From that event onward it follows the same accelerated orbit as the receiver:

$$
\gamma_{\mathrm{rec}}(t)=(t,\sqrt{\rho^{2}+t^{2}},y_0)\quad\text{for } t\ge 0.

This path is C¹, piecewise smooth, and timelike; its velocity is continuous at the join. Its acceleration has a finite jump, not an impulsive momentum jump. The incoming carrier is a material finite internal system, not a compact positive-frequency one-particle field state.

<a id="construction-f1012i13c-boundary-tangent-regional-core-obstruction-and-retained-core-comparison"></a>**Construction F.10.12i.13c (Boundary-Tangent Regional-Core Obstruction and Retained-Core Comparison).**

<a id="construction-f1012i16-finite-conditional-descent-calculus-and-soundness"></a>**Construction F.10.12i.16 (Finite Conditional Descent Calculus and Soundness).**

#### 1. Exact result and trust boundary

The finite PC1 record in Construction F.10.12i.18 instantiates the fourteen inference schemas below. Its proposition is conditional on the eight explicitly printed semantic premises. The relative soundness proof establishes the selected-protocol conclusion in every model satisfying those premises. Source-specific component theorems and physical realization are supplied separately by Constructions F.10.12i.15/17 on their actual domains.

This is a small macro-rule calculus, rather than Lean, HOL, ZFC proof terms, or a general theorem prover. Its trusted mathematical rules are specified and proved below. A checked proof is a finite topologically ordered list of these rules with exact witnesses. The finite checker checks rule application, not these mathematical metaproofs. As with any calculus, trust in its inference-rule soundness is distinct from checking a proof string. There is no `accept_F20`, arbitrary proposition oracle, numerical approximation acceptance, floating-point transcendental comparison, or inference from a file hash.

An overly permissive interpretation would say “all source hypotheses are assumptions, therefore the selected-protocol KMS descent is proved.” That interpretation is explicitly rejected. F.10.12b requests acceptance-active finite records and proofs. The conditional proof is useful and genuinely checked, but does not discharge those source hypotheses.

##### Language and semantics

A record is a finite JSON tree. Integers, rational pairs, finite integer-offset lists, exact polynomial terms, and the enumerated parameter names are its only witness data. The checker accepts exactly the schema and premise names listed in `SCHEMAS`. The fixed parameter binders are universal: $0<p<1/2$; positive $k_B,T,\hbar$; a finite positive integer $N$; finite nonnegative $C_{\mathrm{reg}},C_{\mathrm{geom}},C_{\mathrm{heat}},C_{\mathrm{input}}$; $0<u_\star\le 1/8$. Set $\ell=\log((1-p)/p)>0$ and $g=k_BT\ell>0$. Statements concern every real time, every integer $n\ge 1$ and every finite subset of the $N$ declared ports. Regions use the actual geometric membership map, not independent algebra copies.

All eight assumptions are printed verbatim in Construction F.10.12i.18. They are fixed premises of this conditional instance. They are hypotheses, not proved axioms of the physical world. Semantic validity means: in every ordinary complex C*-algebra/real-analysis model satisfying those hypotheses, all accepted conclusions hold. This provides a precise relative soundness claim.

The checker is not intended to recognize every valid KMS-descent record. Hardcoded, narrowly proved schemas are legitimate inference rules; narrowness is incompleteness, not unsoundness. New schemas require new soundness proofs and a new system version. The rational geometric-envelope schema and its polynomial recurrence check are independently reusable. This calculus does not provide a proof-producing registry of an actual external corpus, or an actual dependency graph.

#### 2. Termination

A JSON input is a finite string. Parsing terminates or fails. The checker requires exactly 14 steps. Each recognized step performs finite dictionary/list comparisons, a fixed $5^4$ lattice enumeration, or finite polynomial arithmetic over arbitrary-precision integers/rationals. No test calls external programs, imports external code, searches for a proof, evaluates a user formula, loops over physical time, loops over all $n$, or enumerates a continuum spectrum. Polynomial multiplication has finitely many monomial pairs. Thus each finite well-formed input terminates, subject to ordinary machine resources; malformed inputs fail. This is the conventional computability notion of a terminating proof checker, not a denial of finite-memory limits or malicious-input resource exhaustion.

#### 3. Sound inference schemas

##### R1. Lattice star and refinement

For $h_n=h_0\cdot 16^{-n}$, a crossing on the initial lattice lies on every finer lattice. A center with integer offset $k$ contains that crossing exactly when $|k_0|+\sqrt{k_1^{2}+k_2^{2}+k_3^{2}}<2$. This forces each coordinate into $\{-1,0,1\}$. For $k_0=0$ there are 27 spatial offsets; for $|k_0|=1$ only the zero spatial offset works. The checker enumerates this with the exact equivalent inequality $\sum\text{spatial squares}<(2-|k_0|)^{2}$ and checks 29 entries.

Every point has a nearest center at diamond distance at most $(1+\sqrt{3})h_n/2<2h_n$, so these diamonds cover wherever the declared finite center list includes the requisite centers. A fine radius is $2h_{n+1}=h_n/8$. The nearest coarse-center bound plus this radius is less than $2h_n$. For a coarse chart containing a port the minimum port margin is $(2-\sqrt{3})h_n$, and $h_n/8$ is smaller, since $3<(15/8)^{2}$. Thus the centered fine child lies in each containing parent and retains the same port. Convex intersections are contractible. Diameters tend to zero. Finite center lists and separated ports are source-data hypotheses, not inferred from this arithmetic.

##### R2. Tensor regions

For each region $U$, $P(U)=\bigotimes_{a\in J(U)}M_2(A_a)$, included by identities into $T=\bigotimes_{a=1}^N M_2(A_a)$. Matrix units give unital injective *-homomorphisms. Let every retained regional stage be $P(U)$, with comparison identity. Compatibility $\sup_{m\ge n}\lVert x_m-x_n\rVert\to 0$ is precisely the norm-Cauchy condition. For a bit string $x$ on a regional set of size $d$, write $m(x)$ for its occupation number and $\rho_x=(1-p)^{d-m(x)}p^{m(x)}$. On each matrix unit $E_{xy}$,

It does NOT prove the source component premises to which this bound is applied.

R11 and the explicitly typed physical input premise give $W_n\le N g[(A+Bn)4^{-n}+C_{\mathrm{input}}\exp(-4^n)]$. The same exact rule applies with $D_w=N g(A+C_{\mathrm{input}})$, $E_w=N gB$. Its closed tail is $q^n[4(D_w+E_w n)+12E_w]$. These carry energy units, unlike R12. $N$ and $g$ are fixed finite constants, so the tail vanishes. This supplies the required weighted accumulation theorem conditional on the stated physical input bound, without confusing max-defect decay with weighted decay.

##### R14. Conjunction/output rule

This rule introduces only the conjunction of R3,R5,R6,R7,R10,R12,R13 plus their standing source assumptions. It labels their declared finite-protocol scope as the conditional F.10.12a-c output. <a id="theorem-f1012g-finite-cosmological-constant-descent-and-quantitative-rigidity"></a>**Theorem F.10.12g (Finite Cosmological-Constant Descent and Quantitative Rigidity).** Let the retained cover nerve at level $n$ be a connected finite graph with oriented incidence matrix $B_n$, graph Laplacian $L_n=B_n^TB_n$, and spectral gap $\lambda_2(L_n)>0$. Let $\Lambda_n\in\mathbb R^{N_n}$ collect the local cosmological integration constants inferred from the cellwise Einstein-response equations, and let
$$
d_n=B_n\Lambda_n,
\qquad
\bar\Lambda_n=\frac1{N_n}\mathbf1^T\Lambda_n.
\tag{F.10.12g.1}
$$
Then
$$
\lVert\Lambda_n-\bar\Lambda_n\mathbf1\rVert_2
\le
\lambda_2(L_n)^{-1/2}\lVert d_n\rVert_2.
\tag{F.10.12g.2}
$$
In particular, exact overlap descent $d_n=0$ forces one constant on the connected cover. If $\lVert d_n\rVert_2/\sqrt{\lambda_2(L_n)}\to0$ along refinement, the local constants converge in the retained $\ell^2$ quotient to their global mean.

If the local residual is written
$$
E^{(i)}_{\mu\nu}=G_{\mu\nu}+\Lambda_i g_{\mu\nu}-8\pi G T_{\mu\nu},
$$
with common overlap conventions, then in four dimensions
$$
\Lambda_j-\Lambda_i
=
\frac14g^{\mu\nu}\bigl(E^{(j)}_{\mu\nu}-E^{(i)}_{\mu\nu}\bigr).
\tag{F.10.12g.3}
$$
Every exact edge defect $d_n=B_n\Lambda_n$ has zero oriented sum around each nerve cycle; conversely, on a connected graph, zero cycle sums are exactly the integrability condition for an edge assignment to be of this form.

*Proof.* The vector $x=\Lambda_n-\bar\Lambda_n\mathbf1$ is orthogonal to the kernel of the connected graph Laplacian. Therefore
$$
\lVert B_n\Lambda_n\rVert_2^2
=x^TL_nx
\ge\lambda_2(L_n)\lVert x\rVert_2^2,
$$
which proves (F.10.12g.2). Equation (F.10.12g.3) follows by subtracting the two overlap residuals and tracing $g_{\mu\nu}$, whose trace is four. The cycle statement is the finite exact-one-form criterion: incidence gradients have zero circulation, and a zero-circulation edge field can be integrated from one root vertex independently of path. ∎

<a id="corollary-f1012g1-localglobal-cosmological-split-and-exact-mean-nonselection"></a>**Corollary F.10.12g.1 (Local/Global Cosmological Split and Exact Mean Nonselection).** Theorems X.4b and F.10.12g together show that local horizon thermodynamics determines the Einstein response up to one global constant response class and that finite descent controls only the consistency of its local representatives. More strongly, no deterministic selector that factors only through the descent record $d_n=B_n\Lambda_n$ can determine the global mean $\bar\Lambda_n$.

*Proof.* Theorem X.4b leaves one cosmological integration constant in each local Einstein-response representative. Theorem F.10.12g controls the edge differences $d_n=B_n\Lambda_n$. Because the cover graph is connected,
$$
\ker B_n=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\},
\qquad
B_n(\Lambda_n+c\mathbf1)=B_n\Lambda_n.
\tag{F.10.12g.1.1}
$$
Any selector factoring through $d_n$ therefore has the same value on the entire common-shift orbit, while $\overline{\Lambda_n+c\mathbf1}=\bar\Lambda_n+c$. It cannot equal the mean on more than one member of that orbit. The exact three-vertex path witness
$$
\Lambda=(0,1,3),
\qquad
\Lambda'=(5,6,8)
\tag{F.10.12g.1.2}
$$
has the same oriented edge differences $(1,2)$ and distinct means $4/3$ and $19/3$. Thus finite descent determines representatives only modulo their common mean. An independent global boundary or normalization law is necessary to select one orbit representative. ∎

// PU-F10.12h-SOURCE-BEGIN
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const VERSION = "F.10.12h-finite-global-obstruction-audit-v1";

function invariant(condition, message) {
  if (!condition) throw new Error(message);
}

function sha256(bytes) {
  return createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
}

// Exact Gaussian-integer arithmetic for the doubled GKLS generator.
const z = (re = 0n, im = 0n) => [BigInt(re), BigInt(im)];
const zadd = (a, b) => [a[0] + b[0], a[1] + b[1]];
const zsub = (a, b) => [a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1]];
const zmul = (a, b) => [a[0] * b[0] - a[1] * b[1], a[0] * b[1] + a[1] * b[0]];
const zconj = (a) => [a[0], -a[1]];
const zeq = (a, b) => a[0] === b[0] && a[1] === b[1];

function zeroMatrix(n) {
  return Array.from({ length: n }, () => Array.from({ length: n }, () => z()));
}

function identity(n) {
  const out = zeroMatrix(n);
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i += 1) out[i][i] = z(1n);
  return out;
}

function madd(a, b) {
  return a.map((row, i) => row.map((value, j) => zadd(value, b[i][j])));
}

function msub(a, b) {
  return a.map((row, i) => row.map((value, j) => zsub(value, b[i][j])));
}

function mscale(a, scalar) {
  return a.map((row) => row.map((value) => zmul(scalar, value)));
}

function mmul(a, b) {
  const out = zeroMatrix(a.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i += 1) {
    for (let j = 0; j < b.length; j += 1) {
      for (let k = 0; k < b.length; k += 1) out[i][j] = zadd(out[i][j], zmul(a[i][k], b[k][j]));
    }
  }
  return out;
}

function dagger(a) {
  return a.map((_, i) => a.map((row) => zconj(row[i])));
}

function meq(a, b) {
  return a.every((row, i) => row.every((value, j) => zeq(value, b[i][j])));
}

function doubledGKLS(H, L, rho) {
  const commutator = msub(mmul(H, rho), mmul(rho, H));
  const LdL = mmul(dagger(L), L);
  return madd(
    mscale(commutator, z(0n, -2n)),
    msub(mscale(mmul(mmul(L, rho), dagger(L)), z(2n)), madd(mmul(LdL, rho), mmul(rho, LdL))),
  );
}

function matrixUnit(i, j) {
  const out = zeroMatrix(2);
  out[i][j] = z(1n);
  return out;
}

function gklsAudit() {
  const I = identity(2);
  const X = [[z(), z(1n)], [z(1n), z()]];
  const H0 = zeroMatrix(2);
  const L0 = X;
  const H1 = mscale(X, z(-1n));
  const L1 = madd(X, mscale(I, z(0n, 1n)));
  const wrongH = X;
  const basis = [matrixUnit(0, 0), matrixUnit(0, 1), matrixUnit(1, 0), matrixUnit(1, 1)];
  const exact = basis.every((rho) => meq(doubledGKLS(H0, L0, rho), doubledGKLS(H1, L1, rho)));
  const mutationRejected = basis.some((rho) => !meq(doubledGKLS(H0, L0, rho), doubledGKLS(wrongH, L1, rho)));
  invariant(exact, "GKLS gauge-equivalent decompositions differ");
  invariant(mutationRejected, "GKLS Hamiltonian-sign mutation was not rejected");
  return { basis_checks: basis.length, hamiltonians_equal: meq(H0, H1), mutation_rejected: mutationRejected };
}

function kron(a, b) {
  const out = zeroMatrix(a.length * b.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i += 1) for (let j = 0; j < a.length; j += 1) {
    for (let k = 0; k < b.length; k += 1) for (let l = 0; l < b.length; l += 1) {
      out[i * b.length + k][j * b.length + l] = zmul(a[i][j], b[k][l]);
    }
  }
  return out;
}

function frobeniusSquared(a) {
  let total = 0n;
  for (const row of a) for (const value of row) total += value[0] * value[0] + value[1] * value[1];
  return total;
}

function colimitAudit() {
  const I2 = identity(2);
  const x = [[z(1n), z()], [z(), z(-1n)]];
  const representedWord = msub(kron(x, I2), kron(I2, x));
  const ambientImage = msub(x, x);
  const witnessNormSquared = frobeniusSquared(representedWord);
  invariant(witnessNormSquared === 8n, "free-product witness vanished");
  invariant(frobeniusSquared(ambientImage) === 0n, "comparison image is nonzero");
  return { ambient_image_norm_squared: "0", witness_norm_squared: witnessNormSquared.toString() };
}

// Permutations use compose(a,b)=a after b.
const pid = [0, 1, 2];
const peq = (a, b) => a.every((value, i) => value === b[i]);
const pcompose = (a, b) => b.map((value) => a[value]);
function pinverse(a) {
  const out = Array(a.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i += 1) out[a[i]] = i;
  return out;
}

function solveHolonomy(vertices, edges) {
  const incident = new Map(vertices.map((vertex) => [vertex, []]));
  for (const edge of edges) {
    incident.get(edge.src).push({ dst: edge.dst, g: edge.g });
    incident.get(edge.dst).push({ dst: edge.src, g: pinverse(edge.g) });
  }
  const h = new Map([[vertices[0], pid]]);
  const queue = [vertices[0]];
  while (queue.length > 0) {
    const src = queue.shift();
    for (const edge of incident.get(src)) {
      const candidate = pcompose(edge.g, h.get(src));
      if (!h.has(edge.dst)) {
        h.set(edge.dst, candidate);
        queue.push(edge.dst);
      } else if (!peq(h.get(edge.dst), candidate)) {
        return { accepted: false, vertices_reached: h.size };
      }
    }
  }
  return { accepted: h.size === vertices.length, vertices_reached: h.size };
}

function holonomyAudit() {
  const swap01 = [1, 0, 2];
  const swap12 = [0, 2, 1];
  const flat02 = pcompose(swap12, swap01);
  const flat = solveHolonomy([0, 1, 2], [
    { src: 0, dst: 1, g: swap01 },
    { src: 1, dst: 2, g: swap12 },
    { src: 0, dst: 2, g: flat02 },
  ]);
  const obstructed = solveHolonomy([0, 1, 2], [
    { src: 0, dst: 1, g: swap01 },
    { src: 1, dst: 2, g: swap12 },
    { src: 0, dst: 2, g: pid },
  ]);
  invariant(flat.accepted, "flat S3 triangle rejected");
  invariant(!obstructed.accepted, "nontrivial S3 holonomy accepted");
  return { flat_triangle: "PASS", obstructed_triangle: "REJECT" };
}

function matVec(a, x) {
  return a.map((row) => row.reduce((sum, value, index) => sum + value * x[index], 0));
}

function difference(x) {
  return [x[1] - x[0], x[2] - x[1]];
}

function meanAudit() {
  const laplacian = [[1, -1, 0], [-1, 2, -1], [0, -1, 1]];
  const ones = [1, 1, 1];
  const lambda = [0, 1, 3];
  const shifted = [5, 6, 8];
  invariant(matVec(laplacian, ones).every((value) => value === 0), "constant mode is not null");
  invariant(JSON.stringify(difference(lambda)) === JSON.stringify(difference(shifted)), "shift changed descent data");
  invariant(lambda.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) !== shifted.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0), "shift did not change mean");
  const principalMinor = laplacian[0][0] * laplacian[1][1] - laplacian[0][1] * laplacian[1][0];
  invariant(principalMinor === 1, "connected Laplacian rank certificate failed");
  return { constant_kernel_dimension: 1, edge_differences: difference(lambda), mean_numerators: [4, 19], mean_denominator: 3 };
}

function canonical(value) {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return `[${value.map(canonical).join(",")}]`;
  if (value && typeof value === "object") return `{${Object.keys(value).sort().map((key) => `${JSON.stringify(key)}:${canonical(value[key])}`).join(",")}}`;
  return JSON.stringify(value);
}

function main() {
  const source = readFileSync(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
  const result = {
    checks: 4,
    colimit: colimitAudit(),
    fixtures_passed: 4,
    gkls: gklsAudit(),
    holonomy: holonomyAudit(),
    mean_descent: meanAudit(),
    node: process.version,
    result: "PASS",
    runtime_sha256: sha256(readFileSync(process.execPath)),
    source_sha256: sha256(source),
    version: VERSION,
  };
  process.stdout.write(`${canonical(result)}\n`);
}

try {
  main();
} catch (error) {
  process.stderr.write(`${VERSION} FAIL: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}\n`);
  process.exitCode = 1;
}

<a id="theorem-f1012l-finite-overlap-classification-and-physical-reset-coefficients"></a>**Theorem F.10.12l (Finite Overlap Classification and Physical Reset Coefficients).** Let $V$ be a finite set of sites with nontrivial matrix factors $\mathcal A_x=B(\mathcal H_x)$, and let $I_1,\ldots,I_m$ cover $V$. For every nonempty membership set $b\subset\{1,\ldots,m\}$ define the nonempty atoms
$$

\tag{F.10.12l.1}
$$
Atoms may contain several sites. For faithful densities $\rho_i$ on $\mathcal A(I_i)$, the modular group $\operatorname{Ad}\rho_i^{it}$ preserves every pair overlap for all $t\in\mathbb R$ if and only if
$$
 \rho_i=\bigotimes_{b\ni i}\rho_{i,b}.
\tag{F.10.12l.2}
$$
If all pair-overlap restrictions agree, $\rho_{i,b}$ is independent of $i\in b$, and the regional states are exactly the restrictions of the faithful global state $\rho=\bigotimes_b\rho_b$. Arbitrary entanglement within an atom is allowed.
