\tag{F.10.12l.5a}
$$
The ordered triple identity follows by adjacent inverse cancellations; no density matrices are commuted past one another. The nonidentity $u_{ij}$ and the restriction homomorphisms are therefore realized on genuine common tensor factors. When the starting overlap densities differ, these starting regional states are not a state-compatible global family. This is a diagnostic of noncommuting order and the implementer maps, not the compatible-state branch used in the product and refinement assertions.

**A $d$-level channel with the same entropy differential.** For any faithful $d$-level reference $\tau=\sum_jp_j|e_j\rangle\langle e_j|$, use the specified memoryless cq channel
$$
 k\longmapsto|\psi_k\rangle=\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}\sqrt{p_j}\,e^{2\pi ijk/d}|e_j\rangle,
 \qquad k=0,\ldots,d-1.
\tag{F.10.12l.6}
$$
Every mixture has diagonal $p$, so pinching bounds its entropy by $H(p)$. The uniform input attains average $\tau$, and all signal states are pure. The finite-alphabet cq coding theorem therefore gives asymptotic reliable classical capacity $S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\tau)$ nats per use (Holevo 1998). For parallel channels every tensor-word signal has fixed diagonal $\bigotimes_ap_a$; arbitrary classical correlations among the input words cannot increase its entropy beyond $\sum_aH(p_a)$, and independent uniform inputs attain that sum. Thus the one-cut parallel min-cut capacity is additive.

On a declared smooth noncrossing spectral chart for $\tau(\theta)$, the encoder family retains its actual eigenframe variations. At a fixed reference $\tau_0$, the capacity differential in physical entropy units is
$$
 dS_{\mathrm{cap}}[X]=k_B\operatorname{Tr}[(-\log\tau_0)X],\qquad\operatorname{Tr}X=0.
\tag{F.10.12l.7}
$$
Feed this output into the same fixed paid reset of Corollary E.9.5h.1 at $\tau_0$. Its bath-export differential is $dQ=T\,dS_{\mathrm{cap}}$, including coherent tangents; its finite relative-tangent defect is bounded by Corollary E.9.5h.2. This uses the channel's asymptotic coding capacity, not a finite-block zero-error decoder or a derivative of a discrete optimized code rate. Signal preparation, label storage/reset, retained purifiers and any executed decoder have their actual separate physical resource entries. It does not identify reset export with an incoming geometric boost flux.

**Full finite coefficient complex.** At each atom retain a finite real space $V_a$ of centered Hermitian modular recalibrations with its positive BKM inner product as in Definition F.10.12e, and a finite trace-zero tangent space $T_a$. Let $L_a\subset T_a^*$ be the actual span of reset heat and channel-entropy differentials. This space is nonzero for the nontracial binary example of Corollary E.9.5h.2. No response-null space is discarded here. On the membership simplex $b(a)$ use
$$
 C^0_{\mathrm{mod},a}=\bigoplus_{i\in b(a)}V_a,\quad
 C^1_{\mathrm{mod},a}=\bigoplus_{i<j\in b(a)}V_a,\quad
 C^2_{\mathrm{mod},a}=\bigoplus_{i<j<k\in b(a)}V_a,
$$
$$
 C^1_{\mathrm{th},a}=\bigoplus_{i\in b(a)}L_a,\qquad
 C^2_{\mathrm{th},a}=\bigoplus_{i<j\in b(a)}L_a.
\tag{F.10.12l.8}
$$
Take direct sums over atoms, the actual tensor-factor restriction maps, signed simplex differences $\delta$, and registered positive thermal inner-product weights. Define
$$
 D^0b=(\delta b,0),\qquad D^1(\Theta,\chi)=(\delta\Theta,\delta\chi).
\tag{F.10.12l.9}
$$
The full block identity $D^1D^0=0$ includes all thermal coordinates. In the coherent product/reset experiment the actual modular mismatch and reference first-law mismatch are both zero; thus every exact, coexact and harmonic part of its obstruction is zero. The modular degree-one cohomology of a simplex vanishes. The thermal harmonic subspace survives: $\delta\chi=0$ means equal copies of one functional in $L_a$, and $D^0$ has no thermal image. Hence it is isomorphic to $L_a$ and detects a nonzero common heat–entropy mismatch. A modular recalibration cannot erase that direction. The particular higher-dimensional construction of F.10.12i.13 is consistent with this general coefficient calculation.

These are finite tensor-algebra and paid-reset results. They do not replace the independent physical reference, clock, flux and regularity premises in F.10.12a–c by an algebraic zero obstruction. $\square$

<a id="theorem-f1012m-product-car-descent-and-the-shrinking-cell-hadamard-obstruction"></a>**Theorem F.10.12m (Product-CAR Descent and the Shrinking-Cell Hadamard Obstruction).** Let $\mathcal K=L^2(\mathbb R^3,\mathbb C^4)$ be the massless Dirac Cauchy space and
$$
 Q=1_{(-\infty,0)}(-i\alpha\cdot\nabla),\qquad
 q(k)=\frac{I-\alpha\cdot k/|k|}{2}.
\tag{F.10.12m.1}
$$
For $0<p<1$, the gauge-invariant quasifree state with covariance $C=pI$ preserves every spatial CAR inclusion and overlap under its modular action. With $c$ the annihilation convention and occupation $p$,
$$
 \sigma_t(c(f))=e^{it\log((1-p)/p)}c(f),\qquad
 \sigma_t(c^*(f))=e^{it\log(p/(1-p))}c^*(f).
\tag{F.10.12m.2}
$$
The full even algebra is retained; its pair-creation operators have nontrivial modular action when $p\ne1/2$.

**Exact finite comparison.** On nested dyadic spatial step-function spaces retain all four spin components, and use coherently exhausting bounded cubes. Their union is dense in $\mathcal K$. Each cell has four CAR modes and a $16$-dimensional local matrix representation. A normalized coarse-cell function maps to the isometric sum of its normalized children, with coefficient $\sqrt{|C_{\mathrm{child}}|/|C_{\mathrm{parent}}|}$ for each child. The CAR embeddings are therefore unital and isometric, not maps that keep only one child. For a regular open region use cells with closures inside it; these subspaces are nested and dense in its $L^2$ space. Their intersections are the actual cell intersections.

The covariance $pI$ restricts exactly at each stage. The finite product density is the tensor product of single-mode $\operatorname{diag}(1-p,p)$, whose density powers give (F.10.12m.2). Those compatible actions agree on the dense local CAR cores; their quasifree GNS modular action has that same gauge formula. All state and modular comparison defects on these cores are zero. The norm inductive limit is the actual spatial CAR algebra. For $p<1/2$ the finite Gibbs gap is $k_BT\log((1-p)/p)$, and the paid reset of Theorem E.9.5h can be used on each actual finite register. This is an internal gauge clock, with no geometric boost identification.

**Failure of the Hadamard principal part.** On every nonempty open Cauchy region $O$, $pI-Q$ has no smooth distribution kernel. Choose $f\in C_c^\infty(O)$, a unit vector $e\in\mathbb R^3$, and a constant unit spinor $u$ with $\alpha\cdot e\,u=u$. Normalize $fu$ and put $f_L(x)=e^{iLe\cdot x}f(x)u$. Dominated convergence of the shifted Fourier multiplier gives
$$
 \langle f_L,Qf_L\rangle\longrightarrow0,\qquad
 \langle f_L,(pI-Q)f_L\rangle\longrightarrow p>0.
\tag{F.10.12m.3}
$$
If the localized difference had a smooth kernel, restriction to a compact set containing the support of $f$ would be Hilbert–Schmidt and compact. But $f_L\rightharpoonup0$, so its diagonal pairings with that compact operator would tend to zero, a contradiction. Two Dirac Hadamard two-point functions differ smoothly, also after restriction to a smooth spacelike Cauchy surface. Thus this product state is not locally Hadamard. No inference about divergent preparation cost is used.

**General shrinking even-product cells.** Let $\Omega$ be a bounded spatial region and $C_{a,n}$ disjoint measurable cells of maximum diameter $h_n\to0$, whose omitted collars have locally vanishing measure. Let $\omega_n$ be an even product state over their CAR algebras; within each cell it may be arbitrarily correlated and nonquasifree. Extend it by any state to $\operatorname{CAR}(L^2(\Omega,\mathbb C^4))$. If these states have a pointwise limit on that physical norm CAR algebra, its two-point covariance is a measurable matrix multiplication operator and cannot have the Dirac Hadamard form.

For smooth compact $f,g$ with positively separated supports, restrict them to the union of the cells. Vanishing collar measure makes these restrictions converge in $L^2$ to $f,g$, so the CAR operators converge in norm. For large $n$ no cell meets both supports. Evenness makes each cell's odd-field expectation zero; product factorization then gives $\omega_n(c^*(f_n)c(g_n))=0$. Passing to the norm-state limit gives the same zero for $f,g$.

The limiting covariance $0\le C\le I$ therefore has no off-support matrix elements. Approximation by compactly supported functions and regularity of Lebesgue measure imply that it preserves every measurable support subspace. It commutes with every scalar multiplication projection and hence is a measurable matrix multiplication operator $C(x)$. Apply the oscillatory argument above with $e$ and $-e$, keeping the same spinor $u$. The $C(x)$ pairing is independent of the oscillatory direction, whereas the $Q$ pairings tend to $0$ and $1$. A locally smoothing difference would have to be compact on the fixed compact support and make both differences tend to zero, which is impossible.

The argument includes infinite-dimensional split product cells when their physical smearings satisfy the stated norm approximation. It does not apply merely because some auxiliary tensor factors are type I: their actual regional comparison maps and the physical-smearing limit are required. Removing a cutoff at a fixed sharp normal Dirac cover instead falls under Theorem F.10.12n; moving comparisons and varying finite-cutoff data are not assigned either theorem's fixed-image hypotheses. $\square$

<a id="theorem-f1012n-all-normal-state-sharp-overlap-obstruction-for-the-dirac-net"></a>**Theorem F.10.12n (All-Normal-State Sharp-Overlap Obstruction for the Dirac Net).** Use the massless four-component Dirac vacuum net and ball diamonds of Theorem F.10.12k on one Cauchy hyperplane. Let $D_i,D_j$ be distinct with nonempty intersection. For at least one side $i$ there is no normal conditional expectation from $M_i$ onto either the actual geometric overlap algebra or the algebraic intersection $M_i\cap M_j$. This holds for the full field net and for the full parity-even observable net on the vacuum parity sector. Consequently no faithful normal replacement state on that side can make the specified overlap invariant under its modular group for all real times.

The conclusion transfers through a normal local isomorphism carrying these concrete inclusions. In particular it holds in the local folia of quasifree Hadamard Dirac representations. The replacement state within that folium may itself be nonquasifree, nonvacuum and arbitrarily energetic. Local normality, rather than a generic nonquasifree two-point Hadamard condition, is the stated representation premise.

**Part I. Expectations force a classical Bell state.** Suppose $N\subset M$ is unital and $\mathcal C\subset N'\cap M$. A normal conditional expectation $E:M\to N$ has, by bimodularity, $E(b)\in Z(N)$ for every $b\in\mathcal C$. For self-adjoint contractions $a_1,a_2\in N$, $b_1,b_2\in\mathcal C$, set
$$
 T=\frac{a_1(b_1+b_2)+a_2(b_1-b_2)}2,\qquad z_j=E(b_j).
\tag{F.10.12n.1}
$$
The $z_j$ are central commuting self-adjoint contractions, so
$$
 E(T)=\frac{a_1(z_1+z_2)+a_2(z_1-z_2)}2,\qquad
 |z_1+z_2|+|z_1-z_2|=2\max(|z_1|,|z_2|)\le2I.
$$
Central functional calculus gives $-I\le E(T)\le I$. Any normal state $\eta$ on $N$ therefore gives a normal state $\eta\circ E$ whose restriction to every joined pair $\mathcal A\vee\mathcal B$, with $\mathcal A\subset N$ and $\mathcal B\subset\mathcal C$, has normalized CHSH coefficient at most $1$. Neither $N$ nor $M$ was assumed to be a factor.

**Part II. The even Dirac tangent pair.** Theorem 5.1 of Summers and Werner (1988) states that tangent double-cone algebras have normalized CHSH coefficient $\sqrt2$ in every normal state on their joined algebra for a local irreducible positive-energy vacuum net on a separable Hilbert space with dilation covariance, locally generated wedges and wedge duality. Its definition of maximal correlation quantifies over all those normal states, not a dense subset.

Here these hypotheses hold for the full even Dirac net. Write $\mathcal F(O)$ for the field algebra, $\Gamma$ for parity, $\mathcal H_+$ for its even vacuum sector and
$$
 \mathcal A(O)=\mathcal F(O)^+|_{\mathcal H_+},\qquad
 \mathcal F(O)^+=\{x\in\mathcal F(O):\Gamma x\Gamma=x\}.
\tag{F.10.12n.2}
$$
This is the full even algebra, including pair creation. Graded field locality gives ordinary locality; vacuum covariance, positive energy, separability and uniqueness of the vacuum restrict to $\mathcal H_+$. Parity averaging of the field Reeh–Schlieder core gives $\overline{\mathcal F(O)^+\Omega}=\mathcal H_+$, and field separation gives separation there. Averaging the global strong closure $B(\mathcal H)$ under parity gives $B(\mathcal H_+)\oplus B(\mathcal H_-)$, so the compressed global even net is irreducible. Compact field supports inside a wedge lie in sufficiently large double cones within it; directed generation and normal parity averaging prove local generation of its even wedge algebra.

For $D=-i\alpha\cdot\nabla$, the Cauchy dilation
$$
 (u_\lambda f)(x)=\lambda^{-3/2}f(x/\lambda),\qquad
 u_\lambda^*Du_\lambda=\lambda^{-1}D
\tag{F.10.12n.3}
$$
commutes with $Q=1_{(-\infty,0)}(D)$. Its CAR action preserves the quasifree vacuum and has a strongly continuous vacuum-preserving implementation commuting with parity. It maps $O$ to $\lambda O$, supplying precisely dilation covariance.

The same-field twisted wedge duality of Theorem F.5a.2 is

$$
\mathcal F(W)'=Z\mathcal F(W')Z^*,
$$

$Z=(I+i\Gamma)/(1+i)$. To compute the compressed commutant, let $S,J,\Delta$ be the field Tomita objects. Parity fixes $\Omega$ and the wedge algebra, hence commutes with $S$ and its polar factors. With $P_+=(I+\Gamma)/2$,
$P_+\mathcal F(W)\Omega=\mathcal F(W)^+\Omega$ is a core for the restriction of $S$ to $\mathcal H_+$. The even modular conjugation is therefore $J_+=J|_{\mathcal H_+}$. Tomita commutation now gives
$$
 \mathcal A(W)'=J_+\mathcal A(W)J_+
 =\bigl(\mathcal F(W)'\cap\{\Gamma\}'\bigr)|_{\mathcal H_+}
 =\mathcal F(W')^+|_{\mathcal H_+}=\mathcal A(W').
\tag{F.10.12n.4}
$$
Conjugation by $Z$ is trivial on even operators. Thus wedge duality after compression is proved, rather than assumed from a possibly smaller field commutant. The tangent-pair Bell theorem applies.

**Part III. Actual overlap geometry and the field representation.** Let $B_i,B_j$ have centers $a_i,a_j$ and radii $R_i,R_j$. Choose side $i$ with $B_i\setminus\overline{B_j}\ne\varnothing$, and a crossing point $p\in\partial B_j\cap B_i$. Set
$$
 n=(p-a_j)/R_j,\qquad0<r<R_j,\qquad
 2r<\operatorname{dist}(p,B_i^c),\qquad
 B_-=B(p-rn,r),\quad B_+=B(p+rn,r).
\tag{F.10.12n.5}
$$
The balls lie on opposite sides of $\partial B_j$, their closures lie in $B_i$, and they touch only at $p$. Their diamonds $O_-,O_+$ are spacelike separated with tangent closures. Moreover $O_-\subset D_i\cap D_j$, and $O_+\subset D_i$ is spacelike separated from $D_j$. This follows directly from the center distances $R_j-r$ and $R_j+r$ and the strict open-ball inequalities.

For the even net, take $N$ to be either overlap algebra in the statement. Then $\mathcal A(O_-)\subset N$ and $\mathcal A(O_+)\subset N'\cap M_i$. PartI would produce a normal state on their joined algebra with Bell coefficient at most $1$, contradicting PartII.

For the full field net, use the even auxiliary algebras $\mathcal F(O_\pm)^+$. The even right algebra commutes with all of $\mathcal F(D_j)$, so it again lies in $N'\cap M_i$. Compression
$$
 \pi_+:\mathcal F(D_i)^+\longrightarrow\mathcal A(D_i)
\tag{F.10.12n.6}
$$
is a normal surjective $*$-homomorphism. It is faithful: $\pi_+(x)=0$ implies $x\Omega=0$, and vacuum separation for the containing field algebra gives $x=0$. Thus it is a normal von Neumann isomorphism with normal inverse, including on the joined auxiliary pair. A normal state on that pair in the full field representation therefore transfers to a normal state on the even-vacuum pair. The same Bell contradiction applies, without commuting odd fields across spacelike regions.

**Part IV. Modular and local-folium consequences.** The faithful-normal-state case of Takesaki's expectation theorem, already used in F.10.12k, turns two-sided modular invariance into a normal state-preserving expectation. The established absence of such an expectation gives the modular conclusion. Normal local isomorphisms preserve the containing algebra and its smaller concrete images. D’Antoni and Hollands (2006, Theorem III.1) supplies local quasiequivalence of quasifree Hadamard Dirac representations on every relatively compact region. The even conclusion follows by restriction to the parity-fixed algebra and the faithful compression above.

For a finite connected family of these diamonds, fixed-overlap two-sided modular invariance under faithful normal local states forces all intersecting diamonds to be identical. After merging duplicates its overlap graph has no edges; a connected union therefore has one distinct region. More generally, suppose a normal automorphism group $\beta_t$ on the concrete generated algebra $M_{\mathrm{desc}}$ preserves every $M_i$ and is the modular group of a faithful normal state $\Phi$. It preserves $M_i\cap M_j$ for both time signs. Its restriction to $M_i$ is the modular action of $\Phi|_{M_i}$, so it supplies a forbidden expectation on the offending side. The conclusion is unchanged if each restriction is written $\operatorname{Ad}v_i(t)\sigma_i^t$ for arbitrary local continuous normalized cocycles: overlap normalizers were not assumed. Separately supplied faithful normal local modular realizations suffice as well.

This concerns the fixed physical sharp images. A moving family $M_i(t)$ or an auxiliary atomic comparison algebra has different hypotheses. The selected finite protocol quotient in Construction F.10.12i.14 is not a normal expectation onto a full sharp Dirac algebra, and is not excluded by this theorem. No uniform approximate-modular defect bound for changing finite cutoffs, nonnormal limiting representation or full entropy/flux/resource conclusion is asserted. $\square$

<a id="theorem-f1012o-atomicity-of-normal-expected-subalgebras-and-split-cover-obstructions"></a>**Theorem F.10.12o (Atomicity of Normal Expected Subalgebras and Split-Cover Obstructions).** For a unital von Neumann subalgebra $N\subset B(\mathcal H)$, there is a normal conditional expectation $B(\mathcal H)\to N$ if and only if $N$ is atomic: every nonzero projection of $N$ dominates a minimal projection. Faithfulness of the expectation and separability of $\mathcal H$ are unnecessary. This is the normal-expectation characterization of Tomiyama 1959; the proof needed here is given in full.

**Necessity.** The net of finite-rank projections increases strongly to $I$. Normality and unitality imply that some rank-one $p=|\xi\rangle\langle\xi|$, $\|\xi\|=1$, has $a=E(p)\ne0$. For $x\ge0$ in $N$, apply the CP Schwarz inequality to $y=x^{1/2}p$. Bimodularity and $pxp=\langle\xi,x\xi\rangle p$ give
$$
 axa\le\langle\xi,x\xi\rangle a.
\tag{F.10.12o.1}
$$
Choose $\delta>0$ with nonzero spectral projection $e=1_{[\delta,\infty)}(a)$. For $x\ge0$ in $eNe$, compress and multiply by the bounded inverse of $a|_{e\mathcal H}$ to obtain
$$
 x\le\langle\xi,x\xi\rangle(a|_{e\mathcal H})^{-1}
 \le\delta^{-1}\langle\xi,x\xi\rangle e.
\tag{F.10.12o.2}
$$
Every nonzero projection $q\in eNe$ therefore satisfies $\langle\xi,q\xi\rangle\ge\delta$. An orthogonal family of such projections has at most $\lfloor1/\delta\rfloor$ members. Choose a family of maximum cardinality among those finite possibilities. Every member is minimal, since splitting a nonminimal member into two nonzero orthogonal projections would increase that cardinality. Thus $N$ has a minimal projection. Apply the same argument to every nonzero corner $q_0Nq_0$, using the restricted normal expectation $q_0B(\mathcal H)q_0=B(q_0\mathcal H)\to q_0Nq_0$. Each such corner has a minimal projection, also minimal in $N$. This is atomicity.

**Sufficiency.** Write the spatial atomic decomposition
$$
 \mathcal H=\bigoplus_\alpha(\mathcal K_\alpha\otimes\mathcal L_\alpha),\qquad
 N=\bigoplus_\alpha\bigl(B(\mathcal K_\alpha)\otimes I_{\mathcal L_\alpha}\bigr).
\tag{F.10.12o.3}
$$
For the central summand projections $p_\alpha$, choose any normal state $\varphi_\alpha$ on $B(\mathcal L_\alpha)$. Then
$$
 E(x)=\bigoplus_\alpha
 \left[(\operatorname{id}\otimes\varphi_\alpha)(p_\alpha xp_\alpha)
 \otimes I_{\mathcal L_\alpha}\right]
\tag{F.10.12o.4}
$$
is unital, normal, CP, $N$-bimodular and fixes $N$. Bounded direct sums and their predual direct sums give normality even without a countability hypothesis.

**Split inclusions and modular invariance.** If $N\subset F\subset M$ are actual unital inclusions, $F$ is a type-I factor and $N$ is not atomic, no normal expectation $M\to N$ exists: restrict it to $F\cong B(\mathcal K)$ and apply the result above. An atomic intermediate algebra also suffices, by composing its normal expectation from an ambient $B(\mathcal H)$ with the restricted expectation onto $N$. By the faithful-normal-state form of Takesaki's theorem, no faithful normal state of $M$ can have $\sigma_t(N)=N$ for every real $t$. Half-sided modular inclusions are not excluded.

In a concrete local net with a proved split property for $\overline{O_1}\subset O_2$, a sharp non-atomic $\mathcal A(O_1)$ is therefore not the range of a normal expectation from $\mathcal A(O_2)$. The positive collar supplies an intermediate type-I factor; it does not make the inner sharp algebra expected. The argument uses no vacuum, Bell theorem, dilation or field equation, and applies to a massive or interacting net only when its actual splitness and non-atomicity are established in the chosen representation.

**The generated-cover condition.** Let $M_{\mathrm{desc}}=\bigvee_i\mathcal A(D_i)$ in one fixed physical representation. Suppose for one $i$ there is a diamond $O$ such that $\mathcal A(D_i)$ is not atomic,
$$
 \overline{D_i}\subset O,\qquad
 \mathcal A(D_i)\subset F\subset\mathcal A(O)\subset M_{\mathrm{desc}},
\tag{F.10.12o.5}
$$
with $F$ a type-I factor. Then $M_{\mathrm{desc}}$ has no faithful normal modular state whose two-sided modular group preserves all its listed patch algebras. Such invariance would give a normal expectation onto $\mathcal A(D_i)$, contradicting the split obstruction. The containment of the actual split enlargement inside $M_{\mathrm{desc}}$ is essential.

Open-cover additivity supplies this containment when $\overline{D_i}\subset U=\bigcup_jD_j$: slightly enlarge that diamond to $\overline{D_i}\subset O\subset U$, and generate $\mathcal A(O)$ by small diamonds inside the cover patches. A common-open-core refinement gives an actual interior patch. Namely, suppose $U_n$ contains a fixed nonempty open $V$, all patch closures have Euclidean diameter at most $h_n\to0$, the relevant patch algebras are not atomic, and this same physical net has splitness and open-cover additivity. Choose $x\in V$ with $B(x,r)\subset V$. A patch containing $x$ has closure in $B(x,h_n)\subset V$ for $h_n<r$, so (F.10.12o.5) applies at every sufficiently small cover.

This is a statement about exactly realized continuum patch images and a faithful normal state on their actual generated algebra. It supplies no uniform finite-cutoff error lower bound: finite matrix algebras are atomic. Moving patches, auxiliary type-I comparison factors, nonnormal states, and a weaker-than-split phase-space replacement have not been assigned the split/non-atomic fixed-image hypotheses. In particular the selected atomic protocol of F.10.12i.14 is outside this obstruction. $\square$
